title: Bagbin urges voters to scrutinise campaign promises, resist political propaganda
body: The Speaker of Parliament, Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, has called on Ghanaians, particularly young people, to take a more critical approach to political campaigns by questioning promises and examining policy proposals before making electoral choices. He cautioned voters against letting political propaganda, slogans, and emotional appeals shape their decisions, stressing that citizens must assess what candidates and political parties offer and consider how they can translate promises into action. “Do not surrender your judgement to political propaganda… examine the issues, compare the alternatives, ask questions and exercise your constitutional rights peacefully and responsibly,” he said. Mr Bagbin made the remarks in a speech read on his behalf at the launch of Voices for the Ballot: Electoral Communication in Ghana , a book authored by strategic communication scholar and media development practitioner Dr Nana Sifa Twum. The publication explores how political communication influences Ghana’s electoral processes and voter behaviour, examining how political parties, candidates, the Electoral Commission, the media, civil society organisations, and citizens communicate before, during, and after elections. The Speaker observed that political discourse was often dominated by campaign slogans, personality-driven messages and emotional appeals, leaving substantive policy discussions and the fulfilment of campaign promises on the sidelines. He said responsible political communication must enable citizens to distinguish between campaign promises and actual policies, as well as allegations and facts. He added that informed voters, credible institutions and public accountability were essential to strengthening Ghana’s democracy. Mr Bagbin also encouraged academics, researchers and authors to investigate weaknesses in the country’s democratic processes and propose practical measures to address them. He called for closer cooperation among journalists, political communicators, electoral bodies and academia to improve media literacy and promote responsible political engagement. “Our ambition must be to build a democracy in which political communication does not merely persuade people to vote but equips them to understand why they are voting, what they are voting for, and how they can hold those elected accountable,” he said. He further highlighted the growing influence of social media on political discourse, warning against the spread of misinformation and falsehoods. He urged media practitioners to uphold professional standards and remain committed to accurate reporting. “Our democracy needs a media that is independent enough to scrutinise power, professional enough to distinguish between facts and fiction, and responsible enough to recognise the consequences of its reporting,” he added. The Speaker commended Dr Twum for contributing to discussions on electoral communication, expressing hope that the book would help promote responsible political campaigns, educate voters and strengthen democratic institutions. Dr Twum said electoral communication should go beyond helping politicians secure power and instead deepen democracy by encouraging citizens to understand their responsibilities and role in national development.

title: Mecca: May God convert our diversity to prosperity — Tinubu
body: —Business Community Will Support You in Whatever Capacity We Can — Rabiu —AbdulRazaq, Fagbemi Seek Divine Guidance for President By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu on Sunday hosted a dinner for members of his delegation in Makkah, Saudi Arabia, where he prayed to God to convert Nigeria’s diversity into prosperity. The President specifically prayed for divine intervention to transform the country’s diversity into an instrument of economic growth and national prosperity Ge expressed the hope that Nigeria’s ethnic, religious, and cultural diversity would continue to serve as a source of strength and national advancement rather than division, stressing the need for citizens to embrace mutual understanding, peaceful coexistence and a shared commitment to the country’s progress. He prayed that Almighty Allah would bless Nigeria with enduring peace, harmony and prosperity, and grant the nation’s leaders the wisdom, courage and foresight to steer the country towards greater development and improved living conditions for its people. “May Almighty Allah bless Nigeria, convert our diversity into prosperity as a country,” the President said. President Tinubu also prayed for divine guidance and protection for Nigerians at home and abroad, asking Allah to strengthen the bonds of brotherhood among citizens and inspire a renewed spirit of patriotism, compassion and service to the nation. The President noted that Nigeria’s abundant human and natural resources, coupled with the talents, creativity and enterprise of its diverse population, provided a strong foundation for building a prosperous and inclusive nation. The dinner with members of his delegation in Makkah provided an opportunity for fellowship and reflection on Nigerians’ shared aspirations for a peaceful, united and prosperous country. President Tinubu urged Nigerians of all faiths and backgrounds to keep working together in the national interest, expressing confidence that, with faith in Almighty Allah, unity of purpose, and collective determination, Nigeria would overcome its challenges and realise its full potential. President Tinubu left Nigeria on Thursday to perform the holy obligation in Mecca. At the dinner, Chairman of BUA Group Abdul Samad Rabiu, speaking on behalf of the country’s business community, pledged that they would continue to support the President in whatever capacity they could. Rabiu, who praised Tinubu’s dedication to national development, described the President as a committed leader working tirelessly to advance Nigeria’s development. He assured him of continued support in advancing his administration’s objectives. “Today is actually the third dinner we’re having with His Excellency Mr President since we came to Makkah on Thursday night or Friday morning when Mr President arrived. “So, we discussed, and the discussion was, you know, to always continue to pray for Nigeria, for peace, for unity and for Nigeria’s prosperity. To again, you know, thank His Excellency for his passion, for what he’s doing for Nigeria. “And also for us, it’s quite important because, as I said, it has given us the opportunity to come and pray not only for ourselves and our families, but also for Nigeria. “We will continue to support His Excellency in whatever capacity we can and definitely, as you all know, Mr President is very passionate about the country. He’s working very hard, and we’ll continue to support him,” he said. Rabiu expressed gratitude to the President for the opportunity to undertake the spiritual journey, particularly the rare privilege of entering the Kaaba to offer prayers. He said the experience had enabled members of the delegation to pray not only for themselves and their families but also for Nigeria at a critical period when the country required peace, unity, and prosperity. Also speaking, Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, on behalf of his colleagues, prayed for divine wisdom, strength, and courage for Tinubu to continue making decisions in Nigeria’s best interest. He said: “We are overwhelmed. Allah will continue to bless you. We will pray for you daily. Pray for Nigeria that you lead. And may Allah continue to strengthen you in making the right decisions. Strengthen your wisdom, your boldness, your audacity, and your courage.” AbdulRazaq expressed appreciation for the President’s invitation to participate in the pilgrimage, describing the spiritual experience as memorable. He prayed that Allah would continue to guide Tinubu, strengthen his leadership, and grant him the wisdom to navigate the challenges confronting the country. On his part, the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, also offered prayers for the President, asking Allah to grant his personal aspirations and answer his supplications. Fagbemi observed that, regardless of an individual’s accomplishments or position in life, there would always be personal aspirations requiring divine intervention. He consequently prayed for the fulfilment of Tinubu’s heart’s desires and continued divine blessings upon his life. President Tinubu performed the Umrah pilgrimage at the Grand Mosque in Makkah on Friday, October 30, offering prayers for Nigeria’s peace, national unity, stability, and prosperity. The dinner was attended by Yobe State Governor Mai Mala Buni, Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani, Jigawa State Governor Mohammed Namadi, Sokoto State Governor Ahmed Aliyu, Borno State Governor Babagana Umara Zulum, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare Professor Mohammed Ali Pate, National Security Adviser Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, Chief Executive Officer of Oando Plc Mr Wale Tinubu, Special Adviser to the President on Political Matters Ibrahim Kabiru Masari, and Chief of Staff to the President Femi Gbajabiamila, among others. The post Mecca: May God convert our diversity to prosperity — Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Oil prices slide more than 3% as Trump signals more time for Iran diplomacy
body: Oil prices fell on Monday morning amid hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough between the US and Iran , easing concerns about further supply disruption. US President Donald Trump reportedly said he wants to give diplomacy with Iran more time before considering renewed military strikes after Tuesday’s US midterm elections. The two key benchmarks slid more than 3 per cent in morning trading. Brent, the benchmark for two thirds of the world's crude, was trading at $110 a barrel at 7.55am UAE time. West Texas Intermediate, the gauge that tracks US crude, dropped to $100.90 a barrel. Mr Trump reportedly told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a phone call that he wanted to give diplomacy with Tehran more time before considering further strikes, Axios reported, quoting sources. CBS News reported that Mr Trump said he believed the US would soon end the war with Iran, "one way or the other". The US President was speaking to Right Side Broadcasting Network before a campaign rally in Iowa on Sunday, according to the report. "We've had such a victory, and we'll put it away very soon, one way or the other," Mr Trump was quoted as saying. "Either they'll make a deal, or we'll just end it … The job we've done is amazing." On Saturday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said no decision had been made on renewed strikes and that Mr Trump preferred a diplomatic resolution. On Sunday, the UK Maritime Trade Operations said it received a report that a ship had been struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz , after an attack on a liquefied natural gas tanker on Friday. The UKMTO also reported a vessel was struck east of Ras Al Khafji, along Saudi Arabia's Gulf coast. An Iranian delegation was in Qatar for discussions with mediators on Saturday, according to a Bloomberg report. Fears of US strikes on Iran have maintained upward pressure on crude, keeping supply risk premiums elevated. Oil prices started sliding on Monday after hitting a six-month high last week on Hormuz strikes and a US threat to hit Iran. Over the past week, both Brent and WTI increased by about 0.8 per cent. On a monthly basis, the benchmarks surged by about 15 per cent and 12 per cent, respectively, to hit their highest levels since April. Meanwhile, Swiss lender UBS said in a report recently it expected Brent crude prices to remain elevated, near $110 a barrel at the end of the year, as Middle Eastern supply remains volatile and geopolitical uncertainty persists. "Record freight costs, constrained tanker capacity, and recovering Chinese imports are other factors likely to keep oil prices high," UBS commodity analyst Giovanni Staunovo said.

title: NPFL Roundup: 3SC thrash Abia Warriors as Rivers United retain top spot
body:
Shooting Stars delivered one of their most convincing performances of the season on Sunday, thrashing Abia Warriors 4-1 in Ibadan, as Rivers United maintained their top spot in the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) after an eventful Matchday 11 that produced 20 goals across eight matches.
The Ibadan-based side dominated the encounter at the Lekan Salami Sports Complex, Adamasingba, to secure a much-needed victory and move into 10th position with 15 points from 11 matches.
Damilola Akinola opened the scoring in the fourth minute, and Sodiq Ibrahim extended the lead in the 41st minute.
Ibrahim completed his brace deep into first-half added time to deliver a commanding 3-0 lead at the interval.
Abia Warriors pulled one back in the 80th minute, raising hopes of a late recovery. However, Issa Yusuf restored Shooting Stars’ three-goal advantage with an 88th-minute strike to complete the emphatic victory.
In Kano, Nasarawa United’s five-match unbeaten run ended in a 2-0 defeat to Kano Pillars at the Sani Abacha Stadium.
Ibrahim Yahaya gave the hosts an early advantage in the 15th minute before Fabian Nworie doubled their lead in the 64th minute to secure maximum points for the Sai Masu Gida.
The defeat saw Nasarawa United drop to the fifth position with 17 points, while Kano Pillars climbed to fourth with 18 points, strengthening their position among the early contenders.
At the top of the table, Rivers United remained leaders despite a 1-1 draw with Rangers International.
The result left both clubs level on 18 points, although Rivers United retained first place with a superior goal difference of 10, compared with Rangers’ five. Rivers have played 11 matches, while Rangers have two games in hand.
Bendel Insurance also moved to 18 points after securing a valuable 2-1 away victory over Kwara United. The Benin-based club climbed to third position, with a game in hand over the two leading sides.
Elsewhere, Enyimba secured a narrow 1-0 victory over Kun Khalifat to move to 16th position with 11 points, offering the Aba-based side some relief in their campaign.
Plateau United and Warri Wolves shared the points in a 1-1 draw, while Katsina United defeated Sporting Lagos 2-1 to strengthen their position in the top half of the standings.
Inter Lagos and Rangers Bees also drew, leaving both sides struggling towards the bottom of the table.
Inter Lagos remain bottom with three points after a three-point and three-goal deduction for an infringement. Warri Wolves, who also suffered a similar deduction, occupy 17th position with 10 points.
The Matchday 11 results leave Rivers United, Rangers International, Bendel Insurance and Kano Pillars separated only by goal difference at the top, with each club having 18 points.
Nasarawa United follow in fifth place with 17 points, while Plateau United, Barau FC, Niger Tornadoes and Katsina United all have 16 points.
With several outstanding fixtures, the battle for early-season supremacy remains closely contested as the 2026/27 NPFL campaign progresses.
Tunde Eludini is a graduate of the Obafemi Awolowo University Ile-Ife, Nigeria where he studied International Relations. He is a Senior Correspondent coordinating the sports section for PREMIUM TIMES. Twitter : @tundeyeludini

title: UPSA graduates urged to embrace positive attitudes
body: Dr Divine Selase Agbeti, the Director-General of the Cyber Security Authority (CSA), has urged graduates of the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA) to cultivate positive attitudes and commit to continuous learning to succeed in their professional careers. He said academic qualifications alone were insufficient to guarantee success in the world of work, stressing that determination, dedication, integrity and a willingness to learn were equally important. Dr Agbeti advised on Monday at the University’s 18th graduation ceremony for students of the Faculty of Information Technology and Communication Studies in Accra. He said the certificates awarded to the graduates represented opportunities for growth and achievement, urging them to approach the next phase of their lives with confidence, discipline and a positive mindset. “Your attitude will shape your career far more than the grades you have earned or the accolades you have received,” he said. Dr Agbeti encouraged graduates who might not have obtained excellent academic results not to lose hope, noting that a third-class degree from one institution could be equivalent to a first-class degree elsewhere. He said graduates could rise to leadership positions regardless of their academic classifications if they demonstrated the right attitude, determination and commitment to excellence. Dr Agbeti expressed concern over what he described as a growing culture of dishonesty, laziness and mediocrity in society, noting that many people were becoming more interested in making quick money than in hard work, integrity and quality service delivery. He urged the graduates to help change that mindset by embracing honesty, diligence and professionalism in their chosen careers. Acknowledging the challenges graduates might face in securing employment, he said the right attitude could help them distinguish themselves in an increasingly competitive job market. He added that retaining employment and advancing professionally would depend on their commitment to quality service delivery, dedication and personal development. Dr Agbeti urged the graduates not to stop learning after obtaining their degrees, particularly in an era of rapid technological advancement and artificial intelligence. He said continuous learning and innovation were essential for remaining relevant in the evolving world of work. He encouraged the graduates to be patient, seek mentorship and, where appropriate, accept opportunities that would allow them to demonstrate their knowledge and skills. Dr Agbeti said challenges should be viewed as opportunities for growth rather than obstacles to success, adding that individuals’ responses to adversity helped shape their character and determine their progress. He urged the graduates to approach their post-graduation journey with positive, growth-oriented and grateful mindsets while remaining kind, passionate and committed to their goals. Professor John Kwaku Mensah Mawutor, Vice-Chancellor of UPSA, announced that the University would begin assembling laptops in commercial quantities by December 2026 as part of efforts to improve students’ access to technology and equip them with practical digital skills. The initiative, which would involve students assembling the laptops themselves, is intended to support the University’s ambition of ensuring that every student owns a laptop upon registration to facilitate teaching and learning. The project follows the launch of a laptop assembly initiative in October, with the University seeking to expand its operations to meet growing demand. Prof. Mawutor said UPSA was also strengthening its focus on innovation and entrepreneurship by encouraging students to develop practical solutions to real-world challenges. He said the University had, during the period under review, brought together 57 student innovators from different academic levels to work in teams on projects addressing challenges in financial technology, healthcare, education, taxation, disaster response and energy. Ms Nancy Atsu Edem, the overall best graduating student at the Faculty of Information Technology and Communication Studies, commended the University for providing her with the opportunity to excel and pledged to embrace the future with confidence. Ms Edem, who graduated with a Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.93, attributed her success to resilience and determination.

title: Attempts to discredit CAR-Russia cooperation won’t change country’s course — Touadera
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. Pressure and attempts to discredit the cooperation of the Central African Republic (CAR) with Russia will not change the republic’s course, CAR President Faustin-Archange Touadera said in an interview with TASS.
"Pressure and attempts to discredit our cooperation with Russia will not change our course, as it is based on real needs in the field of security and development, and not on momentary considerations," Touadera emphasized.
Previously, he noted that Russian instructors helped the CAR army prevent a violent seizure of power in the country by militants, as well as ensure the holding of elections, when in 2020 and 2021 the very existence of the constitutional order was under threat.

title: Ukraine's territorial integrity is in Türkiye's long-term interests – expert
body:
Sinan Demirtürk, a Turkish scholar, lecturer at Gazi University in Ankara and head of the Turkish Foundation for Political and Strategic Research (TÜRPAV), made this statement on CNN Türk while commenting on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's visit to Istanbul, Ukrinform reports.
"Türkiye also has a historical memory. In other words, when it comes to preserving Ukraine's territorial integrity and possible peace talks between Russia and Ukraine, Türkiye understands that Ukraine's stability and territorial integrity will directly affect its policy in the Black Sea region and towards the Turkic world in the long term," Demirtürk said.
According to the expert, meaningful peace talks are unlikely in the short term but could take place in the medium term.
He believes that Russia achieving its desired outcome, including legitimizing the occupation of Ukrainian territories or bringing about a change in the country's leadership by replacing President Zelensky, would not be in Ankara's interests.
"Given the history of Turkish-Russian relations, we can see the problems facing Türkiye's foreign policy and its borders when Crimea is lost and Russians are present in Ukraine. Therefore, as a participant in this process, Türkiye is steering it towards a balanced compromise," the scholar said.
Demirtürk also linked the significance of Zelensky's visit to the fact that it took place immediately after the summit of leaders of the Organization of Turkic States.
"The fact that such an important visit was scheduled immediately after the summit of leaders of the Organization of Turkic States further underscores Türkiye's role in ensuring international peace, security in the Black Sea and building a lasting and sustainable peace that would make it possible to preserve Ukraine's territorial integrity," he said.
According to the expert, while maintaining contacts with the United States and Russia, Türkiye is also demonstrating that it remains a neighbor and partner that does not leave Ukraine to fend for itself.
On October 31, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Istanbul. Much of their talks focused on finding ways to unblock the Black Sea. The leaders also discussed the possibility of holding peace talks in Türkiye.

title: News Reflection: Jonvic Remulla dropped the ball on Bato
body: It was a heartfelt mea culpa from Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla: He should have arrested the fugitive senator Bato dela Rosa when he had the chance. But, alas, there was Alan. Senator Alan Peter Cayetano stood in the way, Remulla said. Doing it now would be too costly, he added. He wouldn’t want to risk the lives of 300 policemen over the arrest of one man, who’s wanted by the International Criminal Court for running a police operation that killed somewhere around 3,000 to 30,000 people — the drug war, remember? Paterno Esmaquel II with this week’s News Reflection. – Rappler.com Presenter, writer: Paterno Esmaquel II Producer, writer, director, video editor: JC Gotinga Videographers: Leone Requilman, Randall Rosales Graphics artist: Sam Calleja Supervising editor: Miriam Grace Go Supervising producer: Beth Frondoso

title: Britain shouldn’t apologise for slave trade; Africa profited — Kemi Badenoch
body: By Nkiruka Nnorom, with agency report Leader of UK’s Conservative Party, Kemi Badenoch, has urged British not to apologise for its role in transatlantic slave trade, saying it would amount to a “navel-gazing distraction”, and would be used as lever for financial compensation by campaigners. Her comments came as UK’s PM, Andy Burnham, said he was considering a formal apology, before he flies to the Commonwealth heads of government meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda next week. Speaking to broadcasters yesterday, Badenoch described slavery as an evil “in which people from every continent and region participated”. She also questioned whether it was worth future leaders attending the Commonwealth summit, given that it was now dominated by calls for reparations. In an article for the Guardian, Burnham said there would not be reparations in the form of financial compensation, but said he was prepared to engage in helping poorer countries restructure debt on more favourable terms. But reacting, Badenoch said leaders should be “honest about the whole history, not select the parts that are politically convenient today, especially given Britain’s leading role in ending the transatlantic slave trade”. She wrote in a social media post: “If Caribbean countries are asking Britain for a formal apology for Britain’s role in the transatlantic slave trade, will they also be asking the same of the descendants of African kingdoms, rulers and merchants who captured, sold and profited from the trade?” “On demands for reparations, whether through cash or debt relief, we have been down this track before,” she said. Badenoch recalled that campaigns such as Jubilee 2000, Drop the Debt and Make Poverty History had pushed for debt cancellation for poorer countries 25 years ago, leading to more than $100 billion in debt being written off. However, she noted that many of those countries had since accumulated even larger debts. Badenoch said Burnham’s apology was unnecessary because of comments made by Tony Blair two decades ago. “The Commonwealth should be looking forward, not endlessly backwards,” she posted. Badenoch told Sky News she believed that even if an apology was offered, campaigners would see it as a step towards financial compensation. “What I’m worried about is that this CHOGM summit is yet another opportunity for people to start asking Britain for money because of the slave trade. We need to start looking at how we can bring the Commonwealth together – start looking forwards, not backwards. “I don’t think we should be giving any money to compensate people for the slave trade, and I don’t think Andy Burnham needs to be apologising because it is a lever to wedge open the door to ask for cash.” Speaking in the same vein, UK’s Chancellor, John Healey, said it would be unfair for the British people to be hit financially for reparations when they had no role in the slave trade. “The prime minister has said, look, we are open to a discussion about an apology. He feels that’s the right thing, particularly ahead of the Commonwealth leaders’ conference. “But he doesn’t believe that reparations are the right approach, and considering a formal apology doesn’t mean accepting that British people now should accept the financial liability for any part in things that happened hundreds of years ago, in which they had no role,’’ he said. The post Britain shouldn’t apologise for slave trade; Africa profited — Kemi Badenoch appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Christians in Nigeria still face unspeakable violence — US Rep Moore
body: •Says fight against persecution must continue one year after CPC designation By Nkiruka Nnorom A member of United States House of Representatives, Riley Moore, has said Christians in Nigeria have continued to face unspeakable violence, one year after Nigeria was designated Country of Particular Concern, CPC. Moore stated this in a post on X to mark anniversary of designation of Nigeria as CPC by President Donald Trump. “Christians in Nigeria, and around the world, continue to face unspeakable violence. On this anniversary, we must rededicate our efforts to defend Christians in Nigeria and anywhere they face persecution,” Moore wrote. The lawmaker’s comment came as he reviewed impact of CPC designation, which he said was right decision by President Trump, alongside efforts by House Appropriations Republicans to condition aid to Nigeria and impose requirements to defend Christians, and advocacy by faith-based organisations. Moore said: “The President’s steadfast and decisive leadership, @houseappropsgop’s work to condition aid to Nigeria and impose requirements to defend Christians, and the tireless work of advocacy and faith based organizations has started to make a difference. “We saw the first Christmas without a massacre of Christians in recent memory. There is much more work to be done, but the government of Nigeria has shown signs of a willingness to address the violence against our brothers and sisters in Christ.” He had earlier noted that Nigeria witnessed first Christmas without massacre of Christians in recent memory, but said much more work needed to be done. Moore, however, hailed the federal government’s efforts, saying Abuja had shown signs of willingness to address violence. Nigeria was first designated as a Country of Particular Concern, CPC, by the United States in 2020 under President Donald Trump over alleged violations of religious freedom. The designation was delisted in 2021 by the Biden administration, a move that was criticised by some US lawmakers and faith-based groups. On November 2025, President Trump, on return to White House, redesignated Nigeria as CPC, citing continued attacks on Christian communities in Middle Belt and North-East. The CPC status under US International Religious Freedom Act allows Washington to impose policy options, including sanctions, aid restrictions and diplomatic pressure on countries adjudged to have engaged in or tolerated systematic violations of religious freedom. Following redesignation, House Appropriations Republicans moved to condition US assistance to Nigeria on demonstrable steps to protect Christians and prosecute perpetrators of religious-based violence. The federal government has consistently rejected characterisation of insecurity as religious persecution, arguing that terrorism by Boko Haram, ISWAP, banditry and farmer-herder clashes affect both Christians and Muslims. The government has noted it was implementing security reforms, engaging with US on fact-finding, and strengthening protection of vulnerable communities across Benue, Plateau, Southern Kaduna and other hotspots. title: Melania Trump calls mission in Alyoshki successful, expresses gratitude to Russia, Ukraine
body:
WASHINGTON, November 2. /TASS/. US First Lady Melania Trump said she considers the humanitarian mission in the city of Alyoshki, Kherson Region, to be successful and expressed her gratitude to Russia.
"The ceasefire concludes. The mission was a success <...>. On behalf of America, I commend to Russia and Ukraine for their leadership and cooperation surrounding the Oleshky (Alyoshki - TASS) ceasefire," she wrote on Sunday on the social media platform X.
"I hope that Oleshky serves as a foundation for lasting peace between both nations. The ceasefire began on October 27, 2026, and continued until November 1, 2026, as planned," she added.
Earlier, Russia and Ukraine, with the assistance of the US First Lady, agreed to a ceasefire in Alyoshki, Kherson Region, to ensure the conduct of a humanitarian operation. The Russian Armed Forces introduced a regime of silence in the Kherson direction from 04:00 a.m. Moscow time on October 27 in connection with preparations for the humanitarian operation in the city. On October 30, the humanitarian mission was carried out: residents were distributed several dozen tons of humanitarian aid--food, hygiene products, generator fuel, and other necessary items, Russian Human Rights Ombudswoman Yana Lantratova said. Also, everyone who expressed a desire was able to leave without hindrance both to other regions of Russia and to Ukraine.
On September 21, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the humanitarian situation in Alyoshki critical. It was impossible to bring either food or medicines into the city due to shelling and drone attacks from Kiev.

title: ECG announces power outage in parts of Ashanti Region on November 3
body: The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has announced a planned power outage in parts of the Ashanti Region on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, to carry out maintenance work to improve electricity service delivery. In a notice issued on Sunday, November 1, ECG said the exercise would run from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., temporarily interrupting power supply to affected communities. title: Nigeria 1-0: Venezuela: Flamingos qualify for U-17 World Cup semi-final
body:
Nigeria’s Flamingos have qualified for the semi-finals of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after edging Venezuela 1-0 in a tense quarter-final encounter in Morocco on Sunday.
Captain Azeezat Oduntan scored the decisive goal from the penalty spot in the 89th minute to send the Nigerian youngsters into the last four for only the second time in their history.
The breakthrough came after Oluebube Umejiaku was fouled inside the penalty area, prompting the referee to award Nigeria a spot kick. Oduntan stepped forward and converted to give the Flamingos a dramatic late lead.
The victory marks Nigeria’s return to the semi-finals for the first time since their historic third-place finish at the 2022 edition in India.
The contest was closely fought, with Nigeria creating several opportunities but struggling to beat Venezuela’s goalkeeper and captain, Valeria Rebanales.
Tosin Rafiu came close in the 19th minute, but Rebanales reacted well to tip her effort over the crossbar. The Venezuelan goalkeeper was again called into action in the 35th minute, denying Mary Dunstan.
Oluwakemi Adegbuyi also threatened before half-time, but neither side could find the breakthrough as the teams went into the interval goalless.
Venezuela had opportunities of their own, with Ariana Ojeda and Migleydys Bolsegui testing Nigeria’s defence.
The second half continued in a similarly competitive fashion, with the Flamingos pushing for a goal against a Venezuelan side that had already demonstrated its resilience by eliminating Germany in the round of 16.
Nigeria eventually found the breakthrough through Oduntan’s late penalty, ending Venezuela’s challenge and securing a place among the tournament’s final four.
The result extends the Flamingos’ impressive run in Morocco. After losing their opening group match 2-1 to Poland, Akeem Busari’s side recovered with victories over Puerto Rico and defending champions DPR Korea to progress from Group B.
They subsequently defeated Mexico 2-1 in the round of 16 before overcoming Venezuela to reach the semi-finals.
Nigeria’s victory also keeps alive their ambition of winning the competition for the first time.
Meanwhile, the other African team in the quarter-finals, Ghana were eliminated on Sunday, with Japan edging them 1-0 to advance.
The Flamingos will now turn their attention to the semi-finals as they seek to take another step towards the title.
Tunde Eludini is a graduate of the Obafemi Awolowo University Ile-Ife, Nigeria where he studied International Relations. He is a Senior Correspondent coordinating the sports section for PREMIUM TIMES. Twitter : @tundeyeludini

title: Power sector fix ‘ongoing work’ — APC-PCC; bonds can’t light homes, says ADC-PCC
body: By Omeiza Ajayi & Luminous Jannamike ABUJA—The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, and African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, were yesterday locked in a verbal war over President Bola Tinubu’s declaration during his campaign in 2023 that if he failed to give Nigerians power, they should not re-elect him in 2027. Read Also: Banks raise lending rates for top borrowers despite CBN cuts While APC-PCC said the President’s fixing of the country’s electricity sector was ongoing and had signed the Electricity Act 2023 to enable states generate, distribute and transmit power, ADC-PCC insisted Nigerians could not power their homes and businesses with laws, bonds and project announcements. In a statement yesterday, the spokesperson of APC-PCC, Dele Alake, said recent public commentary had reproduced the campaign promise without its closing qualification. Speaking to members of the Organised Private Sector, OPS, in Lagos, ahead of the 2023 general elections, Tinubu, then the APC candidate, had reportedly said: “Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills anymore. ‘’A promise made will be a promise kept. If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second term, don’t vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons I couldn’t deliver.” Alake said the commentary left out the final part, that “should he fall short, he would owe Nigerians an adequate explanation before seeking their support for a second term.” He argued that a fair assessment of the pledge should consider the full statement, alongside the administration’s record since 2023, measured against measurable improvements in electricity supply, metering, infrastructure and market stability. “While fixing the power sector crisis remains unfinished, the President is working consistently to deliver on his promise to Nigerians, and his commitment to face the challenges head-on has never diminished,” the council said. The APC-PCC said Tinubu signed the Electricity Act, 2023, on June 9, within two weeks of taking office. According to the council, the law liberalised and deregulated the power sector and moved it away from the Exclusive List, so states can take part in power generation, distribution and transmission. It said Lagos, Enugu, Abia, Ekiti, Oyo, Kaduna and Niger states had started using the law to set up their own electricity regulatory agencies and attract private capital. On debts, the campaign council said Tinubu “took on the over N6 trillion legacy debt that had accumulated from 2015 to 2025,” adding that the administration created a N4 trillion bond programme to settle verified legacy debts owed 21 power generation companies, Gencos, and gas companies, Gascos. The council said the first and second tranches of the programme had raised over N1.2 trillion, and noted that the effect was becoming evident in the ability of Gencos to invest in upgrading their plants. “Just a few days ago, Geregu Power Plc announced investments in new power transformers to enhance operations at the Geregu 1 Power Plant. Other firms are making similar investments,” it said. On metering, the council said Tinubu started a Presidential Metering Initiative to close a gap of over seven million meters, noting that well over 1.5 million customers had been metered under the initiative in the last three years. The APC-PCC added that the Rural Electrification Agency had connected universities, hospitals and rural communities to solar power. It said the government had also unveiled plans to modernise the Osogbo Grid Control Centre, which it said was built over 60 years ago, with plans to build an East-West super grid. On transmission, the council said Tinubu reviewed the Presidential Power Initiative, PPI, which was started by the late President Muhammadu Buhari, and signed an Acceleration Agreement in December 2023 with the German partners. It said the Federal Executive Council, FEC, approved the contract for the first batch of five Transmission Company of Nigeria, TCN, substations in key load centres by December 2024. These projects, it said, “are now being completed and will be commissioned before the end of the administration’s first term.” In June 2026, the council added, FEC approved the contract for a second batch, covering eight new substations and the upgrade of four existing ones. “Power project implementation requires equipment that is a long-lead item and thus cannot be achieved overnight,” the council said. … on tariffs On tariffs, APC-PCC said Tinubu “significantly aligned the tariffs to cost to restore liquidity to the electricity market” and put in place a system to protect low-income households. ‘’The creation of service bands with different tariffs was a first step to improve the financial viability of distribution companies and cash flow in the sector. It also reduced the government’s financial burden from tariff subsidies.’’ ADC-PCC says bonds can’t light homes, slams APC over Tinubu’s power pledge Replying the APC, African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, in a statement by the Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, accused the APC campaign council of celebrating policy documents and financial interventions instead of addressing the failure to translate them into reliable electricity. “The APC should spare Nigerians the spectacle of celebrating paperwork while homes and businesses remain in darkness. After three and a half years, families still struggle to keep their homes lit. Traders and small business owners spend scarce resources on alternative power, yet struggle to keep their businesses alive. ‘’Nigerians are billed for electricity they cannot rely on. President Tinubu promised steady power and an end to estimated billing. That promise has not been kept,” he said. It also faulted the electricity band system, arguing that consumers were paying different tariffs without corresponding improvements in supply.” ADC campaign council cited Band A tariffs of about N209.50 per unit in many areas, before VAT, to illustrate the burden on consumers, insisting that Nigerians across all five bands continued to pay for electricity they could not reliably access. “No family should have to weigh the cost of electricity against the cost of food. No business should be left to pay more while receiving less,” the council said. Electricity subsidies It also demanded clarity on the federal government’s plan to end electricity subsidies from 2027, questioning what the move would mean for household and business electricity bills. The council proposed working with state governments and regulators to abolish the existing band system and introduce what he described as a fairer, more affordable framework that would hold power companies accountable for electricity delivered. ADC-PCC lampooned the administration’s multitrillion-naira bond programme to settle legacy debts owed generation companies which, he said, could not be mistaken for investment in new electricity generation infrastructure. It alleged that the Tinubu administration had not built any new generation infrastructure of its own to expand Nigeria’s power capacity. “Paying old debts is not the same as building new power infrastructure. Bonds cannot be presented as a substitute for power in people’s homes,” he said. He also raised concerns over VAT on electricity and the five per cent surcharge provided for certain fossil fuels, including petrol and diesel, under the Nigeria Tax Act. Vanguard News The post Power sector fix ‘ongoing work’ — APC-PCC; bonds can’t light homes, says ADC-PCC appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: VAST Ghana calls for comprehensive excise tax reforms in 2027-2030 Budget Statement
body: The Vision for Accelerated Sustainable Development Ghana (VAST Ghana) has called on the Ministry of Finance to introduce comprehensive excise tax reforms in the 2027-2030 Budget to reduce the growing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs). A statement copied to the Ghana News Agency by Ms Jennifer Maame Ama Owusu, Communications Manager, VAST Ghana, said the excise tax reform would help protect vulnerable populations and mobilise sustainable domestic resources for healthcare financing. The statement recommended that the Ministry of Finance adopt a comprehensive health tax reform as a strategic fiscal and public health priority. The VAST Ghana called for an extension of the hybrid excise tax structure to all alcoholic beverages (Beer, wine, cider, and ready-to-drink alcoholic products) rather than limiting the reform to spirits. Others were the incorporation of alcohol-by-volume (ABV) principles so that products are taxed according to their alcohol content, and the adoption of a minimum pricing policy to complement excise taxation. It further recommended the increase of the specific tobacco excise tax from GHc 0.28 to GHc 1.00 per cigarette stick to ensure total taxes reach 75 per cent of the retail price, and upward review of the ad valorem tax from 50 per cent to 100 per cent. It said this reform would substantially increase the price of cigarettes, reduce affordability, and strengthen the health impact of tobacco taxation. The statement also called for the abolition of the excise taxation on e-cigarettes and e-liquids, adding that, “Ghana’s public health and fiscal frameworks should not create a situation in which products that are prohibited under the Public Health Act 2012 (Act 851) are simultaneously presented within the excise tax system as taxable commodities.” It stated that removing these products from the excise tax schedule would improve policy coherence and strengthen enforcement. It urged for the reintroduction of the 20 per cent tax on fruit juices in the interest of public health, while the Ministry introduces a hybrid excise tax for all Sugar-Sweetened Beverages (SSB) products. The statement called for earmarking a defined proportion of revenue generated from tobacco, alcohol, SSB, and other health taxes to support NCD prevention, health promotion, tobacco and alcohol control programmes, and other priority health interventions like the Ghana Medical Trust Fund, Free Primary Healthcare policy, among others. It noted that the 2027 to 2030 Budget framework provides Ghana with an opportunity to institutionalise health taxation as a core component of fiscal policy, NCD prevention, and sustainable health financing. “The evidence is increasingly clear that well-designed health taxes reduce consumption of harmful products while generating public revenue,” it stated, adding that WHO’s ‘3 by 35’ Initiative places the taxation approach at the centre of global efforts to reduce NCDs and strengthen domestic financing. VAST Ghana therefore called on the Ministry of Finance to make these reforms a central component of Ghana’s domestic resource mobilisation and public health strategy.

title: ‘No-fees-stress’ policy boosts tertiary education enrollment – SDA College Vice Principal
body: The No-Fees-Stress Policy has boosted access to tertiary education, with beneficiaries at the SDA College of Education expressing appreciation to the government for easing the financial burden on students. Dr Gifty Seiwaa Nyarko, the Vice Principal of the SDA College of Education, Asokore – Koforidua in the Eastern region, said the college recorded 470 beneficiaries under the policy during the 2025/2026 academic year, all of whom were first-year students. Dr Nyarko, who was speaking in an interview with the Ghana News Agency (GNA), added that the beneficiaries comprised 160 males and 310 females. She described the high patronage as a demonstration of students’ understanding of the importance of taking advantage of available government interventions to pursue higher education. She advised beneficiaries to use the money provided by the government judiciously, since their academic user fees had already been covered under the policy. “The government had already supported you financially, so do not misuse the money given to you by your parents. Use it for things that can support your stay on campus and enhance your studies,” she said. The Vice Principal expressed gratitude to the government for the financial relief provided to students. Ms Esther Ansah, a first-year Bachelor of Education student in Early Grade Education, notes that the policy has made it possible for her to pursue her dream career in tertiary education, without any financial difficulty of paying academic user fees. “If the policy had not been introduced, I would not have been able to afford the fees at this initial stage. This would have disrupted my career,” she said. Mr Samuel Okai Ntiri, a beneficiary pursuing Primary Education, also noted that although some money had been provided by his family for his upkeep, it would not have been enough if he were to pay academic user fees. President John Dramani Mahama launched the No-Fees-Stress Policy on July 4, 2025, at the SDA College of Education as part of efforts to increase enrolment in the country’s public tertiary institutions. The policy covers academic user fees for all first-year (Level 100) students in public tertiary institutions, while continuing students at Levels 200, 300 and 400 may access the Student Loan Plus or the regular Student Loan Trust Fund (SLTF) loan scheme for financial support.

title: LIVESTREAM: ICC’s 5th status conference on Rodrigo Duterte’s case
body: MANILA, Philippines – The International Criminal Court (ICC) will hold its fifth status conference on former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte’s crimes against humanity case on Monday, November 2. This comes weeks before the opening of the trial scheduled on November 30 . A status conference is where parties discuss matters related to the case before proceeding to a full trial. So far, the court has had four conferences: on May 27, when it announced that the trial will begin on November 30 ; on June 23 , when the chamber cautioned lawyers against granting media interviews; and the third one, on September 16, when the former president made an appearance. The court held the fourth conference on October 13, where the parties discussed the list of evidence anew. Duterte will skip the Monday hearing after waiving his right to be present. For the fifth status conference, the Trial Chamber III and the parties will discuss the following: Daily schedule Audio-visual link testimony and rights of audience List of witnesses and number of hours for the Prosecution’s presentation of evidence Potentially exculpatory evidence, agreed facts, and calling order Rule 68(3) applications and in-court protective measures Security of defense missions Watch the livestream starting at 4:30 pm (Philippine time). Download the Rappler app and join the Justice and Crime chat room to get live updates from Rappler’s justice reporter Jairo Bolledo. – Rappler.com

title: Senate Roundup: Tinubu’s fresh loan request, convict transfer, Abuja tenancy rules, others
body:
The Senate resumed its plenary last Tuesday with an executive communication in which President Bola Tinubu sought the National Assembly’s approval to process external loans worth $20.5 billion and €1.04 billion under the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.
The president said the proposed loans would finance critical projects across sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms.
In the letter, Mr Tinubu said the borrowing was necessary to support his administration’s reform agenda. He added that the projects had been selected based on technical and economic evaluations and their expected contributions to the country’s socio-economic development.
After reading the letter, Senate President Godswill Akpabio referred the request to the Senate Committees on Local and Foreign Debts and Appropriations for further scrutiny. He directed the committees to report back within one week.
On the same day, Mr Akpabio read another executive communication in which President Tinubu transmitted a bill seeking to empower the Nigerian government to enter into agreements with other countries for convicted Nigerian citizens to serve their sentences in Nigeria.
The bill seeks to amend the Transfer of Convicted Offenders Enactment and Enforcement Act, 2004, to facilitate the transfer of convicted offenders between Nigeria and other countries under mutual agreements.
In the letter, the president said the proposed legislation would empower the Nigerian government to enter into agreements with other countries to transfer convicted offenders to Nigeria.
He also said it would enable Nigeria to honour similar requests from foreign governments, subject to the agreements’ terms.
As part of efforts to curb criminal activities in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), lawmakers of the upper chamber on Tuesday resolved to initiate legislation requiring tenants in the territory (FCT) to present valid means of identification before renting apartments.
Mr Akpabio directed Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele to draft the bill for the National Assembly’s consideration.
He gave the directive during plenary while lawmakers were debating a report by the Senate committees on Diaspora and Non-Governmental Organisations; Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters; Foreign Affairs; and Special Duties on the need to protect Nigerians from being trafficked to Libya for slavery.
The report was presented by Aniekan Bassey, chair of the Senate Committee on Diaspora and Non-Governmental Organisations.
Mr Akpabio expressed concern that many property owners rent out their properties to strangers without obtaining adequate information about their identities, occupations and other relevant details.
He said lack of proper documentation makes it difficult for security agencies to trace suspects when crimes are committed, allowing perpetrators to escape without leaving a clear trail.
The Senate on Wednesday called on the federal government to immortalise the late National Leader of Afenifere, the pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Reuben Fasoranti, who died at the age of 100.
The upper chamber recommended that an educational institution be renamed after the late elder statesman in recognition of his contributions to the advancement of education in South-west Nigeria.
The lawmakers adopted the resolution following a motion sponsored by Adeniyi Adegbonmire (APC, Ondo Central) during plenary.
Moving the motion, Mr Adegbonmire, who chairs the Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters, said Mr Fasoranti’s contributions to education profoundly influenced his approach to governance, particularly his emphasis on human welfare and humanitarian service.
The senator described Mr Fasoranti as a committed follower of the late nationalist and politician Obafemi Awolowo, who led the Action Group during the First Republic and later became associated with the Unity Party of Nigeria (UPN) during the Second Republic.
He also noted that Mr Fasoranti was among prominent Nigerians who opposed military rule and advocated restoring democratic governance in the country.
