title: Netanyahu's opponents have the numbers – now can they make a deal?
body: Israel 's coalition talks will intensify this week as opponents of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu try to wrest the premiership from him after an inconclusive election result. Neither Mr Netanyahu's right-wing coalition nor an opposition bloc led by former army general Gadi Eisenkot won a majority at last Tuesday's election . The opposition could reach a majority by working with Arab politicians, who have offered to help bring down Mr Netanyahu after winning a record 19 seats. Together, the Eisenkot bloc and Arab parties would have 67 seats in the 120-member Knesset. But any such deal would be highly controversial in Israel, especially at a sensitive time in the Middle East conflict. Early talks The constitutional process for forming a government will not start before Wednesday, when President Isaac Herzog receives the certified results. He will then hold consultations before inviting one candidate to form a government within 42 days. Speaking on Sunday, Mr Herzog called on party leaders to find "creative solutions". He has previously urged them to avoid a stalemate that leads to a second election. Informal talks have already begun among potential members of the anti-Netanyahu alliance. Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister whose alliance came third at the election, confirmed on Sunday that he would support Mr Eisenkot. That was unsurprising, even if some had speculated he could be drawn into Mr Netanyahu's camp. Fraud claims won't change result While balloting and counting were continuing, Mr Netanyahu was sowing doubts about the result by accusing Arab parties of having "stolen" the election. Arab politicians dismissed the claims as an attempt to undermine their record result. Authorities have claimed some wrongdoing was being investigated, but said on Sunday that any such inquiries would not undermine the overall result. The elections "were conducted properly", said Noam Sohlberg, the head of Israel's Central Elections Committee, in a joint statement with the country's Attorney General and internal security chief. "The election results reflect the will of the voter." Mr Netanyahu's Likud party called Mr Sohlberg's comments perplexing, maintaining that a "dark cloud" hangs over the results. Arab parties All eyes are keeping a watch on whether the 19 members from the Arab Joint List and the Ra'am party could join a coalition or at least agree to tolerate a minority government. Ahmad Tibi, the leader of the Ta'al or Arab Movement for Change party, told Israel's Channel 12 that "we want to help anyone who wants to bring down this awful government" but said he did not want a ministerial post. "Without the Arab parties there won't be change," Mr Tibi said. Some potential Eisenkot allies had ruled out relying on Arab support during the campaign and any such deal would be seen as politically risky. US ambassador Mike Huckabee has said it would be "troubling" to include any politicians who had not condemned the October 7 attacks on Israel in 2023. Netanyahu's next move Mr Netanyahu remains in office for now. With Americans voting in midterm polls on Tuesday, there are widespread fears that the US and Israel could resume strikes on Iran when both countries' elections are over. It has been speculated that such a move could benefit Mr Netanyahu, perhaps leading to a unity government in which he stays in power. Some opposition figures have suggested it would be improper for him to embark on major military action in his caretaker role. Yair Golan, the leader of the centre-left Democrats, said on Sunday that Mr Netanyahu lacks the "moral legitimacy" to run a new campaign against Iran. "Israel's security must not be allowed to become a tool in Netanyahu's political survival struggle. Therefore, establishing an alternative government as soon as possible is critical," he said.

title: N70,000 allowance showdown: Civil servants fire back at TUC
body: *Insist FG-Labour agreement stands *JNPSNC reveals details of agreement, including 6-month transport allowance, others By Victor Ahiuma-Young Civil servants, under the aegis of Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC, have defended the N70,000 transportation allowance agreement reached between the federal government and organised labour, insisting that the rejection of the deal by the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, would not affect its implementation. Read Also: TUC rejects FG’s proposed N70,000 monthly transport allowance for workers The council said the agreement, signed on October 27, 2026, followed more than six hours of intensive negotiations and constructive engagements involving the federal government, the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, JNPSNC and the Joint Health Sector Unions JOHESU. The position of the council was contained in a circular signed by the National Secretary, Mr Gbenga Olowoyo, and addressed to the national presidents and general secretaries of affiliated unions, as well as state chairmen and secretaries of the Joint Public Service Negotiating Councils across the federation. The unions JNPSNC is made up of the Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria, ASCSN; Nigeria Civil Service Union, NCSU; Nigeria Union of Public Service, Reportorial, Secretarial, Data Processors and Allied Workers, NUPSTRAW; Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria, MHWUN; and National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives, NANNM. Others are Nigeria Union of Agriculture and Allied Employees, NUAAE; Amalgamated Union of Public Corporations; Civil Service Technical and Recreational Services Employees, AUPCTRE; and National Union of Printing, Publishing and Paper Products Workers, NUPPPPROW. On the government side are the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment; Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation; Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation; Federal Ministry of Justice; Federal Civil Service Commission; National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission; Federal Ministry of Finance; Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation; and Budget Office of the Federation. In the circular, Olowoyo explained that the N70,000 transportation allowance would be paid monthly to public servants for six months, beginning from November 2026, to cushion the impact of rising transportation costs on workers and their dependents. He also urged state and local governments to embrace the agreement and complement the federal government’s intervention, particularly in view of the substantial revenue accruing to the sub-national governments. The circular read, among others: “The meeting was not only tough but also took more than six hours before both the Federal Government and labour sides could enter into terms. “On the issue of payment of N70,000 transportation allowance, which will be paid for the next six months to public servants, starting from the month of November 2026, it was meant to subsidise the unbearable transportation cost being experienced by Nigerian workers. “It is expected that state and local governments will be patriotic enough (and with humongous money accruable to both state and local governments) to concur with the agreement in order to complement the federal government’s effort to facilitate its implementation at both states and local government levels purposely to ameliorate the hardship of Nigerian workers and their dependents. “Also, the agreement cemented the implementation of the long overdue 40% peculiar allowance that will reflect the N70,000 minimum wage. The implementation of the peculiar allowance ought to have started since July 2024 when the implementation of 2024 New National Minimum Wage commenced. “This will equally be domesticated at the sub-national levels (i.e. state and local governments) with effect from November 2026, while the arrears from May 1, 2026, will be paid in three tranches to all public servants in Nigeria. “It is very expedient to state loudly that federal government agreed to set up the Tripartite Negotiation Committee (which will comprise government, labour and NECA representatives) with immediate effect, which formed part of focal requests from the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC, under the national leadership of Benjamin Anto Uyanto, that necessitated the three days warning strike called ab initio by the national leadership of JNPSNC on October 2, 2026.” The council further disclosed that the negotiations addressed several longstanding demands in the health sector, including the adjustment of the Consolidated Health Salary Structure, CONHESS, which health workers have reportedly been demanding for the past 13 years. 13-week timeframe According to the circular, the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, NSIWC, was given three weeks to complete its work and forward the outcome to the Presidential Committee on Salaries, headed by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, for final approval and implementation. It also stated that the meeting approved the payment of 19 months’ arrears of health workers’ allowances in three installments, beginning from December 2026. The circular read: “In the same vein, the meeting was able to resolve the issue affecting the issuance of circular that will facilitate the payment of hazard allowance to agricultural professionals officers in the public service in Nigeria. “The National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission is to issue a circular on the template table that will culminate into its implementation within the next three weeks. “On the tax relief to public servants and private sector operators, the landmark resolution on tax relief was that the matter will be presented to the National Economic Council, NEC, to deliberate on it because it will involve both federal and state governments as well as other critical stakeholders in the Nigeria economic management. ‘’Council also disclosed that the parties agreed to reconvene within one month to assess the level of implementation of the resolutions and ensure that no party reneged on its commitments.’’ It expressed concern over the persistent trust deficit surrounding labour agreements in the country, noting that several previous agreements with trade unions had suffered implementation challenges. On the controversy surrounding TUC’s rejection of the N70,000 transportation allowance, JNPSNC maintained that the congress was not part of the negotiations that produced the agreement. The council, however, acknowledged the TUC’s right to express its position, while challenging it to negotiate a higher amount if it believed workers deserved more than the N70,000 already agreed upon. It further argued that the agreement was reached through consultations involving major labour stakeholders representing public servants, adding that opposition from another labour centre should not derail its implementation. NLC membership The council said: “It is equally expedient to disabuse the notion that the NLC, is a union of junior workers, whereas, all the unions affiliated to Nigeria Labour Congress have members across all the ministries, departments and agencies, MDAs, in the public service up to directorate level. “Even some top-notch public servants are due-paying members of trade unions of their respective choices. “The above clarification became necessary because of the position taken on the matter by the TUC that it rejected the approved N70,000 transportation allowance, of which TUC was never part of the discussion (although has explicit right to express its opinion on any matter the TUC is directly involved in, but not on what it was not part of at any stage of the engagement or negotiation with the Federal Government). “However, it will be highly commended that the Trade Union Congress can get a higher amount above N70,000 already agreed to by the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC; Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC, and Joint Health Sector Unions, JOHESU, which will be an added benefit to Public Servants.” The JNPSNC, established in 1948, serves as a negotiating platform between government and public service trade unions on issues relating to wages, minimum wage implementation, workers’ welfare and industrial disputes. Vanguard News The post N70,000 allowance showdown: Civil servants fire back at TUC appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Vice President urges prison officers to respect inmate dignity and support rehabilitation
body: Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has urged Ghana Prisons Service officers to uphold inmates’ dignity and provide them with opportunities for rehabilitation and successful reintegration into society. She said humane treatment of inmates is a fundamental responsibility of the Service, stressing the need for prison officers to discharge their duties with professionalism, discipline, and respect for human rights. Prof. Opoku-Agyemang assured that the government remained committed to working with the Service to improve staff welfare, strengthen institutional capacity, provide essential equipment, and promote professional development. She was speaking at the graduation parade of 609 officer cadets from Intakes 33, 34 and 35 at the Premier Centre for Prisons and Correctional Innovations at Fumso in the Adansi Asokwa District of the Ashanti Region. The graduating cohort comprised 392 males and 217 females, who were commissioned as Assistant Superintendents of Prisons. The Vice President said the government recognised the importance of improving conditions in the country’s prisons to support effective rehabilitation and ensure that inmates had the opportunity to become productive members of society. She announced the commissioning of the Damongo Camp Prison and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to completing the remand facility at Nsawam. Prof. Opoku-Agyemang called for sustained efforts to improve case management, address overcrowding and develop viable alternatives to custodial sentencing. She appealed to the public to desist from stigmatising former inmates and instead support their reintegration into society after serving their sentences. The Vice President said the government had also provided tractors, fertilisers and other agricultural inputs to support farming activities in the prisons. She explained that the initiative was intended to increase food production within the facilities while equipping inmates with practical agricultural and vocational skills to improve their livelihoods after release. She stressed that accountability and public safety must remain central to prison administration, urging the Service leadership to ensure rehabilitation initiatives are supported by comprehensive staff training. “Promotion is not merely a reward for past achievements, but a solemn commitment to upholding even higher standards of duty,” she said. The Vice President was accompanied by the Minister for the Interior, Alhaji Mohammed Muntaka Mubarak, Mrs Patience Baffoe-Bonnie, Director-General of the Ghana Prisons Service, and other senior officials of the Service.

title: Lubinets announces end of ceasefire in Oleshky
body:
According to Ukrinform, Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets announced this on Telegram .
"This was an important stage of joint humanitarian efforts with Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova, coordinated by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump," he wrote.
The ombudsman stressed that both sides had honored their commitments throughout this period. This made it possible to deliver humanitarian aid to Oleshky and assist civilians who wanted to leave the city safely.
"We are now working with Yana Lantratova to explore ways of continuing similar humanitarian efforts. It is important to preserve this mechanism of cooperation so that we can continue helping people and saving lives," Lubinets said.
As Ukrinform reported, at 03:00 on October 27, Kyiv time, Ukraine introduced a ceasefire in a designated area to allow a humanitarian operation in the temporarily occupied city of Oleshky, Kherson region.

title: APC Campaign defends Tinubu’s power sector performance, says scorecard coming
body:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has addressed President Bola Tinubu’s 2023 campaign promise to end estimated electricity billing, saying the pledge must be assessed alongside the administration’s record in the power sector and the qualification he attached to it ahead of the then 2023 presidential election.
Dele Alake, the Council’s spokesperson, said this in a statement on Sunday, responding to public criticism of the president over the electricity pledge.
Mr Alake argued that some commentaries had reproduced Mr Tinubu’s campaign promise without including the part that he would provide Nigerians with adequate reasons if his administration failed to fulfil the estimated billing commitment before seeking re-election.
At a meeting with members of the Organised Private Sector in Lagos ahead of the 2023 general election, Mr Tinubu had promised to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, particularly estimated billing, which he identified as a burden on households and businesses.
“Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills anymore. A promise made will be a promise kept,” he had said.
He added that Nigerians should not re-elect him if he failed to fulfil the promise, unless he provided adequate reasons for his inability to do so.
Mr Alake said a fair assessment of the pledge should consider the full statement and the administration’s performance since assuming office in May 2023.
He acknowledged that resolving Nigeria’s electricity crisis remained unfinished but maintained that Mr Tinubu had been working to fulfil his commitment.
Defending the administration’s record, Mr Alake listed the Electricity Act 2023, the Presidential Metering Initiative, efforts to settle outstanding debts in the power sector and investments in transmission infrastructure as evidence of progress.
He said Mr Tinubu signed the Electricity Act on 9 June 2023, less than two weeks after assuming office, describing it as a major step towards liberalising the electricity market.
The law allows state governments to establish regulatory frameworks for electricity generation, transmission and distribution within their jurisdictions, rather than leaving the sector entirely under federal control.
According to Mr Alake, Lagos, Enugu, Abia, Ekiti, Oyo, Kaduna and Niger states have taken advantage of the legislation by establishing electricity regulatory agencies and attracting private investment.
He also said the administration inherited more than ₦6 trillion in legacy debts accumulated between 2015 and 2025, adding that the government had introduced measures to address the financial challenges confronting the sector.
Among these is the Presidential Metering Initiative, which was launched to address an estimated metering gap of more than seven million customers.
Mr Alake said more than 1.5 million electricity customers had been metered under the initiative in the last three years.
He added that the administration had introduced a ₦4 trillion bond programme to settle verified outstanding debts owed to 21 electricity generation companies (GenCos) and gas companies (GasCos).
According to him, the first and second tranches of the programme raised more than ₦1.2 trillion to settle part of the verified liabilities.
Mr Alake said the intervention had helped restore confidence in the electricity market and encouraged fresh investments by power generation companies.
He cited Geregu Power Plc’s recent announcement of investments in new power transformers to improve operations at its Geregu 1 Power Plant as an example of the emerging investments in the sector.
The APC spokesperson also defended the administration’s electricity tariff adjustments, arguing that aligning tariffs more closely with the cost of electricity production was necessary to improve the financial viability of distribution companies and the wider electricity market.
He said the government introduced different electricity service bands to improve revenue collection and reduce the financial burden of electricity subvention.
However, he maintained that the administration was exploring ways to balance the need for cost-reflective tariffs with electricity affordability for low-income households.
On infrastructure, Mr Alake said the administration was continuing projects under the Presidential Power Initiative (PPI), which was initiated by late President Muhammadu Buhari.
“President Tinubu inherited many power-sector initiatives, including the Presidential Power Initiative (PPI), which his predecessor, late President Muhammadu Buhari, started,” he said.
He said Mr Tinubu reviewed the existing agreement and signed an acceleration agreement with the German partners in December 2023 to speed up efforts to strengthen the national transmission grid.
According to him, the Federal Executive Council (FEC) approved contracts in December 2024 for the first batch of five Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) substations in major electricity load centres.
He said the projects were being completed and would be commissioned before the end of the administration’s first term.
Mr Alake further disclosed that FEC approved another set of projects in June 2026 involving the construction of eight new substations and the upgrade of four existing ones.
He also listed plans to modernise the Osogbo Grid Control Centre, which he said was built more than 60 years ago, and construct an East-West super grid.
Beyond the grid projects, he said the Rural Electrification Agency had connected universities, hospitals and rural communities to solar power.
Mr Alake argued that investments in the power sector take time, particularly because some equipment needed for major projects has long delivery periods.
He said the administration had not abandoned its commitment to addressing the country’s electricity challenges.
“As he seeks Nigerians’ mandate for a second term in office, he will proudly present his scorecard in the power sector and clearly tell Nigerians what remains to be done,” he said.

title: Highly capitalised stocks push gain to N2trn in October
body: * …as investors reap N4.5trn WoW By Peter Egwuatu The Nigerian stock market strengthened Month-on-Month (MoM), in October 2026, as renewed buying interest in heavyweight stocks lifted the benchmark of the Nigerian Exchange, NGX Index above the 250,000-point psychological threshold. Read Also: Banks raise lending rates for top borrowers despite CBN cuts The rally added N2.01 trillion to market capitalisation, reflecting strong price appreciation in selected large-capitalised stocks across the Industrial Goods, Financial Services and Energy sectors. According to analysts, although the market’s upward movement suggests renewed investor confidence, the uneven distribution of gains points to a selective investment strategy. Investors appear to be concentrating on stocks with significant market influence while maintaining a cautious approach towards other equities. This divergence between index performance and market breadth remains an important consideration in assessing the sustainability of the current rally. Specifically, breakdown of trading in October showed that the NGX market capitalisation closed at N165.114 trillion from 163.104 trillion in September. Similarly, the NGX All Share Index, ASI surged by 1.2% to close at 254,299.49 points from 251,211.67 points in September. Meanwhile on Week-on-Week, WoW the market gained N4.595 trillion as market capitalisation rose from N160.519 trillion the previous week in October to close at N165.114 trillion last week while the NGX ASI rose by 2.9% from 247,222.27 points previous week to close at 254,299.49 points last week. On the global market, the oil prices continued to record performance as the retreat in prices last week reflected a reassessment of geopolitical risks as diplomatic efforts sought to revive peace negotiations. However, analysts noted that the outlook for oil remains sensitive to developments in the region, and renewed escalation could quickly alter market expectations. For Nigeria, movements in crude oil prices have implications for government revenue, foreign exchange supply and broader economic expectations. Higher oil prices can support public revenue and external balances, although their overall effect depends on production levels, domestic fuel costs and other economic conditions. Lower oil prices may ease some cost pressures but could also weaken revenue expectations if the decline is sustained. The effect on listed companies will vary according to their exposure to energy prices, foreign exchange movements, production costs and domestic demand. On market outlook, analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited stated: “Investors should therefore consider international oil movements alongside domestic economic indicators and company-specific developments rather than treating changes in crude prices as a uniform signal for the entire equities market. ‘‘More broadly, expectations regarding interest rates, inflation, corporate earnings and foreign exchange conditions may influence portfolio allocation decisions. ‘‘Where investors anticipate improved corporate profitability and more favourable financing conditions, equities may continue to attract demand. ‘‘Conversely, uncertainty over costs, earnings and valuations could encourage profit-taking in stocks that have recorded substantial price appreciation.” Vanguard News The post Highly capitalised stocks push gain to N2trn in October appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Who will be the next chief justice?
body: MANILA, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. will appoint the country’s next chief justice after Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo retires on Friday, November 6. title: Trump says Iran war will be put away very soon, "one way or the other"
body:
Updated on: November 1, 2026 / 11:15 PM EST / CBS News
President Trump told reporters that he'd spoken with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday and had a "very good talk with him."
Mr. Trump gave no details but said the two had discussed the war in Iran.
There was no public comment on the call from Netanyahu, who some Israelis have worried might be eager to attack Iran again to salvage his political standing after he and his allies lost their majority of seats in parliament after last week's elections.
President Trump said he believes the U.S. will soon put the war with Iran away, "one way or the other."
The president was speaking to Right Side Broadcasting Network before a campaign rally in Iowa on Sunday.
"We've had such a victory, and we'll put it away very soon, one way or the other," Mr. Trump said. "Either they'll make a deal, or we'll just end it. … The job we've done is amazing."
Earlier Sunday, Iran's top diplomat said he hopes there is "rationality" on the U.S. side as diplomatic efforts seek to avert a return to all-out war.
A vessel was struck on Sunday by "an unknown projectile" in the Strait of Hormuz, a British maritime security agency said, after Qatari media reported an earlier attack on a gas tanker.
Britain's UKMTO maritime agency said "the master of a merchant vessel has relayed a mayday call... stating that another vessel has been struck by an unknown projectile" in the strait.
Earlier, Qatar's state news agency said a Qatari gas tanker had been attacked on Friday with "unidentified objects" while transiting Gulf waters. None of the crew members onboard the vessel were injured, and there was no environmental impact from the attack, the report said.
The attack struck a liquefied natural gas carrier, Al Mayeda, which belongs to the Qatar Gas Transport Company, Qatar News Agency said.
Since the Middle East war began in February, Iran has been targeting vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Gulf in an effort to assert control over shipping.
Iran's top diplomat said consultations with mediators are ongoing as diplomatic efforts try to avoid a return to all-out war, and the outcome depends on answers provided by the United States to the "Iranian questions."
In an interview shared on his Telegram channel, Abbas Araghchi said Iran hoped the U.S. would choose "diplomacy over other paths." He said Iran was ready for both defense and diplomacy, depending on Washington's "rationality."
Araghchi on Saturday said Iranian negotiators are in Qatar for talks on a proposal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the U.S. meets several conditions. He said no direct talks are being held with the U.S.
The United Arab Emirates is hoping for a breakthrough in negotiations between Iran and the United States while being prepared for the worst, a senior official said on Sunday.
"We're hoping that there is a diplomatic breakthrough," diplomatic adviser to the Emirati president Anwar Gargash said during a conference in Manama.
"It is not the interest of the region to go through another round... But I think we're also, as we've shown before, braced for the worst."
Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday for talks with Qatari mediators aimed at pushing for a deal to end the war between the U.S. and Iran, according to an official quoted by the Reuters news agency.
It is the third consecutive day of talks aimed at stopping an resumption of strikes after the U.S. midterm elections. President Trump has previously hinted at resuming attacks after the vote on November 3.
Both sides have repeatedly exchanged threats and suggestions they would ramp up hostilities, but have also acknowledged talks are underway.
Iran warned on Sunday that any new war with the United States could last longer than the previous conflict and that President Trump would not be the one to determine its duration.
"A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion," said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television.
A Qatari tanker has been attacked with "unidentified objects" while transiting Gulf waters, the country's state news agency reported Sunday.
The attack on Friday evening struck a liquefied natural gas carrier, Al Mayeda, which belongs to the Qatar Gas Transport Company, Qatar News Agency said.
None of the crew members onboard the vessel struck on Friday were injured and there was no environmental impact from the attack, the report said.
The ship was in a "safe condition" and operational, the Qatari company was cited as saying.
Qatar, a mediator in the war, has stepped up diplomatic efforts in recent days in an attempt to revive negotiations between the United States and Iran.
President Trump said on Saturday that the United States has knocked out much of Iran's military but still has to "take care of" one or two targets, as Tehran warned of reprisals if attacked.
Mr. Trump maintained that negotiations with Iran to end the war, which was started by the U.S. and Israel in February, were "going fine but you know they're not very reliable."
The president said the U.S. is not in a hurry to take offensive action because it had already decimated Iran's military and nuclear program.
"We've knocked out their nuclear. We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes," Mr. Trump told reporters at his Florida residence.
"You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex.
The Iranian government denied any nuclear work is carried out there.
Earlier Saturday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Mr. Trump has not made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran and that the U.S. would be open to a diplomatic solution.
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that a new proposal has been reached with mediators that would shorten the time to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz to two days. He said that Iranian diplomats were in Qatar for discussions.
Araghchi last month proposed reopening the waterway within a week if the U.S. agreed to lift its blockade of Iranian ports, release frozen Iranian assets and waive sanctions on Iranian oil sales, among other conditions. That was rejected.
In an interview with Qatar-based broadcaster Al Jazeera, Araghchi said that Iran isn't planning to meet with U.S. officials, but called recent U.S. efforts toward "broader dialogue" a positive step.
Araghchi said a decision on whether negotiations will be direct or indirect would be made "once Washington agrees to Iran's conditions."
The U.S. blockade on the Strait of Hormuz has now redirected 144 vessels, according to U.S. Central Command .
The U.S. had not provided an update on how many ships it had prevented from entering or exiting Iranian ports since exactly two weeks ago when it said it had redirected 138 vessels.
Earlier Saturday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had posted on X that the U.S. has taken out 1.5 billion barrels of oil without providing a timeframe.
Bessent posted that "transit levels are back to pre-conflict levels minus Iranian barrels." The U.S. has been guiding oil tankers out of the Persian Gulf under military escort over the past several months to do ship-to-ship oil transfers in the Gulf of Oman.
However, it's an expensive process and an open-ended mission at this point.
The powerful leader of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, who Vice President JD Vance engaged with a peace proposal last weekend, said on Saturday the country has not made any changes to its nuclear doctrine — but renewed strike might change that.
"No new decision has been made regarding changes to the nuclear doctrine," Secretary Mohsen Rezaei told official news outlet IRNA. "Of course, the discussion is raised that if war breaks out again, do we want to have the previous doctrine or not, but no new official and governmental decision has been made yet."
Iran has said many times the country was never attempting to enrich uranium to weapons grade, a claim largely disputed by the U.S. and Israel. President Trump has repeatedly made it known the main objective of the war in Iran is to prevent the country from ever acquiring a nuclear weapon.
Iran's nuclear sites have been hit repeatedly, both last summer in U.S. and Israeli strikes and in the renewed fighting this year, and it's unclear what capabilities remain.
Rezaei also told IRNA he has not yet responded to Vance's letter outlining some of the U.S. positions for peace talks.
Iran has claimed another ship transiting the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz hit a mine and is on fire, according to semi-official Fars News Agency.
"This afternoon, a violating oil tanker that, disregarding warnings, was transiting in the prohibited and unsafe area in the east of the Strait of Hormuz, caught fire after striking sea mines," the country's navy said, according to Fars News Agency.
The news could not immediately be verified.
Iran has claimed nearly 10 ships have hit mines while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, specifically along the Omani coastline. That shipping lane is favored by the U.S. and is considered prohibited by Iran. Of the 81 attacks on ships in the strait since July 6, 59 of them have been on the southern route, according to the U.K. Marine Trade Operations Centre.
President Trump has not made a decision about new strikes on Iran amid stalled peace talks, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday.
"We can achieve military objectives if we seek to. He hasn't made a decision. I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly," Rubio said at a G20 press conference in Atlanta.
"If we needed to do something militarily, we would have the ability to do it and we have everything we need to be successful," Rubio added. "But we would prefer to do it peacefully."
He also would not characterize whether progress has been made in the last few days and said there is no timeframe on talks between the U.S. and Iran through its mediators.
Rubio continued to echo many of the things Mr. Trump has said in recent weeks and months. The United States' main objective is to prevent Iran from getting a nuclear weapon, and Rubio emphasized the threat to the rest of the world if they do.
"The Iranian regime is basically arguing is, 'Unless we get what we want, not only will we blow up ships, but we will destroy the energy infrastructure of our neighbors and the entire region.' Just think about that," Rubio said. "Because I think that we skip over that like that's some sort of normal behavior. That's not normal behavior, but we are there to help protect against it."
Iran's strikes on more than two dozen U.S. bases in the Middle East focused on early warning systems before hitting aircraft and buildings, causing billions of dollars in equipment damage, according to an Associated Press analysis .
The AP independently verified damage to American targets using satellite imagery from multiple providers and spoke to four regional officials who were briefed or have firsthand knowledge of what was hit. The AP found that, through August, more than 115 drone or missile strikes claimed by Iran or Iranian-backed militias damaged or destroyed structures on 26 military bases and other sites with U.S. equipment.
The AP found that Iran initially focused its attacks on aircraft hangars and systems that detect incoming strikes, clearing the way for further strikes on warehouses, troop housing and more.
The damage has significantly reshaped the American foothold in the Middle East, with two regional officials saying the U.S. has moved many of its assets out of the Persian Gulf. That includes aircraft, air defense systems, communications systems and other equipment crucial to base operations, one of those officials said.
Most of the Iranian attacks have been in Kuwait, while U.S. sites in Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates also have been targeted, the analysis of satellite imagery shows.
Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait was struck at least 30 times, damaging or destroying at least 15 aircraft hangars, numerous warehouses and 10 buildings near a residential area.
Camp Buehring, also in Kuwait, faced even heavier losses. While Iranian attacks made most of its hangars inoperable, gathering places for troops sustained much more damage because the base had limited aircraft. Its gym was destroyed in March and a store for troops to buy products on the base was hit in late July.
Iran's top diplomat on Saturday said there were no plans to hold talks with the United States despite growing concerns over a return to war.
"Currently, there are no plans for meetings with American officials, and any speculation to the contrary is merely media assumption," Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in an interview with Al Jazeera, according to the state news agency IRNA.
"We see no need to meet with the Americans at present, our conditions are clear, and the mediators continue their consultations regarding them," Araghchi told Al Jazeera.
Qatari and Pakistani mediators met in Doha, Qatar, on Saturday, where an Iranian delegation was present. Iranian officials, through the Qatari mediators, received an outline for a peace deal from the U.S. last weekend, spearheaded by Vice President JD Vance.
"The American side's attempt to open the door to broader dialogue and understanding is considered a positive step, and if Washington's goal from Vance's message is to stir up differences, it will be a new mistake added to its previous errors," Araghchi told Al Jazeera on Saturday.
Saudi Arabia's vice minister of foreign affairs said on Saturday the message from the region is that it wants a return to peace. Speaking at a security forum in Bahrain, Waleed ElKhereiji told the audience that efforts were being made to prevent a military escalation and reach an agreement to end the crisis with Iran.
"If you look at … the efforts that everybody is trying to do, the message is very clear. People in this part of the world want to bring peace back to the region," he said. But he said no one can predict the outcome of the efforts.
Concerns are rising about a return to all-out war, especially after Tuesday's midterm elections in the U.S. President Trump has opined during recent rallies that he could quickly bring the war to an end through military action.
Speaking at the same event, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said an escalation in the region would be extremely destructive.
"We are very confident that … the second round will be more dangerous, more destructive, and it will lead to nowhere," he said.
Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, on Saturday warned the United States against launching fresh attacks, amid weeks of heightened tensions and repeated threats.
"If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them," said a statement attributed to Khamenei posted on his Telegram channel.
The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting between them.
Khamenei has not been seen publicly since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's killing in U.S.-Israeli strikes at the start of the war in February.
According to the statement, Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that "any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response."
Saudi air defences intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region on Saturday, according to the spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis.
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone in the Riyadh region," Turki al-Malki wrote on X, adding that "debris from the interception fell without causing injuries." Malki did not say who launched the drone.
In recent weeks, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including by launching deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and the cancellation of flagship events.
On Friday, Malki said the Houthis had targeted the Medina region, home to Islam's second holiest city, but the group later denied the claim.
The Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure, airports and ships come after hostilities resumed in Yemen over the summer between the Houthis and the country's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Riyadh.
More than 1,600 people have been killed and over 275,000 displaced since the fighting reignited, according to United Nations figures.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Friday that a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of oil struck a naval mine and caught fire while using an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported. The Guard said it was the fourth oil tanker to suffer an explosion Friday after attempting to use unauthorized routes through the strait.
Iran has repeatedly warned vessels against passing through the strait without Tehran's permission. It has claimed responsibility for attacks on ships and said last month that vessels attempting to pass through the strait without authorization would face "destruction." Tehran has asserted control over much of the waterway since the U.S. and Israel launched the war on Feb. 28.
Earlier on Friday, the Guard's navy said three other tankers caught fire after striking mines in the strait, Iranian state TV reported. It claimed the vessels had switched off their navigation and positioning systems and ignored repeated radio warnings. Iran's report did not identify the vessels or provide details about the crews. The Associated Press could not verify those claims.
Meanwhile, Oman said it had evacuated 25 crew members from a Panama-flagged tanker that was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, 1.6 nautical miles off the coast of Musandam Governorate, catching fire. It is unclear whether that incident is related to the fires described by Iran.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center also reported Friday that a vessel was struck by an "unknown projectile" south of Lavan, an island just off mainland Iran near Shidvar. The organization, part of the British military that monitors maritime safety, said the crew was safe.
Yemen's Houthis targeted the presidential palace in Aden on Friday with two missiles, a police official told AFP, hours after Saudi forces said they had intercepted an attack by the group on the Gulf kingdom.
Aden, the seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed and internationally recognized government, has been targeted repeatedly since Yemen's dormant civil war reignited in July.
Two eyewitnesses told AFP they saw ambulances entering the palace in Aden, a large compound made up of several buildings including facilities used by government and Saudi-led coalition forces, after the incident.
Shortly before, residents and an AFP journalist said they heard two blasts in the city.
The Houthis, who control the capital Sanaa to the north, most recently struck the perimeter of Aden's airport on Wednesday after saying they had targeted a naval base and a military camp last week.
There were more strikes reported in and around the Strait of Hormuz than any other month during the Iran-U.S. war, according to the U.K. Marine Trade Operations Centre , which is supported by the Royal Navy.
There were just over 30 attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Oman or Persian Gulf reported in October, with only March, the first month of the war, reporting even 30 attacks, according to the UKMTO. There were twice as many attacks in October as there were in September. While there were likely more attacks in the month, the UKMTO only counts attacks reported by verified vessels in the region.
The war also crossed the eight-month mark this week as it started on Feb. 28. Since the war started, there have been 145 reported incidents, the UKMTO said. While the UKMTO does not track who fired the projectiles that hit vessels, the vast majority of strikes came via Iran. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps often claims responsibility for the attacks.
Iran has started to claim a large number of ships hitting mines in the region as well, though they largely do not appear on the list of incidents from the UKMTO.
Since July 6, 59 of the 81 projectile strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz region came along the southern route, the UKMTO said. The U.S. has championed the southern route, and used it to escort oil tankers out of the Persian Gulf, while Iran calls the route illegal and says ships need to travel north, along the Iranian coast.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio opened talks Friday with G20 counterparts including Russia's Sergei Lavrov, in meetings set to be fractious as wars in Ukraine and Iran, alongside surging energy costs, fan discord.
The foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta takes place just days before crucial midterm elections, setting the stage for a December G20 leaders' summit in Miami at President Trump's Doral resort.
But ongoing conflicts have deepened rifts even as the United States seeks to focus on economic growth, trade imbalances and supply chain challenges in areas like energy and critical minerals.
Rubio warned at an opening plenary session that the world faces "interconnected economic and geopolitical crises, many of which pose severe threats" to the global economy.
He urged the G20 to work together against threats including strains to global energy and food supply chains, and on freedom of navigation.
Still, few breakthroughs are expected this week from the Group of 20 economies — which include China, India, Russia, Japan, Germany and France — as officials face divisions over Moscow's war on Ukraine and fallout from the conflict with Iran.
Global energy prices have rocketed since U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran from late February triggered Tehran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
"This is the last test case the G20 has, at least under the US G20 presidency, until Miami," Alisha Chhangani of the Atlantic Council told AFP. Its outcomes will affect how the December summit shapes up.
No new oil leakage has been detected from the tanker GEM NO. 2 following an oil spill from the vessel in the United Arab Emirates' territorial waters, as cleanup operations continue along the UAE coastline, the Persian Gulf nation's official WAM news agency reported.
WAM quoted the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure as saying Friday that technical teams had repaired damaged parts of the vessel, restored some operating systems and assessed the ship's structural integrity. Authorities said the source of the spill had been stopped.
According to the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, the oil slick is concentrated off Umm Al-Quwain, extending toward coastal areas of Ras Al Khaimah, Ajman and Sharjah.
Pollution levels have declined, while monitoring and cleanup operations continue.
The British maritime security agency UKMTO reported on Oct. 9 that a vessel had been hit by a projectile off the UAE coast, causing a fire that was later brought under control. It did not assign blame, but Iran has repeatedly targeted commercial ships in and around the southern Strait of Hormuz, which includes the UAE coastline.
The Saudis intercepted a drone near the capital of Riyadh on Friday afternoon as well as a ballistic missile in southern Saudi Arabia, according to the country's Coalition Joint Forces Command.
The coalition said both were fired by the Houthis. It's unclear exactly where the missile was intercepted in southern Saudi Arabia.
The Houthis have regularly targeted locations in Saudi Arabia, everywhere from just over the border from Yemen to hundreds of miles into the interior, including Riyadh. Airports have been a consistent target of Houthi attacks.
The Saudi coalition had earlier announced it intercepted a drone near the holy city of Mecca, which the Houthis denied was fired by their forces.
A Lebanese military court on Friday charged 13 people for their alleged involvement in shipping explosives to Hezbollah, a judicial source told the AFP news agency, after authorities seized the roughly 1,100-pound cargo earlier this month.
The charges come as pressure mounts on Hezbollah, long a major political and paramilitary force in Lebanon that the U.S. and Israel consider an Iran-backed terrorist organization. The group has been weakened by back-to-back wars with Israel and is now facing a concerted push from authorities in Beirut, with backing from the Trump administration, to disarm its military wing.
Only two of the 13 people charged over the explosives shipment have been detained, and only eight have been identified, with the remaining five known only by noms de guerre.
Proceedings have been opened "against 12 members of Hezbollah, and one of their spouses," a judicial official told AFP. They were charged with "violating government decisions, possession of arms and explosives, and criminal conspiracy to undermine the authority of the state," the source said.
In a rare admission, Hezbollah acknowledged ownership of the vehicle and its cargo, and even demanded the shipment be returned.
Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam has vowed that authorities "will deal with weapons outside the legal framework with the required firmness."
In June, Lebanon and Israel signed a framework peace agreement that included the disarmament of Hezbollah and a gradual Israeli withdrawal from occupied territory in southern Lebanon, with the Lebanese army stepping in to secure the area.
So far, Hezbollah has flatly refused to disarm or acknowledge the ceasefire , and very little of what Israel calls its occupied "security zone" in southern Lebanon has been handed over to Lebanese forces.
Oman's navy has evacuated 25 crew members from a Panama-flagged commercial vessel after it was targeted and a fire broke out on board, the Omani Maritime Security Center said in a statement Friday.
The evacuation was carried out in coordination with the Maritime Security Center approximately 1.6 nautical miles off the coast of Musandam Governorate, the northern tip of Oman that juts out into the center of the Strait of Hormuz.
Crew members were "provided with the necessary medical care," the navy said in a statement.
Earlier Friday, Iran's navy and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said two ships were on fire after striking sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz after attempting to use shipping lanes close to Oman's coast that the U.S. military insists are safe and open, but Tehran considers illegal.
Major U.S. oil and gas giant ExxonMobil reported Friday that its third-quarter profits had more than doubled to $15.4 billion, as it benefited from higher oil prices and refining margins due to the U.S.-Iran war.
Profits in the period were slightly more than double the $7.5 billion in the year-ago period.
Oil prices have been high since the start of the war. As of Friday, the two main benchmark products, Brent crude and U.S. West Texas Intermediate, remained up about 70% compared to a year ago.
The Iranian navy said Friday that an enemy drone was "struck and destroyed" east of the Strait of Hormuz.
In a statement, the navy also said two oil tankers "were damaged and caught fire after striking naval mines," accusing the vessels of ignoring warnings and navigating in prohibited and unsafe waters with their tracking systems switched off.
It was not immediately clear if the two vessels referred to by the Iranian navy were the same tankers that Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps reported earlier Friday to have hit mines in the strait.
President ⁠Donald Trump said Friday that the war with Iran is "going to get wrapped up soon."
Speaking to Kansas ‌City radio station KCMO ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, the president said "it's going to get wrapped ⁠up soon," without specifying how.
"We need a guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon," he added.
The commander of the U.S. military's Central Command, Adm. Brad Cooper, reiterated his longstanding assertions on Friday that Iran's navy is "at the bottom of the sea" and that southern commercial shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz are clear of Iranian mines and safe to navigate.
In a video posted on social media , Cooper said the U.S. had helped Gulf partners export more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude oil since the summer, while the U.S. naval blockade had prevented Iran from exporting any oil through the strait.
Cooper said he had recently flown over the strait and seen U.S. military "assets in the air and on the water."
"What I didn't see," said Cooper, was Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps "out there at all. They patrolled the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waters for decades, harassing and threatening and seizing commercial vessels at will, but they were not out there because Iran's navy is all at the bottom of the sea."
Cooper renewed the claim made by President Trump and the Pentagon since late August that "we also successfully cleared the strait's internationally recognized primary transit routes of Iranian sea mines. And today, U.S. forces remain highly vigilant and present to ensure that all primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear."
His comments came a day after Iran's navy claimed four vessels had struck sea mines and been disabled as the attempted to transit the strait via the U.S.-backed southern route. The U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center said Thursday evening, meanwhile, that a tanker was struck by a projectile in the strait.
It was unclear if the ship reported by UKMTO to have been hit was one of the four Iran said had hit mines.
A source familiar with the ongoing diplomacy confirmed to CBS News that Qatari mediators were in Tehran on Friday to convey the latest edits to a draft proposal to end the U.S. war with Iran.
The source said there were indications of progress being made.
A draft was presented by Qatari mediators last Sunday, and a response from Iran is expected by the weekend. The aim of the proposal is to avert a return to U.S. military action against Iran, which President Trump has threatened multiple times in recent weeks.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Friday that two oil tankers had been halted after unspecified "incidents" as they attempted to transit what Tehran considers an unauthorized route through the Strait of Hormuz.
"Two offending oil tankers, one in the eastern part and the other in the western part of the Strait of Hormuz, which were attempting to pass through the unauthorized route, encountered incidents and were brought to a halt in the waters south of the strait," the IRGC said in a statement.
Iran has repeatedly warned shippers that using the southern route through the waterway, which has been promoted by the U.S., puts them at risk as the regime deems it an illegal passage.
The tankers had "switched off all their navigation and positioning systems and, with the support of the terrorist U.S. military, were attempting to exit through the unauthorized route," the IRGC statement said.
The IRGC did not specify the nature of the incidents, which came a day after Iran's armed forces said at least four tankers had been forced to stop in the area after hitting sea mines.
The U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center said Thursday evening that a tanker was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. It was unclear if the ship reported by UKMTO to have been hit was one of the four Iran said had hit mines, but the timing of the report suggested it could have been a separate incident.
Qatari officials returned to Iran on Friday to push for a peace deal between Tehran and Washington, Iran's state-run IRNA news agency , along with Reuters and AFP, reported.
The talks have been coordinated with the U.S., an official told Reuters.
The delegation is led by a senior adviser to Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister and is scheduled to meet with senior Iranian officials, IRNA said, adding that the discussions would focus on bilateral relations between Iran and Qatar, as well as developments in the region.
An official briefed on the latest diplomacy confirmed to CBS News Wednesday that Qatari mediators had presented Iran with a new draft deal to end the war. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Qatar had only come with "unacceptable" ideas , and that Tehran would not change its stance on the nuclear issue, something Washington wants included in negotiations from the start.
Tehran wants the U.S. to first lift its blockade of Iranian ports and to drop sanctions limiting the country's gas and oil sales.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday in a post on X that Tehran "continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed" and is working with mediators to review ideas that Tehran included in a proposal floated last month, which was summarily rejected by President Trump but which Iran still wants to see used as the basis for a new ceasefire agreement.
On Thursday, Mr. Trump said a letter from Vice President JD Vance to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei — which was reported by multiple outlets as an attempt to restart peace negotiations — was an outreach intended only to help get medical supplies into Iran.
Iran has yet to reply to the letter, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency.
The U.S. Department of Defense has added two more service member deaths to its official account of casualties since the war with Iran started more than eight months ago, bringing the overall death toll to 23.
Both of the newly noted deaths on the Defense Casualty Analysis System portal were noncombat related. In total the DCAS portal says 11 service members have been killed by enemy fire during the war, and 12 others have died under circumstances deemed nonhostile, which includes accidents and sickness.
Both of the service members recently added as nonhostile deaths were airmen, including one who died of an illness and another from unspecified causes that remain under investigation, The Washington Post quoted the Air Force as saying.
The two deaths added to the DCAS system are listed under Overseas Operations , which includes deaths recorded by the Pentagon after it stopped using the name Operation Epic Fury for the offensive against Iran in May, after Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared the operation over.
The Saudi-led coalition said Friday that it had intercepted and destroyed a drone in the Mecca region fired by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels.
"A drone launched by the terrorist Houthi militia has been intercepted and destroyed in the Mecca region," the coalition wrote in a post on X.
The Houthis denied any attempt to strike Saudi Arabia on Friday, the Reuters news agency reported.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said on social media that the group hadn't conducted any operations aimed at Saudi territory, adding that the Houthis only target Saudi oil facilities and military bases.
A tanker was struck Thursday evening by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, the U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center reported, after Iran's navy claimed four ships had struck sea mines in the area.
UKMTO said the ship hit by a projectile was exiting the strait along the southern route, which the U.S. has encouraged international shipping companies to use, when it came under fire.
"There are no reported injuries to the crew or environmental impact … at this time," UKMTO said.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and its military claimed in two separate announcements earlier Thursday that four tankers had struck sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz, causing fires.
It was unclear if the ship reported by UKMTO to have been struck by a projectile was one of the four Iran said had hit mines, but the timing of the report from the maritime monitor suggested it could have been a separate incident.
Iran has not yet responded to a letter sent by Vice President JD Vance to the secretary of the Iranian Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, according to the semi-official Tasnim News agency, which is closely affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
Tasnim said in a Thursday post on its official Telegram social media account that Tehran was not prepared to drop any of its core conditions for a ceasefire, which include lifting the American blockade of Iran's ports, easing sanctions and giving Iran access to its frozen financial assets held abroad, among other things.
Multiple news outlets have reported that Vance's letter to Rezaei was an attempt to restart peace negotiations, but President Trump said Wednesday that it was a focused outreach intended only to help get medical supplies into Iran.

title: Netanyahu urges Trump to attack Iran as US pursues further negotiations before midterms - report
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke with US President Donald Trump on Saturday about US negotiations with Iran and pressed Trump to strike Iran immediately after the midterm elections, Axios reported on Sunday night, citing one Israeli and one US source. The sources said that Trump is currently looking to let negotiations play out while Netanyahu wants to return to combat. Trump confirmed that he had spoken to Netanyahu while speaking to reporters on Sunday, and that they had discussed Iran but declined to share any further details. "We had a very good conversation,” Trump said. Trump told reporters that negotiations with Iran were "going fine" on Saturday, days after Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iran's national security chief Mohsen Rezaei about negotiations.US increases presence in Middle EastHowever, The Jerusalem Post has learned that some of Trump's team is shifting back towards attacking Iran after other methods have been tried to obtain Iranian concessions. The US has also increased its military presence in the region, sending more than 10 military transport aircraft to Israel over the past week. Reports have also emerged of US air defense systems and interceptors being moved to Israel and to other Arab allies. Yonah Jeremy Bob contributed to this report.

title: Abu Dhabi Golf Championship: Rory McIlroy returns and all you need to know
body: Abu Dhabi hosts the penultimate stage of the DP World Tour this week. The Race to Dubai features a three-way tie to be crowned champion, with Rory McIlroy still very much in the hunt. When is it? The Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship takes place from November 5-8. Where is it? The tournament will be held at Yas Links, located on the western shores of Yas Island. The Kyle Phillips-designed course is an 18-hole, par-72 links course ranked among Golf Digest's world top 100. Who is playing? This year's tournament features a star-studded line-up headlined by McIlroy , Race to Dubai leader Eugenio Chacarra, and 2018 Masters champion Patrick Reed. The field also includes defending champion Aaron Rai and former Abu Dhabi winners Tommy Fleetwood and Tyrrell Hatton. The top 70 available players in the Race to Dubai rankings will participate, although there are some notable absences from this year's field, including Shane Lowry, Justin Rose and Matt Fitzpatrick. That field is then cut to 50 for the season-ending DP World Tour Championship at Jumeirah Golf Estates from November 12 to 15. Who is in the hunt for the Race to Dubai? McIlroy is currently third in the Race to Dubai standings on 3,144.9 points. The Northern Irishman trails leader Chacarra (4,143.9) and Reed (3,474.6). 🚨 RACE TO DUBAI RANKINGS UPDATE 🚨 pic.twitter.com/yoa67mScHm — DP World Tour (@DPWorldTour) October 26, 2026 What does McIlroy need to do? McIlroy is attempting to win the race for the fifth year in a row. The 37-year-old is vying for a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai crown to draw level with Colin Montgomerie. There are 1,500 points available for the winner in Abu Dhabi and 2,000 for the winner in Dubai. Chacarra heads into the DP World Tour Play-Offs with a 669-point advantage over Reed and a 999-point cushion over McIlroy, but with 3,500 points still available across the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship and DP World Tour Championship, the Race to Dubai remains wide open. McIlroy has finished runner-up four times in Abu Dhabi. If he wins at Yas Links, and Chacarra finishes third or lower, the Northern Irishman will effectively wipe out the Spaniard's lead, making the DP World Tour Championship a straight shoot-out. Reed can move ahead of Chacarra if he wins and the Spaniard finishes third or lower. He is attempting to become only the second American winner of the Race to Dubai crown after Collin Morikawa in 2021. Victory in Abu Dhabi would put Chacarra in a commanding position, but would not be enough to secure the Race to Dubai title, with 2,000 points still available at the season-ending DP World Tour Championship in Dubai. Prize money The winner at Yas Links will receive a cheque of $1.53 million from a total prize fund of $9m. Tickets General admission is free for the first two days (Thursday and Friday). Paid general admission or weekend tickets apply for Saturday and Sunday, starting at Dh75 each. Children under 18 can go free. Tickets for Bar on Nine start from Dh180. How to watch on TV You can watch all the action live on beIN Sports.

title: Arakas Latheros Turns Frozen Peas Into a Hearty Greek Dinner
body: Arakas latheros turns a bag of frozen peas into a hearty Greek dinner, simmered with tomato, potato, dill and olive oil. Photo: Allrecipes What is arakas latheros? In Greek, arakas means peas, and latheros comes from ladi, the word for oil. So arakas latheros simply translates as “oiled peas”, a plain name for a plain, honest dish. Arakas latheros belongs to the lathera, a family of vegetable stews that rely on olive oil rather than meat. According to Wikipedia’s entry on ladera , these dishes usually come with feta and bread, and they are a common fasting food. Peas are often a side dish elsewhere. In Greece, however, a full plate of vegetables is a normal main course, and these oiled peas make a satisfying one. Our green bean and potato stew follows the same idea, so the two make a natural pair for meat-free weeknights. Ingredients for four serves This version comes from Diana Moutsopoulos, who shared it on Allrecipes. It holds 4.7 out of 5 from 17 ratings, and 13 of those ratings are five stars. In her cook’s note, she explains that she uses far less olive oil than the traditional dish. Instead, she adds more tomato to make up for it. For the peas with tomato, you need: 45 ml (3 US tablespoons) olive oil 6 spring onions, chopped 1 potato, peeled and cut into wedges 450 g (a 16-ounce bag) frozen peas 1 US cup (about 240 ml) crushed tomatoes ½ US cup chopped fresh dill , the herb that lifts oiled peas salt and ground black pepper, to taste 120 ml (½ US cup) water, only if needed A US tablespoon holds 15 ml, while an Australian one holds 20 ml, so measure the oil in millilitres. Any standard 500 g bag of frozen peas also works well. Each serve has about 245 calories, 9 g of protein and 8 g of fibre, according to Allrecipes. How to cook the peas with tomato Arakas latheros takes about 10 minutes to prepare and 40 minutes on the stove. As a result, it is ready in under an hour. First, warm the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Then add the spring onions and stir them for about 5 minutes, until soft but not brown. Next, tip in the peas, tomatoes, potato and dill, and season with salt and pepper. Add a splash of water only if the tomatoes look too dry. Stir well and bring the peas with tomato to the boil. After that, lower the heat, partly cover the pan and simmer for about 30 minutes. Finally, check that the peas and potato are soft and the extra liquid has cooked away. The finished arakas latheros should be thick and glossy, not soupy. If the potato is still firm, simply give the oiled peas a few more minutes. Tips from home cooks In the most helpful review, PKchef made her arakas latheros without tomatoes because of an allergy, using water instead. She still rated it five stars, and she called feta and crusty bread perfect additions. Sara Fogdall Miller found that she did not need the extra water, because the frozen peas and tomatoes gave off plenty. She swapped in a yellow onion and two small unpeeled potatoes, and she found the dish was not overly oily. Beth, by comparison, added paprika to the onions before following the arakas latheros method exactly. She warned that her potato took much longer than 30 minutes, so cut the wedges small if you are short on time. A few cooks wanted more punch. John Hollwedel had no dill, so he cooked garlic with the onion until fragrant. Similarly, one reviewer browned the potatoes with the onions first. TeaLover767 halved the recipe and used canned peas and dried dill. Even so, she said the oiled peas were good enough to make again. Elizabeth Currier summed up the appeal of arakas latheros: “Surprisingly simple with few ingredients, but it’s a winner!” What to serve with Greek peas Serve arakas latheros warm, with a block of feta cheese and crusty bread for the sauce. Carol Manzo did exactly that and wrote: “So, so easy.” For a bigger spread, add our garlic dip recipe and a plate of olives. Ladera are often eaten warm or at room temperature, too, so the peas with tomato suit a relaxed table. If you like pulses and vegetables cooked this way, try the one-pan potato stew or read why lentils and beans stay so central to Greek kitchens. The full arakas latheros recipe, with photos from home cooks, is on the original Allrecipes page .
