title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after record crypto hack
body: Binance customers withdrew a net $3.64bn (£2.72bn) of assets from the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange as it reopened on Sunday following a record hack last week . The firm suspended all transactions after the incident, which affected $6.3bn in digital assets. Major organisations, including the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have accused North Korea of being responsible for the cyber attack , which is said to be the largest hack in history. The company said it has covered around 95% of the stolen assets, but the remaining amount may take longer to source. Binance has repeatedly said it would cover all of the losses linked to the attack. “Between 06:00 and 15:30 [GMT] on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion,” Binance posted on X. There was an “initial spike” in withdrawals, which later declined and “are stabilising as expected”, it added. It also said withdrawals for more than two dozen major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, have resumed, and that more services will resume in phases once security checks are complete. The attack on Binance has been attributed to TraderTraitor, a North Korean cybercrime group also known as the Lazarus Group, which stole a then-record $1.5bn from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025 . The FBI on Saturday published a list of cryptocurrency wallet addresses linked to the group and urged industry partners to help by blocking transactions involving them. The hack hit Binance’s global centralised exchange, Binance.com, while its US-facing platform said it was not affected. The exchange scrambled to urge cryptocurrency issuers to freeze affected assets. Binance said last week that early checks suggest the incident may have started with a compromised engineer’s laptop, allowing hackers to make unauthorised transactions. The withdrawn crypto represents only a fraction of the total value of assets Binance holds. Binance’s exact valuation is unclear because the firm is privately held, though the company said in 2024 that it had more than $160bn in assets in its custody. The firm said last week it has reserved more than $6.34bn to deal with ​the attack’s fallout. Binance said it replaced customers’ assets through a combination of channels, including its corporate treasury and its futures insurance and emergency reserve funds. “Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the firm said. Cryptocurrencies are digital assets traded on exchanges such as Binance. Unlike cash, they have no physical form and are managed on computers, smartphones, and other digital devices. Binance was founded in China and has hundreds of millions of registered users globally.

title: Tinubu to Nigerian Delegation to Makkah: Our Diversity, A Recipe for Prosperity
body: Deji Elumoye in Abuja President Bola Ahmed Tinubu prayed Almighty Allah to transform Nigeria’s rich diversity into a source of prosperity, unity, peace and sustainable development for the benefit of all Nigerians. Tinubu offered the prayer on Sunday in the holy city of Makkah, Saudi Arabia, while hosting members of his delegation for dinner. The president expressed the hope that Nigeria’s ethnic, religious, and cultural diversity would continue to serve as a source of strength and national advancement rather than division. He stressed the need for citizens to embrace mutual understanding, peaceful coexistence, and a shared commitment to the country’s progress. He prayed that Almighty Allah would bless Nigeria with enduring peace, harmony, and prosperity, and grant the nation’s leaders the wisdom, courage, and foresight to steer the country towards greater development and improved living conditions for its people. “May Almighty Allah bless Nigeria, convert our diversity into prosperity as a country,” the president said. Tinubu also prayed for divine guidance and protection for Nigerians at home and abroad, asking Allah to strengthen the bonds of brotherhood among citizens and inspire a renewed spirit of patriotism, compassion and service to the nation. The president stated that Nigeria’s abundant human and natural resources, coupled with the talents, creativity and enterprise of its diverse population, provided a strong foundation for building a prosperous and inclusive nation. The dinner with members of his delegation in Makkah provided an opportunity for fellowship and reflection on Nigerians’ shared aspirations for a peaceful, united and prosperous country. Tinubu urged Nigerians of all faiths and backgrounds to keep working together in the national interest, expressing confidence that, with faith in Almighty Allah, unity of purpose, and collective determination, Nigeria would overcome its challenges and realise its full potential. Chairman of BUA, Alhaji Abdulsamad Rabiu, reaffirmed Tinubu’s commitment to peace, unity and prosperity of Nigeria. Rabiu said, “Today is actually the third dinner we’re having with His Excellency, Mr President, since we came to Makkah on Thursday night or Friday morning when Mr President arrived. “So, we discussed, and the discussion was, you know, to always continue to pray for Nigeria, for peace, for unity and for Nigeria’s prosperity. To again, you know, thank His Excellency for his passion, for what he’s doing for Nigeria. “And also for us, it’s quite important because, as I said, it has given us the opportunity to come and pray not only for ourselves and our families, but also for Nigeria. “We will continue to support His Excellency in whatever capacity we can and, definitely, as you all know, Mr President is very passionate about the country. He’s working very hard, and we’ll continue to support him.” Kwara State Governor and Chairman of Nigerian Governors’ Forum (NGF), Abdulrahman AbdulRazaq, said the forum was overwhelmed by the president’s passion and commitment to achieving a united and prosperous nation. AbdulRazaq stated, “Only Allah can reward you; we will continue to pray for you daily and pray for Nigeria that you lead. May Allah continue to strengthen you in making the right decisions, strengthen your wisdom, your boldness, your audacity, your courage. May Allah lead you to the right path.” Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Mr Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), also prayed for Almighty Allah to continue to strengthen the president in his determination to deliver governance and justice to all Nigerians, irrespective of their religion or ethnic backgrounds. The dinner was attended by Yobe State Governor Mai Mala Buni; Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani; Jigawa State Governor Mohammed Namadi; Sokoto State Governor Ahmed Aliyu; Borno State Governor Babagana Umara Zulum; Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Mohammed Ali Pate; and National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu. Others were Chief Executive Officer of Oando Plc, Mr Wale Tinubu; Special Adviser to the President on Political Matters, Ibrahim Kabiru Masari; and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, among others.

title: Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized following stroke
body: Washington â Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy of Connecticut was hospitalized on Saturday after experiencing a stroke, his office said. "Yesterday afternoon, Senator Murphy started experiencing numbness in his arm while at his son's hockey game. He was taken to a local hospital, where it was discovered he had experienced a stroke," Murphy's chief of staff Allison Herwitt said in a statement on Sunday. Herwitt said Murphy was transferred to Johns Hopkins "for further monitoring and is responding well to treatment." "The doctors are encouraged by his progress, he is awake and alert, and we are optimistic he will make a full recovery," she added. Murphy, 53, has represented Connecticut in the Senate since 2013, after serving three terms in the House. The Connecticut Democrat has been viewed as a possible 2028 White House contender, and has crisscrossed the country in recent weeks propping up Democrats in the midterm elections.

title: Napier sergeant leads team in British Army patrol challenge
body:
Unfortunately you are viewing this website on an outdated browser which does not support the necessary features for us to provide an adequate experience. Please switch to a modern browser such as latest version of Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Apple Safari or Microsoft Edge.
For the first time, a New Zealand Army reserve force team has competed in the British Army’s premier patrolling event in Wales, achieving a silver ranking.
Eight personnel from the lower North Island's 5th/7th Battalion, Royal New Zealand Infantry Regiment (5/7 RNZIR) were among around 35 countries, as well as United Kingdom units, vying for top honours at Exercise Cambrian Patrol, the British Army’s premier All Arms Patrol Exercise this month.
In the largest iteration in 65 years, the exercise involved more 1,000 troops across 140 patrols traversing the undulating terrain of the Brecon Beacons, in all manner of weather, covering around 60km over 48 hours.
It is designed to be arduous, with participants needing to be mentally and physically prepared as they are tested on skills needed to survive and fight on a modern battlefield.
The battalion earned the privilege after winning the 1st (NZ) Brigade Skills at Arms competition in Waiouru in April, the first time reservists have won the competition.
Napier’s Sergeant Karlyn Butcher, patrol commander for the Cambrian team, had led a platoon to victory at Skill at Arms. But transitioning from Waiouru to the Wales was quite a challenge, he says.
Carrying more than 40kg per person, the patrols face casualty evacuation scenarios, intelligence-gathering missions, artillery fire planning, vehicle recognition, chemical and biological incidents, a tactical water crossing, minefield crossings and attacks on enemy positions, all under significant physical and mental pressure.
“There’s a lot more up and down in Wales, whereas Waiouru is more of a plateau,” he says.
“We expected it, and we did quite extensive training, but it was very hard.”
The 5th/7th Battalion Cambrian Patrol team at the coin presentation following the event
The Kiwi team was notably faster than others, causing them to be messaged – via a GPS tracker – that they needed to sit in place while things were prepared ahead.
“The water gap crossing looks daunting, but then you’re issued life jackets. But there was one area where we went up 200 metres over 100 metres in distance. That was quite scary.”
It was a very immersive scenario, fitting the realities of contemporary conflict, he said.
“It’s all basic infantry stuff, revolving around an invasion of a European country, where you’re advancing. You feel like you’re doing everything for real. There are roving tanks you have to avoid and find other routes around, you get buzzed by drones, and there are active ‘minefields’, where your GPS starts beeping.”
“I didn’t sleep for 36 hours, then we got five hours sleep. But if you’re slow, you don’t get any sleep at all.”
“I think we were very close to getting the gold ranking.”
Patrols are awarded a gold, silver or bronze medal, or a competition coin. Ten patrols were awarded gold and 69 teams awarded silver. 14 patrols did not complete the event.
Staff Sergeant Josh Holden was team manager.
“Our team represented themselves and the NZ Army amazingly well, to a very impressive standard. They were very glad it was over when I picked them up!”
Commanding Officer 5/7 RNZIR, Lieutenant Colonel Shaun O’Connor and the battalion’s Regimental Sergeant Major, Warrant Officer Class 1 Murray Macaulay, were at the prizegiving in Wales.
“We are immensely proud of the team’s efforts, both in New Zealand and the United Kingdom,” says Lieutenant Colonel O’Connor.
“It was an outstanding achievement for a reservist unit to get the opportunity to participate and show they can compete with the best.”

title: N70,000 Transport Allowance: Public Service Unions Back NLC as Labour Rift Deepens
body: Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja The disagreement between the two main labour centres, Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and Trade Union Congress (TUC), over the federal government’s N70,000 transportation allowance approved for public servants seemed to be deepening as Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council (JNPSNC) backed NLC against TUC, which rejected the allowance. National Secretary of JNPSNC, Comrade Gbenga Olowoyo, said, in circular to affiliate unions and state councils, that the agreement leading to approval of the allowance was the product of constructive engagement and exhaustive negotiation. Olowoyo said the meeting was presided by Minister of Labour and Employment, Alhaji Mohamed Maigari Dingyadi, and attended by a labour team led by NLC President Comrade Joe Ajaero, with the participation of the leadership of JNPSNC and Joint Health Sector Union (JOHESU). According to the circular, the meeting was tough and lasted more than six hours before both sides reached the terms. Olowoyo said the N70,000 monthly transportation allowance to be paid for the next six months to public servants, starting November 2026, and it was meant to subsidise unbearable transportation costs being experienced by workers. He expressed hope that states and local governments, with their current humongous allocations, will be patriotic enough to concur with the agreement to complement the federal government’s effort to ameliorate the hardship of workers and their dependants. He said the agreement also cemented implementation of long overdue 40 per cent peculiar allowance, reflecting N70,000 minimum wage, which ought to have started since July 2024, when the new minimum wage commenced. The allowance will be domesticated at sub-national levels from November 2026 while arrears from May 1, 2026 will be paid in three tranches. Olowoyo stated that the federal government agreed to set up a tripartite negotiation committee comprising government, labour, and Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association (NECA) representatives with immediate effect, which formed the focal request from JNPSNC under Comrade Benjamin Anto Uyanto that necessitated the three-day warning strike called on October 2, 2026. Olowoyo tried to correct what he termed a notion that NLC was a union of junior workers, saying all unions affiliated to NLC have members across Ministries, Departments and Agencies up to Directorate level. He said the clarification became necessary because of the position taken by TUC, which rejected the allowance, though it was never part of the discussion. “TUC has explicit right to express opinion on any matter it is directly involved, but not on what it was not part of at any stage of engagement or negotiation with the federal government,” he said. He, however, said it would be commendable if TUC could secure higher amounts, above the N70,000 already agreed by NLC, JNPSNC and JOHESU. The circular added that the meeting also resolved other long-standing issues, including CONHESS adjustment demand since the past 13 years. It said National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission (NSIWC) was given three weeks to finish work on the adjustment and forward to Presidential Committee on Salaries headed by Minister of Finance, for approval. It approved payment of 19-month arrears of health workers allowances in three instalments from December 2026, and resolved the issuance of circular for hazard allowance to agricultural professional officers within three weeks. On tax relief, it was agreed that the matter will be presented to National Economic Council as it involved the federal and state governments. The meeting gave a window of one month to reconvene to evaluate implementation level. Olowoyo said rejection of any item by any trade union was inconsequential to implementation because a wider spectrum of workers had applauded the decision as a step in the right direction.

title: NERC: Discos Collected N220.93bn Revenue in August, Billing Efficiency Rose to 75.36%
body: Abuja, Eko lead collection efficiency as Kaduna, Jos struggle Discos recover 77.63% of allowed revenue per kilowatt-hour Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja Nigeria’s electricity Distribution Companies (Discos) collected N220.93 billion from customers in August 2026, representing a 7.49 per cent increase over the previous month, as their revenue collection efficiency rose to 84.62 per cent, according to the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC). The commission’s August 2026 factsheet on the commercial performance of the 11 Discos showed that total billings stood at N261.10 billion, leaving N40.17 billion uncollected during the month. The collection performance, which improved by 2.66 percentage points from July, indicated that the distribution companies collected about 84.62 per cent of the amount billed to customers. However, the figures also showed significant differences in the ability of the individual Discos to collect revenue, with Abuja, Eko and Ikeja recording relatively strong performances, while Kaduna, Jos and Kano continued to struggle. Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC) recorded the highest collection efficiency at 91.91 per cent, collecting N37.57 billion out of N40.88 billion billed to customers. Its performance improved by 10.89 percentage points compared with July. Despite their strong performances, Eko and Ikeja recorded declines of 5.42 and 9.67 percentage points, respectively, in collection efficiency compared with July. At the other end of the table, Kaduna Electric recorded the weakest collection performance, collecting N5.57 billion from N10.05 billion billed, representing an efficiency rate of 55.44 per cent. Jos Disco collected N6.42 billion from N10.35 billion billed, translating to 61.98 per cent, while Kano Electric recorded a collection efficiency of 60.31 per cent after collecting N9.07 billion from N15.04 billion billed. The figures highlighted the persistent disparity in the commercial performance of the distribution companies, with some collecting nearly all the revenue billed to customers while others recorded substantially lower rates. On energy billing, the 11 Discos received a total of 346.49 billion naira worth of electricity during the month but billed customers for N261.10 billion, translating to a billing efficiency of 75.36 per cent. The billing efficiency improved by 0.26 percentage points from July, but the gap between the value of energy received and the amount billed stood at N85.39 billion. Abuja Disco received energy valued at N54.93 billion but billed customers N40.88 billion, while Ikeja received N54.99 billion and billed N40.45 billion. Eko recorded the highest billing efficiency at 84.49 per cent, followed by Kano at 82.24 per cent and Port Harcourt at 80.22 per cent. Kaduna recorded the lowest at 60.92 per cent, followed by Yola at 64.04 per cent and Jos at 66.47 per cent. The NERC data also showed that the distribution companies recovered an average of N101.03 per kilowatt-hour against an allowed average tariff of N130.15 per kilowatt-hour, representing a revenue recovery efficiency of 77.63 per cent. Although the recovery efficiency improved by 2.71 percentage points from July, the actual average collection remained N29.12 per kilowatt-hour below the allowed average tariff. Eko Disco recorded the highest recovery efficiency at 96.29 per cent, with an average collection of N135.58 per kilowatt-hour against an allowed tariff of N140.80. Ikeja followed at 84.22 per cent, while Abuja recorded 83.63 per cent. Kaduna had the lowest recovery efficiency at 41.90 per cent, collecting an average of N51.03 per kilowatt-hour against an allowed tariff of N121.80. Jos followed at 52.80 per cent, while Kano recorded 60.98 per cent. Enugu and Ibadan also recorded recovery efficiencies below 72 per cent, at 71.49 and 71.22 per cent, respectively.

title: Keyamo Unveils Tinubu Aviation Campaign Series Ahead of 2027 Polls
body: 30-second television series to broadcast president’s Tinubu administration’s record in aviation James Emejo in Abuja Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, has launched a television campaign series to promote President Bola Tinubu’s aviation sector record ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The move signals an early push to use the administration’s sectoral performance in its re-election campaign. The 30-second programme, tagged Tinubu Aviation Revolution Series, is scheduled to begin airing on major television stations on November 1, with broadcasts expected to continue until a few days before the presidential election. The initiative follows Keyamo’s appointment as Director of the Directorate of Air Transport Mobilisation under the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC PCC), where he is responsible for coordinating air transportation for authorised campaign activities. A statement issued by the minister’s Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Tunde Moshood, said had mobilised his team to produce the campaign material following his appointment. The statement added that the television campaign had been fully paid for, although it did not disclose the cost of production or broadcast placement. The series is designed to present the Tinubu administration’s aviation policies and achievements in a short, accessible format, using the sector’s contribution to economic activity as part of the case for the president’s re-election. Aviation plays a strategic role in trade, tourism, investment and international connectivity, making developments in the sector a potential component of the administration’s broader economic performance narrative. The campaign will seek to draw public attention to what the government considers its progress in aviation and link the sector’s development to Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. The rollout also marks an early campaign communication initiative by Keyamo in his new role within the APC’s presidential campaign structure, ahead of the 2027 general election. The television campaign is expected to run until shortly before the presidential poll, placing the administration’s aviation record before voters as political activities gather momentum. The statement adds, “With aviation serving as a critical driver of economic growth, tourism, trade, investment and international connectivity, the series is intended to draw attention to the sector’s role in advancing the Renewed Hope Agenda and to encourage an informed public assessment of the administration’s performance. “The launch of the Tinubu Aviation Revolution Series signals the beginning of a focused campaign as the APC prepares for the 2027 general election.”

title: Congo Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,000
body: The death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic ​Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000, government ‌data showed on Friday, as authorities had yet to find a way to control the country’s deadliest ​Ebola epidemic on record. No approved treatments or vaccines can combat the rare Bundibugyo species behind the outbreak in the Central African country. It has ​infected more than 10,000 people since it was declared in May. Delayed detection, conflict, and strained health services have helped the virus spread faster than ​in previous outbreaks. Eight of Congo’s 26 provinces have ‌been ⁠affected, with many deaths occurring outside treatment centres. This year’s outbreak is the world’s second-largest ever, behind only the 2014-2016 one that infected ​over 28,600 ​people and ⁠killed more than 11,000 across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone. Last week Nigeria ​became the fourth African country to ​report ⁠an Ebola case, extending the outbreak’s geographic spread to West Africa. East African countries Kenya and ⁠Uganda ​have also reported cases.

title: Top Swiss court upholds landmark Liberia war crimes ruling
body: The top Swiss court on Friday confirmed a ​guilty verdict against a Liberian warlord, ‌upholding his 20-year sentence in the country’s first-ever war crimes trial. Alieu Kosiah, who ​fought in the 1990s against ​then-president Charles Taylor’s army during Liberia’s ⁠brutal civil war, was originally sentenced to ​20 years in prison in June 2021 ​for rape, murder and cannibalism. An earlier appeal was rejected in 2023 by the Federal Criminal Court ​and the dismissal of his second ​appeal by Switzerland’s highest tribunal the Federal Supreme Court ‌published ⁠on Friday closes the case. “This is a landmark decision, made possible by the courage of these victims, who have ​written a ​page ⁠of legal history,” said Alain Werner, Director of Civitas Maxima, ​an NGO representing victims in ​this ⁠case. However, the court reversed a parallel conviction for crimes against humanity on the grounds that the 2011 law on this crime cannot be applied retroactively.

title: Some Michigan Jewish Democrats disavow Stevens over endorsement of El-Sayed’s GOP rival
body: Key Jewish Democratic figures denounced pro-Israel US Rep. Haley Stevens' endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers for Michigan's open US Senate seat on Sunday.Some, including Michigan congressional candidate Jeremy Moss, spoke at a press conference at the United Auto Workers headquarters in Detroit to support Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed hours after Stevens, a Democrat, endorsed Rogers across town.“There are people who are looking at their ballot right now and feeling genuine anguish. I understand this,” Moss told the crowd, naming the spring's Temple Israel attack in the state. “But Mike Rogers is not the solution to this problem.”Moss has had his own public disagreements with El-Sayed, and has not formally endorsed him. He dropped a subtle dig Sunday at anti-Israel streamer Hasan Piker, a former campaign ally of El-Sayed's who has disparaged both Moss and Jewish voters in his suburban district: “There have been people who have trafficked in antisemitism and have beleaguered Oakland County voters.”Yet Moss also stated, “I would rather debate our disagreements in a democratic institution than one that has been eroded by Trump and Rogers.” Moss is running for the seat in the US House that Stevens abandoned for her unsuccessful run against El-Sayed for the Democratic Senate nomination. Moss appeared with Jewish former congressman Andy Levin, who has backed El-Sayed for months and told the crowd that the candidate “deeply respects Judaism and the Jewish people.”Also present were Michigan state Sen. Mallory McMorrow, who also ran in the Democratic primary against El-Sayed; and pro-Palestinian politicians including Michigan state Senate candidate Abbas Alawieh, a co-founder of the “Uncommitted” movement in 2024 that targeted then-President Joe Biden at the ballot box over Gaza.Their joint message: All Democrats, Jewish and not, should back El-Sayed and reject Stevens' endorsement of Rogers.Democrat Scholten voices disapproval of El-SayedSimultaneously, another Democrat, Michigan Rep. Hillary Scholten, appeared with several rabbis to address a different audience of Jews uncomfortable with El-Sayed's rhetoric on Israel.On that Zoom following Scholten's appearance, some leaders of the Nonnegotiable movement urged their group of Jewish voters to write in “Emma Lazarus,” the 19th-century Jewish poet and activist whose words grace the base of the Statue of Liberty, on their ballots instead.Scholten did not urge the Jews on the call in one direction or another, nor did she mention Stevens. But she has publicly voiced her own disapproval of El-Sayed and refused to endorse him.“We know that in this moment, it has never, ever been more important to stand up and push back against antisemitism that has been given far, far too much of a platform in American politics,” she told the Zoom crowd.One of Nonnegotiable's organizers, Rabbi Aaron Starr of Congregation Shaarey Zedek in the Detroit suburb of Southfield, told people on the call that he has “profound respect for Haley Stevens.” “I have profound respect for her willingness to put herself out there,” Starr said. “I have deep respect for her willingness to stand up, to speak out and take a stand in this difficult moment.”The dual perspectives epitomized the dilemma many of Michigan's Jewish voters are facing in the campaign's final days. A sizable contingent of the state's Jews are increasingly troubled by El-Sayed's statements on Israel and antisemitic acts, including his recent refusal to name whether Israel or Iran posed a greater threat to the United States.Some, including Stevens' fiancée Jason Turkish, a Democratic megadonor, have publicly said they would vote for Rogers.Jewish voices condemn Stevens' Yet the race, which is one of several pivotal to Democrats taking control of the Senate, has also troubled many liberal Jews who see GOP policies as deeply antithetical to their beliefs. Many for that reason view Stevens' endorsement, which she said was meant to stand “against hate,” as a betrayal. New York Jewish progressive congressional candidate Brad Lander castigated Stevens in a video from Brooklyn.“Maybe she doesn't care about throwing away reproductive rights, throwing away civil rights,” said Lander, who has spoken to Michigan Jews in support of El-Sayed. “But to do it all in the name of so-called Jewish safety, boy, as an American Jew I can tell you that's not the way that anybody, Jews or Muslims or anybody else, will be saved.” Ray Wert, McMorrow's Jewish husband, said on X that he had urged Stevens to sign her name to an op-ed condemning Rogers for his own interactions with antisemitic individuals, including a major donor who promotes Christian nationalism and a former student campaign organizer who had tweeted about wanting to send Jews to North Korea. She refused, Wert claimed. He posted a copy of the op-ed, which included the line, “I can't hold one standard for Democrats and a softer one for Republicans and still claim to have a standard at all.”

title: New movies in UAE cinemas in November 2026: Release dates and where to watch
body: November is shaping up to be a busy month for UAE cinemas, with Hollywood blockbusters, Japanese monster movies, Indian productions and Arabic-language releases heading to the big screen. Among the highlights are Godzilla Minus Zero , the sequel to the Oscar-winning Japanese film, and The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , which explores the origins of Haymitch Abernathy. Family audiences can look forward to DreamWorks' Forgotten Island and Disney's Hexed , while Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro reunite for another chapter of the Meet the Parents franchise. Independent cinema also has a strong showing, with Cinema Akil hosting six Hong Kong films from November 6 to 8, including Jackie Chan's Police Story and the acclaimed Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In . Here are the films scheduled across UAE cinemas in November. November 5 Godzilla Minus Zero Takashi Yamazaki returns to the monster franchise following the success of 2023's Godzilla Minus One , which won the Academy Award for Best Visual Effects. Set in 1949, two years after the previous film, the sequel finds Japan struggling to rebuild after the devastation of war and Godzilla 's attacks. Ryunosuke Kamiki and Minami Hamabe reprise their roles. Yamazaki again directs, writes, and oversees the visual effects, continuing his approach of combining large-scale spectacle with human drama. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas, Reel Cinemas and Roxy Cinemas, with special IMAX previews at selected Vox locations on November 3 The Cat in the Hat Dr Seuss 's mischievous creation returns in an animated adventure directed by Erica Rivinoja and Alessandro Carloni. Bill Hader voices the Cat, who has the task of cheering up two siblings struggling to settle into a new town. His attempts to help inevitably descend into chaos. The voice cast also includes Matt Berry, Xochitl Gomez, Quinta Brunson and America Ferrera. The film marks the character's first fully animated theatrical feature, more than two decades after the live-action adaptation starring Mike Myers. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas and Star Cinemas Ramayana: Part One Indian filmmaker Nitesh Tiwari directs this ambitious adaptation of the ancient Hindu epic , with Ranbir Kapoor playing Rama, Sai Pallavi portraying Sita and Yash taking on the role of Ravana. The mythological fantasy follows Rama's confrontation with the powerful ruler of Lanka, drawing on a story that has shaped Indian literature, theatre and cinema for generations. The large-scale production brings the familiar tale to audiences through elaborate visual effects and a cast drawn from across Indian cinema. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas, Reel Cinemas and Star Cinemas A Talent for Murder Helen Mirren portrays celebrated crime novelist Patricia Highsmith in this psychological thriller, alongside Olivia Cooke and Alden Ehrenreich. The story follows a young representative from a New York publishing house who travels to Switzerland to persuade the notoriously difficult author to write another instalment in her Ripley series. His assignment draws him into a dangerous situation involving the woman behind some of literature's most unsettling characters. Highsmith's work has previously inspired films including The Talented Mr Ripley and Strangers on a Train . Where to watch: Vox Cinemas Idiots Dave Franco, O'Shea Jackson Jr and Mason Thames star in this crime comedy about two unqualified men hired to transport a wealthy teenager to rehabilitation. What appears to be a straightforward assignment quickly descends into chaos, with the unlikely trio finding themselves in increasingly dangerous situations. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas The Shawshank Redemption Frank Darabont's 1994 prison drama returns to cinemas, giving audiences another opportunity to experience the acclaimed adaptation of Stephen King's novella on the big screen. Tim Robbins stars as Andy Dufresne, a banker sentenced to life imprisonment for murder, while Morgan Freeman plays Red, a fellow inmate who becomes his closest friend. Despite a modest initial box-office performance, the film developed an enduring following and is widely celebrated for its exploration of hope, friendship and perseverance. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas The Cycle Deborah Ann Woll and Jeffrey Donovan star in this supernatural mystery about a woman investigating her estranged father's disappearance after his body is discovered 36 years later at a crime scene. Her search for answers uncovers disturbing secrets surrounding his death. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas November 6 Mookuthi Amman 2: Maha Sakthi Nayanthara returns for the sequel to the 2020 Tamil fantasy comedy, with Sundar C directing. The original follows a goddess who intervenes in human affairs and challenges religious exploitation. The new instalment promises more mythology, humour and social commentary, with Regina Cassandra and B R Vijayakumar joining the cast. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas Scene Suriya stars alongside Nazriya Nazim and Naslen in this Tamil crime drama about a police officer drawn back into an investigation he previously abandoned. Revisiting the case forces him to confront unresolved questions as new complications emerge. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas and Star Cinemas Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In Soi Cheang's acclaimed 2024 martial arts thriller returns to the big screen as the opening film of Cinema Akil's Hong Kong Film Gala Presentation. Set in 1980s Hong Kong, it follows a troubled young man who finds refuge inside the densely populated Kowloon Walled City, where he develops friendships and becomes embroiled in a violent struggle for control. Starring Louis Koo, Raymond Lam and Sammo Hung, the film was Hong Kong's submission for the 2025 Academy Awards. Actors Kenny Wong and German Cheung will attend a post-screening discussion. Where to watch: Cinema Akil at 25hours Hotel Dubai One Central on November 6 Rocky, Rocky II and Rocky III Sylvester Stallone 's boxing franchise returns to cinemas as the original Rocky marks its 50th anniversary. Released in 1976, the Oscar-winning film follows an unknown Philadelphia boxer given an unlikely opportunity to fight heavyweight champion Apollo Creed. Its two sequels continue Rocky Balboa's career, from his rematch with Creed to his confrontation with Clubber Lang, played by Mr T. The films helped establish Stallone as a Hollywood star and became landmarks of American sports cinema. Where to watch: Reel Cinemas at Dubai Mall, November 6–11 November 7 Dog Day Evening Director Mak Tin Shu turns a mundane frustration into dark comedy as a man's attempts to cancel his television subscription escalate into a hostage situation. The Hong Kong film blends crime, absurdist humour and social satire, with actor Yukki Tai attending a post-screening discussion. Where to watch: Cinema Akil, Alserkal Avenue, November 7. Police Story Jackie Chan's 1985 action classic receives a special outdoor screening as part of the Hong Kong Film Gala. Chan directs and stars as police officer Chan Ka-kui, who must protect a key witness while pursuing a powerful drug lord. Known for its extraordinary practical stunts, elaborate action choreography and destructive set pieces, the film helped establish Chan's international reputation. Its famous shopping centre finale is among the most celebrated action sequences in Hong Kong cinema, making this a rare opportunity to experience it on the big screen. Where to watch: Cinema Akil's outdoor screening at The Yard, Alserkal Avenue, November 7 Dead End Isabella Lam Lok-hin's psychological thriller follows a computer programmer whose life is disrupted when a teenager arrives claiming to be his half-brother. Their encounter forces him to confront his father's death and long-suppressed memories. The Hong Kong production premiered at the Busan International Film Festival. Where to watch: Cinema Akil, Alserkal Avenue, November 7 November 8 Another World Hong Kong animator Tommy Ng Kai Chung makes his feature-length directorial debut with this fantasy drama, which took seven years to produce. Set in a mysterious realm between death and reincarnation, the film follows a spirit tasked with guiding souls through the afterlife. His encounter with a young girl struggling with grief and anger challenges his understanding of the world around him. Released in 2025, the film explores death, loss and emotional healing through elaborate hand-drawn animation. Where to watch: Cinema Akil, Alserkal Avenue, November 8 The Dating Menu Directed by Frankie Chung, this Hong Kong romantic comedy follows a chef whose culinary creations become the setting for a series of first dates. The film uses food and contemporary dating culture to explore relationships in a city increasingly influenced by algorithms and dating apps. Where to watch: Cinema Akil, Alserkal Avenue, November 8 November 12 Forgotten Island DreamWorks Animation draws inspiration from Filipino folklore for this fantasy adventure directed by Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado. H.E.R. and Liza Soberano voice lifelong friends Jo and Raissa, who discover a portal to the magical island of Nakali. There, they encounter mythical creatures, including the terrifying Manananggal. Their greatest challenge, however, comes when they discover that returning home will cost them every memory of their friendship. Dave Franco, Manny Jacinto and Lea Salonga are among the supporting voice cast. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas and Roxy Cinemas Ebenezer Johnny Depp takes on the role of Ebenezer Scrooge in a new adaptation of Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol . Directed by Ti West, whose previous films include X and Pearl , the film follows the miserly businessman as supernatural visitors force him to confront his past, present and future. Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Daisy Ridley, Sam Claflin and Ian McKellen also appear. West's involvement suggests a darker interpretation of the familiar Christmas tale, drawing particular attention to its ghostly origins. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas Victorian Psycho Maika Monroe stars in this gothic horror thriller about an eccentric governess who arrives at a remote Victorian manor, where disturbing incidents raise suspicions about her identity. Thomasin McKenzie and Jason Isaacs also feature in the cast. Set against the oppressive surroundings of an isolated estate, the story combines period drama with psychological suspense. Monroe, whose horror credits include It Follows and Longlegs , returns to a genre in which she has become a recognisable leading performer. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas Les Miserables Directed by Fred Cavaye, this new adaptation of Victor Hugo's 1862 novel stars Tahar Rahim, Vincent Lindon and Noemie Merlant. Set against the social upheaval of 19th-century France, the story follows former convict Jean Valjean and his pursuit of redemption as he is relentlessly pursued by police inspector Javert. The novel has inspired numerous stage and screen productions, most famously the long-running musical. This latest interpretation revisits Hugo's exploration of poverty, injustice and moral responsibility. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas Hadoota Egyptian comedian Ahmed Helmy stars as Hadoota, a 40-year-old criminal who cannot remember where he concealed a witness he kidnapped. Desperate to recover the information, he turns to a hypnotherapist, played by Amina Khalil, who attempts to reconstruct his memories. The process forces him to revisit encounters with old enemies and confront events from his past. Mohamed Mamdouh also stars in the Arabic-language comedy, which combines a crime caper with a story about personal reckoning. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas November 13 Bouma Dileesh Pothan, Sagar Surya and Adithi Balan star in this Malayalam mystery about a struggling singer who returns to an estate connected to her past. Her arrival triggers unsettling experiences and exposes long-buried family secrets, blurring the boundaries between memory and reality. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas Itlu Arjuna This Telugu romantic drama follows a man unable to speak who falls in love and struggles to express his feelings. Starring Anaswara Rajan, Aniesh Reddy and Brahmaji, the film explores communication, emotional connection and the challenges of expressing affection without words. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas November 19 The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping The Hunger Games franchise returns with another prequel, this time centred on a young Haymitch Abernathy, played by Joseph Zada. Directed by Francis Lawrence and based on Suzanne Collins's 2025 novel, the film takes place 24 years before Katniss Everdeen's story, during the 50th Hunger Games. Ralph Fiennes portrays President Snow, while Elle Fanning, Jesse Plemons, Glenn Close and Kieran Culkin join the ensemble. The story explores the deadly competition that shaped Haymitch long before he became Katniss's mentor. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas and Roxy Cinemas Ghost Soldier Jim Caviezel stars as a former special forces soldier whose quiet retirement ends when a powerful foreign corporation attempts to seize his community's land. Refusing to surrender, he puts his military training and advanced weaponry to use in an escalating confrontation. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas November 20 OM – Chapter 1: Udhiram – The Blood Dhanush, Mammootty and Sai Pallavi star in this Tamil crime drama exploring greed, poverty and the pursuit of power. Set in a violent world where criminals and law enforcement collide, the film establishes the conflicts of what is intended to be a larger story. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas Bachelor Party D'eux Tovino Thomas, Kunchacko Boban and Naslen star in this Malayalam comedy, a spiritual successor to the 2012 film Bachelor Party . Featuring a new group of characters, it aims to recreate the original's chaotic mixture of friendship, action and irreverent humour. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas Sathyavan Savithri Keerthy Suresh stars in this Tamil courtroom drama about a woman fighting to prove her husband's innocence in a murder case. Her determination is tested when she finds herself opposing her own mentor, turning the trial into a deeply personal confrontation. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas November 26 Focker In-Law Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro reunite for the fourth instalment of the Meet the Parents franchise, more than 15 years after Little Fockers . This time, Greg Focker's grown-up son Henry, played by Skyler Gisondo, is preparing to marry Olivia, a former FBI hostage negotiator, played by Ariana Grande. Greg suspects his future daughter-in-law is hiding something, although his father-in-law, Jack, played by De Niro, is thoroughly charmed by her. John Hamburg directs, with Owen Wilson, Teri Polo and Blythe Danner also returning. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas Hexed Disney's latest original animated feature follows Billie, an awkward teenager who discovers that her unusual abilities may be magical. The revelation transports her and her highly organised mother, Alice, into a hidden supernatural world, changing their understanding of their family. Directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand, the film features Hailee Steinfeld and Rashida Jones in the leading voice roles, alongside Stephen Fry. The story combines fantasy adventure with a mother-daughter relationship at its centre. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas and Roxy Cinemas Crypto Bassem Samra and Bayoumi Fouad star in this Egyptian crime comedy about two estranged brothers summoned by their mafia boss father after 30 years. Hoping for an escape from poverty, the brothers instead find themselves drawn into their father's dangerous criminal affairs. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas Traveller's Hell A young woman travelling alone on mountain roads encounters a stranded man whose vehicle resembles one linked to a series of murders. This Arabic-language thriller, starring Adwaa Bader and Aziz Gharbawi, builds suspense around the stranger's identity and the dangers of isolation. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas and Roxy Cinemas Paper Tiger James Gray, whose previous films include Ad Astra and The Immigrant , directs this crime thriller starring Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller. The story follows two brothers who pursue the American dream and become entangled in a dangerous scheme involving the Russian mafia. Their actions place their family at risk and threaten their relationship as suspicion and betrayal enter the picture. Gray's films frequently examine family bonds, ambition and the darker aspects of American life, making the material a natural fit for his interests. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas November 27 Gun Maaster G9 Emraan Hashmi, Aparshakti Khurana and Genelia Deshmukh star in this Hindi action film about a man whose pursuit of love brings him into conflict with a dangerous adversary. The story combines romance with escalating confrontations and action sequences. Where to watch: Vox Cinemas and Roxy Cinemas

title: House spends P100M a year on utilities. Why ask for P1B?
body: In the last five years, the House’s utility expenses averaged only P108 million per year, but the chamber keeps on requesting — and approving — an inflated budget, never mind if it has already reached a billion pesos. The underspending is a total head-scratcher, especially because it becomes uncertain how the eventual savings are being utilized. The House enjoys fiscal autonomy, which means that unlike other government agencies, it is not required to return unspent funds to the Bureau of Treasury. In the absence of transparency, critics warn that the funds may be prone to abuse and corruption. Electricity, power spending Take a look at the 2025 budget of the House of Representatives, the latest of which has been subject to complete state auditing. The General Appropriations Act — signed by the President after it was approved separately by the House and the Senate — gave the House a total of P1.35 billion for the chamber’s water and electricity expenses. The Commission on Audit’s report, however, learned that the chamber spent only over one-tenth of its actual utility allocation. Did the House anticipate a major spike in utility needs for 2025 that it needed a gargantuan budget for power and water? They didn’t say so, but trends show that the House has had a habit of securing an inflated utility budget, even though it only needs a small fraction of the funds. Supplies, too The underspending goes beyond utilities. The House’s budget for supplies has also tremendously increased in recent years, from P327.98 million in 2021, to a whopping P1.34 billion in 2025. That’s even though spending for supplies averaged only P83 million annually in that half-decade. Graphics by David Castuciano/Rappler Where did the savings go? Finding out was Congressman Toby Tiangco’s agenda when he interpellated the budget sponsor of the Commission on Audit (COA) during plenary debates in the House. “COA’s job is to audit what was spent, what is being spent. COA doesn’t know where the savings went,” said COA budget sponsor in the House, Representative John Tracy Cagas. For Tiangco, the practice of budget allocation does not make sense. “Why is there high funding for supplies and utilities but are left unspent, and then the following year, you still increase the budget?” Tiangco told Rappler. Extraordinary expenses Tiangco’s suspicion is that savings from utilities and supplies are being realigned to extraordinary and miscellaneous expenses (EME). EME cover unique demands not typically covered by standard budgets. The Department of Budget and Management says these refer to expenses incurred for meetings, seminars, public relations, and official entertainment, among other things. EME should not be used for salaries, wages, allowances, and confidential expenses. Following those guidelines to the dot may be easier said than done. A 2011 concurrent resolution by Congress states that these funds — which fall under maintenance and other operating expenses (MOOE) — require liquidation only by way of certification. In other words, no official receipts are needed to justify these expenses. “Unused funds of the House don’t revert to the Treasury. However, the House Speaker can declare those unused funds as savings as provided under the Constitution and relevant General Provisions on use of savings in an annual GAAs,” budget expert Zyza Suzara told Rappler. “These savings are typically used to provide hefty bonuses for congressional staff of the House of Representatives,” she added. The disparity between the allocated extraordinary funds for the House and its actual expenditure is astonishing. In 2025, the overspending reached P3.74 billion. The question arises: where did the extra funds come from? Budget transparency Transparency on the MOOE allocated to every congressman has been among Tiangco’s recent crusades. COA, after all, has confirmed that the MOOE for districts are not the same. Tiangco has been a thorn in the House majority during the budget process this year. He wrote to Speaker Bojie Dy in August, informing him of his decision to break ranks and become an independent, to allow him “greater latitude to raise questions…in the use of public funds.” This is not the first time Tiangco parted ways with the majority. Close and longtime observers of the House budget process may not find it uncharacteristic of Tiangco to be a champion of budget accountability, but given his background — particularly his perceived kinship to his relative, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. — his vocal opposition to the budget proposal may come across as jarring. Tiangco, alongside over a dozen lawmakers, voted against the 2027 spending bill approved by the House, citing the chamber’s supposed rejection of his proposed transparency reforms. His demands are a tough ask anyway. For one, he wanted the budget of the House of Representatives to undergo actual scrutiny. This meant a public committee hearing for the House’s 2027 appropriations, pegged at P17.6 billion. Tiangco later said the House revised the executive’s proposal and increased its own appropriations by P5 billion for the upcoming fiscal year. The House in recent memory has not conducted committee deliberations on its own budget. The free pass is similar to what’s been given to the Office of the President, the Supreme Court, and the Office of the Vice President before Sara Duterte parted ways with the Marcos administration. A proper committee hearing, or even plenary-level debates, could have provided clarity on various questions surrounding the House’s expenditures, including its underspent utilities and supplies funding. Rappler has emailed Speaker Dy’s office for comment. We will update this story once we receive a reply. Must Watch WATCH: Why the budget process of Philippine Congress is prone to corruption Congressmen’s insertions Since the House’s approval of the 2027 budget, the chamber has faced greater scrutiny after budget watchdogs crunched the numbers and found that the chamber included nearly P190 billion in public works funding despite the absence of published project attachments. In simple words, the House appears to have modified the President’s budget proposal so much that it resulted in hundreds of millions to billions of pesos in insertions in congressmen’s respective districts. Even Tiangco’s constituency isn’t spared. The tracker of People’s Budget Coalition and Better Gov says that P338 million in insertions were made to the district engineering office covering Malabon and Navotas, raising its total funding to P1.12 billion. Tiangco has disclosed a P2.28-billion public works funding for Navotas, up from the P1.61 billion that he said was included in the executive’s original proposal. But Tiangco insists the increase is backed by project details, and is in line with what the Regional Development Council and civil society organizations originally approved for his city. Must Read How to track insertions in House-approved 2027 budget But the seeming top offender for the 2027 budget is no less than the President’s son himself, Majority Leader Sandro Marcos. The DPWH engineering office in the Ilocos Norte district he represents has been allocated P4.74 billion in public works projects, up from the P369 million that was originally proposed by the executive. In short, the House has increased his district’s budget by P4.38 billion. The younger Marcos has not provided an explanation for the budget adjustment. The staggering figures underscore the alarming need for transparency. The watchdogs based their analysis on figures from engineering offices, but they sometimes cover numerous constituencies. This means that the exact allocation per congressional district, and the insertions made by party-list lawmakers, cannot be fully determined, unless the House opens up its books to the public. But does the House really have the guts — or decency — to truly pierce its longstanding veil of secrecy? – Rappler.com

title: Greek Taverna Halo Opens in Melbourne with Olympic Meats Chef
body: Melbourne’s Greek dining scene is set to welcome a major new addition, with Halo , a three storey taverna led by an all-star hospitality team, opening on Chapel Street this summer. The new restaurant at 144 Chapel Street, Windsor , will bring traditional Greek hospitality together with contemporary Mediterranean flavours, led by head chef Evan Georgopoulos , whose recent success at Sydney’s acclaimed Olympic Meats helped put Greek cuisine in the national spotlight. Photograph: Supplied | Halo Melbourne Halo marks the return of Melbourne hospitality heavyweight Simon Blacher to running a single venue after 14 years leading Commune Group, the team behind popular restaurants including Hanoi Hannah, Tokyo Tina and Moonhouse. He is joined by Nick Vas and Greg Stanogias from Elia Greek Tavern, creating one of Melbourne’s strongest Greek hospitality collaborations in years. Greek food takes centre stage The menu is built around the spirit of the traditional Greek taverna, with generous dishes designed for sharing. Guests can expect house made pita cooked to order, seasonal meze, traditional dips, charcoal grilled skewers and gyros inspired by generations of Greek family recipes. Georgopoulos said the philosophy behind the kitchen reflects the heart of Greek cooking. “Greek food has never been about precise technique or perfection, but rather an intense generosity coupled with a feel for ingredients.” His approach builds on the success of Olympic Meats in Marrickville, which recently earned recognition in the Sydney Morning Herald Good Food Guide for its Peloponnesian inspired cooking. A Mediterranean drinks list The Greek influence extends beyond the kitchen. Halo’s drinks menu will feature Mediterranean wines served in carafes alongside cocktails inspired by Greece, including Martinis with Kalamata olives. The restaurant will occupy a heritage listed building dating back to 1925, with three levels including a restaurant and bar, semi private dining spaces and a rooftop designed for long lunches and late night gatherings. Another boost for Greek dining Halo’s arrival comes as Greek cuisine continues to gain momentum across Australia, with restaurants embracing both traditional recipes and contemporary interpretations of classic flavours. With an experienced hospitality team and a chef whose cooking is already making waves, Halo is shaping up to become one of Melbourne’s most anticipated restaurant openings of the summer. title: U.S. National Cathedral holds special prayer for Ukrainian children
body:
The U.S. National Cathedral in Washington, D.C., in partnership with the Ukrainian embassy, held a special All Saints' Day prayer for the children of Ukraine on Nov. 1.
"Today it is something special because it is about Ukrainian children ," Denys Sienik, acting ambassador of Ukraine to the U.S. , said. "Those children who are no longer with us, those children who have been kidnapped by Russia. And it is so important to draw attention, to raise public attention to the matter, and to send a message to all Ukrainian children that no one is forgotten."
The event combined "prayers and Psalms with congregational hymns, showcasing the best of Anglican tradition," according to the Washington National Cathedral.
The service included prayers for peace in Ukraine, led in part by Ukrainian children, and prayers offered by Ukrainian clergy for the people of Ukraine.
A Kyiv Independent reporter on the scene said that hundreds of people participated in the event.
Previously, the cathedral held two other prayer events for Ukraine since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.
As of September 2026, Ukraine's Justice Ministry has officially confirmed 20,610 cases of deportation and forced transfer of Ukrainian children to Russia.
Ukrainian human rights groups estimate that hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian children are under Russian control, including those who have been deported or forcibly transferred and those who remain in occupied territories and are at risk of deportation.
Ukrainian officials estimate the real figure of abducted children could be far higher. Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets puts the number at up to 150,000 , while Presidential Commissioner for Children's Rights Daria Herasymchuk has given a range of 200,000–300,000 .
As of September 2026, more than 3,900 children have been confirmed killed in Ukraine since 2022, according to the United Nations, though the real number is likely higher.

title: Learjet with 9 aboard crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida: FAA
body:
The jet departed from Austin, Texas, for the Bahamas, the FAA said.
A Learjet believed to be carrying nine people crashed on Sunday afternoon in Palm Beach County, Florida, after making a rapid dive of about 350 feet per second, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.
The plane, a 22-year-old twin-engine Learjet 60, crashed after taking off from Austin, Texas, and was headed to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas, according to the FAA.
The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board will investigate the crash, the FAA said.
Photos and videos online showed a jet hitting the ground nose-first and bursting into a fireball. The impact of the crash left a crater near a shopping center.
The jet crashed near Military Trail, between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue, in the Greenacres community of Palm Beach County, authorities said.
There was no immediate word from authorities on deaths and injuries.
The plane went from 35,250 feet to 8,750 feet in a little over a minute, or roughly 350 feet per second, before it slammed into the ground, according to the FAA.
"Obviously, this was a cataclysmic plane crash," Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said during a press briefing on Sunday. "It looked like a missile going down. It left a big crater on the side of the road."
"I think people will recognize this as a major tragedy," he said.
According to records, the plane belongs to a private company and has been used as a rental in the past.

title: CAR Army, Russian specialists thwart large-scale operation by radical groups — Touadera
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. The army of the Central African Republic (CAR) and Russian military specialists thwarted a major operation by a coalition of armed groups in October, delivering a preemptive strike, CAR President Faustin-Archange Touadera said in an interview with TASS.
"It would be premature to speak of stabilization in the definitive sense, and I would not want to engage in wishful thinking. However, let me present the facts as they stand, along with our position on the situation. On October 10, 2026, in the Nabagai-Tissi area of the Vakaga Prefecture, a large-scale operation by a coalition of radical groups was thwarted through the joint efforts of the CAR Defense Forces and Russian military specialists," Touadera said.
He added that the opposing force, numbering approximately 1,300, had planned an offensive against the Vakaga and Bamingui-Bangoran prefectures for the second half of October. A preemptive strike was launched against them. More than 60 militants were neutralized, and a significant quantity of Western-made weaponry was seized. Among those neutralized or forced to flee were several field commanders, including Mahamat Deya and a commander named Khalid from Nourredine Adam's group.

title: Ukrainian Film Festival kicks off in Poland on Nov 2, with 50 films to be screened in 12 cities
body:
Beata Bieronska-Lach, director of the Ukraine! Film Festival, announced this in an interview with Ukrinform.
According to her, despite the full-scale war, Ukraine's film industry continues to develop, particularly thanks to international cooperation and foreign funding.
"Every year, I worry about whether we will have enough Ukrainian films and whether there will be anything to screen. I fear that film production might grind to a halt under wartime conditions... However, my concerns have proved unfounded: Ukrainian films are being made. If not directly in Ukraine, then through numerous international co-productions. Ukrainian filmmakers have started looking for funding abroad, and they are succeeding. There are many funds that finance Ukrainian cinema," Bieronska-Lach said.
She said that this year's festival program will include Polish-Ukrainian and German-Ukrainian co-productions. The competition program will feature eight full-length fiction films, nine documentaries and 23 short films. Screenings of children's films and a separate section dedicated to Belarusian cinema are also planned.
The festival director noted that after the screenings in Warsaw, the festival will continue in 11 other cities: Krakow, Wroclaw, Gdansk, Lublin, Gliwice, Lodz, Rzeszow, Plock, Bielsko-Biala, Zielona Gora and Poznan. The screenings will run until mid-December.
The organizer said the festival's geographical reach is changing. This year, screenings will not take place in Torun because the institution that previously hosted the event is undergoing restructuring. At the same time, new cities and organizations are joining the festival.
"Overall, the cities and cinemas that hosted the festival in previous years want to continue working with us. At the same time, new institutions are emerging and approaching us on their own initiative because they want to screen Ukrainian films," Bieronnska-Lach said.
According to her, these are most often Polish organizations, foundations or cinemas seeking to respond to demand from local communities. In cities with large Ukrainian communities, such screenings make it possible to organize joint cultural events for Ukrainians and Poles and promote integration within local communities.
The festival director said that Bielsko-Biala and Zielona Gora are the new venues this year. According to her, the cities themselves expressed interest in joining the event.
Bieronnska-Lach also noted that Polish cinemas continue to show interest in Ukrainian films. Last year, she feared that amid some cooling in Ukrainian-Polish relations, cinemas would gradually lose interest and withdraw from screenings, sometimes suggesting postponing them until the following year.
"Instead, we can see today that interest remains, which means the films will be screened in various cities," Bieronnska-Lach said.

title: Oman, China sign agreement, 14 MoUs and cooperation protocol
body:
Muscat: His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik and the Chinese President presided over the signing ceremony of an agreement, 14 memorandums of understanding (MoUs), and a cooperation protocol between the Sultanate of Oman and the People's Republic of China, on the sidelines of a state visit paid by His Majesty to China. The agreement relates to local currency swaps between the Central Bank of Oman and the People's Bank of China, while the memorandums of understanding pertain to enhancing investment cooperation in green development, media and news, information exchange, science, technology, and innovation, as well as regulatory cooperation in the fields of securities, futures, data, and the digital economy. The memorandums of understanding also relate to the peaceful uses of space, space science, technologies and applications, artificial intelligence, applications of the BeiDou Satellite Navigation System, central bank digital currencies, investment in industrial and supply chains, competition protection and anti-monopoly, vegetation cover development, management of natural reserves, historical documentation, and records and archives management. The protocol pertains to inspection, quarantine, and sanitary requirements for dried palm dates exported to China.
