In a further statement, Mr Ashie Moore told the police that he did not have the passport and believed it had been deposited at the Registry of the High Court’s Criminal Division in Accra as part of the complainant’s bail conditions. Investigators subsequently contacted the court registry. An Assistant Registrar confirmed that the passport had been deposited there but said he could not recall the identity of the person who submitted it. The case docket also identifies a second suspect, Luibing Liang, who was invited by the police to assist with investigations but reportedly failed to honour the invitation. The police indicated that she remained at large at the time of the investigation. The Attorney-General’s advice specifically recommended prosecution of Mr Ashie Moore for stealing and did not make a similar prosecution recommendation against Ms Liang.

title: Sterling Financial’s Profit Before Tax Up 37.1% to N97.28bn
body: Sterling Financial Holdings Company Plc has announced its unaudited results for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, reporting strong earnings growth, balance sheet expansion and a stronger equity base. Profit before tax (PBT) grew by 37.1 per cent year-on-year to N97.28 billion, while profit after tax (PAT) increased by 21.0 per cent to N75.37 billion. Gross earnings rose by 33.2 per cent to N454.94 billion, and non-interest income increased by 27.6% to N101.16 billion, supported by fee-based activities, commodities trading and joint enterprise investments across the Group’s businesses. The Group’s diversification strategy is also gaining traction, with SterlingFi Wealth Management, now in its second year of operations, beginning to contribute to Group earnings and broadening its income streams beyond traditional banking. Total assets rose by 30.4 per cent from year-end 2025 to N5.10 trillion, while net loans and advances to customers increased by 28.8 per cent to N1.82 trillion. Customer deposits rose by 28.7 per cent to N3.84 trillion, and shareholders’ funds increased by 38.8 per cent to N595.2 billion. The Group recorded a post-tax return on average equity (ROAE) of 20.0 per cent and a return on average assets (ROAA) of 2.22 per cent. Commenting on the results, Group Chief Executive Officer, Yemi Odubiyi , said: “Our nine-month performance demonstrates the collective strength of our businesses and the progress we are making towards building a diversified financial services group. Surpassing N5 trillion in total assets is an important milestone, while SterlingFi’s emerging contribution reflects the potential of our expanding financial services portfolio. “The Group’s priority is to translate this growth into sustainable shareholder value through disciplined capital allocation, effective governance and strategic oversight. We will continue to support our businesses in pursuing sustainable growth while maintaining financial resilience and prudent risk management.”

title: APMT Champions Port Modernisation, Collaboration to Drive Inclusive Growth
body: Oluchi Chibuzor APM Terminals Nigeria has underscored the importance of efficient ports, modern infrastructure and stronger public-private collaboration in enabling trade, improving productivity and supporting Nigeria’s economic growth. The call was made at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit (NES #32), held in Abuja under the theme,“Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity.” The Summit brought together leaders from government, the private sector and other stakeholders to advance conversations around Nigeria’s economic development. Speaking at the Summit, Vice President Kashim Shettima, delivering President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s address, reinforced the importance of improving productivity to translate reforms into prosperity. “Our pursuit of prosperity demands greater productivity from every worker, enterprise, and investment,” he said, noting that government would continue efforts to ease regulatory burdens, strengthen transparency and policy predictability, and expand access to finance. During a plenary session, Chief Executive Officer of APM Terminals Nigeria, Koen De Backker reinforced the critical role ports play in facilitating trade and creating economic value. “Our job is to facilitate trade, to be an enabler for cargo to move in and out of the port, and to create wealth and prosperity for the population of Nigeria,” he said. Highlighting capacity constraints within ports as a key challenge, De Backker explained that containers remaining too long within terminals restrict the capacity required to keep cargo moving. He stressed the need to diversify cargo evacuation beyond road transportation by expanding alternatives such as barging and rail. He cited APM Terminals’ logistics centre in the Ibadan area, where export cargo is consolidated, stuffed into containers and moved by rail into the terminal, as an example of how alternative transport links can support cargo flows. De Backker also emphasised the need to modernise Nigeria’s ageing port infrastructure, noting that technology, specialised expertise and investment are essential to increasing capacity and efficiency. Rather than viewing private sector participation simply as privatisation, he described it as an opportunity for “professionalising the infrastructure, modernising, and getting experts in.” He further highlighted collaboration with government agencies, Customs and clearing agents as central to achieving meaningful improvements. Citing the deployment of cargo scanners, De Backker said collaboration with Customs had enabled containers to be scanned rather than relying solely on physical examinations, improving efficiency and security.

title: 50,000 Former Railway Workers Homeless, Face Eviction from Official Quarters, Says ANRSC
body: Sunday Okobi The Association of Nigeria Railway Senior Citizens (ANRSC) has raised the alarm that over 50,000 former workers of the Nigerian Railway Corporation (NRC) are currently homeless, while others are facing eviction from their official quarters due to the refusal of the NRC management to implement a 2004/2005 Monetization Policy of the Federal Government. Addressing transportation journalists over the weekend, the National Chairman of ANRSC, Segun Esan, said: “It is important to mention here that the federal government introduced the Monetization Policy in 2004/2005 for two major reasons. “The first reason is to relieve the federal government of the huge financial burden of maintaining these government quarters, vehicles, and domestic staff across the country. These quarters are to be sold to the occupants on an owner-occupier basis, whether serving or retired, at discounted and affordable prices.” According to him, “The second reason for the promulgation and implementation of this gazetted monetization policy is to use the reality of the existing quarters to provide homes for the federal government workers and their families. “And the White Paper and the SGF Circular Ref. No. SGF/OP/I/S.3/VII/2003 was very clear about the monetization: To convert all government quarters to an owner-occupier basis by selling them to the legal occupants. “That was the purpose. It was a welfare and retirement security policy. It has been fully implemented in all the Ministries, Departments, and Agencies of the federal government, which includes NNPC, CBN, NPA, FAAN, Federal Ministry of Aviation, Department of Meteorological Services, and even in the Judiciary. “Today, Judges and staff of the Judiciary are proud owners of their former official quarters. Their workers have peace after retirement. And we wonder why the Nigerian Railway Corporation is different. Why are railway workers singled out for punishment by its own management? “This is where we must speak with pains, but with facts. The past management of the Nigerian Railway Corporation, by itself, commenced the implementation of some part of the monetization process. They monetized and shared vehicles – official cars- and they monetized furniture, paying furniture allowances to themselves. They benefited robustly from the policy. But when it came to the most important aspect – the quarters where the poor retirees live – they refused to implement it. This is selective justice. You cannot take your own vehicles and furniture under monetization and deny the retirees their quarters under the same policy. That is injustice and oppression. “Successive managements since 2004 have turned our quarters into a cash cow. Our quarters have been sold secretly to third parties, to money-bags and cronies. They have been leased out at exorbitant rates while the legal occupants – retirees – are being evicted. They used the period of interminable litigation as a window to continue selling our heritage.” He said that on January 6, 2016, Justice Babatunde Adejumo, then the President of the National Industrial Court of Nigeria (NICN), in Suit No. NICN/LA/22/2011, delivered a landmark judgment in their favour after being in court for five years. “The court affirmed that we are entitled to own our quarters under the Monetization Policy. Instead of obeying that judgment, NRC Management in 2016 ran to the Court of Appeal and has kept the case there since 2016-10 years down the line now. “In its glorious days, the Nigerian Railway Corporation was the highest employer of labour in Africa, with over 50,000 workers spread across the North, North-East, North-Central, North-West, Western, Eastern and Lagos Districts of the Corporation. Till today, those 50,000 workers have created millions of families all over the country who today form a critical voting population in every state of Nigeria,” he said. Esan added: “It is on the premise of this injustice and deprivations that we appeal to our President and father, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, for help. We know that our President is a compassionate and just leader with a lot of respect for the retirees. “We implore His Excellency to, please, direct the implementation of the monetization policy. The houses already exist – they are the quarters we live in. With the advancement in technology, provision of quarters for civil servants is no longer in vogue all over the world. “The government has no business keeping the quarters of a privatised and already liberalized railway industry to itself. The quarters are to be sold as expressly directed by the policy while the government, through the Corporation, concentrates on providing rail transport services to the nation.”

title: Ogonis Seek Action on 20 Recommendations, Bori State Creation
body: A coalition of Ogoni youth groups has called on President Bola Tinubu and the federal government to stop delaying the implementation of demands arising from the Ogoni dialogue process, insisting that the creation of Bori State must form a central part of the implementation roadmap. The Coalition of Ogoni Youth Groups (COYOG) also warned against what it described as attempts by politicians, privileged individuals and vested interests to hijack the dialogue process for personal, political, and economic benefits. In a statement jointly signed by 17 youth leaders, including Chief Kpakol Aleema Kpakol, President, Ogoni National Youth Congress; Collins Lebeteh Kenneth, its spokesman; Gen. Ikeh Albert Jnr, President General, Khana Youth Assembly; Chief Barineka Tornwe, President, Ogoni General Youth Assembly; Mene Barisi Kenneth Kaabee, President General, PA-Gokana Supreme Youth Council; Ken Nnaa, President, Yorla Oil Field Youth Association; and Nadum Ana-Ana, President, Ogoni Community-Based Youth Leaders Forum, COYOG expressed concern over what it described as political and elite capture of the dialogue process, warning that the collective aspirations of the Ogoni people must not be sacrificed for personal, political or economic interests. It maintained that the dialogue was a collective struggle for justice, environmental restoration, political inclusion, resource control and sustainable development, stressing that its outcome must reflect the aspirations of the Ogoni people rather than the interests of a few individuals. COYOG said the sacrifices made by generations of Ogoni people in the struggle for justice and development must not be undermined by political manoeuvring, selective representation, or undisclosed arrangements. The coalition said: “The Ogoni dialogue process is a collective struggle for justice, environmental restoration, political inclusion, resource control and sustainable development. It must not become the exclusive preserve of a few individuals seeking to negotiate away the collective aspiration of the Ogoni people.” It called on the federal government to provide a clear and documented commitment to implementing the agreed demands through an interim Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). According to the group, the proposed agreement should specify the responsibilities of relevant institutions, implementation timelines, funding arrangements, monitoring mechanisms and public reporting obligations. The coalition also urged Tinubu to establish a representative of the Presidential Implementation Committee with a clearly defined mandate, measurable milestones and sufficient authority to coordinate the implementation of the recommendations. It said the demands contained in the Ogoni Dialogue Committee’s report should not be reduced to political promises or ceremonial declarations of selective implementation. COYOG specifically insisted that the demand for the creation of Bori State must receive explicit and documented attention in the implementation roadmap. It argued that the demand was fundamental to the political inclusion, equitable representation, administrative accessibility and aspirations of the Ogoni people. The coalition said the federal government and relevant constitutional institutions should identify the appropriate pathway for considering the creation of the proposed state in accordance with the constitutional procedures governing state creation in Nigeria. It added that the Bori State demand must not be ignored, indefinitely postponed, or used as a bargaining instrument by political interests. “For COYOG, the demand for Bori State is a fundamental question of political inclusion, equitable representation, administrative accessibility and the aspirations of the Ogoni people. “Any genuine effort to address the Ogoni question must engage this demand openly and seriously alongside the other provisions of the Ogoni Bill of Rights and the 20 demands contained in the Dialogue Committee’s report,” the statement said. The coalition’s position came amid concerns over the leadership structure of the Ogoni Dialogue Committee (ODC), following a statement reportedly credited to Rev. Fr. Pius Kii during the service of songs for late Mrs. Rosemary Kobani at Corpus Christi Cathedral, Port Harcour,t in Rivers State recently. According to COYOG, Senator Olaka Wogu was reportedly recognised as the leader of the ODC during the event. However, the youth groups disputed the description, insisting that Wogu was a member of the committee’s Harmonisation Subcommittee and not the chairman or leader of the Central Ogoni Dialogue Committee. They identified Professor Don Baridam as the leader of the central committee, saying his leadership and mandate should be respected by all stakeholders. The coalition explained that the Harmonisation Subcommittee was established to harmonise reports and recommendations from the Tactical and Technical Committees before presenting its work through the appropriate structure of the ODC. It said membership of the subcommittee did not confer the authority to assume the leadership of the central committee or independently speak on its behalf. “We respect Senator Olaka Wogu as a political leader and member of the dialogue structure. However, no individual, irrespective of political status or influence, should place himself above the established institutional framework of the ODC,” the statement added. COYOG cautioned Wogu against public conduct or representations that could create confusion about the committee’s leadership. It also urged religious leaders and other public figures to verify institutional positions before making pronouncements capable of misleading the Ogoni people. The coalition further called on the ODC leadership, under Professor Baridam, to strengthen its public communication and provide regular, accurate and comprehensive updates on the progress of the dialogue. It specifically asked the committee to communicate the outcome of its harmonisation exercise, explain the decisions reached, identify outstanding issues and publish a roadmap for implementation. On the reported $300million fund, the youth groups said the Ogoni people deserved verifiable answers concerning the source, status and intended purpose of the money, as well as the arrangements for its management and accountability. They argued that questions surrounding public-interest funds should not be suppressed, politicised or used as an excuse to frustrate the broader dialogue process. “Transparency must be non-negotiable,” the coalition said, adding that accountability and the successful conclusion of the dialogue were not mutually exclusive. The youth groups urged Ogoni political leaders, traditional rulers, community institutions, civil society organisations, women’s groups and other youth formations to remain united and vigilant in protecting the collective interests of the people. They recalled that the Ogoni people had endured decades of environmental devastation, political marginalisation and unmet expectations, arguing that the credibility of the current dialogue would ultimately depend on the implementation of agreed commitments. According to the coalition, the success of the process should not be measured by the number of meetings held, the personalities involved or public statements issued, but by concrete commitments fulfilled, environmental damage addressed, political demands advanced and improvements in the living conditions of ordinary Ogoni people. COYOG reaffirmed its commitment to peaceful advocacy, constructive engagement and democratic mobilisation, while pledging to continue holding relevant institutions accountable for their commitments. “The Ogoni dialogue belongs to the Ogoni people. Its outcomes must serve the Ogoni people. Its implementation must be transparent, inclusive, and measurable. “No political interest, individual or elite group, is greater than the collective future of Ogoni land,” the statement said.

title: Coronation Pushes Africa’s Private Capital, Infrastructure Financing Agenda
body: Nume Ekeghe Coronation Group is set to advance discussions on mobilising domestic capital and expanding institutional investors’ participation in infrastructure financing at the Africa Financial Summit (AFIS) 2026, as two of its senior executives prepare to share insights on unlocking private investment for the continent’s development. Slated to hold from 3 to 4 November 2026 in Luanda, Angola, AFIS will convene senior financial services executives, policymakers, regulators and investors under the theme “Forging Africa’s Financial Powerhouse”. Coronation’s participation reflects its commitment to strengthening African financial markets and connecting capital to productive opportunities that support sustainable wealth creation. Managing Partner of Coronation Capital, Kayode Akindele, will share insight on the panel themed, “The Growth Reset: Crowding in Private Capital as the Era of Easy Globalisation Unwinds.” Moderated by Ntaoleng Lechela of Business Day TV and SAfm, the discussion will feature Mustafa Rawji of Rawbank, Dr Agostinho Kapaia of OPAIA Group, Sergio Pimenta of Africa50 and Victor Cardoso of BAI. The panel will examine how African economies can attract private investment amid foreign exchange restrictions, regulatory complexities and fragmented financial markets. Discussions will explore capital market reforms, local-currency instruments, collaboration across financial institutions, macro-economic imperatives and measures to facilitate cross-border investment. Commenting on the issues the panel will address, Kayode Akindele, said: “Africa’s challenge is not simply to attract more and sustainable capital, but to build financial markets that can effectively mobilisedomestic savings and channel them into productive, long-term investment. This requires stronger institutions, deeper and more efficient capital markets and investment instruments that can act as a store of value in local currencies. “By improving the way capital is raised, allocated and deployed especially for the longer term we can create a more conducive environment for businesses to grow, jobs to be created, infrastructure to develop and African economiespowered majorly by domestic capital.” Also Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Coronation Insurance, Olamide Olajolo will participate in a strategic roundtable, “Beyond a 1 per cent Infrastructure Allocation: How Can Insurers Join the Blended Finance Mix?” Moderated by Asmae Kaddouri of Africa Business+, the session will feature Sameh Wahba of the International Finance Corporation, Richard Lowe of Activa Group, Helena Chicuba of ENSA and Stéphane Defo of Horus Investment Group. The roundtable will examine how insurers can increase their participation in infrastructure financing through blended finance, strategic partnerships and investment structures that balance risk and return. It will also consider the regulatory and market conditions needed to make infrastructure investments more viable for long-term institutional capital. On the potential role of insurance capital in infrastructure development, Olajolo, said: “Insurers have the potential to play a greater role in financing Africa’s infrastructure because their long-term investment horizons can help support projects with extended funding needs. Unlocking this potential will require more than a willingness to invest. Infrastructure opportunities must offer appropriate risk-adjusted returns, supported by sound project preparation, enabling regulation and structures that allocate risk effectively. Through collaboration among insurers, governments, development finance institutions and private investors, blended finance can help make more projects investable and broaden the pool of capital available for Africa’s development.” Together, the two discussions address a critical priority for Africa’s financial ecosystem: mobilising capital is only part of the challenge; ensuring that it reaches viable businesses, infrastructure and other productive investments is equally important.

title: U.S. sanctions push Cuba to the brink, with healthcare at risk
body: Cuban doctors rushed a 2-month-old baby, dehydrated and suffering from malnutrition, to the intensive care unit. He weighed less than 5 pounds and had been taken to William Soler Pediatric Hospital in Havana, Cuba, by protective services after being abandoned. After he was stabilized, the 2-month-old boy needed specialized formulas, many of which come from the United States, according to Dr. Alejandro Chong, head of the ICU. "We have to make do with formulas made from malanga — a starchy root vegetable — and chicken," Chong said. Doctors in Cuba make compromises like that on every shift. Just 90 miles from the U.S., Cuba has always imported much of what it needs — now new restrictions are making it harder to import food and medical supplies. Cuba has been under a trade embargo with the U.S. for decades, but now President Trump has tightened the vice, threatening to sanction those who do business with the Cuban regime. Washington says it does not intend to restrict food and medical supplies, but many foreign companies, fearful of U.S. penalties, won't sell them to Cuba. U.S.-Cuba conflict impact on medical care Cuba's problems long predate the Trump administration's new sanctions. For decades, the U.S. says the regime mismanaged Cuba's economy and let its infrastructure crumble.But only a single tanker of oil has reached the Caribbean island since early January, according to Cuban officials, which has crippled the country's electrical grid. A generator quickly turns on at William Soler Pediatric Hospital, but the moment between when the electricity goes off and the generator turns on can be critical for medical care."Those few seconds might seem insignificant to someone outside the medical field, but they're precious seconds when you're dealing with a patient under general anesthesia or a patient on a ventilator in the intensive care unit," Chong said.Doctors said when the generators fail, they've had to finish surgeries using the light from their cellphones. If ventilators stop working, they pump oxygen for critical patients by hand. Because it's exhausting and poorly paid work, a huge number of doctors have left the profession or the country itself. Many who've stayed have taken second jobs just to get by, including Chong. He makes more money at the food stand he owns than he does running the ICU.Dr. Lórien Rodríguez, a second-year resident in pediatric surgery, supports herself by working as a radio announcer. "There are fewer personnel, fewer resources, and it makes all the work we're doing much more difficult," she said. Doctors told 60 Minutes cancer drugs, anesthetics and lab equipment are all in critically short supply. Rodríguez said doctors are "constantly" forced to tell patients they're unable to help because of the issues. When 60 Minutes visited, doctors said a toddler had been waiting 68 days for an artificial lung machine component critical to surgery she needed, which normally had a wait time of two days. Paloma Blanco, a dancer with the National Ballet of Cuba, is 8 months pregnant with her first baby. She said she trusts the doctors, but she's nervous about the lack of supplies. Blanco said she has asked friends in the U.S. to send surgical supplies just in case she needs a cesarean section. Carlos Fernández de Cossío, Cuba's deputy foreign minister and a main negotiator with the U.S., said he owes it to families "to do as much as we can to ease the situation that the population faces."Conflict between U.S., Cuba goes back decadesCuba has been under communist rule since the 1960s. The government employs most of the country's workers and runs the hospitals and schools. Opposition parties are illegal. Cuba's leaders have jailed critics, limited free speech and Washington says the regime has hoarded billions of dollars.Since former leader Fidel Castro seized power back in 1959, nearly every American administration has tried to force change in Havana.For decades, a U.S. embargo has cut the island off from American trade. Washington blames the crisis in Cuba on Havana, saying a corrupt communist regime has mismanaged the country for decades. Havana blames Washington, saying U.S. policies are designed to turn Cuba into a failed state. "The United States has no legitimacy to what they're claiming. They just have brutal power against the whole population of another country. That is criminal," de Cossío said. In his second term, Mr. Trump has turned up the rhetoric. His administration wants Havana to know there are "no escape valves," as Secretary of State Marco Rubio previously told Axios, and has even threatened potential military action in Cuba. "Actually, what we're gonna do with Cuba is we're gonna come back from Iran, those beautiful ships will pass Cuba. We'll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They'll raise up their hands and then we're gonna send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal," Mr. Trump said at an event last month.Rubio, the son of Cuban immigrants, has made regime change the signature issue of his career and, as secretary of state, turned it into one of the administration's priorities.Rubio declined a request for an interview, but in a statement, a spokesman said, "The failing Cuban regime continues to blame the United States and everyone else for their own incompetence and corruption," adding, "They hide billions in overseas bank accounts instead of investing in electricity, infrastructure … and the daily needs of its people."Negotiations between the U.S. and Cuba stalled earlier this year. Last week, tensions exploded into public view during a speech by Mike Waltz, the U.S. ambassador to the U.N. Cuban officials confronted him, and one Cuban diplomat was expelled from the U.S.Can there be change?For most Cubans, staples are out of reach. Eggs can cost more than a month's salary. That reality has forced people to find their own solutions, such as buying medicine at a black market.De Cossío blames the U.S. for Cuba's worsening crisis, but said, "Every government has responsibility for their people.""The unique position of Cuba is that in addition to whatever responsibility the government has, it has an external, very powerful factor having an influence in the reality of the population," he added. "But our government has a lot of responsibility because there could be decisions that could have been better."Cuba has also lost powerful benefactors. First, it was the Soviet Union. Much more recently, it was Venezuela. When the U.S. captured the Venezuelan president, Nicolás Maduro, on Jan. 3, 2026, Cuba lost its main oil supplier. This year, Cuba made the biggest economic reforms in more than six decades, including dropping its monopolies on fuel, banking and pharmacies. U.S. companies have started exporting fuel to Cuba's private sector. But it's prohibitively expensive. Asked why Cuba had not opted for political reforms, de Cossío said, "I believe that rather than in Cuba, it is in the U.S. where it should be political reform. Cuba does not threaten the U.S. or any country."When it comes to its own country, Cuba has cracked down on dissidents; almost no one 60 Minutes met was willing to openly criticize the Cuban government. De Cossío sees the impasse with the U.S. ending with "a change of attitude from the United States."We see every reason for that to occur. What we see no reason is for the U.S. government to continue to punish the whole population of a country," he said. "How long is that sustainable? How acceptable is that? Just because power exists in the hands of the United States. Does everybody have to bend to that?"This weekend, 60 Minutes checked in with Dr. Chong, and he said the baby 60 Minutes saw being treated during a hospital visit suffered respiratory complications and was readmitted to the ICU, where he died on Thursday.

title: Russian Emergencies Ministry’s mobile app hit by massive cyberattack
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. The mobile application of the Russian Emergencies Ministry has been subjected to a massive cyberattack, which resulted in the dissemination of false information regarding a supposed threat to the public, the ministry’s press service reported.
"The Russian Emergencies Ministry’s mobile app has been hit by a massive cyberattack, allowing perpetrators to send out fake information to the public," the ministry stated.
Efforts are currently underway to address the vulnerability in the mobile app and restore its normal operation.

title: Democratic Rep. Stevens endorses GOP candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan US Senate race
body:
Stevens and Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed have feuded publicly recently.
Democratic U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens has endorsed Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan's race for the U.S. Senate against Democratic nominee Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, she said Sunday – a stunning move after Stevens had previously said she would support El-Sayed.
“Hey Michigan, as you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said that I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away. And he's right, and that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today. I don't belong in Abdul's campaign,” Stevens said in part in a video posted on social media on Sunday .
El-Sayed and Stevens faced off in an acrimonious primary, but had seemingly mended fences afterward. However, in recent days a new dispute spilled out into the open after Stevens had asked El-Sayed to disavow an ad from an outside group that she said was antisemitic. Stevens' fiancé, Jason Turkish, has also said he plans to vote for Mike Rogers, and attended an event with Mike Rogers and Sen. Ted Cruz last week.
In a joint press conference after the endorsement, Stevens defended the decision as one that is right for Michigan, adding that it was about standing "with country."
Stevens said that “90% of the votes I'm going to cast are going to be for Democrats. My vote for Senate, I am just one vote, as is every Michigander. My vote for Senate is going to be with Mike Rogers. And I will tell you why. Because we have to stand with country."
She said El-Sayed boxed her out of his campaign. "I did endorse the Democratic nominee, and he chose to close his campaign by saying I wasn't welcome… This is about looking in the mirror about how real Democrats for Rogers are."
Stevens also attended a Black church service on Sunday in Detroit with Rogers. A Rogers campaign representative posted a photo on X Sunday morning of Stevens and Rogers standing side-by-side at the service.
As recently as last week, Stevens told CNN that she would vote for El-Sayed, saying "Of course I'm voting, you know, for our Democratic nominee for Senate. I'm voting for the Democratic ticket."
El-Sayed attended a Black church service at a different church in Detroit on Sunday. Stevens had been previously expected to appear with him, but the joint appearance was thrown into doubt after the newfound dispute broke out into the open.
"At the end of the day, I actually don't think about Haley Stevens," El-Sayed said of her endorsement Sunday in remarks to the press after the service, alongside Rep. Jim Clyburn (D-S.C), who attended the service with him.
“So I have a sense that you all are here today because of the decisions of somebody who's not here right now. Am I right about that?" El-Sayed said. "But I'm just going to tell you, this is a state of 10 million people who deserve a lot better from the government. I'm a lot more focused on the 9,999,998 that are not the ones you guys are talking about,” he went on, bringing up gas prices, grocery costs, and air and water quality as examples of issues Michigan voters are dealing with.
President Donald Trump lavished praise on Stevens in a social media post Sunday for endorsing Rogers, saying in part that Stevens showed “great and almost unprecedented loyalty” to Michigan in doing so.
But Stevens' fellow Democrats were swift to condemn her endorsement.
"This is a despicable betrayal from Rep. Stevens," Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York wrote in a post on X . "Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors."
“We are dismayed that Congresswoman Haley Stevens has revealed herself to be a sellout who used Black Michiganders for a political stunt," Democratic National Committee Black Caucus Chair Virgie Rollins said in a statement released by the Michigan Democratic Party. "Congresswoman Stevens has lost her way, and Michiganders know that Mike Rogers is a shill for Trump and has failed Michigan. We are ready to elect Abdul on Tuesday.”
"Michiganders ... want leaders focused on making their lives more affordable. That's what they're talking about, not Congresswoman Stevens' continued efforts to get attention,” Michigan Democratic Rep. Debbie Dingell wrote in a statement on X , adding, "we must stay focused on electing Democrats up and down the ballot, and that includes electing Abdul El-Sayed as Michigan's next Senator."

title: Haredi groom arrested days after wedding for evading draft, sentenced to 20 days in military prison
body: Haredi (ultra-Orthodox) yeshiva student Yaari Lieberman, who married just days earlier, was arrested by IDF Military Police in front of his wife on Sunday while the couple was on their way to a family celebration marking their wedding. Lieberman was transferred to a military prison and sentenced to 20 days in jail by a military court, sparking outrage among senior haredi political figures who demanded his immediate release.The incident is expected to trigger violent demonstrations in the coming days.The arrest took place as the newlyweds got off a bus on their way to a Sheva Brachot celebration, one of the festive meals traditionally held in honor of Jewish couples during the week following their wedding.According to reports, the Military Police officers who arrived at the scene were in civilian clothes and not wearing identification badges.  The officers reportedly tracked Lieberman through his cellphone's location. It was also alleged that the officers did not identify themselves as Military Police to his wife, leaving her fearing that her husband had been kidnapped.Lieberman was taken from the scene and transferred to a military prison.Goldknopf blames Netanyahu for arrest of yeshiva studentAgudat Yisrael chairman MK Yitzhak Goldknopf strongly condemned the arrest, accusing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of responsibility for the situation facing yeshiva students."The arrest of a young groom in front of his bride in the midst of the Sheva Brachot festival is a new low in the hunt against Torah scholars," Goldknopf said."The obsessive pursuit of yeshiva students, whose only sin is Torah study, has crossed every line of humanity and sensitivity. This shameful arrest is a disgrace to the Jewish state. I demand the groom's immediate release."Goldknopf also directed his criticism at Netanyahu, accusing him of failing to fulfill his commitment to advance legislation regulating the status of yeshiva students."Prime Minister Netanyahu has not been able to keep his promise to pass a law that will regulate the status of yeshiva students, and the result is the disgraceful arrests we are witnessing. The responsibility for this situation lies on his shoulders," he said.United Torah Judaism chairman MK Yaakov Asher also appealed to the defense minister on Sunday, demanding that he intervene to secure Lieberman's immediate release."This is not a totalitarian state and not a police state. Arresting a son-in-law in the midst of his happy days is an opaqueness that knows no bounds. I demanded that the Defense Minister act for his immediate release and return him to his family and his happiness," Asher said.Shas chairman MK Yinon Azoulay also moved to sign an urgent petition calling on the defense minister to secure the immediate release of the newlywed yeshiva student.Previous arrest attempt thwarted by protestersSunday's arrest was not the first attempt by Military Police to detain Lieberman.On October 6, Military Police arrived at his parents' home in Modi'in in an attempt to arrest him. However, they encountered resistance from protesters who gathered outside the residence.Crowds assembled near the house and demonstrated against the attempted arrest. After approximately two hours, the protesters reportedly succeeded in preventing Lieberman from being taken into custody.Fears of escalation as haredi opposition to IDF draft intensifiesLieberman's arrest is expected to lead to violent demonstrations in the coming days, amid growing opposition within the haredi community to the arrest of yeshiva students as part of the enforcement of the mandatory IDF draft.The incident comes amid the ongoing controversy surrounding the military draft of ultra-Orthodox men and the absence of legislation regulating the military service status of yeshiva students.While the defense establishment continues to enforce mandatory conscription requirements, representatives of the haredi parties are demanding legislation that would regulate the status of yeshiva students and prevent further arrests.

title: Russian SRG activity along Ukraine’s northern border drops significantly – military spox
body:
Andrii Demchenko, Spokesperson for the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine, said this during a televised broadcast, according to Ukrinform.
Demchenko noted that Russian SRGs attempt to infiltrate Ukrainian territory to gather intelligence on defensive positions, attack Ukrainian defenders’ positions and lay mines in the area.
“Overall, the activity of Russian SRGs has decreased significantly in recent times. However, there was a period when such groups were active in both Chernihiv and Sumy regions,” he said.
The spokesperson also noted that Russian forces had previously tried to use infiltrations by SRGs for information operations, including making claims that they had allegedly captured territory or established control over it. title: Verstappen wins Formula 1 Mexican Grand Prix
body:
MEXICO CITY, November 2. /TASS/. Red Bull’s Dutch racing driver Max Verstappen won the Mexican Grand Prix, the 19th round of the 2026 Formula 1 World Championship, held at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City.
Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari finished second, while Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli completed the podium in third place.
Needing only a ninth-place finish to seal the championship, the 20-year-old Italian clinched his historic debut Formula 1 title. Antonelli now tops the drivers' standings with 380 points, followed by Verstappen (261) and Hamilton (259).
In the Constructors' Championship, Mercedes maintains its lead with 630 points and could secure the team title at the next race. Ferrari (504) remains the only team capable of catching the leaders.
The next round of the championship is scheduled to take place in Brazil from November 6 to 8.

title: Pro-Israel Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican Rogers in Michigan US Senate race
body: Michigan pro-Israel Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over her own party's nominee, Abdul El-Sayed, for US Senate on Sunday, telling reporters, “We can't stand with hate.”The surprise move two days before Election Day further exacerbated the growing fracture between Zionist Jewish communities and the Democratic Party, as El-Sayed's critical rhetoric on Israel has alienated many Jewish voters in a state that could decide control of the chamber.  Jewish Democrat leaders were among the voices attacking Stevens, who ran against El-Sayed in the Democratic primary for the seat, following her announcement. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called it “a despicable betrayal.” President Donald Trump, on his social network Truth Social, celebrated Stevens' endorsement as “bravery.”The endorsement capped a whirlwind week for Stevens, whose Jewish fiancée, Democratic megadonor Jason Turkish, announced days earlier he would also be supporting Rogers. Until Sunday, Stevens had publicly claimed to be in El-Sayed's camp and had been scheduled to attend a get-out-the-vote Detroit church event Sunday with him and Black Democratic leaders.El-Sayed refuses to condemn ad blaming Israel for grocery prices sparking conflictBut on Friday, she publicly urged El-Sayed to repudiate an outside PAC ad that had blamed Israel for the rising price of groceries as a condition of appearing with his campaign. When El-Sayed refused, instead calling out the pro-Israel lobby AIPAC's spending heavily in favor of Stevens in the primary, cracks between their camps spilled out into the open.By Sunday, it was an earlier antisemitism-related grievance Stevens referenced in rescinding her endorsement of the Democratic candidate. She named El-Sayed's spring campaign appearances with anti-Israel streamer Hasan Piker on college campuses as a key reason why she was switching her endorsement. “I don't belong in Abdul's campaign. I do not stand with Hasan Piker, who gets trafficked on our college campuses,” the congresswoman said in a video message announcing her Rogers endorsement, saying that “education is on the ballot.” Appearing later in a brief press conference with Rogers, she again referenced the streamer: “We can't stand with hate. We can't stand with Hasan Piker.”Rogers, standing next to Stevens, invoked darker messaging when referencing the PAC ad. “Blaming a certain group of people for your problems, that sounds like 1933,” he said. “And it has consequences for those communities. Jewish Democrats are calling me, afraid for their children to stay in the state of Michigan.”Piker, on social media, called Stevens “a self interested striver who's weirdly obsessed with Israel and has been paid handsomely for this strange obsession.” El-Sayed has distanced himself multiple times from Piker since they campaigned together in the primary, including this week after Piker compared a heavily Jewish Michigan suburb to “a KKK neighborhood.”A Jewish Telegraphic Agency request for comment to the Stevens-Turkish camp was not immediately returned. Stevens, who represents a heavily Jewish district in suburban Detroit, told The New York Times this weekend that she was considering converting to Judaism for their wedding.El-Sayed, in his own press conference Sunday, dismissed Stevens' move and preemptively warned reporters not to ask him about it. “At the end of the day I actually don't think about Haley Stevens,” he said.He did, however, push back on the idea that a Rogers endorsement was standing against hate.“If you are somebody who believes that we should stand up to hate, and you have watched this last campaign, I think we probably would not want to support Mike Rogers and Donald Trump and JD Vance,” he said. The GOP's messaging against El-Sayed has been criticized for leaning heavily into stoking fears about Islam.Stevens' staff push back against endorsementStevens insisted she was “still a very proud Democrat.” Yet many of her staff, including her chief of staff, resigned en masse following her move Sunday. Arik Wolk, Stevens' former campaign spokesperson, wrote on X that her endorsement was “ridiculous and pathetic.”Some Jewish Democrats also heavily criticized Stevens on Sunday, saying she was hurting the party and the country. “Anyone who makes an election this important about themselves, and not Michiganders and our democracy, should think hard about whether they are serving the greater good,” moderate Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin, who is Jewish and who has hit the campaign trail with El-Sayed, wrote on X.J Street, the liberal pro-Israel lobby that did not endorse El-Sayed, said Stevens was “weaponizing real fears about rising antisemitism to further her own grievances.”The Jewish Democratic Council of America, an organizing body for Jewish interests in the Democratic Party, had pointedly not endorsed El-Sayed during the campaign. Yet following Stevens' announcement, its CEO Halie Soifer wrote, “A vote for any Republican in 2026 is a vote for Donald Trump.”

title: Tilly Akua Nipaa appointed Communications Director of RANA
body: The Rights Accountability Network Africa (RANA) has appointed Ghanaian media personality and public relations professional Matilda Mensah Marfo, popularly known as Tilly Akua Nipaa, as its Communications Director. The appointment, announced on Sunday, November 1, 2026, is aimed at strengthening the organisation’s institutional communications, expanding public engagement and making human rights advocacy more accessible to citizens across Ghana and the African continent. Tilly Akua Nipaa has built a career in broadcasting, corporate communications, media relations, brand storytelling and stakeholder engagement. She has worked as a broadcaster and panellist on platforms under Despite Media and the Multimedia Group. She currently serves as Head of Public Relations and Marketing at Crux Global, where she leads the company’s strategic communications and marketing initiatives. Her professional experience also includes leading the 2025 Artist of the Year campaign for musician King Promise at the Telecel Ghana Music Awards and contributing to projects associated with the Basketball Africa League (BAL). Tilly holds a degree in Psychology, English and Theatre Arts from the University of Ghana. She is also preparing to graduate with a Master’s degree in Public Relations and Marketing. In addition to her professional responsibilities, she serves as the 2026 General Secretary of the Graduate Students’ Association of Ghana at the University of Media, Arts and Communication (GRASAG-UNIMAC). In her new position, she will oversee RANA’s communications strategy, media relations, digital engagement and public awareness initiatives. A key part of her mandate will be to translate the organisation’s research, legal interventions and advocacy activities into accessible information to improve public understanding of human rights, encourage civic participation and promote institutional accountability. RANA said effective communication was an essential part of protecting human rights, noting that citizens needed to understand their rights, recognise threats to them and know how to seek appropriate remedies. The organisation expressed confidence that her experience and strategic communications expertise would strengthen its advocacy and public engagement efforts.

title: OPEC+ keeps December oil output targets steady ahead of tougher call for 2027
body: OPEC+ oil-producing countries kept December production targets steady on Sunday, confirming expectations that the group will not make further policy adjustments until next year, as it continues to struggle with export disruptions from the Iran war . Seven core OPEC+ members — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman — made the decision in ​an online meeting on Sunday, OPEC said in a statement. While Gulf members have been boosting exports disrupted for months by the conflict, most are still pumping well below their targets. OPEC+ comprises the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia. Only the seven members — plus ​the United Arab Emirates until it quit OPEC in May — have been involved in monthly output decisions in recent ​years. All members of the 21-country group are due to meet on November 29, when analysts expect it will decide 2027 quotas. “Today’s decision was the easy one,” said Jorge Leon, an analyst at Rystad. “The much more important test comes at the November 29 ​ministerial meeting, when OPEC+ will decide its 2027 production framework.” Oil prices jumped more than 2% on Friday, with Brent ​crude settling at almost $118 a barrel, the highest since April, as traders braced for a potential escalation in the Iran war ‌after ⁠the US midterm elections. The International Energy Agency, opens new tab and other forecasters have warned of excess supply in 2027 should Gulf flows return to normal. “OPEC+ faces an extremely difficult call for 2027,” Leon added. “The group has to plan around huge uncertainty over the US-Iran war, the pace of recovery through the Strait of Hormuz, and the size of the surplus that ​could emerge once disrupted ​barrels return.” OIL CAPACITY REVIEW IN ⁠FOCUS The seven members have been boosting output targets for much of 2026 and in September completed the phased rollback of a 1.65 million-barrel-per-day supply cut first agreed in ​2023. At earlier meetings, they kept the targets steady for October and November . OPEC+ still has one ​more layer ⁠of production cuts of about 2 million bpd covering most members through the end of 2026. The group needs to complete a review of members’ production capacity during the fourth quarter before setting the 2027 baselines that will determine future quotas ⁠and shape ​plans to unwind those cuts, sources have said. The Iran war has ​disrupted projects to expand capacity across the Middle East, throwing estimates of future production potential into uncertainty, Reuters reported in October. As a result, the ​review is now expected to be completed by mid-November.

title: Minister backs 2027 fixed election date as Elections Alberta suggests change
body:
Alberta’s justice minister is pouring cold water on Elections Alberta’s request to delay the next provincial election as concerns over changes to electoral boundaries continue.
In a letter to Elections Alberta, Justice Minister Mickey Amery said the government has “no intention of changing” the date of the provincial election, which is legislated to take place on or before Oct. 18, 2027.
“Alberta’s fixed election date is established by law and provides Albertans with certainty and predictability concerning the democratic process,” wrote Amery.
His letter was in response to Chief Electoral Officer Gordon McClure, who wrote to Speaker Ric McIver suggesting the election either be held with the current electoral boundaries or be postponed.
McClure said in a letter, shared by the Opposition NDP, that either option would give the elections body sufficient time to hold the vote with integrity and safeguards in place.
A contentious report is set to be released this week on new electoral boundaries that the NDP previously said amount to gerrymandering in two cities in southern Alberta – Lethbridge and Calgary.
Gerrymandering, a practice more often seen in the U.S. than in Canada, involves designing voting districts not to reflect geography or population patterns, but to concentrate or fragment voters to benefit a political party.
Though the report has yet to be released, Opposition Leader Naheed Nenshi made the gerrymandering allegation after he was briefed on the report.
Two members of the committee that wrote the report also said the suggested ridings draw a line between rural and urban voters.
The report has been put before an all-party legislative committee and is set to be tabled Monday in the legislature. But McClure cautioned that disagreements could create delays.
A typical provincial vote, McClure said, requires up to 18 months of preparations. He added his agency has been stretched thin.
Amery argued in his letter that the legislature will consider the full report and determine the final electoral boundaries before the end of the fall sitting.
“That timetable will provide your office with approximately 320 days (about 11 full months) to prepare for and administer the next provincial election,” Amery wrote.
He added Alberta law doesn’t guarantee Elections Alberta “lengthy advance notice” of a general election.
In 2024, Smith’s government moved the fixed election date every four years from May to October to avoid clashing with major natural disasters like wildfires or floods which are more common in the spring in Alberta.

title: Nigeria reports two suspected Ebola cases in northeast region
body: Health authorities in Nigeria are investigating two suspected Ebola cases in ​the country’s northeast region, the Nigeria Centre for Disease ‌Control and Prevention said on Saturday. Officials said the two individuals have been isolated while they carry out contact identification, listing, and laboratory testing in a post on X. The cases remain suspected and confirmation ⁠is subject to laboratory results, the post added. Nigeria ​confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a ​decade last week in a Swiss woman who had travelled to Uganda and then returned to the capital, Abuja, in ​central Nigeria. She and her husband were evacuated to ​Switzerland on Monday. The two additional cases, if confirmed, could mean ‌that ⁠the disease has spread within Nigeria, which would be a major public health concern. Authorities did not say whether they believed they were linked to the first case. The centre ⁠of Africa’s Ebola outbreak is in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where more than 5,000 ​people have died since it was ​declared ⁠in May. Kenya and Uganda have also reported cases. No approved treatments or vaccines exist to combat the rare Bundibugyo species behind ​the Congo outbreak.

title: DOJ urges sanctions for database analysis critical of its noncitizen voting claims
body:
The Justice Department is urging a federal judge to consider whether to hold an immigrant rights group in contempt of court for disclosing the results of its analysis of a dataset of alleged noncitizens registered to vote in California
WASHINGTON -- The Justice Department on Sunday defended the accuracy of a list of what it says are more than 20,000 suspected noncitizens registered to vote in California and suggested that a federal judge consider whether an immigrant rights group and its lawyers should face contempt charges after they published an analysis of the names.
On Friday, U.S. District Court Chief Judge James Boasberg allowed the Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights, or CHIRLA, access to federal government data on 20,000 people the Trump administration alleges are noncitizen voters in California. Boasberg, based in Washington, D.C., ordered the plaintiffs not to disclose any names on the list and use the data only for their arguments about why they have legal standing to challenge the Trump administration's use of it.
On Saturday, attorneys for the immigrant rights group filed court papers revealing that their analysis found more than 40% of the people on the list do not appear in the state's voter file. It also identified 22 people on the list who were likely naturalized U.S. citizens while saying that thousands more U.S. citizens appeared to be on it, as well.
The Justice Department said in a filing Sunday that the analysis by the immigrant rights group had nothing to do with the group's legal standing and therefore violated Boasberg's order.
“The report’s political grandstanding about alleged inaccuracies that purportedly impact California voters generally, or comparisons between the government’s list and the full ‘California voter file,’ has no relevance to whether the particular plaintiffs in this case have standing,” it said.
The filing also suggested Boasberg refer the matter to the Justice Department for investigation for possible criminal contempt of court.
Alberto Lammers, a spokesman for the University of California, Los Angeles' Voting Rights Project, which filed the case and did the data analysis for the immigrant rights group, said in an emailed statement: “Plaintiffs’ counsel and their experts fully complied with the Court’s orders.”
In a separate case, the Justice Department on Sunday also appealed a decision from Friday night by U.S. District Court Judge Trina L. Thompson. The ruling by the San Francisco-based judge barred the department from demanding that election offices remove possible noncitizens from voter rolls, separate their ballots or threaten legal action. The Justice Department has noted that Thompson ruled before the federal government was able to file its initial arguments.
Thompson scheduled a Monday hearing on the appeal.
That case is one of many the Trump administration has lost in its battle over its lists of alleged noncitizen voters . A federal judge in California rejected its demand that election officials there be forced to separate ballots cast by those voters, writing that such last-minute orders could “wreak havoc” on the state's election. Two appellate judges agreed .
California election officials also contend the list is riddled with errors and say they have no way to do the painstaking work required by law to remove voters from the rolls in the days before the election. People attest to being U.S. citizens when they register to vote and risk felony prosecution if they cast a ballot when they are not eligible.
The administration has said its list was carefully compiled from the state's own voter registration data and compared to federal citizenship records. The Justice Department issued a series of subpoenas for election offices in California and warned election officials who knowingly let noncitizens vote that they could face criminal charges.

title: Serbia’s REC releases results from 100% of polling stations in snap parliamentary vote
body:
BELGRADE, November 2. /TASS/. The Republic Electoral Commission (REC) of Serbia has released the final results from 100% of polling stations in the country’s snap parliamentary elections, confirming a victory for the Student List movement with 53.01% of the vote.
The United Serbia coalition of former President Aleksandar Vucic secured 38.98%. No other political parties managed to clear the 3% electoral threshold.
The newly elected parliament will also include several lawmakers representing national minorities, who are exempt from the threshold requirement.
On Sunday, repeat voting was held at 53 polling stations nationwide following a directive by the REC.
The snap elections for Serbia's unicameral parliament, the National Assembly, took place on October 25. Vucic had previously conceded defeat and announced his transition into the opposition.

title: Russia in talks with four African states on large nuclear power plants, Rosatom says
body: Russia is ready to supply African countries with nuclear power plants of various sizes and configurations and is ​in talks with four countries on large nuclear projects, ‌the head of the state nuclear corporation Rosatom said on Friday. Rosatom Chief Executive Alexei Likhachev said the company was discussing building large nuclear power plants with Uganda, Ghana, Ethiopia and Egypt. “Our partnership ​is based on the principle that Africa is diverse, ⁠and we have a tailored approach for each country that ​goes beyond a single project,” Likhachev said. Nuclear cooperation was among the ​topics discussed at the third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow this week, attended by representatives from about 50 African countries, including heads of state and government. Director General of Russia’s State Atomic Energy Corporation Rosatom Alexei Likhachev The forum, ​launched in 2019, is part of Russia’s efforts to deepen ​its political and economic ties with Africa. After the summit, Russian President Vladimir ‌Putin ⁠said African countries had shown strong interest in nuclear power plants, small-scale nuclear technologies and nuclear applications in medicine and agriculture. Likhachev said nine African countries had expressed “significant interest” in Rosatom’s floating nuclear ​power plant technology, ​which the ⁠company has promoted as way for coastal countries to enter the nuclear power sector. He said detailed negotiations are underway with Egypt, Tanzania, Togo and ​Namibia. Africa ⁠has only one operating nuclear power plant, South Africa’s Koeberg facility, which was built using French technology and entered service in the ⁠mid-1980s. In Egypt, Rosatom is building the country’s first nuclear power plant, the four-reactor El Dabaa project, and is discussing a possible expansion to six reactors.

title: Police disperse protesters after demonstration turns violent in Jerusalem
body: Police moved to disperse protesters in Jerusalem on Sunday evening after a demonstration escalated into violent clashes, with demonstrators blocking roads and throwing objects at officers, Israel Police said in a statement.The clashes broke out on Haim Bar-Lev Road in Jerusalem, where protesters blocked traffic and confronted officers who had been called to the scene, according to police.Israel Police called for protesters to disperseAn officer declared the gathering unlawful and ordered the protesters to disperse. However, some refused to comply and began throwing objects at officers, police said.Officers from the Lev HaBira police station, assisted by Border Police officers, then used force to disperse the protesters, restore order, and reopen the blocked roads.No injuries or arrests were reported as of the latest police update.Violent protests in Beit Shemesh lead to injuriesOn Sunday night in Beit Shemesh, Israel Police said two young men were injured when a concrete block fell on their feet after they had apparently pushed it.According to police, the injuries occurred after hundreds of rioters set fire to bins and damaged infrastructure, and pushed concrete blocks onto the road."We would like to clarify that the incident occurred in a place where there were no police officers at all, and that there is no connection between the police's activity to disperse the rioters and the injury to the young people."

title: Footage Confirms Russian Su-35 Fighters’ Transition to Fully Modernised Air-to-Air Missile Arsenal
body: New footage of a Russian Aerospace Forces Su-35 air superiority fighter operating in the Ukrainain theatre has shown the integration of R-77M radar guided air-to-air missiles, and the fully phasing out of the older R-77-1 and R-27 which have been the aircraft’s primarily weapons since it entered service in 2014. The R-77M represents a more substantial redesign than the designation might suggest, and introduces redesigned aerodynamic control surfaces, an improved propulsion system and a revised guidance configuration intended to enhance performance against manoeuvring targets at long range. Its development is also closely associated with the requirements of Russia’s Su-57 fifth generation fighter. Russia has lagged significantly behind China, the United States, and even European states in introducing new generations of air-to-air missiles into service, with the R-77-1 having lagged far behind missiles such as the Chinese PL-15 and U.S. AIM-260 in performance. The Russian Aerospace Forces have for the first time been confirmed to have operationalised the R-77M in July 2025, when the missiles were seen integrated onto Su-35s in active service. The fighters at the time carried mixed arsenals of R-77M and R-77-1 missiles, indicating limited availability of the former. One of the most visible differences is the replacement of the R-77-1’s distinctive lattice tail fins with conventional cruciform control surfaces. The redesigned fins reduce the missile’s external dimensions in key areas and are compatible with the internal weapons bays of the Su-57, helping the aircraft preserve its low-observable characteristics when carrying air-to-air weapons. The configuration also changes the missile’s aerodynamic characteristics, although its overall performance depends on the interaction between its propulsion, control surfaces, guidance system and flight profile. The R-77M’s development therefore provides benefits beyond simply extending the range of the earlier missile. The propulsion system is another important area of improvement. The R-77M is widely reported to use a dual-pulse solid-propellant rocket motor, allowing thrust to be delivered in two stages rather than relying exclusively on a single initial burn. This arrangement can help preserve energy during the later stages of an engagement, when a missile must retain sufficient speed and manoeuvrability to intercept a target that may be attempting to evade. The benefit is particularly relevant to long-range engagements, in which a missile can lose substantial energy during its flight before reaching the target area. Published estimates place the R-77M’s maximum range at approximately 190 kilometres, compared with around 110 kilometres for the R-77-1. The Su-35 has been observed in multiple new configurations since operations in the Ukrainian theatre began. Footage released by Russian state media in March showed the aircraft equipped with much larger R-37M long range air-to-air missiles mounted centrally between the engines, one Kh-31PM anti-radiation missile, three R-77-1 medium-range air-to-air missiles, and three R-73/74 short-range air-to-air missiles, for a total of eight missiles. The aircraft were responsible for covering Army helicopters striking Ukrainian personnel and temporary deployment points. The Kh-31 continues to be prioritised even for fighters configured for air-to-air operations, as it provides a means of suppressing hostile radar-guided air defences, the positions of which are often difficult to predict.

title: Ukrainian forces evacuate civilians around Kherson Oblast during Oleshky ceasefire
body:
Ukrainian forces evacuated 167 civilians from around the Kherson Oblast amid the Oleshky humanitarian ceasefire, Ukraine's General Staff announced on Nov. 1.
"During the ceasefire regime," the General Staff said , "the Ukrainian Defense Forces used the opportunities created by the security situation to evacuate residents of the right bank of the Kherson region."
From Oct. 27 to 11 p.m. local time on Nov. 1, Russian and Ukrainian forces observed a ceasefire around the city of Oleshky in the southern Kherson Oblast . Occupied by Russian forces since the early days of the full-scale invasion, 2,000 residents of Oleshky faced starvation and humanitarian crises as Russian forces blockaded aid to the city.
On Oct. 31, evacuated residents of Oleshky began returning to Ukrainian-controlled territory as the humanitarian ceasefire held.
Throughout the war, the Kherson Oblast has remained one of the most beleaguered and hazardous regions of Ukraine, with constant threats trapping citizens even in Ukrainian-held territories.
"Those who were able to leave were those who had not previously had the opportunity to leave the dangerous areas," said the General Staff about the additional residents evacuated from the oblast in the new operation.
Units from Ukraine's "South" task force cooperated with local authorities to evacuate Kherson Oblast residents trapped on the right bank of the Dnipro River to safer areas in the region. 22 children and 21 people with limited mobility were among the evacuated, the General Staff said.
The "South" task force units "strictly" adhered to the ceasefire agreement during the operation while helping conduct the evacuation through mined roads and areas littered with destroyed military equipment and civilian vehicles.
"Despite these risks, the main priority remains the preservation of the lives of the civilian population and the provision of assistance to those who are unable to leave dangerous areas on their own," the General Staff said. "Each person saved is the result of joint work and coordinated interaction of all those involved in the humanitarian mission."

title: Ukrainian judoka Savytskyi wins bronze at Grand Slam in UAE
body:
