title: Democrats eye state supreme court races — this year and beyond
body: Liberal groups have spent millions in a handful of battleground state supreme court races ahead of Tuesday’s elections, looking to lay the groundwork for Democrats to win control of more courts ahead of a crucial redistricting cycle. At the center of the fight are races for Republican-majority state supreme courts in North Carolina and Ohio, where this year’s results could set the stage for Democrats to flip the makeup of the benches in 2028. National groups are also spending to defend the liberal majority on Michigan’s court and on an open seat in Montana, where voters will also decide whether judicial elections remain nonpartisan. The investments are yet another reflection of how state supreme court elections have become national political battlegrounds. The high court justices have become arbiters of major disputes, from abortion rights to election integrity and redistricting. Those who win in the coming cycles will likely preside over challenges to congressional and legislative maps that are drawn in a handful of states after the midterm election — and then nationwide after the 2030 census . Nowhere are the contests more heated than in North Carolina. Democrats’ defense of a seat currently held by Anita Earls is “step No. 2” to flip the North Carolina Supreme Court, said Anderson Clayton, the state’s Democratic Party chair. “In 2028, we’re looking at being able to take three Republican seats on that court.” Democrats lost four seats on the state supreme court in the 2020 and 2022 elections, and the Republican majority cleared the way for a Republican-led gerrymandering in 2023. Clayton said her group has spent more than $1 million on the state supreme court race. Earls has also drawn support from national Democrats like Pete Buttigieg and Maryland Gov. Wes Moore . “If we had won a state Supreme Court race then in 2020 in our state, Hakeem Jeffries would be speaker of the House right now,” said Clayton, adding that her group is trying to build the foundation for congressional majorities “in 2032 and beyond.” The ACLU is among the groups making long-term investments in state supreme court races. It has poured $8 million into state supreme court races in North Carolina, Michigan and Montana this year, in addition to Georgia and Wisconsin races earlier this year , said Deirdre Schifeling, the group’s chief political and advocacy officer, making it one of the top spenders in these contests. The ACLU’s multi-cycle strategy to build “pro-civil rights, civil liberties majorities” is also targeting Arizona, Pennsylvania, Kentucky and Ohio, Schifeling said. The group already set aside resources for supreme court races in Wisconsin and Pennsylvania in 2027 and will begin fundraising for the 2028 races early next year. More than $14 million has been spent on television ads in North Carolina, Michigan, Ohio and Montana, most of it benefiting Democratic and liberal-leaning candidates, according to estimates from the liberal-leaning Brennan Center for Justice . Most of the liberal candidates have also outraised their conservative competitors. By contrast, the electoral headwinds have forced Republicans to defend statewide offices and state legislatures they currently control, leaving fewer resources for the judicial races. Republican-aligned groups like the Republican State Leadership Committee — the party’s chief downballot campaign organization — have largely stayed on the sidelines this cycle after warning for months they were being swamped by Democrats . The organization’s judicial affiliate reported more than $5 million in expenditures across 2024 and 2025. “Democrats understand what is at stake, and have dumped massive amounts of resources into these contests,” said RSLC President Edith Jorge-Tuñón in a statement. “The RSLC is fighting back with smart and targeted spending because the investments we make today will determine whether we are positioned to protect our majorities, compete in the next redistricting cycle, and secure Republican victories for years to come.” The National Democratic Redistricting Committee — the party’s main redistricting-focused group — declined to discuss this year’s total spending in judicial races this year, but NDRC President John Bisognano said in a statement that “the upcoming 2026 and 2028 state supreme court elections are critical to the long-term fight to protect democracy.” And those involved in supreme court fights said they believed spending will only increase down the road, particularly from major industry players. “I think that the money flowing into those races from external interests tells the tale of what big money, big pharma, big data recognize about the next areas that they can seek to leverage and control to their benefit,” said Tish Gotell Faulks, the state courts director at the liberal Alliance for Justice Action. “Those interests are now turning to the state courts and seeking to capture those courts as well.”

title: Lagos teacher wins N10m Maltina prize, gets apartment from Sanwo-Olu
body:
Lagos teacher, Busayo Adeyemo, has won the 2026 Maltina Teacher of the Year award, receiving a N10 million cash prize and a three-bedroom apartment from the Lagos State government.
Ms Adeyemo, of Lanre Awolokun High School, Gbagada, Lagos, emerged winner at the 12th edition of the competition organised by the Nigerian Breweries-Felix Ohiwerei Education Trust Fund (NB-FOETF) on Friday in Lagos.
Apart from the cash prize and apartment, she also received a Honda HR-V, an all-expenses-paid overseas capacity development training, a one-year supply of Maltina and a N30 million school infrastructure project to be built in her honour.
According to a press release from the organiser, Ms Adeyemi also won the Maltina Prize for Best STEM Teacher, for which she received an additional N1.5 million.
The Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, who hosted the event, separately rewarded Ms Adeyemo with the three-bedroom apartment.
Mr Sanwo-Olu commended the NB-FOETF for using its resources to recognise and support teachers, describing the initiative as an opportunity to deepen collaboration between the private sector and government.
He said the intervention demonstrated how corporate social responsibility could contribute to improving education in Lagos and Nigeria.
Speaking after she was announced as the winner, Ms Adeyemo expressed appreciation to the education trust fund, the Lagos State government and other partners for the recognition and rewards.
“I am excited, thankful and grateful about this competition and the rewards that have followed. This award simply means that I should keep giving my best.”
She said the award would also encourage her to contribute more to teacher development and STEM education.
“It’s a reminder that I have a responsibility not to relent but to keep giving my best, committing myself to teachers’ development in Lagos and Nigeria, keep advancing STEM education in Nigeria, and believing in the Nigerian children that tomorrow shall be great,” she said.
Yusuf Cariyat of Wisdom International School of Excellence, Sauka, Lugbe, Abuja, emerged first runner-up and received N5 million, while Ephraim Inyangudo of Comprehensive Secondary School, Ediene Abak Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State, emerged second runner-up and received N3 million.
Seventeen other teachers who emerged as state champions received N1 million each.
The event also featured remarks from President Bola Tinubu, represented by the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Bernard Doro.
Mr Tinubu commended the education trust fund for its investments in classrooms, libraries and other learning facilities, and said the government was ready to partner with the fund on its planned long-term support for out-of-school children from 2027.
The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, also commended the initiative, saying the strong participation in the competition reflected the depth of teaching talent across the country.
According to the NB-FOETF Corporate Affairs Director, Uzodinma Odenigbo, the competition received 2,510 entries from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) this year, representing a 30 per cent increase from the previous edition.
Of the entries, 2,243 were considered valid.
Mr Odenigbo said the competition had so far honoured 305 teachers, supported schools with educational infrastructure and delivered 11 school infrastructure projects.
The Chairman of the NB-FOETF and Managing Director of Nigerian Breweries, Thibaut Boidin, said the competition was established to celebrate teachers and recognise their contribution to society.
He said the 2026 edition was particularly significant as Nigerian Breweries marks 80 years, Maltina marks 50 years, while the education trust fund marks 32 years of investment in education.
“We see your commitment, the sacrifices, surprises that may never appear on a report card. We see the extra time you give to a struggling student, the patience, the courage and the optimism required to keep believing in the next generation. We honour you and we thank you,” Mr Boidin said.
The Maltina Teacher of the Year competition was introduced in 2015 by the Nigerian Breweries-Felix Ohiwerei Education Trust Fund to identify, honour and reward outstanding teachers across Nigeria.
Since inception, the Maltina Teacher of the Year Competition has produced eleven grand prize winners, and they include Rose Obi (2015), Imoh Essien (2016), Felix Ariguzo (2017), Olasunkanmi Opeifa (2018), Ezem Collins (2019), Oluwabunmi Anani (2020), Abanika Taiye (2021), Alaku Ayiwulu (2022), Adeola Adefemi (2023), Esomnofu Ifechukwu (2024) and Serah Yusuf(2025).
With her win, Ms Adeyemo becomes the 12th recipient of the national award.
The Maltina Teacher of the Year competition was introduced in 2015 by the Nigerian Breweries-Felix Ohiwerei Education Trust Fund (NB-FOETF) to identify, honour and reward outstanding teachers across Nigeria.
The competition is supported by the Federal Ministry of Education and other education stakeholders, including the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), the All Nigeria Confederation of Principals of Secondary Schools (ANCOPSS) and the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN).
The NB-FOETF was established in 1994 with an initial capital of N100 million to support sustained interventions in education.
According to the organisers, the fund has worked across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones at the primary, secondary and tertiary levels.

title: Injury toll in Russian strike on Vinnytsia region rises to six, two killed
body:
Head of the Vinnytsia Regional Military Administration Nataliia Zabolotna reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
“The strike hit between a dormitory and an academic building. Unfortunately, two people were killed. A 13-year-old girl died at the scene from her injuries. Another woman died from her injuries later in hospital. As of now, six people have been injured. Four of them are children: three five-year-olds and a 16-year-old boy. One of the five-year-old girls is in serious condition. Three other children sustained moderately serious injuries. Everyone is receiving the necessary medical assistance,” the regional governor said.
The injured also include a man and a woman who were hospitalized with minor injuries, Zabolotna added.
According to her, windows were blown out in the dormitory near the site of the strike. Internally displaced persons were living there. All of them were offered relocation to other facilities. So far, two families have agreed to move.
Rescuers, law enforcement officers, medics and all relevant services are working at the site.
As reported by Ukrinform, Russian forces attacked the Koziatyn community in the Vinnytsia region. Initially, two deaths and four injuries were reported.

title: McDavid earns first star in NHL’s monthly awards
body:
Edmonton Oilers centre Connor McDavid was named the NHL’s first star for the month of October on Sunday.
Minnesota Wild left-winger Kirill Kaprizov and Carolina Hurricanes goaltender Pyotr Kochetkov were second and third in the monthly honours.
McDavid led the NHL with 27 assists, the most by any player in a single October in league history.
He also had 35 points — the third-most by any player in a single October in NHL history — to lift the Oilers to a 10-2-1 month and the top of the Western Conference standings.
Kaprizov scored a league-high 14 goals, two more than the next-closest player, to lead the Wild to a 9-3-3 record in October and into first place in the Central Division.
Kochetkov was a perfect 9-0 in October, with a 1.66 goals-against average and a .919 save percentage to help the defending Stanley Cup champion Hurricanes finish the month with the best record in the NHL.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 1, 2026.

title: U-17 World Cup: Flamingos Beat Venezuela To Set Up Brazil Semi-Final
body: Nigeria’s Flamingos have continued their impressive run at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after edging Venezuela 1-0 in their quarter-final encounter on Sunday. Azeezat Oduntan scored the decisive goal from the penalty spot in the 89th minute to secure victory for the Nigerian side and send the West Africans into the semi-finals. The Flamingos had pushed for a breakthrough throughout the match, with Kanyinsola Yusuf, Mary Dunstan, Tosin Rafiu and Oluebube Umejiaku among those who attempted to find the net. Venezuela also created opportunities, particularly in the closing stages, but Nigeria held on despite late efforts from Astrid Granadillo and Abril Alejo. The match ended after eight minutes of added time, with the Flamingos protecting their narrow lead to book a place in the last four. The victory extends Nigeria’s recovery from a 2-1 opening defeat to Poland. The team subsequently beat Puerto Rico 2-0, defending champions North Korea 3-1 and Mexico 2-1 to reach the quarter-finals. The Flamingos will face Brazil in the semi-finals on Wednesday, November 4, at the Moulay El Hassan Stadium in Rabat. Brazil booked their place in the last four with a 2-1 comeback victory over China in their quarter-final encounter. The post U-17 World Cup: Flamingos Beat Venezuela To Set Up Brazil Semi-Final appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Israel ready to strike Iran with US, but specific joint goals remain unclear - sources
body: The IDF is ready to strike Iran if US President Donald Trump asks it to join the American air force in an operation after the November 3 midterm elections, but a wide cloud of uncertainty is hovering over the situation, The Jerusalem Post understands.Part of what is making this attack more likely after Trump pulled out of prior threats to attack in August, earlier in October, and at other times in 2026 is that other methods have been tried to obtain Iranian concessions and some of Trump's team is shifting back toward attacking, the Post has learned.At earlier points in the war, and in August and October, many of his top advisers, including, critically, sometimes US Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine, were skeptical about the utility of attacking. There are sources who push back on this and some of the below characterizations of positions of Trump officials regarding the conflict with Iran.At certain times, Caine and others were also more worried about a lack of readiness in terms of interceptors, defense capabilities for US forces and allies in the region, and the placement of critical military assets.Trump and many of his non-military advisors were also worried about the impact of an additional round with Iran, which is hugely unpopular in the US, on the Republican Party's chances in the midterm elections.But once the midterms pass – and with Caine now shifting gears to believing Iran will not meet the US president's minimum goals regarding the nuclear and Strait of Hormuz standoffs absent additional military pressure – the main bars to the use of force will have been removed, according to sources. There are those who push back on attempts to characterize the US military as having shifted, concerned that this could be to further an over-aggressive agenda.US increases military presence in Israel, Middle EastOver the past week, more than 10 US military transport aircraft arrived at the Nevatim and Uvda air force bases in the South, seeming to set the table for a serious operation.There have also been reports of US air defense systems and interceptors being moved to Israel and to other Arab allies.But there are still fewer US forces in the region than there were in previous periods.Yet, this is only the starting point.There are disagreements between the US and Israel about what the goals of such an operation would be.Mossad, IDF appear to disagree on targets of renewed fighting with IranPrime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu continues to talk about regime change, and Mossad Director Roman Gofman is working hard on plans to advance that goal, according to sources.In contrast, the IDF's focus tends to be on specific threat reduction items.These could include the Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility, some kind of attempt to reduce the threat that the regime could recover its 60% highly enriched uranium under the rubble of three previously bombed nuclear sites, any newly opened sites relating to the weapons group, new or repaired ballistic missile production sites, and strategic weapons, such as possibly space-related weapons.Top Israeli officials have also publicly threatened to strike Iran's top energy facilities.It is unclear whether they will include assassinations of top Iranian officials, given that Israel has killed dozens of top Iranian officials twice since June 2025, including Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, and other top figures in the regime maintained a hardline stance afterwards.There has been less public discussion about targeting Mojtaba Khamenei, the son of the ayatollah, and the regime's current ruler.Key goal for US is keeping any conflict shortTrump is much more focused on achieving some concessions on the nuclear issue and opening Hormuz.Even in the past Iran operations, the US avoided assassinating top Iranian officials.Next, US officials are highly concerned about keeping any new operation against Iran time-limited, possibly as short as a few days.In contrast, even if Israeli officials do not want another 40-day war, they also have not talked about keeping the operation as short as Washington has emphasized.Trump's public comments have focused on sending a brief message to Iran to advance nuclear negotiations.Israeli officials' public comments have emphasized bringing a longer-term end to the threats posed by Tehran by using extensive kinetic force.US Joint Chiefs Chairman concerned short campaign won't achieve Trump's goalsCaine remains worried about Iran pushing the war for longer than Trump wants – the regime does not need to stop firing ballistic missiles all over the region just because the US stops bombing, the Post understands.But, according to sources, Caine believes this risk must be swallowed given the absence of any sign that Iran will cut a deal at any discernible point simply based on economic pressure.He is not at all sure that another short military campaign will get to Trump's goals, but believes it is one of the last things left to try, the Post understands.Caine also remains firmly against trying to achieve regime change, which he still believes is a pipe dream – at least at this stage, regardless of the harm that America can inflict on the Iranian economy.Spokesperson for the Office of the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Joseph Holstead responded, “We do not discuss the chairman's confidential conversations with the president, the secretary of war, or other senior leaders, nor do we comment on anonymous, agenda-driven characterizations of those conversations by sources who were not privy to them.“The chairman provides the president, secretary of war, and National and Homeland Security Councils with his best military advice and recommendations, along with all associated risks, candidly and confidentially,” he added.The Post sought comment from the Pentagon, which referred to General Caine's office, and the White House, from which it had not yet received a response at press time.

title: Iraq opens first Jewish museum as country's ancient community nears extinction
body: Iraq's first-ever museum dedicated entirely to Iraqi Jewish history was inaugurated in Baghdad this weekend.The Jewish Shamash Museum opened on Al-Rashid Street on the site of the historic Shamash School. The prestigious school was established by the Jewish community in 1928 and by 1939 had 900 students. The building no longer housed the Jewish school by 1951, but the school itself continued operating elsewhere until approximately 1973.The museum is a cultural initiative aimed at reviving Baghdad's pluralistic history and collective memory. It houses official documents, old school records, and academic certificates belonging to families and students who lived in Baghdad, as well as personal belongings such as family photographs, traditional clothing, household utensils, and religious artifacts.Permanent screens display recorded interviews and audiovisual material that documents the testimonies and stories of members of the community.افتتاح متحف يهودي في بغداد وهو الأول من نوعه في مبنى مدرسة شماش الإعدادية اليهودية الواقعة في شارع الرشيد. ومن الفيديوهات التي انتشرت بهذه المناسبة هناك صور عن نمط الحياة اليهودية وصور لعائلات يهودية إضافة إلى شهادات دراسية لطلاب في مدرسة شماش وتوجت احد الجدران صورة يعقوب شماش مؤسس هذه المدرسة الراقية التي خرجت فطاحل. وأفادت التقارير الإخبارية ان عدد الزوار في اليوم الأول من افتتاح المتحف فاق الألف شخص. تأسست مدرسة شماش اليهودية في بغداد عام 1928، وبلغ عدد طلابها في أوجها أكثر من 900 طالب عام 1939. وفي ربيع عام 1951، غادرت المدرسة بنايتها الأصلية في شارع الرشيد، وانتقل طلابها إلى بناية مدرسة فرنك عيني، حيث استمرت الدراسة باسم اعدادية شماش.— إسرائيل بالعربية (@IsraelArabic) October 24, 2026Local news reports indicated that the number of visitors on the first day of the museum's opening exceeded a thousand people.From 150,000 to a handfulThere are only a handful of Jews left in the country today. There are believed to be between four and six Jews in Baghdad and around 50 Jewish families in Iraqi Kurdistan.Iraq used to have one of the oldest and most significant Jewish communities in the world, dating back more than 2,500 years to the Babylonian exile. The community peaked in the early 1900s, with Jews making up nearly a quarter of Baghdad's population. There was an estimated community of between 100,000 and 150,000 Jews in the country before the 1941 Farhud (pogrom), which saw Jewish residents attacked, murdered, and robbed.Following this, from 1950 to 1951, around 120,000 Iraqi Jews left for Israel in Operation Ezra and Nehemiah.The community's last custodiansThere is still a Jewish community leadership figure, a woman named Khalida Elyahu, who is referred to as the head of Iraq's Jewish community. She is a dentist at a health center in Baghdad.Elyahu serves as the chairwoman of the Administrative Committee for Iraqi Jews, a legally recognized body responsible for administering the Jewish community's remaining financial affairs, including communal property and religious endowments. It was responsible for the restoration of the shrine of Rabbi Isaac Gaon in the Qanbar Ali neighborhood of central Baghdad in 2025.According to local Arabic-language Iraqi media, the restoration of the original Shamash School building was also made possible thanks to the same committee.The Administrative Committee for Iraqi Jews was founded on February 25, 1958, and, according to a January 5 federal court ruling this year, seen by The Jerusalem Post, it remains in force as the sole body responsible for the Jewish community's financial affairs in Iraq. Nevertheless, it is unclear who exactly commissioned the restoration.הצגת פוסט זה באינסטגרם‏‎פוסט משותף על ידי ‏‎Linda Menuhin‎‏ (@‏‎linda_menuhin_abdul_aziz‎‏)‎‏A Jewish school that Jews cannot visitWhile local media reported that it was funded by the Jewish endowment, JIMENA (Jews Indigenous to the Middle East and North Africa), a US nonprofit focused on the Mizrahi and Sephardic Jews, suggested another option.In a statement on Saturday, JIMENA said it had met with “Iraqis leading this preservation work” earlier in October, the implication being that these are non-Jewish Iraqis.JIMENA said that while it “welcomes” the restoration of the Shamash School and “stands with those who protect Jewish heritage in Iraq,” it “cannot celebrate this moment without asking a difficult question: 'What does it mean to preserve a Jewish school that Jews cannot visit?'“Preservation that does not include the descendants of these families risks becoming a display of Jewish absence rather than a restoration of Jewish presence,” JIMENA noted.

title: Act of sabotage against oil refinery thwarted in Syria’s Homs — agency
body:
BEIRUT, November 1. /TASS/. Syria’s special services have exposed a terrorist plot against an oil refinery in the city of Homs.
"Syrian intelligence agencies timely tracked the movements of a terrorist cell, cordoned off the area and detained the militants just before they could carry out an act of sabotage," the main general intelligence department under the Syrian transitional government’s interior ministry said in a statement cited by the SANA agency.
According to the statement, suicide vests, makeshift explosive devices, electronic equipment for remote detonation, and detailed maps of the facility were seized from the detainees. There were no casualties among security officers.
The oil refinery in Homs, along with the oil refining complex at the port of Baniyas on the Mediterranean coast, plays a key role in supplying petroleum products to the local market.
According to SANA, an operation against an Islamic State (terrorist organization outlawed in Russia) cell, which had previously attacked military and civilians facilities, was conducted on Sunday in Syria’s eastern Deir ez-Zor governorate. Several militants were neutralized.

title: Zelensky announces visit by Turkish energy companies to Ukraine
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky said this in an interview with CNN Türk following his visit to Turkey, according to Ukrinform.

title: Jordan and Syria tout close ties, but border smuggling and strikes tell another story – analysis
body: Over the past week, tensions between Jordan and Syria appear to have increased in the wake of an attack on a church in Karak and a Jordanian airstrike on a terror cell in southern Syria. Southern Syria borders both Jordan and Israel's Golan. Israel has been carrying out raids into Syria since the fall of the Assad regime. What might come next?Additionally, Jordanian authorities “foiled an attempt to smuggle two million narcotic pills through the Jaber border crossing with Syria, the Public Security Directorate (PSD) said on Sunday,” Jordan Times noted. “The operation was carried out by Anti-Narcotics Department (AND) personnel at the border crossing in coordination with the Customs Department and other security agencies.” A PSD statement described authorities intercepting a suspicious cargo truck as it attempted to enter the country, following intelligence received about the vehicle.The Jordanians found two million narcotic pills; this is not the first time. Jordan has been concerned about drug smuggling from Syria for years. During the reign of the Assads, the regime backed drug smuggling.These days, the government in Syria does not support the smuggling, but the smugglers still exist. Some have said that smuggling routes stretch through and exploit the area of Sweida in southern Syria because of clashes between the Druze in Sweida and the government.Meanwhile, Karaki police on Saturday seized nine automatic firearms and GPS devices after a suspicious bag was found in the Mochi area, according to PSD spokesperson Brig.-Gen. Amer Sartawi, Jordanian media said.“Sartawi said that the bag had been carried by thermal balloons and preliminary investigations indicated that it had drifted with the wind from the kingdom's southern border, adding that investigations are ongoing.”This indicates that there are various security concerns across Jordan. In the past, there have been smuggling attempts from Jordan into Israel, which has increased its border security in the Jordan Valley in the last several years.War and peace in SyriaSyria's Foreign Minister Asaad Al-Shaibani said that Syria and Jordan maintain strategic relations and close security and military cooperation aimed at safeguarding their shared border and ensuring regional stability, Jordan media also noted. Shaibani made the comments at the 22nd Manama Dialogue events in Bahrain over the weekend.Jordan Times noted that the top Syrian diplomat said, “The region faces growing challenges from cross-border militias and armed groups operating outside state institutions, undermining governments' authority over decisions of war and peace.”The diplomat added that “Syria has moved beyond the trenches of conflict to take its place in shaping regional security.” Shaibani visited southern Syria last week and made similar comments. He has argued that Syrian-Jordanian relations are “at their strongest in a century,” stressing that “the incident would not undermine ties between the neighboring countries.”Shaibani added, “Jordan's security is part of Syria's security, and Syria's security is part of Jordan's security.”A century of ties and tensionsSyria and Jordan share a long history shaped by the Arab Revolt, competing political ambitions, and recurring security crises. Their relationship dates back to the end of World War I, when the Hashemite-led Arab Revolt against the Ottoman Empire helped pave the way for Arab forces to enter Damascus in 1918.Prince Faisal briefly ruled Syria before the French expelled him in 1920. His brother Abdullah subsequently established the Emirate of Transjordan in 1921. Faisal ended up ruling Iraq. The division of the region under British and French mandates left the two countries with close historical ties but different political trajectories.Relations were frequently tense during the Cold War.In September 1970, Syria sent armored forces into Jordan during the kingdom's civil war, known as Black September, supporting the Palestinian terrorist groups that attacked King Hussein's Jordanian forces. The intervention failed, but it left a lasting legacy of mistrust between Damascus and Amman.At the time, Israel quietly backed Jordan. Jordan and Israel agreed to a peace deal in 1994.Relations between Syria and Jordan improved periodically, particularly after Bashar al-Assad and King Abdullah II came to power.The Syrian civil war, beginning in 2011, created new challenges. Jordan hosted hundreds of thousands of Syrian refugees and supported some opposition groups in southern Syria. However, Amman later sought to restore relations with Assad, reopening border trade and pursuing security cooperation.Drug trafficking, particularly smuggling of the synthetic stimulant Captagon, remained a major concern, along with Iranian-backed militias operating in southern Syria.Following Assad's fall in 2024, Jordan moved to engage Syria's new government under President Ahmad al-Sharaa.Nevertheless, instability in Daraa and Sweida, cross-border smuggling, and the threat of armed groups continue to complicate relations. For Jordan, the priority remains a stable Syrian neighbor that can secure its borders and prevent regional conflicts from spilling into the kingdom.

title: Iran hopes US will prefer diplomacy to other scenarios — top diplomat
body:
TEHRAN, November 1. /TASS/. Iran hopes that the United States will be pragmatic enough to opt for diplomacy, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said.
"We are doing everything we can and hope that the opposing [American] side will show enough pragmatism to choose diplomacy over other options, but we are fully prepared for other scenarios as well," he told the Iranian television.
According to the top Iranian diplomat, the country’s armed forces are today much stronger than they were during the two previous wars and Iran is prepared both for diplomacy and defense.

title: Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal to resume work in several weeks — justice minister
body:
MOSCOW, November 1. /TASS/. Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal may resume its work within several weeks, Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek said.
"It's only a matter of a few weeks before we have our first court hearings and the first cases are heard on the merits," he told the TVP Info television channel. According to the minister, priority will be given to claims from citizens that have been neglected for years.
A political crisis erupted in Poland following Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s decision to appoint Marcin Bereka, a former minister in his government, as a judge of the Constitutional Tribunal. Protests have been held regularly outside the court building in recent weeks. On October 30, Zurek filed a motion to suspend Bogdan Swieczkowski, acting president of the Constitutional Court, from his duties and to strip him of his immunity. Additional police forces were deployed to guard the court building. Overnight to October 31, protesters gathered outside the courthouse and attempted to break through the fence. Four people were detained.
Due to the escalating crisis, President Karol Nawrocki cut short his trip to Senegal and returned to Warsaw. A number of opposition politicians described the situation as an attempted coup.
This crisis is a continuation of a long-standing conflict over the Constitutional Tribunal that began back in 2015. Back then, the Law and Justice Party (which Nawrocki is a supporter of) began appointing its own judges to positions that were already filled, paralyzing the court and triggering a years-long dispute with Brussels. After coming to power in 2023, the Tusk government promised to restore the supremacy of law, but its efforts were met with resistance from Nawrocki. He refused to swear in several judges elected by parliament. At the same time, Swieczkowski barred these judges from taking up their posts.

title: Why Israel must prepare for an independent, open-ended war against Iran and its proxies - opinion
body: The looming prospect of a joint Israeli-American air campaign against Iran following the upcoming US midterm elections has exposed a profound strategic rift between Washington's exit strategy and Jerusalem's existential imperatives.While US planning reportedly visualizes a short, high-intensity campaign designed to shatter Iran's surviving nuclear infrastructure and strategic industries before declaring victory and withdrawing, policymakers in Jerusalem face a far more perilous aftermath.For Israel, a rapid American withdrawal leaves behind an undefeated, deeply aggrieved Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) that analysts agree will never surrender.With Iran capable of unleashing waves of sophisticated maneuvering warheads, attack drones, cluster munitions, and potentially radiological or chemical payloads, Israel cannot afford to let a temporary American victory transition into a permanent heightened state of vulnerability.To prevent this nightmare scenario, Israel must recognize that striking the Iranian homeland is only half the battle; the Iranian threat cannot be neutralized without systematically severing its regional tentacles. A truly decisive outcome requires the simultaneous, uncompromising destruction of Iran's primary proxies: Hezbollah, the Houthis, and the remnants of Hamas.Leaving these heavily armed forward-operating bases intact on Israel's borders would allow Tehran to conduct a war of attrition by proxy even while its domestic infrastructure burns.By aggressively dismantling the command structures, missile stockpiles, and political control of these asymmetric armies, Israel can completely isolate Iran, stripping the regime of its strategic depth and leaving it geopolitically stranded in the Middle East.If the US executes its plan to hammer Iran and immediately pull back its forces, Israel's operational objective must shift from mere participation to an independent, sustained campaign of long-term containment.To ensure its survival in the vacuum of an American departure, Israel will have no choice but to systematically dismantle Iran's broader war-sustaining infrastructure. This means expanding the targeting bank far beyond nuclear sites to permanently cripple Iran's energy grid, hydrocarbon export capacities, and primary military-industrial complexes.By neutralizing the economic engines that fund the IRGC and the manufacturing plants that build its missile and drone arsenals, Jerusalem can severely degrade Iran's ability to project power across the region.However, destruction alone will not guarantee long-term security against an adversary committed to Israel's elimination. The critical component of Israel's post-war strategy must be the immediate initiation of a domestic crash program to achieve absolute qualitative and technological dominance.Israel must be decisiveWhile holding the line, Jerusalem must rapidly develop and deploy its own arsenal of Intermediate-Range Ballistic Missiles (IRBMs) equipped with Maneuvering Reentry Vehicles (MaRVs), Hypersonic Glide Vehicles (HGVs), and hypersonic cruise missiles (HCMs).These advanced next-generation strike capabilities are essential to penetrate evolving air defenses and hold Tehran permanently at risk, establishing a unilateral deterrent that does not rely on shifting political wills in Washington.Ultimately, the true test of Israel's resolve will begin the day the American bombers return home. Jerusalem must fundamentally accept a brutal new strategic doctrine: the absolute necessity of preventing the rebuilding of Iran's offensive capabilities no matter what the cost.This translates into a policy of continuous proactive interdiction. Any attempt by the IRGC to reconstruct its military-industrial facilities, import critical components, or restore its missile manufacturing capability must be met with immediate, decisive Israeli military action.By committing to an uncompromising multi-year campaign of proxy elimination, strategic denial, and rapid domestic rearmament, Israel can transform a partial American victory into a definitive solution to the Iranian threat.The writer spent 30 years in American prisons after being convicted of spying for Israel. Now living in Jerusalem, he is an investor and co-founder in a handful of technology companies. He also writes and speaks about Israel's need to be militarily self-sufficient.

While more cities are canceling their contracts with Flock Safety, just as many are discovering how difficult that can be in some instances. Plymouth, Minnesota’s city council voted to terminate its contract with Flock in September, but failed to respond to the city’s request. For over a month, the cameras remained up, and the city had received no acknowledgment from the company. So, Police Chief Eric Fadden took matters into his own hands and physically disconnected the cameras.
“After hearing nothing for more than a week, I directed our staff to disconnect the power cords from the cameras in order to be sure that they are not functioning or recording plates,” Fadden told The Drive .
Roughly 20 miles up the road, Dayton, Minnesota , is having its own issues with Flock. In this instance, the company acknowledged the city’s request and said it would take up to 60 days to remove the equipment. Despite this, Flock reconnected two cameras within the city limits without authorization, and following a specific request from the local police not to complete the work order.
Dayton’s local government posted on Facebook :
On September 17, 2026, the Police Department was made aware of a maintenance work order produced by Flock. The City notified Flock on September 18, 2026, that the program was on hold, and no work orders were to be completed. Unfortunately, the City’s direction was not followed, and the camera was placed back into service without authorization.
Flock spokesperson Andrew Smith told The Verge , “We are proud of the impact our technology has had in Plymouth. We respect the city’s decision and are working with the customer to have the cameras removed.”
This follows a similar ordeal in Illinois, where the company refused to take down cameras and uncovered cameras at Elgin Community College after the administration sought to cancel its contract.

title: Haley Stevens endorses GOP candidate in Michigan Senate race, spurning Abdul El-Sayed
body:
Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, right, and Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., attend a service at Perfecting Church, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Detroit. Jose Juarez/AP hide caption
DETROIT — After months of proclaiming support for the Democratic ticket, Rep. Haley Stevens has endorsed GOP Michigan Senate candidate Mike Rogers over her former primary rival Abdul El-Sayed, less than 48 hours before Election Day.
"As you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away, and he's right," Stevens said in a video she posted to social media on Sunday. "And that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the U.S. Senate today."
Her statement followed a surprise appearance with Rogers at a church in Detroit.
Outside a "Souls to the Polls" event at a church in Detroit, El-Sayed told reporters that he doesn't think about Stevens and said voters do not either.
"None of this matters," El-Sayed said. "You know what matters. You can go, like, 15 minutes that way, or 15 minutes that way, or 15 minutes that way. And there are families who are preparing to send their kids to schools tomorrow that look like they did 50 years ago. They're worried about what they're going to feed their kids for lunch. They're worried that if one of their kids gets sick, they're not going to be able to pay the bills."
Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks with reporters before a Souls to the Polls campaign event at Northend Church of God in Christ, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Detroit. Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP hide caption
In her endorsement, Stevens said she does "not stand with Hasan Piker," a streamer that El-Sayed campaigned with during the primary. In August, after Piker implied that Jews' support for Israel puts them at risk of personal violence, El-Sayed sought to distance himself from the controversy, saying Piker did not speak for the campaign. He stopped short of disavowing Piker.
Stevens had been critical that El-Sayed was not doing enough to reassure Jewish and Black voters who supported her during the primary. Even though relations between the pair had been publicly disintegrating for weeks, Stevens' announcement was a surprise.
Tensions accelerated after Stevens' fiance, Jason Turkish, said he planned to vote for Rogers. In a subsequent TV appearance, Stevens maintained she was still planning to support the Democratic nominee. She urged El-Sayed to denounce a recent ad by Cenk Uygur, of Young Turks, that blamed Israel for high grocery prices in the United States.
"The ad tells Michigan families they cannot afford groceries because their money has to be set aside 'for killing Palestinians,' and it blames our close ally Israel for everything Michiganders cannot afford," she wrote.
El-Sayed's campaign had said he had nothing to do with the ad and criticized the contents of the ad on Saturday.
Stevens said she was originally scheduled to attend a different church event in Detroit on Sunday alongside El-Sayed and Rep. James Clyburn, D-S.C. The planned joint appearance was meant to be a unifying event for the party ahead of the election. But on Friday, Stevens set a condition for her participation in the event — that El-Sayed reject the ad and apologize for rhetoric she considered to be inflammatory and offensive.
The event with El-Sayed and Clyburn went ahead as planned, without Stevens.
Stevens' announcement has sent shockwaves through the Democratic Party.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., called it a "despicable betrayal."
"Haley Stevens' decision to campaign with Rogers — a man who has repeatedly sold out Michigan's working class, wants to pass a national abortion ban, and has pledged to be a loyal vote for Trump's agenda — shows that she has abandoned everything she claims to care about," Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel said in a statement.
Stevens' communications director has an email auto reply that says as of Sunday, he is no longer working for the Stevens office. On social media, several former campaign staffers slammed their former boss' actions.
The clash between the two Michigan Democrats highlights a broader rift within the party as it relates to Israel and rhetoric around Israel. That schism is likely to extend far beyond Election Day and will be something the Democratic Party has to contend with, particularly as it prepares for the 2028 presidential nominating process.

title: Arsenal End 14-Year Winless Run At Anfield To Go Top Of Premier League
body: Arsenal moved to the top of the Premier League with their first win away to Liverpool in 14 years as Kai Havertz’s early strike secured a 1-0 victory for the Gunners. The defending champions were made to suffer after the German’s 16th-minute opener but held out for what could be a telling win in their quest to retain the title. Arsenal climbed three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the table. But with City expected to be hit with a severe points penalty, unless they can overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules, Arsenal dealt a huge blow to their most likely rivals for the title. “It’s been such a long time without this feeling here, that we really needed it,” said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta. “We are extremely proud of what the team, the players, everybody has done.” Liverpool produced arguably their best spell of Andoni Iraola’s early months in charge with a blistering 30 minutes after conceding, but failed to take their chances as the Spaniard suffered just his second defeat in 14 games since arriving from Bournemouth. Liverpool’s Argentinian midfielder #10 Alexis Mac Allister (R) vies with Arsenal’s Norwegian midfielder #08 Martin Odegaard (2R) and Arsenal’s English midfielder #41 Declan Rice (L) during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Arsenal at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on November 1, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) Arteta was stinging in his criticism of the Arsenal side that crashed out to fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday in one of the biggest ever League Cup shocks. The Arsenal boss got the response he desired in a strong start from the champions. Havertz was one of the biggest culprits for wasting chances in midweek but made amends with a simple finish from Declan Rice’s precise low cross. The early goal lit the touchpaper for a pulsating first 45 minutes as Liverpool roared back. Isak honesty saves Arsenal Iraola and Arteta played together as boys for Basque side Antiguoko Kirol Elkartea. Arteta’s old friend gave his side one of the most uncomfortable afternoons they have experienced in recent seasons as Arsenal’s rock-solid defence was left clinging on for half-time. “I loved the reaction from my players after going 1-0 down,” said Iraola. “I loved a lot of moments of the game. “We have to keep going. It is very early in the season. Arsenal are in the best of the situations but it is just the start of November today.” Liverpool’s Argentinian midfielder #10 Alexis Mac Allister indicates he’s been butted during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Arsenal at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on November 1, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) All of Liverpool’s three £100 million-plus ($134 million) forwards started together and there are signs the relationship between Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola is beginning to flourish. Isak did Arsenal a favour by not going down as he was pulled back by Jurrien Timber when just failing to connect with a wicked delivery from Barcola. “The Alex one is a clear penalty,” added Iraola. “We can all see that he holds the shirt (but) because he doesn’t go to the floor, you are not going to call the penalty? I don’t understand it.” Wirtz curled a free-kick onto the bar from a narrow angle and Alexis Mac Allister should have buried a header into the goal rather than finding the stand behind David Raya’s goal. Half-time allowed Arsenal the chance to reset and take the wind out of Liverpool’s sails as Iraola’s men tired in the second period. Alisson Becker produced a stunning save to turn behind Christos Tzolis’s shot that was arrowing into the bottom corner to keep Liverpool in the game. That intervention counted for little as Arsenal rode out the closing stages to register another clean sheet and an eighth win in nine league games. Defeat leaves fifth-placed Liverpool nine points adrift of the leaders and already facing a mountain to climb to get back in the title race. AFP The post Arsenal End 14-Year Winless Run At Anfield To Go Top Of Premier League appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Okorocha chasing shadows, Uzodimma says, vows to appeal court judgement
body:
Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma has vowed to appeal the Federal High Court judgement recognising his predecessor, Rochas Okorocha, as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 elections, describing the former governor as “chasing shadows”.
Mr Uzodimma’s Chief Press Secretary, Oguike Nwachuku, said the governor considered the judgement a “travesty of justice” and was confident it would be overturned by the Court of Appeal.
“Obviously, the Governor will appeal the judgement which is a travesty of justice,” Mr Nwachuku told PREMIUM TIMES on Friday in response to questions about Mr Okorocha’s allegations against the governor and his (Okorocha) account of the disputed APC senatorial primary.
The governor’s response followed Mr Okorocha’s appearance on Arise News’ Prime Time on Thursday, where he claimed that he remained the dominant political figure in the APC in Imo State and accused Mr Uzodimma of relying on documents containing irregularities to secure the party’s senatorial ticket.
Mr Okorocha had declared that “the structure of APC in Imo State is Rochas”, insisting that his political influence in the state remained intact despite opposition from the governor’s camp.
In a PREMIUM TIMES report the former governor also alleged that documents supporting Mr Uzodimma’s emergence as the party’s candidate contained inconsistencies, including discrepancies in the primary’s date, the description of the exercise as a consensus arrangement and result sheets allegedly completed by one person across 144 wards and 12 local government areas.
Mr Nwachuku, however, dismissed Mr Okorocha’s account and insisted that the governor won the primary by an overwhelming margin.
According to the governor’s spokesperson, there was a direct primary in Imo West because Mr Okorocha rejected the consensus arrangement adopted in the other two senatorial districts.
He said political stakeholders in Owerri Zone, which produces the Imo East senatorial seat, and Okigwe Zone, which produces Imo North, opted for consensus arrangements that produced Prince Alex Mbata and Senator Patrick Ndubueze, respectively.
Mr Nwachuku said Mr Okorocha insisted on contesting against Mr Uzodimma across the 12 local government areas in Imo West.
He insisted that the governor won the contest with 230,464 votes against Mr Okorocha’s 1,098 votes.
The spokesperson said officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission ( INEC ) were present during the exercise, while the APC National Assembly Primary Election Committee, led by its chairman and returning officer, Williams Kayoda a retired rear admiral supervised the process across the local government areas.
He maintained that the outcome was legitimate and accused Mr Okorocha of attempting to undermine the APC by challenging the result.
“Rochas Okorocha is simply chasing shadows and intentionally working against the interest of the APC he claims to be a founding member and the re-election of President Bola Tinubu,” he said.
Mr Nwachuku also rejected Mr Okorocha’s claim to control the APC structure in Imo State, arguing that the party’s rules recognise sitting governors as leaders of the party in their respective states.
He said President Bola Tinubu remained the national leader of the APC, while Mr Uzodimma controlled the party’s structure in Imo State.
“By the APC rules, the governors are the leaders of the party in their states while the president is the leader in the country. I’m not aware that rule has changed,” he said.
He accused Mr Okorocha of attempting to personalise a party structure that belonged collectively to its members, adding that the former governor was unwilling to submit to the party’s leadership.
Mr Nwachuku also criticised Mr Okorocha’s eight-year administration in Imo State, describing it as a family system of government and blaming his performance in office for his alleged loss of political relevance.
He dismissed the former governor’s public celebration of the court judgement, arguing that the ruling would not survive an appeal.
“No responsible leader anywhere in the world will appear on television the way Okorocha did to celebrate a judgement he knows will be thrown out at the appeal for lacking in facts and for being against the rules of the party,” he said.
He also dismissed Mr Okorocha’s claims of continued popularity among voters in Imo West and the state.
Mr Nwachuku concluded his response with the expression caveat emptor, meaning buyer beware, urging the public to scrutinise the former governor’s claims.
The Federal High Court in Abuja, presided over by Justice Obiora Egwuatu, had ruled in favour of Mr Okorocha in the dispute over the APC’s Imo West senatorial primary.
The court declared him the validly nominated candidate of the party and directed INEC to recognise him for the 2027 senatorial election.
The judgement followed a suit filed by Mr Okorocha challenging INEC’s recognition of Mr Uzodimma as the winner of the party’s 18 May primary.
During his interview, Mr Okorocha said he obtained certified copies of documents relating to the primary from INEC on 26 July 2026, while documents supporting Mr Uzodimma’s emergence were presented to the commission on 22 August.
He alleged that the later documents contained inconsistencies, including a discrepancy in the date of the election and the description of Mr Uzodimma’s emergence as a consensus candidate despite the existence of competing aspirants.
He further claimed that result sheets covering more than 300 polling units across 144 wards and 12 local government areas were completed by one person.
Mr Okorocha also questioned the circumstances surrounding a letter allegedly submitted to the APC national chairman by the Imo resident electoral commissioner, arguing that the document supporting his own claim was certified by INEC, while the one supporting Mr Uzodimma was certified by the APC.
He alleged that these discrepancies were part of the evidence that persuaded the court to recognise him as the winner.
However, Mr Okorocha’s allegations of document irregularities and forgery remain disputed by the governor’s camp. Mr Nwachuku insisted that the primary was properly conducted under the supervision of INEC officials and the APC’s national election committee.
The APC had also indicated that it would study the judgement and pursue available legal remedies.
The dispute is the latest chapter in the political rivalry between the two men. Mr Okorocha governed Imo State from 2011 to 2019 and subsequently represented Imo West in the Senate from 2019 to 2023.

title: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers after clash with Abdul El-Sayed
body: Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic US Senate nomination for Michigan to Abdul El-Sayed , on Sunday broke with her party and endorsed his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers. Ms Stevens announced her endorsement in a video posted on social media after making a surprise appearance next to Mr Rogers at a church in Detroit. “As you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for US Senate, Abdul, said that I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away,” she said. “And he's right, and that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today. I don't belong in Abdul's campaign.” I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today. pic.twitter.com/pQgfSBuhOJ — Haley Stevens (@HaleyforMI) November 1, 2026 The endorsement comes months after Mr El-Sayed, an Egyptian-American doctor, defeated Ms Stevens in the Democratic primary. Michigan is set for a critical Senate race on Tuesday. The outcome could help determine which party controls the Senate for the remaining two years of President Donald Trump's term. Ms Stevens and Mr El-Sayed had initially planned to appear together at a different church in Detroit on Sunday. But in the lead-up to the event, she demanded that Mr El-Sayed denounce a recent advertisement that blamed rising prices in the US on American military support for Israel. Jewish-American groups said the advertisement was anti-Semitic and offensive. Mr El-Sayed said the advertisement was produced by a third party and that his campaign was not involved in its production or content. In response to Ms Stevens's demand, he accused her of relitigating the primary election and said she was no longer welcome in his campaign. Mr El-Sayed, a progressive candidate endorsed by Democratic socialist Bernie Sanders, has been an outspoken critic of Israel and has described its war in Gaza as a genocide. He supports ending US military aid to Israel. If he wins, he would be the first Muslim in Congress. Ms Stevens is an establishment Democrat and a strong supporter of Israel. US President Donald Trump, who has endorsed Mr Rogers, welcomed Ms Stevens's move. “Her following is huge, and the level of respect from the people of Michigan, especially our African American and Jewish populations, is virtually unparalleled,” Mr Trump wrote on Truth Social. “Haley said what few people are willing to say. She showed great and almost unprecedented loyalty to the great people of Michigan with what she did.” Asked by reporters later on Sunday if he would consider accepting Ms Haley in the Republican party, Mr Trump responded: "I’d love to have her." Over the past weeks, Mr El-Sayed has been subject to intense Islamophobic attacks , as well as mockery over his name. Mr Trump and Mr Rogers have accused him of ties to the Muslim Brotherhood and other armed groups in the Middle East, accusations he has repeatedly denied. In her short video, Ms Stevens said she would remain a “very proud Democrat” but did not believe Mr El-Sayed's campaign represented the values she believed Michigan should stand for. “Who we are as Michiganders is not hate, and is not what we are getting out from our Democratic nominee right now,” she said. The move, just two days before the election, brought immediate reactions. Her chief of staff resigned and endorsed Mr El-Sayed. Democrat Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer wrote on X: "This is a despicable betrayal from Rep Stevens. "Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors."

title: Ukraine has not yet received official invitation to G20 summit – Zelensky
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky said this in an interview with CNN Türk following his visit to Türkiye, according to Ukrinform.
“Legally, we haven't received an invitation; but there have been signals from different negotiators. There was at least some indication that President Trump would invite us to the G20 Summit and make an effort to end the war,” Zelensky said.
The President of Ukraine also said that Ukraine would welcome such an invitation if it is extended.
“Of course, if Mr. Trump officially invites us, we will support it,” Zelensky said.
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 31, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky met with President of Türkiye Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Istanbul. A significant part of the talks focused on finding ways to unblock the Black Sea. The leaders also discussed the possibility of holding peace talks in Türkiye.

title: 'Some optimism' in US-Iran negotiations despite major disagreements, sources tell 'Post'
body: “Some progress” has been made in efforts to reach an agreement between the US and Iran, several sources familiar with the negotiations told The Jerusalem Post. However, the sources stressed that "significant gaps remain between the two sides".“There is some optimism that an agreement can be reached. But there is still work to be done,” one source said.Another source said no progress had been made on the nuclear issue and that the advances concerned other matters, including the timeline for implementing a potential agreement.In recent days, Qatari mediators have intensified indirect diplomatic efforts between the US and Iran amid growing fears of a potential military escalation following the US midterm elections.An Iranian delegation traveled to Doha for several days of talks, coordinated closely with Washington, following intensive consultations in Tehran. The discussions reportedly focus on proposals to de-escalate the eight-month-old conflict, including a potential two-day framework for reopening the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz and resuming broader peace negotiations.Significant gaps remain over Iran's nuclear programDespite these diplomatic efforts, significant gaps remain between the two sides. Tehran is demanding that Washington lift recent sanctions, reinstate oil waivers, reduce its regional military presence, and end port blockades before addressing restrictions on Iran's nuclear program.By contrast, US officials, following recent outreach by Vice President JD Vance to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei, insist that any comprehensive agreement must address nuclear concerns from the outset.On Sunday, US President Donald Trump was asked how negotiations with Iran were progressing.“They're going fine, but they're not very reliable. They make a deal and then they back out,” he responded.Trump also said there were “one or two sites” in Iran's nuclear program that the US needed to address.“But we can do that in 10 minutes,” he added.A source familiar with the matter confirmed to the Post that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Trump spoke by phone on Saturday. The call came days after Trump was briefed by US Central Command (CENTCOM) commander Adm. Brad Cooper on military options for a possible operation against Iran.Meanwhile, Iranian Deputy Parliament Speaker Ali Nikzad said Iran had no intention of negotiating over its nuclear program, regardless of the pressure exerted on it.Can Washington and Tehran overcome the nuclear deadlock?Dr. Raz Zimmt, head of the Iran and Shi'ite Axis Research Program at the Institute for National Security Studies (INSS), told The Jerusalem Post that each side currently needs something from the other that cannot be reversed, while neither is willing to make what would constitute an irreversible concession.“The Americans are prepared to lift the naval blockade and some of the sanctions, since these measures can be reinstated, and in return they are demanding something on the nuclear front, such as an inspectors' visit and/or action regarding the enriched uranium. The Iranians, meanwhile, are prepared to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and perhaps even allow inspectors to visit certain sites, but they are unwilling to give up their enriched uranium. Instead, they are demanding something permanent, such as the unfreezing of Iranian assets.“I find it difficult to see how this deadlock can be resolved,” Zimmt said.Nevertheless, he added that, given the risks of another round of military confrontation, he would not rule out the possibility that the two sides could ultimately reach a compromise, even if only a temporary one.

title: South-East governors urge Ndigbo to shun deception and vote for Tinubu in 2027
body:
Governors Peter Mbah of Enugu State, Charles Soludo of Anambra State, Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi State, and Hope Uzodimma of Imo State have called on the people of South-East region to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election and ignore every form of deceipt and political distractions.
The governors made the call during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme for the South-East flagged off by the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu at Okpara Square, Enugu, on Saturday.
Speaking, the host governor, Dr. Peter Mbah, urged the people of the region to support Tinubu’s re-election bid to enable him to consolidate the gains of his administration’s economic reforms.
He attributed ongoing development projects, including the construction of primary healthcare centres, to the federal government’s economic reforms.
“If I ask what future you want for your children, I’m sure you are seeing that future unfold gradually through the bold and courageous reforms of Mr President.
“It is through those reforms that enough money has been made available to all the states. Which is why in Enugu, when you look around you, you will see the Smart Green Schools, Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres, and numerous other projects and initiatives we have undertaken in just three years.
This is happening because of the bold and courageous reforms of Mr President and we know the job is not finished yet. A good sailor does not abandon his ship mid-sea because of challenges.
“So, we must finish the journey we all started together. We must come out on January 16 with our PVC and ensure that the good work Mr. President is doing will continue.
“Don’t listen to any voice. Those voices telling us a different thing. We, the Igbos have gone to communities outside our zone to build businesses. And we also know how to build relationships. And that is being put to test. We are not a people that are ethnic bigots. We are a people that are strategic.
“And that is why we must all come out in our numbers and support Mr President to continue the good work. Support all our APC candidates to ensure that they are returned come January and February,” he emphasised.
Speaking on the empowerment programme targeting 5,000 women across the South-east, Mbah said the initiative followed the empowerment of more than 2,000 women, including payment of hospital bills, in Enugu by the First Lady, within 48 hours.
“When you empower a woman, you strengthen the family. When you empower a woman, you build a strong community,” he said.
Also speaking, Governor Uzodimma reiterated the commitment of the region to supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.
He explained that Igbos had experienced marginalisation for over 60 years, but were beginning to witness a new era of political inclusion and development under Tinubu.
He commended the president for expanding the scope of infrastructure and economic development in the South-East.
“We are now seeing good roads, electricity, health reforms as well as educational reforms in the country. A winning team must not be changed,” he said.
The governor urged the electorate to sustain the current development trajectory, saying the federal government’s economic reforms had increased resources available to states for development.
“We have more money to build Okigwe to Owerri, Umuahia to Owerri, Orlu to Owerri and Owerri to Port Harcourt roads,” he said.
Like Mbah, Uzodimma added that the improved financial position of the state had enabled his administration to pay salaries and pensions consistently, including 13th-month salaries for workers.
In his remarks, Governor Nwifuru said that the number one mission for Ndigbo in 2027 elections was to re-elect President Tinubu, describing the APC as the only political party with a clear and identifiable manifesto capable of sustaining the country’s development and truly advancing the course of Ndigbo.
He dismissed suggestions of his involvement in any political coalition, stressing that his loyalty remained with the APC, urging urged supporters to vote for APC candidates at all levels in the 2027 elections.
Similarly, Soludo, represented by his Deputy, Dr Gilbert Ibezim, said the South-East had a responsibility to support Tinubu’s re-election in appreciation of his administration’s achievements, adding that the region stood to benefit more from continued collaboration with the federal government.
Also speaking, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Benjamin Kalu, urged Igbos to embrace political inclusion by supporting Tinubu’s re-election.
Kalu said the Igbo had not produced a president of Nigeria in the past 60 years, and was therefore not party to any one-term arrangement for the Presidency of Igbo extraction by anybody.
He, however, stressed that the Igbo needed to to strengthen its political alliances across the nation to actualise a full two-term Igbo presidency in the near future.
He recalled that Tinubu, while serving as governor of Lagos State, maintained cordial relationships with Igbos and included them in his cabinet.
He commended the Tinubu administration for establishing the South East Development Commission (SEDC).
He described it as a major step towards addressing the region’s developmental challenges.
Meanwhile, addressing the rally, the First Lady conveyed President Tinubu’s goodwill message and urged Nigerians not to be discouraged by the economic challenges associated with the President’s reforms, insisting that the country was moving towards prosperity.
She likened the process to childbirth, noting that although the period of labour could be painful, it ultimately led to delivery.
“Mr. President said I should greet everyone. We have done reforms and we are now in prosperity. Don’t allow anyone to deceive you. The worst is over. We are stepping into prosperity,” she said.
The First Lady described the empowerment initiative as an indication of the APC government’s commitment to translating its promises into practical interventions, noting that the party was combining political mobilisation with economic support.
The First Lady urged the women to mobilise support for President Tinubu and APC candidates in the forthcoming 2027 general elections, asking them to hold political aspirants accountable for their records of empowerment and development interventions.
Other dignitaries at the massive rally were Wife of the Vice President, Mrs Nana Shettima; wife of the Senate President, Mrs. Uloma Akpabio; wives of the South East governors; Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Doris Uzoka-Anite; Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr. Kingsley Udeh (SAN); and Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Mrs Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim.
Also present were the APC Deputy National Chairman (South), Dr Ben Nwoye; National Women Leader of the APC and Director-General of the Women Wing of the Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Mary Alile-Idele; South-East Zonal Woman Leader of the APC, Dr Oby Ajih; members of the National and State Assemblies, local government chairmen and other party stakeholders.
The rally by the Remi Tinubu-led Women Mobilisation Directorate of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, which kicked off in the South East, will also be held across the remaining five geopolitical zones of the country.

title: Iliana Iotova winning runoff presidential election in Bulgaria — exit poll
body:
SOFIA, November 1. /TASS/. Bulgaria’s incumbent President Iliana Iotova is winning in the runoff presidential election.
According to exit polls conducted by the Alpha Research and Myara pollsters and cited by the Bulgarian National Television, Iotova was supported by 51% of voters while her rival, the opposition-backed former prime minister of the technical government Andrey Gyurov, is winning around 44.7%. As many as 4.3% of those who took part in the election voted against all.
According to the exit polls, voter turnout was around 26.8%. Voter turnout in the first round of voting was 22.98%.
According to the country’s interior ministry, no serious violations were reported during the voting.
A winning candidate needs to garner a simple majority of votes.

body:
