title: In Zamfara, 9 a.m is 9 a.m: How Lawal is killing ‘African time’ mentality, By Yusuf Ladan
body:
Nigerians are widely known for what is popularly described as “African time” a culture of lateness where an event scheduled for 9:00 a.m may not begin until 10:00 a.m or even 11:00 a.m.
Over time, this habit has become normalised in our society, with people often arriving late to appointments, meetings and official functions without considering the inconvenience it causes others.
However, my working experience as part of the press team of Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has significantly changed my perception of time management and challenged my long-held African Time stereotype.
On my first day in Gusau, I approached government functions with the usual mindset, assuming that even when an event was scheduled for a particular time, there would always be some extra minutes before it commenced.
Like many Nigerians, I would sometimes add a few minutes to the scheduled time before setting out for an event, believing that punctuality was not necessarily a strict requirement.
But that assumption was quickly challenged.
On my first day attending an official function involving the governor, I arrived only to discover that I had been locked out just a few minutes before the scheduled commencement time.
It was then that I was told something that has remained with me: “Governor Dauda Lawal’s 9:00 a.m. means 9:00 a.m., and his 2:00 p.m. means 2:00 p.m.” That experience became a turning point for me.
Gradually, I adjusted to the governor’s schedule and developed the habit of arriving at least 30 minutes before his expected arrival.
For over a month of observing his official engagements, I have yet to witness Governor Dauda Lawal arrive late for a scheduled function.
In fact, there was an occasion when the governor arrived ahead of schedule while some participants were yet to arrive.
This consistency has gradually influenced the conduct of government appointees, political office holders, civil servants and other participants attending official functions.
People now understand that keeping to time is not negotiable because the governor does not compromise on punctuality.
Beyond the personal discipline it demands, this culture sends a strong message about leadership, respect for other people’s time and the importance of institutional efficiency.
When a leader takes time seriously, those working with him are compelled to do the same. It also helps to change the mindset that lateness is an acceptable part of our social and official engagements.
My experience in Zamfara under Governor Dauda Lawal has taught me that punctuality is not just about arriving early; it is about discipline, responsibility and respect for others.
Perhaps, one of the less-discussed changes taking place in Zamfara under Governor Dauda Lawal is this growing culture of punctuality.
In Zamfara, at least from what I have personally observed, African Time is gradually losing its place. Governor Dauda Lawal has made it clear that when time is fixed, it must be respected.
And that is a leadership lesson worth taking beyond the walls of Government House.
* Yusuf Ladan is a Gusau, Zamfara State-based journalist

title: Lebanese priest’s murder sparks sectarian outrage, calls to deport Syrians
body: The brutal murder of Catholic priest Samir Daou, allegedly by a Syrian, in the Lebanese town of Ain Jrein in the Jbeil District of Mount Lebanon, has sparked sectarian outrage and calls for the deportation of Syrians, according to Lebanese media reports.Daou was murdered in his home last week after initially being reported missing. He was stabbed more than 20 times and robbed of his personal possessions, including his wallet, car and clothes. The supect is a Syrian Muslim he had hired to help him harvest olives.The Daou family condemned the killing in a statement Thursday, according to L'Orient Today, describing it as a “heinous crime” and Daou as a man who “dedicated his life to serving others and lived sincerely, humbly, and with love for everyone,” adding that he “harmed no one and left behind nothing but love, a good reputation, and a positive impact.”Since the murder, Lebanon's Christian community has called for government action against Syrians living in the country.In one op-ed published earlier this week in the Arabic An-Nahar newspaper, for example, the writer argued that crimes committed by Syrians can no longer be treated as “isolated incidents,” and “their recurrence in multiple areas necessitates a serious discussion about the security situation in Lebanon and the ability of security forces to control the number of Syrian refugees and residents.”The author of the opinion piece noted that the priest's murder recalled to collective memory the murder of Pascal Sleiman, a Lebanese official and IT executive whose abduction and murder in April 2024 had sparked national political tensions and anti-Syrian refugee backlash in Lebanon.تسريع عودة النازحين السوريين على بلدن صار ضرورة حتمية ، شبعنا جرايم وقتل وسرقة ، ولازم الدولة تتحرك بقا وتتحمل مسؤولية تقاعسا عن حماية الناس والابرياء، لانو عن جد يللي فينا مكفينا الله يرحم الكاهن #سمير_ضو وتكون نفسو بالسما! المسيح قام ! https://t.co/zQFAuDXBpi— Elissa (@elissakh) October 29, 2026“Lebanon cannot remain in a state of temporary management of this issue while its security and social burdens accumulate. What is needed is a shift to an organized and effective return policy, alongside monitoring all residents and pursuing wanted individuals, without holding an entire community responsible for crimes committed by individuals,” the author argued.“The primary responsibility lies with the state to enforce the law, protect society, and prevent security and administrative gaps from becoming a permanent threat.”Outrage on social mediaAcross social media, Lebanese users have shared similar frustrations.Nancy Lakkis, a journalist with Elsharq News, posted on X/Twitter: “The crime of murdering Father Samir Daou in Jbeil has crossed all redlines, and it proves that unregulated displacement has now become a threat to our existential security. We are no longer prepared to tolerate chaos and violations under any pretext.“The discussion is not for moral generalization, but in sovereign measures, comprehensive deportation and the enforcement of the law must include everyone without exception. Protecting lives and sovereignty is an utmost national necessity that brooks no delay!”Lebanese singer: 'We're fed up'Elissa, a well-known Lebanese singer, wrote on X: “Speeding up the return of the displaced Syrians to their country has become an absolute necessity.”In her statement, which has drawn notable attention across Lebanese media, she said, “We're fed up with crimes, killings, and thefts. The state must now step up and take responsibility for its negligence in protecting people and the innocent because honestly, what we've been through is more than enough for us.“May God have mercy on the priest and may his soul be in heaven! Christ is risen!”Other accounts have questioned whether the killing was connected to the Islamic State (ISIS), theorizing that stabbing someone over 20 times is excessive for a simple robbery.

title: Russian drone strike near school dormitory housing displaced people kills 13-year-old in Vinnytsia Oblast, injures more children
body:
A Russian drone strike on the grounds of a vocational school dormitory in Vinnytsia Oblast killed two people, including a 13-year-old girl, on Nov. 1, the State Emergency Service (DSNS) reported.
Another six people were injured, including three 5-year-olds, a 16-year-old boy, and a 24-year-old man.
One of the injured five-year-olds is hospitalized in serious condition following the Russian attack that also set two cars ablaze before the fires were extinguished, Vinnytsia Oblast Governor Natalia Zabolotna said .
The dormitory damaged in the attack was currently being used to house internally displaced people escaping Russia's war, she added.
Photos shared by authorities also show first responders tending to a victim on a playground.
The Russian drone strike took place between the dormitory building and a school building in Vinnytsia Oblast's Kozyatyn district, Zabolotna said .
Russia regularly targets civilian infrastructure in cities across Ukraine as it continues to wage its war.
On the morning of Oct. 29, Russian forces struck a train platform at Dnipro railway station , killing at least 15 people and wounding at least 14 more, authorities said.
"A horrific Russian attack on Dnipro train station," President Volodymyr Zelensky wrote on social media in response to the attack. "The Russians used a drone to attack a platform where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing."

title: Connecticut Senator Chris Murphy is hospitalized with a stroke
body:
Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., appears at a news conference at the U.S. Capitol on September 18, 2025. Murphy's office says he was hospitalized this weekend with a stroke. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images hide caption
Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., has been hospitalized following a stroke, according to his office.
In a statement on Sunday, Murphy's chief of staff, Allison Herwitt, said he is expected to make a full recovery.
"Yesterday afternoon, Senator Murphy started experiencing numbness in his arm while at his son's hockey game," Herwitt wrote. "He was taken to a local hospital, where it was discovered he had experienced a stroke. He was transferred to Johns Hopkins for further monitoring and is responding well to treatment."
Murphy, 53, is a prominent figure in the party and has been a prolific campaign surrogate for candidates through the midterm cycle. Viewed as a possible 2028 presidential contender, Murphy has carved out a position as a foreign policy leader and champion of aggressive executive branch oversight.
He recently returned from a multistop tour in the Middle East, after which he warned that President Trump would dramatically escalate his war on Iran after the midterm election.
The lawmaker is the latest in a string of lawmakers to experience a health crisis this year. Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., missed months of Senate work during a lengthy hospital stay and rehabilitation process. Rep. Tom Kean, R-N.J., was missing from the Capitol for months for what he later announced was treatment for depression.
In 2022, three prominent Democratic lawmakers — Sen. Ben Ray Lujan of New Mexico, Chis Van Hollen of Maryland, and then-Senate candidate John Fetterman — were all hospitalized for strokes.

title: UK nuclear defence investment to rise by over £20 billion as submarine and warhead work expands
body: The increase covers the financial years 2026–27 to 2029–30 compared with the preceding four years. Spending commitments include work on Dreadnought submarines, the replacement Astraea warhead and facilities supporting nuclear submarine production and maintenance. An £8.4 billion investment supports delivery phase four of the Dreadnought construction programme, including a £5.9 billion contract with BAE Systems announced in July 2026. The ministry says the investment will support tens of thousands of jobs across the country, with construction based at Barrow-in-Furness. This phase will take HMS Dreadnought, the first submarine in the class, through sea trials. The vessel is due to be ready to enter Royal Navy service in the early 2030s. The sovereign nuclear warhead programme has been allocated £15 billion over 2025–26 to 2029–30. That funding covers development of Astraea and modernisation of the associated infrastructure. At HMNB Devonport, £7 billion will be invested over ten years in facilities supporting submarine maintenance, modernisation and disposal. A £50 million Defence Growth Deal for Plymouth accompanies the investment, while improvements to local infrastructure and housing are intended to accommodate a growing workforce. Sheffield Forgemasters is modernising and expanding its facilities with total MOD investment of £1.3 billion. This includes more than £420 million in additional funding announced in the 2025 Spending Review, with the programme sustaining over 700 skilled jobs and supporting apprenticeships. Work at the site includes a 30,000-square-metre machining facility for submarine components. McLaughlin and Harvey received a £210 million construction contract for the facility in December 2025. Rolls-Royce’s approximately £9 billion Unity agreement, signed in January 2025, provides support for the Royal Navy’s nuclear submarine fleet. The ministry says it will create more than 1,000 UK jobs, including at the reactor production facility in Derby, and safeguard another 4,000 roles. Recruitment and training are backed by £290 million in nuclear skills investment. The Nuclear Skills Plan brought around 1,300 graduates and 3,100 apprentices into defence nuclear during its first two years. The figures are drawn from the Ministry of Defence’s UK Defence Footprint 2026 report, which brings together investment commitments, contracts and employment estimates. The individual programmes cover different periods and activities, with spending extending from weapons development and submarine construction to factory capacity, maintenance facilities and training.

title: 2027: South-East Has No Presidential Candidate, Umahi Declares
body: Minister of Works David Umahi has declared that the South-East has no viable presidential candidate for the 2027 election, urging the region to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Speaking on Sunday at a town hall meeting in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, organised by the Directorate of Infrastructure, Mobilisation and Sensitisation of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Umahi said the region had aspirants but no candidate capable of commanding a consensus. “Let us stop deceiving ourselves. We do not have a presidential candidate in the South-East for 2027. We only have aspirants, and Ebonyi has the right to make its own choice,” he said. Umahi also questioned the credentials of Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the New Democratic Congress (NDC), asking whether he was better than prominent leaders from the South-East, including former Senate President Pius Anyim, former Education Minister Sam Egwu, former chairman of the Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission, Elias Mbam, and Umahi himself. “If you don’t support Peter Obi, you are labeled a saboteur and insulted. But who is Peter Obi better than? Is he better than Sam Egwu? Is he better than Elias Mbam? Is he better than the ‘Lion of the South-East’, myself? Is he better than Anyim Pius Anyim? Whom is he better than?” he asked. The minister argued that supporting Tinubu for a second term would position the South-East to secure the backing of other regions when it is time for the presidency to rotate to the zone. He said an Igbo president would need more than one term to provide effective leadership, insisting that the region should build strategic alliances rather than rely on sentiment. “There is no way an Igbo man, after waiting for 60 years, will accept being President for only four years. Nobody will accept that, and the North will certainly not agree to a four-year presidency,” Umahi said. “An Igbo man needs wisdom, not sentiment. We must not allow individuals to dish out hate speech on social media on our behalf. Today, our business people clear their goods with ease, and our roads are being rehabilitated to drive economic activity.” He added that the South-East had become more integrated into the Federal Government under Tinubu, pointing to appointments in key positions. “Today, we can boldly say we are integrated,” he said. “In the past, when service chiefs were selected, we only had the Chief of Naval Staff. This time, we have the Chief of Air Staff, the Minister of Works, several other ministers, and Senior Special Assistants. When I say the South-East has been fully integrated and included, I mean it.” Umahi said he was willing to defend his position because he believed the region needed to establish a political foundation for its future presidential ambition. “My mouth will not be shut because I am laying down a reference point for tomorrow. We are supporting President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to complete his remaining four years so that the South-East strategically earns the support of another region,” he said. “When it is our turn, we won’t get it through hate speech or sentiment; it will be through strategic alliances. Yet, when leaders in the South-East point this out, they are insulted.” The minister also appealed to traditional rulers and religious leaders, particularly the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), to openly support Tinubu rather than remain neutral. “I want to tell our religious leaders and the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN): do not stay on the fence,” he said. “I remember when I was struggling to become governor, CAN took a decision and insisted that justice must prevail. CAN should not keep quiet now. Let us toe the path that sustains our collective freedom.” He urged traditional and religious leaders to guide their communities, saying political leaders in the North and South-West did not remain neutral during elections. “Traditional fathers and religious leaders must not sit on the fence. Our people in the North don’t sit on the fence; our people in the South-West don’t sit on the fence. Guide our people and let them know the truth,” Umahi said. On the 2027 governorship election in Ebonyi, Umahi dismissed opposition parties challenging Governor Francis Nwifuru’s re-election bid as “jokers”, adding that he would not watch another party take over the state. He said Ebonyi had 1.8 million registered voters and challenged the state to deliver at least 1.3 million votes for Tinubu and Nwifuru. “We have 1.8 million registered voters in Ebonyi State. If we do not deliver at least 1.3 million votes for the President and the Governor, then we are doing ourselves a great disservice,” he said. The post 2027: South-East Has No Presidential Candidate, Umahi Declares appeared first on Channels Television .

title: 2027: Christian, Muslim youth groups sign peace accord ahead of elections
body:
Christian and Muslim youth organisations in Lagos have signed an interreligious peace accord, committing to reject political violence, religious intolerance and the use of young people as political thugs ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The accord was signed on Saturday at the South-West Zonal Interreligious Peace Accord Summit organised by the Youth Wing of the Christian Association of Nigeria (YOWICAN), in collaboration with the National Council of Muslim Youth Organisations (NACOMYO).
The summit was held at the Senator Oluremi Tinubu CAN Secretariat, Alausa, Ikeja, Lagos, with the theme, “Building Bridges of Faith and Politics: Strengthening Peace, Unity, and National Development Through Christian-Muslim Collaboration.”
The groups said the 2027 elections would test Nigeria’s unity and urged young people not to allow politicians to recruit or manipulate them into violence.
In the communique issued at the end of the summit, the groups said the signing of the accord represents their collective determination to reject political violence, religious manipulation, hate speech and other divisive actions “capable of threatening the peace and stability of the country.”
They also called on Christian and Muslim youths to promote tolerance and peaceful coexistence in their communities, institutions and places of worship.
Speaking at the summit, the Chairman of CAN in Lagos State, Stephen Adegbite, said the peace accord aims to foster religious tolerance, reject political violence, and promote peaceful coexistence ahead of the elections.
Mr Adegbite criticised politicians who make derogatory statements against their opponents.
“What we must do is what youths have done today; both Christians and Muslims have done well to bring peace and restore confidence in our great nation,” he said.
He urged young people to lead by example, saying the summit was intended to demonstrate that Christians and Muslims want peace before, during and after the elections.
“We don’t want anybody to be killed for any elective position,” he said.
Mr Adegbite also cited the Bible and the Quran as texts that promote peaceful coexistence.
The National Secretary of NACOMYO, Shehu Ibrahim, said the accord is particularly important as the country approaches the 2027 elections.
Mr Ibrahim said the organisation would take the message of peace to communities across the country, including through Imams, Friday prayers, Islamic schools and other religious gatherings.
He said the groups would mobilise young people at the grassroots to discourage violence during the elections.
Also speaking, the Lagos State APC Youth Leader, Damilare Orimoloye, said young people must understand that disagreements do not have to result in violence.
“Peace speaks against violence, how to tolerate each other, showing love amidst misunderstanding,” Mr Orimoloye said.
He added that disagreements were likely during the election period, making tolerance and peaceful communication important.
The South-West Chairman of YOWICAN, Nnamdi Obasi, said the summit was significant because Christian and Muslim youths needed to bridge existing gaps and avoid being used against one another.
He urged young Nigerians to remain united and resist attempts by politicians to exploit religious differences to create conflict as the 2027 elections approach.
The communique, signed by YOWICAN’s National Chairman, Orowolo Daniel, and National Secretary, Nehemiah Michael, alongside NACOMYO’s National Secretary II, Shehu Ibrahim, and its representative for the Southern Secretary, Mudashir Bello, outlined seven commitments.
Among them is a rejection of the recruitment and manipulation of young people as political thugs, as well as a commitment to religious tolerance and peaceful coexistence.
The groups also called on religious, traditional, community and political leaders to discourage intolerance, political manipulation and incitement to violence.
They said the peace message should extend beyond the summit to states, local government areas, communities, schools and religious institutions.
The groups further resolved that the peace accord should not end with its signing but should serve as a framework for continued dialogue, mutual accountability and peacebuilding between Christian and Muslim youths.
They urged Nigerian youths, political leaders, religious institutions and other stakeholders to work towards a peaceful and inclusive 2027 election.

title: Syria seeks Islamist expansion into Lebanon, Golan to serve Turkish interests, expert tells 'Post'
body: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa is serving Turkish interests by seeking to join the Mecca Pact and expand a Sunni Islamist axis led by the Muslim Brotherhood, potentially positioning it to fill the power vacuum should Iran's Islamic regime fall, Yoni Ben-Menachem, a senior researcher at the Jerusalem Center for Public Affairs, told The Jerusalem Post on Sunday.Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani confirmed on Saturday that “discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the Mecca alliance,” according to Syrian state media. The alliance currently includes Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and, potentially soon, Egypt, bringing together several major Sunni powers.“They estimate that Iran is about to collapse, so they created this Mecca Pact, this Mecca alliance, which will also include Sunni countries that are not part of the Muslim Brotherhood but are also Sunni. They will fill the vacuum left by the collapse of the Shi'ite axis following the fall of the Iranian regime,” he said, theorizing that Qatar would soon announce it is considering joining.Despite this, Iran has responded positively so far to the Mecca Pact, with experts previously telling the Post that the regime viewed the new security alliance as a shift away from Washington, weakening the United States' power in the Middle East and Gulf. Senior officials from the pact countries held open talks with Tehran in Iran last week.He noted that since the fall of the Assad regime, there have been growing calls among Syrians in large-scale demonstrations and mosques calling for jihad against Israel, specifically to claim the Golan Heights, territory Israel claimed during the 1967 Six Day War.Expansionist ambitions go beyond Israel's security zone, Menachem arguesagainst Israel, specifically to claim the Golan Heights, territory Israel claimed during the 1967 Six Day War.That desire for expansion, he continued, was not simply a response to Israel's security zone, though Menachem argued that it justified the zone's presence, but part of an expansionist aspiration.“They always had aspirations to take over Lebanon, and up until 2005, there was a military presence of the Syrian army in Lebanon,” he said. “They had to withdraw from Lebanon after the assassination of Rafic Hariri,  the [former] Lebanese prime minister.”Syria seeks to rebuild army from armed groups with Turkish supportNow, Syria is focused on building up its army with the more than 130 armed groups currently dispersed across the country, with Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham forming the “backbone” of this new venture, he continued, all with Turkish support.“According to Israeli security sources, this new army poses a danger to Israel if it succeeds in being formed, because its members are jihadists who are considering attacking Israel in the future. They are also supported by Turkey, which is very hostile toward Israel,” Menachem said.“This is why Israel says the threat justifies the establishment of the security zone. We cannot take the risk of withdrawing from the zone, because they could do to us what Hamas did to the Jewish communities along the Gaza border.”

title: CAR president thanks Russian specialists for helping rebuild army
body:
MOSCOW, November 1. /TASS/. Russian military specialists have helped the Central African Republic (CAR) rebuild its army and train military personnel, President Faustin-Archange Touadera told TASS.
"Thanks to Russian military experts, we have been able to rebuild our army, train our soldiers to defend our territory and borders against hostile forces, reestablish full control over the territory of the Central African Republic, and restore security," he said.

title: Russian diplomat dismisses talk of Russia’s isolation as wishful thinking
body:
VIENNA, November 1. /TASS/. All the talk of Russia's isolation on the world political stage is nothing more than an attempt to pass off wishful thinking as reality, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the Vienna-based international organizations Mikhail Ulyanov said, commenting on the recent Russia-Africa summit.
"The isolation of Russia is nothing more than the West’s wishful thinking," he wrote on X, commenting on a user’s post, saying that they were told in Europe that "Russia would end up isolated due to the war in Ukraine" whereas the fact 48 out of 54 African Union countries took park in the third Russia-Africa summit suggests otherwise.
"By definition, 12 percent of the world’s population can not isolate the largest country , which has so many friends around the world. And it is not even 12 percent-it is much less-since Russia also has so many friends in Western countries," Ulyanov added.
The third Russia-Africa summit ended in Moscow on October 3. It was attended by 48 African delegations, including 22 heads of state. The previous two summit were held in St. Petersburg in the summer of 2023, and in Sochi in the fall of 2019.

title: Indra backlog tops €22 billion as defence revenues double and IRIS² contracts lift orders
body: Orders totalled €8.085 billion in January–September, with third-quarter intake rising 139% year-on-year, mainly because of IRIS² contracts in the Space division. Group revenues increased 29% over the nine months, with every division reporting growth and Air Traffic revenues rising 23%. In August, the SpaceRISE consortium concluded negotiations with the European Commission and European Space Agency for the development of IRIS². The consortium comprises Eutelsat, SES and Hispasat, in which Indra holds a majority stake. Hispasat will act as prime contractor for the ground infrastructure and help develop the system’s very-low-Earth-orbit layer. IRIS² is due to enter service in 2030, giving Indra a role in a programme intended to strengthen Europe’s secure communications and technological sovereignty. Nine-month EBITDA rose 62% and EBIT increased 42% from a year earlier. The EBIT margin widened to 9.8% from 8.8%, while net profit grew 22% to €355 million. Free cash flow reached €1.692 billion, compared with €57 million in the first nine months of 2025. Indra maintained its full-year targets of revenue above €7 billion in local currency, EBIT exceeding €700 million and free cash flow of more than €375 million. During the quarter, Indra announced an agreement to acquire 30% of cybersecurity company TRC to complement its IndraMind offering. It also announced the acquisition of Dares Technology within Defence and the purchase of an industrial plant in As Pontes, Galicia. The board approved a management restructuring on 29 September, appointing Juan Ramón Hernández as general manager of Defence and Space and Frank Torres as general manager of Operations. The changes also bring international activities into the business units, merge Air Traffic with Mobility, and establish a Strategy, Technology and Product management function.

title: Zelensky says he is ready to meet Putin in Türkiye
body:
He said this in an interview with CNN Türk , according to Ukrinform.
“Yes, we are ready. We are ready for this meeting in Türkiye. Turkey’s position on this issue is clear. President Erdogan’s position is clear. We have close and good relations with Türkiye,” Zelensky said in response to a question about his readiness to meet Putin in the country.
The President said Türkiye could be a practical and realistic mediator and also recalled Ankara’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
“I know that President Erdogan has his own communication with Putin. Therefore, we support a meeting in Türkiye,” he stressed.
According to Zelensky, despite talks held in various formats by technical teams and delegations, the war continues. He stressed that a meeting between the leaders is necessary because societies expect the war to end and concrete progress through diplomacy.
“Technical teams may have difficulties achieving results during meetings. But I do not think there is a problem that we, the leaders, cannot resolve if we demonstrate our will. That is why I want to meet as one of those who make decisions,” the President said.
In addition, Zelensky believes that security guarantees, Ukraine’s reconstruction and the territorial issue should be discussed at the leaders’ level.
At the same time, the President stressed that Ukraine would not give up its territories and would not recognize the temporarily occupied territories, including Crimea, as Russian, as this would contradict the Constitution and the will of Ukrainian society.
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 31, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky met with President of Türkiye Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Istanbul. A significant part of the talks focused on finding ways to unblock the Black Sea. The leaders also discussed the possibility of holding peace talks in Türkiye.

title: Iranian ship captain martyred in US attack on vessel in PG
body:
TEHRAN, Nov. 01 (MNA) – An Iranian ship captain was martyred in a US attack on his vessel in the Persian Gulf on Friday.
Nasser Ebrahimi Nejadian, an Iranian ship captain from Abadan, was killed by shrapnel on Friday following a US attack on a vessel in international waters of the Persian Gulf, Iranian media reported on Sunday
The incident happened on Friday, Cctober 30, the media also said.
The farewell ceremony for the martyr's body will be held on Sunday, November 1, at 8:30 PM at the night gathering place of Shahid Montazeri Park in Abadan.

title: From APKWS to LADAC: France joins the race for cheap laser-guided rockets to down drones
body: Recent months have left little doubt that conflicts in which an adversary launches massed raids of one-way attack drones and cruise missiles cannot be won with traditional, costly weapons alone. More economical solutions are essential. For at least two years, the United States has been relying not only on advanced and expensive missiles such as the AIM-9 Sidewinder and AIM-120 AMRAAM, but also on the long-established, inexpensive 70 mm (2.75-inch) rocket, carried by fighters in underwing launchers. Adapting it for the counter-drone role took several years of development and extensive testing. The result is the configuration now used by the US Air Force: the Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS) II. From unguided rocket to drone killer The key change is guidance. Thanks to a guidance section developed by BAE Systems and installed mid-body, between the motor and the warhead, the formerly unguided rocket now homes in on a target illuminated by a laser designator, including targets in the air. The kit can be used by aircraft such as the F-16, F-15 and A-10. Because the weapon demands considerable skill, particularly in designating airborne targets, pilots need dedicated training and exercises before using it in combat. The most striking feature is the sheer number of rounds a single aircraft can carry. An F-16 – a type that has frequently used this capability against drones launched by the Houthis in Yemen – can be fitted with up to six seven-round launchers, giving it 42 guided rockets on a single counter-drone sortie. Combined with the internal cannon, this loadout meets the air force’s current requirements for countering massed raids. Lessons from April 2024 The lack of such a capability was painfully exposed during Iran’s massed drone and missile attack on Israel on the night of 13–14 April 2024. Allied fighters, typically carrying around four air-to-air missiles each, were forced out of the engagement once their weapons stations were empty. Attempts to engage drones with guns proved largely unsuccessful. The lessons learned from that night contributed to the wider adoption of APKWS in the air-to-air role. France: MICA stocks run dry In recent months, France has begun employing a similar solution based on its own 68 mm rockets, close in calibre to the American 70 mm round. Like every country confronted with cheap drones in recent conflicts, France urgently needed a less expensive domestic weapon. By spring 2026, its stocks of MICA IR/EM missiles were running low. While protecting the airspace of the United Arab Emirates, French Rafales expended a significant share of their MICA inventory, at an estimated unit cost of around USD 700,000. For a time, these medium-range missiles were used against Shahed-type drones costing an estimated EUR 50,000–80,000 each, despite the unfavourable cost-exchange ratio. Once missiles ran short, pilots were left with the far cheaper but risky and demanding option of engaging drones with the cannon. The interim domestic solution, which has proved successful, was developed jointly by the French defence procurement agency (DGA) and the French Air and Space Force’s test and evaluation centre. The programme, named LADAC (*Lutte Anti-Drone sur Avion de Combat* – counter-drone warfare from combat aircraft), is set to equip both the Rafale and the Mirage 2000 RMV. The 68 mm rockets will be integrated on the Rafale in 12-tube launchers, compared with the seven-tube launchers used by US F-16s for APKWS. Thales has also proposed the Telson JF12 launcher, which works with the aircraft’s radar and the company’s TALIOS targeting pod, used to track and laser-designate targets. The associated munition is most likely the Aculeus LG laser-guided rocket, with a range of up to 7 km. Light jets as drone hunters It is not yet clear whether lighter, cheaper aircraft are being considered in France. Elsewhere in Europe, however, interest is growing in light combat and advanced jet trainers as a way of reducing the cost of airborne drone hunting – among them the Czech L-39 Skyfox, the Italian M-346 and the Korean FA-50, which Poland has recently begun using for quick reaction alert duties. Czech manufacturer Aero Vodochody recently announced that it had signed a letter of intent with Thales Belgium covering the integration of Thales guided rockets on its platform. The agreement could pave the way for a low-cost European drone hunter in the same class as the M-346 and the FA-50GF/PL used by Poland. Such a combination could significantly cut the cost of counter-drone missions by pairing long-undervalued trainer and light attack aircraft with some of the cheapest drone-capable munitions on the market. These aircraft are considerably cheaper to operate – reportedly around half the cost of an F-16 – but their limited payload restricts the weapons they can carry. The L-39 Skyfox, for example, can carry around 1.6 tonnes on five hardpoints, two of which may be occupied by external fuel tanks – essential for the long endurance that counter-drone patrols demand. That leaves little room for air-to-air missiles such as the AIM-9 Sidewinder, which cost several hundred thousand dollars apiece. Rockets costing in the low tens of thousands of dollars each are therefore an attractive option, especially as seven FZ275 LGR rounds fit into a single Thales FZ800 launcher. FZ275 LGR: range and lethality The rockets allow drones to be engaged from several kilometres away, far safer than closing to a few hundred metres to fire a 12.7 mm gun pod from an L-39. The FZ275 LGR is a 2.75-inch (70 mm) rocket fitted with deployable fins, a semi-active laser seeker and a warhead optimised against drones and similar aerial targets. The 4.1 kg warhead consists of several thousand steel balls surrounding about 1 kg of explosive, producing a fragment cloud with a lethal radius of several tens of metres. The quoted range of up to 7 km most likely applies to ground targets or to launches at high altitude, where the rocket can glide after its motor burns out roughly one second into flight. Against airborne targets, the effective range may be as little as half the advertised figure. About the author Col. (Ret.) Józef M. Brzezina, a former Polish Air Force officer, is a defense writer and analyst with more than 25 years of experience contributing to leading military publications and online outlets. His work focuses on unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), manned combat aviation, and the employment of weapons and military equipment in modern armed conflict.

title: Sudan army voices regret over South Sudanese role in war
body: Sudan’s Army Chief of Staff, Lt. Gen. Yassir al-Atta, has expressed regret over the alleged recruitment of tens of thousands of South Sudanese nationals by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to fight in Sudan’s war. Speaking to troops in Khartoum on Sunday, al-Atta described South Sudan as a “sisterly country” but accused the RSF of recruiting thousands of its nationals as mercenaries. “Unfortunately, there are tens of thousands of mercenaries from our sisterly country, South Sudan,” he said. He also accused the RSF of recruiting fighters from Chad, Libya, Niger, Ethiopia, Somalia, other West African countries and Colombia. Sudan and South Sudan share a long border and maintain close economic ties. South Sudan relies on Sudanese infrastructure to transport its oil exports to international markets. A UN Panel of Experts on South Sudan said in an April 2024 report that South Sudanese nationals had fought on both sides of Sudan’s conflict. Some had joined independently, while others appeared to have been forcibly recruited. The report did not establish that they were acting on behalf of the South Sudanese government. Former South Sudanese Interior Minister Angelina Teny also acknowledged in November 2023 that South Sudanese nationals were participating in the conflict. Al-Atta further accused the United Arab Emirates and Israel’s intelligence agency, Mossad, of supporting the RSF, portraying the conflict as a campaign against foreign-backed efforts to undermine Sudan. He also sought to distance the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) military campaign from ethnic targeting in Darfur and Kordofan, saying the army had no intention of targeting communities or seeking revenge for atrocities allegedly committed by RSF fighters. Al-Atta named the Hawazma, Misseriya, Rizeigat, Habbaniya, Beni Halba and Salamat tribes, saying they are not targets of the military campaign. He indicated that the army intends to fight the RSF and its “mercenaries” in Darfur and Kordofan. “We are fighting a war that does not belong to any tribe, nor to communities in specific geographical areas of our beloved country,” he said. He added that the army is seeking to protect civilians in Darfur and Kordofan rather than punish entire communities for the actions of the RSF. ‘We are going to fight the mercenaries,’ he said. al-Atta also said attacks on electricity and infrastructure would not deter the army from defeating the RSF and capturing all Sudanese territory. The RSF and the South Sudanese government had yet to comment on al-Atta’s remarks. Sudan’s war erupted in April 2023 following a power struggle between the army, led by General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, and the RSF, commanded by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti. The conflict has divided control of the country, with the army holding most of the north, east and central regions, while the RSF controls much of Darfur and parts of Kordofan. The post Sudan army voices regret over South Sudanese role in war appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Article of Faith: Ways of the Kingdom of God (1), By Femi Aribisala
body:
Jeremiah had a bone to pick with God. He asked:
“Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why are those happy who deal so treacherously?” (Jeremiah 12:1).
God offered him no satisfactory answer. Instead, He assured him that more things would confound him. God replied Jeremiah’s question with a question:
“If you have raced with men on foot and they have worn you out, how can you compete with horses?” (Jeremiah 12:5).
The wicked prosper because the prosperity of men is not the prosperity of God. God can give what men give, and He sometimes does. But men cannot give what God gives. The prosperity that comes from men is temporal. But God’s prosperity is eternal.
It is like the current fad of regular exercise from going to the gym. Paul says instead:
Exercise yourself toward godliness. For bodily exercise profits a little, but godliness is profitable for all things, having promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come. (1 Timothy 4:7-8).
Men give what only has value in this world. But God gives what has value in this world and in the world to come.
The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly. (John 10:10).
Everything man values can be stolen, killed, or destroyed. But nothing like that can happen to things of God. Solomon says:
“I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever. Nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it.” (Ecclesiastes 3:14).
The blessings of God are everlasting, while those of men are time-bound. That means the blessings of men can be lost, and what can be lost can bring sorrow. But,
The blessing of the Lord makes one rich, and He adds no sorrow with it. (Proverbs 10:22).
The riches of this world must be relinquished.
For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. (1 Timothy 6:7).
That means the riches of this world are fake. They are illusory.
For riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away like an eagle toward heaven. (Proverbs 23:5).
True riches must be eternal. They only come from God.
Habakkuk faces a dilemma similar to Jeremiah’s. He asks God: “Why are things so bad and You do nothing?” “How can things be this bad when You are so good?”
God does not explain. Instead, He tells Habakkuk, “Just Wait. I am going to make things so much worse.”
Kingdom dynamics refer to God’s seemingly peculiar ways. Occasionally, we can understand why God does things the way He does. But He does not owe us an explanation. The important thing is to know the ways He does things and come to terms with them.
With God, expect the unexpected. Expect the extraordinary. The commonplace is of men. God can do and sometimes does the ordinary. But He only does this to humour men. His speciality is the extraordinary. God can do what man does. But man cannot do the amazing things God does.
Moreover, if we deserve what we get, then it is unlikely to be from God. God gives what we do not deserve. He says:
I will show mercy to anyone I choose, and I will show compassion to anyone I choose. (Exodus 33:19).
Solomon throws more light on this peculiarity:
“The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise, nor riches to men of understanding, nor favour to men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.” (Ecclesiastes 9:11).
Therefore, with God, be ready to receive what you don’t deserve.
If you can easily understand what is happening and why, then it is likely to be of men. But if you cannot easily understand it, then it is more likely to be of God. So, don’t be surprised if what happens to you surpasses your understanding.
Believe all things. (1 Cor 13:7). That means assume the best in all circumstances, whether good or bad. God works all things together for good for His children. (Romans 8:28). Therefore, in everything, give thanks. (1 Thessalonians 5:18).
Kingdom dynamics validate God. They make us aware that the invisible God is at work. Jesus’ kingdom is not of this world. (John 18:36). Therefore, His actions will be peculiar. They will be extraordinary. If they were normal, they could easily have been man-made. But because they are peculiar, they obviously do not originate from this world.
Do not be held captive by what happened in the past. The past is never a blueprint for the present. God says:
Behold, I will do a new thing, now it shall spring forth; shall you not know it? I will even make a road in the wilderness and rivers in the desert. (Isaiah 43:19).
Don’t complain like the church in the wilderness if there is no water. God can bring water out of the desert. He even brought water out of a rock. Job testifies to this wonderful work of God. He recalled a time:
When (his) steps through rich pasturage were washed with butter, and the rock poured out for (him) streams of oil! (Job 29:6).
God is a God of originality. No two things of God are the same. No two fingerprints are the same. No two irises are duplicates.
Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever. But He is the same in that He always does new things, and not that He only does the same things.
Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus. (Philippians 3:13-14).
From now on, regard no one according to the flesh. (2 Corinthians 5:16).
That is the reason why many people missed Christ. He came in the flesh but was 100 per cent divine.
According to the flesh, Jesus was common. He was born in a manger of very poor parentage. His parents could not afford a lamb as a sacrifice for the male child who opens the womb. They had to make do with the poor man’s substitute of a pair of turtledoves. (Luke 2:22-24). (Leviticus 12:8).
Jesus came from Nazareth, a city not even on the map. When Philip introduced Him to Nathanael, he asked disparagingly:
“Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” (John 1:44).
Jesus did not go to school. He did not graduate from a Theological Seminary. This confounded the Jewish religious elite. They marvelled, asking:
“How does this Man know letters, having never studied?” (John 7:15).
But educational qualifications and credentials are only relevant in the world. They are irrelevant in the kingdom of God. God qualifies the unqualified and disqualified.
“For you see your calling, brethren, that not many wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called. But God has chosen the foolish things of the world to put to shame the wise, and God has chosen the weak things of the world to put to shame the things which are mighty; and the base things of the world and the things which are despised God has chosen, and the things which are not, to bring to nothing the things that are, that no flesh should glory in His presence. (1 Corinthians 1:26-29).
When Amos was challenged because of his pedigree, he said to Amaziah:
“I was no prophet, nor was I a son of a prophet, but I was a sheepbreeder and a tender of sycamore fruit. Then the Lord took me as I followed the flock, and the Lord said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel. Now therefore, hear the word of the Lord: You say, ‘Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not spout against the house of Isaac.’ Therefore thus says the Lord: ‘Your wife shall be a harlot in the city; your sons and daughters shall fall by the sword; your land shall be divided by survey line; you shall die in a defiled land.” Amos 7:14-17).
Don’t believe what you see, feel, or touch. That was the first contradiction I confronted in my relationship with God. He told me nothing would happen to me, and then I was shot. A bullet was lodged in my leg, but He insisted there was nothing wrong with my leg.
The naked eye cannot see what God is doing. Therefore:
Do not look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporary, but the things which are not seen are eternal. (2 Corinthians 4:18).
To see, we have to be blind. Jesus puts this cryptically. He says:
“For judgment I have come into this world, so that the blind will see and those who see will become blind.” (John 9:39).
When God sent Samuel to anoint a son of Jesse as king of Israel, He warned him:
“Do not look at his appearance or at his physical stature, because I have refused him. For the Lord does not see as man sees; for man looks at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.” (1 Samuel 16:7).
Children of God must learn to appreciate the beauty of holiness. (2 Chronicles 20:21). CONTINUED.

title: How to think about the midterms — and the political moment the country is in
body:
President Donald Trump spoke to members of the media during a Halloween party at his Mar-a-Lago club on October 31, 2026 in Palm Beach, Florida. Andrew Harnik/Getty Images North America hide caption
📲 Get the latest on the midterms & more in the NPR App
President Trump was elected in 2024, in large measure, with a mandate to bring down prices. But that hasn't happened. Instead, Trump is facing record-low approval ratings, record-high intensity of opposition, and voters are blaming him for prices that have continued to rise since he took office this second time around.
Most presidents get more blame and credit than they deserve for the economy. But the war with Iran and Trump's tariffs were choices that have directly led to increased prices on goods and energy.
The economy is increasingly bifurcated with the wealthy doing well, in large part, because of increasing stock portfolios dominated by AI companies, while regular Americans are turning against AI data centers, struggling because of inflation that is outpacing wages, a middling labor market and interest rates that are creeping higher. Those rates are making it harder to buy a home or a car, making millions of people feel like they're treading water.
The latest NPR/PBS News/Marist poll showed a plurality — 44% — said their finances have mostly stayed the same and another 38% saying their economic situations have worsened. Only 15% said things have actually gotten better for them from a money standpoint.
Add to that the disapproval of the administration's hard-line immigration enforcement tactics, cuts to domestic spending on programs like Medicaid and other health care programs, and the slashing of regulations and the government workforce, and it's angering swing voters and firing up Democrats.
As a result, the president's party is likely to pay the price. Midterms are usually difficult for the president's party to begin with.
Only twice since World War II has the president's party gained seats in the House in a midterm election. On average, the president's party loses 26 seats in midterm years, and it's worse when a president's approval rating is below 50%, as Trump's has been. When that's the case, the presidents' parties have lost an average of 35 seats. When they're above 50%, they still lose seats but only 15 on average, 20 seats better than when a president is unpopular.
The fact that presidents' parties lose seats in midterms is something Trump himself has acknowledged multiple times at campaign events.
Meanwhile, Democrats have had political success in this Trump term. They have consistently overperformed in special elections, which are indicators of midterm prowess, and they cleaned up in the 2025 off-year elections. Since then, the political landscape has only gotten worse for Republicans because of the unpopular Iran war that has led to skyrocketing gas prices.
All of that points to Democratic gains this cycle. They are favored to win control of the House, and they are in striking distance of winning the Senate, something that had been seen as a longshot at the beginning of this cycle.
While the landscape has undoubtedly moved more in Democrats' direction over the last several months, the extent of the likely potential gains is not clear.
A big reason for that is structural. When looking at the Cook Political Report's ratings, there are about 30 fewer competitive districts — ones rated as lean or toss up — this year than in 2018 when Democrats won a net gain of more than 40 seats in the House.
Mid-decade redistricting has also helped to insulate Republicans this cycle, even if marginally. After all the redistricting fights across the country, with Trump explicitly pushing GOP-led state legislatures to get more Republican seats, an NPR analysis shows Republicans netted an estimated 8-seat advantage out of redistricting.
Depending on how Latinos in South Texas, in particular, vote those gains might be lower.
While Republicans face significant headwinds and the GOP is not viewers favorably, the Democratic Party is also not viewed positively. Democrats have had trouble wrangling a base of voters who should be Democrats but are restive and unsatisfied by the party.
That said, the latest NPR poll showed that self-identified "democratic socialists" were very engaged in these midterms and hotly disapprove of the job Trump is doing.
As the old saying goes, the enemy of my enemy is my friend. This group of voters may vote in big numbers in this election as a check on Trump — 44% of poll respondents said their vote was a vote against Trump while 21% said it was a vote for him. But there's a likely clash of ideals and approach coming on the left over the next several months, as the Democratic presidential primaries.
And make no mistake, the 2028 election begins almost immediately after these midterms. It's an open election — the first one post-Trump, post-Obama-Biden, post-Clintons and Bushes. Candidates who want to make a splash and need a national boost tend to announce earlier rather than later. Think: January, February.
It's important to remember nothing is a done deal until the results are in. A lot of this is going to come down to Republican turnout.
That's why Trump has been deployed to red states to try and push and plead with his base to get out and vote. Without a big GOP turnout in these places, a one- or two-seat pick up for Democrats in the Senate can quickly turn into six or seven.
Be ready for surprises. But if Democrats don't win the House, it would be the shocker of all shockers and represent a polling error like we haven't seen this century.
While most states and districts will be called by the time people go to bed on election night, some will not. Those lingering races may be in key places, and given the margins, particularly in the Senate, it's possible party control won't be known for days, if not weeks.
Trump is already laying the groundwork for claims of rigged elections. That's no surprise. He's done that after every election that hasn't gone his way previously in one way or another. After the 2020 election, his false claims of fraud led to the Jan. 6 siege at the Capitol.
The latest NPR poll found most people across parties overwhelmingly believe their states will run fair and accurate elections and that their preferred candidate should accept the outcome, no matter what it is.
But a quarter of Republicans said their candidate likely shouldn't accept the results. That leaves room for potential chaos and misinformation if elections are close and not decided for weeks.
Trump has been a clear drag on the GOP this cycle. You don't have to believe polls to know it's the case. Look at what Republican candidates are doing. Their mentions in ads of Trump during the primaries were sky high.
Republicans will admit privately that Trump is a double-edged sword — he's needed with the base, but toxic with swing voters.
And that's been the story of Trump for the past decade — beloved by an ardent slice of the country and loathed by an even bigger one.
But this year, with the economic strain on people and the U.S.'s continued involvement in the kind of ongoing war he promised to keep the country out of, polls have found consistently over a long period of time this year that his support with many of those who crossed over to vote for him in 2024 has cratered.
That hardly sets up Trump and his party for success Tuesday and beyond — despite what will be claims of nefariousness that will hold little weight. But that doesn't mean either party will have massive majorities, and compromise will be necessary to get big things done.
NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. Anyone who makes such an offer or request is not an NPR employee and does not represent NPR.

title: Mbappe Scores After China Controversy As Madrid Beat Santander
body: Kylian Mbappe moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander on Sunday. The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d’Or to Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. Real Madrid’s match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout. Real Madrid’s Ivorian forward #25 Yan Diomande (C) celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Spanish league football match between Racing de Santander and Real Madrid CF at El Sardinero Stadium in Santander on November 1, 2026. (Photo by ANDER GILLENEA / AFP) Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande were also on target to keep third-place Madrid within three points of leaders Barcelona, who thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday. Jose Mourinho’s side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind city rivals Atletico Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0. “In the first half we were very strong; we came out to play well,” Mourinho told reporters. “The team is growing and playing well; I think we should have scored even more goals with the chances we had.” Mbappe won a soft penalty as he went down under little pressure from Matteo Prati, smashing it home to put Madrid ahead at the Sardinero stadium in the 11th minute. It was the 27-year-old’s 12th league goal of the season, trailing only Barcelona’s Raphinha with 15 in the scoring charts. Madrid had control of the game, and a fine pass from Arda Guler sent Bellingham through on goal for the second. The England international knocked the ball past the goalkeeper and rolled home for his 50th goal since joining Madrid in 2023. Guler spun a good opportunity for the third after being set up by Mbappe, before Madrid’s record-signing Diomande lashed home from the edge of the box. The hosts started the second half well, pushing Madrid back, much to the chagrin of Mourinho, who yelled at his players. Madrid regained their control and racked up several more chances, with Mbappe hitting the post and Bellingham denied by Racing goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala. Racing won a penalty after Madrid’s Aurelien Tchouameni handled in the box, but the award was cancelled after a VAR review. Bellingham had a second goal ruled out in stoppage time after he strayed offside before finding the net, and Endrick bent an effort narrowly wide from distance. Hosts Racing, 16th, back in La Liga for the first time in 14 seasons, fell to their first home defeat of the campaign. Earlier, Sevilla, sixth, suffered a 3-1 loss at Getafe, who moved into mid-table. “(Madrid’s penalty award) annoys me,” Racing coach Jose Alberto told DAZN. “Evidently we came across a great Madrid, who put us under a lot of pressure in the first half hour and were much better than us, but what conditions? Everything was the first goal and the penalty.” Later, on Sunday, Athletic Bilbao host Real Sociedad in a Basque derby, and Valencia visit Elche. The post Mbappe Scores After China Controversy As Madrid Beat Santander appeared first on Channels Television .

title: APM Members Defect To PDP In Katsina, Back Danmarke’s Governorship Bid
body: At least 5,000 members of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) in Katsina State have reportedly joined the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), pledging support for the party’s governorship candidate, Senator Yakubu Lado Danmarke, ahead of the 2027 elections. The defectors, led by the Chairman of Katsina Frontiers, Alhaji Aliyu Sani, formally joined the PDP at a rally in Katsina on Sunday. Sani said the decision followed the group’s confidence in Danmarke’s leadership qualities and record of humanitarian support, particularly for the poor, vulnerable, elderly and children. He cited the senator’s provision of food and cash assistance, especially during Ramadan, describing him as a humble and compassionate leader who puts the welfare of the people above personal comfort and material wealth. Also speaking at the rally, Muhammad Hassan El-Makki said Katsina needed a leader genuinely committed to the well-being of its people. He described Danmarke as experienced and capable of transforming agriculture, healthcare, energy and infrastructure, while pointing to his scholarship programmes and contributions to community development. El-Makki urged residents to support the senator’s governorship ambition, describing him as “tested and trusted” in humanitarian service. In his remarks, Danmarke thanked the new members for joining the PDP, saying their defection reflected growing confidence in the party and his candidacy. He said the new entrants included political structures associated with a former governorship aspirant, prominent personalities, retirees and grassroots coordinators from across the state. Danmarke identified insecurity as Katsina’s most pressing challenge, pledging to make restoring security his administration’s immediate priority if elected. He also promised to revive the education, health, agriculture and infrastructure sectors, while accusing the incumbent administration of failing to meet the expectations of residents. The PDP candidate called on the people of Katsina to join what he described as the party’s movement for change, promising people-centred governance and a rebuilding of the state. The state PDP Chairman, Alhaji Nura Amadi Kurfi, gave the vote of thanks, expressing confidence that Lado’s candidacy would usher in progress and development in Katsina. The post APM Members Defect To PDP In Katsina, Back Danmarke’s Governorship Bid appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Ukraine’s air defenses down 274 Russian drones, six Banderols on Sunday
body:
The Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
According to the military, from 6:30 to 19:00 on Sunday, Russian forces attacked Ukraine with 326 attack UAVs (55 of them jet-powered), Gerbera and other types of drones, as well as six S8000 Banderol/Dan-T loitering munitions.
Preliminary reports indicate that air defenses shot down or jammed 274 enemy drones, 46 of them jet-powered, as well as six S8000 Banderol/Dan-T munitions.
At this time, according to the Air Force, more than 20 Russian UAVs are still in Ukrainian airspace. Combat operations against the enemy targets are ongoing.
As reported by Ukrinform, on November 1, Russian forces attacked the Koziatyn community in the Vinnytsia region, killing two people and injuring four others.

title: Up to three years in jail for insulting Oman's national anthem
body: Insulting the national anthem of Oman could now result in a three-year prison sentence under a decree issued by Sultan Haitham . The punishment for failing to respect the anthem Salute to the Sultan has been brought in line with the penalty for insulting the country's flag. Published on Sunday, the decree covers anyone who "desecrates the anthem verbally, in writing, by gesturing, by distorting it, or by committing any other act that conveys hatred or contempt". Anyone found guilty of such behaviour is to be imprisoned for no less than three months and no more than three years, the decree says. The same penalty already applies to anyone who lowers or destroys Oman's flag, or conveys "hatred or contempt" for the flag or emblem. No reason was given for the crackdown. Several other countries have introduced similar laws. France passed a law in 2003 introducing fines for booing the national anthem, La Marseillaise . Hong Kong introduced prison sentences of up to three years in 2020 for insulting China 's anthem, March of the Volunteers . A first prison sentence was handed down in 2023 to a man who mixed the anthem with a protest song. Oman's Salute to The Sultan was composed in 1932. It was rewritten in 1970 after Sultan Qaboos came to power, and again in 2020 when he was succeeded by Sultan Haitham .

title: Boeing CEO says order for 22 more F-15EX fighters brings total under contract to 120
body: “In the quarter, we also received a contract to manufacture 22 more F-15EX aircraft for the U.S. Air Force,” Ortberg said during Boeing’s third-quarter earnings call. “This award brings the total number of aircraft under contract to 120, with the potential for additional upside as the F-15EX continues to demonstrate the value of its unmatched payload and range capability.” Ortberg returned to the fighter during the analyst question-and-answer session, referring to “a big new order on F-15EX, and there’s more to come on that.” He did not identify the prospective customer, quantity or timing of any further order. The F-15EX contract adds to demand that has improved Boeing’s expectations for its defense business. Ortberg said the company had anticipated low single-digit defense revenue growth a year earlier but now expected growth “more towards the middle single digit or higher going forward.” Alongside F-15EX, he cited Boeing’s sixth-generation fighter selections, PAC-3 seeker production growth and progress on the MQ-25 and T-7 programs. He said demand across the defense portfolio and available budgets supported further growth. Ortberg also stressed the importance of contract terms as Boeing takes on new work after difficulties with earlier development programs. His comments covered the broader defense business, rather than the specific terms of the latest F-15EX agreement. “The important part is all these programs are also being underwritten with the right contract type,” he said. “Not only are we booking more orders, we’re booking more orders that won’t result in some of the challenges we’ve had.” Chief Financial Officer Jay Malave said Boeing Defense, Space & Security booked $23 billion in quarterly orders and ended the period with a record $101 billion backlog. The executives did not disclose the value of the additional F-15EX contract or when the 22 aircraft would be delivered. Source: Boeing Company (The) (BA) Q3 FY2026 earnings call transcript.pdf

title: Police Kill Suspected Robber, Recover Two Vehicles, Other Items In Ogun
body: The Ogun State Police Command says it has neutralised a suspected member of a robbery syndicate and recovered two vehicles, a locally made pistol and several other items following a robbery attempt in the Onipanu area of Ado-Odo/Ota Local Government Area. The police said operatives of the Onipanu Division, under the Ota Area Command, foiled the robbery in the early hours of Sunday, November 1, 2026, after responding to a distress call from a resident. In a statement issued in Abeokuta, the state capital, the Police Public Relations Officer, Oluseyi Babaseyi, said the patrol team arrived at the scene in Ijaba, Iyesi, Ota, at about 1:45am. He said the suspects opened fire on sighting the operatives, prompting the police to respond. “The ensuing exchange of gunfire resulted in the neutralisation of one suspect, while other gang members fled with suspected gunshot injuries,” Babaseyi said. A search conducted after the encounter led to the recovery of a Nissan Almera and a Toyota Camry, as well as a locally made pistol and two live cartridges. Other items suspected to have been stolen included HP and Dell laptops, a PlayStation console, four mobile phones, a Samsung television, a standing fan, a rechargeable radio, a Wi-Fi device, clothing, an OPay ATM card, a deck, two MP devices and other household items. The police also recovered a Tecno mobile phone, three passport photographs, an MTN SIM pack, two National Identification Number (NIN) cards and cash from the deceased suspect. Babaseyi said the Command had launched a manhunt for the fleeing members of the gang, particularly those who might have sustained gunshot injuries. He added that investigations were ongoing to establish the ownership of the recovered vehicles and other exhibits, as well as determine their possible links to other criminal activities. The Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, commended the operatives for their prompt response, professionalism and courage. He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to intelligence-led policing, sustained patrols and rapid response to security concerns across the state. The police urged residents to remain vigilant and report suspicious movements or activities, assuring them that the Command remained committed to protecting lives and property. The post Police Kill Suspected Robber, Recover Two Vehicles, Other Items In Ogun appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Judge tosses Trump's attempt to block Alaska Senate results if GOP incumbent loses
body:
President Trump listens as Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan of Alaska, who is running for reelection, speaks at an Oct. 13 campaign rally in Wasilla, Alaska. Alex Brandon/AP hide caption
A federal judge has thrown out the Trump administration's highly unusual attempt to block the certification of results from a key U.S. Senate race in Alaska if the Republican incumbent loses.
In a ruling released Sunday, U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason found the federal government does not have the ability to bring this lawsuit, which cited the preamble of the National Voter Registration Act.
It asked the judge to stop state officials from certifying election results to allow for an investigation into whether voters were confused by having two similarly named Senate candidates appear on Alaska's ranked-choice ballot.
But Judge Gleason concluded that such a court order would likely violate Alaskan voters' right to a secret ballot .
"The absence of any explanation from the United States as to how its requested relief could redress its alleged injury while simultaneously maintaining the secrecy of the ballot is telling," wrote Gleason, a nominee of former President Barack Obama.
The Justice Department is planning to appeal , spokesperson Kiersten Pels told NPR in a statement. "Alaskan voters deserve a fair election, not to be misled in an attempt to rig outcomes," Pels added.
Voting rights groups that stepped in to help defend Alaska against the lawsuit cheered the ruling.
"DOJ's attempt to throw out Alaska's election results before a single ballot was counted was lawless from the start, and the court saw it for exactly what it was. It was a reckless waste of taxpayer money aimed at silencing hundreds of thousands of Alaska voters," Sophia Lin Lakin, director of the American Civil Liberties Union's Voting Rights Project, said in a statement.
President Trump said he ordered this lawsuit to be filed because out of the four Senate candidates on Alaska's ballot , two have similar names — Sen. Dan Sullivan, the Republican incumbent, and Daniel Sullivan Jr., who is not affiliated with a political party.
Alaska's Republican Party supported an earlier effort in state court that tried to keep Sullivan Jr., the non-incumbent, off the ballot. But in June, the Alaska Supreme Court ruled Sullivan Jr. has the right to run as a candidate.
Still, Republican allegations of Democrats propping up Sullivan Jr. to spoil the incumbent Sullivan's chances of winning reelection have long hung over this closely watched Senate contest.
A New York Times report about Democratic campaign operatives' efforts to recruit Sullivan Jr. — which NPR has not independently confirmed — drew new attention to those allegations. Alaska's Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy has ordered an investigation and indicated the results of the race may not be certified by the state depending on how that investigation turns out.
"If we find out there's wrongdoing, and if that means that the certification then is stopped or changed, then that's what happens," Dunleavy said during an Oct. 30 interview with NewsNation .
At an Oct. 30 press conference in Anchorage, U.S. Attorney Michael Heyman said there is an "ongoing" criminal probe by the Justice Department.
The Democratic candidate, former Rep. Mary Peltola, has denied any involvement.
In an interview Sunday with CNN's State of the Union, incumbent Sullivan said that he would accept the election results, win or lose.
This controversy hasn't stopped Alaskans from voting. Over 86,700 voters in the state have cast their ballots during early voting , according to the latest figures from Alaska's Division of Elections . And more Alaskans are expected to exercise their rights as voting continues through Tuesday's Election Day.
Additional reporting by NPR's Eric McDaniel. Edited by Benjamin Swasey
