title: Iranians defy Islamic regime with Halloween celebrations as several reportedly detained
body: Iranians defied the Islamic regime over the past week by dressing up in costumes and celebrating Halloween despite restrictions and warnings, according to Iranian media reports and videos of the festivities shared online. Several people were reportedly detained and beaten for taking part in the celebrations.While some Western advocates have used footage of the celebrations to argue that claims about repression in the Islamic Republic are Western propaganda, Iranians have stressed that the festivities took place despite the regime, not because it is becoming more lenient.Her tweet is misleading and wrong. People in Iran have flouted the regime's repression by dressing up for Halloween for years, same for Valentine's Day, and Christmas—albeit to a lesser degree. The people of Iran push boundaries at their own risk (which very much still exists because repression is codified into law), it's not that the boundaries are being eased by the regime. Regime officials have already publicly commented on, and threatened, businesses that participate in Halloween events.— Nazanin Nour (@NazaninNour) October 30, 2026Nazanin Nour, an Iranian-American actress and writer, pushed back against such claims online, writing that the “people of Iran push boundaries at their own risk (which very much still exists because repression is codified into law); it's not that the boundaries are being eased by the regime.”Iranian security forces and plainclothes officers broke up a celebration in central Tehran on Friday, Iran International reported, citing witnesses. Several participants were reportedly beaten and detained.Young people wearing makeup and costumes were also dispersed by the Basij after gathering near Tehran's Artists Park, according to the report.Halloween in Tehran, Iran  https://t.co/T2ETwRFS3D— WANA Visuals (@wana_visualss) October 31, 2026“It was like the protests. They were running after people and shouting, 'Disperse!'” a witness told Iran International, describing how families were ordered to flee.In footage shared online, several women can also be seen defying the Islamic Republic's strict dress code by leaving their hair uncovered and exposing parts of their legs. The celebrations come amid a renewed crackdown on violations of Iran's mandatory hijab laws and efforts to redeploy morality police across the country.Restrictions with no basis in lawThe Iranian legal advocacy network Dadbaan warned earlier this week that new restrictions had been imposed on Halloween celebrations in several cities, prompting a number of cultural centers to cancel planned events. Isfahan's Isal Café and the Madam and Monsieur Mansion were among the venues that issued cancellation notices. Staff at the Madam and Monsieur Mansion specifically cited compliance with the law and “Islamic proprieties” as the reason for the decision.The Cultural Heritage Department in the city of Aran va Bidgol also prohibited Halloween celebrations, citing the need to preserve “Islamic and Iranian values.”Dadbaan emphasized that no law in Iran prohibits the sale of Halloween-related goods and items, the holding of celebrations, or the use of themed decorations in restaurants and cafés.The regime in #Iran grudgingly allows young men and women in Tehran to celebrate Halloween, while those it has recruited from Pakistan to Yemen, Kuwait, Iraq, and Lebanon are expected to die fighting for it. https://t.co/yzJt9VRpw0— Ahmed Quraishi (@_AhmedQuraishi) October 31, 2026The Islamic Republic has frequently cracked down on gothic and alternative subcultures, labeling them “satanic.” Even before the latest wars with Israel and the crackdown on January's protests, during which tens of thousands of people were reportedly killed by regime security forces, shops accused of selling clothing bearing “unconventional logos and symbols” had faced threats of closure.'Everyone protests individually'Beni Sabti, an Iran expert at INSS, told The Jerusalem Post that he believed Halloween had grown in size and significance in Iran this year, describing it as a kind of cultural protest.“Listening to music, playing music in the streets, going without hijab, all these clips that you see, it's kind of a protest,” he said. “They don't even know if they want to be in a huge protest. So everyone protests individually.”He noted that this year the costumes had become more daring, with masks and more gothic costumes, as opposed to the cat and mouse costumes seen in previous years.Halloween in Iran… The Islamic Republic calls Halloween a “Western vice” and tries to ban it. But young Iranians have a message for the ayatollahs: You don't get to decide how we live, dress, dance, or celebrate. While the new “supreme leader “ and other mullahs hide in fear, the young generation is out there celebrating their own lifestyle. The regime wants to turn Iran into a graveyard. This generation is determined to turn it into a dance floor.— Masih Alinejad (@AlinejadMasih) November 1, 2026

title: Israel, US have plan ready for third Iran war, Tehran's hidden weapons pose challenges - analysis
body: How a third Iran war would be fought has already taken shape.Foreign sources have reported that the Israeli Air Force flew through Syria and Iraq up to the Iranian border to rehearse its strikes on the Islamic Republic.Israel has already used its F-35s to outwit and eliminate Iran's radar four times dating back to April 2024, followed by using its F-15s and F-16s to carry out massive bombing raids.Over 200 Israeli fighter jets struck the Islamic Republic in the first wave in February of this year.The US and Israel carved up Iran into sectors, with Israel focused on the western and Tehran sectors, and American forces focused on the southern sector and some targets in the Tehran region.This plan worked and is likely to repeat itself on some level, with the first goal being to establish air supremacy so that drones, which are easier to shoot down than fighter jets but have advantages in being able to stand over a target for an extensive time period, can take a large role in the battle.There is little Iran can do to prevent Israeli and US aircraft dominance.Pickaxe Mountain: The facility where Iran could secretly make nuclear weaponsUS President Donald Trump has focused the most on the Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility.The reason is not that the facility is already operational, as sources have conveyed to The Jerusalem Post that it still is not.Rather, the reason is that it is unclear whether either Israeli or even US aircraft using mega 30,000 bunker-buster bombs can destroy it.And if Iran succeeded in moving both highly enriched uranium and centrifuges to that facility, as well as making it operational, it could conceivably sneak out to a nuclear weapon without anyone knowing or being able to do anything about it from the air.The US used 12 of its 30,000-pound Massive Ordnance Penetrator (MOP) bombs to destroy Iran's Fordow nuclear facility.Fordow was deep enough under a mountain that many senior Israeli military officials believed it could not be damaged long-term by the smaller Israeli weapons.The nuclear facility at Pickaxe Mountain is much deeper underground, such that more defense experts have raised doubts that even the US MOP bombs can destroy it.In that case, the best moves would be to cause cave-ins across the facility before any important nuclear material, machinery, or know-how makes it into the facility.Israeli officials have pressed Trump to deal with it, and anytime he has made threats relating to the facility, Iran has responded with harsh language, showing it also views the facility as one of its top strategic assets.Think tank identifies potential weak points at Pickaxe MountainA new survey of the facility published on Friday by the Institute for Science and International Security focuses on two ventilation shafts as possible targets to better strike the insides of the facility: the probable ventilation port/shaft north of the ridge and the possible ventilation shaft south of the ridge.This think tank report also flags the eastern and western primary tunnel entrances as the main likely points from which the Iranians would likely try to transport nuclear assets into the facility under the mountain.All of these locations would need to be struck at a minimum to try to disrupt the facility's functioning, but it is a large, sprawling facility with many other assets noticeable from satellite footage, which would also likely need to be struck.Of course, that is still only one strategic target.How will Israel handle Iran's underground ballistic missile facilities?In early 2026, Israel and the US mostly caused cave-ins at these facilities, only to find that within days and sometimes less than a day, Iran's bulldozer crews were able to reopen areas which had been caved in.Even over the nearly 40-day war, Israeli tactics did not change much and did little to solve this issue.In addition, between the June 2025 and early 2026 wars, Iran altered its ballistic missile strategy.Instead of trying to fire concentrated huge barrages from a small number of centralized locations, it spread out its missile crews across the country, and often fired only small barrages at a time.While these small barrages did not threaten massive nationwide harm, they did cause much of the country to regularly shut down, as they were more frequent and continuous.Also, Iran watched where Israel was centering its air defense, and adapted mid-war to strike other areas, at one point striking Israel's South with a high degree of lethality only days after the IDF had said the South could go back to its more regular routine for lack of Iranian missiles being fired at it.In early 2026, Iran also managed to destroy American bases in several countries, causing at least $5 billion in damage. All of this means that Iran can yield air supremacy to Israel and the US, while still managing to wreak havoc across the region, including against Israel.Has Israel figured out new techniques to take out the underground missile cities for longer, to find and destroy spread out missile crews, and to prevent Iran from taking advantage of Israel's shortage in air defense systems and interceptors?Length of a renewed Iran operationWill the operation last a few days or run on for weeks?Trump has said he wants a fast and "clean" three-day operation, but Iran's regime does not need to cooperate.They have said they will fire more directly on US ships, on underwater internet cables, and on critical energy facilities of US allies.Already, the Saudis have faced mass-casualty lethal attacks from the Houthis on high profile economic and transport facilities.And what will really be achieved in three days?If Iran retains ballistic missiles, some of its nuclear assets which remain under rubble, drones, and the ability to harass naval ships trying to pass through Hormuz, will it change its fundamental negotiating position because its military damage went from $200-300 billion to $220-320 billion?Many Israelis are skeptical that anything but a longer and more sustained operation will change Iran's behavior.Likewise, some Israelis, such as former defense minister Yoav Gallant, have suggested that only a ground operation, not airstrikes, can neutralize some of Iran's highly enriched uranium buried deep underground.US, Israeli targets in IranWill Israel and the US finally strike Iran's top energy facilities, which some Mossad officials believed could lead to regime change at an earlier date?Or will they hold back fearing such strikes will turn Iranians into supporting their regime and against any outsiders?What will happen when Trump wants to end the conflict earlier than Israel, and given that he, and especially his advisors, have lost interest or faith in any near-term regime change?How will Israelis feel about having been shot at by Iranian ballistic missiles for the fifth time in three years without the latest operation seeming to lead to a clearer end game regarding at least the nuclear threat, let alone the ballistic missile threat, or leading to regime change?There is no question that a US and Israeli third war against Iran can push off the nuclear, and especially the ballistic missile threats deeper into the future.But it is unclear how Israel will grade the success of such an operation.

title: Detained teenager confesses to promoting Nazism on TikTok — FSB video
body:
MOSCOW, November 1. /TASS/. The teenager, who was detained in Moscow during an investigation of US intelligence regarding preparations for a terror attack in Moscow’s Tsaritsyno Park, has confessed to have made posts with propaganda of Nazism on TikTok, according to a video released by the Federal Security Service (FSB).
"On my TikTok page, I posted various content promoting Nazism, fascism, and violence against migrants and people of other ethnicities," he said.
The FSB said earlier that while checking US intelligence regarding a potential terror attack in Moscow, it detained a teenager who posted a video on TikTok threatening to commit a crime in Tsaritsyno Park. posted photos of himself on the short-video platform TikTok wearing tactical clothing, a balaclava, a cap, sunglasses, and headphones holding an object resembling an automatic weapon, as well as photos taken at the Tsaritsyno Museum with the caption: "I found a place." The search of his place of residence, FSB officers seized clothes and accessories he was wearing on the photos. His phone contained a TokTok account where he posted threats, a subscription to a neo-Nazi Telegram channel, and a significant number of search queries regarding past terrorist acts and mass murders.

title: The midterms will test the nation's political direction and confidence
body:
Voting stickers rest at Contra Costa County's election operations facility on May 27, 2026 in Martinez, Calif. Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images hide caption
Millions of Americans are looking to Tuesday's midterm elections with heightened anticipation or anxiety.
At this point, we can expect at least some portion of the nation to have its political confidence — and perhaps even its sense of security — tested in the days and weeks ahead. That test could also continue for some time to come.
The first place to look for elevated anxiety about the midterms would be among those voters most loyal to President Trump. He calls them MAGA, borrowing from his 2016 "Make America Great Again" theme. Alternatively, with a broad smile, he just calls them "my base."
But winter may be coming. Polling suggests that on Tuesday the midterm electoral pendulum will once again swing back against the White House incumbent — as it has in every midterm over the last 100 years with very few exceptions.
More punishment for the party of the second-term president would be expected in the blue states that he lost in each of his three White House campaigns. But this fall's polls are also pointing to significant losses for Republicans in swing states and even in some of the red states Trump won all three times — often by double-digit margins.
That is why the president spent the last weekend of this campaign on making an electoral "goal line stand" for the Senate by visiting Iowa and Kansas.
When Trump, then a first-time candidate, was at high tide 10 years ago, he won 31 Iowa counties that had previously voted for Democrat Barack Obama in 2008 and 2012. And as for Kansas, the historically Republican state has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1932.
Yet Trump put live visits to Iowa and Kansas on his schedule for the final weekend, even as he did remote "tele-rallies" in 19 other states. (The Iowa-Kansas plan was briefly cancelled late in the pre-election week, then reinstated just before the weekend.)
That strategy suggests Trump's political team remains focused on limiting GOP losses in what will be a tough environment for their party. Most observers, including those searching hardest for objective measurements, now predict Trump's party will lose its slim majority in the House. The consensus is that the Senate is too close to call , and it is possible the GOP could hold the majority using the tie-breaking vote to which Vice President Vance is entitled.
But precedent is not really the explanation for Trump and his party's expected defeats. Midterm elections inevitably act as referenda on current officeholders, and there is no current officeholder in the world so visible as the U.S. president — especially the Oval Office's current mega-mediagenic occupant. Put another way, presidents are the leaders and symbols of their party, but Trump has taken the personalization to another level. Presidents routinely campaign for their party's midterm candidates, but Trump (" Pretend I'm on the ballot ") has worked hard to make the election about himself.
In Trump's first term he tried out a more conventional approach, acting as an executive in a system of shared powers. This time around, Trump has taken that role as a starting point. He has cast himself as the driver of historic events and the avenger of many wrongs — large or small, real or imagined. He presents himself as the architect of a new Washington and the author of a new era.
And he has done it all despite objections from U.S. allies around the world and from Congress and from the federal bench.
While Trump's bravura interpretation of his role has played well with his base, the larger electorate is a different story. Among the more effective themes taken up by anti-Trump rallies has been the ultra-simple, anti-autocrat mantra of "No Kings."
Critics and Democrats have been able to focus on promises and pronouncements Trump has made but on which he has yet to deliver. Peace in Ukraine on Day 1? A new era for Israel and the Palestinians? Not so far.
These foreign policy issues matter, but to voters the greater disappointment is economic. Trump said he would make things cheaper and tame inflation. But inflation remains elevated and the public sees the price of gas leading a sustained surge in everyday costs.
So it should be no surprise that any average of Trump's recent approval numbers shows them falling from a clear majority (52% in average of polls) early in 2025 to an average of 37% now — breaking below the 40% threshold that has signaled brutal midterm results in the past.
On the other hand, the confidence some Democrats are showing may be premature. If they win the House , their majority will be on the modest side by historic standards. If they eke out a majority in the Senate it will be so narrow that the primary beneficiaries are likely to be the mavericks who are willing to buck the party leadership — on both sides of the aisle.
Moreover, even robust Democratic majorities would need to confront the significant divisions that persist — and may be growing — in their ranks. The most glaring is the contrast between majoritarian consensus builders on one hand and the party's firebrands on the left. The latter group has been pleased with the party's class of nominees for Congress this year, including a cadre aligned or associated with the Democratic Socialists of America.
The DSA candidates have attracted attention from the media and been prominently featured in Republicans' fall campaign ads and messaging, even in places where the DSA favorite lost in the primary and is not on the November ballot.
To some degree, the 2026 Democrats have been able to unite around issues such as energy and grocery prices and the war on Iran. Opposing vast data centers to be built to serve the AI industry has been another shared cause. And whatever their differences, this year's Democrats have been a chorus of opposition to Trump.
But there are reasons to doubt the united front can be preserved if the Democrats get back into power. Most expect at least one chamber of Congress to be theirs in the new year, and there will be a new president after 2028.
One political demographer and author who has been focused on the Democrats' internal issues is Ruy Teixeira, who spent most of his career at think tanks associated with Democrats such as the Center for American Progress and the Brookings Institution but is now at the business-oriented American Enterprise Institute. He is best known for his 2002 book with John Judis entitled, The Emerging Democratic Majority , but Teixeira has long been focused on the party's history with white, non-college educated voters and is also the author with Joel Rogers of America's Forgotten Majority: Why The White Working Class Still Matters.
In October, Teixeira published 11 questions he said Democrats must confront if they regain congressional power. The final question was whether the party would embrace positions that resonate with working-class voters and prioritize their interests rather than its recent concentration on race, gender, energy, environment and social policy.
Beyond the questions for the two major parties, these midterms have cast doubt on the conduct of U.S. elections themselves. For generations, Americans have generally shown confidence in their electoral systems and results, but that too has become a target.
There is a haunting song on Eric Clapton's classic 1992 album Unplugged that repeats the title line: " Running on Faith."
That is one way to think of democracy. Faith in the democratic system is required if the system is going to work and survive.
Democracy has often been called an ongoing experiment. It tests whether people can have a voice in their own governing, and whether that voice can be heard and heeded.
It tests the mechanisms and individuals involved, to be sure. But ultimately, it tests voters' faith in the system itself. Will the will of the people be clear and will it drive the next phase of American political life?
Nonpartisan experts in voting laws and machinery — academics, journalists, lawyers and others — have, as a rule, defended the current state of American processes. Legislation, administrative professionalism and fresh funding at the national and state levels have upgraded the administration of American elections since the Help America Vote Act became law two decades ago, following the Florida vote-counting debacle in the year 2000. HAVA enabled states and localities to replace punch-card ballots and other outdated methods with touch-screen technology and preservable paper trails, improving voter confidence and security.
And yet, faith in the system is likely to be tested in the days ahead. It's not just about one race or one state. It's not just about candidates and issues. It's about the system that Trump repeatedly calls into question without evidence.
As far back as his first nomination in 2016, Trump was telling his crowds that if he lost it would be because the process was fraudulent. There was no way the Democrats could win unless they cheated, he said, and a defeat would simply prove his assertion.
Four years later, Trump was able to summon thousands of his supporters to Washington on Jan. 6, 2021 to protest and deny his defeat in the previous November's presidential election. "Stop the steal" was the cry, based on nothing but conjecture and emotion and a preference for a different outcome.
In contrast, Trump accepted the results in 2024 as he and his party won. But he continues to label information — be it polling results or simple daily news reporting — as fake. He responds to a question from a White House credentialed reporter by asking: "Who are you with?" Then he says: "You're fake news."
He regularly tells his audiences to ignore "fake news" and "fake polls." It is easy to imagine him exhorting his followers to ignore "fake results."
There will be tension on election night this week, as there always is. But the greater stress may come in the days and weeks ahead.

title: 4 killed, about 15 injured in US Dallas
body:
TEHRAN, Nov. 01 (MNA) – Four people were killed and approximately 15 others were injured after multiple overnight shootings in one of Dallas’ vibrant nightlife neighborhoods, US police said.
According to CNN, the incidents occurred at three separate locations, all in the city’s Deep Ellum neighborhood east of downtown.
Police have not found a connection between the incidents but say they are continuing to investigate whether they are linked, Dallas Police Chief Daniel Comeaux said during a Sunday morning news conference.
The total number of people injured is “still moving a little bit,” according to Comeaux, as some transported themselves for medical care.
The first shooting took place at around 12:20 a.m., while the second happened shortly after 1 a.m. and the third shooting in the string occurred about a half hour later, according to a news release from Dallas police, citing the preliminary investigation.
Multiple people have been arrested and are being questioned as police work to identify the potential shooters, he said, although their possible connection to the shootings is unclear.
The department had increased its staffing in anticipation of Halloween crowds, the chief said. “We had more presence out here, and this was something that we were ramped up for,” Comeaux said.
All three incidents appear to have been within about a half mile of one another, along streets checkered with local restaurants, art galleries, bars and concert venues.
The neighborhood refers to itself as “Dallas’ premier arts and entertainment district,” according to its website. Several venues in the area had advertised Halloween events for that night.
It is unclear whether the shootings took place inside any businesses or on the street, Comeaux said.
He praised the department’s “amazing” response time, adding one officer successfully performed lifesaving measures on an injured person.
Victims’ identities and the conditions of the injured were not released Sunday morning as Dallas police continue to investigate the incidents.
The department is asking the public for photos and videos from the area as it works to piece together what happened, Comeaux said in the news conference.
“We’re going to do everything that we need to do to get everyone in custody that’s responsible,” he added.
The overnight incidents took place roughly six months after a pair of overnight shootings within a block of each other in Deep Ellum left a 26-year-old security officer dead and five others injured, according to CNN affiliate KTVT.
CNN has reached out to Dallas police for more information.

title: Nearly 50 Ukrainian drones taken down over Russian regions during day
body:
MOSCOW, November 1. /TASS/. Nearly 50 Ukrainian drones were shot down over Russian regions during the day, the Russian Defense Ministry said.
"From 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Moscow time (5:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. GMT), Russian air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 47 Ukrainian fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles ver the Belgorod, Nizhny Novgorod, Kursk, Kaluga, Tula, Voronezh, Smolensk, Rostov, and Moscow Regions," it said.

title: Ahead of budget, Poilievre urges Carney to end diesel taxes and cut spending
body:
Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre is reiterating his call for the federal government to end all taxes on diesel and cut wasteful spending as Prime Minister Mark Carney prepares to unveil his budget Thursday.
“Conservatives are demanding that he (Carney) cut wasteful spending to bring down deficits, inflation and taxes so Canadians can afford a good life,” Poilievre said during a news conference Sunday.
He went on to cite data from the Parliamentary Budget Officer, who projected $733 billion in additional debt in the next five years. That includes a $63.3-billion deficit in the 2026-27 fiscal year, down from a forecast $71.8 billion in the PBO’s June outlook.
In a letter, Poilievre urged Carney to reduce the cost of government. He wrote this should include cutting bureaucracy, wasteful foreign aid, and cancelling the ALTO high-speed rail project between Toronto and Quebec City.
The leader of the official opposition also called on Carney to “keep your promised debt anchors,” urging the prime minister to reduce the deficit until the budget is balanced.
The PBO has predicted the government will not meet its fiscal anchor of maintaining a declining deficit-to-GDP ratio; instead, the office expects the measure to rise in 2027-28 and 2029-30.
“This budget should be judged against his promise to Canadians,” Poilievre said.
Poilievre also called for the elimination of federal taxes on diesel until Canada Day and for Ottawa to suspend the GST on fuel until summer and scrap what he called the Fuel Standard Tax.
Earlier this week, the federal government unveiled its title and theme for the upcoming budget, which Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne’s office said reflects a period of “profound change and uncertainty.”
Titled “MASTERS OF OUR DESTINY: BUDGET 2026,” Champagne’s office said the title was inspired by the 1962 Quebec electoral campaign of then-premier Jean Lesage.
The note from Champagne’s office said the slogan at the time was “a defining expression during a moment of profound change and uncertainty,” as the Lesage government was planning to build up hydroelectric resources and institutions that would support the economy.
Ottawa’s latest budget comes as Carney’s government continues to rework Canada’s economy and trade relationships to reduce reliance on the U.S., amid ongoing tariffs and trade tensions.
As Poilievre outlined his demands Sunday, Carney released a statement saying he had a “good conversation” with President Donald Trump and the teams from both countries were going to work in the coming weeks towards a “mutually beneficial” trade deal.
— with files from Global News’ Ariel Rabinovitch and The Canadian Press

title: Passports being issued to evacuated Oleshky residents who lost documents – Vyhivskyi
body:
As reported by Ukrinform, Minister of Internal Affairs Ivan Vyhivskyi said this in a Facebook post .
According to him, more than 300 employees of the Interior Ministry system have been involved in receiving and assisting people evacuated from Oleshky.
“Our units were there at every stage. Border guards ensured the necessary processing and were among the first to say: ‘Welcome to Ukraine!’ Rescuers set up tents where people could warm up and rest. Police officers escorted convoys of buses and ambulances and helped people with limited mobility once they were in hospitals. Two trucks belonging to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine transported belongings and animals,” the minister said.
According to Vyhivskyi, State Migration Service employees are currently processing Ukrainian passports for the evacuated Oleshky residents. Many people lost all their documents during the occupation. There are also children who will be receiving their passports for the first time. “Dozens of applications have already been accepted. We are doing everything to make the process as convenient and free of charge as possible,” Vyhivskyi stressed.
Interior Ministry units began helping Oleshky residents back when the people were still under occupation. National Guard troops and border guards, together with other units, used drones to deliver food to the left bank of the Kherson region, including canned goods, cereals and children's food packages. Today, the evacuated residents say this assistance helped them survive.
As reported by Ukrinform, emergency medical teams in Kyiv conducted initial medical examinations and arranged further transportation of Oleshky residents to healthcare facilities in the capital.

title: Iran rapidly changing its defense doctrine — supreme leader’s adviser
body:
TEHRAN, November 1. /TASS/. Iran’s defense doctrine is undergoing a rapid transformation, with the geography of threats no longer determining the geography of response, Mohammad Mokhber, and adviser to the Iranian supreme leader, said.
"Iran's defense doctrine is rapidly evolving. Naturally, the geography of threats no longer determines the geography of response, he wrote on X. "The redefinition of deterrence's scope has transcended the regional framework, and the origin, extent, and location of threats impose no limitations on Iran's deterrence calculations.".

title: IDF avoiding killing certain Hamas officials in Gaza over fear of civil order collapse
body: The defense establishment is implementing an unprecedented policy in the Gaza Strip that includes granting immunity to mayors and senior officials in Hamas's governmental and municipal systems.Military sources confirmed to Walla that the decision not to target heads of local Hamas authorities stems from a deep and tangible concern that killing them could lead to the collapse of governing institutions in the Gaza Strip and trigger civilian chaos that Israel would ultimately have to deal with. This includes an assessment that international aid organizations would be unable to fill the power vacuum left by killing the Hamas officials.As noted, the current government opposes the Palestinian Authority taking control of the Gaza Strip and demands that a third party administer the territory instead of Hamas.IDF, Shin Bet to continue targeting Hamas terroristsIt is important to note, however, that the IDF and Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) are maintaining a high operational pace, carrying out two to three targeted killings each day against terrorists and commanders in Hamas's military wing.The killings include terrorists who participated in the October 7 massacre, as well as others preparing attacks against Israel or taking part in rebuilding Hamas's terrorist infrastructure.Behind the IDF and Shin Bet's new policy is a dramatic improvement in intelligence-gathering capabilities. Security officials note that over the past year, Military Intelligence Directorate units and the Shin Bet have made significant advances, including developing human intelligence sources and exploiting conditions on the ground to obtain accurate, real-time intelligence.These capabilities are combined with the capabilities of the IDF Southern Command and the Israel Air Force.The developments in intelligence stand in stark contrast to pre-October 7 capabilities, when Israeli intelligence suffered from a shortage of human sources in the Gaza Strip and relied on intelligence gathered from mobile phones. Today, the defense establishment is able to closely track senior terrorists and carry out targeted killings.Conditions on the ground indicate that Hamas has been severely weakened. Terrorists now have fewer hiding places, fewer tunnels, and, above all, a significant shortage of senior commanders with operational experience who are familiar with Israel's security establishment and know how to operate under strict conditions.Meanwhile, Hamas's military wing is working to rebuild its intelligence on IDF activity along the Yellow Line and deeper inside Gaza by gathering information through various methods.Hamas maintains control over Gaza civil institutionsDespite the blows inflicted on Hamas by the IDF and Shin Bet, the terrorist organization continues to maintain control over the Gaza Strip's civilian administration.It controls the economy, internal security, energy, education, healthcare, and local authorities, with all the implications this entails.Even in areas where its grip appears weaker, Southern Command officials claim that the terrorist organization shapes public sentiment through arrests, interrogations, violence, and intimidation. One of the methods Hamas uses to control the population is highly coercive tax collection.Israel fully understands that severely damaging these systems could have direct consequences for regional stability and provoke criticism in the international arena. Therefore, a decision has been made to keep senior civilian officials off the target list for the time being.Alongside efforts to preserve civilian infrastructure, the IDF continues to act decisively against senior figures in Hamas's military wing.Among other developments, the Southern Command and the Israel Air Force have developed advanced operational techniques over the past year that make it possible to carry out targeted killings even within densely populated tent compounds, while keeping collateral damage to an absolute minimum and preventing harm to innocent civilians.

title: US First Lady hopes humanitarian mission in Slyoshki will promote lasting peace
body:
WASHINGTON, November 1. /TASS/. US First Lady Melania Trump hopes that the humanitarian mission in the city of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region will contribute to resolving the conflict in Ukraine and establishing lasting peace.
"The ceasefire across Oleshky (Alyoshki - TASS) and the surrounding Kherson region has provided residents with the freedom to move, access to food, clean water, medicine, plus a renewed sense of dignity without the constant threat of attack," she wrote on X. "Let Oleshky become the starting point for lasting peace."
Earlier, Russia and Ukraine agreed on a US First Lady Melania Trump-mediated ceasefire in Alyoshki to carry out a humanitarian operation. The ceasefire in the area came into force at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time (1:00 a.m. GMT) on October 27 to prepare and conduct the humanitarian operation in the city. A humanitarian mission was carried out on October 30. Several dozen tons of humanitarian aid - food, hygiene and sanitation products, fuels for power generators, and other daily essentials - were handed out to the city residents, Lantratova said. All those willing to leave the city were given the opportunity to evacuate either to Russia or to Ukraine.
Russian presidential press secretary Dmitry Peskov on September 21 described the humanitarian situation in Alyoshki as critical as food and medicines could not be delivered to the city amid Ukrainian shelling and drone attacks.

title: Troops Kill High-Ranking ISWAP Fighters In Borno
body: Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI, have killed several Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters, including a member of the group’s Shura Council, Abu Hajara, and a prominent commander, Abul Walid, during an encounter in Kukawa, Borno State. Two other high-ranking Arab fighters were also killed in the engagement, which took place on October 31, 2026. Abul Walid was identified as a close associate of Ba Shuwa, the overall Wali of ISWAP. The development was disclosed in a statement signed by the Acting Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force (North East), Captain Mohammed Goni. According to the statement, troops deployed to Kukawa repelled a major ISWAP attack on their positions, with ground forces supported by air assets from the Air Component of Operation HADIN KAI. The troops recovered several weapons, ammunition and communication devices following the engagement. The military described the operation as a demonstration of the troops’ combat readiness, vigilance and superior firepower, adding that it reflected the sustained pressure being mounted on terrorist groups across the theatre. The attack on the troops’ positions in Kukawa came barely three days after the assault on Buni Yadi, where 55 terrorists were neutralised, according to the military. Those killed in the Buni Yadi operation included key commanders identified as Ali Mandara Abba Gajiri, also known as Munzir; Habu Ikkima Nakif Yana Faruk; and Commander Gogore. The Theatre Command reaffirmed its commitment to protecting law-abiding residents and sustaining operations aimed at eliminating terrorist groups and destroying their camps across the region. The post Troops Kill High-Ranking ISWAP Fighters In Borno appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Christie’s debut Abu Dhabi sale totals $8.94 million, setting nine auction records
body: Christie’s first fine art auction in Abu Dhabi totalled $8.94 million on Sunday, delivering the auction house’s highest total for an evening sale of modern and contemporary Middle Eastern art in more than a decade. Held at The Abu Dhabi Edition, Mawasim: 20 Years of Modern and Contemporary Middle Eastern Art brought together 70 lots by 58 artists from 13 countries. The sale marked two decades since Christie’s first UAE auction in Dubai in 2006. Anthea Peers, Christie’s president for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, tells The National : “We were absolutely thrilled this evening to see bidding from across our global client base. We felt enormous excitement in the room, and there was a real sense of engagement and dynamism.” She adds: “This is only the beginning. We are very excited to build on tonight to make our contribution to the ecosystem of Abu Dhabi.” Iranian artist Monir Shahroudy Farmanfarmaian’s Variations on the Hexagon (2006) led the sale, fetching $844,800 after almost seven minutes of bidding. The work had been estimated at $150,000 to $250,000. Turkish artist Fahrelnissa Zeid’s Composition (1948–1949) sold for $524,800. Iraqi artist Faisel Laibi Sahi’s Baghdad Cafe (The Coffee Shop) (2016) and Iranian artist Ali Banisadr’s Homo Deus (2018) each fetched $512,000. Armenian-Lebanese painter Paul Guiragossian ’s Noces (Wedding) (1958–1959) achieved $486,400, a price matched by Egyptian artist Mahmoud Said’s Portrait de Princesse Fadia (Portrait of Princess Fadia) (1952) and Zeid’s Endless Thoughts , from the 1970s. Palestinian artist Samia Halaby’s Yesterday (1978) sold for $358,400, while Lebanese artist Ayman Baalbaki’s Babel Tower (2012) fetched $281,600. Iranian artist Farhad Moshiri’s Untitled (2003) completed the 10 highest-priced works at $230,400. Christie’s reported nine auction records, including records for particular media for Guiragossian and Halaby. Emirati artists Rami Farook, Fatma Lootah and Afra Al Dhaheri made their auction debuts, alongside Lebanese artist Nabil Kanso. More than 30 per cent of registrants were millennials or Gen Z, while 37 per cent were new to Christie’s, according to the auction house. The auction followed a week of exhibitions and events and included works from the Dalloul Collection in Beirut and Barjeel Art Foundation in Sharjah.

title: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers for Michigan Senate
body: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers in the Michigan Senate race on Sunday — a stunning break with her party that derails Democrats’ attempts to create a united front for Abdul El-Sayed. Stevens’ seismic step across party lines comes just days after she insisted she was still going to support El-Sayed despite their escalating public feud. Tensions crescendoed through the weekend as Stevens attempted to condition a Sunday joint appearance with El-Sayed and Rep. Jim Clyburn (D-S.C.) on El-Sayed’s rejection of an ad from one of his allies that was critical of Israel. El-Sayed’s team then asked Stevens to stay away from his events, as POLITICO first reported . “Abdul said that I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away. And he’s right,” Stevens said in a video posted to social media on Sunday after she appeared at a Detroit church alongside Rogers . “And that’s why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today,” she said. “Who we are as Michiganders is not hate, and it is not what we are getting out from our Democratic nominee right now.” Her cross-party endorsement of the man she’d once hoped to defeat for a Senate seat, just two days out from a critical Senate election, underscores how fragile her public truce with El-Sayed was after a bitter August primary that deeply divided the party. And their infighting is splashing across social media at the most inopportune moment possible, as Democrats race to hold a competitive seat that could decide control of the chamber. Rogers said he was “honored to have Haley Stevens’ support” and that they had spoken by phone earlier in the morning about her endorsement. “We talked about America, what was better for Americans, what was better for the future of our state by bringing people together,” Rogers said while speaking to reporters alongside Stevens after the church service. “What we decided is: Sometimes the hate grows so loud that it jeopardizes some of our citizens in this state. … This is more a statement about standing together against hate and the future of this state and the future of this country than it is anything else.” Stevens insisted she’s “not trying to harm anyone” and that she’s “not turning my back on Democrats.” Representatives for El-Sayed did not immediately respond to requests for comment. But the Democratic nominee told reporters Sunday, "I actually don't think about Haley Stevens." "I'm just less interested in the politics of it all than I am in the policy of it all. And so, look, if you're somebody who believes that we ought to have more rights, not less, then I would think you would support me in this race," El-Sayed said. Stevens’ endorsement sparked immediate, scorching backlash from various corners of the Democratic Party. Several members of her team, including her chief of staff for eight years Justin German, resigned Sunday morning and said they will continue to work to elect El-Sayed on Nov. 3. “Many amazing staffers went to work for Haley Stevens to fight for shared democratic values and keep this Senate seat blue. Some of those incredible people are now working their asses off to elect Abdul,” Stevens’ former campaign communications director, Arik Wolk, posted on X. “There are two Supreme Court seats and so many other values Haley claimed to care about on the line. By endorsing Mike Rogers she has betrayed all those values.” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee Chair Kirsten Gillibrand reiterated their support for El-Sayed in statements Sunday. "This is a despicable betrayal from Rep. Stevens," Schumer wrote on social media . "Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors." Stevens had denied she would endorse Rogers or go to church with him to senior Michigan and top national Democrats as recently as Saturday night, according to a Michigan Democratic official briefed on the matter, granted anonymity to share private details. Earlier Sunday morning, Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.) told NBC that he spoke to Stevens the night before and she would be “voting straight down the line on the Democratic ticket, and she’s going to be celebrating with Democrats across the country when we win on Tuesday night.” Stevens also told a Michigan Democratic Party official Saturday afternoon that she planned to vote for El-Sayed, according to screenshots of text messages obtained by POLITICO. “I am voting straight Dem!!!!,” she wrote. “I had a dream last night we won,” she added. “And I believe he will win! P.S. it was a happy dream.” Her reversal just hours later confounded many Democrats. “Michiganders are worried about how they are going to pay their mortgage and fill up their gas tanks … That’s what they’re talking about, not Congresswoman Stevens’ continued efforts to get attention,” Rep. Debbie Dingell (D-Mich.), who had been attempting to broker peace and helped organize the joint appearance between the primary rivals, said in a statement. “We must stay focused on electing Democrats up and down the ballot, and that includes electing Abdul El-Sayed as Michigan’s next Senator.” Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel said in a statement — shortly before Stevens officially endorsed Rogers — that her decision to campaign with the Republican “shows that she has abandoned everything she claims to care about.” “[El-Sayed] will still win. Haley swings no votes at this point. She just lit her career on fire for no reason,” said one senior Senate Democratic aide, who was granted anonymity to speak candidly. In addition to their fury at Stevens, some Democrats are livid with El-Sayed for appearing to escalate the back and forth with Stevens in the final days. “He couldn't leave it alone,” said another senior Democratic aide, who was granted anonymity to speak candidly. Stevens said in the video that she does “not stand with Hasan Piker,” the far-left streamer who El-Sayed campaigned with ahead of the Democratic primary. (El-Sayed has since distanced himself from the streamer amid Piker’s controversial remarks about Sept. 11 .) She said remains a “proud Democrat.” Republicans latched onto the endorsement quickly. Some believe this will strengthen their messaging that Democrats are a party of socialists and radicals in the final days of the election. "When Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who ran against Abdul El-Sayed and knows him better than anyone, stands with Mike Rogers, Michigan should take notice. Democrats who feel Abdul has abandoned them have a home with Mike,” RNC spokesperson Hunter Lovell said in a statement. The news is blowing up in some House GOP group chats, said Rep. Jack Bergman (R-Mich.). “We always talk about the October surprise. It can be good or bad. Well, I think this is a bit of a positive surprise here 2 days before the before the polls finally close," he said. Adam Wren, Meredith Lee Hill, Jordain Carney, Mia McCarthy and Aaron Pellish contributed reporting.

title: New York City Marathon: Sweden's Almgren and Kenya's Chepkirui win as 60,000 take part
body:
Sweden's Andreas Almgren, right, approaches the finish line during the New York City Marathon in New York, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Angelina Katsanis/AP hide caption
NEW YORK — Andreas Almgren of Sweden won the men's race of the New York City Marathon in his debut in the event while Sheila Chepkirui of Kenya won the women's race on Sunday for the second time.
Almgren was making his debut at 26.2 miles after a successful career running half-marathons. He pulled away from Yemaneberhan Crippa of Italy in the final mile to take the victory in 2 hours, 6 minutes and 1 second. Crippa finished 13 seconds behind. Kamohelo Mofolo of Lesotho was third, edging out defending champion Benson Kipruto.
Almgren's time was the third fastest in the course's 50-year history, and the top seven finishers all were among the top 10 all-time times. He became the first marathoner to win his debut in the event since Gebre Gebremariam of Ethiopia won the 2010 race.
American Zouhair Talbi finished sixth and ran the fastest time ever by a U.S. runner in the event.
Chepkirui, who also won the race in 2024, pulled away from countrymate Hellen Obiri in the final 150 meters to seal the victory in 2:24:36. American Jessica McClain finished second, passing Obiri — a two-time winner — in the final few strides. It was the first time a U.S. woman finished in the top three since 2018. McClain was 6 seconds behind Chepkirui.
Sheila Chepkirui of Kenya competes in the women's division of the New York City Marathon in New York, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Angelina Katsanis/AP hide caption
It was the 50th time that the race has run through all five boroughs of the city. There were just over 2,000 competitors in 1976, the seventh running of the race, including only 88 women. About 60,000 runners stepped up to the starting line Sunday, with nearly half of them women.
There were runners from more than 140 countries competing Sunday, including defending men's Kipruto. He won in thrilling fashion last year, edging Alexander Mutiso by three-hundredths of a second.
The New York City Marathon began in 1970, and the first six years it was run entirely inside Central Park, with runners doing loops. The race was moved out of Central Park in celebration of the U.S. bicentennial and to help uplift the city, which was struggling. It ended up turning into one of the marquee events in New York.
For the first time in 15 years, there was a minor change in the course. The runners took a slightly different route at Mile 20 when the race entered the Bronx. The move was made to reduce the number of turns in the borough from seven to five and ease some of the street closures in the area.
Marcel Hug won the men's wheelchair race for the eighth time, edging Daniel Romanchuk by just over a second. Romanchuk made a move to take over the lead in the last mile as the pair entered Central Park for the final time. Hug passed him in the final 100 meters to win.
Hug's Swiss countrymate Catherine Debrunner pulled away from the field early to win the women's wheelchair race, finishing in 1:40:02. It was the second-fastest time in race history, trailing her own mark by about 30 seconds from 2023. Two-time defending champion Susannah Scaroni finished third, three months after giving birth to her first child, more than eight minutes behind Debrunner.
A previous version of this story incorrectly referred to Marcel Hug and Catherine Debrunner as Swedish. They are from Switzerland.

title: General Staff: Ukrainian troops evacuated 167 civilians from Kherson region during ceasefire
body:
According to Ukrinform, the General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces announced this on Facebook .
"During the ceasefire introduced in designated areas of the Kherson region to carry out the humanitarian mission in Oleshky, Ukraine's Defense Forces took advantage of the security conditions created to evacuate residents of the right bank of the Kherson region," the statement said.
According to the General Staff, the evacuees came from settlements in Ukrainian-controlled territory along the Dnipro River that had been subjected to daily shelling by the Russian army. Those who had previously been unable to leave the dangerous areas were able to evacuate.
Civil-military cooperation units of the South Operational Group of Troops, together with local authorities, evacuated 167 civilians to safer locations in the Kherson region. Among them were 22 children and 21 people with limited mobility who required special attention and assistance.
The General Staff noted that the evacuation took place in extremely difficult and dangerous conditions. The routes passed along mined and damaged roads, as well as through areas where military equipment and civilian cars had been burned out. All this significantly hampered movement and required particular caution and coordinated efforts by all units involved.
"Despite these risks, the main priority remains protecting the lives of civilians and helping those who cannot leave dangerous areas on their own. Every person rescued is the result of joint efforts and coordinated cooperation among all those involved in the humanitarian mission," the statement said.
The General Staff stressed that units of the South Operational Group of Troops were strictly and consistently observing the ceasefire in the area where the humanitarian mission was being carried out.
As reported, Ukraine introduced a ceasefire in a designated area from 03:00 Kyiv time on October 27 to carry out a humanitarian operation in the temporarily occupied city of Oleshky, Kherson region.

Reddit user pdfu found hints hidden in the HomeView 27.2 code that Apple could be adding security camera features to its smart home hub. The strings describe a security camera mode with motion detection, live streaming, and recording options, as well as privacy functions. According to pdfu, there is a setup page that even explicitly reads: “Your HomeView can be used as a security camera with HomeKit Secure Video.”
Supposedly, the video feeds will only be visible to members of the home, and will both show an indicator light and play a sound when either someone is watching the camera feed or when it starts to record. Home members will also get a notification anytime settings are changed for the Secure Video mode. It will also include customizable options for what to detect, stream, or record, based on whether you’re home, away, or asleep.
Some wondered why Apple did not allow HomeView to double as a security camera at launch, and the company hasn’t said anything to suggest the features are coming. But, considering how central privacy is to Apple’s marketing , the company may be waiting to fine-tune those features before launch.
