title: UAE hopes to avert new Iran conflict, prepares for worst-case scenario
body: The United Arab Emirates is hoping that a “breakthrough” could end the conflict with Iran, its Al-Ain media said on Sunday. The report was based on comments by Anwar Gargash, the diplomatic advisor to the president of the UAE.Speaking at the 22nd annual Manama Dialogue conference in Bahrain, he affirmed that the security of the Gulf states is interconnected, expressing the Emirates' hope for an end to the war in the Middle East.The two-day conference, organized by the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS), took place over the weekend.The Manama Dialogue event attracts key leaders and policymakers from around the region. It is often used to advance regional security and discuss what may come next in the Middle East.Gargash, according to the UAE report, said that “the security of the Gulf states is interconnected and what affects any of them affects the UAE,” adding that “trust with Iran has been shaken.” He expressed hope for a “diplomatic breakthrough,” adding, “We do not want to see another round of confrontation.”Nevertheless, the UAE is also preparing for a “worst-case” scenario.UAE seeks diplomacy as tensions with Iran persistThe rumors of war have persisted as the US prepares for midterm elections. Israel is also in the midst of a post-election scrum as parties seek to form a coalition government.“As we have shown on previous occasions, we are prepared for the worst,” Gargash said. He is one of the important voices in the UAE and the region in terms of understanding the broader trends in the Middle East. He hopes for a return to the status quo in the Strait of Hormuz, to before the United States and Israel began strikes on Iran on February 28. The Islamic Republic has been attacking ships since the war began.Meanwhile, Syria's Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani reaffirmed Syria's commitment to diplomacy and negotiations as the best means of establishing peaceful and secure relations with all parties. Syrian state media noted that the minister “said Israel had pursued a hostile approach toward Syria and its people, carrying out thousands of airstrikes and provocative actions on the ground.”Shaibani was at the Manama Dialogue event and was quoted as saying: “Syria had pursued negotiations since the beginning of its liberation.” He added that “Syria believes US mediation aimed at ending Israeli attacks could deliver positive results for all parties.”Shaibani described Syria as entering a new phase. This comes amid some tensions with Jordan over the past week. Addressing the economic and development challenges facing Syria during recovery and reconstruction, he said that World Bank estimates put the cost of rebuilding what the war destroyed at approximately $250 billion, SANA noted.The minister also participated in a session on the foundations of regional security at Manama. He met on Saturday with Bahrain's National Security Advisor and Royal Guard Commander, Lt. Gen. Sheikh Nasser bin Hamad Al Khalifa.Qatar has been a major supporter of the new government in Syria.Syrian Defense Minister Maj.-Gen. Murhaf Abu Qasra met with Qatar's Deputy Prime Minister and Defense Minister Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani to discuss regional and international developments and ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation.SANA reported that “the meeting, attended by several military officers, also addressed issues of mutual interest between the two countries.”It added that “the talks followed an August 4 telephone conversation between the two ministers, during which they discussed regional and international developments, bilateral coordination, and efforts to support regional security and stability.”Saudi-led coalition targets Houthi military capabilitiesIn Riyadh, the Saudi-led military coalition said it had “carried out a military operation on Sunday morning targeting resources used by the Houthis to support attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure.”Coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki said the operation sought to counter threats to Yemen, Saudi Arabia, and shipping lanes in the southern Red Sea.Al-Maliki said that the Iran-backed Houthis were “exploiting vital resources to bolster their military capabilities, particularly ballistic missiles and drones,” Arab News reported. The coalition “launched the operation in response to those attacks and the threat they posed to civilian lives and infrastructure,” it said.This illustrates that, even as some countries gather in Manama and express hope for the future, the Houthis are still terrorizing Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

title: Carney says Canada, U.S. working in coming weeks towards trade deal
body:
Prime Minister Mark Carney says the U.S. and Canada will be working in the coming weeks to deliver a “mutually beneficial” trade deal after a conversation with President Donald Trump.
Carney confirmed the chat between the two world leaders in a post on social media Sunday.
“This builds on our recent constructive discussions on the outlines of a mutually beneficial trade deal that would create jobs for our workers, boost affordability for families, and fully respect Canada’s languages, culture, and sovereignty,” Carney said.
“Our teams will now be working in the coming weeks to deliver that outcome.”
Trump signaled a deal was near as he spoke with reporters Sunday before a campaign rally he was holding in Iowa.
“We have the concept of a deal that’s going to be great for our farmers, great for our country and it will be fine for Canada too,” Trump said.
The president told reporters the Keystone XL pipeline was a part of the potential deal. He also claimed there would be “no tariffs” on products like dairy being sent to Canada – an issue that has been a key sticking point in previous talks.
While the comments are the latest signal a trade deal could still occur, it also appears to suggest an agreement won’t be reached before the U.S. midterms on Tuesday.
The prime minister’s comments come after he told reporters Wednesday that the federal government was “not at that position right now” in terms of reaching a trade deal.
Asked by reporters Wednesday why he was willing to entertain a deal before the midterms — and whether Canada was being set up to be the “fall guys” by the U.S. administration if it loses — Carney said they’re after the right deal.
Last Monday, Global News reported that the once-stalled talks between the two countries were “moving quickly” at the political level, according to multiple sources with direct knowledge of the negotiations.
Canada walked away from talks with the U.S. in August, with Carney saying the U.S. had made a last-minute push for language that would limit Canada’s ability to enter trade deals with other countries, water down French language requirements, and hurt the country’s struggling auto industry.
The break down in talks led to Trump’s previously threatened 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian goods to take effect, with Canada responding with dollar-for-dollar retaliatory duties.
Trump previously commented on Canada during a campaign rally on Thursday in South Carolina for the Republican senate candidate. He suggested Canada had been “treating us extremely nicely recently,” adding his tariffs on their northern neighbours had the effect of improving relations.
“The Trump Administration welcomes continued engagement with Canada as we work toward finalizing the details of a deal that will deliver meaningful results for the American people,” said a White House official on background.
Asked about Carney’s statement, Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre pushed Carney to “get a great deal.”
“It’s time for Mr. Carney to put the big talk in the past and deliver real results,” Poilievre said Sunday at a news conference.
Talks of a potential trade deal also come days before the federal government is set to announce its latest budget on Thursday.
— with files from Global News’ Reggie Cecchini, Alex Boutillier and Mackenzie Gray

title: Donald Trump makes final midterm campaign push
body: President Donald Trump is set to hold back-to-back rallies in Iowa and Kansas on Sunday, capping a flurry of campaign events ahead of the midterm elections . Tuesday is election day. Mr Trump, who is not on the ballot, had initially cancelled the in-person appearances and replaced them with tele-rallies. But on Friday, he reversed course. “I feel very good. I mean, I feel like we're doing well,” he told reporters in Florida on Saturday. “We're going to Iowa first, then Kansas second. I think we're going to do very well,” he said. “I think we're going to surprise a lot of people.” Iowa and Kansas are traditionally Republican strongholds. Mr Trump won both states by comfortable margins in the 2024 presidential election. But Republicans are battling to hold on to critical Senate seats in both states. In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton is mounting a serious challenge to Republican Senator Roger Marshall. If Mr Hamilton wins, he would become the first Democrat in 94 years to win a Senate seat in the state. Mr Trump is heading into the midterms with historically low approval ratings , amid voter discontent over the economy and rising fuel and food prices. The war in Iran has also proved unpopular with voters. More than 53 million people have already cast ballots through a combination of in-person early voting and mail-in voting. Much is at stake on Tuesday, when all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 Senate seats are up for grabs. Republicans currently hold narrow majorities in both chambers. Polls show Democrats ahead in a number of vital races. If the Democrats win back control of Congress, they could curtail the President's legislative agenda during the remaining two years of his term. There is also concern among Republicans that Democrats could seek to impeach Mr Trump once again. “There need to be hearings, because there’s so much corruption,” Illinois Governor JB Pritzker said in an interview with NBC on Sunday. “The hearings will uncover things, and then some decisions will have to get made about that,” he said. “But the American public doesn’t know the extent of the corruption.” Mr Trump was impeached twice during his first term in office. He was acquitted by the Senate on both occasions.

title: Ukraine war latest: Russian oil refinery in Kstovo ablaze after reported overnight drone strike
body:
A major Russian oil refinery in Kstovo, Nizhny Novgorod Oblast, was reportedly targeted in a drone attack overnight on Nov. 1, according to Ukrainian monitoring channels.
The Exilenova+ and Supernova+ Telegram channels published reports and footage of the alleged attack on the NORSI, or the Lukoil-Nizhegorodorgsintez refinery.
The reports could not be immediately verified by the Kyiv Independent.
NORSI refinery is Russia's fourth-largest oil refinery and second-largest gasoline producer, processing around 15-17 million metric tons of crude annually. It also produces bitumen, as well as diesel and aviation fuel used to support Russian forces.
The refinery is approximately 800 kilometers (500 miles) from the Ukrainian border.
Ukraine has targeted the facility a number of times, including a confirmed strike on Aug. 26 that sparked a large fire. The NORSI suspended operations due to damaged sustained in that attack.
Since the beginning of 2026, Ukraine has engaged in a sustained campaign of long-range drone strikes on Russian energy facilities, focusing on oil refineries and fuel depots, which are critical to sustaining Russia's war effort.
A Russian airstrike destroyed the Kramatorsk City Council's executive committee building in Donetsk Oblast on Oct. 31, local authorities reported.
The building, located on Peace Square in central Kramatorsk , survived the city's occupation by Russian-backed militants in 2014 and its subsequent liberation by Ukrainian forces.
"An hour ago, Russia destroyed the central building of Ukrainian statehood in Kramatorsk with an airstrike," Oleksandr Honcharenko, head of the city's military administration, wrote on Facebook , referring to the city council's executive committee.
Honcharenko described the building as a symbol of the city's history and identity.
"They can destroy a building, scorch our land and steal our memories. But they cannot destroy our right to a future," he wrote.
The building had previously sustained damage during a Russian airstrike on the city centre in March 2026. Information about casualties from that strike was not immediately available. Russian attacks elsewhere in Kramatorsk on Oct. 31 also injured civilians, according to Suspilne. Kramatorsk, a major Ukrainian-held city in Donetsk Oblast, has faced increasingly frequent Russian attacks as Moscow's forces continue their offensive in eastern Ukraine.
A Russian attack struck an energy facility in Kyiv on the evening of Oct. 30, leaving parts of four districts without electricity, Ukrainian energy company DTEK reported.
Ukraine's capital is home to more than 3 million people, roughly the same population as Berlin.
The outages affected the Obolonskyi, Darnytskyi, Desnianskyi and Podilskyi districts, according to a statement from DTEK .
Kyiv Independent staff in the capital reported explosions and widespread fluctuations in power, with some buildings and streetlights temporarily losing electricity.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Telegram that there were problems with the water supply in the city after three drone strikes hit critical infrastructure facilities, posting that the Left Bank of the city was without water.
The full extent of the damage remains unclear. There were no immediate confirmed reports of casualties from the latest attack.
The incident follows Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv overnight on Oct. 29–30 that killed at least one person and damaged residential and commercial buildings.
The overnight attacks also left approximately 350,000 residents in and around Dnipro without electricity.
Russia has repeatedly targeted Ukraine's energy infrastructure as the country prepares for winter, damaging power facilities and forcing emergency electricity restrictions.
Ukrainian drones and Neptune cruise missiles targeted the Kamensky Factory, one of the largest chemical plants in Russia, in Rostov Oblast overnight on Oct. 31, the General Staff reported.
The plant, located in the Russian city of Kamensk-Shakhtinsky, some 15 kilometers (9.3 miles) east of the Ukrainian border, produces solid rocket propellant for the Uragan, Smerch, and Tornado-S multiple-launch rocket systems, as well as other missile systems and aircraft weapons.
The Kamensky factory has been sanctioned by the E.U., U.K., and U.S. for its role in Russia's war against Ukraine.
According to the Ukrainian military, the attack caused a fire at a warehouse storing finished products and damaged four production units.
"Strikes on solid rocket propellant production facilities reduce the Russian army's ability to attack Ukrainian settlements with multiple-launch rocket systems," the General Staff said .
Ukrainian forces also struck four Russian military supply depots near Russian-occupied Khartsyzk and Dokuchaievsk in Donetsk Oblast, Novovasylivka in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, and Novoaidar in Luhansk Oblast.
The Kyiv Independent couldn't independently verify the reports. Russian officials haven't commented on the General Staff's statement.
The reported attack comes as Ukraine has intensified its long-range strikes inside Russia and across Russian-occupied territories since the summer, hitting targets such as oil refineries, military-industrial plants, and airfields, aimed at degrading Russia's military-industrial capacity.
Earlier in the week, Ukraine reported on Oct. 26 hitting the territory of the Energia plant, the sole Russian manufacturer of batteries for glide bomb guidance and correction modules.
CHERNIHIV OBLAST — Evacuees from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have reached Ukrainian-controlled territory on Oct. 31 after an arduous 19-hour journey.
The city's residents, who had been trapped in a worsening humanitarian crisis for months on end, arrived to an emotional reception at the border crossing with Belarus by relatives, health workers with ambulances, aid organizations, police, and media.
President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the mission was successful, thanking all parties involved, including U.S. First Lady Melania Trump.
"When there is the attention of the world, there is the salvation of people," Zelensky wrote.
"Further de-escalation steps and a real approach to peace are also needed."
In recent months, Oleshky residents faced severe shortages of food, drinking water, electricity, and medical supplies. Russian forces had effectively blockaded the town, preventing humanitarian organizations from delivering aid.

title: Trump says would run for president again if such possibility existed
body:
NEW YORK, November 1. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump has said that he would like to run for another term if the law allowed him to do so.
"I'd love to run again if I had the chance, but the language (of the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution that limits presidents to two elected terms in office - TASS) is very exacting," Fox News quoted him as telling the New York Posts’ Pod Force One podcast.
He recalled that he has two more years left as president. "That's a long time. You can do a lot in that period of time," he added.
"By law, Trump’s second term as president is set to end in January 2029. The 22nd Amendment to the US Constitution, which was adopted in 1951, limits the president to two terms in office. Nevertheless, Trump has repeatedly suggested that he may be seeking reelection for a third term.
Trump was reelected to his send time in office in November 2024. His first presidential term was from 2017 to 2021.

title: Leader's advisor stresses shift in Iran's defensive doctrine
body:
TEHRAN, Nov. 01 (MNA) – A senior advisor to the Leader of the Islamic Revolutio says Iran’s defense doctrine is changing, and the country will no longer limit its retaliation to attacks on the aggressors’ regional assets.
In a Sunday post on his X account, Mohammad Mokhber said Iran is “rapidly” changing its military deterrence strategies to enable it to strike targets far beyond the West Asia region in response to a potential new act of aggression, Press TV reported.
“Of course, the geography of the threat no longer determines the geography of the response,” Mokhber said in the Farsi-language post.
“The redefinition of the scope of deterrence has gone beyond the regional framework, and the origin, scale, and location of a threat no longer impose any limits on Iran’s deterrence calculations,” he said.
The post comes amid concerns that Iran could face a new act of aggression by the United States and the Israeli regime, more than eight months after the two attacked the country without provocation.
Iran responded forcefully to the aggression by attacking targets deep inside the Israeli-occupied Palestinian territories, as well as military bases and assets controlled by the US in regional countries.
The extensive Iranian retaliation forced the US and Israel to end their 39-day aggression in mid-April under a ceasefire brokered by regional countries.
Iran has indicated that it will respond decisively to any new aggression, with military and security officials warning that the scope and scale of its counterattacks will be much greater this time.
On Saturday, Ayatollah Khamenei directed Iran's top military brass to prepare to deliver a swift and powerful response to any threat "without any geographic limitations."
Meanwhile, regional mediators have been trying to work out a diplomatic solution to the Iranian-US standoff, which has disrupted international energy and commodity supply chains.
Iran has indicated that it remains open to such a diplomatic solution if the US accepts its conditions for permanently ending the aggression and lifting its blockades and sanctions against the country.

title: Marine Corps spox: Ceasefire in Oleshky holding, we are prepared for any eventuality
body:
Pavlo Drohal, spokesperson for the Ukrainian Navy's Marine Corps, said this in a comment to an Ukrinform correspondent.
"The ceasefire introduced as part of the humanitarian mission in Oleshky is currently in effect and remains in place. Our units – Marine Corps units and other units of Ukraine's Defense Forces – are not violating it; we are fully observing the ceasefire. As for the enemy, it has attempted to discredit the Ukrainian Armed Forces by spreading reports on its Telegram channels claiming that Ukraine's Defense Forces are violating the ceasefire and even allegedly striking civilians in Oleshky. This is not true," Drohal said.
He stressed that Ukraine's Defense Forces were not violating the ceasefire, while the enemy had been using it for its own military purposes. In particular, he said, Russian troops had been carrying out various logistical operations, supplying their units, evacuating their dead and wounded, rotating personnel and fortifying their positions.
"We have repeatedly detected enemy reconnaissance UAVs monitoring the operational area here during this period. There were even several instances when they dropped munitions on our positions. Fortunately, none of our service members were injured in these drops," the spokesperson said.
He also noted that before the ceasefire came into effect, the enemy had been conducting remote mining of the right bank, which had resulted in people being injured and killed.
The spokesperson noted that the ceasefire remains in effect for now. It is very difficult to predict what will happen next or how the enemy will act. Drohal stressed that Ukraine's Defense Forces are preparing for any eventuality.
"Given the tactics the enemy used before the ceasefire, we can assume that shelling may resume, as may attempts to advance into the island area and establish a foothold there. But we are ready for this, we are preparing for it and are ready to respond to any changes in the operational situation," Drohal said.
As reported, U.S. First Lady Melania Trump said she had secured a local ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine covering only Oleshky. According to the White House press office, the parties agreed to temporarily suspend all hostilities in Oleshky to ensure the delivery of humanitarian aid and prepare for the evacuation of civilians through an agreed safe corridor.
The General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces said that Ukraine had introduced a ceasefire in a designated area from the night of October 27 to carry out a humanitarian operation in Oleshky.
Davyd Arakhamia, head of the Servant of the People parliamentary faction, said the ceasefire will remain in effect until 22:59 on Sunday, November 1.

title: Iran has a hidden network of military agencies managing to smuggle hardware past US blockade
body: Iran has created a secret network of military agencies with global reach to import at least $2 billion in hardware, explosives and heavy-duty trucks since January 2025, evading both the US naval blockade and Western sanctions, a Reuters investigation has found.Hidden behind names starting with the letters MOD, for the Ministry of Defense, are more than 5,000 agencies that form a formidable financial and military machine. Their financial footprints are on bills of lading and other shipping data dating back to 2016. Some are tied to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and to business conglomerates known as bonyads that are controlled by Iran's elite.The findings offer a window into one of the war's great mysteries: How is the IRGC replenishing its missile and drone arsenals while firing them in the thousands?In the 18 months from January 2025 to June 2026 - including four months into this year's war - a single one of these agencies, MOD 346428, imported huge quantities of rocket propellants, explosives and weapons components that are critical for making drones and missiles, as well as heavy-duty trucks that can serve as missile launchers. The hardware came in by land, sea and air - much of it recorded as originating in China, Russia and Germany.This investigation of the MOD network is based on thousands of Iranian bank and government records, corporate filings and import data.The secret agencies all share the same Tehran address as Iran's Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics, or MODAFL. They list their incorporation date as February 11, 1979, the day Ayatollah Khomeini took power in Iran after overthrowing the monarchy. Most were actually established in 2013, the records show, as Iran struggled under sanctions that saw its crude exports and currency plunge.The agencies, identified for the first time by Reuters in collaboration with the Israeli-American risk consultancy 240 Analytics, form the backbone of Iran's military procurement and sanctions evasion apparatus. They operate a web of frontmen and foreign shell companies, collectively known as trustees, who use the proceeds from illicit oil sales to buy goods for the Islamic Republic.Senior military leaders involved in Iran's ballistic missile and drone programs use the network. Phone numbers registered to 91 of the agencies also appear in records from state-run Bank Sepah of IRGC personnel with accounts there. Among them are at least two commanders the US has accused of abuses against civilian protestors.While Iran's military has been under multiple US sanctions for decades, Reuters could find no evidence that any of the numbered agencies referenced in the documents have been designated by Western governments.“What you have here is the regime's military lifeline during this conflict and for many years before,” said Miad Maleki, a former senior official at the US Treasury Department who helped design the American sanctions program against Iran. “This is the complete ecosystem of the Iranian military's trade business.”The weapons import network has provided many of the raw materials Iran needs to make missiles and drones. Those munitions are responsible for Iran's relentless precision attacks against Gulf energy infrastructure, allowing the Islamic Republic to blunt America's military assault. In other reports this year, Reuters has shown how Iran withstood US pressure by exploiting crypto exchanges and illegal gambling networks to tap illicit revenues and circumvent sanctions, how the IRGC consolidated control of the Strait of Hormuz, and how the war has ushered in a new era of repression.Maleki was one of four experts on Iranian sanctions and weapons who reviewed the Reuters findings and confirmed that many of the materials could be used in Iran's missile and drone programs.None of the Iranian government entities or companies contacted by Reuters responded to detailed requests for comment, including Tehran's UN delegation to Geneva and the presidency.In a statement in response to the Reuters findings, a Treasury Department spokeswoman said the United States “has severed the regime's economic lifelines.”“While the regime may continue its desperate attempts to evade our powerful sanctions, fund its military and weapons programs, and access foreign currency, we are always 10 steps ahead,” the spokeswoman said.In tracking the materials, Reuters cross-checked a portion of some 19,000 import records using the shipping documents, footage from social media, and state media reports. Nearly all of the items that Iran imported were exempt from duty and specifically marked as military equipment, the data shows. The experts noted that much of the material, even explosives, can be considered dual-use, and so could also have civilian purposes.The Wall Street Journal reported some of the shipments from China on September 23.Parallel trade systemThe secret military agencies form a foreign-trade system parallel to the formal global economy that allows Iran to spend the money it earns abroad selling illicit oil on military hardware, said Maleki, who was the associate director of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control until last year.Money rarely crosses borders, where it might trip a sanctions alarm. Instead, for 97% of the shipments Reuters reviewed, the transactions were settled “without currency transfer,” the import data shows. Trusted frontmen in the diaspora, using cash held in foreign banks, bought the goods and shipped them home.One end user of the network is the military unit overseeing Iran's ballistic missile program. Another is Sahara Thunder, which was sanctioned by the US in 2024 for manufacturing and supplying drones to Russia that have devastated Ukraine. Reuters and 240 Analytics identified the Iranian military units by cross-referencing the import data with corporate registry filings, and emails and documents compiled on the website WikiIran.Reuters could not determine the identities of the people who run WikiIran, a website that solicits leaked documents from the Islamic Republic and says it is operated by Iranians opposed to the government and “forced into exile.”During the first six months of this year, according to the import data, deliveries included $1.9 million worth of detonators, tonnes of explosives, aircraft engine parts, rocket fuel ingredients and heavy-duty launch vehicles. All could be used as key components to build and fire ballistic missiles and drones, including the Shahed series, according to weapons and sanctions experts.“This looks like an industrial-scale effort to rebuild or expand Iran's existing fleet” of drones and missiles, said Peter Salisbury, an adjunct assistant professor at Columbia University who has spent the past several years researching Iranian arms transfers and supply chains. “This data clearly shows the Iranian ecosystem's adaptability and its ability to find new routes.”Salisbury and one of the other experts said they have used WikiIran's data in the past and have found it to be accurate.The United States and Israel have targeted Iran's ballistic missile and drone operations from the start of this year's war on February 28, including factories the Pentagon said were turning out munitions. Reuters could not determine the extent of the damage, but Iran has continued to fire on its neighbors and on ships trying to transit Hormuz.The material entered Iran by cargo ship across the Caspian Sea from Russia, by truck from Central Asia, and by freight planes from China,, according to documents reviewed by Reuters and records provided by ImportGenius, a platform that aggregates import-export data.In response to detailed questions about the Reuters findings, China's Foreign Ministry said it was “unaware of the situation you describe.”“We firmly oppose attempts to maliciously link regional hostilities to China or smear China's reputation,” the Foreign Ministry said in a faxed statement.Russia's Defense Ministry, the White House and CENTCOM did not respond to requests for comment.Beyond individual components, Iran is buying precision machinery that could be used to manufacture its own military equipment. The purchases include items coded as sophisticated computer-controlled lathes, electron-beam furnaces and particle accelerators, according to import data that runs to June. All have industrial purposes and can also be used to make military equipment, including drone and missile bodies.On October 12, US President Donald Trump said he did not believe China and Russia were providing support to Iran. “If they are, it's at a very low level, but I don't believe they are at all,” he posted on social media. “They have too much to lose, and we would know about it, and know about it very fast!”Since the war started, the data shows that $27 million worth of goods purchased by Iran's military were recorded as originating in the United Arab Emirates, nearly all arriving by sea.Iran targeted UAE infrastructure through May and continues to hit its crude tankers with drones and missiles.The most recent shipment from the UAE, listed as electronics, was on June 27 by sea, nine days after the United States announced it was suspending its naval blockade. The blockade resumed in mid-July and remains in effect.A UAE official sent Reuters a statement after publication of this story, saying that the government "categorically rejects and refutes these baseless allegations. These claims are entirely unfounded and misrepresent the UAE's policies and actions." The statement added that the Emirates is committed "to preventing any attempts to misuse its territories for illicit activities."In addition to Maleki, the arms experts included Henry Thompson and Wolf-Christian Paes, both specialists in Iranian weapons supplies; and Damien Spleeters, founder of Heimdall, a specialist organization focused on illicit supply chains and weapons procurement.IRGC relies on these agencies to evade sanctions“These numbered agencies are the plumbing behind the Islamic Republic's global sanctions evasion network and so much more,” said Noam Binstok, a senior analyst at 240 Analytics, which collates and analyzes data on terrorism risk and financing for corporate and government clients. “The amount of money going through these agencies is staggering, and no one has noticed them before.”Binstok, a 35-year-old economist, said he discovered the numbered entities in June 2025 while uploading thousands of pages of Bank Sepah documents that he found on Telegram and on WikiIran - where they are freely available - to 240 Analytics' online platform. Bank Sepah is the Iranian lender that handles salary and pension payments for the IRGC.Bank Sepah did not respond to a request for comment about the hack. The heist was claimed by a group called Codebreakers that later announced other hacks of Iranian government data.“We can confirm that the materials are authentic and that their origin was verified through our sources and contacts both inside and outside Iran,” WikiIran said in an emailed response to Reuters questions about the data.240 Analytics was founded as a service for companies and governments to vet potential business partners and clients. Binstok said he thought the documents would help reveal Iran's financial operations. He soon realized that thousands of those accounts were held by agencies with the same naming pattern. All began with the letters MOD - or VODJA in Farsi - followed by a five- or six-digit number that was spelled out longform, rather than as numerals. And all shared the same registration date and address.The bank records, which Reuters reviewed, included the account holder's name, various ID numbers, and balances.When he first saw the size of the Sepah account balances, Binstok said, he thought he had misplaced a decimal point. He found that 36 of the agencies had foreign exchange accounts with $1.2 billion on deposit at the end of 2024. The rest of the network had around $1.8 billion in local currency, averaging about $360,000 per account.At the time juggling a doctoral thesis, his job at 240 Analytics and a newborn, Binstok mothballed the project. He returned to it this August, searched more recent documents, and found the same agencies receiving money from contraband oil sales and buying large quantities of dual-use equipment.“That was the major breakthrough that led me to start understanding the actual scope that we are talking about, and to find actual examples of imports,” said Binstok. “It was then I knew we were onto something really big.”Each MOD agency was also identifiable by a unique 11-digit government identity number and appeared in Iran's corporate registry, an official database of thousands of Iranian businesses. That 11-digit number or the MOD number itself cropped up repeatedly on bills of lading, invoices, and bank accounts, making the network traceable even when the agency was using a front company, Binstok realized.That's when 240 Analytics approached Reuters to help map the network of agencies. Using the 11-digit identity numbers from Binstok, Reuters reviewed confidential shipping documents and up-to-date import data, and used Iran's corporate gazette to expose the scope of the network and how it allowed Iran to restock during the war.One agency with purchases dating back to 2016 stood out: MOD 346428.The overseas purchases of MOD 346428 had steadily increased over the years, from $442 million in the 12 months ending March 2023, to $988 million the following year, according to customs statistics published in Iranian media. That placed the agency in Iran's top 10 importers.From January 2025 through June 2026, Reuters found that MOD 346428 imported $2.3 billion of military hardware, according to the ImportGenius records.Between January and April 2025, MOD 346428 imported 886 tonnes of chemicals into the Iranian port complex of Bandar Abbas, the import data shows. Their origin was listed as China under the code which includes sodium chlorates and other perchlorates, key precursors for solid rocket fuel. Three days after the final shipment, an enormous explosion shook the port.Two people with knowledge of the April 26 explosion said it was caused when sodium perchlorate ignited while in dockside shipping containers. Iranian state media reported that the chemicals were stored by Sina Port and Marine Services Development Co., which is owned by Bonyad Mostazafan, a multi-billion dollar foundation directly controlled by the supreme leader of Iran.The explosion killed at least 70 people and injured more than 1,200. Sina's chief executive officer at the time said the explosion stemmed from a “false statement” about the contents of a consignment which was delivered “without documents and tags.” Reuters could not determine whether the chemicals in the final 75-tonne shipment were responsible for the explosion.The US sanctioned Bonyad Mostazafan in 2020. Ostensibly a charity serving the poor, the US Treasury alleged it was used by the supreme leader to enrich his office and reward allies.The bonyad is run by Hossein Dehghan, who was named Iran's defense minister in 2013, when most of the agencies got their start. Dehghan served in that post for four years. Earlier, he was the commander of IRGC forces in Lebanon during the deadly bombing of international peacekeeping forces in Beirut in 1983 that killed 241 US troops in their barracks and 58 French paratroopers along with Lebanese civilians, according to the US Treasury sanctions statement about him. The United States has blamed the attack on Iran.Dehghan did not respond to a request for comment about the explosion, the MOD agencies or his position sent via the bonyad and its legal representative.Alongside ingredients that could be made into missile fuel, the data also shows Iran importing heavy-duty trucks that the military uses as camouflaged mobile launchers for missiles and drones.One example of such imports surfaced early for Binstok. In autumn of 2022, an Iranian car dealer living in Italy purchased six Iveco Eurocargo trucks for 426,000 euros, records from WikiIran show. He shipped the trucks to another company called Deilami Trading Co. in Dubai. Deilami delivered them to Bandar Abbas.The end buyer's 11-digit ID number belonged to MOD 346428. According to the packing list, the vehicles were ultimately delivered to Sahara Thunder, which has a key role in manufacturing and selling drones. Deilami did not respond to a request for comment about the transaction.Matching VINs used to track vehiclesBetween January 2025 and June 2026, MOD 346428 imported 435 more Iveco trucks. Using satellite imagery and social media, Reuters tracked some of those vehicles to a customs lot on the outskirts of Tehran in February 2025 and used the import data to match three of their VIN numbers - unique codes that track a vehicle's manufacturer and origin.Another Iveco truck appeared during the war, when the US Central Command released footage on social media in March showing what it said was a strike on a disguised Iranian mobile missile launcher. Reuters could not determine if the vehicle was among those imported by MOD 346428. But the truck shown being blown up in the footage is an Iveco model of a type imported by Iran, according to analysts at Janes, a UK-based open-source defense intelligence company.“Official distributors are required to guarantee that these products are not utilized for military, chemical, biological, or nuclear purposes," Iveco said in response to the Reuters findings. The company said it has contractual safeguards to ensure its products do not go to “prohibited destinations, entities or individuals.”Iveco, which is based in Italy, said it had no control over “products transferred or exported by third parties with whom there is no direct contractual relationship.”“We have confirmed that any presence of Iveco vehicles in Iran occurred beyond Iveco Group's control and responsibility,” the company said. The company said it had no record of the 2022 sale to the Iranian in Italy and said most of the trucks Reuters identified in the customs yard in 2025 had been destined for Central Asia.Using MOD 346428, Iran also imported thousands of Toyota Hilux and Land Cruiser trucks, which the IRGC and its proxies modify to mount heavy machine guns on the flatbed.Video footage from protests in Iran earlier this year shows security forces with machine guns in a convoy of Land Cruisers driving through the streets of the city of Tonkebon in northern Iran.In January 2025, MOD 346428 imported four Toyota Tundras - a vehicle the IRGC uses to haul drones.A Toyota spokesman said the company doesn't conduct any business in Iran. “Toyota was not involved in, and has no knowledge of, the purchases reported by Reuters,” the spokesman said.Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry said it could not comment on the specifics of the Reuters investigation but said it maintains strict controls over goods related to national security.“We also conduct awareness-raising and outreach activities to inform businesses about these export control regulations,” the Japanese ministry said.Iran receives weapons materials from China, RussiaOn February 9, 2026, a ship arrived in Bandar Abbas with 93 tonnes of unwrought Chinese titanium, a high-strength metal that the weapons and sanctions experts said can be used to build missile airframes and rocket motor casings.In all, throughout the month leading to the war's start on February 28, ships also brought in a total of 268 tonnes of nitrocellulose and 276 tonnes of other chemicals originating in China and listed under the code that includes perchlorate - ingredients for both rocket propellant and explosives.Even with the war in full swing and a blockade on its ships, Iran's military kept bringing in materials from abroad. According to the data, monthly import volumes initially plunged by 47% to $54 million in March compared to the previous month, but by May they had increased to $77 million.A June 2026 shipment of $1.9 million in Russian detonators, which can be used to trigger high explosives such as those in drone and missile warheads, was the last of five similar Russian shipments, which have delivered a total of $7.6 million worth of detonators since the start of 2025.Imports didn't just originate in Russia and China. Companies in the European Union (EU), which has sanctioned Iran's Defense Ministry, also shipped goods to Iran's military.Hundreds of millions of dollars worth of trucks, airplane engine components and electronics - including $34 million in Iveco trucks - were all listed in import data as coming from Germany and elsewhere in the EU. On all of it, the paperwork listed MOD 346428.Not all of the import data contained detailed descriptions of the shipments. In many instances, Reuters relied on customs codes to identify their contents and declared origins without being able to independently confirm them.A European Union spokesperson said member states are responsible for enforcing EU sanctions, which include Sahara Thunder and others.“The EU continues to assess very carefully information related to Iran's reinforcement of its drones and missiles programs,” the spokesperson said. The governments of Germany and Italy did not respond to requests for comment.The pink droneMuch of Iran's economy is controlled by quasi-governmental foundations known as bonyads, which are run by the country's elite. Many were created after the 1979 Islamic Revolution using assets confiscated from the ousted royal family and other people deemed enemies of the new state.The bonyads are how Iran's elite holds on to power, binding loyal lieutenants through a vast network of patronage, according to a Reuters investigation from 2013 and multiple sanctions documents from the US government. Like the IRGC, the bonyads play a critical role in the violent repression of Iranians dating back years, both the US and Europe allege in years of sanctions.One of them, the Foundation for the Preservation of Relics and Publication of Sacred Defense Values, shows how deeply the MOD network runs through Iran's economy and its apparatus of repression. Transactions include not just imports, but also internal cash transfers, as Reuters saw in years of documents linking the foundation to at least two separate MOD agencies.Tasked with promoting “the culture of resistance, sacrifice, jihad and martyrdom,” the foundation is a key propaganda arm of the government, responsible for safeguarding the legitimacy and ideology of the Islamic Republic.In 2017, the foundation took delivery of four shipments of electronics and refrigeration units, according to the WikiIran data. The ID on the shipments - yet again - matches that of MOD 346428.How the foundation used those materials is unknown, but it counts senior IRGC commanders in each of Iran's 31 provinces among its leadership. In Khuzestan, that includes Brigadier General Hassan Shahvarpour, the longtime commander of its elite troops in the restive region.Shahvarpour did not respond to a detailed request for comment.Shahvarpour responsible for deaths of protesting civilians Units under Shahvarpour's command killed at least 100 Iranian civilians in Mahshahr in 2019 during protests against high gas prices, according to a US sanctions document. They encircled people trying to flee in armored vehicles and fired machine guns into the crowd, the US said.A local human rights activist who described witnessing the killings said Shahvarpour's troops then set fire to sugarcane fields where some of the fleeing protestors were hiding. His account was backed by a second activist who was present that day.After the US sanctioned Shahvarpour in 2020 for alleged human rights abuses, a prominent cleric kissed him on the head during a religious ceremony and told him sanctions are a “source of pride.”In 2021, Shahvarpour asked for 50 billion rials, then the equivalent of more than $1 million under the official exchange rate, from a state-owned steel company to finance a new IRGC building in Khuzestan, according to a document reviewed by Reuters. The holder of the account into which the money was to be paid, according to paperwork that bears his signature, was MOD 424000.At the start of this year, according to the two activists, Shahvarpour's men crushed new demonstrations in Khuzestan that were part of a nationwide uprising to protest Iran's economic collapse. Across Iran, thousands died and tens of thousands were jailed. In Khuzestan, the activists said they documented the names of 46 dead and said most of them were killed on January 8 and 9 when the IRGC opened fire on demonstrators.State media footage from a parade earlier this year shows Shahvarpour's IRGC troops driving through a town in Khuzestan in white Toyota Tundras of the sort favored by the MOD network. One of the trucks hauled a bright pink Shahed drone.

title: In Lome, a soviet-era sport celebrates Togo-Russia ties
body:
On the sand of Lomé Beach, Anthony Yao Sodjinê warms up for a match. The sport he's preparing for - sambo - began in the USSR and takes its name from a Russian expression meaning "unarmed self-defense."
Now, a new partnership between Togo and Russia is giving the discipline a foothold in West Africa.
Anthony came to sambo from judo, and the transition was deliberate. "I decided to take up competitive sambo to test myself, to see how it would turn out in life," he says.
In three years, he has already competed in four African tournaments. His personal journey now sits inside a broader partnership between Togo and Russia, with sports as the channel.
For Anthony, the stakes go beyond competition.
The initiative, he says, "could enable us to receive scholarships to travel to Russia to participate in training programs for athletes, coaches, and all practitioners of this discipline."
The Togolese Sambo Federation has been organizing demonstrations in Lomé since June 2024. The Africa Initiative Cup is in its first edition.
The groundwork was laid earlier: in April 2023, the Russian and Togolese sports ministers signed a memorandum of cooperation covering school and mass sports, infrastructure, and training.
"Our mission here is to develop this type of sport in Togo, as part of cultural and sports exchanges, as well as training exchanges," says Andrey Belogonov, representative of Africa Initiative and organizer of the Africa Initiative Cup.
"Today, our federations may be invited by the Russian Federation to participate in sports initiatives and international competitions," says Gneny Tchagbele, representative of Togo's Ministry of Youth and Sports.
Despite the progress, sambo remains relatively unknown in Togo compared with sports like football.
But the nascent partnership between Lomé and Moscow could earn it the visibility it needs.

body:

Leakers have pieced together a playable version of the canceled Portal prequel F-Stop . Most of the assets came from the massive 12-terabyte leak that dropped this August. That didn’t include the game’s source code or map data, but those final pieces apparently hit the Valve Cut Content Discord this week, allowing a nearly complete version to be pieced together.
Some dialog and elements of F-Stop eventually found their way into Portal 2 . But it differs dramatically from the mainline Portal games in that it’s built around a camera mechanic that lets you capture an item by taking its picture and place it elsewhere using the resulting Polaroid-like photos. It’s not unlike Viewfinder in that way.
The game is short, with videos showing off its full campaign all clocking in at under an hour. That’s not terribly surprising, though. F-Stop was developed as part of the “Directed Design Experiments,” a three-month period in 2007 when Valve broke into five teams to build new video game experiments.

title: Election workers prepare for contested results ahead of U.S. midterms
body:
As U.S. President Donald Trump’s approval dips across the country, election workers are bracing for a fight that could test their authority if results do not swing in his favour.
Asked last week if he would respect the results of the midterms , Trump said he would, “if they’re honest elections.”
What the president considers an “honest” result remains unclear. But election workers across the U.S. are tasked with making sure every valid vote is counted, regardless of their own political affiliation.
In the U.S., election administration is largely under the purview of states and local officials, each with different laws and procedures.
In recent weeks, the Trump administration has been questioning voter eligibility, alleging illegal registrations and demanding hundreds of ballots be set aside.
“We are bound by state law. And state law really does not give us the authority to do what the federal government is asking us to do,” Mary Hall, election auditor in Thurston County, Wash., told Global News.
On Sunday, U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason dismissed a lawsuit filed at the direction of the Trump administration to stop the certification of a possible narrow Democratic win in Alaska.
The decision came after the state’s Republican-led state government asked the judge on Saturday to dismiss the lawsuit.
The Department of Justice had alleged the Democratic senate candidate Mary Peltola recruited a nominee with the same name as incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan to confused voters.
In its Saturday filing, Alaska said the Justice Department’s request to separate all ballots cast for the second Dan Sullivan was “both disturbing and impossible.” It added doing so would violate voter privacy.
The Justice Department says it plans to appeal the decision.
Election officials say targeted claims can undermine voter confidence, even if they have no direct reason to doubt the election.
“There’s 50 different ways that elections work. Rhetoric has that type of effect,” Samantha Alfaro from the Loudoun County Elections Office in Leesburg, Va., told Global News. “Not so much people doubt their own results, it’s other results.”
Trump made similar claims during the 2020 election, which he falsely claimed was “rigged and stolen.”
During the fallout, election workers in Georgia faced threats and intimidation as false accusations of fraud took hold.
But recent polling suggests Trump’s newest accusations may not be bringing in the support he wants.
A new poll from Emerson College released Friday showed the president’s approval rating dipped to 37 per cent, an all-time low.
According to the same poll, Democrats lead Republicans by 10 percentage points in a generic congressional ballot.
Despite the results, election workers say they hold themselves to the standards of accountability and transparency.
– With files from Global News’ Reggie Cecchini and Sean Previl, and The Associated Press

title: OPP release details of victims, injured in fatal collision near Guelph
body:
One of the people injured in a fatal early morning single-vehicle crash Saturday has life-altering injuries, with police saying the second received non-life-threatening injuries.
Wellington OPP, fire and paramedic services responded to reports of the collision shortly after 1:30 a.m. Saturday on Watson Road South between Maltby Road East and Wellington Road 34, south of Guelph, Ont.
Six people were in the vehicle, police said. Four were pronounced dead at the scene, while two were transported to hospital.
“Our investigation has determined that six occupants were travelling in the vehicle when it left the roadway, struck a guardrail and entered the ravine,” said Insp. Karen Medeiros, detachment commander for Wellington OPP.
No names were released but OPP said the victims include a 19-year-old man from Mississauga, 19-year-old man from Brampton, a 17-year-old girl from Mississauga and a 15-year-old girl from Milton. A 17-year-old female remains in hospital with life-altering injuries as does a 16-year-old who received non-life-threatening injuries. Both teens in hospital are from Mississauga, according to police.
Medeiros said investigators continue to gather and preserve evidence in what she calls a complex investigation, but said it is too soon to determine exactly what happened. Anyone who may have been travelling in the area early Saturday, or who has surveillance or dashcam footage, is asked to contact OPP.
Asked about seatbelt use, Medeiros cautioned that the investigation is looking into whether speed or seatbelt use were contributing factors. But she said she did not believe there were enough seatbelts for the number of people in the vehicle.
— with files from Global News’ Rachel Morgan

title: Latvia takes over UNSC presidency for first time in history — foreign ministry
body:
VILNIUS, November 1. /TASS/. Latvia has taken over presidency in the UN Security Council for the first time in history, the Latvian foreign ministry said.
Latvia will be chairing all of the UN Security Council’s official and non-official meetings in November, it stated.
According to Latvia’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations Sanita Pavluta-Deslandes, the top priority objective of Latvia's foreign policy is to strengthen the republic's security, and the UN Security Council is a means to achieve this goal.

title: Pope Leo XIV hopes humanitarian mission in Alyoshki will be followed by peace initiatives
body:
VATICAN CITY, November 1. /TASS/. Pope Leo XIV has expressed hope that the humanitarian mission in Alyoshki will be followed by other peace initiatives and will strengthen dialogue between the sides.
"In recent days, a humanitarian operation has been carried out to assist the civilian population in the city of Alyoshki. I hope that the cooperation between the parties, which made this necessary gesture of humanity possible, will foster a greater willingness to engage in dialogue and lead to new concrete initiatives for peace," he said during his traditional Angelus address in St Peter’s Square.
Since late September, the humanitarian situation in Alyoshki has been critical as food and medicines could not be delivered to the city amid Ukrainian shelling and drone attacks. On October 16, Pope Leo XIV held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The situation in Alyoshki was among the topics of the call.
Earlier, Russia and Ukraine agreed on a US First Lady Melania Trump-mediated ceasefire in Alyoshki to carry out a humanitarian operation. The ceasefire in the area came into force at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time (1:00 a.m. GMT) on October 27 to prepare and conduct the humanitarian operation in the city. A humanitarian mission was carried out on October 30. Several dozen tons of humanitarian aid - food, hygiene and sanitation products, fuels for power generators, and other daily essentials - were handed out to the city residents, Lantratova said. All those willing to leave the city were given the opportunity to evacuate either to Russia or to Ukraine.

title: Egyptian bill to strengthen sexual assault penalties, end honor killings' leniency faces backlash
body: A proposed bill to toughen penalties for rape and sexual assaults against children and women has sparked fierce backlash in Egypt, particularly over a provision that would abolish reduced sentences for honor killings, according to Egyptian media reports and an announcement by the bill's sponsor, MP Fatima Adel.Adel submitted the draft legislation calling for an end to reduced sentences for murders committed on grounds of “honor,” an issue that remains controversial in Egypt and across much of the Middle East. The draft prompted an online backlash, with Egyptian men accusing the lawmaker of promoting immorality and depravity.An honor killing is the murder of an individual, most often a woman or girl, by relatives or members of their community who believe the victim has brought shame or dishonor upon them. Under Article 237 of the Egyptian Penal Code, a husband who catches his wife in the act of adultery and immediately kills her and her partner can receive a reduced sentence rather than the standard penalties for murder, which can include life imprisonment or the death penalty.Constitutional law expert Islam Qanawi told CNN Arabic that abolishing reduced sentences for honor killings raised questions about equality between men and women. The current provision grants husbands reduced punishment in certain circumstances, but does not provide the same treatment to wives who catch their husbands committing adultery and kill them and their partners.There were calls for changes in Egypt's legislation in September after an Egyptian man killed his wife and two men in Sohag after receiving AI-generated images from an anonymous Facebook account that depicted his wife in a sexual relationship, according to Egyptian media.Legislation aims to protect rape victims, avoid reduced sentences for perpetratorsAdel's legislation would abolish the reduced sentence under Article 237, toughen penalties for sexual assaults against children and prohibit courts from treating a victim's clothing, appearance or social relationships as grounds for reducing a perpetrator's sentence. It would also amend Article 267 to establish life imprisonment as the standard punishment for sexual intercourse without the victim's consent, with the death penalty in aggravated circumstances.These include cases in which the victim is under 18, the perpetrator is a relative or someone responsible for the victim's upbringing or supervision, or otherwise holds authority over them; where multiple perpetrators are involved; or where the crime results in serious injury, permanent disability or death.The legislation would also raise the minimum sentence for indecent assault committed through force, threats or coercion to 15 years of rigorous imprisonment. Life imprisonment would apply in cases including assaults against anyone under 18, crimes involving multiple perpetrators, the use of a weapon or means capable of causing serious injury, or cases resulting in permanent disability. The penalty would rise to death if the crime resulted in the victim's death.It would further establish a minimum sentence of 10 years of rigorous imprisonment for indecent assault against a child under 18, even when committed without force, threats, or coercion. The penalty would increase to life imprisonment in certain circumstances, including when the victim is under 12 or when the perpetrator exploits a relationship of authority, care, dependency or trust with the victim.The draft also seeks to amend Article 17 to restrict the use of judicial leniency in specified sexual assault cases, preventing courts from reducing sentences below the statutory minimum where the law explicitly prohibits it.Many Egyptians oppose bill as threat to 'natural law'Though many Egyptian women thanked Adel for the bill on Facebook, stressing the need for such measures, numerous individuals also complained that the bill threatens the “natural law,” and others complained that there should be stronger legislation to prevent wives from committing adultery.“The punishment for an adulterous wife is stoning,” one individual wrote to Adel. “Likewise, the adulterous husband. Either you present laws that comply with Islamic law, or we have no need for you or your proposals whatsoever, and we disavow them.”Another wrote, “It is absurd to demand that society stand idly by while its moral system is dismantled under the guise of freedom, and then simultaneously demand that it confront the consequences of this moral decay, such as harassment and assault. Even more perplexing is the condemnation of sound human instinct when it rejects any infringement upon honor and dignity. No legislation or sound logic can undermine the innate human instinct to protect and defend one's honor, and laws can never replace the violated dignity of the individual."It also read, "I call it the era of legalizing prostitution and debauchery through laws I don't know where you get them from. The problem is the nudity and freedom granted to girls, which came from the most depraved aspects of Western societies in the name of freedom, and which they despise, yet we boast about it today in our inherently conservative society!"

title: Did police overstep? Mandelblit pressed on limits of Netanyahu investigation in Case 2000
body: Former attorney-general Avichai Mandelblit testified Monday that, to the best of his recollection, he had not authorized a broader investigation into Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's relationship with Israel Hayom, as the defense challenged whether police questioning about the newspaper exceeded the scope of Case 2000.The exchanges at the Jerusalem District Court focused on the distinction between investigating a suspected deal involving newspaper coverage and examining a politician's wider dealings with journalists and publishers. Mandelblit said his approval centered on recorded conversations between Netanyahu and Yediot Aharonot publisher Arnon Mozes, rather than a general inquiry into Netanyahu's ties to Israel Hayom.Case 2000 concerns discussions about more favorable coverage of Netanyahu in Yediot Aharonot in exchange for steps to curb its rival, Israel Hayom. Netanyahu denies wrongdoing and faces a charge of fraud and breach of trust in that case.Mandelblit, who authorized the investigations and later approved the indictment, was called as a defense witness. Under Basic Law: The Government, opening a criminal investigation into a sitting prime minister requires the attorney-general's consent. The defense has questioned both the documentation of those approvals and whether investigators stayed within their limits.His testimony continued almost a week after the October 27 election, with Netanyahu's bloc short of a parliamentary majority and the formal publication and submission of the results to President Isaac Herzog scheduled for Wednesday. Mandelblit began testifying during the election campaign; his questioning has continued into the period of negotiations over the next government. Netanyahu's lawyer, Amit Hadad, asked whether Mandelblit had ever authorized an examination or investigation of Netanyahu's relationship with Israel Hayom. Mandelblit said he did not believe he had, while emphasizing the difficulty of recalling discussions held years earlier.He explained that the recordings distinguished Case 2000 from a case based on circumstantial evidence. He understood them to be the investigation's central focus. He also recalled being troubled by his assessment that Netanyahu did not intend to carry out the arrangement under discussion.Mandelblit denies authorizing investigation into Netanyahu's ties with Israel HayomHadad then presented questioning of former Israel Hayom editor-in-chief Amos Regev about Netanyahu's involvement in matters concerning the newspaper. According to the account Hadad presented, Regev had described Netanyahu speaking harshly about a reporter and opposing his participation in a flight.“To the best of my knowledge, I did not authorize investigating that line of inquiry," Mandelblit said.Hadad also challenged questions about editorial decisions and the involvement of the newspaper's owners in its coverage. Mandelblit said he did not recall approving that questioning.The distinction matters to the defense's contention that police pursued subjects beyond those Mandelblit permitted them to examine. His answers, however, were testimony about what he authorized and remembered, rather than a finding that the questioning was unlawful. In earlier hearings, he said he expected major investigative steps to be brought to him, but had neither intended nor been required to approve every police action. Hadad raised a further example involving Shlomo Filber, Netanyahu's former aide and later a state witness in Case 4000. He presented questions police had asked Filber about a declaration denying, to the best of Filber's knowledge and belief, that Netanyahu controlled Israel Hayom or had an organizational connection to it.Hadad argued that questioning Filber about whether the declaration was false fell outside Cases 1000 and 2000. Mandelblit said he had not authorized that line of inquiry.The hearing also returned to Mandelblit's approval of the amended indictment. Hadad argued that his signature had been copied from the original document and challenged how closely he had examined the amendments.Mandelblit maintained that he had approved the revised indictment and recalled reading its expanded account of the alleged benefits in Case 4000. He disputed the suggestion that authorizing someone to place his signature on a document meant it lacked his approval.“I remember reading the indictment,” he said.Monday's questioning followed last Wednesday's 2-1 decision to keep Mandelblit's testimony focused on investigation approvals. The defense had sought to question him more broadly about alleged misconduct by police and prosecutors. Judge Moshe Bar-Am expressed concern that restricting the questions could leave relevant matters unexplored, but the majority retained the limits on his testimony. The defense can pursue its broader arguments through other witnesses and evidence. The trial began in May 2020 and remains in the defense stage. Alongside Case 2000, Netanyahu faces fraud and breach-of-trust charges in Case 1000, concerning gifts from wealthy businessmen and alleged actions to benefit Arnon Milchan. In Case 4000, he faces bribery, fraud and breach-of-trust charges over alleged regulatory benefits for Bezeq in exchange for intervention in Walla's coverage. He denies wrongdoing in all three cases. Hadad said he expected his questioning of Mandelblit to take Monday and Tuesday. Mozes's lawyer, Sharon Kleinman, is then expected to question him, followed by the prosecution's cross-examination.

title: 'Dark cloud over results': Netanyahu questions Sohlberg's decision over election interference case
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party on Monday questioned a statement by Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg that, even if suspicions of foreign interference in last week's Knesset election are substantiated, they do not undermine the integrity of the vote or its overall results.“It is highly perplexing that Justice Sohlberg describes the allegations of foreign funding as extremely serious, yet simultaneously - and before the investigation has even concluded - preemptively determines that they have no impact on the election results,” read the statement, posted on Netanyahu's account on X, formerly Twitter.“A mere 4,612 votes stood between the shifting of a parliamentary seat from Ra'am to the right-wing bloc - a change that would have completely altered the election results and the political landscape,” the party added.הליכוד: תמוה מאוד כיצד השופט סולברג אומר שמדובר בחשדות חמורים מאוד של מימון זר, ובאותה העת קובע מראש שאין להן השפעה על תוצאות הבחירות בטרם סיום החקירה. 4,612 קולות בלבד הפרידו בין מעבר מנדט מרע״ם לגוש הימין, דבר שהיה משנה לחלוטין את תוצאות הבחירות והמפה הפוליטית. אנו דורשים חקירה מהירה ויסודית על מנת לשמור על טוהר הבחירות לכנסת וריבונות העם. עד לסיום החקירה עננה שחורה מוטלת מעל תוצאות הבחירות בישראל.— Benjamin Netanyahu - בנימין נתניהו (@netanyahu) November 2, 2026“We demand a swift and thorough investigation to safeguard the integrity of the Knesset elections and the sovereignty of the people,” the statement concluded. “Until the investigation is over, a dark cloud hangs over Israel's election results.”This is a developing story.

title: Saab Unveils CB90 CX Combat Boat With ISR Anti-Ship and Air Defense Capabilities
body:
Saab has unveiled the Combat Boat 90 Capability X (CB90 CX), a larger, optionally crewed combat boat designed for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), anti-ship warfare and short-range air defense (SHORAD).
Designed to address evolving maritime threats, the CB90 CX features increased payload capacity, upgraded onboard systems and operations across a wider range of sea states. It uses Saab's Autonomous Ocean Core to support optionally crewed operations while retaining the established characteristics of its troop-carrying predecessors.
The platform will initially be available in three configurations. The ISR variant incorporates Saab's Giraffe 1X radar for multi-domain situational awareness. The anti-ship variant provides over-the-horizon strike capability against surface vessels, while the SHORAD configuration uses an anti-aircraft autocannon to counter aerial threats, including the growing proliferation of uncrewed air systems (UAS).
The configurations are designed to operate together, combining surveillance, surface strike and air defense capabilities to support distributed naval operations and wider joint-force missions.
Sweden is the launch customer, with the CB90 CX currently in production. It will operate alongside the smaller CB90 NG rather than replace it. The wider CB90 family is in service with nine navies, with deployments across Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia-Pacific and the Americas.

title: China s GJ-21 Stealth Drone Makes First Take-off Landing From Amphibous Assault Ship
body:
China’s GJ-21 stealth reconnaissance and strike drone had taken off from and landed on the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan using its electromagnetic catapult and recovered with an arrested landing.
China's state media reported quoting the Chinese Navy that the flights took place "recently." No photographs or video of the flights had been released. Some publications went a CCTV provided video or clips from it.
The official announcement said the flights indicated, "that the PLAN now has the capability to operate fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime combat platforms."
The GJ-21 is a naval derivative of the GJ-11 drone. It has a subsonic, tailless flying-wing configuration, a single turbofan and internal weapons bays, and adds catapult-compatible landing gear and an arresting hook.
"The Type 076 ‘ Sichuan ’ was launched at Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding in Shanghai on December 27, 2024. She began sea trials in November 2025, and commissioning was then tentatively scheduled by 2027.
The ship has one electromagnetic catapult, three arresting wires and two side-mounted aircraft elevators. A stern well deck can accommodate two Type 726 air-cushioned landing craft, and the ship has space for more than 1,000 troops in addition to her crew. he said.
Besides the GJ-21 drone, it can also host helicopters and drone boats.
