title: Rapper Ja Rule comes to Tel Aviv, speaks on legacy, aging, and Tupac-Biggie row - interview
body: Hip-hop legend Ja Rule rolled into his hotel press room heavily bundled up but radiating energy, topped with a hat and dark sunglasses that masked half his face. His most defining feature, however, remained a massive, unmistakable smile.Fresh off his flight, he laughed and admitted his entire journey to Israel was spent binge-watching Marvel series and running through a massive Batman marathon.The 50-year-old rapper, who was in the country last week for his highly anticipated headline performance at Hangar 11 on Thursday, cuts a completely different figure today than the fiery icon of the early 2000s. He is now a settled family man and a doting grandfather navigating the relentless ticking of the clock, eyeing what comes next for his career and his family.In an intimate conversation last week, Ja Rule opened up about the emotional weight of aging, finding renewed artistic fire at a titan's funeral, and his firsthand memory of the moment the East Coast-West Coast rap war became deeply personal.For Ja Rule, hitting the stage these days is about taking his audience on a profound journey.Ja Rule performs live in Tel Aviv“If you've never seen me perform live, you're in for a treat,” he noted when discussing his approach to touring. “There's a lot of energy. I like to take my audience on what I call an emotional rollercoaster – ups and downs. So, we're going to dance, and we might even shed a few tears.”Traveling to the region during a tense climate might deter some, but for Ja Rule, the decision came down to community and celebration.“I came to celebrate and enjoy myself,” he explained. “I have many friends with ties to Israel – lots of good friends. So, I asked them, 'Is it okay to come here? Is everything alright?' And they said, 'Yeah, absolutely.' And here we are.”As Ja Rule looks toward the future, the realities of time and legacy are heavy on his mind, catalyzed by his young granddaughter, Bella. Mentioning her instantly transforms his expression. Early reports suggested he wanted Bella to call him “Big Poppa” in a nod to the Notorious B.I.G., but the veteran rapper has since softened his stance.“Yeah, you know, I think I've kind of walked back that idea a bit,” he chuckled. “I mean, I'm 50 now, so it really doesn't matter to me what Bella decides to call me. It's all good by me. Whether it's 'Grandpa,' 'Gramps,' 'Big Papa,' or any other funny names she might come up with, it's all fine. She actually just turned six months old today.”Becoming a grandfather has naturally forced a career re-evaluation and a new perspective on how he will spend his coming years. Reflecting on his past, Ja Rule admits his hustle came at a cost.“Back when my own kids were small, I was constantly on the move – I was working so much,” he said. “So, as they grew up, I still wanted them to see their dad doing what he does. I'm not sure if Bella will get to see that. I'm 50, so by the time she's old enough, I'll likely be in my 60s.”“Still very young, for sure,” he added. “But yeah, I'm not certain if I'll keep working as hard as I do now, even at 50. Then again, you never know. You just never know.”A trip to the funeral of music industry titan Clive Davis completely disrupted Ja Rule's thoughts on retirement and shaped how he views his next chapter. Sitting in the pews, he initially found himself craving a slower pace.“I learned a lot there. I left feeling truly inspired,” he reflected. “The people who got up to speak talked about how stubborn and determined [Clive] was, and how he was still talking about releasing music ... a few weeks before he passed away.“In other words, he remained the same person until the day he died. And I'm sitting there in the audience, I'm 50 years old, thinking to myself that perhaps it's time to slow down a bit and spend more time with my children and grandchildren.”But the narrative shifted entirely when Alicia Keys stepped up to pay tribute.“She shared how, at the age of 67 – after being let go from his job – he simply got up and started all over again. He discovered her, as well as [R&B singer] Mario, and all those other great artists,” Ja Rule said, his voice tightening with reverence. “And at that moment, I realized I wasn't done yet.”Seismic eraJa Rule's entry into hip-hop coincided with the genre's most seismic and tragic era, placing him on the East Coast circuit just as the feud between Tupac Shakur and Biggie Smalls reached its boiling point. While the bad blood simmered with Biggie's “Who Shot Ya,” it shattered all boundaries when Tupac unleashed the famously vicious diss track, “Hit 'Em Up.”Ja Rule happened to be in the room the exact moment Biggie first experienced the track, a memory that continues to shape his perspective on the vulnerability of the genre's biggest icons.“We were at a music video shoot, so all of us were there,” Ja Rule recalled. “Lil' Cease walked in with the disc or the tape – I don't remember exactly which. The tension was high, because it was personal. I think that moment was deeply personal for him; he dealt with it the way he did because he was a very sensitive person.”With recent landmark convictions finally breathing new life into the Tupac murder case, Ja Rule remains hopeful that the same closure will eventually find Biggie's family as the culture moves forward into a more accountable future.“Yeah, you know, you always want justice when someone dies so young. They were both massive figures in hip-hop,” he said quietly. “And the fact that we're only just beginning to understand what really happened on those fateful, deadly nights ... that says a lot, even without stating it explicitly, about how hip-hop is viewed.”When asked if he genuinely believes Biggie's murder case will finally be solved or officially reopened in the wake of recent legal breakthroughs, the veteran's answer was simple and fiercely protective of the culture's legacy: “I really hope so. Yes, I really hope so.”Review: A euphoric escapeWhen Ja Rule finally took the stage at Hangar 11, he delivered exactly what an exhausted, highly expectant crowd needed: a portal back 20 years.Arriving just hours after the final vote counts concluded in the 2026 elections, the audience had one clear goal in mind: to dance and escape the country's current political and social quagmire. Despite a long delay stretched out by far too many opening acts, the crowd's devotion never wavered.Throughout the energetic set, Ja Rule masterfully commanded the room with his signature raspy voice. Singing short snippets of his catalog and paying homage to his formative '90s influences, he would occasionally pause to ask, “Tel Aviv, What's happening?”The choice of phrase perfectly bridged a nostalgic echo of his breakout era with the anxious, collective question Israelis have been asking themselves daily. He didn't pander or try to artificially adapt his style; instead, he relied on music as a universal language to sweep the venue away.Ultimately, the night dissolved into a rare, unfeigned euphoria. While hip-hop is heavily associated with political protest, its origins remain rooted in the dance clubs as a medium giving raw expression to the body. The collective movement of the crowd served, first and foremost, as a plea for liberation.Ja Rule came to Tel Aviv to check in on the culture, helping an eager audience dance and shake off their pent-up energy before landing back on the ground of reality.

title: October 7 Nir Oz infiltrator among four Hamas terrorists killed in IDF strikes
body: The IDF killed four Hamas terrorists, including one who invaded Israeli territory on October 7, 2023, in a series of strikes in the Gaza throughout the day on Saturday, the military announced on Monday.In a strike in the southern Gazan city of Khan Younis, Israeli forces killed Nukhba terrorist Muhammad Kamel Masleh Qadih, who infiltrated Kibbutz Nir Oz during the October 7 massacre and oversaw the preparation and training of Hamas's Nukhba forces. In another strike in the area of Nuseirat in central Gaza, the IDF killed Diaa Abd al-Mohsen Muhammad Abu al-Rous, another Nukhba terrorist in Hamas's military wing. In the northern Gaza Strip, the IDF struck two Hamas terrorists on Saturday: Nabil Hamad, a senior member of Hamas's military recruitment framework, and Mohannad Nader Mahmoud Dahdouh, a sniper commander who the military said had been actively involved in combat against Israeli troops. IDF also announces two additional Hamas operatives killed in previous strikesAlso on Monday, the IDF announced that on October 22, two more Hamas terrorists were killed in strikes, one of whom - Wael Naif Fahmi Muslim - was a member of the Nukhba forces and was one of the terrorists who invaded Israel in 2023.The second terrorist killed on October 22 was Arafat Kamal Muhammad Ar'air, a squad commander in Hamas's rocket array.

title: Likud maintains contact with Mansour Abbas's Ra'am, journalist claims
body: Senior Likud officials and people close to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have maintained contact with Mansour Abbas's Ra'am party despite public opposition to cooperation with Arab parties, Channel 12 journalist Mohammad Magadli revealed in an interview with 103FM on Monday.Magadli, who also hosts a program on Radio Al-Nas, spoke with Gideon Oko and Amichai Attali on their 103FM program Sheva Tesha (Seven Nine), as political debate over cooperation with Arab parties continues to stir controversy. Behind the scenes, however, a more complex reality is unfolding, with Magadli claiming that contacts between the ruling party and Abbas's Ra'am party are continuing."People close to Netanyahu and within Likud have spoken with Mansour Abbas more than once since the polls closed," Magadli said at the beginning of the interview.Asked whether the channel of communication between Likud and Ra'am remained open, Magadli replied emphatically: "It was never closed. Even the most senior figures in Likud approach Ra'am and talk to them. Ra'am knows why it doesn't want to publicize these things and why it keeps this channel open. Ultimately, they understand that they have a way to exert influence, that there is coordination there, and that they are constantly talking to Likud."Magadli went on to argue that Netanyahu's political camp would be prepared to rely on Arab parties if doing so were necessary to secure power.Magadli criticizes Yair Netanyahu over comments on Arab Israelis"Netanyahu's camp will stop at nothing to remain in power. If he were a few seats short of winning, he would do anything to rely on Ra'am. Netanyahu's bloc is prepared to do anything to come to power, and if it needs to rely on both the Joint List and Ra'am to form a government, it will do so. There is no question about it."Later in the interview, Magadli addressed a post on X by Yair Netanyahu, the prime minister's son, in which he claimed that "the next October 7 will come from Israel's Arabs."ה7.10 הבא יגיע מערביי ישראל— Yair Netanyahu (@YairNetanyahu) November 1, 2026Magadli strongly condemned the statement, pointing to the contributions of Arab citizens to Israel since the October 7 attacks."As an Arab citizen of the State of Israel, Arab citizens have been contributing to and mobilizing for this country since October 7. Not one of them has left it. Yair Netanyahu should do us the courtesy of coming back here before lecturing Arab citizens, or any other citizen, about morality."Magadli also criticized National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir."This kind of racist rhetoric simply ignores the most important thing: Arab citizens were also kidnapped and murdered, and they played a very significant role in getting up and rebuilding this country. But it is not surprising, because the same Yair Netanyahu applauded Ra'am and spoke about how good and important they were when it suited his father. He is an irrelevant person, so let's not waste our time on him," he explained.Likud rejected Magadli's allegations in a statement, denying that it had maintained contact with Arab parties."Complete fake news! There has been and will be no contact whatsoever between Likud and Arab parties that support terrorism. This is another transparent and dishonest attempt by the propaganda media to legitimize the left-wing bloc relying on parties that support terrorism," the party said in a statement.

title: Israeli duo reaches European cheerleading final in landmark debut
body: An Israeli duo reached the final of the ICU European Performance Cheer Doubles Championships in Heraklion, Crete, marking a milestone for the sport in Israel.Competing in the Youth Pom Doubles category, Mili and Romi secured a place among the 10 finalists from a field of 31 pairs representing countries across Europe.Their achievement came during Israel's first appearance at the championships since cheerleading was officially recognized as a sport in the country and the Israeli Cheerleading Union was recognized as its national governing body.The championships brought together more than 1,100 participants from 24 countries. Israel was represented by four pairs competing in youth and senior categories.The result follows years of work to develop cheerleading in Israel, establish a competitive framework and prepare athletes for international competition. Combining athleticism, strength, flexibility, precision, coordination and teamwork, the sport continues to expand its presence in Israel.Milestone comes after years of developing cheerleading in Israel“This is an exciting and meaningful moment for all of us,” said Dr. Lyudmila Yasinska-Demri, founder and professional director of the Israeli Cheerleading Union.“After years of working to develop cheerleading in Israel, we received official recognition this year, and at our very first European Championships as a recognized national governing body, we have reached the final. Mili and Romi's achievement shows that Israel has talented athletes who can compete at the highest levels in Europe. We are proud of all the athletes representing Israel and will continue working to develop the sport and achieve further international success.”The appearance in the final marks an early competitive achievement for the newly recognized union as it works to nurture the next generation of athletes and strengthen Israel's presence in international cheerleading.

title: Kyari: 33.5m food insecurity projection not political forecast
body: The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, has cautioned opposition politicians against using the October 2026 Cadre Harmonisé food security assessment for political propaganda ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kyari, in a statement on Monday, said the projection that 33.5 million Nigerians could face severe food and nutrition insecurity between June and August 2027 should not be interpreted as an assessment of the performance or electoral prospects of any political administration. He described attempts by opposition voices to link the projection to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid as a misrepresentation of the technical assessment. The minister explained that the Cadre Harmonisé was developed by the Permanent Inter-State Committee for Drought Control in the Sahel (CILSS), alongside regional and technical partners, to identify food and nutrition security risks and enable governments and development partners to respond early. He said the assessment, supported by organisations including the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), World Food Programme (WFP), FEWS NET, UNICEF and the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), was not designed as an election forecast. According to him, the projected figure of 33.5 million represents a decline from the 34.8 million projected for the corresponding period in 2026. Kyari, however, noted that the assessment does not conduct retrospective analysis after the projected period to establish whether the forecasts were accurate. He identified climate change, inconsistent rainfall, prolonged dry spells and disruptions to weather patterns associated with the Super El Niño phenomenon as some of the factors contributing to food and nutrition insecurity. The minister said these challenges had affected planting seasons and crop production, particularly among farmers dependent on rain-fed agriculture. He added that the assessment did not attribute the projected food insecurity figures to the continuation of any particular political administration. Kyari said the Federal Government was responding to the identified risks through expanded access to fertiliser and other agricultural inputs, increased mechanisation, irrigation and dry-season farming, improved agricultural financing, and investments in storage, processing and climate-resilient agriculture. He also highlighted improved security in some farming communities, saying it had enabled farmers who previously could not access their farmlands to resume cultivation. According to him, areas such as Marte and Guzamala in Borno State, which were previously inaccessible to data collectors, have recorded improved stability, allowing the Cadre Harmonisé assessment to be conducted. The minister further listed progress in fertiliser distribution and local blending, support for smallholder farmers, mechanisation partnerships, expansion of dry-season farming and improved agricultural financing through the Bank of Agriculture as some of the government’s interventions. He acknowledged that the interventions would not resolve the country’s food insecurity challenges overnight, describing the problem as longstanding and structural. “Food insecurity is a longstanding and structural challenge that has developed over many years and predates this administration,” he said. Kyari, however, maintained that agriculture had recorded progress since Tinubu assumed office, adding that the government remained committed to increasing food production and strengthening the country’s food supply systems. “As Minister, I accept the responsibility that comes with this challenge. When the data identifies a risk, our duty is to act on it, not to hide from it,” he said. He urged political actors to exercise caution when discussing food security data, warning against reducing the livelihoods and welfare of millions of Nigerians to political talking points. The minister said the government welcomed scrutiny and constructive criticism but insisted that technical assessments should not be deliberately misrepresented for electoral purposes. He added that the government would use the findings of the Cadre Harmonisé to strengthen interventions, support farmers, protect livelihoods and improve access to safe, nutritious and affordable food. The post Kyari: 33.5m food insecurity projection not political forecast appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Central Asian Cinema Showcased at Asian Film Festival Barcelona
body: A young Kazakh couple who fake a terminal illness to raise money online are at the center of Sicko , one of several Central Asian films screened at this year’s Asian Film Festival Barcelona. The festival, which concluded on November 1, also featured the award-winning Kyrgyz drama Kurak and other productions from across the region. Organized by the Spanish cultural institution Casa Asia, the festival ran from October 22 to November 1. Its program included more than 100 films from 25 countries across Asia and the Pacific. Although India was the main focus, organizers also highlighted Central Asian cinema, with productions from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan. The Kazakh satirical thriller Sicko (2025), directed by Aitore Zholdaskali, competed in the festival’s official competition. Set in Almaty, the film follows the couple as their fundraising scam attracts far more attention than they anticipated. The film addresses the pressures of debt and shows how social media can turn public sympathy into a source of income. It made its international premiere at the International Film Festival Rotterdam earlier this year. The second Kazakh film was Crickets, It’s Your Turn , a Kazakhstan-France co-production directed by Olga Korotko. A young photographer named Merey is invited to a birthday party at a secluded house in the mountains outside Almaty. There, she encounters a group of men, and the gathering gradually descends into violence. The film had its world premiere at Switzerland’s Locarno Film Festival in 2024, in the Cineasti del Presente section, which showcases emerging filmmakers. In Barcelona, it competed in the NETPAC section, named after the international Network for the Promotion of Asian Cinema. The screening took place on October 30. Farz (2026), directed by Sarvar Karimov, was Uzbekistan’s contribution. The film follows a man who sacrifices the money he has saved for a pilgrimage to Mecca to build a home for his late friend’s family. It screened on October 27 in the festival’s Special Section, having previously featured at the Kazan International Film Festival. Kyrgyzstan was represented by Kurak (2025), a drama directed by Erke Dzhumakmatova and Emil Atageldiev. The title refers to traditional Kyrgyz patchwork sewing, in which individual pieces of fabric are joined to create a single textile. The film similarly weaves together several stories. One woman is blackmailed by a law enforcement officer, while another seeks justice following the suicide of her 18-year-old daughter after she was drugged and raped. The dramatized scenes are interwoven with real testimonies from women. By the time it screened in Barcelona, Kurak had already won several international awards. In 2025, it received two awards at the Busan International Film Festival in South Korea. In 2026, it won Best Film at the Dhaka International Film Festival in Bangladesh and received the international jury’s Grand Prix, along with the critics’ and high school jury awards, at the Vesoul International Film Festival of Asian Cinemas in France. Despite its success abroad, Kurak faced obstacles in Kyrgyzstan. The Times of Central Asia previously reported that Kurak had been denied a distribution certificate in Kyrgyzstan and was not screened at the Bishkek International Film Festival, despite the organizers’ initial plans.

title: Russian forces strike Ukrainian UAV assembly, storage sites in past day — top brass
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. Russian forces struck Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) assembly and storage sites and enemy deployment areas over the past 24 hours in the special military operation in Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
"Operational/tactical aircraft, attack unmanned aerial vehicles, missile troops and artillery of the Russian groups of forces struck energy and transport infrastructure facilities used by the Ukrainian army, workshops assembling and sites storing unmanned aerial vehicles, and also temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries in 142 locations," the ministry said in a statement.
The Ukrainian army lost roughly 925 troops in battles with Russian forces in all the frontline areas over the past 24 hours, according to the latest data on the special military operation in Ukraine released by Russia’s Defense Ministry.
The latest figures show that the Ukrainian army lost roughly 110 troops and three armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup North, about 115 troops and three armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup West and over 150 troops and two armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup South.
During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army also lost roughly 335 troops and 11 armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center, about 195 troops and three armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup East and around 20 troops and eight motor vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup Dnepr, the latest figures show.
Russia’s Battlegroup North inflicted roughly 110 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed three enemy armored combat vehicles in its areas of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup North units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army and a National Guard brigade in areas near the settlements of Kolodeznoye, Shipovatoye, Vodyanoye and Martovoye in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.
In the Sumy Region, Battlegroup North units struck formations of a mechanized brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Ivolzhanskoye and the city of Sumy, it said.
The Ukrainian army lost roughly 110 personnel, three armored combat vehicles, five motor vehicles and an electronic warfare station in the areas of responsibility of Russia’s Battlegroup North over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup West inflicted roughly 115 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed three enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup West units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, an assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Studenok, Glushchenkovo and Vishnevka in the Kharkov Region and Rubtsy in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 115 personnel, three armored combat vehicles, eight motor vehicles and an artillery gun in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it said.
Russia’s Battlegroup South inflicted more than 150 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed two enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup South units improved their tactical position and inflicted losses on formations of three mechanized brigades, a mountain assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Kramatorsk, Slavyansk, Nikolayevka and Vasilevskaya Pustosh in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 150 personnel, two armored combat vehicles and 25 motor vehicles in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Center inflicted roughly 335 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed 11 enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Center units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of three mechanized brigades, an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army, a special operations brigade and a National Guard brigade in areas near the settlements of Stepanovka, Sergeyevka, Krinitsy, Kamyshevakha, Andreyevka and Kamenka in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 335 personnel, 11 armored combat vehicles, seven motor vehicles, an artillery gun and two electronic warfare stations in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup East inflicted roughly 195 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed three enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup East units advanced into the depth of the enemy’s defenses and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of a mechanized brigade, two air assault brigades, an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Novorozovka and Tersyanka in the Zaporozhye Region, Pokrovskoye, Ivanovka and Pavlovka in the Dnepropetrovsk Region," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 195 personnel, three armored combat vehicles, three motor vehicles and a field artillery gun in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Dnepr eliminated roughly 20 Ukrainian troops and destroyed eight enemy motor vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Dnepr units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on formations of a mechanized brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Preobrazhenka and Orekhov in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
"Up to 20 [Ukrainian] military personnel and eight motor vehicles were destroyed," it said.
Russian air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 658 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Air defense capabilities shot down 658 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles," the ministry said.
Overall, the Russian Armed Forces have destroyed 674 Ukrainian combat aircraft, 284 helicopters, 277,381 unmanned aerial vehicles, 672 surface-to-air missile systems, 31,502 tanks and other armored combat vehicles, 1,794 multiple rocket launchers, 36,859 field artillery guns and mortars and 76,161 special military motor vehicles since the start of the special military operation, the ministry reported.

title: Should Finland test every pupil at a national level? Researchers say no
body:
The idea stems from concern about declining skills.
A group of researchers has criticised proposals to test primary school pupils in Finland.
The researchers said tests covering entire age groups would not improve learning outcomes. Instead, they argued the drawbacks of such exams would outweigh the benefits.
"The link between national tests and improved learning outcomes has been either weak or contradictory elsewhere. Weaker performing schools in particular have not benefited from national tests," said Jaakko Kauko , an education policy expert at Tampere University.
Parliament's Audit Committee has proposed that Finnish schools could trial national tests for entire age groups. The aim is to gain reliable information on pupils' learning outcomes.
The proposal stems from concern about declining skills. Children's and young people's learning outcomes have continued to worsen, for example, in international Pisa (Programme for International Student Assessment) assessments that test how well pupils can apply what they have learned.
Economists who have studied education have highlighted the benefits of national tests. They say they would provide comparable data on learning outcomes across regions and schools.
Christian Ydesen , a professor at the University of Zurich, said introducing national school tests in Denmark has not raised learning outcomes.
"Denmark's Pisa results have weakened again. National tests do not solve the learning crisis," Ydesen told Yle.
A Danish pupil now sits ten national tests in total during their time at school.
Parliament will debate the Audit Committee's report on national tests on Thursday this week.
Yle News' video podcast recently asked why Finnish pupils, once among the world’s best readers, have tumbled down the rankings.

title: Thales Wins 53 9M U S Navy Contract for Remote Minehunting Systems
body:
Thales subsidiary Advanced Acoustic Concepts (AAC) has secured a $53.9 million U.S. Navy contract to produce and deliver two integrated Remote Minehunting (RMH) modules, along with technical support.
Options for additional modules could raise the contract's total value to $196.2 million.
The system supports the Navy's Mine Countermeasures (MCM) mission by enabling remote detection, location and classification of underwater mines, reducing risks to sailors and naval platforms in contested maritime environments.
The modular RMH suite combines advanced sonar, mission management software and remotely operated vehicle technology. Its multi-view towed Synthetic Aperture Sonar (SAS) delivers high-resolution underwater imaging to improve mine detection and reduce false targets.
The system also features AI-enhanced Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) algorithms that help operators process, classify, map and manage mine countermeasure data, accelerating target assessment and improving classification accuracy.
