title: Iran killed her teenage daughter – now she is facing up to the regime
body: Samira says she never used to be political. “I worked in sales in Iran. I sold cosmetics,” she tells BBC Panorama. But that all changed the day her only child was shot dead in front of her by Iranian security forces. Sixteen-year-old Sevda was taking part in protests against Iran’s repressive regime that engulfed the country earlier this year – before the US and Israel launched widespread air strikes which killed the country’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Samira’s grief became fury as Iran’s authorities then hindered, rather than helped, her search for her daughter’s body, she says. “I realised that finding Sevda wasn’t the end, but just the beginning of all the harassment they put me through.” Samira made a dramatic escape from Iran on foot, navigating dangerous mountainous terrain. She now lives abroad in hiding, describing herself as a “one-woman army fighting the regime”. In a search for accountability and justice after her daughter’s death, she is intent on naming the members of the security forces and officials she believes were responsible for firing fatal shots during the protests. “They’ll bring me to the brink of death before they kill me, but finding me won’t be easy… Return to normal life? There is no going back,” she says. Samira is among several Iranians the BBC has spoken to since the start of the year. Some, still inside the country, told Panorama they wanted to speak out despite the risks, saying they had found it difficult to hold on to hope once the mass protests had been brutally crushed. The Iranian embassy in London told Panorama that peaceful and legitimate protests had been hijacked by foreign powers, including the US, which promoted violence, provided weapons and equipment, and compromised public security. Sevda was killed on 9 January as she and Samira took part in huge demonstrations on the outskirts of the capital Tehran which had begun the previous month. They had been sparked by economic discontent, before escalating into calls for an end to the country’s Islamic Republic. Though Samira denies she was especially political then, she says her daughter was. Sevda’s idols were two other young women – Mahsa Amini, whose death in custody after an alleged violation against the mandatory headscarf triggered mass protests, and Nika Shakarami, who was killed during a subsequent uprising against Iran’s strict Islamic dress code for women. “She kept them alive in her thoughts and always wanted to continue their path [of resistance],” Samira says. The day before Sevda was killed, the numbers protesting had been particularly high. Samira says she and Sevda had responded to a call by Reza Pahlavi, the exiled son of Iran’s last shah (king), for demonstrations. “The security forces had lost control,” she says. The swell in numbers had spooked Iran’s government, and the following day a shoot-to-kill order was announced, Samira says. But she had thought it just an empty threat. “They lied so much in Iran… We couldn’t imagine a massacre of that scale.” And they were reassured, she says, by US President Trump’s promise that he had their backs. He had told US media on 8 January: “I have let [the Iranian authorities] know that if they start killing people, which they tend to do during their riots… we’re going to hit them very hard.” But nevertheless the crowds appeared smaller on the 9th, Samira says. Sevda seemed to know the risks, she says. Her daughter took off her earrings and gave them to her grandmother. She also shared her phone passcode with Samira. The mother and daughter gathered with the rest of the protesters. Sevda then stood on a dustbin and began leading a chant. “It seemed there were more forces than people,” Samira says of the area where they were. “I don’t know how, within one day, they gathered so many… Basijis and IRGC [Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps] forces.” The IRGC defends the country’s Islamic establishment, and the paramilitary Basij Resistance Force are volunteers for the IRGC. “A sniper fired from the roof of a building on our right. The bullet must have come from the rooftop. The bullet went through her heart. I couldn’t even scream. I just stared at Sevda – her body lying lifeless. Blood was gushing out her mouth and nose. I couldn’t believe it, I couldn’t believe she was dying. Her eyes were still looking at me.” Samira says she managed to get Sevda to hospital and she was told they were operating on her, but then the door opened and she saw Sevda had been zipped into a body bag. Sevda’s body was taken away. Samira says it took her days to find her daughter again. Like many others, she found herself at one of Tehran’s largest morgues. “Teenagers – young boys and girls. So many had been killed,” she cries. “I died with every bag I unzipped. I’d never seen so many bodies. But I wouldn’t give up.” She finally found her daughter. “Three bodies were piled on top of Sevda. That’s how we found her.” Iranian authorities acknowledgethat more than 3,000 people were killed in the protests, but claim some were members of the security forces. One human rights group, Hrana, however, estimates the number of dead stands at more than 7,000, most of them protesters. Finding Sevda’s body was just the beginning of Samira’s battle with the authorities, she says. To be allowed to take away the body for burial, she says she was forced to say that “terrorists” rather than the security forces had been responsible for Sevda’s death. “They did this to cover up what they’d done on 8 and 9 January, to hide how many people they had killed. They silenced families by telling them to say their loved ones were killed by Israeli or American terrorists.” Nevertheless she was barred from visiting the grave after the funeral, or organising a tombstone, she says. And Samira says the harassment continued. A few days before the ceremony to mark 40 days since Sevda died – highly significant in Iranian culture – she says she was summoned by a local branch of the Ministry of Intelligence. “They told me: ‘You should give us an interview and say that Sevda was a Basiji and she was killed by the protesters. Then we will announce her [as] a martyr – you will then receive perks, a house, or anything that you want.'” She is sure this offer was prompted by fear, because she had shared Sevda’s death with an Iranian media organisation based in London, once the internet had been reconnected in the country. “It scared them that I was in touch with external networks or those outside Iran.” To avoid giving the interview, Samira fled Iran as soon as the 40th day anniversary was over. “I didn’t want to trade with my child’s blood.” She says people smugglers helped her to escape. She crossed rivers and mountains to get to safety. A video she made of herself fleeing makes clear her fury. “This crap government, these bastards, they’ve harassed me so much,” she tells the camera as she marches along a mountain path bordered by a deep ravine. Samira says after she continued to give interviews to foreign media from abroad, she was charged in absentia with a string of offences, including “moharebeh” – waging war against God – which can carry the death penalty. To mark what would have been Sevda’s 17th birthday, her relatives and friends held a vigil – with Samira watching from exile on a livestream. “Then suddenly, the feed cut out,” she says. She discovered that the event had been raided, she says, and some of her family and friends arrested by the IRGC. She says her family was warned by the authorities that, if they continued to gather at Sevda’s grave, her body would be exhumed and moved elsewhere. Now, Samira shares the names, online, of Iranian security force members and officials she believes were responsible for firing fatal shots during the 8 and 9 January protests she and Sevda joined. “I want justice to be served for every single person whose name I expose, because they have killed so many young people. My goal is for them to be identified so they can be put on trial,” she says. When one of the men Samira named online was later found dead, a regime supporter offered a $5,000 (£3,732) reward for information about her whereabouts, presuming she was responsible. Iranian state media has since reported the arrest of nine people in connection with the death. Despite the risks, Samira says she refuses to be silenced. “Every day and every second without Sevda is very difficult for me. It’s like a mother who has lost her heart, who has lost her being, has lost her life… “But the fact that Sevda is not breathing has made it possible for me to stand on my feet… to think about honouring her life and her path… all those bodies I saw, all those body bags I opened looking for Sevda, they all made me fight the Islamic Republic until my last breath.”

title: Gazprom sets new record for daily gas supplies to China via Power of Siberia pipeline
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. On November 1, Gazprom set a new record for daily gas supplies to China via the Power of Siberia pipeline, the company announced.
Gazprom has reached an all-time high for daily gas supplies to China via the Power of Siberia pipeline. "A new record was set on November 1," the statement said.
The company noted that Russian gas supplies are being delivered under a long-term gas purchase and sale agreement between Gazprom and China’s CNPC.
Previously, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak stated that Russia would supply 39 bln cubic meters of gas to China this year via the Power of Siberia pipeline.
In 2025, Gazprom became the largest gas exporter to China. Supplies via the Power of Siberia pipeline reached 38.8 bln cubic meters, exceeding initial contractual obligations by 800 mln cubic meters.
Power of Siberia is the largest gas transmission system in eastern Russia, with an export capacity of 38 bln cubic meters of gas per year. The first pipeline shipments of Russian gas to China via the eastern route began in December 2019, under a 30-year contract signed in 2014 between Gazprom and China’s CNPC. The total volume of supplies over the entire term will exceed 1 trillion cubic meters of gas, with a contract value of $400 bln.

title: IDF's next-generation artillery gets NIS 600 million training boost with Elbit deal
body: The Defense Ministry and IDF have signed a 15-year agreement worth approximately NIS 600 million with Elbit Systems to establish a dedicated training facility for the Artillery Corps, supporting the new Ro'em (SIGMA) self-propelled howitzer and Lahav (PULS) rocket launcher systems.The agreement includes the development and supply of advanced technological training infrastructure, as well as instruction, maintenance, and logistical support services.The deal follows a separate $235 million contract announced on October 19 to supply Elbit's PULS rocket launchers and EXTRA-MR rockets to an unnamed European country.The Ro'em, known internationally as the SIGMA 155, is a 155 mm. self-propelled howitzer mounted on a highly mobile 10x10 truck chassis.The Defense Ministry decided to procure the system in 2017, and development began in 2019. In 2021, it was determined that the howitzer would enter operational service in the IDF under the name Ro'em. Elbit has also been expanding its international operations, including plans announced in October for a new production and maintenance facility in Sweden.In late 2025, the first unit officially declared the system operational following an extensive period of testing and deployment across a range of operational environments.Ro'em offers significant advantages over older artillery systemsThe Ro'em offers significant advantages over the US-made M109 Doher self-propelled howitzer, which remains in IDF service.Thanks to its automated ammunition loading and gun positioning systems, the Ro'em requires a crew of just three soldiers: a commander, gunner, and driver, compared with eight crew members operating the M109.The new howitzer has a firing rate of six to eight shells per minute, more than twice that of its predecessor. It can also fire its first shell in less than 60 seconds after the vehicle comes to a halt.Tests have demonstrated a high degree of accuracy, with a reported deviation of approximately 0.7%.The Ro'em also features independent navigation and fire-control systems installed in each howitzer, allowing it to operate without relying on a separate command-and-control vehicle.The system is designed to meet the IDF's operational requirements for at least the next 50 years. It also provides protection for the crew inside an armored driver's cabin.Elbit expands international defense salesThe Ro'em is not intended exclusively for the IDF. Elbit Systems also markets the howitzer internationally and, according to foreign sources, it has been sold to Singapore. Denmark, Thailand, and the Philippines have purchased an earlier version of the system.Thailand has continued procuring Israeli defense technology. In October, Israeli manufacturer IWI announced the delivery of its ARBEL anti-drone system to Thailand, amid broader Thai military modernization plans that also include artillery acquisitions.Elbit has also been broadening its portfolio beyond land-based weapons. On October 20, the company announced its acquisition of Canadian underwater drone manufacturer International Submarine Engineering, expanding its maritime defense capabilities.Zeev Landau, deputy director-general and head of the Directorate of Production and Procurement at the Defense Ministry, said the agreement reflects the ministry's strategy of strengthening operational readiness and supporting Israeli industry.Boaz Cohen, general manager of Elbit Systems' Land Division and IMI, added that the artillery school and training framework for Artillery Corps soldiers would enable the corps to maintain its fire capabilities at the highest level of readiness.

title: Six in seven journalist murders go unpunished, UNESCO reports
body:
Global impunity for journalist killings has risen for the first time in more than a decade, while the growing use of drones is an emerging threat for reporters in conflict zones, according to the latest report from UN cultural organization UNESCO.
“Journalists are increasingly paying with their lives for reporting from the frontlines of war and far too often those responsible for their killings are not held accountable,” said Director-General Khaled El-Enany.
UNESCO first began measuring the proportion of journalist killings that go unpunished in 2012. The rate reached 86 per cent in 2024-2025, up one per cent from the previous two-year period.
A confirmed total of 189 journalists and other media workers lost their lives in 2024-2025, or 20 per cent more than during the previous biennium and the highest number since 2014-2015.
More than two thirds, 127, were killed in conflict zones, accounting for 67 per cent of the death toll.
The findings come in the Director-General’s Report on the Safety of Journalists and the Danger of Impunity, which is published every two years to mark the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists , observed on 2 November.
“Over the past year, at least 34 journalists paid the ultimate price. Six of every seven such killings go unpunished. In conflict settings, the rate of impunity is close to 100 per cent,” UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in his message for the Day.
“This is a heinous affront to the victims and their loved ones, as well as all of us who depend on journalists to remain informed and engaged.”
Killings were recorded across all regions of the world during the 2024-2025 biennium, representing “a global scourge”, the report said.
The highest number of verified cases were in the Arab States (97) followed by Latin American and the Caribbean (37), Asia-Pacific (34), Central and Eastern Europe (14), Africa (6) and Western Europe and North America (1).
The State of Palestine had the highest number of killings in both years, at 30 and 32, respectively.
The report also identified what UNESCO called “a disturbing new threat” – the growing use of drones to kill journalists. During 2024-2025, drone strikes killed 50 journalists, or 40 per cent of all those killed in conflict zones.
It documented seven incidents in which several journalists were targeted and killed in a single attack, including strikes on media workplaces and temporary reporting centres. Fifteen journalists were reportedly killed while wearing press vests or in vehicles clearly marked ‘Press’.
“I reiterate my call for the respect of UN Security Council Resolution 2222 unanimously adopted in 2015 on the protection of journalists, media professionals and associated personnel as civilians in situations of conflict, a status reaffirmed in the Pact for the Future ,” said Mr. El-Enany.
The report also highlighted progress, as impunity in non-conflict countries has continued to decline. The rate has fallen from 94 per cent in 2012 to 77 per cent in 2026, or one percentage point per year.
The number of journalist killings in non-conflict zones, 85, is also the lowest in 18 years.
“This demonstrates that when governments invest in investigations, prosecutions and protections for journalists, progress is possible,” UNESCO said.
The agency noted, however, that women journalists continue to face particular risks, both in war zones and online. Thirteen out of the 14 women killed in 2024-2035 were in countries experiencing armed conflict.
Furthermore, a 2025 study by UN Women and the International Center for Journalists found that 75 per cent of women journalists had experienced online or offline abuse and harassment. More than 40 per cent reported offline violence linked to online attacks, up from 20 per cent in a 2020 UNESCO survey.
“Across the world, journalists continue to pay an outrageous price for telling the truth,” the UN Secretary-General said.
“On this International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists, we demand justice. When journalists are targeted and their reporting is extinguished, it makes victims of us all.”
As online abuse, gender-based attacks and impunity ramp up the threats to women reporting from crisis zones, journalists and UN leaders are calling for urgent action to protect those who document conflict.
In Mexico’s armed forces, an order from a superior is meant to be obeyed without question. For many women in uniform, investigative journalist Zorayda Gallegos found, that can include an order to step into an officer’s bedroom.

title: Could the US midterms cause a surprise stock market rally?
body: Investors have a lot on their plate. Oil, inflation and interest rates are climbing, while tech stocks are volatile amid growing fears of an AI bubble . Throw in US President Donald Trump's unpredictability, mounting government debt, regional wars and stretched stock valuations, and it’s all getting a bit much. Now comes another challenge: Americans go to the polls on November 3 for the midterm elections , which will determine control of Congress and the direction of Mr Trump's presidency. Yet here’s a curious twist. History shows that midterm elections have typically been followed by a strong run for Wall Street. JP Morgan Asset Management’s analysis shows the S&P 500 has risen in the 12 months following every midterm since 1950. Might history repeat itself? If so, stock market bulls have plenty to look forward to, says Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell. “The past is no guarantee, but the third year of a presidential term is, on average, the best one for the US stock market.” The average third-year gain across postwar presidencies is a stellar 16.1 per cent. No other presidential year averages a double-digit gain, he says. One theory is that presidents have an incentive to boost the economy ahead of the next election. Another is that the midterms often deliver a lame-duck president who struggles to pass legislation, allowing businesses to operate without interference from Washington. Markets are often volatile before the vote, but when the result is known, investors can focus on policy rather than polling, says Jason Hollands, managing director at Evelyn Partners. Gridlock could boost stocks Mr Trump looks on course to lose control of both the House and Senate. If that happened, it could actually help stocks. “A divided Congress would make major new legislation harder to pass. That could limit the prospect of sweeping changes to areas such as tax and regulation,” Mr Hollands says. But investors shouldn’t assume divided government means quiet government. Aliasgar Tambawala, co-chief investment officer at Klay Group, warns that political gridlock brings problems of its own. “A divided legislature may lead to greater disruptions around issues such as the debt ceiling and government funding.” Mr Trump's executive powers, including tariffs, would remain largely intact, while the President retains his veto. Mr Tambawala expects political volatility to persist, but says GCC investors face bigger concerns, notably the situation in the Strait of Hormuz . “A durable resolution would augur well for the region.” Despite recent volatility, the S&P 500 and tech-focused Nasdaq are up around 12 per cent this year, says Tony Hallside, chief executive of STP Partners. Further gains depend on earnings. “Getting the election out of the way helps sentiment, but it does not create earnings growth. If inflation persists or profits fall short of expectations, the historical election pattern will offer little protection.” AI is another concern. Can the technology justify the huge sums being invested by generating sustainable revenue and profits? “Political clarity will not compensate for disappointing commercial results,” Mr Hallside says. Reality checks for investors Madhur Kakkar, chief executive of Elevate Financial Services, warns that markets face formidable headwinds. Brent crude has hit $117 a barrel, the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates in September and may do so again in December, while 10-year Treasury yields are approaching 5 per cent. “Higher Treasury yields give investors a competitive income alternative at a time when US equity valuations remain demanding,” Mr Kakkar says. The S&P 500's Shiller price-to-earnings ratio ended October at 40.88, a level exceeded only during the dot-com boom. On October 29, Alphabet shares plunged 13 per cent, wiping $500 billion off its value after heavy AI infrastructure spending contributed to negative quarterly free cash flow of $9.1 billion. Yet the US economy remains resilient, with third-quarter GDP growing at an annualised 3.4 per cent. Mr Kakkar urges investors to maintain balanced portfolios rather than chase a post-midterms rally. Vijay Valecha, chief investment officer at Century Financial, believes AI and interest rates, rather than politics, will determine whether markets finish 2026 strongly. “Easing inflation and a successful Anthropic IPO could still fuel a year-end rally.” For the GCC, the outlook is firmer than headline figures suggest, he says. The IMF expects Gulf output to shrink 4.8 per cent this year because of the Iran war, before rebounding 9.1 per cent in 2027. Saudi Arabia and the UAE are shipping substantial oil volumes around the Strait of Hormuz, while high crude prices bolster revenue. Non-oil activity remains strong, but a full recovery depends on the strait reopening, which the IMF assumes will begin in March 2027. Mr Mould remains cautious. Inflation is sticky, interest rates may rise, the Middle East war could drag on, oil and equity valuations are high, and the AI boom could end in an investment bust. History suggests the midterms could unleash another Wall Street rally. But with so many risks stacking up, investors may discover that this time, history really is bunk.

title: Russia says stepping up diplomatic efforts to normalize situation around Iran crucial
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. Intensifying diplomatic efforts to normalize the situation around Iran is important and Russia is ready to facilitate the process, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said.
"We consider it necessary to step up diplomatic work to normalize the situation," she said. "We support the mediators’ efforts and, for our part, we assist the negotiation process, we confirm our readiness to contribute both to finding mutually acceptable solutions and their further implementation.".

title: Anambra govt seals orphanage, gives reason
body:
The Anambra State Government has sealed an orphanage in Nwelle Ezunaka, Oyi Local Government Area, over poor service delivery and unhygienic conditions.
The Commissioner for Women’s Affairs and Children’s Welfare, Esther Onyekesi, disclosed this on Saturday during an inspection of the facility.
The inspection aimed to assess operational standards and children’s welfare at the Arrow of God Children’s Home.
Mrs Onyekesi said the facility fell below prescribed standards, while its unhygienic environment raised concerns about the children’s welfare.
“The Arrow of God Children’s Home, Nwelle Ezunaka, Oyi Local Government Area, is operating below the required standards, with an unhygienic environment posing concerns for the welfare of the children,” she said.
She added that the inspection team sealed the facility, owned by retired Lieutenant Colonel Deborah Ogoo, for failing to meet regulatory requirements.
“This home is hereby sealed by the inspection team over its failure to meet the prescribed standards,” she said.
Mrs Onyekesi reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to protecting children and ensuring residential care facilities provide safe, clean and conducive environments.
She stressed that no children’s home would be allowed to compromise the safety, dignity and well-being of children under its care.
The News Agency of Nigeria reports that eight children were rescued from the facility.

title: Government directs up to 20% of printing jobs to Ghana Publishing Company – MD
body: The government has issued a Cabinet directive allocating up to 20 per cent of all government printing assignments to the Ghana Publishing Company Limited (GPCL), according to its Managing Director, Nana Kwasi Boatey. Mr Boatey said the directive, secured through the intervention of the sector Minister, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, was part of efforts to strengthen the capacity of the state-owned printing company and improve its commercial sustainability. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at Jubilee House on Monday, November 2, he said the company had already regained the confidence of government institutions after securing major printing contracts, including the national budget, the mid-year budget review and the 2025 State of the Nation Address. He noted that the company had secured the prestigious national budget printing assignment for the first time in more than seven years. He further disclosed that the Finance Minister had announced GPCL as the country’s primary printer during the presentation of the 2026 budget, with a mandate to lead the production of materials for the government’s nationwide free textbook programme. “We stand ready to take on this challenge and deliver timeously on all printing contracts and at the highest quality,” he said, urging corporate Ghana to partner with the company to expand its printing and publishing operations.

title: Hypersonica raises €100 million to accelerate development of European hypersonic deep-strike systems
body: Lightspeed and General Catalyst co-led the Series B round, with participation from existing investors including Plural and 201 Ventures. The financing, announced on 2 November, follows a February flight test of the company’s HS-1 prototype. Hypersonica said the prototype exceeded Mach 6 over a range of more than 300 kilometres, making it the first privately funded European defence company to reach that milestone. The company also said its development model reduces costs by more than 80% compared with conventional approaches. “Series B marks our transition from demonstration to delivery,” co-founders Dr Philipp Kerth, chief executive, and Dr Marc Ewenz, chief technology officer, said in a joint statement. “This funding will accelerate development, increase testing cadence, support European reindustrialisation and help ensure Europe has access to sovereign capability developed and produced in Europe.” Since the test flight, Hypersonica has expanded its engineering team, deepened engagement with governments and strengthened European industrial partnerships. It develops, owns and controls its technology in Europe, with the aim of supplying European allies with capabilities free of US International Traffic in Arms Regulations restrictions. The company cited an initial £770 million over four years allocated to the UK-German Deep Precision Strike programme under Britain’s Defence Investment Plan. It also highlighted a NATO-led multinational initiative announced in July that envisages £37 billion of investment in deep precision strike capabilities over the next decade. “Hypersonica is redefining how advanced defence capability gets built,” said Alexander Schmitt, a partner at Lightspeed. “The team pairs deep technical expertise with exceptional speed of execution, and the strength of our support reflects our confidence in both the technology and their ability to deliver.” The new capital will fund more frequent tests and help build the technology and manufacturing capacity needed for the programme. Hypersonica said its goal remained to develop and produce hypersonic strike systems in Europe for European and allied customers. “Strategic autonomy begins with the ability to build critical technologies at speed, at scale and at a fraction of the cost of traditional systems,” said Jeannette zu Fürstenberg, president and managing director at General Catalyst. “That is exactly what Philipp, Marc, and the Hypersonica team are doing.”

title: Last week 208 incidents recorded at power facilities in Ukraine
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. The number of incidents that resulted in the destruction or damage of Ukraine's energy and oil and gas infrastructure amounted to more than 200 over the past week, Ukraine's Energy Ministry said.
"During the last week a total of 208 incidents were recorded that resulted in the destruction or damage of energy and oil and gas infrastructure," it said on Telegram.
The ministry added that the situation in the energy system remains difficult.
In recent weeks, power outage schedules have been introduced daily in several Ukrainian regions because of damage to the energy infrastructure. Emergency shutdowns are often necessary due to shortages in the system. Water supply disruptions were reported in some localities.

title: Tender announced for 2027 food procurement for AFU
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Ministry of Defense reported this.
According to Deputy Minister of Defense Mstyslav Banik, “all 360 items listed in the food catalog have been fully updated. These changes were made to specify the requirements for food supplied to the military. Key changes include standardizing the water content in frozen meat, specifying calorie counts, and setting size limits for fruits and vegetables.”
These changes were approved in June of this year. Updated data was added to the product descriptions primarily to ensure that military personnel receive higher-quality food.
Information on the nutritional energy value for each item has been added to the product descriptions, as well as the protein and fat content per 100 g for products subject to DSTU standards. These include, in particular, meat, fish, and dairy products. This will allow for better control over the total caloric content of meal kits.
The new specifications include permissible water content limits for frozen meat and poultry. While these percentages may vary depending on the type of meat and the freezing method, they cannot exceed 5%.
For fruits and vegetables, both maximum and minimum size limits have been specified.
In the procurement announcement for 2027, the price per person per meal kit has increased. The expected cost for 2026 was 171.48 UAH, and for 2027, 181.74 UAH. The reasons for the price increase are rising energy costs and the inflation rate.
However, the final price will be determined based on the results of the bidding process. For example, last year a meal kit cost between 120 and 155 UAH, depending on the contract.
Compliance with quality requirements and contractual obligations will be verified by specialists from the Main Directorate for State Quality Assurance through random inspections.
“It is important for us not only to plan purchases in advance but also to monitor contract fulfillment. The agency uses the SLA methodology, which allows us to assess the completeness and timeliness of deliveries, as well as suppliers’ compliance with contractual obligations. This helps us track contract fulfillment at various stages and respond promptly to deviations,” noted Artem Romaniukov, acting director of the Agency.
A Service Level Agreement (SLA) is a tool for monitoring the effectiveness of logistics processes; it quantifies the quality of suppliers’ work and records the accuracy of delivery times and the completeness of each shipment.
Orders for 2027 have been divided into more than 20 lots, varying in volume and value. This will allow suppliers with varying capacities to participate in the bidding process and secure government contracts.
Deliveries will be organized according to a regional model: each supplier will be assigned a specific region. This helps plan logistics and ensure timely delivery of food to military units.
For the third consecutive year, the agency is announcing the food procurement tender in advance so that suppliers have time to prepare production, organize logistics, and fulfill orders on time. Consequently, this will ensure that military personnel receive their food on time.
As reported by Ukrinform, the Defense Procurement Agency began purchasing tactical missiles and aircraft for the Defense Forces in 2026.

title: US journalist's proposal to demilitarize Russia's Kaliningrad exclave misguided — expert
body:
KALININGRAD, November 2. /TASS/. The Kaliningrad Region's security cannot be bargained away in international negotiations, Andrey Kropotkin, the speaker of the region’s Legislative Assembly, told TASS, commenting on an article in an American publication that proposed the "demilitarization of the Kaliningrad Region as a condition for future negotiations on Ukraine."
Earlier, the US military-analytical outlet Breaking Defense published an article by Zack Schneider, a researcher at the Casimir Pulaski Foundation, suggesting that the demilitarization of the Kaliningrad Region be considered as a precondition for future negotiations on Ukraine. The article effectively advocates using the Ukrainian crisis as leverage to reshape the entire military balance in the Baltic region.
"First and foremost, it must be borne in mind that the Kaliningrad Region is not a subject of political horse-trading; it is an integral part of Russia. Issues concerning its security cannot be decided on the basis of proposals put forward by foreign experts. Any attempt to link a settlement of the conflict in Ukraine to restrictions on the defensive capabilities of a particular Russian region is fundamentally misguided, especially when such proposals are accompanied by discussions about the possibility of launching strikes against the Kaliningrad Region.
"As I have said many times, the Kaliningrad Region is first and foremost its people - their families, businesses, schools, and universities. It is our history and our future. The region's security is not a bargaining chip in international negotiations," Kropotkin told TASS.
As part of Russia, the Kaliningrad Region is a semi-exclave, geographically separated from the country's mainland by the territories of European Union and NATO member states. Recently, rhetoric targeting the Russian region has become increasingly hostile, with foreign media outlets publishing threats of an economic and territorial blockade of the Kaliningrad Region.

title: Syria, Iraq stir hope despite memories of war with resumption of Shiite pilgrimages- analysis
body: DAMASCUS — Syria and Iraq are discussing the restoration of organized Shiite pilgrimages to the Sayyida Zaynab shrine near Damascus, following high-level talks on October 28. The prospect has raised hopes of reviving businesses that once depended on religious tourism, while reopening painful questions about the role of Iran-backed armed groups during Syria's civil war.The discussions took place during Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi's visit to Damascus, where he met Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa. The two leaders proposed establishing a committee to arrange visits and ensure pilgrims' safety, but no timetable or final agreement has been announced.For Ali al-Hassan, who has kept his shop opposite the shrine closed since the fall of Bashar al-Assad's government in December 2024, the possibility of renewed tourism offers hope of recovering his livelihood.“I used to sell perfumes and fabrics that pilgrims would take home as gifts for their families,” al-Hassan told The Media Line. “Visitors came from Iraq, Iran, Lebanon, and several other countries, and they were all Shiites.”The shrine, traditionally believed to contain the tomb of Zaynab, a granddaughter of the Prophet Muhammad, is among the most important pilgrimage destinations for Shiite Muslims. Before Assad's overthrow, thousands of visitors supported a local economy of hotels, restaurants, shops, and transportation services.Although small groups have continued visiting since the change of government, organized religious tourism has declined sharply, leaving many businesses closed and hotels largely empty.The prospect of renewed activity has also revived concerns among Syrians who remember the involvement of Iran-backed armed groups in the country's civil war.A diplomatic openingAl-Zaidi's October 28 trip was the first visit by an Iraqi prime minister since Assad's overthrow.During his stay, he visited the Sayyida Zaynab shrine and the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus, accompanied by Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani.The Iraqi prime minister's office announced that he had donated $10 million from his personal funds, allocating $5 million to each religious site.The gesture carried religious and diplomatic significance. The Sayyida Zaynab shrine is revered by Shiite Muslims, while the Umayyad Mosque is among the most important historic sites in Sunni Islamic tradition.Al-Sharaa had previously told Iraq's Dijlah television channel that Shiite religious sites remained accessible and that Syria was preparing to receive Iraqi delegations. He attributed delays to security problems following the former government's collapse.Protecting worshippers remains a concern. In January 2025, Syrian authorities announced that they had thwarted an Islamic State plot to bomb the Sayyida Zaynab shrine, arresting four suspects.Memories of war complicate the returnDuring Syria's civil war, Iran-backed Iraqi and Lebanese armed groups fought alongside Assad's forces, frequently invoking the defense of Shiite shrines to justify their intervention.Their activities extended beyond protecting religious sites to military campaigns against opposition-held areas. Forces supporting the former government have faced documented allegations of killings, displacement, sieges, and other abuses.In Idlib province, political activist Bilal al-Khalaf told The Media Line that Iraqi armed factions had contributed to civilian suffering and the destruction of residential neighborhoods.He argued that those responsible for wartime crimes should face investigation and prosecution, but ordinary Shiite worshippers should not be held accountable for the actions of armed groups.“Pilgrims should not be held responsible for the actions of armed groups, just as victims should not be asked to forget their memories or give up their right to justice,” he said.Religious rituals raise local concernsNot all concerns about the return of pilgrims are tied to the armed conflict.Nawfal al-Ahmad, who has lived in Sayyida Zaynab for 40 years, recalled how large religious processions previously blocked streets, disrupted traffic, and interfered with residents' daily activities.He was particularly troubled by public performances of tatbir, a mourning ritual practiced by some Shiite Muslims that involves striking the head with sharp instruments to draw blood.The practice commemorates the suffering associated with Imam Hussein ibn Ali, who was killed at the Battle of Karbala in 680. It remains controversial within Shiite Islam, and some prominent religious authorities oppose it because of the physical harm involved.“These practices were disturbing, and they disappeared after Assad's fall. But now, with delegations potentially being allowed to return, we hope they will perform their rituals in an orderly manner and without bloody scenes,” al-Ahmad told The Media Line.He stressed that he did not oppose pilgrimages themselves but wanted ceremonies conducted without disrupting neighborhood life.Objections have also emerged within Syrian religious circles.In a statement issued Friday following al-Zaidi's visit, the Forum of Levantine Preachers, known in Arabic as Multaqa Duat al-Sham, warned against allowing armed factions associated with abuses during the civil war to reestablish themselves under the cover of religious tourism.The forum called for preventing individuals implicated in violence or sectarian incitement from exploiting religious gatherings to regain influence. It also urged respect for religious sanctities and restrictions on rhetoric that could inflame sectarian hostility.Syrian official promises protection, oversightAhmad Anwar al-Alabi, who spoke as an official responsible for religious endowments at Syria's Ministry of Awqaf, said the government regarded access to religious shrines as a legitimate right protected by freedom of worship.He explained that authorities were considering organized groups and designated visiting periods, with security coordinated through the Interior Ministry and other relevant agencies.“The objective is not to impose restrictions on religious practices, but to ensure that visits take place in an organized manner that respects the sanctity of the site and Syrian laws,” al-Alabi told The Media Line.He rejected the possibility of religious gatherings being exploited for military or political purposes.“A visit to the Sayyida Zaynab shrine is purely religious. It is not an entry point for military activity, displays of armed force, or political mobilization,” he said.Al-Alabi said the arrangements should prohibit weapons, displays supporting armed organizations, and activities likely to inflame sectarian divisions.He also stressed that religious affiliation or nationality should not be grounds for suspicion. Responsibility for wartime crimes, he said, must be established individually through evidence and legal procedures.Economic recovery and regional relationsThe pilgrimage initiative forms part of broader efforts by Damascus and Baghdad to rebuild relations following Assad's overthrow.During al-Zaidi's visit, the governments also discussed trade, investment, border security, and rehabilitating the Kirkuk-Baniyas oil pipeline, which could give Iraq another route for exporting oil through Syria to the Mediterranean.Religious tourism could help revive the economy around Sayyida Zaynab, where hundreds of families have depended directly or indirectly on businesses serving pilgrims.But before larger groups return, the two governments must finalize arrangements that protect visitors and residents while addressing concerns that armed factions could exploit the reopening.Al-Hassan, meanwhile, is considering reopening the shop that supported him for more than two decades. For now, its doors remain closed.

title: Ukraine enacts law to resume direct Ukrnafta dividend payouts to Naftogaz
body:
Law No. 5020-IX "On the Valuation of Property," which, among other things, restores the procedure for direct payment of dividends by JSC Ukrnafta to its direct shareholder, NJSC Naftogaz Ukrainy, took effect on October 27, Oleksiy Movchan, deputy chairman of the Verkhovna Rada Committee on Economic Development, said.
"Several days ago, the provisions of Law No. 5020-IX took effect. The law incorporated my fundamental amendment restoring a fair, European-standard procedure for state-owned companies to pay dividends on a consolidated basis," he wrote on Facebook on Monday.
As the lawmaker recalled, in 2024 the Verkhovna Rada adopted a historic corporate governance reform through Law No. 3587-IX, establishing a key rule in line with OECD standards: subsidiaries pay dividends to their parent companies, and the parent company, after assessing the overall financial results of the entire group, distributes profits and transfers dividends to the state budget.
However, subsequent targeted amendments to the legislation created an exception: Ukrnafta was required to pay dividends directly to the state budget, bypassing its direct shareholder, Naftogaz of Ukraine. "In practice, this created the risk of funds being withdrawn twice and undermined the very philosophy of the group. When the parent company cannot see the actual consolidated flow of funds, it loses the ability to properly plan investments, manage risks and ensure the financial stability of the entire group," Movchan added.
"The amendment I introduced restores a single, transparent standard rule: Ukrnafta pays dividends to its shareholder, Naftogaz Ukrainy. Naftogaz consolidates the results of all its subsidiaries and pays the appropriate share to the state budget," he said.
The lawmaker added that the decision fully complies with OECD principles and restores predictability to relations between the state and state-owned companies.
"My position remains unwavering: the rule of consolidated financial management must be the same for all state-owned giants, without any legal conflicts or 'special' regimes," the lawmaker emphasized.
Under the dividend payment requirements approved by the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine for state-owned companies for 2025, Naftogaz Ukrainy was required to transfer 30% of its net profit, or UAH 970 million, to the state budget.

title: Bichi assures APC of Tinubu, Yusuf’s victory in 2027
body: By Hadiza Yusuf The Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Appropriations, Abubakar Kabir Bichi, has expressed confidence that the All Progressives Congress (APC) will secure victory for President Bola Tinubu and Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf in the 2027 general elections. Bichi made the declaration on Sunday during a strategic meeting with APC members of the Kano State House of Assembly and 40 party candidates at his office in Bichi Local Government Area of the state. The lawmaker, who represents Bichi Federal Constituency, said the meeting was convened to strengthen cooperation among party members and develop strategies for the forthcoming elections. “I brought together APC members of the State House of Assembly and 40 candidates to discuss campaign strategies and coordinate our efforts towards securing victory for President Tinubu, Governor Yusuf and the party in the 2027 general elections,” he said. Bichi thanked the Speaker of the Kano State House of Assembly, Jibril Ismail Falgore, and other participants for attending the meeting. “I appreciate the Speaker and all members for honouring the invitation. Unity is our strength, and together we will deliver victory, Insha Allah,” he said. The post Bichi assures APC of Tinubu, Yusuf’s victory in 2027 appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Google Pay Uzbekistan Launch Enabled by Data Reforms, Executive Says
body: Google Pay’s launch in Uzbekistan follows changes to the country’s personal data protection rules, which have made it easier for international technology companies to enter the market, according to a senior Google executive. Doron Avni, Google’s vice president for government affairs and public policy for emerging markets, said in a LinkedIn post that replacing strict rules on storing data locally with a more flexible approach had enabled the launch. Under legislation signed on March 26 , most categories of personal data can now be stored and processed abroad under certain conditions. However, biometric and genetic data, as well as data belonging to customers of telecommunications operators in Uzbekistan, must still be stored in the country. “Modern policy isn’t just written on paper – it’s felt directly in people’s pockets,” Avni wrote. Google Pay was announced in Uzbekistan on October 19, with support for cards issued by participating Uzbek banks becoming available on October 27, alongside Apple Pay. The introduction of both platforms allows users to make contactless payments through compatible smartphones and other devices. Initially, both services support eligible Visa and Mastercard cards, while integration with Uzbekistan’s domestic UZCARD and HUMO payment systems remains under development. Avni linked the launch to technology cooperation between Uzbekistan and the United States. It was announced during U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visit to Samarkand for the C5+1 ministerial meeting with his counterparts from the five Central Asian countries. He said the visit reflected a shared interest in advancing digital modernization in Central Asia, including cybersecurity, cloud technology, and digital education. “My sincere gratitude to the Government of Uzbekistan and the U.S. Ambassador Jonathan Henick for their exceptional vision and partnership,” Avni wrote.

title: Ghana Publishing Company invests €1.5m in security printing equipment to expand operations
body: The Ghana Publishing Company Limited (GPCL) has committed approximately €1.5 million towards acquiring specialised security printing machines and other production equipment as part of efforts to expand its operational capacity and diversify revenue. Managing Director Nana Kwasi Boatey said the investment forms part of a broader retooling strategy aimed at positioning the state-owned printing company to undertake high-value security printing assignments and compete more effectively in the local and international markets. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at Jubilee House on Monday, November 2, he disclosed that management was also converting an existing warehouse into a dedicated security printing section to accommodate the newly acquired machinery and provide an appropriate production environment. According to him, the investment is expected to improve productivity, strengthen operational efficiency and create opportunities for new business. “This investment is aimed at strengthening the company’s capacity to undertake high-value security printing assignments, diversify its revenue streams, improve operational efficiency, and position GPCL to compete more effectively in the printing industry,” he said. He added that the initiative would enhance the company’s ability to meet changing market demands and improve its long-term profitability.

title: Derik Cultural Festival to promote peace through culture
body: The Derik Cultural Festival is set to return for its sixth edition in Juba next week, starting from 7 th November to 14 th November 2026, with organizers calling for greater recognition of culture as a tool for peacebuilding and reconciliation in South Sudan. Speaking at a press conference in Juba on Monday, Mathiang Cirilo, chairperson of the organizing committee, announced that this year’s festival will be held under the theme “Advancing Peace Through Culture.” “As one of our nation’s most prominent figures, he left behind a celebrated legacy that continues to inspire,” Cirilo said. According to the organizing chairperson, the annual event honors the memory of the late Derik Uya Alfred, who dedicated his life to cultural development across Sudan and South Sudan. “In keeping with this tradition, the festival’s sixth edition is themed “Advancing peace through culture.” This theme reaffirms our commitment to the vision of our mentor, Derik Alfred, who steadfastly viewed cultural engagement as a bridge to peace,” he said. The committee said Alfred left behind a legacy of cultural preservation and nation-building, with culture serving as an important instrument for fostering unity and reconciliation. The sixth edition will also honor Professor Peter Adwok Nyaba for his intellectual contributions, particularly in promoting dialogue on governance and national affairs. The organizing committee described Nyaba’s concept of a “House of Nationalities” as an important framework for building a peaceful society through continuous dialogue. “His intellectual contributions, marked by analytical rigor and clarity, have been vital in driving continuous dialogue on governance and reforms,” he stressed. The festival is expected to feature various cultural events and activities at the University of Juba’s Main Campus in Atlabara. In addition, Cirilo acknowledged the support of its partners, including the University of Juba’s School of Arts, Music and Drama, Al Markaz Al-Salam and Norwegian People’s Aid for their support towards the event. Other sponsors include Digital Telecommunications, the Center for Strategic and Policy Studies, Zack for Print and Design, the South Sudan Broadcasting Corporation (SSBC), Black Lion Medical Center, Fair Pharma and Million Items. As the committee invited members of the public to participate in the week-long festival, registration for any cultural group, drama clubs, and individuals who wish to participate is free, and activities will be broadcast and updated live across the group’s official social media platforms. The post Derik Cultural Festival to promote peace through culture appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Otti explains Abia’s preference for electric buses over CNG
body:
Governor Alex Otti of Abia State says his administration chose Electric Vehicles (EVs) over Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) powered buses because EVs represent an upgrade in transportation technology.
Mr Otti explained that the government opted for electric buses for its public transportation system for this reason.
He spoke at the October edition of his monthly media briefing, held at the Michael Okpara Auditorium in Umuahia on Friday night.
He said that despite the preference for EVs, the Abia State Government still encouraged establishing additional CNG stations in the state.
“We are not opposed to CNG, but we chose electric vehicles for our public transportation system,” the governor said.
He said both petrol and CNG vehicles operate on internal combustion engines, while EVs require a different propulsion system.
He added that some companies had expressed interest in establishing additional CNG stations in the state, and that agreements had been reached with them.
He explained that the proposed stations would cater for privately owned vehicles and other consumers, rather than the state’s public transportation system.
Mr Otti said that CNG is cheaper to use than petrol and expressed optimism that converting petrol and diesel vehicles to CNG would gain more traction in the country.
He also said that Nigerian companies specialise in converting internal combustion engine vehicles to CNG.
Mr Otti also responded to purported complaints about the continued street trading at Umuahia city centre, popularly called Isi-Gate.
According to him, street trading cannot be eliminated; it still operates in other developed parts of the world, including London.
He promised compensation to traders who might be displaced by the state’s urban renewal efforts.
Mr Otti said the Abia State Government was working to restore order in the capital city, particularly by tackling challenges associated with street trading.
He said the relocation of traders from Isi-Gate would be gradual, considering that many petty traders on the street depend on that income for their livelihoods.
He said the government was still exploring alternative locations for affected traders to avoid pushing them into activities that could further undermine public order.
“We are a compassionate government. So, if we move you out of your shop, we will pay you compensation. We will ensure that,” he said.
Mr Otti argued that displacing traders without considering their economic circumstances would defeat the purpose of the government’s urban renewal programme.
“It doesn’t make sense to drive everybody away. Who are you even sanitising the place for?
“So, it is a balancing act. We are handling it step by step,” he said.

title: Jake Paul to fight Cedric Doumbe in Dubai on Christmas Eve
body: Jake Paul will fight French mixed martial artist Cedric Doumbe in Dubai on Christmas Eve as the American makes his comeback after a year out. Paul, 29, will be favoured to make a successful return to the ring when he faces Doumbe, a decorated kickboxer, in an eight-round cruiserweight boxing contest at Coca-Cola Arena on December 24. Paul (12-2, 7 KOs) has not fought since suffering a double jaw fracture in a knockout defeat to former heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua in December 2025. However, he revealed last Thursday that he was heading to the UAE to resume his career, following a co-operation agreement between his company, Most Valuable Promotions (MVP), the Dubai Sports Council and Dubai's Department of Economy and Tourism (DET). Paul said: “Cedric Douchebag was calling me out two years ago after knocking some dude out in nine seconds. Well, Douchebag, now you get your chance. I’m rusty, my jaw is janky and I don’t have kickboxing world titles like you do. But guess what, this isn’t kickboxing, mon ami . This is boxing.” MVP was founded in 2021 and has grown into a major player in combat sports, largely on the back of Paul's own in-ring exploits. He has faced a variety of opponents during a short and colourful career, including boxers, UFC and NBA athletes, as well as former heavyweight champion Mike Tyson in a record-breaking 2024 bout streamed on Netflix. Khalfan Belhoul, vice chairman of the Dubai Sports Council, said: “Our growing calendar of major international events reflects both the city’s rising stature and thirst for global sport and the confidence organisers place in our ability to deliver outstanding experiences. Welcoming Jake Paul’s return to the ring adds another compelling occasion to that calendar.” View this post on Instagram Doumbe, 34, is a former two-time Glory kickboxing world champion who boasts a 6-1 record in MMA, including a stint with the PFL. He has boxed professionally once before, picking up a solitary victory back in 2015. “Jake Paul calls himself the 'Problem Child', but he's never faced a problem like me – he has no idea what a Frenchman is capable of,” said Doumbe. “Jake loves to talk, and so do I, but after what Joshua did to his jaw, I'm not sure how much talking he has left. I'm going to finish the job Joshua started.” Tickets for Paul versus Doumbe will be available through the Coca-Cola Arena's official website from midday on November 15. Fans can also register for presale access.

title: Russia officially withdraws from European Anti-Torture Convention
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Council of Europe announced this on its website .
"The withdrawal of the Russian Federation marks the end of the CPT's monitoring mandate in the country. It also marks the end of any independent monitoring of places of deprivation of liberty inside the Russian Federation. Nevertheless, the Convention's preventive approach remains as important as ever: independent monitoring of places of detention is a fundamental safeguard against torture and ill-treatment," said Alan Mitchell, President of the Committee.
He also stressed that the preventive approach of the Convention remains critically important and that independent monitoring of places of detention is a fundamental safeguard against torture and ill-treatment.
The CPT recalled that since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, it has received numerous reports of alleged torture and ill-treatment by Russian officials in places of detention, both in occupied Ukrainian territories and within Russia itself.
"Due to the non-cooperation of the Russian authorities, the CPT has been unable to conduct a visit to the Russian Federation to examine the situation for itself," the statement said.
The Committee contrasted this with its cooperation with Ukraine, which continues to allow CPT visits to any place of detention on its territory at times determined by the Committee. Ukraine also ensures the automatic publication of the Committee's reports.
The Russian authorities notified the Council of Europe of their decision to denounce the Convention on October 30, 2025. Russia had been a party to the Convention since 1998.
According to the report, between 1998 and 2021, the CPT conducted 30 visits to Russia, inspecting more than 450 places of detention.
At the same time, Russia was the only member state with a declared policy of withholding consent to the publication of the Committee's reports and the authorities' responses to them. As a result, Russia allowed only four reports to be published.
Among the documents that remain unpublished are reports on ten visits to Chechnya and the North Caucasus between 2000 and 2017.
As Ukrinform previously reported, Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a law denouncing the European Convention for the Prevention of Torture.

title: NYPD seeks info as jogger stabbed in Brooklyn remains in critical condition
body:
The NYPD said the woman had "sustained multiple stab wounds to the neck."
The New York City Police Department said it was seeking additional information on the alleged stabbing in Brooklyn of a 28-year-old jogger, who remains in critical condition.
Katie Suarez was hospitalized and on life support at NYU Langone Hospital-Brooklyn, ABC News' New York station WABC reported, citing police and information released by investigators.
She was alleged to have been attacked on Friday while she jogged along the Shore Parkway near the city's Bath Beach and Bensonhurst neighborhoods, according to police.
The NYPD said in a statement posted on social media that Suarez "sustained multiple stab wounds to the neck" when she was attacked at about 8 p.m.

title: Russia exploits ceasefire to mask military movements, General Staff says
body:
Russia used the humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky to rotate soldiers, improve fighting positions, expand anti-drone netting on key logistics routes, and resupply soldiers with ammunition, Ukraine's General Staff said on Nov. 2.
The statement came after a temporary ceasefire in Kherson Oblast , agreed between Russia and Ukraine to allow for the evacuation of residents from Russian-occupied Oleshky .
"During the regime of silence, the rotation of Russian units, strengthening of positions, expansion of anti-drone means on the roads and the increase in logistics, in particular the delivery of ammunition, were recorded," the General Staff said in a statement .
British outlet Sky News also reported Russian soldiers using the ceasefire as cover for military operations, broadcasting Ukrainian drone footage showing Russian forces using heavy armored and logistics vehicles to reinforce positions and reposition soldiers.
None of this was related to the humanitarian mission , Ukrainian soldiers of the 34th Separate Marine Brigade, interviewed by Sky News, claimed.
Russia has a history of using humanitarian ceasefires as cover for a renewed increase in offensive operations, one Ukrainian military source told the Kyiv Independent.
"As part of the ceasefire introduced for the humanitarian operation in Oleshky, units of the Ukrainian Defense Forces ensured compliance with the regime of silence and acted exclusively within the framework of the agreements reached," the General Staff claimed.
The ceasefire, brokered with the help of U.S. first lady Melania Trump to facilitate the evacuation of civilians, lasted from 3 a.m. on Oct. 27 until 11 p.m. on Nov. 1. Neither Ukraine nor Russia reported any violations of the ceasefire during that period.
Ukraine's Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said 25 buses with a total capacity of 750 passengers had been prepared for the evacuation. Melania Trump said on Nov. 2 that nearly 800 people were evacuated during the humanitarian operation.
Residents were given the option of choosing whether to evacuate to Ukraine or Russia, but the exact number of people who left for each country remains unclear.
According to Lubinets , he and Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova are exploring ways to continue similar humanitarian efforts.
Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since the early days of Russia's full-scale invasion. Located across the Dnipro River from Kherson , the city has been effectively blockaded by Russian forces, which have prevented humanitarian aid from reaching residents.

title: GES warns staff found guilty of sexual harassment face dismissal
body: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has reiterated its commitment to dealing firmly with sexual harassment in schools, warning that any staff member found culpable faces dismissal. Deputy Director-General in charge of Quality and Access at the GES, Dr Issahaque Munwaru, said a substantiated case of sexual harassment would be sufficient grounds for terminating the employment of the staff member involved. He made the remarks during an interview on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Monday, November 2, while providing an update on investigations into allegations of sexual misconduct at Obuasi Senior High and Technical School. According to him, a committee established by the GES had visited the school to investigate the allegations and was expected to engage the relevant parties before submitting its findings. Dr Munwaru said the investigative process must give everyone involved a fair hearing before conclusions are reached. He explained that the GES operates a four-tier disciplinary structure, with decisions at each level subject to review by the next higher authority. “The four levels of disciplinary structures are subject to review of the next higher level,” he said. He added that the committee was expected to speak to those who had made the allegations, examine available video evidence and ensure that all parties were heard. However, Dr Munwaru stressed that the Service’s position on sexual harassment was unequivocal. “One on sexual harassment is equal to dismissal,” he stated, emphasising that a finding of sexual harassment could attract dismissal regardless of whether the accused person subsequently apologised. He said the GES headquarters took allegations of sexual misconduct seriously and would review the committee’s recommendations before deciding on the appropriate action. “If there is need for us to even review the stance of the school committee, we will do that,” he added. Dr Munwaru did not provide a definite timeline for the committee to conclude its work, explaining that he needed to establish whether the investigators required additional time. The allegations at Obuasi Senior High and Technical School have raised concerns about student safeguarding and the responsibility of education authorities to protect learners from sexual abuse and misconduct. The GES has assured the public that it will consider the committee’s recommendations and take the necessary disciplinary action in line with its procedures. Watch the full documentary below.

title: Two Oyo commissioner, special adviser resign from Makinde’s government
body:
Two senior officials in the Oyo State Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning have resigned their appointments, in the latest departures from Governor Seyi Makinde’s administration.
The officials are Ayobami Ojo, the Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning, and Simeon Oyeleke, the ministry’s Special Adviser on Budget and Economic Planning.
In separate letters dated November 2, and addressed to Mr Makinde, both officials said their resignations would take effect immediately, while thanking the governor for the opportunity to serve but did not give specific reasons for their decisions.
In his letter, Mr Ojo referred to his appointment letter dated 22 June 2026 and formally announced his resignation as commissioner.
“With reference to your letter dated 22nd June, 2026 (SP.S.662/2/VOL.IV/192), I respectfully write to formally resign my appointment as Honourable Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning, with effect from today, 2nd November, 2026,” he wrote.
He described his time in government as an honour and said he appreciated the opportunity to serve the state.
Mr Oyeleke also tendered his resignation with effect from 2 November.
In his letter, he thanked Mr Makinde for the confidence reposed in him and the opportunity to contribute to the administration’s policies and development programmes.
He also expressed appreciation for the governor’s leadership, support and encouragement during his time in office.
“I remain grateful for the opportunity to have been part of this administration and to have contributed to its laudable achievements. I also remain committed to the peace, progress and development of Oyo State,” he wrote.
The latest resignations come amid a series of exits of political appointees and other officials from the Makinde administration in recent months.
PREMIUM TIMES reported on 12 October that Segun Ogunwuyi resigned as the governor’s chief of staff, a position he had held since July 2021. His resignation took immediate effect, although he did not state a reason for his departure.
A few hours after Mr Ogunwuyi departure, Mr Makinde appointed Bashorun Akinwole, popularly known as Wolekanle, as his replacement.
On the same day, Tara Adefope, the Director-General of the Oyo State Due Process Office, also resigned from her position, while in late October, Kabiru Salami, the governor’s Executive Assistant on Security Coordination, also tendered his resignation .
Other officials who have left the administration include Funmi Arulogun, a Senior Special Assistant on Diaspora Matters, who resigned in August, citing personal and political considerations.
Babatunde Oduyoye, a member of the Oyo State Advisory Council, also stepped down from in July, while Fatai Owoseni, a former Commissioner of Police who served as the governor’s Special Adviser on Security resigned in May.
The latest departures come as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections, with Mr Makinde running as the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM).

title: VP Shettima Arrives In Calabar For APC Campaign Rally
body: Vice President Kashim Shettima has arrived in Calabar in Cross River State to lead the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally. Vice President Shettima’s aircraft touched down at about 12:10 in the afternoon at the Margaret Ekpo International Airport, Calabar, where he was received by Governor Bassey Otu, alongside officials of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, with hundreds of party faithful, supporters, and key political stakeholders from across Cross River State and the South-South region on the ground. ​Adding vibrant colour to the arrival, local Calabar cultural troupes were on ground performing traditional dances and drumming routines, highlighting the rich cultural heritage of the ancient city. ​Following brief airport formalities and interactions with party leadership, the Vice President’s convoy has proceeded to the Calabar Stadium, venue of the APC campaign rally, where a massive crowd of party loyalists has gathered.
