title: Tajik Prisoners in Russia Say They Face Pressure to Fight in Ukraine
body: Tajik citizens imprisoned in the Russian city of Volgograd say they are being put under pressure to sign military contracts and fight in Ukraine, allegations which the Russian prison authorities have rejected. The prisoners are asking Tajikistan to facilitate their transfer home. Two inmates contacted Radio Ozodi , the Tajik service of Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty , on October 29. They said about 150 prisoners from Central Asia were facing pressure, including approximately 60 Tajik citizens. The outlet said it knew the men’s identities but had withheld them for their safety. The men said that despite difficulties, they had obtained a mobile phone, contacted Tajikistan’s embassy in Moscow, and hoped to complete their prison sentences in Tajikistan rather than face military service. “We want to go home. We are ready to serve our sentences there,” one prisoner said, even offering to work without pay on Tajikistan’s Rogun hydropower project if that would secure his return. “Here they are taking us to our deaths,” he added. The inmates said Central Asian prisoners were being held in blocks with particularly harsh conditions. They described facilities used for inmates considered dangerous and claimed many convictions were based on false accusations. More seriously, the men alleged that over 100 Central Asian inmates had left one Volgograd prison for the Ukraine war during the previous year. They said about 40 were Tajik citizens and claimed none of those sent had survived. There is no independent confirmation of those figures, the alleged deaths or the circumstances in which the men entered military service. The original report did not identify the prison by name. On October 31, the Federal Penitentiary Service’s Volgograd regional directorate issued a denial , stating that claims Tajik inmates were being pressured to sign military contracts “do not correspond to reality.” The outlet said its calls to Tajikistan’s embassy on October 30 went unanswered. Earlier Warnings from Volgograd The latest allegations follow an earlier warning from the same Russian city. In April 2025 , relatives said eight Tajik prisoners had been taken from Correctional Colony No. 26, apparently for deployment to Ukraine. Another inmate at that facility described attempts to secure military contracts. “First they try to persuade us, then they start threatening us,” he said. He alleged that prisoners who refused were put in punishment cells and denied calls or visits. Russia has recruited prisoners for its war since the invasion began in February 2022. The Wagner private military group initially conducted much of that recruitment before the Defense Ministry took a larger role. Changes to Russian legislation in 2023 and 2024 expanded opportunities for convicted people and criminal defendants to sign military contracts to gain relief from criminal prosecution or punishment under specified circumstances. An August 2026 UK government assessment summarized reports of coercion in Russian detention facilities, including beatings and threats. A Request to Serve Sentences at Home The prisoners are not asking for their convictions to be overturned, but to serve out the remainder of their terms in Tajikistan, beyond the reach of the alleged recruitment campaign. There is a precedent for such discussions between Moscow and Dushanbe. In April, Russian human rights commissioner Tatyana Moskalkova said President Emomali Rahmon had responded positively to a proposal involving approximately 200 Tajik women serving sentences in Russia. Moskalkova had previously acknowledged that requests from Central Asian families often became bogged down in paperwork. She cited differences between domestic laws and international agreements, as well as lengthy processing times. On October 20, Ukraine’s state-run I Want to Live project said it had identified 20,437 citizens from five Central Asian states who had signed contracts with Russia since 2022. Its total included 5,308 citizens of Tajikistan. Russian military bloggers have estimated that soldiers survive an average of just 20–35 minutes after entering frontline combat in Ukraine. Historian Peter Frankopan cited the figure in Foreign Policy in June. The same accounts put the period between arrival at training grounds and death at ten days to three weeks. In July, CIA Director John Ratcliffe said U.S. intelligence was consistent with reports that newly deployed Russian soldiers survived just 20–30 minutes on the battlefield. He attributed the heavy losses partly to Ukrainian drone warfare, Defense News reported . A 2024 investigation by BBC News Russia examined the cases of 1,040 prisoners killed in Ukraine whose recruitment and death dates could be established. Among those recruited by Russia’s Defense Ministry, half died within eight weeks of signing their contracts. The comparable period for Wagner recruits was three months. The BBC stressed that these figures did not establish the overall survival rate of prisoners sent to war. In February, Tajikistan’s prosecutor general , Habibullo Vohidzoda, said the country’s laws prohibit unauthorized participation in foreign conflicts. He distinguished citizens who also hold Russian passports, saying they must meet their obligations under Russian law. The Tajik authorities acknowledged that they had not prosecuted anyone for involvement in the Ukraine war.

title: Former military barracks in London transformed into luxury residences with eye on security
body: For the best part of two centuries, the well-heeled and genteel north London suburb of St John’s Wood echoed to the sound of soldiers on horseback. Established as barracks in 1812, the area served as home to the Royal Horse Artillery and later The King’s Troop, welcoming visits from King George VI and Queen Elizabeth II. The King’s Troop conducted its final ceremonial parade down St John’s Wood High Street in 2012 before relocating to Woolwich. Now, instead of hooves and parade calls, it’s the cries of cranes and construction workers emanating from the 2.2-hectare site as 120 luxury residences are developed. The National was given a tour of the site, including the first show apartment, priced at £14.895 million, the shell of a penthouse and its original riding school that has been renovated and will make up a sports hall and leisure amenities. The first homes have been launched to market, with the first occupants due to arrive in 2028. St John’s Wood Square was conceived by Ananda Krishnan, the Malaysian-born entrepreneur and philanthropist behind the Petronas Towers and the Kuala Lumpur City Centre (KLCC) development, and he acquired the site in 2012. He died in 2024, with the project now being spearheaded by executive chairman, Sir George Iacobescu, and chief executive Gareth Stow, who worked closely with Mr Krishnan for many years. The team commissioned a YouGov survey of 758 “motivated buyers” from the UAE and Saudi Arabia with an active interest in purchasing UK property to discover the core drivers behind Gulf buyers' choices of luxury property in the UK. In a nod to the development's military past, they found security was the most important overall property feature for 33 per cent of respondents. About 29 per cent selected safety as a leading factor when choosing a specific neighbourhood. Security services ranked as the most appealing amenity by a wide margin, at 56 per cent. The survey also found strong buying intent for London, with 63 per cent actively looking to purchase a property in the city in the next 12 months. They also considered lifestyle, privacy and connectivity important, with 21 per cent identifying quick access to central London, Mayfair, the West End, and key business districts as a critical consideration. Wellness, dining, and sporting amenities emerged as lifestyle priorities. Tom Mann, sales, leasing and marketing director at St John's Wood Square, said security is the “cornerstone of what makes a home” and should be “effective, but unobtrusive”. Security personnel roam the site, backed up by more than 400 cameras fitted with AI technology designed for behavioural recognition to alert the team of anything out of place. Access control means only residents and key personnel have access tofloors, whilst the circa 185-kg front doors give a physical sense of security. “We have an airlock approach for access to the car park, where two sets of gates will only allow entry once the other is closed, and the same goes for residential entrances to the apartment buildings,” Mr Mann said. “From the 24-hour security team to the Category 3 wired alarms in every home, we have planned both the operational and physical security to be incredibly thorough and integral to the estate." The research findings “reinforce what we see in the priorities of international buyers”, he said. “When choosing a home in London, security, privacy and peace of mind are fundamental.” The development covers apartments, penthouses and townhouses starting at £35.5 million and averaging 3,260 square feet. Amenities include a wellness centre, 20-metre swimming pool, spa, sports grounds, private dining room, cinema, games room, business suite and children’s play area. The development has been launched with a three-bedroom show apartment by British designer Portia Fox, who has an established portfolio in the Middle East, particularly in Dubai, spanning high-end private residences and branded developments. Her projects include AVA at Palm Jumeirah and Regent Residences in Business Bay.

title: Feature: From a kiosk to big dreams: John Kennedy’s story of resilience to success
body: With little capital but a determination to succeed, a young South Sudanese trader turned a small quantity of cooking oil and beans into the beginning of a business journey. Today, he is encouraging other young people to create jobs rather than wait for employment. Before John Kennedy Clement had a business center bearing his name, before customers began recognizing his shop, and before he started dreaming of a music production studio and a bookshop, his business was little more than a modest table under a tree. There was no sophisticated shop, no elaborate business plan, and no guarantee that customers would come. There was cooking oil, a small quantity of beans, and a young man determined to make something of himself. For Clement, the journey began in 2014, while he was still a secondary school student. Today, he runs John K. Business Center in Ikotos Town in Eastern Equatoria State, where he sells essential household goods and hopes to expand into new services. His story is not simply about selling products; it is about recognizing an opportunity, starting with what is available, surviving difficult economic conditions, and refusing to allow limited resources to determine his future. “I decided to start operating the business,” Clement recalls, explaining how a vision that his classmates had noticed in him gradually became a reality. Even while studying, he says, his classmates recognized his ability to manage his belongings and handle money. Their observations helped him begin to see entrepreneurship as something he could pursue. While studying during the day, Clement was invited by his brother, Tom Lususa, to look after a hotel at night while the latter travelled to Kenya. The arrangement allowed him to continue his education while taking responsibility for the hotel after dark. Yet, in the quiet hours of the night, his thoughts were turning towards something of his own. He wanted to start a business, but he had little capital. Clement says he prayed to God for an opportunity and began thinking about placing a few items outside the hotel to start selling. The following morning, a telephone call from his brother in Dubai brought unexpected encouragement. His brother offered to send him some money. Clement was excited. He had not spoken with his brother for quite some time, and the offer opened a door he had been hoping to find. Rather than spend all the money on himself, he decided to put part of it towards his business ambitions. He also had a small quantity of beans that relatives had sent from his village. Instead of consuming them, he saw another possibility: they could become part of his starting stock. He combined the money with the beans and sent them to Torit, where he obtained 20 liters of cooking oil. That was the beginning. He placed the goods under a tree and started selling, measuring out the beans and oil for customers. For Clement, the significance of that first stock was not how much he possessed. It was that he had finally begun. He says he has learned that closing the shop out of discouragement only makes the situation harder. “When you close, that means there will be no money coming in,” he says. His response to difficult circumstances is straightforward: keep the business operating, even when the available stock is limited, and continue working towards something better. He acknowledges that the economic situation can be discouraging. Yet he believes that remaining active creates the possibility of recovery and progress. “Even if I have little,” he says, recalling the advice that helped him persevere, “you go up, continue, continue, continue.” For Clement, persistence is not merely a personal virtue. It is part of his responsibility to the customers and community that depend on his services. Inside John K. Business Center, the products are chosen with the everyday needs of customers in mind. Asked what he would keep if every item in the shop disappeared except one, Clement chooses cooking oil. His reasoning is practical. Cooking oil, he explains, is an important household commodity used in daily life. He says he also welcomes customers who have very little money to spend. If someone arrives with only a small amount, he may recommend buying a sweet, one of the cheapest items available. Clement promotes his business through Facebook, WhatsApp and word of mouth. He says its location opposite County Freedom Square also helps customers find it. He plans to install a signpost to make the business easier to identify. He says he encourages customers and other young people to study how businesses operate, so that they too can become sellers rather than remaining only consumers. He believes that people should share knowledge and encourage others to pursue their own ideas. “We are not selfish,” he says, explaining that he wants customers to learn from what he is doing and develop businesses according to their own visions. His message is particularly directed at young people who may believe that the only route to success is securing employment with the government or a non-governmental organization. Clement does not dismiss the importance of education or employment. Instead, he argues that education can also provide the knowledge needed to create a business and provide opportunities for others. He says he has pursued business administration training through the Whittaker Peace and Development Initiative (WPDI) in Ikotos and expresses gratitude to a mentor he identified as Dudu Judith for helping guide his development. For him, the lesson is that practical experience should be strengthened by knowledge. “Because when you do the business without knowledge you will not prosper,” he says. His advice reflects a wider challenge facing young South Sudanese: how to turn education, skills and limited financial resources into sustainable livelihoods in a country where opportunities can be difficult to find. Clement believes young people should learn to identify local needs, develop useful services and begin with the resources available to them. He also encourages those who earn small amounts of money to consider their future responsibilities before spending everything they receive. Rather than immediately using their income for entertainment or other personal expenses, he urges young people to identify priorities, save where possible, and invest in activities that may support them and their families in the future. He wants them to understand that starting small is not something to be ashamed of. Although John K. Business Center began with cooking oil and beans, Clement says he does not want it to remain limited to selling household goods. His ambitions include establishing a music production studio and a bookshop within the next five years. He says he has also established another structure intended to accommodate a computer center, which he hopes to transfer there as the business develops. These plans remain ambitions rather than completed achievements, but they reveal the direction in which he wants to take his enterprise. For Clement, expansion means exploring different services instead of depending entirely on one product or source of income. The idea is to build a business that can serve different needs while creating opportunities for further growth. He also hopes that some of the services he develops in town could eventually reach people in villages, where access to business and other services may be more limited. He says he has completed his studies and is also pursuing further education through distance learning. Yet he has chosen to continue building his business rather than treating formal employment as the only measure of success. He believes creativity and innovation can help young people build independent livelihoods and employ others. He also warns against allowing access to political office or a government appointment to become the sole foundation of a person’s future. In his view, people need skills and alternative livelihoods that enable them to continue contributing to society when circumstances change. He argues that when individuals depend entirely on a particular position, losing it can leave them without a clear direction. For him, developing businesses and creating employment opportunities are among the ways people can build more secure futures. The challenges confronting the country cannot be solved by small businesses alone. But Clement believes that a culture of creativity, investment, and self-reliance can help communities build livelihoods and reduce dependence on a limited number of employment opportunities. The post Feature: From a kiosk to big dreams: John Kennedy’s story of resilience to success appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: New Belfast fabrication hall to support shipbuilding for decades
body:
New fabrication hall opens today at Navantia UK’s Harland & Wolff site in Belfast, the centrepiece of a £157 million investment programme across their four UK shipyards.
The hall will support construction of three new Fleet Solid Support ships for the Royal Fleet Auxiliary, and 900 skilled jobs and apprenticeships in Belfast.
Follows record-breaking defence investment in Northern Ireland’s industry, which rose by 63% in real terms in 2025/26 to £464 million.
Belfast welders, fabricators, and crane operators are set to benefit from a record-breaking year of defence investment in Northern Ireland, as Navantia UK opened the new Resurgent Hall at the iconic Harland & Wolff site in Belfast today.
The opening marks a major milestone in the construction of three new support ships for the Royal Fleet Auxiliary (RFA), cementing Belfast’s role at the heart of the UK’s shipbuilding renewal.
During the site opening today, the Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard officially opened the fabrication hall, the new centrepiece of Navantia UK’s £157 million investment programme across its four UK shipyards. Around £100 million is being invested in Belfast alone.
Supporting over 900 skilled jobs and apprenticeships, the newly extended hall adds 5,000 square metres of fabrication space, fitted with new cranes, robotic plasma-cutting technology and a new mechanised panel line. Navantia UK’s Harland and Wolff site will now be able to deliver the Fleet Solid Support (FSS) programme.
Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard MP said:
Few sights in the UK are more evocative of our industrial heritage than the Samson and Goliath cranes, and it’s fitting that this new hall sits on the shoulders of these iconic giants.
Belfast continues with its proud shipbuilding history by building the modern shipbuilding capability the country needs today, with this new fabrication hall at the heart of it.
Navantia’s £157 million investment across its UK yards shows what sustained investment in shipbuilding delivers: good jobs, growing skills, and the support ships our Navy needs.
Minister for Northern Ireland Sarah Owen said:
Standing in Navantia’s state-of-the-art fabrication hall is a great reminder of the scale of UK Government defence investment in Northern Ireland, with £460 million spent here by the Ministry of Defence in the last year - equivalent to £240 per person.
This impressive facility is a key milestone in the UK Government’s Fleet Solid Support (FSS) programme, which has invested around £100 million in Belfast alone.
Navantia is building on Belfast’s historic shipbuilding legacy while supporting hundreds of skilled jobs and apprenticeships, ensuring that it remains at the heart of the UK’s defence industry while boosting economic growth.
Alongside investment in the new hall, Navantia UK is refurbishing Samson & Goliath – the two yellow cranes that dominate the skyline of Belfast’s docks – rounding off a programme of modernisation that will expand the yard’s capacity and increase its capability to deliver complex builds.
Navantia UK is prime contractor for the FSS programme and is leading on fabrication and final assembly of the three FSS ships, RFA Resurgent, Reliant and Resourceful, backed by £1.6 billion of Ministry of Defence (MOD) funding. The ships will replenish Royal Navy task groups at sea, directly linking today’s investment in Belfast to the operational capability of the fleet. Work is progressing on schedule and within budget, with all three ships due to enter service in the early 2030s.
Since completing its acquisition of Harland & Wolff, Appledore, Methil and Arnish sites in January 2025, Navantia has grown into one of the UK’s leading shipbuilding employers, now supporting more than 1,300 jobs and over 340 apprentices across Northern Ireland, England and Scotland, and has committed to creating 750 apprenticeships by 2030.
Navantia UK CEO, Donato Martinez, said:
Shipbuilding is returning to Belfast. We are turning Harland & Wolff into one of the most advanced shipyards in Europe. Our new fabrication hall will be equipped to build state-of-the-art ships to serve and defend the UK for generations to come.
We’ve named it Resurgent for a reason. Jobs, investment and activity are resurgent in shipbuilding. Belfast is at heart of that revival, and the fleet solid support programme is the first of many projects we aim to deliver here for the Ministry of Defence.
The opening comes as recent figures show MOD investment in Northern Ireland’s defence sector rose by 63% in real terms in 2025/26, to £464 million, the highest level since records began. That investment, equivalent to £240 for every person living in Northern Ireland, is helping give people in Northern Ireland breathing room day-to-day, while fuelling the growth and reindustrialisation of communities across the country.
Keith Bethell, NAD Group Maritime Director, said:
The opening of the Resurgent Fabrication Hall is a clear sign that growth in UK shipbuilding is happening right now, in Belfast. This investment is renewing our industrial capability, creating skilled jobs and apprenticeships, and strengthening the supply chains that underpin our national resilience. It gives us the modern capability we need to deliver the Fleet Solid Support ships for the Royal Fleet Auxiliary and lays the foundations for Belfast to compete for future UK naval and maritime programmes.
UK naval shipbuilding is backed by the Defence Investment Plan, which commits £298 billion of UK defence investment over the next four years.

title: Millions of Nigerian workers face growing social security risks, NSITF warns
body: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund, NSITF, has raised the alarm over growing social security risks facing Nigerian workers, warning that the rapid transformation of the labour market through artificial intelligence, AI, automation, digital platforms and the gig economy could leave millions of workers without adequate protection. The Fund has consequently called for urgent measures to close existing social protection gaps, strengthen employer compliance and build a sustainable safety net that guarantees workers’ welfare, dignity and economic security, irrespective of their employment arrangements. The NSITF also emphasised the need for government, employers, organised labour, social security institutions and the media to work together to ensure that technological advancement and changing employment patterns do not create a new generation of economically active but inadequately protected workers. The Managing Director/Chief Executive of NSITF, Oluwaseun Faleye, raised the concerns in his keynote address at the Labour Writers’ Association of Nigeria (LAWAN) Annual Workshop, in Lagos, The address, titled Social Security and Workers’ Welfare in Nigeria’s Political Transition: Closing the Protection Gaps and Building a Sustainable Safety Net, was presented on his behalf by the Deputy General Manager, and Head of Corporate Affairs Department, Alexandra Mede. Faleye described social security as an investment in human dignity, social stability and economic resilience, insisting that its importance should not be measured merely by institutional structures, regulations, financial contributions and statistics. According to him, social security is fundamentally about protecting workers and their families against unforeseen circumstances, including workplace injuries, disabilities, occupational accidents and the sudden loss of a family’s principal breadwinner. He said, “At its heart, social security is about people. It is about the worker who suffers an injury in the course of employment. It is about the family that suddenly loses its principal breadwinner. It is about a worker whose ability to earn an income is affected by an occupational accident.” The NSITF MD/CEO warned that Nigeria’s rapidly changing world of work was creating new challenges for traditional social protection systems, particularly with the growing adoption of technology, artificial intelligence, remote work, automation and digital employment platforms. While acknowledging the opportunities associated with these developments, he expressed concern that workers operating within emerging employment arrangements might be left outside established social protection structures. He questioned how the welfare of workers engaged through digital platforms could be guaranteed and how protection could be extended to people whose employment relationships no longer follow conventional patterns. “How do we ensure that technological progress does not create a new generation of workers who are economically active but insufficiently protected?” he asked. Faleye maintained that Nigeria’s social protection framework must evolve in line with developments in the labour market to ensure that technological progress does not undermine workers’ welfare and security. On the existing protection gaps, he identified the exclusion of workers outside formal employment structures, inadequate integration of employers into social protection systems and insufficient awareness of available protection mechanisms as major challenges. He stressed that closing these gaps required more than legislation, noting that awareness, compliance, accessibility, efficient institutions, reliable data and sustained stakeholder collaboration were essential. According to him, social security advocacy must move beyond government offices and conference halls to workplaces, businesses, communities and emerging sectors of the economy. He also underscored the importance of the Employees’ Compensation Scheme (ECS), describing it as a critical instrument for protecting employees against work-related injuries, disabilities and occupational risks. The scheme, he explained, represents a social compact involving employers, workers, workplaces and the wider society, adding that its effectiveness depends largely on awareness, compliance and efficient administration. Faleye called on employers to understand and fulfil their responsibilities while urging workers to become more aware of their rights and the benefits available under the scheme. He noted that institutions responsible for administering social protection programmes must continuously improve their efficiency, transparency and accessibility to deliver better services to beneficiaries. “The message must therefore be clear: Social protection is not simply a benefit to be discussed after a worker suffers an unfortunate incident. It is a system of preparedness and protection that should exist before the risk occurs,” he declared. The MD/CEO further challenged employers to regard workers’ protection not merely as a statutory obligation but as an essential component of responsible corporate citizenship. He argued that compliance with social security obligations contributes to workplace stability, productivity, employee confidence and sustainable enterprise, urging employers to see it as an investment rather than a burden. He said NSITF would continue to engage employers, simplify processes, improve service delivery and deepen understanding of the Employees’ Compensation Scheme. Turning to the role of the media, particularly labour journalists, Faleye urged members of LAWAN to go beyond reporting industrial disputes and become active interpreters of labour policies and social security issues. He said responsible labour journalism could help workers understand their rights, educate employers about their obligations and enable institutions to appreciate the concerns of the people they serve. He encouraged journalists to interrogate policies, ask critical questions, report accurately and explain complex social security issues in language accessible to ordinary Nigerians. On the implications of political transition for workers’ welfare, Faleye maintained that although political transitions naturally generate debates about governance and national development priorities, the responsibility to protect workers must remain constant, irrespective of changes in government. He called for sustainable, accountable and responsive social security institutions capable of providing continuity across successive administrations and generations of workers. Looking ahead, he identified digital and platform workers, informal-sector employees, technological disruption, occupational diseases, artificial intelligence and automation as emerging issues that Nigeria’s social protection system must adequately address. He stressed that no single institution could close the country’s social protection gaps without collaboration among government agencies, employers, workers, organised labour, the media, technology experts, academia and development partners. Reaffirming NSITF’s commitment, Faleye said the Fund would continue to strengthen stakeholder engagement, embrace technology, improve service delivery and deepen public awareness of the protections available under the Employees’ Compensation framework. He added that the Fund’s ambition was to become increasingly accessible, responsive, transparent and trusted, with the Nigerian worker remaining at the centre of its mandate. Faleye called on stakeholders at the LAWAN workshop to translate discussions into practical ideas and actions capable of strengthening social security, advancing workers’ welfare and promoting inclusive national development. He maintained that an effective social security system should go beyond responding to vulnerability to become a foundation for economic resilience, decent work and sustainable development. The post Millions of Nigerian workers face growing social security risks, NSITF warns appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Jordan will not allow terrorists to undermine its security and unity, King Abdullah says
body: Jordan will remain defiant in the face of any aggressor, King Abdullah II said on Monday, after a deadly terrorist attack on a church in the kingdom last month. “Jordan has been, and will remain, unyielding against any brutal aggressor, and formidable in the face of anyone who chooses to ignore its history,” the king said in a speech to parliament. Gunmen killed nine Christians and wounded 34 others last month during a funeral service at St the George's Greek Orthodox Church in Karak governorate. The church is in the village of Hmoud, about 80km south of Amman. Jordanian authorities arrested three men on suspicion of carrying out the attack. “A few days ago, the treacherous hand of terror sought to test our state's resilience and our people's resolve. But we will stand firm,” King Abdullah said. “We will not allow the terrorist outlaws to undermine the security and unity of this nation,” he added. “These people are not [part] of us. They have left our great Jordanian family and betrayed it. They have no place among us, today or ever.” It was the deadliest attack against Jordan's Christian minority since the 1950s. Christians number about 250,000 of Jordan's population of 11 million. All nine victims were men, several of them members of the prominent Halasah clan. The king said the blood of the Karak victims would remain a “debt we carry” as he asked members of parliament to observe a minute of silence in their memory. King Abdullah said Jordan's strength lay in its people, who grew more united, perceptive and wise when faced with hardship. “I continue to place my faith in Jordanians, in their awareness during times of uncertainty, their wisdom when emotions run high, and their devotion and loyalty when adversity strikes,” he said. Jordanian authorities have largely maintained stability in the kingdom since the 1970 civil war, which ended with the expulsion of the Palestine Liberation Organisation. However, the country has faced prolonged economic challenges, with sluggish growth and high unemployment. The official unemployment rate stands at about 16 per cent. In his speech, the king called on the government to accelerate the implementation of major projects aimed at boosting the national economy, strengthening its resilience and building on Jordan's pivotal regional role. He also described water security as a national priority, saying Jordan would not allow access to water to become hostage to any party. “There is no room for complacency or compromise,” he said, ordering the government to continue water-security projects and to develop plans to protect the country's resources, ensure their sustainability and safeguard the rights of future generations.

title: Linkage Assurance Grows Profit by 31% in Nine Months
body: Deborah Ndinorouba Linkage Assurance Plc grew its profit after tax(PA) by 31 per cent to N4.09 billion in the nine months ended September 2026, while its total assets climbed to N100.8 billion, reflecting growth in its financial position despite a challenging operating environment. The insurer’s unaudited financial results filed with the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) showed that PAT increased from N3.12 billion recorded in 2025 to N4.09 billion in 2026. Profit before tax also rose by 29 per cent to N4.32 billion, compared with N3.34 billion in the same period last year. The growth in profitability was largely supported by investment and other income, which rose 27 per cent to N7.71 billion from N6.05 billion a year earlier, helping the company manage rising claims and other insurance-related costs during the review period. Insurance revenue increased by six per cent to N20.55 billion from N19.30 billion, reflecting growth in the company’s insurance business, while the company continues to meet its obligation to customers as reflected in gross claims pay out of N5.59 billion during the nine-month period, compared with N4.02 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. On the balance sheet, the insurer recorded stronger growth, with total assets increasing by 31 per cent to N100.83 billion as of September 30, 2026, compared with N76.90 billion at the end of December 2025. In its outlook, Linkage Assurance said its strategic focus for 2026 was centred on consolidation, with emphasis on business growth, operational excellence, financial excellence, and customer and people development. Commenting, Managing Director/CEO, Linkage Assurance Plc, Daniel Braie, said the company’s strategy would guide its efforts to increase market share in profitable business segments while improving customer experience in an increasingly competitive insurance market. He also identified technology and digital transformation as important components of its growth strategy, particularly in improving products and services for direct and personal insurance customers. Braie said: “ Linkage would offer customers different motor insurance options based on their risk exposure, willingness and ability to pay, while continuing its brand awareness and customer value initiatives.” Linkage Assurance’s nine-month performance comes as Nigeria’s insurance industry enters a new phase following the recapitalisation exercise, which has increased expectations for stronger underwriting capacity, improved claims settlement and more sustainable business growth.

title: Mission to Alyoshki followed months of difficult negotiations — ombudswoman
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. The humanitarian mission to Alyoshki in the Kherson Region was preceded by many months of difficult negotiations and preparations, Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova said at a press conference.
"Our humanitarian mission took place on the 30th [of October], but <...> it was preceded by very long months of complex negotiations and preparations. Most importantly, I want to say that the humanitarian mission had a single goal - to deliver humanitarian aid to those who need it, and to ensure that those who expressed a desire to leave the combat zone were given the opportunity to do so as safely as possible," Lantratova emphasized.

title: SBU exposes five more enemy agitators who praised RF and called for strikes on Ukraine
body:
The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) has exposed five more pro-Kremlin agitators in various regions of Ukraine who publicly justified Russia’s armed aggression, spread fakes about the Defense Forces, and called on the enemy to launch new strikes on our state.
"Thus, in Kyiv region, a resident of Brovary was exposed who urged Ukrainians to lay down their arms before the aggressor country. According to case materials, the suspect spread enemy propaganda on his page in the banned social network Odnoklassniki. The offender also questioned Ukrainian statehood and praised the war crimes of the Rashists," the SBU reported in a Telegram post on Monday.
It is reported that in Kropyvnytskyi, suspicion was served to a local resident who in Telegram channel chats called for intensified Russian shelling of Ukrainian cities. To distribute Kremlin content, the suspect published his comments under posts by Russian bloggers with millions of followers belonging to Putin's media pool.
In another instance, in Kherson, SBU cyber specialists exposed a local female resident who justified the temporary occupation of the port city and called on Russia armed formations to launch new attacks on the region's right bank. It was documented that she circulated relevant publications on her Facebook and Odnoklassniki pages. In addition, the suspect published disinformation about the combat work of the Defense Forces and the operational situation at the front.
In Bukovyna, two more Rashism agitators were exposed. Both distributed enemy content on social networks. One of them, in Telegram channels, justified Russia's full-scale aggression and the seizure of part of Ukraine's territory. The other spread pro-Russian narratives with insulting fabrications about Ukrainians on the Russian social network Odnoklassniki. Mobile phones and computer equipment containing evidence of crimes were seized from the detainees during searches.
Court linguistic examinations initiated by the SBU confirmed the facts of the suspects' information-subversive activities in the interests of the aggressor country.
Security Service investigators notified them of suspicion in accordance with their committed crimes under Parts 2 and 3 of Article 436-2 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine (justification, recognition as lawful, or denial of the armed aggression of Russia against Ukraine, glorification of its participants).
The offenders face up to 8 years in prison with confiscation of property.

title: Iran’s IRGC Navy says 11 tankers violating Hormuz passage rules catch fire since Oct 25
body:
TEHRAN, November 2. /TASS/. Eleven tankers violating passage rules in the Strait of Hormuz have caught fire since October 25, with some of them sinking, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said.
"Eleven violator tankers have caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz since October 25 alone (when Commander of the US Central Command (CENTCOM) Bradley Cooper made a demonstrative visit to the Strait of Hormuz). Some of the vessels sank," the IRGC Navy wrote on X.

title: Dep. sec. of Iran SNSC meets China’s top diplomat in Beijing
body:
TEHRAN, Nov. 02 (MNA) – Deputy for International Affairs at Iran’s Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) Ali Bagheri met and held talks with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in the capital Beijing on Monday.
Ali Bagheri has travelled to Beijing for talks with Chinese officials to discuss bilateral ties and the latest developments in the region and the world.
During the meeting, the two sides exchanged their views on bilateral relations as well as regional and international developments.
Chinese foreign minister, for his part, emphasized that dialogue and negotiation are the only solution to resolving the current conflict in West Asia, reaffirming Beijing’s support for Tehran in safeguarding its sovereignty and security.

title: FG, DICON Renew Push For Self-Sufficiency In Military Equipment
body: Nigeria’s quest for self-sufficiency in military equipment production has received a fresh boost as DICON-D7G unveiled plans to expand indigenous defence manufacturing, attract foreign investment and create 7,000 employment opportunities for retired military personnel and civilians. The initiative, being promoted at the ongoing Africa International Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX) in Lagos, also includes plans to secure 40,000 square metres of land for the establishment of a world-class international exhibition centre. The Chief Executive Officer of DICON-D7G, Mr Osman Chennar, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists on Monday, saying the initiative was aimed at accelerating Nigeria’s transition from dependence on imported military equipment to local manufacturing, technology transfer and industrial self-sufficiency. DICON-D7G, a major sponsor of AFRIDEX, is using the international exhibition to promote its vision of building a stronger Nigerian military-industrial complex through local production, strategic partnerships, investment mobilisation and employment generation. The renewed push comes 61 years after the establishment of the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria (DICON) in 1964, with the country still working towards developing the capacity to manufacture a substantial proportion of the military equipment required by its armed forces. For decades, Nigeria has depended considerably on foreign suppliers for military hardware, ammunition, components and other defence technologies, raising concerns about foreign exchange expenditure, supply-chain vulnerabilities and the sustainability of national security operations. Chennar said DICON-D7G was seeking to address the challenge by bringing government institutions, private investors, indigenous manufacturers, research organisations and international technology partners together. “Our ambition is to move Nigeria from dependence on imported military equipment to a country that can increasingly manufacture, maintain and sustain its own defence requirements,” he said. According to him, Nigeria possesses the human resources, technical expertise and industrial potential to achieve defence industrial independence through strategic investments and effective partnerships. He said the organisation’s objective was to move Nigeria beyond importing finished defence products to developing the capacity to design, manufacture, maintain and eventually export military equipment. As part of its international expansion, DICON-D7G recently made its debut at an exhibition in Qatar, where it sought partnerships with foreign manufacturers, investors and technology companies to facilitate technology transfer and strengthen local production. “Our engagement with international partners is designed to encourage technology transfer, attract investment and build the technical capacity required to strengthen Nigeria’s defence industry,” Chennar said. He described AFRIDEX as an important platform for bringing manufacturers, investors, technology developers and other stakeholders together to advance Nigeria’s defence industrial ambitions. The exhibition, he said, would provide opportunities to promote indigenous innovation, attract investment and encourage collaboration capable of translating Nigeria’s industrial potential into practical defence manufacturing capabilities. In another major development, DICON-D7G is pursuing the acquisition of approximately 40,000 square metres of land in Lagos for a proposed international exhibition centre. The facility is expected to host international defence exhibitions, industrial trade fairs, technology showcases, manufacturing conferences and investment forums, while providing a platform for Nigerian manufacturers to showcase locally developed products. “The proposed exhibition centre in Lagos will provide a permanent platform for international defence exhibitions, technology showcases and investment opportunities,” Chennar said. The proposed centre is also envisaged as a commercial asset that could generate revenue and support the organisation’s long-term industrial objectives. The organisation is also projecting 7,000 employment opportunities, comprising 2,000 positions for retired military personnel and 5,000 for civilians. The retired military personnel are expected to contribute their experience and technical expertise in areas including training, engineering, logistics, administration and project management. The civilian employment opportunities are expected to cover manufacturing, engineering, information technology, research and development, skilled trades and other supporting services. “We are looking beyond military equipment production. We also want to create opportunities for retired military personnel and young Nigerians to contribute their skills to national development,” he said. Beyond employment generation, the initiative is seeking to strengthen Nigeria’s military-industrial ecosystem by expanding local production and reducing dependence on foreign suppliers. DICON-D7G has also indicated plans to expand its manufacturing activities beyond arms and ammunition to include tanks, armoured personnel carriers, mine-resistant vehicles, boats and drones. The broader ambition is to develop local capacity that can support the country’s defence requirements, conserve foreign exchange, create jobs and stimulate technological advancement. The development comes amid renewed efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s defence manufacturing framework following President Bola Tinubu’s signing of the DICON Amendment Act into law in November 2023. The legislation provides an expanded framework for promoting indigenous defence production and strengthening the country’s military-industrial capacity. The post FG, DICON Renew Push For Self-Sufficiency In Military Equipment appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Dino Melaye challenges Tinubu to Quranic citation contest
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Kogi West Senator and ADC Chieftain, Dino Melaye, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to a Quranic citation contest, following the President’s ongoing spiritual visit to Saudi Arabia for Umrah, the lesser Hajj. Melaye issued the challenge in a post on his X handle on Monday, saying he was ready to compete with Tinubu in citing passages from the Quran when the President returns to Nigeria. He wrote, “Now that Alhaji Bola Tinubu is in Umrah. Immediately he comes back I challenge him to a Quanic citation competition with me. No one can mock God. SDM” Now that Alhaji Bola Tinubu is in Umrah. Immediately he comes back I challenge him to a Quanic citation competition with me. No one can mock God. SDM pic.twitter.com/lssJkwMUz6 — Senator Dino Melaye. (SDM) (@_dinomelaye) November 2, 2026 The challenge comes amid public attention surrounding Tinubu’s spiritual activities in Makkah, where he performed the Umrah pilgrimage and was granted access to pray inside the Holy Ka’abah. Vanguard reported that Tinubu arrived in Saudi Arabia on Thursday, October 29, ahead of the religious exercise, which he performed at the Grand Mosque, Masjid al-Haram, on Friday, October 30. The President was granted the rare privilege of entering the sacred structure by Saudi Arabia’s King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques. According to the Presidency, Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal of Masjid al-Haram led Tinubu into the Ka’abah, where he offered prayers of gratitude and sought divine guidance for Nigeria. In his reflection on the spiritual experience, Tinubu said he had prayed for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians. He also cited Surah Aal-Imran, Verse 26 of the Quran, which speaks about Allah’s ultimate authority over power and sovereignty. “There is no other God but Almighty Allah. He is the giver and the taker. He owns power and authority,” the President said. Tinubu subsequently reaffirmed his commitment to national development, saying his determination to build a prosperous Nigeria had been strengthened by the spiritual experience. The President travelled to Saudi Arabia with a delegation that included the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi; Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate; and governors of Borno, Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Yobe and Kwara states, among other officials and business leaders. title: Gov Eno appoints chief of staff
body:
Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State has appointed Aniefiok Johnson as his chief of staff, less than a year before the end of his first term in office.
The Secretary to the State Government, Enobong Uwah, announced the appointment in a statement on Friday.
Mr Johnson, who previously served as the governor’s executive assistant and chief delivery advisor, will assume his new position with immediate effect.
According to the statement, Mr Johnson distinguished himself in his previous role through diligence, loyalty and commitment to the administration’s Arise Agenda.
Mr Johnson has more than three decades of experience in international diplomacy and senior management roles with the United Nations.
Before joining the Akwa Ibom State Government, he served as chief of staff, at director level, in the Office of the United Nations Special Envoy for the Great Lakes Region in Nairobi, Kenya.
His international assignments included roles with the African Union-United Nations Hybrid Operation in Darfur (UNAMID), the African Union-United Nations Joint Mediation Support Team in Doha, Qatar, and Nigeria’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations in New York.
He also served in diplomatic postings involving German and Caribbean embassies.
During a sabbatical from his international career, Mr Johnson served as senior special assistant to the president of Nigeria on special projects, overseeing federal infrastructure, power and development initiatives.
In Akwa Ibom, he served as executive assistant and chief delivery advisor to Governor Eno, helping coordinate government priorities and policy implementation under the administration’s Arise Agenda. He also led the state’s power sector reform committee.
Mr Johnson holds a Master of Arts in International Relations from Dublin City University, Ireland, and a degree in Political Science.
His appointment comes as the Eno administration approaches the final year of its first term, with the governor’s office expected to remain central to coordinating government activities and implementing the administration’s policy commitments.

title: Tinubu Pays Tribute To Sultan On 20th Anniversary
body: .Describes him as a leader, friend, bridge between faiths Deji Elumoye in Abuja President Bola Tinubu has paid a glowing tribute to the Sultan of Sokoto, His Eminence, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, on his 20th anniversary on the throne. The President described the revered first class monarch as a leader, friend, bridge between faiths, voice of moderation, and a steady counsellor to leaders nationwide. Tinubu, in the nine-paragraph tribute issued on Monday stated, inter alia: “My Dear Leader and Esteemed Brother, His Eminence, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III. “Today, I join millions of your subjects and friends in Nigeria and abroad to celebrate you as you mark 20 years on the exalted throne of your forebears as the 20th Sultan of Sokoto. “Twenty years ago, you ascended the throne with humility, courage, and a profound sense of duty. In the two decades since, you have not only preserved the glorious heritage of the Sokoto Caliphate; you have enriched it, redefined it, and made it a formidable instrument for peace, unity, and national development. “Your uncommon wisdom, your calm in moments of tension, and your unwavering commitment to Nigeria have always struck me. You have been more than a traditional ruler. You have been a moral authority, a bridge between faiths, a voice of moderation, and a steady counsellor to leaders across the country. “As Sultan and as President-General of the Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs, you have consistently stood for religious harmony and tolerance. Under your leadership as Co-Chairman of the Nigeria Inter-Religious Council, Christians and Muslims have found common ground, and our diversity has become a source of strength rather than division. “Your advocacy for peace in the North and across the Sahel, your passion for education, especially for the girl-child, your support for our farmers and for public health, and your quiet but effective interventions for the poor and vulnerable speak to a reign that is truly people-centred. “Personally, I value our friendship deeply. Your counsel has been honest, patriotic, and always in Nigeria’s best interest. Thank you for your support and your prayers for our nation. “As you celebrate this historic milestone, I pray that Almighty Allah (SWT) will continue to grant you good health, long life, and renewed wisdom. May your reign continue to bring peace to Sokoto, unity to Nigeria, and honour to the Ummah. “Congratulations, Your Eminence.”

title: Democrats lead in key battleground states ahead of Senate midterms race - NYT poll
body: US Senate midterm poll results published by The New York Times and Siena University on Sunday indicate that Republicans trail the Democrats in most battleground states.The survey shows that Texas is ready to flip Democratic. If accurate, that means that Texas is primed to elect a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in nearly forty years.Kansas, which is in a similar situation, has not elected a democrat since 1932.The polls point to a major shift in the political landscape of the US and signal that a significant blow is underway for the Trump administration, which has benefited from a Senate majority in Congress since the 2024 elections.In order to win a majority in the Senate, the Democratic Party must hold all of its seats and flip at least four of the seats currently held by Republicans.Democrats lead in key states for majority control of SenateThere are seven "battleground states" - closely contested states determined by narrow voting margins where candidates from either party could secure the win.Democrats lead in five Republican strongholds, according to the NYT poll. Those leads are significant in Kansas, Maine, Ohio, and Texas. Meanwhile, Democrats lead narrowly in Alaska, while a sixth Republican state, Iowa, shows an extremely tight race.Dissatisfaction with Trump administration a major factor in electorate shiftThe results reflect dissatisfaction with the incumbent administration. US President Donald Trump's approval rating has recently been polled at 32%, slightly higher than his all-time low. A Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll released last month found that 52% of Americans strongly disapproved of Trump, with mounting economic fallout from the war with Iran being a central issue.The president has been campaigning consistently in the run-up to the November third midterm elections, with recent rallies having been held in Florida, Kansas, and Iowa.At one of the rallies, Trump said Democrats left the US in a "dark age" but "we quickly turned it into the golden age of America" during his administration.

title: Elbit Systems Secures 170M Contract for IDF Artillery Training Center
body:
Elbit Systems has secured an approximately $170 million contract from Israel’s Ministry of Defense to establish and operate an advanced training and simulation center for the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) Artillery Corps.
The 15-year agreement will support the integration of the ROEM (SIGMA) self-propelled artillery system and LAHAV (PULS) precision rocket launcher system.
The center will feature mission and driving simulators, training classrooms, dedicated facilities, automation, AI-based functionalities and advanced driver-training solutions. Elbit will also provide training, maintenance and technical support throughout the contract period.
The project aims to improve personnel readiness, accelerate qualification timelines and increase training efficiency while reducing resource consumption and wear on operational platforms.
Elbit Systems Ltd. will showcase its Unmanned Underwater Vehicle (UUV) capabilities for the first time at Euronaval 2026, expanding its autonomous maritime portfolio across air, surface, and underwater domains
