title: HUR Confirms Russian Su-57 Explosion at Akhtubinsk Airfield
body:
Ukraine’s Military Intelligence Directorate (HUR) confirmed that Russia lost a Su-57 (NATO: Felon) stealth fighter on Thursday, Oct. 29, due to an engine startup failure.
The initial report came out on Friday, when a Ukrainian monitoring channel shared a satellite image showing the wreckage of a fighter jet resembling a Su-57 at the Astrakhan region’s Akhtubinsk airfield.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
On Monday, HUR said in a press release that the Su-57 was lost during engine start-up, confirming earlier speculations.
The agency suspected subpar jet fuel quality caused the incident.
“The Su-57 is equipped with an AL-41F1 turbojet engine (the so-called ‘Izdeliye 117’). One of the reasons why engines of this type can explode or suffer catastrophic failure is poor-quality fuel,” it said.
It added that the same fuel is also used by other Russian jets, including the Geran 4 and 5 jet-powered drones, whose usage has spiked since the summer of 2026.
“Recall that Jet A-1 is an analog of the Russian-Soviet aviation fuel TS-1 and RT for gas turbine aircraft engines. Jet A-1 fuel is fully compatible and suitable for use by Russian aircraft in service with the aggressor state’s army – MiG-29, Su-34 (NVO), Su-35S, Su-30SM, Su-57, Su-24M, Tu-95MS (MSM),” the press release says.
The Su-57 is Russia’s premier fifth-generation multirole fighter and its most advanced aircraft currently in service.
It first flew in 2010, with serial production beginning in 2019 following a troubled development process that included India’s withdrawal from the project in 2018.
The National Interest estimated that Russia had around 32 Su-57s, including prototypes, against the 76 originally envisioned.
The Su-57 lost on Thursday made it the fourth Su-57 Russia has lost this year.
HUR noted that Russia has imported jet fuel and gasoline from third countries, including India, where the Vadinarsky refinery of Nayara Energy is 49.13% owned by Russia’s Rosneft.
Imports rose because Ukraine’s refinery attacks reduced output. Russia, the world’s third-largest oil producer, reported a record import of seaborne oil products in August, amounting to several times the total in 2025, before reducing imports by 44% the following month.
HUR added that most of the companies involved in the shipments are under foreign sanctions, including OOO RN-Aero, which the agency said supplies jet fuel to the fighter jet’s manufacturer, United Aircraft Corporation (UAC).
Because of the fuel shortage, Russia also lowered the standard for jet fuel in August, allowing a freezing point of -50°C (-58°F) instead of the previous -60°C (-76°F), according to The Moscow Times .
In September, civilian airports in Russia also imposed fuel rations , according to Russian outlet Vertska .
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Kyrgyzstan Pasture Restoration Plan Includes 7,200 Kilometers of Road Repairs
body: Kyrgyzstan plans to repair hundreds of bridges and more than 7,200 kilometers of roads to help livestock farmers reach remote grazing land as pastures near villages deteriorate. The Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture and Processing Industry outlined the plans on October 29. It estimates that 184,000 hectares of pasture near settlements have been degraded and need restoration. To ease grazing pressure near villages, the ministry has identified a need to repair and restore 553 bridges and improve 7,206.3 kilometers of pasture access roads. It also plans to establish 406 livestock watering points and install 170 milk collection tanks. Plans to restore vegetation include reseeding pastures, controlling weeds unsuitable for livestock feed, and rotating grazing areas. Tractors would be used for sowing on flat terrain and specialized drones in areas that are difficult to reach. According to the ministry, pasture grass seeds were sown on 34,376.5 hectares of degraded land between 2023 and 2025. In September, it reported purchasing more than 186 metric tons of seeds for 50 million soms (about $570,000). Sowing was still underway in October. Kyrgyzstan already has a pasture development program for 2024–2029 , approved in August 2024. It also calls for restoring degraded grazing land and improving pasture infrastructure. The latest announcement did not explain how the new plans differ from the existing program or specify their overall cost. In March 2025, the ministry said it had recommended annual restrictions on grazing near villages from April 15 to September 15. At the time, it estimated that 139,069 hectares had been degraded. It is unclear whether the higher figure in the latest announcement reflects further deterioration or a revised assessment. The ministry estimates the country’s total pasture area at about 10 million hectares. Pastures are the main source of livestock feed, so their deterioration affects feed availability and farmers’ incomes. Kyrgyzstan’s livestock numbers continued to rise in 2025, reaching approximately 1.8 million cattle and 6.3 million sheep and goats by the end of the year, increases of 1.7% and 0.8%, respectively, over 2024.

title: 2027: Obi promises to begin construction of Ibom Deep Seaport if elected president
body:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress ( NDC ) Peter Obi has promised to begin construction of the Ibom Deep Seaport in Akwa Ibom State, renewing attention on a project that has featured prominently in the campaign promises of Nigerian presidential candidates.
Mr Obi made the promise in a Facebook post on Saturday, following his visit to Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, on Friday, where he attended a homecoming ceremony organised in honour of Seriake Dickson, a senator and national leader of the NDC.
He said his proposed administration would begin efforts to upgrade ports across the Niger Delta, including those in Warri, Port Harcourt and Calabar, while commencing construction of the Ibom Deep Seaport in Akwa Ibom and establishing a new port in Bayelsa State.
“In Bayelsa, I pledged that we would begin efforts to upgrade ports throughout the Niger Delta, including those in Warri, Port Harcourt, and Calabar. We will also begin construction of the long-delayed Ibaka seaport in Akwa Ibom State and establish a new port in Bayelsa State to serve our riverine communities and the broader Niger Delta more effectively,” he wrote.
The latest pledge is noteworthy because the Ibom Deep Seaport, originally conceived as the Ibaka Deep Seaport and Industrial City, has remained unrealised decades after its conception.
It also places Mr Obi alongside President Bola Tinubu, who promised to deliver the project during his 2023 presidential campaign in Akwa Ibom.
At the All Progressives Congress campaign rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo on 30 January 2023, Mr Tinubu told supporters: “We will do mechanised farming. We will export food from Akwa Ibom. We will build your deep seaport.”
He cited the Lekki Deep Seaport, developed during his tenure as Lagos governor, as an example of what he could achieve in Akwa Ibom.
Mr Tinubu’s promise was followed by further assurances after he became president. In January 2024, Governor Umo Eno said the president had asked him to submit a memorandum seeking federal government support for the project.
Mr Eno disclosed this after meeting Mr Tinubu at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, saying he had requested the president’s intervention in the seaport and the state’s oil palm development programme.
In March 2026, the governor again publicly acknowledged the president’s assurances, saying Mr Tinubu had repeatedly told him during their discussions: “I will give you the Ibom Deep Seaport.”
“I hold on to that promise, and I know it shall come to pass,” Mr Eno said.
Mr Obi had also promised to develop the seaport during his 2023 presidential campaign.
At a Labour Party rally in Uyo in December 2022, he said he would ensure the project was put in place if elected president, describing the decades of promises surrounding it as unacceptable.
He subsequently told journalists that Akwa Ibom was not asking for a favour by seeking the seaport, arguing that it would provide Nigeria with an export channel and strengthen the country’s productive capacity.
In an interview published by Vanguard in January 2023, Mr Obi said: “We are not doing Akwa Ibom a favour by developing the Deep Seaport; rather, Akwa Ibom is offering us a space to develop an export channel which I am going to develop.”
Former Vice-President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress , Atiku Abubakar, who was the Peoples Democratic Party presidential candidate in the 2023 election, campaigned in Uyo in October 2022. However, reports of his campaign promises at the rally focused on national economic recovery, security and unity, rather than a specific commitment to construct the Ibom Deep Seaport. He promised to build a refinery in Akwa Ibom.
Atiku, however, promised in February 2023 to complete the deep seaport project in Bonny, Rivers State, if elected president.
The Ibom Deep Seaport was conceived during the administration of former Akwa Ibom Governor Victor Attah. The project was intended to create a major maritime and industrial hub in the state’s coastal area.
Its proposed location spanning the Atlantic Ocean in Mbo and Ibeno local government areas is expected to provide access to international shipping routes and support trade, industrial development and employment.
Despite repeated political commitments, the project has yet to materialise.
Mr Obi’s latest statement did not provide a construction timeline, financing arrangement, implementation framework or details of the proposed federal and state government partnership.
He also did not indicate whether his pledge was based on any existing approval or agreement with the relevant federal maritime agencies.
In his Facebook post, Mr Obi also pledged investments in healthcare and education, improved national security, the fight against corruption and measures to lift Nigerians out of poverty.

title: GPL: GFA charge Kotoko’s assistant coach for assaulting Medeama’s Ebenezer Adade
body: The assistant coach of Asante Kotoko, Diogo Peral, has been charged by the Disciplinary Committee of the Ghana Football Association (GFA) for assaulting a Medeama SC player. Peral was sent off for slapping Medeama’s Ebenezer Adade during Kotoko’s Ghana Premier League fixture over the weekend at the Baba Yara Stadium. The slap came as a reaction after the Medeama player seemed to have pushed the coach in his attempt to recover the ball for a quick restart of proceedings. Kotoko announced a disciplinary action has been taken against the coach with a fine in line. In addition to that, the GFA has also now communicated the decision to charge the technical team member for breaching Article 12(1)(h) of the GFA Disciplinary Code. Peral has until Wednesday, November 4, to respond to the charge. With their draw against Medeama, Kotoko are now winless in their last two games and sit ninth on the league table with 13 points. They face Berekum Chelsea in their next league game.

title: Top security official comments on West as a ground for human vices and Russia’s might
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. Western countries have been a breeding ground for the worst human vices, Russian Security Council Secretary Sergey Shoigu said in opening remarks at the international week Peoples of Russia.
Meanwhile, Russia’s strength as a power is underpinned not only by its ever-strengthening economic sovereignty and powerful combat capabilities but also in the people’s unity and their trust in the government.
TASS has compiled key statements from the top Russian security official.
Western countries have been a breeding ground for the worst human vices, Shoigu argued: "The collective West which once claimed global dominance is rapidly degrading, and the worse vices are blooming there, while human rights and freedoms have lost their original meaning, currently becoming a tool for destroying society and imposing permissiveness."
According to him, "justice has given way to a presumption of guilt, and any accusations no longer require evidence. This practice has been widespread in the system of international relations," Shoigu added.
Western attempts to counter Russia have been increasingly aggressive in light of the imminent victory and successes in the course of the special military operation, he argued: "The closer we get to victory and the successful conclusion of the special military operation, the more aggressive and sophisticated these attempts [by the West] become."
An active campaign is currently underway to recruit and provide funding to those willing to support the destruction of Russian statehood from within, Shoigu revealed: "It’s no secret that there’s an ongoing effort to recruit, finance, and support individuals willing to destroy Russian statehood from within."
At the same time, Shoigu stressed that Russia had "always stood united in repelling the aggressor:" "There have repeated attempts to occupy Russia’s soil, seize its resources and enslave our peoples, but never this was achieved militarily. We have always stood united in repelling the aggressor."
Russia has no plans to destroy any country, as former colonial powers are collapsing on their own, Shoigu continued: "I don’t quite get why we should do that. We have no plans to destroy any country. Many of them - colonial powers - are collapsing on their own."
"The reason is that those whom they once enslaved and turned into their colonies, are awakening and rising as their self-consciousness and self-determination are reviving," Shoigu added.
According to him, while the West has "a constant need for an enemy," Russia is not going to attack Europe: "Look, our President [Vladimir Putin] has stated three or four times in the past two months that we are not going to attack Europe. And they insist that ‘Russia is waging a hybrid war on us.’"
The West’d better "take a chill pill" and leave Russia alone, he emphasized: "God forbid you live to see a day when Russia launches a hybrid war against you. Chill out, and don’t you attack us, as we are not going to attack anyone."
European participation in the Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi requires discussion among all parties, Shoigu argued.
"A meeting in Abu Dhabi is being prepared. Our president confirmed that and said it would most likely take place in the second half of November. The meeting will be held at the same level as before. The delegations will remain unchanged: the US, Ukraine and Russia. This has already been confirmed," he said. "As for how Europe will be represented, that requires discussion and a decision by all three sides," Shoigu added.
According to Shoigu, Russia’s strength as a power lies not only in its strengthening economic sovereignty and powerful combat capabilities but also in the unity of its citizens and their confidence in the government: "Our strength lies not only in the ever solidifying economic and technological sovereignty and the most powerful arsenal of weapons at our disposal but primarily in the underlying unity of the people and their confidence in the government and in the support from our country’s citizens toward its prosperity and the achievement of those goals that our population sets for ourselves.".

title: Mutfwang vows to protect every inch of Plateau land
body: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has vowed to protect every inch of the state’s territory, assuring residents that his administration will intensify security efforts and facilitate the return of internally displaced persons (IDPs) to their ancestral communities. Mutfwang gave the assurance on Monday in Jos during the formal inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council, where he also called on party members to intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor said his administration remained committed to protecting communities and preventing further displacement, adding that efforts were underway to strengthen security operations across the state. “If the people of Plateau knew the magnitude of the damage planned against our state, they would appreciate that only God’s intervention and our strategic efforts have helped us thus far. “One thing I have committed myself to is that I will ensure the protection of every inch of land in Plateau State. “Very soon, we are going to be taking practical steps to facilitate the return of internally displaced persons back to their communities,” he said. Mutfwang disclosed that his administration would deploy additional security personnel, announcing plans to commission a new batch of retrained Operation Rainbow operatives the following week. He added that at least 800 trained forest guards would also be deployed within four weeks as part of efforts to strengthen security across the state. “One of the things we have waited for is to get more boots on ground and, by the grace of God, next week we are going to commission a new batch of retrained Operation Rainbow operatives. “And in another four weeks, we are going to also release at least 800 trained forest guards. “We are determined to ensure that our people return to their ancestral homes,” the governor said. He commended President Bola Tinubu for what he described as his commitment to the welfare of Nigerians and support for efforts to address insecurity. Mutfwang appealed to residents to remain patient and trust his administration, assuring them that it would continue to work towards restoring peace and security. “And so, all we are asking Plateau people is, trust us, be patient with us, and by the grace of God, you will not regret it,” he said. On the 2027 elections, the governor urged members of the campaign council to take the APC’s message to communities across the state, saying his administration needed another mandate to complete ongoing projects and programmes. He said the campaign would seek the people’s endorsement for a second term to sustain the administration’s development agenda. “We are going to the nooks and crannies of Plateau State to solicit their endorsement and approval for a second time in office because the many things we have begun must not be aborted. “We must ensure that we bring things to a very glorious height,” he said. Describing governance as a continuous process, Mutfwang likened it to a relay race, noting that successive administrations should build on the achievements of their predecessors. “We can collectively make Plateau State better. This is our desire, and by the grace of God, we are determined that we will leave Plateau State better than we met it in every sense of the word,” he added. The governor also declared his support for Tinubu and the APC ahead of the 2027 general elections, expressing confidence that Plateau voters would support the President’s re-election bid and renew his own mandate. “We are talking about a unification movement, that Plateau people have decided in 2027 to go one direction. “And we have chosen that the wings on which we have chosen to fly in 2027 are the wings of the APC. “I am confident that come January 16, 2027, by the grace of God, Plateau State will return President Bola Ahmed Tinubu with a resounding victory. And that two weeks later, the people of Plateau will renew their mandate for us to continue on the good journey we have started,” he said. Mutfwang charged APC candidates and campaign council members to lead mobilisation efforts in their respective communities, wards, local government areas and constituencies. He urged them to serve as bridge-builders, promote unity and avoid actions capable of deepening divisions within the party. Earlier, the Plateau State APC Chairman, Rufus Bature, thanked members of the campaign council for accepting to serve, saying their participation demonstrated commitment to the party’s electoral efforts. Bature also urged members to conduct peaceful campaigns based on facts and honesty, warning against violence during the electioneering period. “We have no reason to be courtiers of violence. We are known for peace and we will continue on that trajectory. “Let’s travel together. We’ll do all we can to make sure that the campaign is seamless and flawless,” he said. The post Mutfwang vows to protect every inch of Plateau land appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: HUR: Eight Chinese and four US manufacturers supply parts for Russia’s upgraded Gerbera drone. One with warhead already turned up on Poland’s coast
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russia’s cheap drone is no longer just a decoy. An enlarged version of the “Gerbera", built to bait Ukraine’s air defenses, can now fly up to 1,200 kilometers and carry a warhead of up to 25 kg, Defense Intelligence of Ukraine (HUR) said in a new teardown of the “Gerbera-2” published on its War&Sanctions portal, along with an interactive 3D model and a list of the drone’s parts. Russia loads ever more capability onto airframes it once treated as throwaway, narrowing the gap with its far pricier Geran strike drones. The bigger fuel tank pushes the Gerbera’s reach past Ukraine’s borders, and one such drone, carrying a warhead, turned up on Poland’s Baltic coast in September. From throwaway bait to a 1,200-km firestarter The Gerbera began as a cheap decoy meant to soak up Ukraine’s air defenses, in reconnaissance and kamikaze versions, Defense Intelligence said. Over time, its insides crept toward those of the costlier Geran: anti-jam “Kometa” antennas, mesh modems, expensive gimbal-mounted cameras. The enlarged model has a 3-meter wingspan, a 2.6-meter fuselage, and a new 63-liter fuel tank, split into sections to keep the drone steady in maneuvers, giving it a range of up to 1,200 km. Its two-cylinder, two-stroke engine is effectively half of a Geran-2 engine, which the agency says is produced at Russia’s Alabuga plant. The drone examined by HUR carried a 10-kg high-explosive fragmentation-incendiary warhead plus separate bags of incendiary mixture, though Russia claims the type can lift a warhead of up to 25 kg. A drone built mostly from Chinese and American parts Its electronics, HUR said, include an updated flight controller, a 12-channel “Kometa” antenna, a mesh modem made by China’s Shenzhen Sinosun Technology, and a new video-processing unit nicknamed “Sosiska” (Sausage), built on a Chinese Coke Pi microcomputer. The sample had a dual IP camera mounted above the fuel tank to spot interceptors, and the agency said it has also found versions with forward-facing cameras and three-axis gimbals. Of all the parts, the largest shares come from Chinese - 8 and American - 4 manufacturers. Why its range now reaches past Ukraine The bigger fuel tank is what the investigators flag as the most significant: the extended range means the Gerbera-2 could be used beyond Ukrainian territory. In mid-September, Defense Intelligence noted, a Gerbera-2 carrying a warhead was found on Poland’s Baltic coast, one of several Russian drones to drift or stray toward NATO shores. title: Filipino embalmers – last caretakers of the dead, seldom cared for
body: PART 1 | Inside the world of Filipino embalmers Last of 2 parts When Jonnel Cribello received his license to embalm in 2009, one question followed him everywhere. “The most frequent question people asked me [was] whether I washed my hands before shaking theirs,” he said. A registered nurse who once dreamed of becoming a surgeon, Cribello turned to embalming after coming across a media feature on an embalming school. “If I wanted to work with the human body, the easiest route for me then was to work in the mortuary industry,” he said. Today, he helps teach the next generation of embalmers as an accredited trainer and program director at the Philippine College of Advanced Studies (PCAS) in Cebu, one of only four active accredited embalming schools in the country and the only one outside Luzon. Embalmers disinfect, preserve, and restore a body so families can hold a wake — often for days — before burial or cremation. But while the industry has made strides in shedding its perception as dirty work, the systems around it — licensing, data, and pay — have been slower to catch up with other medical-adjacent fields. Changing image For years, embalmers were seen as untidy and uneducated, said James Patrick Ovejera, president of the Professional Embalmers Association of the Philippines Inc. (PEAP). “There was an idea that it’s dirty work, the person is untidy, the person is illiterate, and the person is technically a low-class person,” he said. “There were even depictions in the movies wherein it’s a person that works in a dark place… a hunchback.” That image began to shift around 2010, when the Department of Health (DOH) set out to professionalize the field, Ovejera said. The rules governing embalming date back to 1975, when then-president Ferdinand E. Marcos issued Presidential Decree No. 856 , or the Code on Sanitation of the Philippines. Its chapter XXI, on the disposal of dead persons, covers everything from burial grounds to funeral and embalming establishments. Detailed rules for embalmers came only in 1996, more than two decades later. They called for the DOH to create a Committee of Examiners for Undertakers and Embalmers (DOH-CEUE), which licenses embalmers and accredits training schools. In 2010, the DOH reinstated the committee with new members, who worked with the University of the Philippines to streamline the curriculum and licensure exam, under Administrative Order No. 2010-0033 . The order also, for the first time, mandated minimum wage for all embalmers. The committee and the five training schools at the time then went region by region to explain the rules to local officials. Feedback led to new measures, including a refresher program for embalmers with long-expired licenses and a Filipino version of the exam, which was previously in English. “There are a lot of people [who] are very skilled coming from the provinces…but they couldn’t really understand English well,” said Ovejera. At the time, he had been teaching at the Philippine Embalmers and Undertakers Review and Training Center (PEURTC), and enlisted in the roadshow efforts. In 2018, embalmers like Ovejera formed PEAP as their own professional counterpart to the Philippine Mortuary Association, which represents funeral homeowners. “At the time, there was no collective body representing us, and we wanted to do something about that,” he said. In the classroom LEARNING. Embalming students at PCAS watch an instructor lead a demonstration on a cadaver. Photo courtesy of PCAS Under current DOH rules, aspiring embalmers need a high school diploma, at least 140 hours of instruction from an accredited institution, and proof that they have embalmed at least 10 cadavers within a year. They then take a licensure exam held twice a year, every March and September. Under rules revised in 2021, licenses are issued by the DOH’s Health Facilities and Services Regulatory Bureau (HFSRB) after applicants pass the committee’s exam. These are valid for three years and can be revoked if not renewed within five. Students spend about two months in class and a month embalming real cadavers at partner funeral homes. Tuition ranges from about P27,000 to about P30,000 depending on the training institution. Over half of Cribello’s students at PCAS have worked in funeral homes or come from families that own one. His oldest student was 75; the average age is around 45. “It’s such a unique challenge because people [are] going back to school after years of not having a good habit of reading or studying,” he said. PCAS now runs two cohorts a year of about 60 students each, up from 10 per cohort in 2009. At PEURTC in Manila, where Ovejera still teaches, local classes run 40 to 60 students, plus a separate class of five to eight from neighboring Southeast Asian countries like Singapore, Thailand, and Malaysia who come to the Philippines for mortuary education. Affordability and English as a medium of instruction are the main attractions. Tools of the trade EMBALMING. Tools and chemicals found in an embalming preparation room at Arlington Memorial Chapels in Quezon City, Manila. Jake Gomez/Rappler Philippine embalmers train on only a handful of tools and chemicals. In the US, Cribello estimated, training incorporates 30 to 35 pieces of equipment. “There are very simple kinds and sets of tools that have been used in the past and continue to be taught today here. That much has not changed,” he said. Most local funeral homes rely on formalin, a cheap formaldehyde solution. Other chemicals used abroad, in what is called soft embalming, can make a face look more natural. But culture and climate shape the practice, Ovejera said. Filipino wakes routinely run around the clock for days, sometimes weeks, and softer chemicals do not hold up in humid weather. Cost matters too. A 200-liter drum of formalin costs around P11,000 to P15,000, while soft-embalming chemicals can cost 20 times more, according to Ovejera. For that reason, only select funeral homes offer more technical and upscale embalming options. An industry behind Demand for an embalmer’s work is guaranteed. Fair pay, Cribello said, is not. “There is a certain opportunity to review the industry regulations in terms of the kind of salaries imposed within the industry,” Cribello said. “I personally feel that we are behind [compared with] similar professionals like nurses and doctors.” Entry-level salaries still hover around minimum wage (P401 to P755 per day, depending on the region), according to PCAS and PEAP, and embalmers get no hazard pay despite chronic exposure to chemicals like formaldehyde, which the International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies as a Group 1 carcinogen . The 2010 rules set minimum wage as the entry point, Ovejera said, but smaller funeral homes often pay per body instead, pushing many embalmers to freelance and work between funerary businesses. Change in any regard would require legislation. “I agree that there must be changes. But how do we do that? It has to be in legislation,” Ovejera said. Embalmers also have no seat on the body that licenses them. Under the current rules, the DOH-CEUE’s five members are a chairperson, vice chairperson, sanitary engineer, pathologist, and legal officer. No mention of an embalmer sitting on the committee of examiners. Licensed embalmers take part only as assessors for the oral and practical exam. By contrast, the board that licenses nurses is made up of nurses. Counting embalmers The number of active, licensed embalmers in the country is hard to pin down. The DOH-CEUE has not formally published updated figures in recent years, according to PCAS. The embalmers association recorded about 5,000 licensed embalmers in 2018, though that count includes those who have died, moved abroad, or let their licenses lapse. Exams were suspended in 2020 and 2021 during the COVID-19 pandemic. Since resumption, each exam has licensed roughly 100 people, bringing the total to between 6,000 and 6,300, according to the embalmers association. PCAS estimates 200 to 300 new embalmers a year. In March 2026, 75 aspirants earned their licenses. After the September 2026 written exam, 125 moved on to the oral and practical portion. Better data would help as Singapore, Malaysia, and employers in the Middle East, Europe, and North America look to hire Filipino embalmers, Ovejera said. “Without knowing the actual figures…we don’t even know: do we have enough [at home]?” Ovejera said. The counts also miss a group that’s harder to track: people who embalm without a license, which DOH rules prohibit. Several embalmers we spoke with said the practice persists, particularly in provinces where training is inaccessible. Room to grow Both men remain hopeful that the industry will continue to catch up. For Cribello, the work remains “the ultimate noble cause.” In his classes, he pushes the fundamentals of hygiene and care for grieving families, along with sounder business practices for a new generation of operators. “While it’s [grim] and tiring, it gives fulfillment that I can have a platform where I can influence not just one student, but operators and embalmers all throughout the country,” he said. For Ovejera, it became all the more personal in 2023, when his father died. “I wanted to make sure that we do the best for him,” he said. He helped embalm his father himself. That experience, he said, further strengthened the importance of the work to grieving families. “The picture of an individual lying there inside the casket…will always be in the cognitive footprint of the family members,” he said. PEAP has also explored ladderized programs through the introduction of embalming into more Filipino universities, Ovejera said. For now, it remains a short certificate course rather than a degree. “There’s a lot more work to do… We want to be more globally competitive,” he said. – Rappler.com * Jake Gomez is a 2026-2027 Henry Luce scholar.
