title: GES to reprimand two Techiman SHS teachers who allegedly assaulted student in viral video
body: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has announced disciplinary measures against teachers of the Twene Amanfo Senior High Technical School in Techiman who allegedly assaulted a male student, following an incident captured in a viral video. The teachers are to be reprimanded and removed from their positions as Masters on Duty as part of measures recommended by a committee set up by the school’s management to investigate the incident. Deputy Director-General in charge of Quality and Access at the GES, Dr Issahaque Munwaru, disclosed this in an interview on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Monday, November 2. He said the teachers would also be referred for guidance and counselling alongside the affected students, while the school would surcharge them for the medical expenses incurred in treating the children. “The teachers would have to be reprimanded, and they are also to be taken off their positions,” he said, explaining that they would no longer be assigned duties as Masters on Duty. Dr Munwaru said preliminary findings indicated that the teachers had allegedly assaulted students after discovering that some of them were bullying their colleagues and extorting money from them. According to him, the students were reportedly using the metallic parts of their belts to lash colleagues who refused to pay the money demanded from them. He, however, maintained that the teachers were not justified in taking the law into their own hands, stressing that the GES Code of Conduct prohibits staff from inflicting physical punishment on students. “The law does not permit anything that will inflict pain on the child,” he said. Dr Munwaru explained that the incident constituted professional misconduct under Part Three, Section Eight, Subsection A of the GES Code of Conduct. He said the Service would continue to enforce its regulations against corporal punishment and other forms of abuse in schools. Under the Code of Conduct, teachers are prohibited from administering corporal punishment, subjecting students to painful body postures, threatening them with harm or assaulting them. Dr Munwaru said the GES regularly educates teachers on the Code of Conduct through orientation programmes, professional learning communities and continuous professional development sessions. He warned that teachers who repeat similar offences would face more severe disciplinary action. “Any further misconduct along the same line will not receive the same level. It is going to be more punitive,” he said. The GES Deputy Director-General added that the Service was cooperating with security agencies investigating the incident, following the arrest of the teachers by the Bono East Regional Police. He said the Service would provide the necessary information to support the police investigation, while its own disciplinary processes continued. READ ALSO: Two Techiman SHS teachers arrested over alleged assault of 17-year-old student

title: Russia looks forward to Putin, Xi meeting at APEC summit — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. Preparations for the meeting of Russian President Vladimir Putin with President of China Xi Jinping at the APEC summit continue, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
"The preparation for this meeting is confirmed. We are looking forward to this meeting," he said. "We are indeed looking forward to summit meetings with our Chinese friends every time," he said.
The program of stay of the Russian president at the APEC summit is at the stage of preparation for the time being, Peskov noted. "We are in touch primarily with the organizers, with the Chinese side," the Kremlin Spokesman said.
No details are available thus far on a possible trilateral meeting of Russian President Vladimir Putin, President of China Xi Jinping and US leader Donald Trump at the APEC summit, Peskov noted.
"No exact details are available for the time being as regards the possible trilateral meeting," he added.

title: Stakeholders Laud Ogun Free Trade Zone’s Education Programme
body: James Sowole in Abeokuta Education stakeholders and community leaders in Igbesa, Ado-Odo/Ota Local Government Area in Ogun State have commended the Ogun–Guangdong Free Trade Zone (OGFTZ) for its sustained investment in educational development across its host communities. The leaders described the OGFTZ interventions as significant contributions to improving learning opportunities, nurturing talents and shaping the future of young people. The stakeholders, who spoke during separate interactions with journalists, highlighted the impact of its educational initiatives, particularly the establishment of the China–Nigeria Friendship Model School, scholarship opportunities for deserving students and various academic, sporting and extracurricular programmes. Speaking on the zone’s contributions, Mr. Joseph Ibikunle, head of Academics and School Services at the Ado-Odo/Ota Local Government Education Authority, described OGFTZ’s educational interventions in the community for the past 15 years as remarkable and worthy of commendation. Ibikunle noted that the zone had consistently supported learners through interventions in school infrastructure, the provision of educational materials, and scholarship opportunities for deserving students. According to him, these sustained contributions had positively influenced the learning environment and created opportunities for students across the host communities. He expressed appreciation to the management of OGFTZ for its continued commitment to educational development, urging the organisation to sustain its interventions, which he said had made a meaningful difference in the lives of learners across the local government. Also speaking, High Chief Ezekiel Adewumi Durojaiye, the Otunba Amona of Igbesa, identified the establishment of the China–Nigeria Friendship Model School as one of the most significant contributions of the zone to the community. He observed that since the arrival of OGFTZ and the establishment of the school, Igbesa had increasingly become associated with China, to the extent that residents and visitors sometimes jokingly refer to the town as “China in Nigeria.” Describing the school’s impact as remarkable, Durojaiye recalled discussions surrounding its development during the visit of the Chinese Consul-General, expressing optimism that the institution would continue to grow. He said the community would welcome the expansion of the school to accommodate secondary education, and eventually, tertiary-level programmes, adding that such development would further strengthen educational opportunities for children in the area. In a similar account, Chief Ajidagba Jamiu, family head of Ilu Idofin in Igbesa, highlighted the personal impact of the zone’s educational intervention, revealing that four of his children attended the China–Nigeria Friendship School. He also disclosed that some indigenes of the community had benefited from OGFTZ-funded scholarships to study in China and had completed their studies, with some now working in their respective professional fields. While expressing appreciation for the zone’s contributions, he appealed for an expansion of the scholarship programme to accommodate more students from the host communities. He noted that increasing the number of scholarship beneficiaries would give more young people access to quality education and the opportunity to acquire knowledge and skills that could contribute to the development of their communities. The Chairman of the Igbesa Educational Committee, Alhaji Saheed Animashaun, also commended the OGFTZ partnership for its consistent educational and developmental programmes over the past three years. According to him, the zone has maintained a deliberate commitment to organising initiatives that promote the educational advancement and overall development of children in the host communities, with hardly a year passing without at least one programme designed for their benefit. He identified the annual Children’s Day celebrations, which bring together primary and secondary school pupils, as one of the initiatives through which the Zone recognises and encourages young people. Beyond the celebrations, Animashaun said OGFTZ had consistently organised academic, sporting and cultural competitions, including quiz and recitation contests, football, athletics and dancing competitions, providing platforms for students to discover and develop their abilities. He explained that these activities had helped build students’ confidence, encouraged healthy competition and demonstrated that public schools in the host communities are home to talented, intelligent and promising young people. The Education Committee chairman particularly emphasised the importance of these initiatives in identifying and nurturing talents beyond the conventional classroom environment. He added that participating students were rewarded with various gifts and prizes, including musical instruments, mowing machines, educational materials and other useful items, describing the incentives as additional motivation for students to work harder and pursue excellence. Animashaun maintained that investment in education remained one of the most valuable contributions any organisation could make to society, noting that developing the intellectual capacity and talents of young people was essential to building responsible future leaders. He, therefore, expressed appreciation to OGFTZ for its sustained commitment to educational development, urging the Zone to continue its interventions for the benefit of present and future generations.

title: Belgian PM de Wever submits his resignation to king — royal palace
body:
BRUSSELS, November 2. /TASS/. Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever has submitted his resignation to the king over the failure of coalition negotiations on the kingdom's 2027 budget, a statement of the royal palace says.
As a rule, the monarch rejects the first resignation request from the head of government and instructs him to undertake another negotiation effort. Often, under the threat of a political crisis, parties compromise unless most of them find it more politically advantageous to arrange new elections.
Currently, the Belgian government lacks 10 billion euros because of increased military spending, which entails either cutting social spending or raising taxes and fees.
Last year, Belgium's debt stood at 735 billion euros, or an unprecedented 110% of GDP. De Wever is trying to make every effort to prevent its further growth, that is, not to plug in the deficit with new loans.

title: Gov Eno Approves 13th-Month Pension For Retirees
body: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has approved the payment of a 13th-month pension bonus to all pensioners in the State, as well as a N10,000 one-time welfare support for November, 2026. Governor Umo Eno disclosed this during the presentation of a Merit Award by the State Council of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, who also endorsed him for re-election in 2027. Governor Eno, who was particularly impressed by their sense of gratitude and quality organisation, assured that the Government under his leadership will continue to prioritize the welfare of pensioners and elderly citizens in the State. “This is indeed humbling to me. It shows that you are truly technocrats with a laudable sense of organization. You may be retired but not tired. I celebrate and appreciate you greatly. “I am now directing that N10,000 be added to the November 2026 pension payment of every pensioner in support of your welfare,” he said. Governor of Akwa Ibom State, Pastor Umo Eno waves to retirees at the meeting. He urged them to equally enroll in the State’s health insurance scheme, which he said was free for 65-year-olds and above, to enable them to enjoy quality healthcare and a good rest across the state. Gov noted that he had promised to clear the backlog of gratuities, stressing that N100 billion has so far been paid, from the accumulated N111 billion since 2012, assuring that before the end of his first term, the balance will be cleared. He commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for making funds available to states, which, according to him, has made it possible for him to keep to his promise of clearing the arrears of gratuity. Governor Umo Eno during the presentation of a Merit Award by the State Council of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners. Earlier, in his welcome remarks, the State Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, Pastor Sylvester Nkodo, thanked the Governor for his compassionate and impactful leadership, describing his commitment to the welfare of the elderly and retired public servants as heartwarming and unprecedented. He also noted that Gov. Eno’s policies have significantly improved their living standard and lifted them from abject poverty to a life of dignity. He expressed gratitude to the Governor for the release of over N100 billion for the payment of inherited gratuities dating back to 2012 and prayed that God will grant the wishes of pensioners by granting him a second term in 2027. Following a motion moved and seconded by Comrade James Inim and Dr. Mrs. Uduak Udoaka, respectively, the pensioners unanimously endorsed President Tinubu, Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Governor Umo Eno and other candidates of the APC for re-election in 2027. The post Gov Eno Approves 13th-Month Pension For Retirees appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Building a gemini server in python
body:
7 years after its invention, I discovered the Gemini protocol . It’s a kind of “back to first principals” alternative to the web, aimed at providing value to independent content creators away from the noise, bots and trackers of the main web.
In Gemini, a website is called a capsule, the web is called the geminispace. The standard document format is kind of stripped down markdown format called gemtext (Gemini’s HTML equivalent). To surf the geminispace, you need a Gemini client (equivalent of a web browser). After trying a few options such as deedum , I found the Lagrange client, an amazing piece of software written by Jaakko Keränen @skyjake who works for Nokia. The client works on all platforms (mobile and desktop) and is a real pleasure to use.
There are no big corporations on Gemini. Lagrange comes with a bookmark to a “ Getting started ” page which lists some search engines like keneddy which I understand runs entirely on one guy’s mac mini including the crawler.
After exploring the geminispace a little, I wanted to have a go at implementing my own server. It may not be the ideal language to implement a server, but I’m doing an increasing amount of python development so it seemed like a fun project to use it on. The rest of this post follows a similar step by step process that I went through to implement a Gemini server in python trying to use minimal external dependencies.
The first thing to do was to create a TCP socket to listen on the Gemini port (which is 1965, the year of the Gemini 5 rocket launch). To do this we do
These are quite low level APIs that wrap OS system calls, let’s explain some some of them.
We bind the socket to 0.0.0.0 which is a special address to indicate we want to listen on all network interfaces. You could also use 127.0.0.1 , but this causes problems when running inside a docker container for example.
If you run the code outlined above, you can test out your server by using a TCP client. I recommend either using telnet or nc as it is likely that you already have them installed. Run the python script and then in another terminal window one of these.
If all is working properly, you should see hello printed.
Currently, we’re only returning hello from our socket server. In order to return a valid Gemini response , We need to return something like
A valid Gemini request, always consists of only an absolute URL which cannot exceed 1024 bytes of data. We can read 1024 bytes from the connection object. Let’s return Hello if the path is /hello and /goodbye if the path is /goodbye . We can send a 51 “Not found” for any other case.
At this point if you re run your test with your TCP client, you should be able to send a URL and observe different responses depending on the path.
So far, we are sending unencrypted data over our socket (similar to plain HTTP requests). Gemini mandates the use of TLS, so for a Gemini client to understand our request we need to encrypt the data with a TLS certificate.
Unlike on the web, which pretty much mandates that server certificates be issued by a specific set of certificate authorities (CAs), it is quite common in Gemini to use self signed certificates. Gemini operates a “Trust on first use” (TOFU) policy for TLS. This works similar to SSH connections where the first time you connect to a host, your client associates it’s certificate with that host. If the certificate changes for subsequent requests, you will get a TLS error (or warning at least) that the server’s identity has changed.
Let’s generate a self signed certificate to identify our server. To do this we’ll use the openssl tool which is also likely already installed on your system.
This will generate a self signed certificate.pem and key.pem file which we can use to identify our server to Gemini clients. Using the ssl module, create a context and load the certificate and key files generated by the previous script. The ssl lib allows you to wrap an unencrypted TLS socket so that you can use it in the same way but encrypted. Change your current code to use the wrapped tls_connection .
Success 🎉, you should now have a server that a real Gemini client will understand. You should be able to point lagrange (or any other Gemini client) at gemini://localhost/hello and get a page with a Hello heading returned.
What we’ve done so far in enough to serve static pages, however there will come a time where you’ll want to accept user input. To indicate that input is required, the server needs to return status 10 which tells the client to prompt the user for input.
This is a lot more basic than what you’re probably used to with HTML forms and HTTP post. You get a single prompt which is then sent to the same URI as the entire query string once the user fills it in. You cannot send multiple query parameters or provide different input types, the user gets a text box with a single field, that’s it.
Let’s add another route to echo back what the user input
We can now accept user input from the user, but how do we know which user it came from? In HTTP world there are many ways to do this, basic auth, oauth2 are common but another way is mutual TLS (mTLS). In this scenario, both the server and client present there own TLS certificates. The server can then identify the client based on its certificate.
mTLS is quite commonly used in enterprise applications for machine to machine communication, but not very common for end user applications due to to the fact that generating, maintaining and instructing the browser to use a client TLS certificate is quite complicated and cumbersome for the average user. Certificates expire, the server needs to agree to trust them, etc.
Unlike with HTTP, where TLS was bolted on later with HTTPS, TLS is native to the Gemini protocol. There is a special set of status codes (6X) around client certificates. If a server sends status code 60, it means that the client must provide a client certificate to access this page. As a result, creating and managing client certificates is encouraged to be supported by Gemini clients (the browsers). Lagrange handles this very well. When a server responds with status 60, the user gets prompted to either use a certificate they created previously, or to create a new certificate with a friendly interface that hides away the complexities of TLS. Once the certificate is created, the page can reload, this time using mTLS with the client supplying the newly created certificate.
Gemini uses TLS in a more simplified way to HTTPS which is not without security trade offs and criticism , but does provide much improved security over unencrypted connections. TLS is used as an asymmetric (public/private key) encryption protocol it is common place in Gemini
These 2 points are where things get difficult with the standard library SSL python module.
The problem is (as far as I could tell) that the ssl module requires the server to be configured to trust the client’s certificate authority upfront before it serves the request. In enterprise / corporate networks this is generally OK as there would likely be conversations upfront to configure the certificate before it was used. This is not practical for a public website (or capsule). With the python ssl module, a certificate generated by an unknown CA will be rejected before we can trust it. This is what led me to use the pyOpenSSL library.
The key difference is that it allows you to configure ssl to accept client certificates and override the certificate verification to supply your own implementation via the set_verify method. By always returning True we can move certificate verification and reading logic up into the Gemini protocol specific code.
In order to resume TLS sessions with client certificates, we also need to set the session id context otherwise one the first request will work and subsequent requests will be rejected .
Then later in our “protected route” we can get the certificate and use its information to lookup the user in the existing records or to create a new user.
The fingerprint in the code above essentially acts as a unique identifier for the certificate. You can create a user and identify them with this value. The common_name is a more friendly name which clients will prompt the user for on creation. You can use this like a user name that is displayed but not to identify them.
Gemini uses status code 60 to indicate to clients that this resource requires a client certificate. In our protected route, if no peer can be found from get_peer_certificate() we need to return the 60 status code which tells the client that it needs to prompt the user to create or use an existing certificate.
Thankfully migrating to pyOpenSSL isn’t too difficult. Here’s a full example modified to use pyOpenSSL with client certificates, with a /hello-user route that responds with the certificates name and fingerprint.
What we’ve built so far is a single threaded synchronous server. This means that the server handles one request at a time and cannot accept new connections until the previous request has been dealt with. This works fine when testing on your machine, but will struggle once you have multiple users and your routes are handling more complicated logic and interacting with other systems like databases or third party services. There are several ways to deal with this problem.
The first 2 are parallelism solutions, the second is a concurrency solution. This article explains the subtleties between the 2 better than I can I strongly recommend it. As the article states, concurrency is probably the better choice for I/O bound applications like servers.
In python async/await is handled by the asyncio module. Amongst many other things, asyncio provides a function to start a TCP server using async connection handling . This will replace what we used the socket module for at the very start of this post. Coming from the JavaScript world where everything is async by default it may be a little frustrating that in order to use async await, you may need to rewrite or wrap your code. Going into this in detail perhaps deserves another post but in short pyOpenSSL doesn’t natively support async await so it was necessary to create some wrapper code to interact with it in a non blocking way.
After doing all of this we now have a working Gemini server. The next thing to do is to share it with the world! I wanted to stick to Gemini’s do it yourself kind of ethos and self host this. I found an old Raspberry Pi Model 3 B lying around. This model is from 2016 and has 1GB of RAM. I purchased a memory card and flashed Raspberry Pi OS lite onto it using the raspberry pi imager tool.
I had trouble getting wifi working on the pi, I think it’s something to do with 5GHz not being supported on this model but in the end I thought that a server is probably better wired so I plugged it into my router via ethernet.
Initially I thought of deploying using a docker image but I didn’t really want to rely on docker so I went with a simple systemd service that I deployed using scp and ssh.
I then did something that I haven’t done before, expose a port publicly on my router. I think I did this fairly safely, from the router user interface, I made a firewall rule for TCP port 1965 and routed traffic to that port to the pi and gave it a static IP. There we go I had joined the Geminispace!
What I made was a basic TODO application. I’m not sure it has much practical usage with all the fully featured todo list applications available, but it was a fun to make. You can visit it in a gemini client by going to gemini://todo.willmunn.xyz . The source code is available on codeberg .

title: Nigerian Players Watch: Osimhen, Orban, Onyedika shine as Nigerian stars deliver goals across Europe
body:
Nigerian footballers enjoyed a busy weekend across Europe, with several Super Eagles stars making decisive contributions for their clubs in domestic competitions.
Victor Osimhen and Gift Orban led the charge in Turkey, both finding the net. Orban also registered an assist in Amedspor’s emphatic victory over Eyüpspor, while Osimhen marked the birth of his second daughter with another goal for Galatasaray.
In Germany, Raphael Onyedika and Terem Moffi were both on target as Eintracht Frankfurt defeated Hamburger SV. Tolu Arokodare continued his scoring form in the Netherlands, while Taiwo Awoniyi opened his Premier League account for the season in Coventry City’s victory over Sunderland.
There were also important contributions from Friday Etim, Samuel Adeniran, Umar Sadiq and Josh Maja, while Kelechi Iheanacho saw his remarkable run of scoring in 12 consecutive league matches come to an end.
Osimhen had another memorable outing for Galatasaray, scoring in their commanding 4-0 away victory over Konyaspor in the Turkish Süper Lig.
The Nigerian striker opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a powerful header from a free-kick, setting Galatasaray on their way to an emphatic win.
The goal carried extra significance for the 27-year-old, who had welcomed his second daughter, Liora Audrey, with his partner, Stefanie Kim Ladewig, shortly before the fixture. Osimhen had remained in Istanbul for the birth before travelling to Konya on matchday.
He was withdrawn after an hour, having taken his league tally to nine goals, alongside three assists in eight appearances. He has now scored four times in his last three matches.
Orban was arguably one of the standout Nigerian performers of the weekend, combining a goal with an assist as Amedspor thrashed Eyüpspor 5-1.
The forward found the net in the 35th minute, finishing emphatically after being set up by Rayan Lutin. He then turned provider seven minutes later, supplying Samuel Ballet for Amedspor’s third goal of the afternoon.
Orban was substituted in the 78th minute, with Mohamed Khalil taking his place. The 24-year-old, who is on loan from Hoffenheim, has now scored nine league goals and registered four assists this season.
His latest contribution also places him level with Osimhen at the top of the Süper Lig scoring chart.
Trabzonspor extended their winning run to five consecutive league matches with a 2-0 victory over Gaziantep FK, with both Nigerian players involved.
Nwaiwu delivered another full shift in defence, helping his side secure a clean sheet. The 23-year-old has now featured in every one of Trabzonspor’s league matches this season, underlining his growing importance to the team.
Onuachu, meanwhile, returned to the starting line-up after missing three matches with a muscle injury sustained during the Conference League victory over KuPS on 15th October.
The striker was unable to get on the scoresheet and was replaced by Umut Nayir in the 63rd minute. His return was nevertheless encouraging for Trabzonspor, with coach Thomas Reis previously expressing uncertainty over whether the Nigerian could manage the full 90 minutes.
Onuachu has scored twice this season, both goals coming against Gençlerbirliği in September.
Iheanacho’s remarkable scoring streak finally came to an end as Bursaspor defeated Bandırmaspor 3-0 in the Turkish 1. Lig.
The former Leicester City forward played the entire match but could not find the net, bringing an end to his run of scoring in 12 consecutive league appearances.
Halil Akbunar opened the scoring in the seventh minute before Lewis Baker struck twice in the 12th and 23rd minutes to put Bursaspor firmly in control.
Iheanacho’s Nigerian compatriot, Olanrewaju Kehinde, started for Bandırmaspor but was booked in the second minute and substituted in the 59th minute.
Despite failing to extend his scoring run, Iheanacho remains the championship’s leading scorer with 16 goals and three assists. Bursaspor sit top of the table with 31 points.
Victor Osimhen and Orban’s compatriots were not the only Nigerians in action in Turkey. Chidozie Awaziem played the full match for Konyaspor in their defeat to Galatasaray.
Onyedika marked an important milestone by scoring his first goal for Eintracht Frankfurt since joining the Bundesliga side from Club Brugge in the summer.
The midfielder struck in the 47th minute as Frankfurt defeated Hamburger SV 3-1, restoring his side’s advantage after Terem Moffi had equalised for the visitors.
Celebration for Onyedika [Credit: Eintracht Frankfurt Facebook Page] Frankfurt had taken the lead in the 10th minute when Warmed Omari inadvertently turned the ball into his own net. Moffi responded four minutes later, finishing from close range after Albert Grønbæk picked him out.
Onyedika then reacted quickest after goalkeeper Daniel Heuer Fernandes parried Lilian Brassier’s header from a corner, firing Frankfurt back in front. Younes Ebnoutalib added the third in the 69th minute to seal the victory.
Moffi continued his encouraging start at Hamburg with another goal against his former Club Brugge teammate’s new side.
The striker was alert to Albert Grønbæk’s pass in the 14th minute, finishing from close range to bring Hamburg level after Omari’s own goal.
Although his effort was not enough to prevent defeat, it was another positive contribution from the Nigerian forward, who had also scored a late consolation when Hamburg lost 3-1 to Frankfurt in the DFB-Pokal on 27 October.
Boniface was introduced in the 83rd minute but could not help Bayer Leverkusen avoid a 4-2 home defeat to Stuttgart.
Ermedin Demirović scored twice for the visitors, while Jamie Leweling and Bilal El Khannouss also found the net. Patrik Schick and Ibrahim Maza scored for Leverkusen.
The defeat was Leverkusen’s first home loss in the Bundesliga this season, leaving them with 13 points from eight matches. Nathan Tella missed the encounter because of a fitness issue.
Arokodare continued his impressive scoring run, netting the only goal as Ajax secured a 1-0 victory over AZ Alkmaar.
The Nigerian striker rose above Mees de Wit in the ninth minute to head home Abdellah Ouazane’s delivery, giving Ajax an early advantage that they managed to protect until the final whistle.
Ajax had to withstand pressure from their visitors, particularly late in the game, when goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen produced an important save to deny Mexx Meerdink.
The victory ended Ajax’s long winless run against AZ and lifted them to second place, one point behind league leaders Feyenoord. Arokodare has now scored in three consecutive matches.
Awoniyi ended his goal drought in the Premier League by scoring in Coventry City’s 3-1 victory over Sunderland at the Coventry Building Society Arena.
The Nigerian striker doubled Coventry’s advantage in the 37th minute after dispossessing Luke O’Nien before beating goalkeeper Robin Roefs with a composed finish.
Tatsuhiro Sakamoto had opened the scoring in the 17th minute, while Jack Rudoni extended the lead shortly after half-time. Enzo Le Fée converted a penalty in the 67th minute to pull one back for Sunderland, before Omar Alderete was sent off in the 99th minute.
Awoniyi was substituted in the 72nd minute after making a significant contribution to the victory. It was his first Premier League goal of the campaign, having previously scored once in the EFL Cup.
Frank Onyeka was not included in Coventry’s matchday squad.
Iwobi and Bassey both started as Fulham fought back to earn a 1-1 draw away to Aston Villa.
Villa had an opportunity to take an early lead when John McGinn struck the woodwork from the penalty spot in the 15th minute. Nicolas Jackson eventually put the hosts ahead before half-time.
Fulham restored parity in the 64th minute when Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki turned the ball into his own net following an attacking delivery from the visitors.
Iwobi was replaced by Tom Cairney in the 75th minute, while Bassey completed the full match. Both Nigerians recorded their ninth league appearances of the season.
Ajayi played the full 90 minutes as Hull City shared the points in a 2-2 draw against Ipswich Town.
Hull trailed at half-time but fought back with two goals after the break to take the lead. Julio Enciso eventually rescued a point for Ipswich with a long-range effort.
The Nigerian defender produced a busy performance, recording six clearances, two tackles and one interception. He was also booked in the 88th minute.
The result extended Hull’s winless run in the league to seven matches.
Aina started for Nottingham Forest but was withdrawn at half-time as they suffered a 2-0 defeat away to Brentford.
Forest fell behind in the 30th minute when Nikola Milenković turned Dango Ouattara’s cross into his own net. Igor Thiago doubled Brentford’s advantage in the 76th minute after another effort took a deflection off Milenković.
Aina made way for Daniel Muñoz at the interval, while Ryan Yates was also introduced for Xaver Schlager.
The full-back has featured in only one of Forest’s last three league matches. Forest have six points from nine games and face Manchester City in their next fixture.
Sadiq made an impressive return from injury, scoring the decisive goal as Valencia defeated Elche 1-0 away from home.
The Nigerian striker came off the bench in the 60th minute and found the net eight minutes later to secure all three points for Valencia.
It was a timely contribution from the forward, who had been sidelined for seven weeks. His return and match-winning goal will be an encouraging development for Valencia as they look to build momentum in La Liga.
Lookman made a late appearance as Atlético Madrid continued their strong league form with a 2-0 away victory over Alavés.
The Nigerian international came off the bench and featured for approximately 15 minutes as Atlético extended their unbeaten run.
Lookman has found goals harder to come by in the league this season, but his involvement gives him another opportunity to build rhythm as Atlético prepare for their next fixtures.
Dele-Bashiru came off the bench in the 55th minute as Lazio recovered from behind to defeat Cagliari 2-1.
M’Bala Nzola put Cagliari ahead in the 21st minute before Gustav Isaksen equalised for Lazio 15 minutes later.
The Nigerian midfielder was involved in an appeal for a penalty around the hour mark after contact with Cagliari defender Rodríguez, but referee Andrea Colombo waved play on.
Lazio eventually secured the victory through Andrea Pinamonti’s 83rd-minute header.
Maja was among the goals again, but his early strike could not prevent Le Havre from suffering a heavy 5-1 defeat against Paris Saint-Germain.
The Nigerian forward gave Le Havre the lead in the 18th minute, finishing from close range after a delivery from Rayan Fofana.
PSG responded emphatically, with Achraf Hakimi scoring a hat-trick while Mika Godts and Senny Mayulu also found the net.
The goal was Maja’s fourth in Ligue 1 this season and his third in two appearances, following his brace in the 4-3 defeat against Marseille five days earlier.
Despite the disappointing result, Maja took encouragement from his side’s start to the contest, admitting afterwards that the team were disappointed but would try to take positives from the experience.
Etim played a part in Midtjylland’s remarkable comeback from two goals down to defeat Nordsjælland 3-2 away from home.
The hosts had taken a two-goal lead through Justin Janssen and Ibrahim Adel before Midtjylland began their response after the break.
Etim’s effort struck the post before rebounding into the net off goalkeeper Tobias Salquist for an own goal in the 66th minute. Kjell Wätjen drew Midtjylland level in the 74th minute, before Sofus Johannesen completed the comeback with a stoppage-time winner.
Etim was substituted in the 86th minute for Mikael Uhre. The victory was Midtjylland’s first in Farum in more than six years and kept them unbeaten after 13 league matches.
Adeniran supplied an important assist as LASK came from behind to defeat WSG Tirol 2-1.
Moritz Wels gave the visitors the lead in the 16th minute, but Alessandro Schöpf restored parity seven minutes later.
Adeniran then produced the decisive contribution shortly after the restart, driving down the flank before delivering the ball across the area for Robert Ljubičić to finish in the 48th minute.
Usor entered the game in the 68th minute as LASK held on for a valuable victory following their defeat to Red Bull Salzburg the previous week.
Dessers started for Panathinaikos as they secured a 2-0 victory over AEK Athens in the Greek Super League.
Tetteh gave the hosts an early lead shortly after kick-off, while Andino doubled their advantage early in the second half.
The Nigerian striker was replaced by Vicente Taborda in the 57th minute as Panathinaikos completed an important victory in the ninth round of the league season.
Fernandez started in defence as Rangers defeated Aberdeen 1-0 at Hampden Park to book their place in the Premier Sports Cup final.
Ryan Naderi scored the decisive goal with nine minutes remaining, converting James Penrice’s delivery to send Rangers through.
Fernandez was substituted in the 87th minute, with Rangers now set to face the winners of the Edinburgh derby in next month’s final.
Durosinmi played the full match but could not prevent Genk from suffering a narrow 1-0 defeat away to Mechelen in the Belgian Pro League.
Simion Michez scored the only goal early in the contest, and Genk were unable to find a response despite making attacking changes in the second half.
Osimhen and Orban were the headline performers in Turkey, with both forwards reaching nine league goals. Onyedika and Moffi also shared the spotlight in Germany, while Arokodare and Awoniyi delivered important goals for Ajax and Coventry respectively.
Maja continued his productive spell in France despite Le Havre’s heavy defeat, while Sadiq made the most of his return from injury by scoring Valencia’s winner.
For Iheanacho, however, the weekend brought an end to a remarkable personal run. His 12-match scoring streak may have stopped, but his 16 league goals and three assists remain a major return as Bursaspor continue their push at the top of the Turkish second tier.

title: Trust and collaboration are key to preventing violent extremism – NPC Chairman
body: The Chairman of the National Peace Council, Most Rev. Emmanuel Kofi Fianu, has called for a united national effort involving security agencies, traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations, families and local communities to prevent violent extremism. He said sustainable peace and security could not be achieved through enforcement measures alone, stressing the need to address the social and economic conditions that make communities vulnerable to extremist influences. Speaking at the National Dialogue on Civil-Security Engagement in Preventing Violent Extremism in Accra last week, Most Rev. Fianu highlighted inclusive governance, job opportunities for young people, community trust and effective early warning systems as essential elements of prevention. He also underscored the importance of building stronger relationships between civilians and security personnel, noting that cooperation and confidence between the two groups could help communities identify and respond to potential threats before they escalate. The National Peace Council has been working with Catholic Relief Services (CRS Ghana), with support from the Government of the Netherlands since 2023, to promote trust and collaboration between communities and security actors. The dialogue was organised under the Prevention of Violent Extremism Through Social Accountability (PoVETSA) Project, implemented by CRS with funding from the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Most Rev. Fianu also appealed to parties involved in the Bawku conflict and other disputes to pursue peaceful and democratic means of resolving their differences, emphasising that lasting peace requires commitment and collective responsibility from all sections of society.

title: Zelensky says he's ready to meet Putin in Turkey
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky voiced readiness to meet with Russia's President Vladimir Putin in Turkey to discuss peace talks, in an interview with CNN Turk published on Nov. 1.
A meeting between the leaders is essential, said Zelensky , adding that Turkey can be a practical and realistic mediator of future talks between Moscow and Kyiv.
The comments come ahead of expected technical-level talks between Ukraine, Russia, and the U.S. in Abu Dhabi later in November.
Kyiv hopes the discussions could pave the way for an eventual leaders' summit — likely involving U.S. President Donald Trump — which it sees as crucial for resolving territorial issues.
The Kremlin has long avoided a face-to-face meeting between Zelensky and Putin, proposing a phone call instead, the Kyiv Independent has learned.
Ukraine's president met with Recep Tayyip Erdogan , his Turkish counterpart, in Istanbul on Oct. 31 to discuss bilateral relations and security in the Black Sea.
Turkey has carefully balanced its relationship with both Kyiv and Moscow, maintaining economic ties with Russia while providing arms to Ukraine.
Ankara played a central role in establishing the Black Sea Grain Initiative in 2022, enabling the safe maritime export of grain before Moscow exited the deal a year later. Turkey has also hosted three rounds of peace talks between Ukrainian and Russian delegations in 2025.
Zelensky's comments come amid Washington's efforts to revive peace talks, which have effectively stalled earlier this year as Russia demands that Kyiv cede Donbas, a partially occupied and strategically important region in Ukraine's east.
In the interview, Zelensky said the upcoming technical talks would focus on the possibility of a partial energy and maritime ceasefire, as well as exchanges of captives.
The leaders' summit would then tackle a path toward a full ceasefire and security guarantees, he said.
The president rejected the possibility of formally recognizing occupied territories as part of Russia and said a ceasefire should be established along the current front lines as a first step toward further talks.

title: Dino Melaye throws Quranic citation challenge at Tinubu
body: Former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to a Quranic citation contest following the President’s recent pilgrimage to Saudi Arabia. Melaye issued the challenge in a post on his X handle on Monday, saying he was ready to compete with Tinubu in citing verses from the Quran after his return to Nigeria. He wrote, “Now that Alhaji Bola Tinubu is in Umrah. Immediately he comes back, I challenge him to a Quranic citation competition with me. No one can mock God, SDM.” The challenge comes after Tinubu’s spiritual visit to Saudi Arabia, where he performed Umrah, the lesser Hajj, and was granted access to enter the Holy Kaaba alongside members of his delegation. In a statement on Monday by Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to the President on Information & Strategy, Tinubu said he prayed for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians while reaffirming his commitment to national development and prosperity. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that prayer has been granted. Before the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then, and He did. And I promised that I would come back to thank Him,” the statement quoted Tinubu. Tinubu also expressed gratitude to Saudi Arabia’s King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for granting him and members of his delegation the rare privilege of praying inside the Holy Kaaba. Tinubu, reflecting on Surah Aal-Imran, Verse 26 of the Holy Quran, said all power and authority belonged to Almighty Allah, who could grant leadership to anyone and take it away at will. “There is no other God but Almighty Allah. He is the giver and the taker. He owns power and authority. He says, ‘If I give you, use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person. I am the only One who has that authority,” he said. He also reaffirmed his commitment to national development, declaring, “My commitment to Project Nigeria is higher. I am determined to usher in prosperity and fully develop the country, consistent with the wish of Allah and the support of the people.” On the economy, Tinubu expressed optimism about the country’s progress, saying, “The foundation is solid, and the economy has come out of the dark tunnel. This is inspiring.” He also stressed the need to invest in young Nigerians, adding, “We need to build a future for our youth. If we don’t invest in their future, how do we want to be remembered as leaders 50 years from now? The post Dino Melaye throws Quranic citation challenge at Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ghana’s galamsey crisis: The tragedy of the commons, market failure and the economics of environmental destruction
body: Why Ghana must move beyond enforcement to correct the economic incentives driving illegal mining. Ghana’s illegal gold mining crisis, popularly known as galamsey, is often treated primarily as an environmental or law-enforcement problem. Yet its persistence reveals a deeper economic failure: those extracting gold capture much of the income, while communities and taxpayers bear much of the cost. Effective policy must therefore go beyond disrupting mining sites to changing the incentives that make environmental destruction profitable. The Tragedy of the Commons In 1968, Garrett Hardin popularised the concept of the tragedy of the commons: individually rational exploitation can collectively degrade resources on which everyone depends. Ghana’s rivers and watersheds illustrate the problem. A miner operating along the Pra River earns income from gold, but downstream households, farmers and water utilities bear the consequences of sedimentation and pollution. The miner benefits from additional extraction without fully paying for the resulting damage. Multiplied across many operators, private gains can produce collective losses. Nevertheless, as Nobel laureate Elinor Ostrom demonstrated, shared resources need not be destroyed: effective rules, community participation and credible monitoring can sustain them. Ghana’s challenge is therefore as much institutional as environmental. Private Profits, Public Costs Economists describe costs imposed on others but excluded from private decisions as negative externalities. Mining equipment, fuel and labour appear in an operator’s accounts; polluted drinking water, damaged cocoa farms and future restoration costs often do not. This divergence can make environmentally destructive mining privately profitable even when its overall contribution to national welfare is negative. A 2024 peer-reviewed study of selected Ghanaian farming communities found that 38% of surveyed farmers reported mining-related land degradation, while 79% of affected farmers reported that degraded areas had not been reclaimed. These are local findings, not national estimates, but they illustrate the erosion of productive assets. In October 2026, the Government announced GH¢200 million for reclaiming 5,000 acres of mining-degraded land from 2027. Environmental restoration is essential. But why should taxpayers routinely pay to repair damage while private operators and financiers retain the proceeds? When profits are privatised and environmental costs socialised, the country may record gold income while losing natural capital. Public restoration expenditure also diverts scarce resources from other development priorities, including healthcare, education and productive infrastructure. Why Enforcement Alone Falls Short Arrests, excavator seizures and military operations remain necessary, particularly in protected forests and waterways. But illegal mining can persist when expected profits exceed production costs and the perceived risk of meaningful punishment. Enforcement targeted only at workers on mining sites also misses financiers, gold buyers and commercial intermediaries. Success should therefore be judged not solely by arrests or confiscations, but by cleaner rivers, restored farmland and a sustained decline in destructive mining. Credible sanctions and enforceable rehabilitation liabilities must complement enforcement. GoldBod: Turning Traceability into Economic Incentives The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) offers an opportunity to influence mining behaviour through market access. GoldBod already has a responsible-sourcing policy covering environmental compliance, pollution controls and supplier due diligence. In August 2026, its Chief Executive Officer acknowledged that GoldBod could not yet establish what share of its purchases was responsibly mined, while announcing plans for a national gold-traceability system. The real policy test is not whether GoldBod can identify where gold originated, but whether it can verify how that gold was produced. GoldBod and its authorised buyers should purchase only from licensed mining operations whose environmental compliance has been independently verified. A licence alone is insufficient. Mine-level records should link each gold lot to its source, environmental permits, pollution-control performance and rehabilitation obligations. Serious violations should trigger suspension from authorised purchasing channels, subject to fair verification and review. To prevent legally sourced gold from becoming a cover for illegally mined supplies, transactions should be cross-checked against plausible mine production and independently audited. Public reporting should disclose the proportion of GoldBod purchases traceable to environmentally compliant sources. Controls against smuggling and illicit buyers must accompany these measures. This approach would reward responsible miners with formal market access while raising the commercial cost of pollution. Alongside accessible licensing, cleaner technologies and viable rural livelihoods, it would distinguish legitimate small-scale mining from destructive illegality. Conclusion Galamsey is simultaneously a tragedy of the commons, a negative-externality problem and a test of economic governance. Ghana must protect waterways through enforcement, make polluters pay for restoration and ensure that public gold purchasing does not reward environmental destruction. A nation does not become wealthier merely by extracting more gold. It becomes wealthier when the benefits of extraction exceed the full costs imposed on its people, productive land and future generations. *** The author, Nana Eghan, PhD is an agricultural economist and private citizen who is a resident of Adenta, Greater Accra. He can be reached via nanaeghan@gmail.com

title: N. Bahr El Ghazal approves $80,000 health budget for elections
body: The Northern Bahr El Ghazal State Council of Ministers on Friday passed a budget for health interventions during upcoming general elections, health officials said. Riiny Riiny, the state’s caretaker health minister, told Radio Tamazuj over the weekend that he submitted the proposal to the council of ministers, which passed it on Friday. “I submitted the proposed budget to the state council of ministers because elections attract many gatherings of voters, and we know that period will be summer with a lot of diseases that need health interventions,” he said. “The Council of Ministers successfully passed the USD 88,000 budget. The governor, minister of finance and I will have a closed meeting to mobilize the budget at the state level, and a portion may be covered by the central government in Juba.” Ayai Deng, an inhabitant of Awiel Town, warmly welcomed the initiative and commended the government for stepping up health precautions and measures ahead of the polls. “It is a positive idea from the state government to pass the health budget because health problems easily happen if medical personnel are not employed to address illnesses,” he stated. Meanwhile, Peter Diing Ngong, the Information Secretary for Northern Bahr El Ghazal State Civil Society Network, said peace, security and health are very important elements during elections. “ Peace, security and health-related interventions are very important during the elections,” he said. “We need peace to prevail in the state before the elections.” The post N. Bahr El Ghazal approves $80,000 health budget for elections appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Almaty Museum Opens Exhibition About Mountaineering Legends
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – The Museum of Almaty has opened “Peaks Reaching for the Sky,” an exhibition on the history of mountaineering in Kazakhstan from the 1930s to the present day. Photo credit: Aleksandr Pavsky / Kazinform. Visitors can learn how mountain camps helped train generations of athletes and explore the life stories of the climbers who shaped the sport. The display brings together archival photographs, documents, personal belongings, and the equipment climbers carried to the summits. It traces how mountaineering took root in Kazakhstan, from the first ascents and landmark expeditions to the achievements of today’s athletes, reported Kazinform news agency. From the first ascents to today’s climbers One of the key milestones in the history of Kazakh mountaineering came on July 17, 1930. That day, Ivan Mysovsky, Vladimir Gorbunov, and Alexander Berggrin, led by Grigory Beloglazov, made the first organized ascent of the mountains around Almaty. In the years that followed, climbing clubs began to appear in the city. In 1935, around 250 climbers from across the country gathered in Almaty and climbed the surrounding peaks, including Talgar Peak. A separate part of the exhibition is devoted to World War II. A school near Gorelnik trained instructors for the Soviet Union’s mountain rifle units, and around 15,000 service members passed through it. Photo credit: Aleksandr Pavsky / Kazinform. The stands also display archival photographs of expedition members, materials on how climbers prepared for their ascents, and the stories behind famous summits, including Khan Tengri, the best-known peak in Kazakhstan. The exhibition pays tribute to the climbers who built the reputation of the Kazakh school. Among them are Kazbek Valiev, Valery Shevtsov, renowned coach and expedition leader Ervand Ilyinsky, and Maksut Zhumayev, who has climbed all 14 of the world’s 8,000-meter peaks. It also honors the legendary Anatoli Boukreev, who held the Snow Leopard title, and Denis Urubko, who also summited all 14 eight-thousanders. A separate section of the exhibition is dedicated to women climbers and their contribution to the sport. Kazbek Valiev, one of Kazakhstan’s best-known climbers and the first Kazakh to summit Everest, attended the opening. “I want to congratulate everyone on the opening of the mountaineering department of the Museum of Almaty. I think it is well deserved, because the history of mountaineering in Kazakhstan is vast. Most of its achievements are tied to Almaty climbers. The Almaty Mountaineering Federation is doing a lot to popularize the sport among city residents,” he said. Lyazzat Sagyndikova, director of the Association of Almaty Museums, said the exhibition is meant not only to tell the history of the sport but also to show the contribution of people who devoted their lives to the mountains. She added that their stories “inspire the younger generation to strive for new heights.” The exhibition is open from Oct. 28 through the end of November 2026. The post Almaty Museum Opens Exhibition About Mountaineering Legends appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Ghana must not confuse access to AI tools with readiness for AI-powered education – KNUST AI coordinator
body: The Coordinator of AI Courses at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Prof. Eric Appau Asante, has called for practical national and institutional guidelines to regulate the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education, warning that access to the technology alone does not guarantee its effective integration into teaching and learning. He said clear guidelines were needed to ensure that AI was adopted responsibly and ethically, rather than allowing poorly regulated technologies to become embedded in educational practices without adequate consideration of their impact. Speaking on the topic of AI in Teacher Education: Navigating Innovation and Implementation at the 17th congregation of Wesley College of Education, Prof. Appau Asante said teachers must develop the competence to use AI while maintaining the professional judgement required to guide the learning process. He explained that the changing educational landscape required teachers to move beyond conventional teaching methods and incorporate artificial intelligence into curriculum development, lesson preparation and classroom instruction. He stressed, however, that being familiar with AI tools was not enough, insisting that teachers must understand the ethical responsibilities that come with using the technology. “…the teacher of today’s world must be knowledgeable in the use of artificial intelligence, and our word is not just knowledgeable but rather they must be responsible in the use of the AI, and they must be guided by ethics,” he said. Prof. Appau Asante cautioned against excessive reliance on AI, saying teachers must not allow the technology to undermine their wisdom, critical thinking and professional judgement. He noted that while AI could improve teaching efficiency, reduce errors and help educators align their practices with international standards, its benefits depended on how effectively it was used. “AI is just one of the tools and if you use it effectively it enhances your work, you grow less error and you match up with international best practice,” he said. He warned that using AI indiscriminately without assessing the quality and accuracy of its outputs could compromise the benefits it offers to the education sector. The KNUST professor also raised concerns about the potential for AI integration to widen existing inequalities in education, particularly if well-resourced urban schools gained greater benefits from the technology than rural institutions with limited access to digital infrastructure and other resources. He said the adoption of AI must therefore be guided by measures that ensure its benefits are accessible across schools, rather than creating further disparities between institutions. Meanwhile, the Principal of Wesley College of Education, Dr Kennedy Ameyaw Baah, said the focus of AI training for teachers must shift from acquiring knowledge of the technology to applying it in practical teaching situations. He explained that implementation involved translating the knowledge gained through AI courses into classroom practice, while innovation required teachers to explore how the technology could help them develop lessons suited to the different learning needs of students. “When we talk of implementation, we’ve taught them what AI is about. They’ve taken a lot of courses in AI. As they are going on, how are they going to use AI in teaching? That is implementation,” he said. Dr Ameyaw Baah said teachers must also be able to use AI tools creatively to develop teaching materials and lessons that respond to the specific needs of their learners. He said educators were expected to develop sufficient command of the tools to ensure that their application of AI translated into meaningful benefits for students. “We expect them to leverage technology. We expect them to ensure that the AI tool that they are going to use, they have that command to use it to benefit the students or the learners,” he said.

title: Program
body:
In the 20th century we had radio and television programs ; a television executive at ABC could program Thursday nights as a comedy block; the television itself became the vessel for playing Video Computer System game programs in the 1970s. By the 1980s one could program their VCR to record television or even program their home computer on that same screen.
Programs have been ubiquitous your entire life. You heard them. You watched them. You played them. You may have even made them. And as broadcasting has given way to narrowcasting and analog signals have given way to digital software, programs are increasingly watching you and using that information to alter everything from prices to our perception of reality.
We have all noticed this but no one seems to know what to do about it. He have created a world where anyone can program media - including the programs themselves. While access has never been greater, literacy has never been lower. The vast majority of people havenât been taught even the most basic principles of this new media. We are ignorantly grazing in a field filled with danger - unable to understand the warnings so many have been shouting for decades.
The arrival of programmable interactive media led to a frenzied interest that crescendoed in the 1990s with the introduction of the DVD and the world wide web. By this point, the information age had become tangible in the everyday life of ordinary people. But people generally engaged new media like they did television: passively. But programmeable media is too powerful to tolerate passive consumption. Realizing this, a group of media theorists emerged to publish the Principles of Technorealism on March 12, 1998. The twelve original contributors were David Bennahum, Brooke Shelby Biggs, Paulina Borsook, Marisa Bowe, Simson Garfinkel, Steven Johnson, Douglas Rushkoff, Andrew Shapiro, David Shenk, Steve Silberman, Mark Stahlman and Stefanie Syman. The final document was based on the concept originated by Shapiro, Shenk and Johnson. They opined that âin a world driven by the flow of information, the interfaces â and the underlying code â that make information visible are becoming enormously powerful social force, [therefore] the creation of better tools should be an important part of being an involved citizen. These tools affect our lives as much as laws do, and we should subject them to a similar democratic scrutiny.â Or as Technorealist contributor Douglas Rushkoff summed it up, program or be programmed .
Rushkoff is not a computer programmer in any formal sense. He is a media theoretician. So while he laments the absence of ubiquitous computer programming education in US public schools, he is really talking about digital media more broadly.
Digital media takes the notion of âanalog programsâ as we saw them on television and turns them into flexible, programmable code. Today that often means code that drives capital intensive recommendation algorithms which now underpin the media ecosystem. If not as social media, then as the innocuous Google News app that defaults on your phone. If not as the Google News app, then as the digital newspaper that is constantly re-configuring itself based on engagement metrics As C. Thi Nguyen has said , âMetrics are technology that standardize attention.â from social media and the hundreds of advertising networks that fester in the ecosystem like flies on a decaying corpse. The Technorealists proposed to guard against this form of Surveillance Capitalism 16 years before the term was coined. Point 3 of the manifesto reads: âGovernment has an important role to play on the electronic frontier [â¦] it is foolish to say that the public has no sovereignty over what an errant citizen or fraudulent corporation does online. [â¦] Technology standards and privacy issues, for example, are too important to be entrusted to the marketplace alone. Competing software firms have little interest in preserving the open standards that are essential to a fully functioning interactive network. Markets encourage innovation, but they do not necessarily insure the public interest.â
The 225 partners of DW noyb recently filed a GDPR complaint against dict.cc due to their consent agreement featuring an astounding 1,741 partners. âFelix Mikolasch, data protection lawyer at noyb: âIt would take days or even weeks to properly read and understand the data protection policies of 1,741 companies. It is ridiculous to assume that this would allow for an informed decision.ââ by David Schmudde is licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0Â Â
The internet is truly a different type of media; digital interactivity facilitates the same physical reach to both the institutional power and the distributed peer. The interface to this media is a sophisticated language colloquially known as programming . The name programming elides its expressive power, which is somewhere between mathematics and natural language. And if you do not know how to speak it, the institutional powers will speak it for you.
Take the basic example of RSS/atom. I love RSS and use it to this day. The premise is simple: in a diverse information ecosystem, you can select feeds from major corporate news agencies, collectively funded information providers, and self-funded bloggers and they all get equal space in your reader. The feed is flexible; the sources inevitably change from year to year as you discover new things and get tired of old things. But this intellectual freedom comes at a cost - you must make choices. You must create the program. The alternative is an algorithmically defined news app that makes the program for you. And the organization controlling that program makes tiny, seemingly innocuous tweaks every week which can have profound consequences over time. For example, the person who added the infinite scroll to the Facebook timeline, Aza Raskin, now says he regrets it . It turns out that removing the ânext pageâ button is a great way to keep people on Facebook but not a great way to consciously use time. Or how about the time that Amazon paid the USA Federal Trade Commission $2.5 billion to settle a case built around what its own employees called the âIliad Flowâ - an Amazon Prime-cancellation process spread across four pages and fifteen options, where every button except one routed a user back to the start. Leaked internal documents showed that when Amazon simplified the flow, cancellations dropped 14 percent, so the company reversed course and kept the maze.
Digital mediaâs flexibility, reach, subtlety, and power demands our active engagement unique to any other preceding media.
The ability to speak the language of programming tended to favor white males - but not exclusively and not historically. When programming was less well-compensated and less highly regarded, it was a job for women. And as Prophets of Computing demonstrates, there have been a large number of local approaches to machine programming throughout Asia and Latin America.
But the current crop of programmers - the people who by definition control programmed media - does seem like more of a monoculture. A more egalitarian world is possible but we will not arrive there in a generation by putting iPads in classrooms. The Technorealists have understood this for decades. Again from the Technorealists: âWiring the schools will not save them. The problems with Americaâs public schools â disparate funding, social promotion, bloated class size, crumbling infrastructure, lack of standards â have almost nothing to do with technology. Consequently, no amount of technology will lead to the educational revolution prophesied by President Clinton and others. The art of teaching cannot be replicated by computers, the Net, or by âdistance learning.â These tools can, of course, augment an already high-quality educational experience. But to rely on them as any sort of panacea would be a costly mistake.â To the contrary, multiple studies have shown that tablets and laptops largely detract from the learning environment The Laptop and the Lecture: The Effects of Multitasking in Learning Environments (Hembrooke & Gay, 2003); Dividing Attention in the Classroom Reduces Exam Performance (Glass & Kang, 2019); Examining the impact of off-task multi-tasking with technology on real-time classroom learning (Wood et al., 2011); Donât Throw Away Your Printed Books: A Meta-Analysis on the Effects of Reading Media on Reading Comprehension (Delgato et al., 2018), etcâ¦ and tablets are a poor tool for teaching programming; they are designed primarily for media consumption.
LLMs are the latest consumer layer of digital media. At a minimum, they promise to become a metamedia Marshall McLuhan coined the term âmetamediaâ to describe the relationship between form and content, especially in the context of new technologies and new media. of our everyday lives. Much has been written about how LLMs will eliminate the entire field of programming - as if people will no longer need to know how to speak for themselves. Programming will still exist. But much will be obscured by a consumer veneer.
The language of programming is actually the language of systems. Self-trained hackers were aware of this language when they were hacking the telephone networks of the 1970s. And freshmen at MIT in the 1980s understood this after reading the Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs . Humans build systems. And systems contribute to our view of the world that we are born into. LLMs can provide a surface-level understanding of a system but only hands-on experience can provide knowledge.
You are constrained by any system that you cannot inspect. This is true of both designed and emergent systems such as cities, forests, and networks. The natural sciences, including informatics, The term informatics is often used interchangeably with computer science - where the latter focuses on either the theory of computation or the study of the physical computer. produces the notation we use to describe what we know about these systems. As long as there are systems and networks, there will be programming.
The physical computer is unique because it is the artificial embodiment of a natural science. The theoretical computer has no politics. But the physical computer is bound to the systems used to create it. The first point from the Technorealist manifesto: âTechnologies are not neutral. A great misconception of our time is the idea that technologies are completely free of bias â that because they are inanimate artifacts, they donât promote certain kinds of behaviors over others. In truth, technologies come loaded with both intended and unintended social, political, and economic leanings. Every tool provides its users with a particular manner of seeing the world and specific ways of interacting with others. It is important for each of us to consider the biases of various technologies and to seek out those that reflect our values and aspirations.â And those systems have historically been large, well-funded bureaucratic projects or globally scaled, highly-capitalized consumer products. So the end result of decades of effort to âdemocratize computingâ has produced an oligarchic class of unimaginable wealth and a consistent decade-over-decade decline in the share of any productivity gains created by the computer. âThe labor share â the percentage of economic output that accrues to workers as compensation in exchange for their labor â has been declining in the nonfarm business sector throughout most of the post-World War Two era [â¦] reaching a low of 56.0 percent in the fourth quarter of 2011.â ~ Labor share of output has declined since 1947 March 07, 2017 Or take the example of newspapers. The papers were revolutionized by productivity gains starting with the arrival of digital layout tools. The industry employed 458,000 people in June 1990 and declined to 367,200 in December 2005 while the revenues rose, profits remained strong, and the papers were a prized acquisition asset. Average employee pay did not benefit from the gains in efficiency. See also the wage calculator to see how your work has been systematically devalued since 1979.
So how do we fight back against these overwhelming odds? We program. Not as an offense into their territory. But as a defense of our territory - our mind.
Civilization is built on media. You cannot shelter your sons and daughters; you have already seen the impact on your friends and neighbors. It is past time to accept that in a programmable world of digital media, we can no longer blame the television executive or the media baron for their programs. We must support and participate in alternative systems. From food to computing - we must create and participate in systems that minimize cruelty as a bulwark against systems that maximize profit.
The lingua franca of these systems is software. This language is at least as important as the language you speak with your friends. Learning the language of systems - a.k.a programming - will be a mind-opening second or third language that you can use to manifest the world you want to see in everyday media.

title: Kremlin Downplays Prospect of Resuming Gas Shipments to Europe via Ukraine
body:
Russia is unlikely to resume natural gas deliveries to Europe via Ukrainian pipelines anytime soon, the Kremlin said Monday, downplaying reports that the option was being discussed as part of a proposed winter energy ceasefire.
The Wall Street Journal reported earlier that the Trump administration suggested the idea during talks in September as an incentive for Moscow to halt strikes on Ukraine’s energy grid. According to U.S. and European officials, advocates of the plan argued it would also allow Ukraine to collect transit fees while helping lower European heating costs.
Under the proposal, Russian gas would be sold through a U.S. intermediary to navigate European sanctions, with proceeds placed in an offshore escrow account to prevent Moscow from using the funds to finance its war effort.
“Frankly, the situation on the ground speaks all too clearly to the fact that those kinds of plans are impossible to implement right now,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters during a daily briefing. “But as for what the future holds, we’ll see.”
Peskov said any renewal of gas shipments through Ukraine would “depend on the willingness of buyers, the willingness of sellers and the capacity of sellers.”
He noted that, while the European energy market remains a “premium one,” countries in the Global South have demonstrated themselves as “centers of economic growth,” meaning that their consumption of oil and gas will only increase in the coming years, with Moscow poised to supply all of their energy needs.
Russian gas shipments to Europe by pipeline have largely stopped since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and Brussels has committed to ending all imports of Russian oil and gas by the end of 2027.
According to the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis, a U.S.-based think tank, the EU imported 6.9 billion cubic meters of Russian gas in the first three months of 2026, a 16% increase from the first quarter of last year and the highest volume since 2022.
Still, Russia now accounts for just 11% of Europe’s natural gas consumption, down from 45% on the eve of the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
