title: Royal Navy continues to track Russian naval vessels around UK supported by RAF Protector drone deployed for first time
body:
RN warships and helicopters conducted three operations during late September and October to monitor Russian naval and sanctions-linked shipping around the UK. The activity also saw the RAF’s new Protector RG1 remotely piloted aircraft (RPAS) used operationally in UK airspace for the first time, providing more than 10 hours of surveillance over the English Channel.
HMS Dauntless and patrol ship HMS Tyne were tasked between 1 and 14 October to monitor Russian Baltic Fleet frigate RFS Neustrashimy as she escorted sanctioned shipping through the English Channel. The frigate has spent much of the summer operating in the Channel and North Sea, apparently retained in the area specifically to protect Russian-linked merchant traffic.
Neustrashimy has repeatedly escorted vessels associated with Russia’s shadow fleet since the UK began taking more direct action against sanctions evasion. In July, she escorted tanker MV Vulkan through the Dover Strait and on 20 July conducted a 30-minute live-fire exercise about 74km (40nm) south of Plymouth, watched at close range by HMS Tyne. The RN says the need to provide naval escorts is forcing Moscow to divert warships from other duties. Neustrashimy continues to loiter in the southern North Sea, often drifting for short periods to save fuel.
The October operation was supported by the RAF’s Protector RG1, which flew its first operational sorties in UK airspace. The MQ-9B-derived aircraft provided more than ten hours of persistent intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance support while working alongside RN ships and helicopters. Based at RAF Waddington, Protector has an endurance of more than 40 hours and, unlike its Reaper predecessor, is certified to operate routinely alongside other aircraft in controlled civilian airspace.
Further north, Merlin Mk2 helicopters deployed at short notice from RNAS Culdrose to Prestwick tracked Russian AGI Viktor Leonov in waters west of Scotland between 29 September and 8 October. The Vishnya-class vessel was operating around the Outer Hebrides while NATO forces were conducting Exercise Strike Warrior, involving more than 2,000 personnel from six nations.
This confirms that Operation Iceblast had real-world surveillance components alongside its previously announced training tasks. Four Merlin Mk2s and around 90 personnel were deployed to Prestwick during the exercise.
HMS Tyne was called into action again between 11 and 14 October, sailing from North Shields to intercept the Ropucha-class landing ship RFN Aleksandr Shabalin. The Russian warship was escorting cargo ship MV Energy-2 and tug Proton towards the Baltic, with a Wildcat from 815 Naval Air Squadron providing additional surveillance.
The tempo of these operations has been rising steadily. RN activity monitoring Russian movements increased by 25% during the first seven months of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025. In the 2025-26 financial year RN vessels were activated 116 times under Operation ADDISON, monitoring 61 Russian warships and 28 merchant vessels around UK waters.
The tougher posture follows the boarding and detention of shadow fleet tanker MV Smyrtos by Royal Marines and National Crime Agency officers in June. Other sanctioned vessels do not necessarily present the same opportunity for boarding, but the operation appears to have increased the cost to Moscow of moving sanctioned cargo through the Channel, including the diversion of scarce warships to provide escorts.
Four months after her seizure, the Smyrtos is still at anchor off Portland with around 100,000 tonnes of crude oil aboard, potentially exposed to winter storms if not moved soon. Leaving the ship to swing at anchor for so long suggests there was no considered plan for disposing of the cargo or dealing with the vessel after its seizure. Although the operation demonstrated Britain’s willingness to take direct action against Russia’s shadow fleet, the unresolved fate of Smyrtos exposes the practical and legal difficulties of enforcing sanctions at sea.

title: Five transport unions threaten nationwide shutdown over trading activities at bus stops
body: Commercial transport services across Ghana could be disrupted on Wednesday, November 4, after five transport unions announced plans to withdraw their services in protest against trading at designated bus stops and on pedestrian walkways. The unions, led by the Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) of TUC, say the planned action follows the government’s failure to enforce regulations restricting commercial activities at transport terminals. They are demanding the enforcement of Regulation 142 of Legislative Instrument (L.I.) 2519, arguing that the continued occupation of bus stops by traders is making it difficult for commercial drivers to operate. The unions also contend that drivers are being unfairly penalised for traffic violations, particularly through the government’s TraffiTech-GH monitoring system, while trading activities at bus stops and pedestrian walkways remain unchecked. As part of the protest, commercial drivers have been directed to park their vehicles on Wednesday, November 4, and stay off the roads until further notice. The unions say the decision follows unsuccessful attempts to get the relevant authorities to address their concerns. They have apologised to commuters and the general public for the inconvenience the withdrawal of services could cause. The action is being jointly organised by five groups: the GPRTU of TUC, Commercial Transport Operators of Ghana, True Drivers Union, Ghana Committed Drivers Association and Concerned Drivers Association of Ghana. The planned shutdown could affect thousands of commuters who depend on commercial transport for their daily journeys, including workers, traders and students. Passengers are therefore being urged to make alternative travel arrangements ahead of the proposed industrial action.

title: Iran ready for talks with all parties, determined to defend national security — official
body:
BEIJING, November 2. /TASS/. Tehran will resolutely defend national sovereignty and security while remaining ready to hold talks with all parties, Iranian National Security Council Deputy Secretary Ali Bagheri Kani said at a meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing.
According to the Chinese Foreign Ministry, the senior Iranian security official outlined Tehran’s position on the situation in the region. He pointed out that Iran would firmly defend its national security, sovereignty and territorial integrity, and resist pressure and threats, while remaining open to dialogue with all parties and actively seeking to promote regional peace and stability.

title: Motorists caught speeding above 130km/h where 50km/h is permitted as Traffitech begins operation
body: The Police Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) has recorded thousands of speeding offences on the first day of the implementation of its Traffitech system, with some motorists caught travelling above 130km/h on roads with a 50km/h speed limit. Speaking in an interview on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Monday, November 2, the Director of Education, Research and Training at the MTTD, Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Alexander Kwaku Obeng, said the digital traffic monitoring system was activated on Sunday, November 1, with the police using the first day to monitor motorists’ behaviour, particularly on open roads where drivers are more likely to exceed speed limits. According to ACP Obeng, although many motorists complied with the prescribed speed limits, the exercise also uncovered several cases of excessive speeding. He identified Mahama Road, from Boundary Road, as one of the locations where motorists were captured travelling above 130km/h despite the 50km/h speed limit. Similar offences were recorded at Boteyman, from School Junction towards the motorway, and along the Mallam-SCC-Kokrobite Junction stretch. He also mentioned the road from the police station at the toll booth towards Kasoa, as well as the stretch from the toll booth through Amanfrom and over the Kasoa flyover. ACP Obeng explained that the initial monitoring was deliberately conducted over the weekend to assess motorists’ behaviour when traffic was relatively light, and police presence was limited. He said that straight, flat and open roads were among the factors that encouraged speeding, particularly when drivers assumed they could travel at high speeds without being detected. “We leveraged that to observe and see whether it is the same, and there were many compliant drivers who were driving within the speed limits,” he said. However, he expressed concern about the number of motorists who disregarded the speed restrictions. “Some were doing above 130km/h on Mahama Road from Boundary Road,” he disclosed. ACP Obeng said the police had gathered digital evidence against thousands of motorists during the first day of the exercise. When asked how many traffic tickets had been issued so far, he declined to give an exact figure but indicated that the number of offences recorded was in the thousands. “I would like that we allow those who have them to start posting them. But the law, the L.I., says that we should issue the ticket to the offender. The offender should be forthcoming,” he said. “But yesterday [Sunday], we were worried because it was in the thousands.” He urged motorists, particularly those driving in Accra over the weekends, to reduce their speed and comply with traffic regulations. He specifically drew attention to Boteyman, where he said the Police had recorded several fatal crashes. “Please, we are picking up a lot of fatal crashes there. So, when the road is straight and flat in the city, don’t think it is a highway or motorway,” he cautioned. ACP Obeng explained that motorists captured by the system would receive traffic tickets containing details of their speeding offences and the evidence gathered by the police. He said the tickets are powered by GPS MTTD technology and contain the vehicle registration number, the name used in registering the vehicle or the relevant insurance details, as well as the date, time and location of the offence. The tickets also contain a reference to Regulation 211 of the Road Traffic Regulations, the applicable penalty units, the total fine and a two-week deadline for payment. “We have your vehicle numbers embedded. Your name you use in registering the car or the insurance. We have the date, time, and place,” ACP Obeng explained. He said motorists would have two options when responding to the tickets: pay the fine or contest the alleged offence. According to him, the payment link provided on the tickets directs vehicle owners to where they can follow the instructions to complete the process. Motorists can also access the service through the USSD code * 710 *0#. However, before making payment or contesting a ticket, vehicle owners will be shown a six-second video clip and photographs capturing the alleged speeding offence. ACP Obeng said this would enable motorists to review the evidence gathered by the police before deciding how to respond. He said that the system was designed to demonstrate the police’s capacity to detect and document speeding offences through digital technology, even on roads where officers are not physically present. He said that the issuance of digital tickets would encourage motorists to comply with speed limits beyond the first day of the system’s operation. Traffitech-GH is an automated system developed by the Ghana Police Service to enforce road traffic laws and regulations and improve road safety in the country. The system uses cameras and sensors to automatically take a picture and/or video of vehicles that flout road traffic laws and regulations, such as speeding and running a red light.

title: Some people decide to stay in Alyoshki due to family issues — human rights commissioner
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. Some Alyoshki residents have decided to stay in their homes due to various family issues, Russian human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova said at a press conference summing up the results of the Alyoshki humanitarian mission.
"We spoke with the people who remained there. It was an emotional and difficult conversation. One of the women was standing there, crying. I said: ‘Come with us. It's not safe here. We’ll provide you with a place to stay. We’ve prepared very good temporary shelters.’ She cried and said: ‘I can’t because my mother had a stroke. She simply won’t make the trip'," Lantratova recalled.
"Another woman’s husband is in the hospital, and she can’t leave him," the ombudswoman said. "And some have elderly parents who have already grown accustomed to living here. This is their home and their life, and they’re not ready to leave, no matter what. Of course, their adult children couldn't bring themselves to leave their parents alone, so they decided to stay," Lantratova concluded.

title: It is hardly possible to talk now about Russian gas transit to EU — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. it is hardly possible so far to speak about the resumption of Russian gas transit to Europe via Ukraine in the future, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
"It is hardly possible to talk about that so far. Actually, the state of affairs on the ground more than clearly demonstrates impossibility of implementing such plans at the moment. But we will see what will be in the future," Peskov said.
The United States reportedly support the soonest possible restart of Russian gas supplies to Europe over pipelines through the Ukrainian territory, The Wall Street Journal said earlier.

title: [VIDEO] God Has Granted Me Wisdom To Continue To Serve Nigerians – Tinubu
body: President Bola Tinubu has said that God has granted him the wisdom to continue to rule Nigerians following his recent visit to the holy mosque in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. President Tinubu, while speaking with journalists, said he felt fulfilled after observing prayers at the holy mosque in Ka’aba. “I feel fulfilled and grateful to Almighty Allah for giving us the opportunity and the health. The day went very well. “The prayer is for Allah to convert our diversity. Nigeria is full of diversity. It is made up of all the faiths. May Allah convert all the diversity to prosperity for the country. That is my prayer”. Speaking on his requests while there, Tinubu noted that God had granted him the “wisdom to continue to serve Nigerians”. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that has been granted. “Prior to the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then. He did, and I promised that I would come back to thank him, Almighty Allah. “There is no other God but him. He is the giver and the taker. “He owns the power. He said, use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person. “So, I have faith in that and believe extremely well that he has done me a favour to be the president of this great country. On commitment to Nigeria, President Tinubu noted that his commitment is “higher” and determined to bring prosperity. “My commitment is higher, and committed to bringing prosperity. To develop the country consistently with the wish of Allah and the support of the people”. He enjoined all to serve Allah and be guided by their consciences. “It is important to put Allah first. Then follow your conscience, follow the right path that will lead Nigeria to that greatness.” He reiterated that the economy was out of the woods and that the reforms were yielding good results. “The foundation is solid. The economy has come out of the dark tunnel. It is inspiring. We need to build the future for our youths. “If we don’t invest for their future, in 50 years from now, how do we want to be remembered as leaders? I am not looking for anything else.” He thanked management of the Ka’abha for granting him access to the holy mountain, saying that it was a historical moment for him. He assured Nigerians that the current economic challenges would soon be over. “I want to thank everyone for the faith and recognition. I can’t believe that the colour of the Ka’aba was green-white-green. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as a leader of the delegation. “We are all facing challenges and hostility around us. We will overcome it with faith in the Almighty. “I am grateful forever. I thank the King and the royal crown prince. It is their honour to have allowed me to enter the Ka’aba. It is history.” The post [VIDEO] God Has Granted Me Wisdom To Continue To Serve Nigerians – Tinubu appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Russia’s Perekop training ship docks at Cameroon’s Douala port
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. The Russian Navy’s Baltic Fleet training ship Perekop has arrived at the port of Douala in the Republic of Cameroon, the fleet’s press service reported.
"The Baltic Fleet training ship Perekop arrived at the port of Douala in the Republic of Cameroon as part of a long-distance voyage. The route to the port of Douala passed through the waters of the Atlantic Ocean, the Gulf of Guinea, and two rivers, the Cameroon and the Wouri, through the deltas of which the ship reached the port," the press service reported.
It said that Russian Charge d’Affaires ad interim in Cameroon Sergey Ustinov and Jean Marie Tchuissang, Russian Honorary Consul in Douala, attended the welcoming ceremony for the Russian ship. Representing the Republic of Cameroon at the event were the deputy commander of the Douala Naval Base and representatives of the city administration.
According to the press service, while the ship is berthed at the Douala port, Russian and Cameroonian sailors will play a friendly football match. Cameroonian Navy personnel will tour the ship and observe a shipboard damage control demonstration exercise. A tour of local attractions is planned for the crew and cadets of the Perekop. To continue their practical navigation training, cadets from the Republic of Cameroon are scheduled to board the training ship Perekop.
Cadets from the Admiral Ushakov Baltic Naval Institute are completing navigation training aboard the Perekop. Along with the Russian cadets, foreign military personnel from the Republic of Namibia and the Republic of the Congo, who are studying naval disciplines in Russia, are also taking part in the voyage. When the ship crossed the equator, the crew and cadets, in accordance with tradition, were presented with certificates recording the coordinates of the crossing point.
During the passage from the previous port, combat divers from the anti-sabotage unit conducted an anti-sabotage inspection of the ship’s underwater hull, checking the propeller-rudder system for foreign objects or damage.
The Perekop training ship’s long-distance voyage began in early July and will continue until mid-December. In total, the ship is set to travel approximately 30,000 nautical miles. Its route passes through the Northern Sea Route, four oceans, 14 seas, 23 straits, and nine gulfs. According to the itinerary, the ship is scheduled to visit 11 ports in foreign countries.

title: Tinubu inherited Nigeria on brink of collapse from Buhari — Plateau gov
body: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Ahmed Tinubu inherited a Nigerian economy that was “tottering on the brink of collapse” from the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2023. Mutfwang stated this on Monday during the formal inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Campaign Council in Jos, where he also defended the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms and urged Plateau residents to support the President in the 2027 election. “Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria, tottering on the brink of collapse, Nigeria that could not service its external debts, Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home.” “And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria, because they could not get the dollars to take back their money.” “Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades.” “Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” he said. Mutfwang further alleged that the previous administration resorted to printing money to manage the economy, claiming that more than N30 trillion was printed. “When the President took over in 2023, the government that he succeeded had run out of ideas on how to manage the economy, and they resorted to printing money in the Central Bank. “They printed over N30 trillion, which went down the drain.” “Today, by the grace of God, the Central Bank has stabilised, and that deficit has been done away with,” the governor said. On fuel subsidy, Mutfwang described the system under the previous administration as fraudulent, alleging that the country borrowed money to pay claims supported by what he called fictitious documents. “I say it was a fraud because we were borrowing money to pay people who brought fictitious documents. They never brought any wealth. They brought fictitious documents, claimed monies and subsidies. “You cannot continue to borrow money to give to thieves. You have to stop it at some point. And when it is stopped, there will be a payback; there will be a recovery time,” he said. The governor said the availability of fuel had improved despite the increase in its cost, recalling the long queues that previously characterised fuel stations across the country. “Today, by the grace of God, we have solved one side of the equation. Today fuel is available. It may not be cheap, but it is available.” “Those of us who are in my age bracket or a little below will remember the times when we spent days in petrol stations queuing for fuel that we could hardly get. But we have been able to resolve that,” Mutfwang said. He also claimed that the previous administration had sold crude oil in advance, saying the country was now servicing obligations arising from such arrangements. “Part of the problem of the Buhari regime is that they got to a point that they didn’t know what to do, so they sold our future crude. The crude we are yet to dig from the ground has been sold in advance.” “And today we are paying that debt. We are paying that debt. And so we cannot expect things to simply change overnight,” he said. Mutfwang said his administration was taking steps to cushion the effects of the economic adjustment on Plateau residents, citing the introduction of metro buses and the revival of the railway system within the Jos metropolis. “I’m glad that Plateau people have commended us for the metro buses that we bought early in the regime. I’m glad we’re able to revive the railway system within the metropolis.” “I’m glad that we’re able to reduce school fees for our students in tertiary institutions by 50 per cent. I’m glad that we’re able to raise their allowances by about 300 per cent,” he said. The governor also commended the Federal Government’s student financing initiatives, saying Plateau indigenes studying in universities had benefited from the scheme.” “It is also a great joy in my heart that the President also came up with a new scholarship for students called NELFUND.” “Today, hundreds of millions have been given to Plateau indigenes who are studying in different universities. Some are getting N20,000 monthly, N40,000 monthly. It has never happened before,” he said. On the 2027 elections, Mutfwang called for power rotation between the North and South, saying political arrangements should be respected. “We must agree that power should rotate between the North and the South. And if the North spends 8 years, which we have nothing to show for, it is only fair that we allow the South to do another 8 years.” “Because if we don’t respect that sharing arrangement, it will come back to haunt us someday,” he said. Mutfwang also declared that there was no vacancy in the Plateau State Government House ahead of the 2027 governorship election. “And that is why in Plateau State, we have already agreed that it is two terms per senatorial zone. Except the northern zone does not want to produce a governor until 2035, then you can toy with my mandate.” The governor urged APC candidates and campaign council members to communicate the achievements of the administration to the electorate and avoid actions capable of deepening divisions. “We must therefore go about this campaign with facts, with honesty, and with seriousness. ” Part of the reason why people are still apprehensive is because we have not communicated the real message, and we have a responsibility to ensure that that message is properly communicated.” “I’d like to urge all our candidates for the various positions; you must lead from the front. You must be bridge-builders.” “I am confident that come January 16, 2027, by the grace of God, Plateau State will return President Bola Ahmed Tinubu with a resounding victory. And that two weeks later, the people of Plateau will renew their mandate for us to continue on the good journey we have started.” On security, Mutfwang acknowledged the persistence of insecurity and said his administration was taking steps to strengthen security and facilitate the return of displaced persons to their communities. “On security, I know our opponents will say there is hunger in the land. We don’t deny it. They will say that the insecurity situation has not abated. We don’t deny it.” “But if they say we have not taken steps at all to address those issues, they know they are lying.” “Insecurity is not like tap water, where you simply turn on the tap and it flows down. It requires concerted, deliberate, intentional, sustained efforts before you get results.” “By the grace of God, we have understood what the issues are, and we have begun to make sure we propose solutions in the right places that matter,” he said. The governor said his administration would continue to protect communities and disclosed plans to deploy additional security personnel. “One thing I have committed myself to is that I will ensure the protection of every inch of land in Plateau State.” “Very soon we are going to be taking practical steps to facilitate the return of internally displaced persons back to their communities.” “And so, all we are asking Plateau people to do is trust us and be patient with us, and by the grace of God, you will not regret it.” The post Tinubu inherited Nigeria on brink of collapse from Buhari — Plateau gov appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Fire kills 1, injures 5 at boarding house near Kyiv – SES
body:
In the early hours of November 2, a fire broke out in a three-story boarding house building in the village of Sofiyivska Borshchahivka, Bucha district, leaving one person dead and five others injured, the State Emergency Service (SES) reported.

"On November 2 at 02:56, the Bucha District Rescue Service received a report of a fire at a boarding house on Oksamytova Street in the village of Sofiyivska Borshchahivka. ... It was established that the fire originated in one of the rooms on the second floor of the three-story building," the SES said in a Telegram post on Monday.

It is reported that at the time of the fire, 51 people were inside the boarding house, including four staff members. Rescuers organized the evacuation of residents using gas and smoke protection teams. During operations, SES units rescued 30 individuals with limited mobility.

"Unfortunately, during the extinguishing of the fire, the body of a person born in 1952 was discovered. Five other people were injured …

title: Vlisco launches Vlisco VIBE — A new expression for everyday life
body: Global textile brand Vlisco introduces Vlisco VIBE — a fresh take on its iconic prints, made for the contemporary wardrobe. Where the brand’s distinctive designs have been woven into moments of celebration and ceremony, Vlisco VIBE now extends that legacy into the rhythm of daily life – from professional to casual occasions, season after season. Launching this October, the inaugural collection of fabrics arrives in vibrant colourways and modern motifs, built for versatile styling. To bring it to life, Vlisco has partnered with acclaimed Nigerian fashion designer Lisa Folawiyo, whose signature blend of printed textiles and effortless tailoring defines a five-piece capsule designed exclusively for the brand. Sewing patterns for each of Folawiyo’s designs will be available alongside the fabrics, inspiring customers to recreate the styles and make them their own. Crafted for effortless movement in fine cotton satin, Vlisco VIBE offers breathable comfort and an elegant drape, creating flowing silhouettes at more accessible prices. The launch collection features four new designs across 18 colourways, available in two- and four-yard pieces supporting versatile styling for contemporary separates. Vlisco VIBE redefines the role of print beyond special occasions, making it an intuitive part of everyday style. Each design serves as a creative canvas — a starting point for tailoring, layering, and mixing with existing wardrobe pieces. Designed for modern lifestyles, the collection transitions seamlessly from day to evening, workdays to weekends. “Vlisco has always invited people to express themselves, especially during life’s most meaningful moments. With Vlisco VIBE, we’re bringing that same creative spirit into everyday moments. Rooted in 180 years of craftsmanship, the collection reimagines our heritage through a fresh, contemporary lens, with versatile prints that feel relevant and easy to make your own. At its heart is something we deeply believe: the creativity of transforming fabric into fashion is worth preserving, celebrating and passing on.” — Marlou van Engelen, Creative Director, Vlisco With Vlisco VIBE, the brand enters a new era of everyday luxury, connecting generations through the power of print while honouring its heritage of craftsmanship, creativity, and cultural expression. Vlisco VIBE will be available online and in Vlisco retail stores from October 13, 2026. Discover the Vlisco VIBE collection at vlisco.com/pages/vibe. About Vlisco Founded in 1846, Vlisco is a heritage textile company renowned for its unique printed fabrics, crafted using time-honoured techniques and exceptional-quality materials. Across generations, each design is infused with imagination, storytelling, and craftsmanship, creating textiles with a character and spirit of their own. Vlisco’s history is deeply intertwined with the cultural exchange between the Netherlands and Africa. Its distinctive prints have become cultural treasures, embraced and redefined by generations of African women. Over time, the fabrics have acquired names, meanings, and deep cultural significance, transforming them into treasured markers of identity, occasion, and community across West and Central Africa. For 180 years, the brand has continued to push the boundaries of textile design through process-driven innovation, balancing an enduring respect for its heritage with a creative curiosity for what comes next. Each unique Vlisco print sparks the imagination, celebrates culture and community, and inspires bold, joyful self-expression. Media enquiries: contact@annatourepr.com Images are attached. Additional materials are available upon request.

title: CIBN Confers Honorary Fellowship on Keystone Bank Chairman, Ada Chukwudozie
body: * Awardee pledges renewed commitment to service The Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) has conferred an honorary Fellowship on the Chairman of Keystone Bank Limited, Dr. Ada Chukwudozie, in recognition of her contributions to business, enterprise leadership and institutional development. The prestigious recognition was bestowed on Chukwudozie at the Institute’s 2026 Fellowship Investiture held on Friday, October 30, at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos. The ceremony, themed ‘Bank Recapitalisation: Leveraging New Bank Capital for Nigeria’s Industrial Transformation,’ attracted prominent figures from the banking industry, government and private sector, with discussions centred on strengthening Nigeria’s financial institutions to drive industrialisation, investment and sustainable economic growth. Speaking in an interview with newsmen shortly after receiving the honour, Chukwudozie expressed profound appreciation to CIBN, describing the recognition as both an encouragement and a call to greater responsibility. She said: “I am deeply honoured and grateful to the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria for finding me worthy of this prestigious recognition. It is an honour I receive with humility and a profound sense of responsibility. “Recognition of this nature is not just about celebrating individual achievements; it is also a reminder that leadership comes with an obligation to serve, to create opportunities and to contribute meaningfully to the development of our institutions and society.” The Keystone Bank Chairman further reaffirmed her commitment to service, noting that the recognition would strengthen her resolve to contribute more to the growth of the banking industry, manufacturing sector and the Nigerian economy. “I see this honour as renewed encouragement to do more. I remain committed to purposeful leadership, excellence and service. I will not relent in contributing my quota towards building stronger institutions, supporting enterprise development and creating sustainable economic opportunities. “Across banking and manufacturing, we must continue to promote innovation, accountability, responsible leadership and investments that create real value for the economy. Ultimately, the true measure of leadership is the positive impact we make on people’s lives,” she added. The honour comes at a significant period in the institutional transformation of Keystone Bank. Under the oversight of its Board and the leadership of management, the bank has recorded progress in strengthening its liquidity position, expanding its deposit base and growing its customer franchise. It has also intensified efforts to reinforce corporate governance, internal controls, accountability and risk management, while advancing technology across its digital banking channels to improve customer experience and accessibility. According to Chukwudozie, “These developments reflect the collective efforts of the board, management and staff, as well as the continued confidence of customers, as the institution pursues sustainable growth, operational resilience and improved service delivery.” She acknowledged the importance of collective leadership in achieving institutional success, stressing that sustainable progress requires the commitment of every stakeholder. “At Keystone Bank, we recognise that institutional growth is a collective responsibility. The Board, Management and staff all have important roles to play in building an institution that customers can trust and that consistently delivers value. Our commitment is to sustain the progress we have made, strengthen our systems and continue improving the quality of service we offer,” she stressed. Speaking at the investiture, CIBN President and Chairman of Council, Dr. Dele Alabi, challenged banks to translate the benefits of recapitalisation into increased financing for productive businesses, particularly micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. Lagos State Governor, Mr. Babajide Sanwo-Olu, underscored the importance of affordable and long-term financing in driving industrial expansion, enterprise development and economic prosperity, while emphasising sound governance and responsible lending practices. In his keynote address, the Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Economic Summit Group, Dr. Tayo Aduloju, called for increased financing of manufacturing and other productive sectors, urging stronger collaboration among financial institutions, government and regulators to address structural barriers to industrial investment. Other distinguished personalities honoured at the ceremony included Mr. Segun Ogunsanya, Chairman of the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority; Mrs. Olubunmi Kuku, Managing Director and Chief Executive of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria; Chief Folorunsho Alakija, Vice-Chairman of Famfa Oil Limited; Dr. Ibrahim Stevens, Governor of the Bank of Sierra Leone; Mr. Tokunbo Talabi, Secretary to the Ogun State Government; and Mr. Samuel Egube, Deputy Chief of Staff to the Lagos State Governor. Chukwudozie, who also serves as Group Managing Director of Dozzy Group and Chairman of the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN), South-east Branch, brings extensive experience across banking, manufacturing and enterprise development. Her recognition by CIBN further highlights the growing importance of cross-sector leadership in strengthening the relationship between financial services, industrial development and national economic transformation. For Chukwudozie, however, the fellowship represents more than a personal milestone. It reinforces her conviction that leadership must be measured not merely by positions occupied or accolades received, but by the institutions strengthened, opportunities created and lasting contributions made to society.

title: TraffiTech-GH: Police expect automated traffic enforcement to reduce road crashes
body: The Ghana Police Service says the introduction of its automated traffic enforcement system, TraffiTech-GH, is expected to significantly reduce road crashes, injuries and fatalities. Enforcement of the system began on Sunday, November 1, 2026, initially targeting motorists who exceed prescribed speed limits. Director of Education, Research and Training at the Police Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD), Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Alexander Kwaku Obeng, said early results from public education and the issuance of electronic caution notices showed a positive impact on road safety. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Monday, November 2, he said road crashes declined by 9.4 per cent in September 2026 compared with the same period in 2025. The number of vehicles involved in crashes also fell by 12.19 per cent. He said injuries reduced by 15.02 per cent, fatalities by 7.82 per cent and motorcycle-related crashes by 7.43 per cent. “What we have done, the evaluation has shown clearly that if you confront a person with the evidence, he or she tends to change. It has manifested itself in the data of September 2026 when we enhanced sensitisation and the issuance of caution notices,” he said. ACP Obeng disclosed that the Police had issued more than 200,000 electronic caution notices since the public education campaign began, including over 50,000 since its latest phase started in September. The notices, sent through the GPS-MTTD sender identification system, contain details of the offending vehicle, its registration number, the owner’s name, the time and location of the violation, as well as photographic evidence and a six-second video of the offence. How TraffiTech-GH works TraffiTech-GH is an automated enforcement system developed by the Ghana Police Service to improve road safety through the detection of traffic violations. It uses cameras and sensors to capture images and videos of vehicles committing offences, including speeding and running red lights. ACP Obeng said speeding was selected as the initial focus because it accounts for between 60 and 62 per cent of serious injuries and fatalities resulting from road crashes. The Police have deployed mobile speed cameras in patrol vehicles and tripod-mounted cameras at selected locations across the country. The cameras are being deployed in Accra and other major urban centres, including Takoradi, Kumasi, Sunyani, Tamale, Koforidua, Tema and Ho. Fines and payment Motorists caught exceeding speed limits will receive electronic tickets, with penalties determined by the extent of the violation. ACP Obeng said the minimum fine is GH¢240 for motorists caught driving between five and 20 kilometres per hour above the prescribed speed limit, with higher penalties applying to more serious violations. Vehicle owners will have 14 days to pay the fines or contest the violations through the designated electronic platform. Those without internet access can also use the USSD code *7100# and follow the prompts to enter their ticket numbers. Police warn against evading the system ACP Obeng said the MTTD had introduced a mechanism for motorists to challenge tickets, particularly where vehicle ownership or registration details were inaccurate. He urged vehicle owners who had permanently transferred their vehicles to other people to ensure that the change of ownership was duly registered with the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA). He cautioned that failure to complete the transfer within the stipulated two-week period could leave the previous owner liable for traffic violations committed with the vehicle. On attempts to develop applications to circumvent the enforcement system, he said the Police had established a cyber team to identify and deal with individuals seeking to defraud motorists or undermine the initiative. He added that although the initial enforcement phase focused on speeding, the Police could extend the technology to other traffic offences based on operational capacity and evidence. Motorists urged to observe speed limits ACP Obeng urged motorists to exercise restraint, particularly during the Christmas season, when increased travel and pressure to make more trips often contribute to dangerous driving. He reminded drivers to observe the prescribed speed limits of 50 kilometres per hour in built-up areas, 90 kilometres per hour on highways and 100 kilometres per hour on motorways. He expressed optimism that public education, automated enforcement and greater compliance with traffic regulations would result in fewer crashes, injuries and deaths by the end of the year.

title: Kula Boat Tragedy: Oil profits must never trump human lives, HOMEF tells oil firms, govt
body:
The Health of Mother Earth Foundation (HOMEF) has condemned the circumstances surrounding the deaths of seven people in Kula Kingdom, Rivers State, warning that commercial interests in Nigeria’s petroleum industry must never take precedence over human lives and environmental protection.
The environmental advocacy group said the 20 October boat tragedy, which occurred during a protest over the removal of an offshore crude oil vessel, exposed the dangers of an oil-dependent economic system that prioritises resource extraction and commercial interests over the safety and livelihoods of host communities.
In a statement issued on 29 October and signed by its Media and Communications Officer, Kome Odhomor, HOMEF said the incident raised serious questions about the responsibilities of oil companies and public institutions towards communities affected by petroleum operations.
The tragedy occurred in the waterways of Kula Kingdom, in Akuku-Toru Local Government Area, when a speedboat carrying 15 people capsized during an operation involving the movement of the Anambra Basin Floating Storage and Offloading (FSO) vessel.
Eight people survived the incident, while seven died. The deaths followed tensions between community members and those involved in the operation to remove the oil vessel from the coastal waters.
The protest was reportedly triggered by unresolved community grievances, including an alleged oil spill, outstanding payments to local vendors and contractors, and what residents perceived as neglect by the operators of the facility.
HOMEF’s Executive Director, Nnimmo Bassey, said the tragedy is proof of the injustice of an extractive industry in which communities bear the environmental and human costs while commercial interests take precedence.
“The Kula tragedy exposes the cruelty of an extractive model that places commercial interests above human lives and the wellbeing of communities. No barrels of crude oil are worth a human life,” Mr Bassey said.
He argued that decades of petroleum extraction had left communities grappling with oil pollution, damaged fishing grounds, threatened food security and declining livelihoods.
Mr Bassey said the consequences were particularly severe for fishing communities such as Kula, where waterways and aquatic resources sustain livelihoods and underpin community life.
He said environmental justice should go beyond compensation after pollution has occurred to include preventing environmental damage, restoring affected ecosystems and respecting the rights of communities.
“Companies and public institutions must recognise their responsibilities to the people and ecosystems affected by extractive activities,” he added.
The Kula incident has also raised questions about the circumstances surrounding the operation that preceded the boat capsize.
As previously reported, community members had opposed the removal of the Anambra Basin FSO vessel in the face of unresolved grievances over alleged pollution and other outstanding obligations.
Max Shipping Services Limited, an Ibeto Group subsidiary which owns the vessel, expressed sadness over the incident but denied responsibility. The company said its involvement was limited to owning and retrieving the vessel, which it had hired to Menal Technical Services Limited for crude oil evacuation.
The police in Rivers State said they had commenced an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.
The seven deaths were confirmed after search and rescue teams recovered the bodies of the two remaining victims, following the earlier recovery of five bodies.
HOMEF said the tragedy illustrated how the pursuit of natural resources, without adequate regard for community welfare, could deepen grievances, insecurity and preventable human suffering.
It rejected the treatment of oil-producing communities as sacrifice zones for commercial interests, insisting that residents of resource-rich areas should not be regarded as obstacles to petroleum operations.
The organisation called for a shift away from what it described as extractivism towards a development model that prioritises ecological wellbeing, human dignity and community livelihoods.
It called on the government and oil industry operators to prevent pollution, rehabilitate degraded ecosystems, protect fishing grounds and ensure that host communities participate meaningfully in decisions affecting their lands and waterways.
It also called for effective safeguards to protect communities and ensure that residents can express environmental concerns and defend their livelihoods without being exposed to violence or preventable danger.
HOMEF expressed solidarity with the bereaved families, survivors and people of Kula Kingdom, warning that the deaths must not become another statistic in the history of suffering associated with petroleum extraction in the Niger Delta.
“The lost lives represent families, relationships, aspirations and futures cut short,” the organisation said.
It urged Nigeria to confront the inequalities associated with petroleum extraction, arguing that development cannot be built on the destruction of communities and their environment.
“No profit is worth a human life. No resource is more valuable than the people and ecosystems that sustain life,” HOMEF said.

title: Russian attack damages cat shelter in Odesa
body:
Lyubov, the owner of the shelter, said that an enemy drone struck a neighboring building.
"Not a single window in our building is intact. All the doors have been warped, and we now have no heating. Part of the roof is missing," she said.
According to the woman, one animal was killed. Four other cats that lived in the shelter's courtyard are still being searched for.
Two elderly internally displaced women from the Kherson region also lived in the building where the cats were kept. During the explosion, the ceiling collapsed on them.
Aftermath of the Shahed drone attack on Odesa. / Photo: Nina Liashonok, Ukrinform
Before Russia's full-scale invasion, one of the women had worked as a teacher for 45 years at a school in the Beryslav district. Her former students helped evacuate her from the settlement destroyed by Russian forces.
"I have been living here for three years because nothing was left of my home. Today, at three in the morning, I heard an explosion. The ceiling collapsed onto the bed, and shards of glass went flying everywhere. The neighboring building was burning fiercely, and we were afraid the fire would spread to ours. We grabbed our bags with our documents, put on our rubber clogs, and ran outside in whatever we had been sleeping in," said Lyubov Mykolaivna.
As Ukrinform previously reported, Russian forces attacked Odesa on the night of November 2, injuring four people.

title: Israeli man allegedly brutally murders wife with an axe in front of their four children
body: A 43-year-old woman was found dead in Petah Tikva on Sunday night shortly after midnight, according to police and emergency medical responders. After receiving reports of a violent incident, emergency personnel discovered the woman with severe wounds, no pulse, and not breathing, and ultimately pronounced her dead at the scene. Police are still investigating the incident as of press time; however, the woman was allegedly beaten with an axe in her apartment in front of her four children, the oldest of whom is 12 years old. Her husband was found a few hundred meters from the crime scene, having apparently taken his own life. Initial police investigations indicated that the couple had no history of domestic violence, and neighbors were shocked by the news.   The issue of femicide has plagued multiple sectors of Israeli society for several years, although it largely fell out of the mainstream news cycle with the outbreak of the Israel-Hamas war in 2023. Nevertheless, Israeli activists and researchers have continued to document and battle the pattern of violence toward and murder of women. 'This murder could have been prevented'"While politicians are busy playing musical chairs, a murderer has taken a woman's life with an axe in front of her children," said Tal Hochman, head of the Israel Women's Network (IWN). "The most devastating part is that this murder could have been prevented; violence against women never begins with murder."According to the IWN, 17 women have been murdered in 2026 in cases of gender-based violence, and the main suspect in 80% of those cases is a spouse or ex-spouse.  What is more, according to a 2025 IWN report, in over one-third of femicide cases, welfare services or police were aware of domestic violence in the home before the murder happened. In a few cases, welfare services were even aware that the suspect was unstable before the murder. The Michal Sela Forum, an Israeli non-profit dedicated to combating domestic violence, also issued a statement pointing out that the latest murder was the fourth case of femicide since the beginning of October, and that 2026 has seen a total of 25 people killed in domestic settings, including four men and four children. "The murder of women in their own homes is merely the tip of the iceberg," the Michal Sela Forum said in its statement on Monday. "We must not accept a reality in which women are murdered in their own homes—sometimes even before the eyes of their children."'The murder of women is not an inevitable fate'Rivka Neuman, who chairs the Women's Status Advancement Division at the Women's International Zionist Organization (WIZO), noted that, behind the statistics, "lie lives cut short, families shattered, and children left orphaned at a young age—bearing the weight of lifelong trauma.""The murder of women is not an inevitable fate," Neuman added. "We must not wait for the next victim before taking action." Alon Hachmon contributed to this report.

title: TLP Advisory Warns Nigeria Risks Losing Tech Wealth As Fintechs Shun NGX
body: Funmi Ogundare Cross border law firm, TLP Advisory, has warned that Nigeria risks losing a significant share of the economic value generated by its fast-growing technology sector as its leading homegrown fintech companies remain absent from the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX). The firm said despite the emergence of multibillion-dollar Nigerian technology companies, including Flutterwave, Moniepoint and Paystack, not a single homegrown fintech is currently listed on the NGX, limiting the opportunity for local investors to participate in their growth. The concern was raised at the launch of TLP Advisory’s third annual report, titled, ‘Home and Away: Tracking African Tech’s Global Footprint’, weekend, in Lagos. The report, which surveyed 100 of Africa’s top startups, found that 67 per cent were incorporated in the United States, 32 per cent in the United Kingdom and 22 per cent in the United Arab Emirates, underscoring the growing offshore structure of African technology businesses. Speaking at the launch, TLP Advisory founding partner, Funkola Odeleye, explained that Nigerian startups were often compelled to move their intellectual property and corporate structures offshore because of their dependence on foreign venture capital. According to her, investors typically prefer to invest in companies incorporated in jurisdictions where they can more easily protect and realise the value of their investments. “Investors will not put money in a Delaware entity and let your IP remain in Nigeria,” Odeleye said. “Where the money comes from is where the assets go. “Plus, if you raise in dollars, you cannot rely on the naira to return value to your investors. The only real solution is building deep local capital pools so startups can raise at home.” She warned that unless Nigeria develops stronger domestic sources of venture funding, the country could continue to produce successful technology companies without retaining a proportionate share of the wealth and value they create. While major telecommunications companies such as MTN and Airtel have established a strong presence on the local bourse, Nigeria’s most successful technology startups have largely remained outside the NGX. In her remarks, the co-founder, Odunoluwa Longe, said the challenge was not necessarily a lack of opportunities for technology companies to list locally, noting that the NGX had created a specialised technology board to attract firms in the sector. However, she identified poor awareness and the perceived complexity of listing requirements as major barriers preventing startups from exploring the local market. Longe called on regulators and market operators to intensify efforts to bridge the information gap and make the listing process more accessible to high-growth technology companies. She also urged policymakers to consider models such as Egypt’s recent MNT-Halan listing, which opened up opportunities for ordinary citizens to participate in the growth of a technology company. “It’s not an either-or choice. Startups can serve global markets and still list locally,” Longe said. “Policy and awareness must catch up so our best companies don’t exit entirely overseas.”

title: Akwa Ibom revenue hits N3.218 trillion in 41 months under Eno
body:
The Akwa Ibom State Government has received at least N3.218 trillion in public revenue within the first 41 months of Governor Umo Eno’s administration, further expanding the state’s financial resources despite persistent concerns over the government’s failure to publish comprehensive spending records.
An analysis of the state’s third-quarter 2026 Budget Performance Report shows that Akwa Ibom received N284.37 billion between July and September 2026.
The latest figure, added to the N2.934 trillion previously reported by PREMIUM TIMES for the period between May 2023 and June 2026, brings the administration’s cumulative revenue to N3.218 trillion.
The latest report shows that N275.37 billion of the third-quarter receipts came from recurrent revenue, comprising N250.61 billion from the state’s share of the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) and N24.76 billion from independent revenue, also known as internally generated revenue.
The state also recorded N9 billion in Capital Development Fund receipts, which comprise loan proceeds, bringing its total revenue for the quarter to N284.37 billion.
The figures point to the substantial increase in financial resources available to Mr Eno’s administration since it assumed office.
Despite the substantial revenue inflow, the state government reported total expenditure of N87.2 billion during the three-month period.
An examination of the expenditure figures shows that personnel costs, including pensions and gratuities, accounted for N36.25 billion.
Another N19.7 billion went into other recurrent expenditure, while N31.25 billion was recorded as expenditure on capital projects.
The figures indicate that personnel costs and other recurrent expenditure together accounted for N55.95 billion, exceeding the reported capital expenditure of N31.25 billion during the quarter.
However, the published report provides no detailed breakdown of the revenue sources showing the receipts from each of the FAAC sources, the type of loan obtained and what each ministry, department and agency of government remitted to the state coffers.
The report also failed to provide capital expenditure showing the individual projects funded, their locations, the amounts spent on each project or the ministries and agencies responsible for implementation. It also failed to show performance for the ministries and agencies to aid independent assessment of government priorities.
The latest report also raises fresh concerns about the quality of financial information being made available to the public.
Although the government published an eight-page third-quarter budget performance document, only five pages contained information. The remaining three pages were blank.
This limited disclosure comes against the backdrop of repeated findings by PREMIUM TIMES that the Eno administration has progressively reduced the level of financial details available in its public records.
In July, PREMIUM TIMES reported that the administration had received at least N2.934 trillion within its first 38 months but was no longer publishing detailed capital expenditure records, making it difficult for citizens to independently track spending on projects and government programmes.
The newspaper also found that the state’s audited financial statements for 2023, 2024 and 2025 did not contain detailed capital expenditure schedules.
Similarly, budget performance reports published from the first quarter of 2025 through the second quarter of 2026 omitted detailed capital expenditure information.
In an earlier investigation published in January, PREMIUM TIMES reported that Akwa Ibom had slipped deeper into fiscal secrecy under Mr Eno, with the government failing to provide the level of financial disclosure required by the state’s fiscal responsibility framework.
The state previously published more comprehensive quarterly budget implementation reports, sometimes exceeding 40 pages, containing information that enabled citizens to examine revenue and expenditure across ministries, departments, agencies and programmes.
The reduction in disclosure has limited the ability of citizens, civil society organisations and journalists to independently assess how public resources are allocated and spent.
The Akwa Ibom State Fiscal Responsibility Law requires the government to conduct its fiscal and financial affairs transparently, including the full and timely disclosure and wide publication of transactions involving public revenues and expenditure.
With the latest figures, the administration’s cumulative revenue has risen beyond N3.2 trillion, but the absence of comprehensive financial records continues to make it difficult to point to how much has been spent on individual projects and programmes across the state.

title: Turkish Media Alarmed by Greek Frigates with 1,000km Missiles
body: Turkish media have reacted with concern to the strengthening of the Greek Navy, reporting that Greece is acquiring frigates capable of carrying missiles with a range of 1,000 kilometres. According to the Turkish network A Haber, of the Belharra frigates ordered from France, the first delivered was Kimon . A flag-raising ceremony has now also taken place for the Nearchos frigate. The report noted that this vessel can carry SCALP Naval cruise missiles, manufactured by France’s Naval Group, with a 1,000km range. Greek Defence Minister Nikos Dendias attended the ceremony in Lorient, France. A Haber claimed that by equipping its navy with these frigates, Greece aims to send a message to Turkey and strengthen its negotiating position. It also reported that an agreement was signed with France on the same day to upgrade Greece’s four frigates to Standard 4+ level. The Turkish channel argued that Athens is seeking to close the gap with Turkey in naval power. The report was cited by SKAI’s Istanbul correspondent Manolis Kostidis. body:

title: Ericsson introduces 5G drone detection system for defense and critical infrastructure protection
body: The Integrated Sensing and Communication System uses sensing-capable 5G radios, edge computing, AI and signal processing to track objects across wide areas. It is designed to supplement radar and other sensors by drawing on existing towers, backhaul and spectrum rather than requiring an entirely separate detection network. “Low-flying drones create a detection coverage gap that no single sensor can effectively address. Ericsson ISAC System enables multiple 5G sites to deliver coordinated wide-area detection and continuous tracking, with data that can be integrated with traditional sensing technologies and operational systems,” said Freddie Södergren, Ericsson’s global head of Mission Critical Networks and Defense. The system analyzes radio signals reflected by objects, using geographically separated sites to transmit and receive sensing signals. Observing an object from several angles helps improve positioning and maintain its track as it moves through the coverage area, according to Ericsson. The company said validated tests reliably detected and tracked micro drones at kilometer-scale distances with precise three-dimensional positioning. Performance varies with the target, its flight path, the arrangement of sensing sites, terrain, surrounding conditions and system configuration. “Detecting small drones across large areas is a growing operational challenge. The possibility of using distributed infrastructure to complement existing sensors could provide an important additional layer of situational awareness,” said Carl Lundqvist, chief architect at Swedish Armed Forces Headquarters. Initial commercial pilots will provide sensing only, with integrated communications capability to be added as the technology develops toward 6G. Tracking data and AI-based classifications can be shared securely with authorized external systems, including security and command-and-control platforms. “Ericsson’s ISAC System shows that mobile-network sensing can perform far better than many expect, turning complex radio reflections into remarkably accurate tracking of low-flying, uncooperative objects,” said Joe Madden, principal analyst at Mobile Experts. “By building on an extensive footprint of existing sites, Ericsson has the potential to deliver wide-area drone detection faster and more cost-efficiently than deploying new dedicated sensor infrastructure.” A trial with AT&T in Arlington, Texas, detected, located and tracked multiple drones, with their movements displayed on sensing dashboards. A separate demonstration with Erillisverkot in Helsinki used multiple 5G sites to detect and track drones, showing how mobile-network sensing could extend coverage alongside traditional sensors. “The next evolution of connectivity is about networks that don’t just move data but help organizations with insights to better understand and respond to the events in the real world,” said Shawn Hakl, senior vice president and head of product at AT&T Business. “Bringing Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) capabilities into existing 5G infrastructure can provide telemetry and intelligence in situations where it is not possible or desirable to pre-deploy sensors or cameras.” In Poland, Ericsson, Play and Asseco demonstrated drone detection and positioning by combining mobile-network sensing with Asseco’s PUSZCZYK acoustic detection system. Potential uses include surveillance of borders and coastlines, protection of ports and power plants, and drone traffic management. “The Ericsson ISAC System shows that dual-use technology can strengthen national security by extending sensing capabilities to help authorities protect people and critical infrastructure,” said Antti Kauppinen, chief technology officer at Erillisverkot. “Together with Ericsson, we are exploring how this capability can be developed responsibly to enhance Finland’s resilience, security, and preparedness.”

title: Every evacuee from Alyoshki to receive medical treatment — ombudswoman
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. All residents evacuated from Alyoshki will receive the medical care they need, with healthcare professionals and psychologists providing assistance at temporary accommodation centers, Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova said at a news conference following a humanitarian mission to the city.
"The first group of people who decided to remain in Russia arrived at a temporary accommodation center, initially in Simferopol. Some subsequently relocated to the Krasnodar Region, while others expressed a desire to stay in Skadovsk. Temporary accommodation centers were established at health and recreation facilities, where medical personnel were on hand to receive the evacuees. They were provided with initial medical assistance, and doctors are taking care of them. Everyone will receive the necessary medical treatment. Psychologists are also available on-site," she said.

title: Oyedepo ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‍⁠​‌⁠​‍‌​tasks Africa with indigenous solutions to challenges
body: The Chancellor of Covenant University, Ota, Ogun, Dr David Oyedepo, has urged African countries to look inward and deploy indigenous solutions to address the continent’s numerous challenges. Oyedepo gave the advice in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Monday in Ota. He said that developing homegrown solutions to local challenges was the way forward for Africa to reduce its heavy dependence on foreign countries. “Man is created to solve his problems wherever he is planted. Therefore, African countries should provide solutions to their challenges without constantly seeking foreign assistance,” he said. The chancellor said that Africa’s slow pace of development was not because its people were Black but largely because they were blind to their potential. ‘’Africans should take absolute responsibility for their destiny,” he said. Oyedepo attributed the continent’s inability to adequately address its challenges to what he described as a “what will happen will happen” mentality. According to him, the mindset has contributed significantly to Africa’s present situation by discouraging proactive thinking and responsibility. He said that the greatness of any nation depended on the valuable contributions of individuals and organisations within its borders. ‘’Africa will make meaningful progress only when its countries recognise the importance of indigenous solutions and take responsibility for addressing their challenges rather than relying excessively on foreign assistance,” he said. The chancellor urged African leaders and citizens to harness their local knowledge, resources and capabilities to drive sustainable development across the continent. title: Gas market larger than European market — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. The natural gas market in itself is much larger than the European market alone, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
Everything will depend on the desire of the buyers, the desire of the sellers, and the capabilities of the sellers, the Kremlin Spokesman said, answering a question whether Moscow assumes the possibility of the resumption of Russian gas supplies to Europe.
"The gas market, as you know, is much larger than the European one, although the European market is the premium one," Peskov said.

title: ABSA Bank woos aspirational customers with enhanced Prestige Banking benefits
body: ABSA Bank Ghana is seeking to broaden the appeal of its Prestige Banking proposition by attracting more young professionals and individuals working towards their financial goals, moving beyond its traditional focus on established business owners and corporate executives. The bank is positioning the service as a more personalised banking experience, combining preferential financial benefits with lifestyle privileges to meet the changing needs and expectations of a wider customer base. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Monday, November 2, Princess Tettey, Head of Prestige Banking at ABSA Bank Ghana, described the proposition as “a lifestyle beyond banking”. She explained that the service is designed around customers’ income levels, financial goals and personal aspirations, allowing the bank to provide products and services that reflect their individual circumstances and different stages of life. Among the benefits available to Prestige Banking customers are preferential rates on loans, investments and foreign exchange transactions. The service is also designed to support customers through significant financial milestones, including career advancement, purchasing homes and acquiring vehicles. Ms Tettey further highlighted the complimentary Signature Card offered to customers, which provides airport lounge access, travel insurance coverage of up to 750,000 and Visa Concierge services. These include assistance with flight bookings, hotel reservations and airport transfers. She emphasised that the proposition was not reserved for individuals who had already attained financial success but also catered for those building their careers, growing their businesses and working towards their financial ambitions. “We want to grow with you. Whether it’s your promotion, you’re buying that new house, that new car, Prestige Banking wants to be there for you and to grow. It’s not for people who have arrived necessarily, but people who are aspiring to arrive, and we want to go on that journey with you,” she said. Building relationships beyond traditional banking The expanded focus reflects ABSA Bank Ghana’s efforts to respond to changing customer expectations and strengthen its relationship with customers across different income levels and stages of their financial journeys. As customers increasingly look for more than conventional banking services, the bank is emphasising combining financial solutions with convenience, personalised support and lifestyle benefits. Through Prestige Banking, ABSA seeks to establish relationships that can grow alongside customers, offering financial services that respond to their evolving needs, whether they are advancing in their careers, making major purchases or pursuing longer-term investment goals. The approach also signals the bank’s interest in engaging a younger generation of customers who are increasingly conscious of the value, flexibility and personalised experiences they expect from financial institutions. By broadening its target market, ABSA is seeking to position Prestige Banking not simply as a service for people who have accumulated wealth, but as a banking proposition for individuals with ambitions to build it.

title: All possible assistance to be provided to civilians staying in Alyoshki — Russian official
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. All possible assistance will be provided to civilians who have chosen to stay in Alyoshki, Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova said at a press conference following a humanitarian operation in the town.
She explained that some people had declined evacuation for various reasons, including health problems.
"There were many such families, and we recorded their details. In fact, we are monitoring every family that has contacted us to better understand their needs and continue providing as much assistance as possible," Lantratova said.

title: Notis Sfakianakis Turns 67 on a Bittersweet Anniversary
body: The Notis Sfakianakis birthday falls on Monday 2 November 2026. The Greek singer turns 67, one year after Kili, the mother of his children, died on the same date. Greek media marked the day with tributes to a career that made him one of the country’s best-selling artists. However, many also noted that the singer now lives far from the stage and the spotlight. For his fans, the date now carries a different weight. Kili Sfakianaki, whom he married in 1991, died on his birthday in 2025 at the age of 62. She had faced serious health problems. The couple separated in 2019 but stayed on good terms. Six months later, in May 2026, the family suffered another loss. His sister, Polyanna Sfakianaki, died after a long battle with cancer . Her funeral was held on Kos, the island where she was born. A Notis Sfakianakis birthday tribute Born Panagiotis Sfakianakis in Heraklion , Crete, on 2 November 1959, he moved to Kos as a child. His parents had separated. There, he worked as a DJ and began singing with a small band in 1985. He met Kili, a British woman working as a tour guide on Kos, in 1984. The couple married in 1991, had twins, Apollon and Aphrodite, and separated in 2019 but remained close. Kili chose to stay out of the public eye and devoted herself to the family. Also in 1991, he released his first album, Proti Fora . Soon afterwards, his shows at Bio Bio in Athens drew growing crowds. He became one of the biggest names of the 1990s nightlife scene. Each Notis Sfakianakis birthday brings back memories of that decade. His 1994 album Notioanatolitika tou Kosmou included “O Aetos” (The Eagle), the song that became his signature hit. The family had already known grief. His brother, Giorgos, died of cancer, and his 2004 album Me Agapi O,ti Kaneis reflected his mourning. As a result, this Notis Sfakianakis birthday arrives after several difficult years. Hits that defined an era Other albums followed, including 5o Vima (1996), Oi Notes Einai 7psyhes (1998) and the live album XXX Enthimion (1999). He has sold more than five million records. His songs include “Opa Opa”, “Ta Klemmena” and “Genethlia”, which means “Birthday”. His last studio album, …ki o Eros Theos Einai… , came out in 2018. Since then, he has stepped away from nightclub stages, although rumours of a comeback surface regularly. Whether that break is permanent remains unclear. Even so, this Notis Sfakianakis birthday shows that his voice still holds a firm place in Greek popular music. Fans continue to send him their wishes.
