title: American Airlines returns to Haiti after nearly two years, but Port-au-Prince remains off limits
body:
American Airlines has returned to Haiti after an absence of nearly two years, launching daily flights between Miami and Cap-Haïtien while Port-au-Prince remains off limits to US carriers.
Flight AA2492 departed Miami on November 1 for Cap-Haïtien, restoring American's presence in a country it had served since 1971 before suspending operations in late 2024. The inaugural service was operated by Boeing 737-800 N957NN, although the 737 MAX 8 is scheduled for the regular route.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
According to American, Cap-Haïtien became its 100th destination in Mexico, the Caribbean and Latin America. The inaugural flight also had an all-Haitian, Creole-speaking crew led by Captain Oliver Jean.
American previously served Cap-Haïtien from 2014 until 2020, when the route was suspended during the Covid-19 pandemic. Its return to the northern city is possible because the airport lies outside the area where the Federal Aviation Administration still restricts US civil aviation operations.
US airlines stopped flying to Haiti in November 2024 after three commercial aircraft were hit by gunfire around Port-au-Prince. A Spirit Airlines Airbus A320 approaching the capital was struck several times and diverted to Santiago, Dominican Republic, with a flight attendant suffering minor injuries.
Bullet damage was also discovered on JetBlue and American aircraft after separate flights from Port-au-Prince. The FAA initially prohibited US civil aviation operations throughout Haiti before limiting the restriction to the region around the capital.
The current prohibition covers operations below 10,000 feet in specified areas around Port-au-Prince and is scheduled to remain in effect until March 2, 2027. The FAA says armed groups control much of the capital and have weapons capable of threatening aircraft at low altitude.
Cap-Haïtien, about 85 miles (135 km) north of Port-au-Prince, lies outside that area and has retained international service, including flights by Haitian carrier Sunrise Airways.
When American announced the route in June, it described Haiti as the largest Caribbean market by passenger demand without service from a US airline. The daily flight also connects Cap-Haïtien with more than 90 US destinations through Miami.

title: ​The Battle for Brand Supremacy: Inside the 2026 Nigerian Marketing Awards
body: In today’s hyper-competitive consumer landscape, a brand is much more than a logo or a catchy tagline; it is a living, evolving relationship with the public. Across Nigeria, corporate storytelling has reached sophisticated new heights, making the recognition of true market leadership both more challenging and more prestigious. It is against the background that the Nigerian Marketing Awards (NMA) has become an institution that has rapidly become the gold standard for celebrating excellence, transparency, and professional rigour in West Africa’s largest economy. With the announcement of the finalists for the coveted Brand of the Year 2026 award, the spotlight has shifted intensely onto three titans of the Nigerian market: Heineken, Malta Guinness, and MILO. ​The path to the final three is no small feat. It represents months of rigorous evaluation by the Awards Decision Council (ADC), a body comprised of some of the most distinguished marketing and communications professionals in the industry. For Heineken, Malta Guinness, and MILO to emerge from a crowded field of exceptional contenders speaks volumes about their enduring cultural resonance, commercial resilience and marketing innovation. ​Yet, what makes the 2026 competition particularly fascinating is its commitment to a hybrid democratic model. The ultimate winner will not be chosen by industry experts alone, nor purely by popular sentiment. Instead, the final victory relies on a finely balanced 50/50 split between judges’ scores and public votes. This dual approach bridges the gap between technical marketing brilliance, assessing strategy, equity and execution—and the visceral, emotional connection a brand holds with everyday consumers. ​As Founder and Convener of the NMA, Tony Agenmonmen, aptly noted during the announcement: “Three outstanding brands. One coveted title. Our judges have made their assessment, and now the public has a say. By giving equal weight to expert judgement and public votes, we recognise both marketing excellence and the connection brands build with consumers.” ​By opening the voting lines to the public from November 1 to November 9, 2026, the NMA reinforces a vital modern marketing truth: consumers are no longer passive recipients of advertising messages; they are active co-creators of brand value. In an era marked by consumer fatigue and scepticism, brands must earn their stripes daily. Whether it is Heineken’s premium lifestyle positioning, Malta Guinness’s sustained vitality narrative, or MILO’s generational imprint on family nourishment and grassroots sports, each finalist has mastered the art of staying relevant in a dynamic economic climate.

title: TikTok Becomes Business Tool for Kazakhstan’s Entrepreneurs, Survey Finds
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA — A new survey by TikTok and the Atameken National Chamber of Entrepreneurs found that more than 70% of surveyed companies use the platform for business at least once a month, while 88.3% reported a positive effect on attracting new customers. The study also found that more businesses associate TikTok activity with a share of their revenue. Photo credit: Dado Ruvic (REUTERS) The findings were presented at the TikTok Impact Forum in Almaty on Oct. 28, ahead of Entrepreneur’s Day, as the platform and Atameken released the second annual edition of their study, The TikTok Effect: The Platform’s Impact on Small and Medium-Sized Businesses in Kazakhstan. From visibility to revenue The survey, conducted in September and October this year, covered 206 companies across all 20 regions of Kazakhstan and seven industry groups: culture, entertainment and tourism; health, beauty and sports; food and nonfood products; catering; education; and real estate services. Among respondents, 43.7% said they used TikTok for business monthly, up from 29.5% in the previous survey, an increase of 14.2 percentage points. Another 27.2% reported using the platform weekly or more often. Regular use is not limited to recently established companies. Among businesses operating for more than 10 years, 31% said they use TikTok for marketing weekly or more frequently. Comparable figures were 15.4% for companies established less than a year ago, 30.8% for those operating for one to three years, 32.2% for businesses with three to five years of experience, and 20% for companies operating for five to 10 years. The survey also found that 57.8% of respondents attributed more than 5% of their revenue to TikTok activity, an increase of 12.3 percentage points from the previous survey. For 14.6% of companies, revenue associated with the platform accounted for at least 25% of total income. Among businesses using TikTok weekly, approximately 11% said that half or more of their total revenue was linked to activity on the platform. Organic content leads, but paid promotion is growing Organic video content remains the most common way surveyed companies use TikTok. In 2026, 77.6% said they published videos on the platform. Collaboration with content creators more than doubled, rising from 10.4% in the previous survey to 22.8%. Paid advertising was used by 18% of respondents. Overall, 75.7% of respondents said they allocated a budget to TikTok-related promotion in 2026, up from 62.3% in 2025. The measure includes paid advertising and creator partnerships, as well as content production, social media management and other marketing activities. Spending levels also tracked with the share of revenue businesses attributed to the platform. Companies without a dedicated TikTok budget attributed an average of 3.9% of their revenue to it. Among businesses allocating more than 70% of their marketing budget to TikTok, the average reached 42%. Beyond revenue, 83.5% of respondents said TikTok helped them interact with customers, while 73.3% said it helped their businesses stand out from competitors. Real estate and tourism report the sharpest increases The share of surveyed businesses attributing at least 5% of their revenue to TikTok rose most sharply in real estate services, increasing by 40.6 percentage points to 66.6%. Culture, entertainment and tourism rose 24.7 percentage points to 60.5%, while food products rose 18.1 percentage points to 56.8%. Catering retained one of the highest shares, at 68%, up from 57.7%. Education rose to 56.2% from 44.4%, while health, beauty and sports rose to 54.5% from 37.5%. Nonfood products showed little change, edging up from 53.3% to 53.5%. The results show considerable variation across sectors, with the largest reported increase in real estate services and consistently high figures in catering. Estimating TikTok’s potential economic scale To estimate TikTok’s potential revenue scale, researchers developed a model using respondents’ reported turnover, the share of revenue they attributed to the platform, and official statistics on the number of small and medium-sized enterprises in Kazakhstan. The model considers three scenarios based on the proportion of entrepreneurs actively using TikTok: 10%, 15% and 20%. Under the conservative scenario, assuming 10% of entrepreneurs use TikTok actively, estimated TikTok-related revenue reached 531.6 billion tenge in 2026. Under the moderate scenario, with 15% active use, the estimate rises to 797.4 billion tenge. Under the accelerated digitalization scenario, assuming 20% active use, it reaches 1.0632 trillion tenge. The researchers selected the 10% scenario as the conservative baseline, citing comparable studies in countries including the United Kingdom and Australia. The three estimates are equivalent to 0.33%, 0.50% and 0.67% of Kazakhstan’s gross domestic product, respectively. In the previous survey, the corresponding ratios were approximately 0.16%, 0.25% and 0.33%. These are model-based estimates of revenue that entrepreneurs associate with TikTok, not measurements of the platform’s direct contribution to GDP. The calculations do not establish how much of that revenue would have been lost without TikTok and exclude indirect effects such as job creation, supply-chain development and changes in household consumption. The researchers also note that the 2025 and 2026 samples are not identical or statistically representative of all small and medium-sized businesses in Kazakhstan. The figures therefore reflect reported experiences and scenarios based on surveyed companies’ responses, rather than measured growth across the entire small and medium enterprises (SME) sector. Local businesses put the platform to work The survey and forum also highlighted companies using TikTok to expand their audiences and sales. One Shymkent-based clothing brand increased its TikTok audience by approximately 15,000 followers over one year, while sales rose by about 20%, according to the company. A one-hour TikTok livestream generates an average of 15 to 20 inquiries and between three and six sales. In East Kazakhstan, a natural honey producer has focused on organic content showcasing its products and beekeeping operations. The company has found customers outside Kazakhstan and links growth in export revenue to interest from international audiences generated by its TikTok content. One of Almaty’s fast-food chains has used the platform to build relationships with its audience. Its account now has more than 1 million followers, and some customers travel from other cities to visit the restaurant after discovering it through videos. Over four years, the business has expanded to 13 locations in Almaty and plans to enter another city soon. Last year, it received a TikTok award for Best Small Business Account. The team attributes its success to keeping content authentic and lively, saying this helps sustain audience interest and turn casual viewers into regular customers. Expanding support for entrepreneurs TikTok says it is seeking to expand its role in Kazakhstan’s business community beyond content distribution. “Every business has its own story. Sometimes it begins with a small idea, a family enterprise or a short video that unexpectedly resonates with thousands of people,” said Yulia Kushnir, TikTok’s head of business development for Central Asia and Eastern Europe. “The updated study shows that Kazakh entrepreneurs are increasingly confident and effective in using TikTok, and that the platform is increasingly becoming not only a place to raise awareness but also a full-fledged tool for promotion, sales and growth. We want businesses of every size to be able to find their audience on TikTok and grow with it — and we are doing everything we can to make that possible,” she said. Atameken said the research was intended to better understand how new technologies work in practice and what opportunities they offer domestic businesses. “For Atameken, it is important to understand how new technologies work in practice and what opportunities they offer domestic entrepreneurs. That is why studying business experience has become one of the areas of our cooperation with TikTok,” said Aslan Kaligazin, a member of the board and deputy chairman of the board of the Atameken National Chamber of Entrepreneurs. “This year, with the active participation of regional chambers of entrepreneurs, we updated the study and collected practical examples of how Kazakh companies use the platform,” he said. The partnership builds on several initiatives. TikTok for Business was introduced in Kazakhstan in 2021, offering tools for businesses of different sizes. In 2022, TikTok and Astana Hub launched the TikTok Startup Academy, which had graduated three cohorts by 2025. In 2024, TikTok and Atameken organized the Made in Kazakhstan competition, bringing together more than 800 micro and small enterprises working on social and environmental projects. The latest survey suggests that TikTok has become a regular part of marketing for many of the businesses questioned, with some reporting substantial revenue linked to their activity on the platform. Whether that translates into a comparable impact across Kazakhstan’s wider SME sector remains an open question. The post TikTok Becomes Business Tool for Kazakhstan’s Entrepreneurs, Survey Finds appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: OpenAI prepares lobbying blitz for a post-midterm Washington
body:
OpenAI is gearing up for a political lobbying and PR push after the US midterms. According to Axios , the company is bracing for a tougher fight in Washington if Democrats win control of the House.
After two years under a friendly administration, big tech companies with close ties to President Trump are facing growing regulatory pressure. Rivals like Meta are already building bridges to Democrats. OpenAI's policy chief Chris Lehane plans to steer the AI debate through 2028 with a mix of new and repackaged proposals. The pitch centers on one idea: AI doesn't replace people. To back that up, OpenAI is proposing binding safety rules that build on earlier ideas . Lehane calls them "speed limits."
The company is also responding to growing local backlash against data centers. According to Axios, OpenAI wants to rebrand the facilities as "AI Compute Campuses" and is promising economic benefits to host communities. Lehane says the company's top priority in the new Congress is fast-tracking safety rules for frontier models. Ad Ad

title: UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ends after 35 years
body:
The United Nations' long-running peacekeeping mission for the disputed Western Sahara ceased operations Sunday after 35 years, as a result of a US-Russia standoff at UN headquarters over the territory’s future.
The end of the mission raises concerns about stability in the region. Rich in minerals and fisheries, Western Sahara is a vast desert territory roughly the size of Colorado along Africa’s northwestern Atlantic coast. Once ruled by Spain, it is claimed by both Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front .
“This 1 November 2026 marks the start of the liquidation period,” Stéphane Dujarric, spokesperson for the UN secretary general, said in a statement. “A smaller team reporting to the United Nations’ Department of Operational Support will oversee the orderly transportation of assets belonging to troop-contributing countries to their respective nations, and the appropriate disposal of equipment belonging to the United Nations.''
The mission had been repeatedly extended since it was established in 1991. In the UN Security Council on Friday, Russia vetoed a draft US resolution that would have supported Morocco’s demand for sovereignty over Western Sahara and ended the peacekeeping mission next year.
Then a rival Russian resolution to extend the mission was voted down. The disagreement led to an abrupt end of the force’s mandate.
Morocco’s royal palace welcomed the non-renewal of the mission. It called it an “instrument to internationalize the dispute.''
The Polisario Front, backed by Algeria, called it “an unacceptable decision.'' The Algerian foreign ministry said it profoundly regrets the non-renewal of the mandate and criticized what it called the ‘’excessive bias' ' of the US draft resolution.
The UN classifies Western Sahara as a “non-self-governing territory,” while critics of Morocco’s control describe it as Africa’s last colony. Morocco administers nearly all of the disputed territory, except for a narrow strip known as the “free zone” that lies east of a Moroccan-built sand wall.
After Morocco annexed it in 1975, the dispute escalated into an armed conflict that lasted more than 15 years and claimed more than 16,000 lives on both sides, according to the French Senate.
Bringing Western Sahara under its full sovereignty has been a central objective of Morocco’s foreign policy for decades. Rabat, which has secured the backing of a growing number of Western capitals, including Washington, Paris and London, refers to the territory as its southern provinces. The dispute has become a defining feature of Morocco’s diplomacy, with the kingdom often measuring its relations with other countries by their position on the issue.
The Polisario Front seeks independence for the territory, which it considers the homeland of the Indigenous Sahrawi people. Operating from refugee camps in the Algerian city of Tindouf, the movement aims to establish an independent Sahrawi Republic. Mainly backed by Algeria, Russia and South Africa, the Polisario has seen its international support dwindle in recent years.
A UN-brokered cease-fire took effect in 1991. The agreement also paved the way for the creation of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara, known as MINURSO.
The settlement plan provided for a referendum on self-determination, with independence among the options. But the vote never materialized. Morocco wanted the voter list to include Sahrawis living in the territory it controls, while the Polisario objected, arguing that their inclusion would tilt the outcome toward integration with Morocco. The movement insisted on using Spain’s colonial census to determine voter eligibility.
Twenty MINURSO personnel lost their lives in the mission. The UN force was authorized to have 534 personnel, and its 2026-2027 budget was more than $62 million. The top military contributors to the force were Egypt, Ghana and Pakistan.
As the mission ends, the UN secretary-general ‘’calls upon all parties to respect and promote the rights of the people of Western Sahara,'' Dujarric said, and “remains concerned about the security situation throughout the Territory and the risk of escalation of hostilities. He calls on all concerned to exercise maximum restraint.”
The Polisario withdrew from the ceasefire in 2020 after clashes and the territory has since remained the scene of tensions and low-intensity hostilities, the UN said last month.
Western Sahara is the major flashpoint in the rivalry between regional heavyweights Morocco and Algeria. Algiers, which arms, funds and hosts the Polisario Front, sees full Moroccan sovereignty over the territory as a major diplomatic defeat. The two countries severed diplomatic relations in 2021, and the end of the mission risks further straining ties and fueling an arms race.

title: Russian medics accompanied those who decided to leave Alyoshki for Ukraine — Lantratova
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. Russian medics accompanied Alyoshki residents who decided to evacuate to Ukraine, human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova said at a press conference summing up the results of the Alyoshki humanitarian mission.
"For those who wanted to travel to Ukraine, we organized a special convoy to take them to Anapa [in Russia’s southern Krasnodar Region]. From there, a flight was arranged to take them to Ukraine via the Gomel Region in Belarus. Staff members from our office accompanied them. Since there were several bedridden individuals, we provided our own medical personnel to accompany them. We provided food, water, and everything else they needed and ensured their complete safety," she noted.

title: Economic growth centers are in collective South — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. Economic growth centers are not in Europe but in the collective South, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said at a briefing.
The natural gas market in itself is much larger than the European one, the Kremlin Spokesman noted.
"Global economic centers are far from being in Europe, they are actually in the collective South," Peskov stressed.

title: Power station drone strike escalates water crisis in White Nile’s Kosti
body: Drinking water supplies and healthcare services in Kosti City in Sudan’s White Nile State have been severely disrupted following a power outage triggered by a drone attack on the Um Dabakir thermal power station on Thursday, 29 October 2026. The disruption has affected water supplies, forcing the authorities to operate the New Kosti water station on fuel according to a restricted schedule. In an appeal to residents, the Kosti Water Administration said the station will run on fuel from 2 p.m. to 10 p.m. on Thursdays. On other days, operations will be limited to operating from 6 a.m. to 11 a.m. and from 6 p.m. to 11 p.m. In the health sector, Salah-Eddin Ahmed, secretary-general of the Friends of Kidney Patients Association, warned that fuel and water shortages could disrupt hemodialysis sessions at the Kosti center. “The center requires one and a half barrels of fuel daily to operate its generators, at a daily cost of three million Sudanese pounds,” he said. “The center also needs water to carry out dialysis sessions, with the associated cost reaching one million pounds.” Ahmed said solar power could serve as an alternative to electricity and called on the state governor and relevant authorities to provide solar panels, as had been done at other centers. Meanwhile, Al-Jaili Al-Tayyib, a resident of Kosti, said several neighborhoods including Al-Tarafiya, Al-Shabbak and Abu Sharif lacked water distribution networks. He added that fuel shortages and rising prices had further compounded residents’ hardship. “Our problems are many, particularly when it comes to fuel availability. We cannot find it at all, and fuel station operators refuse to supply us,” he said, urging the authorities to ensure adequate supplies. The effects of the attack have raised fears that the disruption of essential services in the city could worsen, particularly given the reliance of water stations and healthcare facilities on electricity and fuel. Residents are calling for urgent intervention to secure water and fuel supplies and ensure the continuity of life-saving services. The post Power station drone strike escalates water crisis in White Nile’s Kosti appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Attack on Izium leaves one dead and 11 injured, damaging homes and stores
body:
Oleh Syniehubov, head of the Kharkiv Regional Military Administration, reported this on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
“The number of casualties from the Russian shelling in Izium has risen to 11. In particular, an 11-year-old boy suffered an acute stress reaction,” the post reads.
According to Syniehubov, around 9:00 a.m., the occupiers struck the city with several guided aerial bombs. In particular, the Russians hit a five-story apartment building; as a result of the strike, the building was destroyed from the first to the third floors. Another strike hit a 4-story residential building.
At least 14 private homes, 2 stores, and 6 cars were also damaged. An assessment of the area and cleanup efforts are ongoing, Syniehubov added.
As previously reported, on the morning of November 2, Russian troops attacked Izium with guided aerial bombs . One person was killed, and at least three others were injured. The city’s military administration reported that Izium is completely without power due to damage to high-voltage power lines.

title: China not interested in US-Russia summit on Ukraine, German president claims
body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has shown no interest in hosting a three-way summit on Ukraine with Russia and the U.S., German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said on Nov. 1 after speaking with the Chinese leader in Beijing.
From Xi's perspective, there are no preparations underway for Chinese-hosted Ukraine talks, Steinmeier said in an interview with German television, when recounting his talks with his Chinese counterpart on Oct. 30.
China's leader was surprised by the proposal and noted that European officials should be involved in resolving the war, as it is taking place on the European continent, the German president added.
While U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Xi may meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in Shenzhen, China, in mid-November, the latest comments cast doubt on whether Ukraine would be on the agenda.
The U.S. president has expressed readiness to meet with his Russian and Chinese counterparts in November — specifically to discuss arms control and denuclearization.
But the Wall Street Journal also reported, citing its sources, that Putin wanted to use the meeting to secure a peace deal in Ukraine favorable to Moscow, capitalizing on the warming U.S.-Russia ties.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov confirmed on Nov. 2 that preparations for a meeting between Putin and Xi at the APEC summit are underway, but said there are no details regarding a possible three-way summit with Trump.
Kyiv has lambasted the idea of a peace summit in China without Ukraine at the table, urging a meeting between President Volodymyr Zelensky, Trump, and Putin instead to negotiate an end to the war.
While claiming neutrality in the war, China has been a key economic lifeline for Russia during the full-scale war and the leading source of dual-use goods fueling the Russian defense industry.

title: 2027 Politics Watch – Sunday’s Roundup: Atiku challenges Tinubu on power as Kwankwaso tells him to stand down
body:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, challenged President Bola Tinubu’s electricity record on Sunday and proposed replacing Nigeria’s tariff-band system.
Atiku’s intervention followed the All Progressives Congress’ (APC’s) defence of President Tinubu’s apparent failure to deliver on his 2023 campaign promise to provide reliable electricity and end estimated billing.
In a statement by campaign spokesperson Dele Alake , the APC argued that the president’s pledge should be considered alongside his undertaking to explain any shortfall before seeking a second term.
The party cited the Electricity Act 2023, metering programmes, transmission investments, state-level regulatory reforms and a ₦4 trillion bond programme intended to settle verified legacy debts in the power sector.
It also claimed that more than 1.5 million electricity customers had been metered under the administration.
Atiku rejected the defence in a response issued through Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council.
“The APC should spare Nigerians the spectacle of celebrating paperwork while homes and businesses remain in darkness,” he said.
He argued that outages and estimated billing persisted despite the administration’s interventions and questioned the fairness of the existing tariff-band system.
Under the system, consumers pay different tariffs according to the number of hours of electricity they are expected to receive.
Atiku said Band A customers often paid approximately ₦209.50 per kilowatt-hour before value-added tax, even when supply was unreliable.
He also questioned the administration’s reported plan to end electricity subsidies from 2027 and its possible effect on household bills.
His proposed alternative would involve working with state governments and regulators to replace the tariff bands with a pricing arrangement more closely tied to electricity actually delivered.
The proposal has not been accompanied by a tariff formula, subsidy plan or costings.
The competing positions address different aspects of the electricity problem. The APC points to legislation, infrastructure, and debt settlement, while Atiku proposes changes to consumer pricing.
Neither the government’s cited interventions nor a different tariff structure, on their own, establish that households will receive more reliable electricity.
Regulatory records on metering, service hours and distribution performance would provide a firmer basis for assessing the APC’s claims. Atiku’s campaign, meanwhile, would need to explain how its alternative would affect consumers’ bills and electricity providers’ revenues.
Meanwhile, Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice-presidential candidate Rabiu Kwankwaso has questioned the regional basis of Atiku’s candidacy.
Speaking to journalists in Kano on Sunday , the former governor urged Atiku to withdraw from the presidential contest and support Peter Obi, the NDC candidate.
Mr Kwankwaso argued that the South had not completed its turn under Nigeria’s informal arrangement for rotating the presidency between North and South.
He said respecting that understanding remained important to national cohesion and said his acceptance of the vice-presidential nomination was consistent with the principle.
He questioned the ADC’s choice of a northern presidential candidate.
The public disagreement exposes a potential obstacle to cooperation between the two camps. Any attempt to negotiate a common presidential ticket would have to address their competing positions on zoning.
The principle is political rather than constitutional. Nigeria’s Constitution does not reserve the presidency for either region, and Atiku remains eligible to contest if he meets the applicable electoral requirements.
Neither Atiku nor the ADC had issued a verified response to Mr Kwankwaso’s remarks by filing time.
The intervention also came as Atiku’s campaign faced complaints from within the ADC about established party officials’ involvement in election preparations
A Sunday PUNCH investigation reported complaints by ADC officials in the South-west that Atiku’s associates were organising campaign activities without sufficiently involving established party structures.
The concerns had been raised during a meeting with ADC National Secretary Rauf Aregbesola in Ibadan on 4 September.
Atiku subsequently met officials virtually and requested five nominees from each of the six South-west states for campaign appointments.
Some officials said the consultations had not resolved their complaints.
Adewole Ijaogbomo, chairman of ADC local government chairmen in Lagos, alleged that recognised officials were being sidelined.
Some chairmen who travelled to Abuja for a meeting on 17 September also reportedly complained that they received no transport support.
Mr Shaibu’s explanation addresses the allegation of exclusion from formally constituted councils. It does not settle the separate complaint about how campaign activities are being coordinated before those appointments.
PREMIUM TIMES had not received a response from ADC National Publicity Secretary Bolaji Abdullahi by filing time.
The dispute comes ahead of the party’s presidential campaign launch in Sokoto on Wednesday, 4 November .
The event was postponed from 31 October, with the party citing planning and coordination considerations.
Preparations have also been accompanied by allegations of interference, including a reported confrontation involving ADC governorship candidate Manir Dan’iya .
Atiku and former Sokoto governor Aminu Tambuwal condemned the reported incident and demanded an investigation.
The Sokoto APC disputed allegations of politically motivated interference, while the police said they were investigating.
The confrontation was reported to have occurred on Friday. The subsequent reactions and demands for security protection did not establish another attack on Sunday.
The ADC also faces a separate challenge from a faction associated with Nafiu Gombe, which announced a North-west campaign council on Saturday.
That announcement did not, by itself, change INEC’s recognition of the party’s leadership or presidential candidate.
Wednesday’s launch will bring the campaign’s organisational and security concerns into public view as Atiku seeks to focus attention on his policy proposals.
The disputes over party arrangements were not confined to presidential campaigns.
In Kano, an INEC official cited a Federal High Court order to explain why NDC governorship candidate Abdulsalam Gwarzo and his running mate, Rabiu Mustapha, were missing from the commission’s updated candidate list.
According to a report by the Nigerian Tribune , the unnamed senior official said INEC had no objection to Mr Gwarzo’s candidacy but was restrained from publishing the names by an ex parte order issued on 27 October.
That account differs from the NDC’s earlier explanation that the omission resulted from a computer error.
It also distinguishes a cshows ourt-reshows shows shows lated restriction on publication from an outright rejection of the nominations.
PREMIUM TIMES had not independently examined the order or established the next hearing date.
In Cross River, meanwhile, LEADERSHIP reported that Nkoyo Toyo and Magam Dino Ntui appeared on INEC’s updated listt as the ADC’s governorship and deputy governorship candidates.
The APC faced a separate court-related dispute in Zamfara North, where a fresh senatorial primary was scheduled for Monday, 2 November, after a Federal High Court nullified the May exercise and the Court of Appeal upheld that decision.
Aspirant Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi objected to the arrangements , saying he learnt of the timetable through social media.
He complained about the short notice, questioned security arrangements and raised concerns about the involvement of former governor Bello Matawalle.
Mr Shinkafi also referred to further litigation involving Senator Sahabi Ya’u.
The operative effect of any pending Supreme Court proceedings needs to be established from court records.
The dispute puts the conduct of the fresh primary, aspirants’ participation, and INEC’s monitoring of the exercise under scrutiny.
Political mobilisation continued to attract donations and empowerment pledges, but the full financial arrangements were not publicly detailed.
In Osun on Saturday, the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement received 30 campaign vehicles reportedly donated by Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo.
A similar donation of 30 vehicles had previously been reported by PREMIUM TIMES in Imo State .
The reported donations total 60 vehicles across the two states. Their purchase costs, ownership arrangements and applicable campaign-finance disclosures were not established in the cited accounts.
Other initiatives combined financial assistance with political mobilisation.
On 29 October, First Lady Oluremi Tinubu announced Renewed Hope Initiative assistance for elderly citizens and persons with disabilities, with APC senatorial candidates assigned coordination roles.
She said beneficiaries should not be selected on the basis of party affiliation.
The announced allocation was ₦110 million per participating senatorial district, divided into two ₦55 million components.
However, the specified payments of ₦200,000 each to 500 beneficiaries amount to ₦100 million.
The published direct-payment figures therefore leave ₦10 million unaccounted for in the breakdown. That difference does not establish wrongdoing, but the programme’s detailed budget would be needed to explain it.
In Kano, the Leke Abejide Foundation announced a ₦600 million programme comprising ₦500 million in interest-free loans and ₦100 million for widows at an event associated with mobilisation for Tinubu and APC candidates.
Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf reportedly pledged another ₦100 million, while organisers discussed recruiting polling-unit coordinators from among participating women.
The reports do not establish that assistance was conditional on support for any candidate or that campaign-finance rules were breached.
In Jigawa, some PDP and NDC members reportedly defected to the APC during the inauguration of a pro-Tinubu grassroots campaign office.
Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, Director-General of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), led the event.
Some defectors cited development interventions associated with the agency among their reasons for joining the APC.
There is no established evidence that NITDA resources were improperly used for the political activity.
The funding arrangements for these initiatives matter because private political donations, charitable assistance and expenditure involving public institutions are subject to different accountability requirements.

title: One Last Thing: Sarah Hermez on room service, bad music and hating questionnaires
body: Sarah Hermez has spent more than a decade proving that fashion can be a vehicle for something greater. A Parsons graduate, the Lebanese designer and educator returned home and, in 2011, co-founded Creative Space Beirut , a tuition-free fashion school created to give talented young people access to an industry that might otherwise have remained closed to them. The journey has not been straightforward. Hermez has kept the school going through Lebanon’s economic collapse, the Covid-19 pandemic, the 2020 Beirut port explosion and regional wars. Creative Space’s alumni have gone on to establish their own labels and win major industry recognition, including prizes from Fashion Trust Arabia. Now, Hermez herself has been recognised with a place on The Business of Fashion’s BoF 500 , cementing her position among the people helping to shape the global fashion industry. We caught up with her for our One Last Thing questionnaire. What is your favourite time of day and why? When I’m asleep. Because I’m asleep. What is your favourite restaurant anywhere in the world? Room service. When was the first time you realised your parents were human? I’m still convinced they’re not. What do you want to be when you grow up? Free. Do you have any hidden talents? I’m very smart, but it’s very hidden. Your favourite book? Facebook. What type of music can’t you stand? My husband’s. What puts you in a bad mood? Questionnaires. What can you not live without? Ice cubes. Dream dinner guests? I can’t cook. Sitting on the sofa or out with friends? Out with the sofa. What smell takes you straight back to childhood? Cigars. What food takes you back to childhood? Escalope. Which city do you love, but would hate to live in? Paris. Can you play a musical instrument? No. I married a musician instead. Have you ever been on a motorcycle? I’m not comfortable answering this question. Any words to live by? Trust the process. Biggest pet peeve? Questionnaires. Do you believe in aliens? Sure. What is your favourite Arabic word? Merci. The most niche thing you watch on YouTube? That’s between me and YouTube. How do you take your tea? Teacup. What makes you cry? I try to keep it all in until my eye starts twitching. What do social algorithms think you’re interested in? Design, babies, dogs, unhinged AI-generated short films, and random videos of people falling over. TikTok or Instagram? Instagram. What is it about you that would surprise most people? I’m originally Assyrian, from Iraq and Armenia. What was the last thing you did for the first time? Became pregnant.

title: If You Have Lungs, You Can Get Lung Cancer
body: . The Pope’s diagnosis should change how Africa thinks about lung cancer, and about TB By Caleb Egwuenu A diagnosis that should change how we think On Tuesday, 13 October 2026, surgeons at Rome’s Gemelli hospital removed the lower lobe of Pope Leo XIV’s right lung. The Vatican then confirmed what the tissue showed: the 71-year-old pontiff has lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer. The nodule was found early, during routine medical tests, and was well localised. And Pope Leo is not known to have ever been a smoker. That last fact matters more than any other this November, Lung Cancer Awareness Month. It breaks the most dangerous myth about this disease: that it only happens to smokers. The truth is simpler and harder. If you have lungs, you can get lung cancer. Not just a smoker’s disease Smoking remains the leading cause of lung cancer, and quitting is still the best thing a smoker can do for their lungs. But as many as 1 in 5 lung cancers occur in people who have never smoked. The World Health Organization’s cancer agency, IARC, now ranks lung cancer in never-smokers as the fifth highest cause of cancer deaths worldwide. In never-smokers it appears almost always as adenocarcinoma, the same type the Pope has. Adenocarcinoma is now the most common lung cancer worldwide. In 2022 it made up 45.6% of cases in men and 59.7% in women. As one MD Anderson oncologist put it, “the face of lung cancer is changing”: more women, more younger people, more people who never touched a cigarette. What else is in the air we breathe IARC estimates that about 200,000 adenocarcinoma cases in 2022 were linked to outdoor air pollution alone. The American Cancer Society also lists radon gas, asbestos, radiation and secondhand smoke as risks. For many Africans, the most dangerous air is inside the home. Around 2.1 billion people still cook over open fires or inefficient stoves burning wood, charcoal, dung, crop waste or kerosene. In sub-Saharan Africa, 923 million people lacked access to clean cooking in 2022. In a poorly ventilated kitchen, smoke can carry fine particles at 100 times acceptable levels. WHO lists lung cancer among the diseases this causes, and women and children carry the heaviest burden because they spend the most time by the fire. Add the exhaust from generators and old vehicles, dust from mines and quarries, open burning of waste, and asbestos roofing still found in older buildings. A grandmother who has never smoked a day in her life may have breathed more smoke than many smokers. Africa’s blind spot: when cancer is treated as TB In Africa, a persistent cough, weight loss, chest pain or coughing blood usually points one way: tuberculosis. In countries with some of the world’s heaviest TB burdens, Nigeria among them, that instinct often saves lives. It also hides lung cancer in plain sight. The two diseases look alike on a chest X-ray and in the clinic. A patient is started on six months of TB drugs. When they do not improve, the treatment is often restarted. Months pass before anyone asks for a CT scan or a biopsy. A study at Zimbabwe’s largest cancer centre shows the cost. Among 73 patients with confirmed lung cancer: · 53% had been diagnosed with pulmonary TB in the year before their cancer was found · the median delay to a cancer diagnosis was more than eight months, and up to three years · only 15% were diagnosed within three months of first seeking care · 77% had stage IV cancer, already spread, by the time it was found. The authors’ conclusion is blunt: most lung cancer patients there were first misdiagnosed as having TB. The same study notes that only 1% of the world’s recorded lung cancer deaths are reported from Africa. That figure says less about how rare the disease is here than about how rarely we look for it. Compare that with the Pope. His nodule was found early, on a routine test, and removed within days. Most African patients never get that chance. What must change Lung cancer is very treatable when caught early. Surgery, as in the Pope’s case, can remove it completely. The difference between a cure and a late diagnosis is often whether someone thought to look. For health workers : if a patient on TB treatment is not getting better, or their sputum tests keep coming back negative, think cancer. Refer for a CT scan and a biopsy instead of restarting the same drugs. For governments: build lung cancer into TB programmes, which already reach patients with chest symptoms. Fund CT scanners, pathology and thoracic surgery in more than a handful of cities. Speed up access to clean cooking fuel and enforce clean-air rules. For families and communities: usea cough lasting more than three weeks, coughing blood, chest pain, hoarseness or unexplained weight loss needs a proper check, whether or not the person smokes. Ask the doctor directly: could this be cancer? Cook outdoors or in well-ventilated spaces where you can, and keep children away from smoke. For all of us: drop the stigma. A lung cancer patient is not someone who “brought it on themselves”. They could be a market woman, a miner, a teacher, a child of a cook, or a Pope. This November, Move Against Cancer Africa (MACA) asks every reader to remember one sentence and pass it on. If you have lungs, you can get lung cancer. Knowing that could save a life. *Caleb Egwuenu is Executive Director of Move Against Cancer Africa (MACA), a pan-African cancer non-profit, and Deputy Chair of the IASLC Patient Advocacy Committee.

title: Those who wished to leave Alyoshki for Ukraine got there — Russia's ombudswoman
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. The people who decided to leave Alyoshki for Ukraine have already arrived safely, Russia’s Commissioner for Human Rights Yana Lantratova said at a press conference after the humanitarian mission in Alyoshki.
Lantratova noted that these people were accompanied by Russian doctors.
"As far as I know, we are in regular contact with my colleague, Ukraine’s ombudsman, and the people have already safely arrived home," she said.

title: Russian LNG supplies to Europe up 10% over 9M 2026
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies to the European Union gained 10% annually in January - September 2026 and totaled 16.5 bln cubic meters, according to TASS estimates based on data of Bruegel, a European analytical center.
EU imports of Russian LNG totaled about 16.5 bln cubic meters over nine months, compared to 15 bln cubic meters a year earlier. In particular, deliveries of Russian gas in Europe totaled 1.1 bln cubic meters, 59% more than in August and flat in annual terms.
Total LNG imports by Europe amounted to 10.4 bln cubic meters in September, according to Bruegel. Natural gas procurements by EU countries lost 5% to 104 bln cubic meters in January - September 2026.

title: Over 50 foreign journalists covered Alyoshki humanitarian mission — ombudswoman
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. More than 50 journalists from various countries, including the US and Ukraine, worked in Alyoshki during the humanitarian mission, Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova said at a press conference on its results.
"A pool of reporters worked alongside us, including US journalists whose participation had been approved by the US side. There were representatives of Ukrainian and Russian media, as well as journalists from various countries around the world. If I’m not mistaken, the quota was for more than 50 people. War correspondents also worked there," she noted.

title: My reflex of assuming our servers need ever-growing amounts of RAM
body:
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access some part of my blog (Wandering Thoughts) or CSpace , the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on Wandering Thoughts I'm experimenting with (attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your browser of choice, you can contact me at my current place at the university (you should be able to work out the email address from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're using and so on, ideally with its exact User-Agent string.
I am not blocking Inoreader's feed fetcher or considering it to be too old, and it routinely fetches feeds from me. I don't know why Inoreader is showing you this page. It is possible that they're periodically trying to fetch feeds or pages with an old browser HTTP User-Agent (or an actual old browser) and taking the results of that fetch (this page) as what they should show people instead of the results of their syndication feed fetcher agents. This is a bad mistake today; the results of modern HTTP fetches depend partly on the HTTP User-Agent used .
Much like Inoreader, Feedly is periodically fetching my syndication feeds with a fake, old browser HTTP User-Agent header, which fails, and is then grimly latching on to the results for their actual feed fetching with their regular Feedly HTTP User-Agent. There is nothing I can do about this; you should contact Feedly support, if you can find them. See this comment of mine in Wandering Thoughts for more details.
Due to an ongoing attack, you may need to change the "User Agent Brand Masking" setting so that your Vivaldi identifies itself as Vivaldi, instead of Google Chrome. This applies to even the current version of Vivaldi.
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is, and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses (which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival crawler and can crawl my blog (Wandering Thoughts) .

title: Elbit Systems to build SIGMA and PULS artillery training facility under 15-year Israeli agreement
body: The ministry’s Defense Procurement Directorate arranged the contract in cooperation with the IDF Ground Forces, with its Land Procurement Unit leading the project. The agreement is valued at approximately NIS 600 million. The facility will include classrooms, driving simulators and mission simulators for Artillery Corps commanders and soldiers. The ministry said the training approach would shorten qualification times, improve proficiency and reduce costs and maintenance demands on operational platforms. “The agreement we signed is significant news for strengthening the power and readiness of the IDF, and directly reflects the Ministry’s strategy of enhancing operational readiness, strengthening Israeli industry and ensuring a long-term technological and logistical response for field forces,” said Zeev Landau, the ministry’s deputy director general and head of the Defense Procurement Directorate. “The combination of advanced training and simulation technologies with a full, long-term support envelope will help the IDF Artillery Corps realize the full firepower potential of the SIGMA howitzer and the new systems, while saving and optimally utilizing resources.” “Elbit, as a partner to the needs of the defense establishment and the IDF, has developed for the Ground Forces one of the world’s most advanced training and instruction arrays,” said Boaz Cohen, executive vice president and general manager of Elbit Systems Land. “The Artillery School and the training array for Artillery Corps soldiers will enable the Artillery Corps to receive high-quality and efficient training, maintaining the fire array at the highest level of readiness.”

title: Russians advance near Huliaipilske, Hirke in Zaporizhia region, expand red zone by 4.84 sq km – DeepState
body:
Russian occupiers have increased the area under their control near the settlements of Huliaypilske and Hirke in Zaporizhia region by 4.84 square metre, while the gray zone in these areas shrank by 2.44 square metre, the DeepState OSINT project reports.

"The enemy has advanced near Huliaypilske and Hirke," according to a post on the project's Telegram channel on Monday.

Map data shows that the red zone expanded to 47,416.52 square metre from 47,411.68 square metre the previous day. At the same time, the gray zone contracted from 62.8 square metre to 60.36 square metre.

title: WPL 2026/27: Police Ladies continues impressive start; FC Savannah record first win
body: Police Ladies continued their strong start to the 2026/27 GoldFields Women’s Premier League following their victory over Immigration Ladies. In an all-security affair, Police Ladies sealed a thumping 4-0 victory over Immigration Ladies at the Alajo Astro Turf to move to the top of the league table in the Southern Zone. Fidous Yakubu scored a brace in the fixture, while Sophia Agyakwa and Beatrice Tsifokor scored the other two to give Abu Kassim Tabasu’s side all three points. In Takoradi, Cecilia Acquah scored in the 38th minute for Hasaacas Ladies, who recorded their first league victory over Jonina Ladies in three games. Barbara Marfo was the star of the day for Oak Ladies who defeated FC Samartex Ladies for their first league win over the season at the Hearts Complex. Epiphany Warriors fought from a goal sown to salvage a point in their home game against Army Ladies. Both teams are now without a win in their first two games. LadyStrikers also made it two wins from their opening two games of the season after Betsheba Nyarko scored the only goal of the game in their victory over Roots Sistaz. In the Northern Zone, Ampem Darkoa Ladies were exempted from action due to their participation in the CAF Women’s Champions League, leaving their game against Supreme Ladies postponed. Ashanti Ladies recovered from their defeat last weekend to claim a 1-0 win over Northern Ladies in the latter’s first outing of the season. Dreamz Ladies continue their search for a first win of the season as they were held again to a goalless draw by Tamale Super Ladies at home. Prisons Ladies sealed a 1-0 victory over Fosu Royal Ladies on the second match week while FC Savannah defeated Dormaa Candy Soccer Ladies 2-0.

title: Court users stranded as Kumasi High Court and other lower courts shut down over JUSAG strike
body: Court users seeking various services have been left stranded at court premises in Kumasi as critical staff of the judiciary lay down their tools over their 2026 salary review and outstanding arrears. The Kumasi High Court and other lower courts in the Ashanti region, like in many parts of the country, have been shut down as the ongoing industrial action by the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) brings the judiciary to its knees. A tour of the Kumasi High Court, the Court of Appeal, the Asokwa Circuit Court and the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) Court confirmed that the facilities were closed with no judiciary staff around but a handful of persons seeking legal services. Some clients who had cases scheduled for hearing today, Monday, November 2, arrived at the court premises only to find the gates locked and adorned with red cloth announcing the strike. One of the affected persons, Joyce Konama, whose case was scheduled for judgment at the High Court on Monday, expressed her frustration. Madam Konama noted that she was unaware of the strike and had travelled a considerable distance to attend the proceedings only to meet empty courtrooms. “I didn’t know they were on strike today, and I am very worried after travelling all the way from my town to find the court closed. The government should fast-track negotiations on their conditions of service,” she said. Speaking to Joy News, some of the affected court users appealed to the government to prioritise the welfare and conditions of service of judicial service staff to ensure the smooth administration of justice. “If this strike continues for days, things will escalate in this country,” some of the clients warned.

title: AI Knittaker
body:
Skip your next meeting. Let an AI Knittaker take it, while you visit Iceland instead!
Introducing AI Knittakers. Not Artificial Intelligence—real Authentic Icelandic knitters who attend your “could’ve been an email” meetings for you, skillfully knitting one important takeaway (if there was one), and free you up for something better.
AI Knittaker works in three easy steps. Pick a Knittaker. Invite them to your meeting. Get your knitted summary. Meantime, you escape to do something more fun.
Real Icelandic knitters, each with a free hour this week.
Choose a free hour. The invite lands in your inbox, ready to forward.
One knitted takeaway, if there was one. Meanwhile you do something better.
Meet the Icelanders willing to sit through your meetings…so you don't have to!
Times shown in your time zone (Reykjavik).
Salka Sól Eyfeld is our Chief AI Knittaker for Visit Iceland’s AI Knittakers campaign. An Icelandic singer, actress, presenter and lifelong knitter, she first learned to knit at the age of eight and still regularly meets friends to knit and socialise. Her passion for knitting has helped inspire a younger generation to pick up the needles and embrace the craft. She also co-authored UNA , a knitting book created in collaboration with Sjöfn from Stroff Knitting.
A prominent and versatile figure in Iceland’s creative scene, Salka is known for fronting the reggae band AmabAdamA, her work with Reykjavíkurdætur and her role in the acclaimed Icelandic drama Trapped . Her creative career spans music, theatre, film and television. She has composed music for theatre productions, performed on stage, appeared in films and television series, written theatrical productions and lent her voice to countless animated characters.
She has also worked with national broadcaster RÚV, served as a judge on Iceland’s The Voice and won Female Vocalist of the Year at the Icelandic Music Awards.
Bergþór Pálsson is one of Visit Iceland’s AI Knittakers. An Icelandic baritone singer, actor, voice teacher and experienced knitter, his career has spanned opera, operetta, musical theatre and stage performance, including appearances with the Icelandic Opera and as a soloist with the Iceland Symphony Orchestra.
Bergþór first learned to knit decades ago while working night shifts and later returned to the craft more seriously while performing at the National Theatre of Iceland. His projects have included traditional Icelandic waistcoats, intricately patterned sweaters, hats and handmade gifts for his family.
Iceland’s capital has colorful rooftops, geothermal pools, and a harbor that’s close by. Our AI Knittakers will tell you it’s the perfect place to find culture and cafes as you start or end your stay.
From the Golden Circle and South Coast to glaciers, volcanoes, and the Westman Islands, South Iceland has it all. Our local AI Knittakers especially love its geothermal wonders, charming towns, and breathtaking scenery.
Discover the historic Silver Circle, magical Snæfellsnes Peninsula, and saga-steeped valleys of Dalir. It's this mix of natural wonders and rich Icelandic history that makes our West Iceland AI Knittakers so proud of their region.
Our Westfjords AI Knittakers adore their remote corner of Iceland for its unspoiled landscapes, dramatic coastlines, and rich folklore. With few crowds and endless natural beauty, it's a paradise for adventurous explorers.
Steam rises from the ground, black lava stretches to the sea and the Blue Lagoon waits just minutes from the runway. Our AI Knittakers will tell you this is where Iceland shows off its wild side.
From sweeping valleys and rugged mountains to ancient lava fields, North Iceland is a land of contrasts. Ask our local AI Knittakers, and they'll tell you there's nothing quite like its wild beauty and midnight sun.
Snow-capped mountains, deep fjords, cascading waterfalls, and charming fishing villages make East Iceland a peaceful escape. It's no wonder our AI Knittakers love calling this beautiful region home.
Thinking about visiting Iceland? Whether it’s your first trip or your fifth, there’s always something new to discover. Volcanoes, glaciers, geothermal pools, and a few surprises along the way. You might find yourself chasing the Northern Lights, soaking in a hot pool in the rain, or wondering how the landscape can change so much in just a few miles.
Whatever brings you here, there’s plenty more to explore.

title: IDF ends controversial Hebron operation after days of terror probe, forced evacuations
body: The IDF on Monday announced it is exiting the Hebron neighborhood it has occupied since last weekend.The Jerusalem Post reported on Thursday that this might occur as early as this past weekend.None of this was certain, and the situation was highly dynamic, since, to date, pre-elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected the clear recommendation from IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir to leave the area and allow the at least 2,000 evacuated Palestinians to return to their homes.But there was some increased expectation that Netanyahu might show more flexibility to IDF recommendations now that the election has passed and he feels in a stronger political position than expected.The IDF occupied the area in response to last Friday morning's deadly Hamas terrorist attack and noted that the terrorists were connected to a broader Hamas clan in the neighborhood in question, though the IDF never presented concrete evidence of how most of the 2,000 evacuees could be connected to any specific crime.IDF recommended return of evacuated Palestinians last weekAlready by Sunday-Monday of last week, the IDF was recommending that it allow the evacuated Palestinians to return, saying that it had inspected all of the relevant areas, and there was no clear military reason to remain.The forced evacuations from Hebron appear to be different from other recent incidents.Although in early 2025, Israel cleared areas of Jenin, Tulkarm, and Nur al-Shams in the West Bank, evacuating close to 40,000 Palestinians, those areas had experienced well-documented mass terror incidents dating back to early 2022.The IDF carried out multiple temporary evacuations at that time and even sent in the Palestinian Authority to fight large and organized terror groups before undertaking the mass evacuation and destroying several structures in those areas.In contrast, this time, the IDF provided little information about the offenses of the 2,000 evacuated Palestinians, other than to say that they were familially connected to the Hamas-linked Gaza clan.While during the 2015-2016 stabbing intifada and in earlier years, Hebron had been one of the most violent and unstable areas – and there have been some terror incidents emanating from Hebron over the past three years of war – generally, it has not been one of the leading problem spots.In addition, the IDF said it destroyed illegally built structures that could make security operations harder to carry out. However, the military was extremely vague about what those operations were and why entire buildings needed to be destroyed to carry them out.Pressed about how many of the 2,000 hamula (“clan”) members have records linking them to terror (or at a minimum, to rock throwing), multiple IDF sources did not appear to have any specific information on the topic.Rather, the operation seemed to be motivated by public statements made by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz about clearing or destroying the neighborhood of the two men involved in the terror incident on Friday – apparently a collective punishment measure.While Israel has placed closures on terror-emanating areas in the past, it has not carried out mass evacuations and building demolitions to such an extent without a specific connection to those being impacted.Meanwhile, Adalah petitioned the High Court of Justice last Thursday on behalf of Hebron's municipality and seven residents, seeking to halt what it described as forced evacuations and demolitions during an IDF operation, and secure the return of residents ordered out of their homes.The petition asks for an immediate order barring further evacuations and the demolition of homes, businesses and other civilian buildings while the case is considered. It also seeks safe passage for medical teams, emergency vehicles and municipal workers, arguing that sweeping movement restrictions are cutting residents off from essential services.Petition alleges troops seized homes, demolished civilian infrastructureAccording to the petition, troops ordered families in the Ein Deir Baha and al-Jalda neighborhoods of western Hebron to leave their homes around 12:30-1 a.m. on the night of October 23-24. Orders were announced over loudspeakers, leaving residents insufficient time to prepare, the petitioners said.Residents were told they could not return until further notice, without being given a timetable or conditions for their return, the petition alleges. It says some families spent the night outside and some residents were unable to take their vehicles with them.Municipal figures cited in the petition put the number of families affected by the operation at 780, which could reach much higher than the original 2,000 estimate, up to 4,969 people, which itself was up from 488 families and 3,171 people earlier. The petition alleges that troops took over some homes and turned them into military positions, while demolishing civilian buildings and requiring traders to remove goods from their businesses at short notice.It says restrictions also affect residents who remain at home, hindering access to medical treatment and the movement of ambulances and emergency vehicles. According to the municipality's figures cited in the filing, blocked access routes had prevented rubbish collection and left approximately 1,200 tons of waste accumulating across the city by Wednesday.Adalah argues that the scale and open-ended nature of the evacuations violate international humanitarian law. Article 49 of the Fourth Geneva Convention permits temporary evacuation where civilian safety or imperative military reasons require it, and requires evacuees to be returned once hostilities in the area have ended. The petitioners contend that no specific justification has been provided for evacuations on this scale. They argue that barring residents' return indefinitely, while damaging or taking over their homes, risks making their displacement lasting.They also invoke the convention's prohibition on destroying property unless military operations make it absolutely necessary, arguing that a general reference to security needs cannot justify demolitions across residential neighborhoods.The petition further alleges collective punishment, citing both the measures imposed on residents and statements by Israeli officials presenting the operation as a means of exacting a price for the shooting. The convention prohibits punishing protected civilians for offenses they did not personally commit. Adalah said it approached the authorities on Sunday and sent a reminder the following day, but had received no substantive response by the time it filed the petition.The case names the defense minister, the head of IDF Central Command, the military advocate-general and the attorney-general as respondents. Alongside an urgent hearing, the petitioners seek immediate protection against further evacuations and demolitions, followed by orders lifting the challenged restrictions and ensuring residents' safe return.Already on Sunday, the Association for Civil Rights in Israel (ACRI) demanded that displaced residents be allowed to return, movement restrictions be lifted, and demolitions carried out as punishment be halted. It also requested the orders authorizing the measures already taken.It argued that public statements by ministers indicated a punitive purpose, including Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich's description of demolitions as serving as deterrence and as exacting a price for the attack.“No attack, however grave, gives the military license to punish an entire city,” ACRI executive director Noa Sattath said.In an initial decision last Friday, Justice Gila Canfy Steinitz directed the state to respond and said she expected it to refrain from changing the existing situation or demolishing additional buildings, pending a further decision.

title: 'You murdered your son': Right-wing protesters target Eisenkot outside his home
body: Right-wing protesters gathered outside the home of Yashar Party chairman Gadi Eisenkot on Sunday, shouting "traitor" and accusing the former IDF chief of staff of killing his own son, prompting sharp condemnation from his party and political allies, who blamed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the atmosphere of incitement.One protester used a megaphone to shout, "You murdered your son, traitor!" Other demonstrators at the scene joined in chants of "traitor."Footage of the protest sparked widespread condemnation.Eisenkot's party and political allies condemn protesters' remarksEisenkot's party issued a statement saying, "The despicable attack outside the home of party chairman Gadi Eisenkot is a direct result of rotten, unrestrained political leadership that has erased all red lines to remain in power. This is what losing one's way looks like. This is the spirit blowing from Netanyahu's office, and it is further proof of the urgent need to replace his government as soon as possible, for the sake of the State of Israel and Israeli society. At this stage, there is not even an expectation of condemnation. The shame is entirely yours."Democrats Party chairman Maj.-Gen. (res.) Yair Golan issued a message of support for Yashar party head Gadi Eisenkot on Monday morning, after videos circulated on social media showing the crowd outside Eisenkot's home on Sunday evening."I support my friend Gadi Eisenkot in the face of this horrific attack," Golan wrote on Twitter/X. "Soon, we will form a new government [and] put an end to the regime of incitement." "This is the poison that Netanyahu and his people are spreading," Golan added, and also condemned the remarks, criticizing Netanyahu and his associates, whom he accused of responsibility for the rhetoric that led to the verbal attacks."Last night, members of Netanyahu's poison machine came to the home of my partner, Gadi Eisenkot, and shouted at him that he murdered his son. His own son. This is the poison Netanyahu and his people spread. They will cross no line and sink to no depth. This is Netanyahu's legacy, the only policy he will be remembered for leaving behind."Golan went on to express his support for Eisenkot and called for a change in Israeli public discourse: "Soon, we will establish a new government, put an end to the rule of incitement, and restore public discourse in Israel that has responsibility, boundaries, and human dignity."אמש, אנשיה של מכונת הרעל של נתניהו הגיעו לביתו של שותפי, גדי איזנקוט, וצעקו לעברו שהוא רצח את בנו. את הבן שלו. זה הרעל שנתניהו ואנשיו מפיצים. אין גבול שהם לא יחצו ואין תחתית שהם לא יגיעו אליה. זוהי מורשת נתניהו זוהי המדיניות היחידה שתיזכר שהשאיר אחריו. אני מחזק את חברי גדי איזנקוט מול המתקפה הנוראה הזאת. בקרוב נקים ממשלה חדשה, נשים סוף לשלטון ההסתה ונחזיר לישראל שיח ציבורי שיש בו אחריות, גבולות וכבוד אנושי.— Yair Golan - יאיר גולן (@YairGolan1) November 2, 2026Former prime minister and Yesh Atid chairman Yair Lapid also condemned the protest and sent support to Eisenkot and his family."Who are these people? What is Jewish about them? What is Israeli about them? How did sick leadership manage to make them hate like this? We must lead Israel on a new path, and that is what we will do," Lapid's statement read.Journalist Ben Caspit also responded to the remarks heard during the demonstration, referring to Eisenkot's decades of military service and the devastating losses suffered by his family."How dark must the soul be of someone who shouts such a thing at a man who served in uniform for 41 years and then buried a son and two nephews? How dark."

title: GPL 2026/27: Kotoko fine assistant coach Diogo Peral over slap incident
body: Asante Kotoko have fined assistant coach Diogo Peral following his sending-off for slapping a Medeama SC player during their Ghana Premier League clash at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium. The club confirmed the disciplinary action in a statement, describing the coach’s conduct as inconsistent with its values. “The Club wishes to state that such conduct does not reflect the standards and values we uphold at Asante Kotoko. “Consequently, the Club has imposed a fine on Coach Diogo Peral as part of its internal disciplinary measures. This decision reinforces the Club’s commitment to maintaining the highest standards of discipline, professionalism, and accountability.” “We firmly believe that emotions must never compromise the professionalism, discipline, and respect expected of everyone representing this great institution.” Peral was shown a red card after allegedly assaulting Medeama player Ebenezer Adade during the 1-1 draw between the two sides. The Ghana Football Association (GFA) has also charged the Portuguese coach over the incident. Peral has until Wednesday, November 4, to respond to the charge. Meanwhile, the result leaves Kotoko ninth in the league standings with 13 points. The Porcupine Warriors will now shift their focus to their next league fixture against Berekum Chelsea.

title: FSB Reports Interception of More Booby-Trapped FPV Goggles
body:
The press service of Russia’s State Security Service (FSB) reported on Monday, Nov. 2 , that it had intercepted a consignment of booby-trapped first-person view (FPV) drone pilots’ googles. According to their account, an unnamed number of goggles were purportedly donated by volunteers to military units engaged in Russia’s “special military operation” – President Vladimir Putin’s term for his war on Ukraine.
In what appears to be a repeat of the February 2025 scheme , which was attributed to Ukraine’s Main Intelligence Directorate (HUR), the goggles were found to contain improvised explosive devices (IEDs) containing plastic explosives intended to function when the operator switched on the goggles while wearing them.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
According to the FSB the plan was detected when a Russian serviceman in the Volgograd region became suspicious of two sets of goggles he had received in the post, and, remembering warnings issued after last year’s attack, handed them over to the FSB who x-rayed them. This showed that the cooling fans in the equipment had been removed and replaced with IEDs.
The FSB then published a video of the devices being dealt with using a “demining robot,” before issuing a general warning and attempting to track down more devices originating from the source. From the images posted by the FSB, the goggles seemed to be the same or a similar model of goggles used in the earlier attack – the Chinese made Skyzone Cobra X v4 FPV googles.
As in the 2025 attacks this plan followed much the same structure according to the FSB account.
It said that Ukrainian intelligence officers, posing as patriots, used anonymous Telegram accounts to establish contact with and offered support to representatives of legitimate Russian volunteer organizations. Having identified an ongoing need for drones and FPV goggles they offered to supply the goggles directly to individual servicemen asking for the targeted soldiers to post “video messages of gratitude” on social media.
The FSB said, “As a result of the measures taken, security agencies in various regions of the Russian Federation seized a batch of similar IEDs camouflaged inside FPV goggles, transmitted by the enemy through the Russian Post.”
In issuing its general warning, the FSB emphasized that the “perpetrators” “acted covertly, did not disclose their personal information, phone numbers, or place of work, and refused to switch to the Max messenger app.”
It added that it was searching for those who sent the IEDs and further warned that “The Ukrainian special services’ persistent focus on ‘committing terrorist attacks’ against Russian military personnel,” and called on “ volunteers, charitable organizations, and individuals of the need to obtain humanitarian aid from verified sources only and to ensure they [donations] are screened for explosive devices and toxic substances.”
It followed this with a description of how “various items can be disguise IEDs. For example, IEDs disguised as perfume sets, power banks, music speakers, gift figurines, church utensils, auto parts, paving slabs, and heated shoe insoles,” saying these were examples of devices that have previously been defused.
The investigative Department of the FSB in the Volgograd region said it has opened a criminal case under those parts of Russia’s criminal code relating to the illegal trafficking in explosives or explosive devices, the illegal manufacture of explosives, manufacture, alteration or repair of explosive devices and preparation for a terrorist act.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Nigerian soldiers kill top ISWAP commanders including foreign fighters
body:
Troops of Operation Hadin Kai, a joint task force in North-east Nigeria, have killed four high-profile commanders of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), including two “high ranking” Arab fighters in an offensive operation in Kukawa, Borno State, an official has said.
In a statement on Sunday, Mohammed Goni, the task force’s spokesperson, said the offensive, launched on 31 October, targeted ISWAP leadership, identifying those killed as Abu Hajara, a member of the group’s Shura Council, and Abu Walid, a close associate of wanted ISWAP Wali (governor), Ba Shuwa .
Mr Goni, a Nigerian Army captain, said several foot soldiers were also killed in the offensive, which combined air assets and on-the-ground gunfight.
The military spokesperson said the troops recovered many weapons and communication devices.
Mr Goni said the battlefield victory demonstrated the commitment of the task force “in sustaining pressure on terrorist elements across the theatre.”
