This followed a similar victory in Buni Yadi, Yobe State, where troops foiled an ISWAP attack, killing about 55 terrorists, including key commanders such as Ali Gajiri (Munzir), Habu Faruk and Commander Gogore. One soldier was killed, and two others were injured in the Yobe attack, which targeted the North East Theatre Training School (NETTS).

title: Egypt signs $1 billion World Bank deal as war compounds economic pressures
body: Egypt has signed a $1 billion financing agreement with the World Bank, the latest foreign funding for an economy buffeted by regional war, a sliding currency and rising prices. The deal, signed by Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty on Sunday, is the second of three concessional development policy operations. Approved by the bank's board in May, it includes a $200 million British credit guarantee and is tied to reforms of state-owned enterprises, competition rules, tax collection and the cost of government borrowing. The bank said at the time that Egypt had endured “two years of successive external shocks”. Those pressures have since deepened. The US-Israeli war on Iran has raised oil, shipping and insurance costs for a country reliant on imports. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly told the Egypt Forum in late October that oil was trading around $110 a barrel, against $75 assumed in the budget. He considered passing costs to citizens, borrowing to absorb them, or risking power cuts of six to eight hours a day. The government chose to absorb them “at this stage”, he said. President Abdel Fattah El Sisi told the same forum that fuel and electricity prices were “completely uneconomic” and sold below cost, and that limited resources often forced the state to borrow to keep supplies flowing. Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk put subsidies at 840 billion Egyptian pounds ($15 billion) this fiscal year, with borrowing costs adding about 20 per cent to bring the real bill near EGP 1 trillion ($17.9 billion). The strain has since reached the local currency. The dollar rose by almost 8 per cent, from about EGP 52 at the start of October to break a record above EGP 56 on October 26. It is estimated that about $4 billion of foreign money left Egyptian government debt between October 15 and 26 as markets prepared for further turmoil in the region. Central Bank Governor Hassan Abdalla told the same forum that a flexible exchange rate was the “first line of defence” against external shocks. “The most important thing for us is unifying the exchange rate, not the exchange rate itself,” he said. For import-dependent Egypt , the priority is keeping dollars flowing through banks rather than into the black market, even at the cost of a weaker pound, Mr Abdallah said. Before the March 2024 currency float, a wide gap between official and parallel rates diverted remittances away from banks and left businesses struggling to secure foreign currency to pay for imports. On Thursday, the bank raised rates by 100 basis points to 20 per cent, citing “challenging external conditions”. It was the first increase since March 2024 and reversed an easing cycle that had cut 825 basis points from April 2025 before pausing when the war began. The bank also pushed back its inflation target to late 2027. On the stock exchange, trading was halted for 30 minutes on October 25, the first suspension since 2021, after the EGX100 index fell 10 per cent. Egypt's other dollar earners offer only partial cover from the war-related pressures. Remittances hit a record $33.9 billion in the first eight months of the year, but tourism revenue grew 1.7 per cent over the same period, compared with 16.3 per cent growth in the fiscal year ending June 2025. Suez Canal income, near $10 billion a year before Red Sea attacks began, has recovered only to about $4.4 billion, and the canal's chief has warned that renewed tension at Bab Al Mandeb strait greatly threatens that recovery. In the shops, the effect is immediate. Shoppers in Cairo told The National on Monday that they were shocked by the increases in some food items over the past couple of months. Cooking oil, more than 95 per cent of which is imported, has risen from EGP 75 ($1.34) to EGP90 ($1.61) per bottle in a month, meat rose by EGP 100 ($1.79) a kilo in five months and a bar of soap from EGP 20 ($0.36) to EGP 35 ($0.63) since the summer. Traders blame more expensive imported milk powder for cheese price rises, animal feed for meat increases, and imported chemicals for rising soap prices. The squeeze comes on top of a heavy debt load. External debt reached $166.45 billion at the end of June, according to World Bank data, and Egypt owes about $60.9 billion in repayments and interest between July this year and June 2027. That includes some $19.1 billion in central bank deposits, mostly from Gulf states. The acute hardship has been acknowledged by leaders. Mr El Sisi said he had convened the Egypt Forum amid discontent over rising prices and the difficulty of paying electricity bills, conceding that “electricity is indeed expensive” and that energy feeds into the price of everything. Closing the event, he said the cost of reform “has borne heavily upon the Egyptian citizen” and urged officials to prioritise “alleviating cost-of-living burdens”. For households, that relief has yet to arrive. Official data has yet to capture October. Urban inflation eased to 13.9 per cent in September, though food inflation picked up. After household electricity tariffs rose an average of 12 per cent in August, the cabinet's spokesman said there would be no fuel or power price rises “at this stage”. An IMF mission is in Cairo for the final review of Egypt's loan programme, which could release about $2.3 billion before it ends on December 15. The government has signalled it will not seek a successor deal.

title: Why AI agents struggle with chip design (RTL) debugging, and what helps
body:
I asked an AI coding agent to fix a bug in the RISC-V An open instruction set architecture. Many open-source processor cores implement it. processor inside Caliptra A large open-source system on chip from CHIPS Alliance. It is a hardware root of trust: a security block with its own RISC-V processor and firmware. . It usually found the faulty line of RTL Register-transfer level: the code that describes a chip’s hardware, usually written in Verilog or SystemVerilog. A simulator runs it; synthesis tools turn it into gates. within five minutes. Proving the fix took much longer, because the agent first had to make the bug show up in simulation. Over ten trials, two hardware-specific problems took most of that time: the internal signals that explain a failure are invisible unless the simulation records them, and simulations run long enough that the agent has to guess when they finish. A third problem, a build that depends on settings the agent's shell doesn't keep, isn't specific to hardware but is common in RTL projects. With tools aimed at all three, the same agent's mean time to a verified fix fell from 56 minutes to 21.
Coding agents are built mostly for software work. Their working loop assumes that a test runs in seconds, that a failure prints a useful message, and that a command is cheap to rerun. Hardware design breaks all three. Chips are described in RTL Register-transfer level: the code that describes a chip’s hardware, usually written in Verilog or SystemVerilog. A simulator runs it; synthesis tools turn it into gates. code and tested in a simulator. A simulation of a large design takes minutes to compile and run, so every rerun is expensive, and the state that explains a failure lives in internal signals that nobody printed.
Current models reason well about RTL. This note looks at what happens when that reasoning meets a real hardware debug loop. It asks where the agent's time goes, which of that time comes from hardware work rather than from agent setups in general, and what the agent's harness The environment around an AI agent: the tools it can call, how its commands run, and the instructions it gets. can do about it.
The scope is debugging: finding a bug, reproducing it, and proving the fix. Other RTL tasks, such as writing new design code or building verification environments, run into different problems. Later notes will cover those.
To answer it, I ran the same agent on the same bug in two setups: a plain shell, and Booley , an open-source agent harness for FPGA and ASIC work. I build Booley and ran this experiment myself, so weigh the comparison with that in mind. The problems described below, though, come from the plain-shell runs and apply to any agent setup for RTL.
I wanted a bug where the environment, not the model's reasoning, would limit the agent. I started with bug-fixing tasks from a subset of CVDP , NVIDIA's benchmark of hardware design and verification problems. Those tasks were too small for this question: agents solved them quickly with any tooling, so the environment never had a chance to matter. I needed a design where reproducing a bug takes real simulation work.
So I looked for the largest high-quality open-source RTL codebase I could find. I chose Caliptra , a hardware root of trust: a security subsystem with its own processor and firmware.
I settled on a historical bug in VeeR EL2, the RISC-V processor inside Caliptra, and reintroduced it by reverting an upstream fix from the VeeR EL2 1.4 release .
In the scenario the bug report describes, firmware checks the contents of the processor's ROM Read-only memory. Here it holds the processor’s boot program. during startup. Under a particular sequence of reads and writes, that check fails even though the stored program is correct: the word at ROM address 0 reads back as zero.
The agent's task was to find and fix the cause in the RTL, then add a test that fails before the fix and passes afterward.
The agent received an issue-style report describing this behavior:
Early in boot, the firmware recomputes a digest over its own ROM image and compares it with a constant fixed at build time. Normally the check passes. In one case the digest comes out wrong, even though the ROM is unchanged and the constant is correct. No fault, no exception, no ECC event, fully deterministic. The trigger is a coding pattern: the failing routine reads ROM word by word and, in the same tight loop, writes partial results to a scratch buffer in DCCM Data closely coupled memory: the processor’s fast on-chip data memory, reached without going over the system bus. . Keep the accumulator in registers, or move the buffer out of DCCM, and the digest is correct. Only the first word of the ROM input looks corrupted.
Find and fix the RTL root cause. Add a test that reproduces the problem and passes after the fix.
The upstream release notes describe the fix as "Store data collision with DCCM DMA error when address is 0x0".
The processor uses store-to-load forwarding : a read can take its value directly from a recent write to the same address instead of waiting for memory. To save power, it also blanks the address and data of a write that goes to its on-chip data memory (DCCM), setting both to zero. The forwarding check was missing its "this write goes out on the bus" condition, so it compared each read against that blanked address of zero. A read from ROM address 0, issued right after an on-chip write, "matched", skipped the real ROM read, and got the blanked value: zero.
In both setups, the agent usually identified the faulty line within five minutes. It then had to write a test that failed on the original design and passed after the fix. That would demonstrate the fault and help catch it if it returned later.
Two details made that test difficult to write:
Most of the work went into building a test, simulating it, inspecting what happened, and adjusting it until it failed for the right reason.
Finding the bug took reading, and current models read code well. Reproducing it took repeated experiments: build, simulate, look at the result, change the test. Hardware and software differ most in that loop, so the rest of this note measures it.
I ran ten trials in each of two setups, with the same agent, model, prompt, and container:
The Booley setup's AGENTS.md (also linked as CLAUDE.md ) explains how to use Booley's tools and has two lines describing the repository; it contains no build commands, environment variables, or debugging hints.
Table 1. Test conditions, identical for both setups unless noted
The harness changed three things, each aimed at one of the problems described below:
Both setups produced an accepted fix and a reproducing test in all ten trials, so the comparison is about time. Mean completion time was 55.8 minutes with Claude Code alone and 21.3 minutes with Booley (Figure 1); the medians were 53.3 and 21.4 minutes. Average cost per trial at Sonnet 5.5 API prices was $2.33 and $1.98.
In the plain-shell runs, only about a third of the time went into building and simulating. The rest went to observing internal signals, sleeping on jobs that had already finished, and recovering from broken builds. Each recurred across the trials. The first two follow from how hardware is simulated; the third is a general agent problem that showed up here too. I identified them from the run histories; I didn't run separate experiments to isolate the contribution of each fix.
When a software test fails, it usually prints what went wrong, and a debugger can stop the program anywhere. In RTL simulation, the state that explains a failure is spread across thousands of internal signals, and none of them are visible unless the testbench records a waveform or prints them. Adding a print means editing the design or testbench and recompiling. Caliptra simulates with Verilator, which compiles the design into a C++ program, so each recompile and rerun takes several minutes.
This matters most when a test passes despite a suspected bug, which happened repeatedly here, and the agent needs to see why the bug didn't fire.
What the agent did with only a shell. It debugged the simulator the way it would debug a software program: with prints. In pair b3 (Figure 2), it added $display Verilog’s print statement, similar to printf in C. statements, rebuilt the simulator, reran the test, and searched the output. Every new question meant another recompile. It repeated that loop seven times and spent 37.8 minutes on signal observation.
Recording a waveform was an option in this setup too, but a recording only helps if the agent can read it. Caliptra's waveforms are in FST, a compressed binary format that takes a dedicated library to parse, and a quick Python script is too slow on a dump this size.
What worked: record once, then query. With Booley, the agent built once with waveform recording enabled and asked B-Wave 16 questions about the recorded signals. That work took 9.8 minutes.
In trial b1, the agent searched the waveform to find whether the faulty address comparison ever fired. Listing 1 shows equivalent command lines, with output trimmed.
The comparison fired 32 times, yet the test still passed. The agent then asked for the surrounding signal values at the first match (Listing 2). Signal names end in their pipeline stage: _m for the load, _r for the store one stage ahead of it.
The read matched a write that should not have been eligible for forwarding: a DCCM store ( lsu_busreq_r = 0 ) whose address had been blanked to 0. But the test's memory setting ( is_sideeffects_m = 1 ) blocked forwarding ( ld_full_hit_m = 0 ) and hid the bug.
The agent changed that setting in the test. Half a minute later, the test failed on the buggy design.
The agent could ask follow-up questions of the same recording without rebuilding. Across all ten pairs, it spent 9.4 minutes less on average observing signals with Booley.
The b3 chart's final segment (Figure 2), roughly 47 to 85 minutes, is a sequence of final tests. That time isn't counted as signal observation.
In hardware debugging, a new question about the design should be answerable from an existing recording. A tool that searches a recorded waveform by signal name and reads values at a given cycle gives an agent roughly what a debugger gives it in software.
Agents' habits come from commands that finish in seconds. In hardware, minutes are normal: compiling a design like Caliptra for simulation and running a firmware test takes several, and synthesis or a full regression can take hours. So the agent runs the job in the background and has to decide when to check on it. If it guesses, it either checks too early or sleeps long after the job has finished.
Sleeping after the job already finished: 30.7 min
Sleeping after the job already finished: 0.0 min
What the agent did with only a shell. In several runs, it started work in the background and used a fixed sleep before checking the result. In b10 (Figure 3), a build started at 4.3 minutes and failed one second later. The failure was hidden: the command ended with ; tail , so it reported exit code 0. Seconds later the agent requested sleep 540 , a nine-minute wait, and didn't check the result until 13.4 minutes.
It made similar waits four times in that run, spending 30.7 of its 60 minutes asleep after jobs had finished.
What worked: return when the job ends. Booley's simulation command waits for the job and returns the result. For long jobs it returns a run ID instead, and the agent calls a poll tool ( booley_poll ) that returns as soon as the job ends, so there is no fixed sleep to guess.
The Booley run in pair b10 took 13 minutes in total. Across all ten pairs, it spent 11.2 minutes less on average waiting on finished jobs. These waits affected six pairs. I counted only waits where I could establish that the job had finished, so the estimate is a lower bound. The sleeping is an agent habit. Hardware makes it expensive because the jobs are long, so the guessed waits are long too. There is a cheap partial fix: one line in CLAUDE.md telling the agent to wait for the process instead of sleeping would likely recover much of this time. Hiding exit codes behind pipes, as in ; tail , makes it worse, because a failed build looks like a running one.
This problem isn't specific to hardware. Any project whose build depends on undocumented environment variables trips agents up the same way, and RTL projects often have such builds. Caliptra's simulation needs the simulator, toolchain paths, and a firmware image compiled by a separate cross-compiler and loaded into the simulated memory, and its Makefiles locate these through environment variables. An engineer sets them once in a terminal and forgets about them. An agent works through a series of separate shell calls, and state set in one call doesn't necessarily survive to the next. When a step fails, the next one often runs anyway: a simulation without its firmware doesn't crash; it runs until it times out.
What the agent did with only a shell. All ten plain-shell runs hit missing build configuration; most recovered within a few minutes. In b1 (Figure 4), the agent worked out which variables to set and exported them in a shell call. Those values didn't carry over to later calls in this run. The firmware build then failed to produce program.hex , and the simulation started without a program. It waited until its timeout. This happened three times before the agent put the configuration in a single run.sh script.
The run spent 30 minutes dealing with setup. Sleeps after jobs had already finished, including two minutes after the first hung simulation was killed, are counted separately (Figure 4), as in Figure 1.
What worked: configuration in files, prerequisites checked. The Booley project's FuseSoC core files already held the dependency paths, so the agent didn't have to rediscover the Makefile variables. Each simulation invocation supplied its build configuration and firmware build step, without relying on exports from a previous shell call. If the firmware build failed, Booley stopped the run and reported the build error before starting a simulation without its program.
The Booley run in pair b1 spent no time repairing setup. Across all ten pairs, the average setup saving was 3.6 minutes ; b1 was the unusually costly case. Configuring the project once avoided repeating that work during debugging.
Build configuration should live in files that every run reads, and each simulation run should carry its whole configuration and stop at the first failed prerequisite. A checked-in script that the agent's instructions point to gets part of the way there. The plain-shell agent in b1 arrived at exactly that, a run.sh , after 30 minutes.
Both setups still had to work out how to make the bug appear: noticing that the test template's side-effect setting disabled forwarding, and moving the test loop into ICCM to get the store and the load back to back in the pipeline. That is reasoning about microarchitecture, and the harness didn't do it for the agent. It changed the cost of each experiment the agent ran on the way there, and that was enough to cut the total time by more than half.
This is a case study, not a benchmark: one bug, one design, one model, and ten trials per setup. I chose a bug that needed substantial simulation work and used an already configured Booley project. These results don't establish the same speedup for other models or other debugging tasks, or tell us which fix would help most on its own. They also say little about design or verification work, which have their own problems and will get their own notes.
Still, the plain-shell runs show where a general-purpose agent loses time on an RTL project, and none of it was spent finding the bug. The lessons below don't depend on a particular tool. The first two are about hardware. The third applies to any agent setup, but RTL projects need it often:
Booley implements all three tooling fixes, but a project can apply them with any waveform library, build system, and job runner.
The Caliptra project used here is public; its README explains the setup. The reproduction details below list the recorded versions, the original prompt, and the patches. To try the same workflow on a smaller design, the PicoRV32 demo comes preconfigured.
These are the inputs used in the experiment. Prepare the bug before starting the agent, and give it only the prompt below. The patch and the rest of this article reveal the answer.
Check out the Caliptra revision above and initialize its submodules, then pin Adams Bridge to the recorded revision (Listing 3):
Both setups also received the same tracing patch . It makes waveform recording opt-in with +trace and changes the trace depth from 24 to 4. This is a testbench adjustment, separate from the RTL bug below. Download it and the bug mutation outside the source directory, then apply them from the Caliptra root (Listing 4):
The agent received a source snapshot without Git history or the saved patches. The Booley setup also contained the pinned .booley_project , with root-level AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md symlinked to .booley_project/AGENTS.md . The other setup contained Caliptra's native build scripts without that project directory or guidance. Start each attempt from a fresh copy of the prepared snapshot.
These steps recreate the source mutation and task. The reported timing comparison also used frozen container images and the archived Booley project, so a run with a different toolchain or project revision is not an exact repeat of that environment.
The mutation removes & lsu_busreq_r from all four address-match expressions in src/riscv_core/veer_el2/rtl/lsu/el2_lsu_bus_intf.sv . Restoring the removed guards fixes the bug. Listing 5 shows the four changed lines; the downloadable patch also includes the surrounding context.

title: JP Morgan boosts UAE presence with wealth management branch at DIFC
body: JP Morgan Chase has expanded its private banking offerings in the Middle East with the opening of a dedicated wealth management branch at Dubai International Financial centre . Regulated by the Dubai Financial Services Authority, the DIFC branch will enable JP Morgan Private Bank to better serve clients across the UAE and the wider region, it said in a statement on Monday. In the 12 months leading up to the final DFSA approval, JP Morgan more than tripled the size of its Dubai-based private banking team to build capabilities before launch, it said, without specifying the number of bankers added. The team in Dubai is led by Selim Elgen, UAE market head and senior executive officer, and Karim Rekik, regional head, Middle East at JP Morgan Private Bank, the lender said. “JP Morgan Private Bank’s expansion into DIFC reinforces Dubai’s position as a global hub for private wealth,” said Arif Amiri, chief executive of the DIFC Authority. JP Morgan is the latest among major global financial institutions that have expanded in the UAE this year despite Iran war-driven uncertainty and economic headwinds. HSBC, Barclays as well as several Swiss wealth managers have also boosted their operations in the country to leverage the rapid growth of domestic wealth as well as the migration of global capital into the UAE. In October, Dubai and Abu Dhabi were ranked among the top 10 destinations for next-generation wealth despite the fallout from geopolitical tension. Dubai was ranked eighth and the UAE capital was 10th among favoured cities for the $84 trillion of wealth expected to be transferred between generations over the next two decades, consultancy Savills said in a report. Net wealth in the UAE is set to jump to $6 trillion by the end of this decade despite the short-term volatility, according to Boston Consulting Group data. In the five years to the end of 2030, net wealth in the Emirates is set to increase by more than $2.3 trillion, at an annual growth rate of 10.6 per cent, the consultancy said in a report last month. Long-term relations JP Morgan Private Bank said its dedicated money management branch is the latest chapter in the bank’s five-decade relationship with the UAE. Over the past 20 years, the company has also used DIFC as its regional base for corporate and investment banking and, more recently, broadened its activities with authorisation to provide asset management services through JP Morgan International Advisers. "The UAE and the broader Middle East represent a significant and growing opportunity for us as a business and for our clients,” said Mr Rekik.

title: Russian drone attacks civilian car in Kherson, leaving two injured
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Kherson City Military Administration reported the incident on Telegram .
"At approximately 08:00, Russian occupying forces attacked a car with a drone in the Korabelnyi district," the statement said.
Two people were injured: a 62-year-old woman and a 73-year-old man. Both were taken to hospital to receive the necessary medical treatment. They sustained blast-related injuries and are currently undergoing further medical examinations.
As Ukrinform previously reported, on the morning of November 2, Russian forces attacked a medical facility in central Kherson. Several rooms were damaged, and windows and interior doors were blown out.
Russian forces are resuming their so-called "free hunting" of vehicles using fiber-optic-controlled drones.
From October 27 to November 1, Ukraine had introduced a ceasefire regime in a designated area to facilitate a humanitarian operation in Oleshky.

title: Bauchi LGA chairman dies in auto crash after APM meeting
body: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Chairman of Zaki Local Government Area of Bauchi State, Masud Aliyu Umar, has died in a road accident while returning from an Allied Peoples Movement (APM) stakeholders’ meeting in Bauchi. Umar reportedly died on Sunday night when his private car crashed at Konkiyal Village in Darazo Local Government Area, about 100 kilometres from Bauchi metropolis. The late chairman was returning to Zaki after attending the political meeting when the accident occurred. Before his election as Zaki LGA chairman on August 17, 2026, Umar served as Director-General of the Bauchi State Emergency Management Agency, SEMA. Reacting to his death, Governor Bala Mohammed expressed shock, describing the deceased as a dedicated public servant, committed grassroots politician and compassionate leader whose contributions to public service and community development would remain indelible in the history of the state. In a condolence message issued by his media aide, Mukhtar Gidado, the governor said Umar’s tenure at SEMA was marked by his commitment to alleviating the suffering of vulnerable citizens and providing timely interventions to communities affected by emergencies and humanitarian challenges. Mohammed added that as chairman of Zaki Local Government, the deceased demonstrated commitment to grassroots development through initiatives aimed at empowering youths and women, improving livelihoods and promoting inclusive development. He described the death as a devastating loss to the deceased’s family, the people of Zaki and Bauchi State, particularly the public service and local government administration. The governor urged the family, political associates, friends and people of Zaki Local Government to find strength and comfort in Almighty Allah during the difficult period. The funeral prayer is scheduled for Monday, November 2, 2026, at 2pm at the Palace of the District Head, Mur Mur, Zaki Local Government Area of Bauchi State. The post Bauchi LGA chairman dies in auto crash after APM meeting appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: China's Xi tells Oman's Sultan Haitham Gulf should not become arena for great-power rivalry
body: Chinese President Xi Jinping said that the Middle East and the Gulf region should not become an arena for great-power rivalry, as he met Oman's Sultan Haitham in Beijing on Monday, with the two countries calling for the resumption of safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. “The Middle East Gulf region should not become an arena for great-power rivalry and geopolitical conflict. Peace and stability in the region require joint nurturing and protection by all parties,” Mr Xi was quoted as saying by China’s Foreign Ministry. He added that China remained committed to helping to end the US-Iran war, and was willing to work with Arab countries including Gulf Co-operation Council states, with the aiming of achieving lasting regional stability and security. In a 20-point joint statement, China and Oman called for normal and safe navigation to resume in the Strait of Hormuz and urged the US and Iran to pursue peaceful options, to return to the agreement reached in June aimed at ending the conflict and to restart dialogue. Mr Xi also said China was ready to deepen the alignment of its development strategies with Oman, according to Xinhua news agency. He described the two countries as stable and reliable energy partners, investment partners with significant potential, and partners in high-tech innovation. The talks came during Sultan Haitham’s two-day state visit to China, the first by an Omani head of state since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries in 1978. Sultan Haitham said Oman appreciated China’s positions on key regional issues, stressing that development and stability were closely linked and required security, respect for state sovereignty, adherence to international law and the peaceful resolution of disputes. He also said Oman was open to a preferential bilateral trade and investment agreement with China, saying it could create new opportunities for commercial and investment exchanges. The joint statement said the two countries would deepen co-operation in oil and natural gas and expand partnerships in renewable energy, including solar power, wind energy, electricity transmission and transformation, and energy storage. China is Oman’s largest trading partner. The two countries have also sought to expand co-operation in energy supply chains, investment and digital commerce. During the visit, Oman’s Foreign Minister Badr Al Busaidi and Transport, Communications and Information Technology Minister Said Al Maawali met representatives of Chinese companies. They discussed potential partnerships in priority sectors, including transport, logistics, communications and information technology, as well as artificial intelligence, advanced technologies and drone-based air transport, the Omani Foreign Ministry said. The two sides also explored how Chinese companies can invest their expertise and capabilities in Oman, including by leveraging the sultanate’s strategic location, infrastructure and economic potential. The proposed co-operation aims to support Oman’s economic diversification, enable the transfer of knowledge and technology, and advance the objectives of Oman Vision 2040 and the National Digital Economy Programme, the ministry said. Separately, China’s Foreign Ministry said its special envoy to the Middle East, Zhai Jun, would visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month.

title: Monyemiji launches Juba festival to reconnect youth with cultural heritage
body: Organizers of the Monyemiji Cultural Festival say they plan to use a cultural gathering in Juba in February 2027 to reconnect young people with traditions they fear are becoming less familiar to children growing up away from their ancestral communities. The festival committee officially launched the initiative in Juba on Sunday evening and invited members of the Monyemiji communities living in South Sudan and abroad to support the preparations and participate in the celebrations. Otwari James Odiongo, chairperson of the festival, said Juba was chosen because many children and young people growing up in the capital have limited knowledge of their cultural traditions. “Most of the young children and most of the youth who have grown up in Juba do not know their culture,” he said. “So, we want to make this festival happen in Juba as an introduction to the young generation so that they can learn their culture and the tradition.” Odiongo said the festival will bring together communities from different parts of Eastern Equatoria, including the Dongotono, Logir, Lango, Bira, Lotuko, Lopit and Lokoya, among others. He called on people living in Juba, other parts of the country and the diaspora to support the initiative, saying the organisers hoped to make the event a shared celebration of their cultural heritage. He added that the committee hoped to take the festival to Torit in the future after holding the planned gathering in Juba. Meanwhile, Zacharia Ebul, a Monyemiji elder who addressed the launch, urged families to take responsibility for teaching children their cultural traditions, saying cultural identity was important in helping people understand their origins and sense of belonging. He said bringing children to cultural gatherings would help them learn about their heritage and understand the traditions of their communities. “If we do not tell our children our culture, they will not know where they belong,” he said, encouraging parents to continue exposing young people to traditional practices. Ebul also urged community members not to feel ashamed of their cultural identity, including those living abroad, saying cultural traditions deserved to be preserved and celebrated wherever people settled. The launch featured traditional dances and cultural displays by young men and women, which Ebul described as an important way of demonstrating the identity of the community. The organisers said the February 2027 festival would be open to members of the communities who register to participate. The registration fee was announced at 250,000 South Sudanese pounds. Odiongo said the initiative was not entirely new, recalling that a similar gathering involving Otuho-speaking communities was held in 2010. However, he said the forthcoming event would be organised specifically as the Monyemiji Cultural Festival. The post Monyemiji launches Juba festival to reconnect youth with cultural heritage appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: No plans to destroy countries as colonial powers crumble — top Russian security official
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. Moscow has no plans to destroy any countries, as former colonial powers are falling apart on their own, Russian Security Council Secretary Sergey Shoigu said.
"I don’t quite get why we should do that. We have no plans to destroy any countries. Many of them - colonial powers - are collapsing on their own," he said on the sidelines of the Peoples of Russia International Week.
"The reason is that those whom they once enslaved and turned into their colonies, are awakening and rising as their self-consciousness and self-determination are reviving," Shoigu added.
"An old man in Vietnam told me: ‘You know, I’m from the generation that still remembers and that was told about portable French guillotines in Vietnam.’ This is, in fact, what those countries brought to the colonies they ruled and sought to use for decades and centuries," he noted. "Our goal is different. The goal is to make sure that our country remains united and indivisible for decades and centuries and for us to respect and understand each other," the top Russian security official said.
According to Shoigu, this policy does not always receive support in the West because "they have a constant need for an enemy."
The Peoples of Russia International Week, organized in accordance with President Vladimir Putin’s order, is being held to coincide with People’s Unity Day, celebrated on November 4. The event is coordinated by the office of the Russian Security Council. The focus of discussions is on national unity, historical memory, the continuity of generations, service to the country and responsibility for its future, and the promotion of strong families.
The Peoples of Russia International Week brings together government officials, members of international organizations, the business community, academic and expert circles, cultural figures and public organizations from Russia, as well as about 50 delegates from 35 countries, including those considered unfriendly.
TASS is a strategic information partner of the event.

title: Roblox embraces AI-generated games as Steam raises concerns about quality
body:
Two days after Steam admitted it has an AI slop problem, Roblox basically bragged about the same thing.
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .
Valve recently admitted that it has a problem with AI slop games and clones flooding Steam—it doesn't know what to do about it just yet, but it at least acknowledges that it's an issue. Now we have Roblox, speaking from the other side of that coin in its Q3 2026 shareholder letter , in which it bragged that the July release of Build, its AI-powered "prompt-to-game creation tool," users have published more than 70,000 games.
"During the last three months, we have witnessed an inflection point in AI adoption and content generation in the gaming industry overall, and on Roblox in particular," the letter states. "AI-enabled game creation, automation in code generation and AI supported asset creation are leading to an explosion of content. The time it takes to go from an idea to a playable game is compressing dramatically, and so is the time it takes to adapt a game for new devices."
The "explosion of content" remark is what jumps out at me first and foremost. Is that really a good thing— content , in explosive quantities? That is essentially what Valve is facing on Steam that's widely considered a problem—an ever-growing mountain of content —yet in the world of Roblox, it's a feature, not a bug. And Roblox is not looking to stem the tide.
"We have been embracing AI to accelerate creation since the first release of Roblox Studio Assistant in December 2023," the letter continues. "Over the past month, more than 80% of the top 100 games on Roblox (ranked by hours engaged) used AI tools to accelerate creation, and the number of daily asset uploads to the Roblox cloud tripled month-over-month.
"Since Q2, time spent using AI tools (including Build, Studio Assistant, and external AI via MCP) tripled among our top creators, and those using our MCP server daily grew nearly 5x. In Q3, Break and Steal an Egg and Huss Valley were both created almost entirely with AI and both broke into the Roblox top 20 (ranked by concurrent players). Build is our new prompt-to-game creation tool. Since its alpha launch in New Zealand, Singapore, Serbia and Thailand, more than 500,000 users have used Build—and have published over 70,000 games."
As content becomes abundant, attention and connection become scarce. What sets our distribution apart is that it runs on social connections.
Take a moment to think about that: Build launched in July, five months ago, which means we're looking at a rough average of 14,000 games per month. And that's with Build still not fully launched yet, so only a fairly small portion of the Roblox userbase has access to it. I can't help but wonder, with a certain sense of alarm, what will happen when the doors are opened to more populous parts of the world.
Roblox, however, says it is "uniquely positioned to capture this moment," which is seeing "traditional barriers to software and content creation" giving way to a focus on "distribution, audience aggregation, monetization, discovery, and safety."
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
To further capitalize on that, Roblox has kicked off two new initiatives: Roblox Everywhere, revealed in September as a way to make Roblox games playable outside of the Roblox platform, and the Universal Player, which is basically the reverse of that: "AI is used to seamlessly import any existing game into the Roblox cloud platform while transforming it to run multiplayer, on any device (at the upper edge of the device's performance capabilities), with instant join, instant UGC updates, local 3D, and access to Roblox services for discovery, safety, communication, and monetization."
That's interesting: Details are scant but the idea seems to be to make Roblox a platform for all game developers, akin to Steam, GOG, or the PlayStation Store, with minimal fuss or muss: Just make your game, then zippity-pow it through the AI machine, and suddenly you've got a full-on Roblox game and access to a massive audience that previously would've been much more of a headache to reach. And Roblox gets basically the same: Its goal "is to capture 10% of the global gaming market and an even greater share in the US."
"As content becomes abundant, attention and connection become scarce," the letter says, extolling the virtues of Roblox's platform. "What sets our distribution apart is that it runs on social connections: people come to Roblox to play with their friends, so every new game can reach players through an existing social graph, through friends inviting friends, and through social influencers, which we believe enables great content to find its ideal audience faster than on any other platform."
Maybe Roblox is right. Hell, maybe EA chief Andrew Wilson was right—maybe the future really is all about billions of people cranking out content while corporations fight over where to put it all. It's hard to argue that Roblox hasn't put up serious shareholder value so far, after all, and while Steam doesn't have shareholders it's still making bank, AI slop problem or no. Still, I can't say that making speed and quantity the key indicators of success really represents the kind of future for videogaming that I'd like.

Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. title: PZ Cussons shareholders approve N9.926bn dividend payout
body:
Shareholders of PZ Cussons Nigeria Plc , a leading manufacturer of personal healthcare products and consumer goods, have unanimously approved a final dividend payout of N9.926 billion for the 2026 financial year.
The dividend was approved at the company’s 78th Annual General Meeting (AGM) held at the Fraiser Suites in Abuja on Wednesday, 28 October 2026.
Speaking during the Annual General Meeting, the Chair of the company’s Board of Directors, Mrs Ifueko Omoigui Okauru, explained that each shareholder would receive a final dividend of N2.50k per ordinary share of 50k each.
Mrs Omoigui Okauru also announced that the board has equally approved the implementation of a Scrip Dividend Scheme, under which qualifying shareholders may elect to receive new ordinary shares in the company in lieu of all or part of their cash dividend entitlement. She stated that the company has demonstrated strong resilience and shown remarkable improvement in operating performance backed by a restructured balance sheet.
“Our performance is improving year-on-year, and we will continue to leverage our strategic operating model and a more stable macroeconomic environment to drive growth and create value for all stakeholders”.
Shareholders at the meeting commended the board and management for approving the dividend despite the challenging business environment in Nigeria.
One of them, the Chairman, Viewpoint Shareholders Association, Uyo, Chief Peter Essien applauded the company’s leadership for managing the business effectively, citing the improved performance in profit and revenue recorded in the 2026 financial year.
“Special kudos to the board and management of the company for the outstanding performance recorded for the financial year ended May 31, 2026. I am happy and satisfied with the growth witnessed over the last few years,” Essien said.
Also speaking, the Chairman, New Dimension Shareholders Association, Hon Pat Ajudua, lauded the company’s management for its financial prudence and the deleveraging of the balance sheet, the impact of which has been the transition from a negative equity position of -N17.3bn to +N66.6bn.
On Scrip Dividend, Shareholders moved a resolution for the extension of the election deadline from 23rdNovember 2026 to 4th November 2026. It was also approved that the final dividend of N2.50k will be paid on the 6th of November 2026.
The Board Chair stated that the company remains focused on growth and the continuous creation of value for stakeholders, especially after the conclusion of the Strategic Review of the African businesses and the decision by the parent company to retain its Nigerian operation as part of the wider Group.

title: Russia attacks Ukraine's energy sector 94 times in week, damaging infrastructure 208 times – Energy Ministry
body:
Russia targeted Ukrainian energy and oil and gas facilities 94 times over the past week, resulting in 208 recorded incidents of destruction or damage to energy and oil and gas infrastructure, the Ministry of Energy reported.
According to its statement on Telegram on Monday, targeted and systematic Russian strikes on energy facilities over the past 24 hours caused new power outages as of Monday morning affecting consumers in Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhia, Odesa, Kirovohrad, Rivne, Cherkasy, and Kharkiv regions.
"The electricity supply situation remains most critical in Dnipropetrovsk and Kyiv regions. The energy infrastructure in these regions sustained extensive damage as a result of Russian strikes. Due to damage to power equipment, electricity transmission capabilities to consumers have been disrupted, necessitating the emergency application of blackout schedules," the ministry explained.
At the same time, the Ministry of Energy reported that a power engineer was injured in Kharkiv region and another power worker was killed in Kramatorsk, Donetsk region, as a result of Russian attacks.
"Our sincere condolences go out to the family and loved ones of the deceased. Eternal memory to the heroes who continue restoring light to Ukrainians under the most difficult conditions," the Ministry of Energy noted.

title: Number of journalists killed worldwide rises by 20% compared to previous years — UNESCO
body:
PARIS, November 2. /TASS/. A total of 189 journalists were killed in connection with their professional activities in 2024-2025, up 20% from 2022-2023, according to a report by the UNESCO Director General on the safety of journalists and the risk of impunity for crimes against them.
Of the deaths recorded in the report, 127 occurred in combat zones. The document noted that 40% of these journalists were killed by drone strikes. The highest number of journalists were killed in Palestine: 62, followed by Mexico: 17, and Sudan: 14. According to UNESCO, the conflict in Ukraine claimed the lives of 12 media workers during the period in question.
"Local and international war reporters face increased safety risks, especially due to direct exposure to crossfire as well as deliberate targeting even far away from the frontline. In conflict zones, groups of journalists totalling 36 were reportedly killed in temporary field media houses and workplaces in four countries. In one instance, a single attack led to the killing of nine journalists," the report said.
Over the past 20 years, UNESCO has recorded the deaths of 1,600 journalists, yet only 14% of these cases have been investigated. Meanwhile, according to the document, the proportion of unresolved investigations in countries without armed conflict has fallen from 94% in 2012 to 77% in 2026.
"Nevertheless, the commitment to press freedom is more urgent than ever, as it remains under severe threat in both conflict and non-conflict settings, and journalists continue to pay a heavy price," UNESCO Director General Khaled El-Enany emphasized.

title: 3 children die from scorpion stings in Yirol East
body: Three children have died from scorpion stings in separate incidents over the past two weeks in Malek Payam in Lakes State’s Yirol East County, while another child is battling the effects of the venom, a family member said. Thon Mabor Adool, a resident of Malek Payam, said the latest incident occurred last Thursday evening at his uncle’s home, where two children were stung. One died immediately, while the other remains affected by the venom. “The other week, a scorpion stung one child, who died immediately,” he said. “It happened again on Thursday at another incident at my uncle’s house, where two children were stung by a scorpion. One died immediately, and the other is battling the venom now.” He appealed to church leaders and members of the public to pray for the affected family and residents of Malek Payam. Scorpion stings can be particularly dangerous to children, who are more vulnerable to the effects of the venom. While most stings cause local pain, severe cases can lead to life-threatening complications and death. Health researchers have identified delayed access to medical treatment, antivenom, and critical care as major factors contributing to scorpion-related deaths, particularly in low-resource settings. Estimates indicate that Eastern and Southern Africa record about 79,000 scorpion stings annually, resulting in approximately 245 deaths. The post 3 children die from scorpion stings in Yirol East appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: JUSAG strike begins to bite as courts shut down in Accra
body: The nationwide industrial action declared by the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) has affected court operations across the country, forcing the closure of several court premises, including the Supreme Court, Court of Appeal, Accra High Court, Circuit Court and some District Courts. Access to the affected facilities has been restricted, with security officers reportedly directed to keep the gates closed following the commencement of the strike. In a show of protest, red pieces of cloth have been placed at the entrances of some court premises to highlight the workers’ grievances. At the Accra High Court, JoyNews’ Legal Correspondent, Fatawu Bayaga, reported that several persons were outside the Court as they were denied entry. The association is demanding the payment of outstanding salary arrears arising from the revised salary structure, which dates back to January 2026. Amid the disruption, Judicial Secretary Musah Ahmed has urged JUSAG to reconsider its decision and suspend the strike to allow negotiations to continue. He explained that management had engaged relevant government stakeholders in high-level discussions conducted in good faith to find a lasting solution to the concerns raised by the association. Mr Ahmed also acknowledged the frustration among judicial staff over the delay in implementing the 2026 salary review, assuring them that management was attentive to their concerns.

title: How much will Kimi Antonelli earn for winning 2026 F1 world title?
body: Kimi Antonelli rewrote the record books as the Italian became the youngest F1 world champion. Antonelli clinched the drivers' title at 20 years and 68 days old on Sunday ⁠as he finished third for Mercedes at the Mexican Grand Prix. Antonelli broke the record of Sebastian Vettel who became world champion in 2010 at the age of 23 years and 134 days, kicking off an era of domination for Red Bull. He also became the first Italian champion since 1953, having taken an unassailable 119 points lead in the F1 championship race. “I’m speechless. ⁠I’m trying to process what has just happened,” Antonelli said after his momentous win. “It’s been an incredible season, and to share this podium with Max (Verstappen) and Lewis (Hamilton) is truly incredible. title: ‘No room for debate’ over human control of AI, says Sam Altman
body: People, not artificial intelligence, must stay in control of the future, OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said on Monday. “There are a lot of other things we can debate, but on this one, we think there must be no room for debate,” he said in conversation with The National 's Editor-in-Chief Mina Al-Oraibi. Speaking at the opening ceremony of Adipec in Abu Dhabi, Mr Altman said there “should not be a handoff to AI” and that the technology “needs to be a tool built for people and needs to serve people, not the other way around”. “I can’t believe that this differentiates us from other AI companies, but it does,” he said. “This is a value that we intend to really go fight for. And I wish it didn’t need to be said.” The remarks followed OpenAI's agreements with Abu Dhabi, covering energy, education, investment and government. These include a deal with Adnoc and Abu Dhabi technology group G42 to use OpenAI’s most advanced models on the energy industry’s hardest problems. Mr Altman’s message was that AI has crossed a threshold. By his account, it has gone from trailing the world’s best scientists at the start of the year to mostly outperforming them. Its demand for power is growing just as fast, he said. “AI was mostly not as smart as our smartest scientists, and now it’s mostly smarter than them,” Mr Altman said, adding that AI could now do “a lot of parts” of many white-collar jobs. He said he believed society would “navigate through this all fine”. But he warned that the industry must show it can prevent harm as its systems become more capable. “How do we guarantee, and how do we give the world comfort with that guarantee, that we are going to avoid serious safety and alignment incidents?” he said. “I think that’ll be increasingly important for our industry to demonstrate.” Energy challenge In a quick-fire round, Mr Altman was asked what challenge he faces today. He answered with one word: “Energy.” He said the energy needed for each AI query had dropped sharply, but demand kept climbing . Six years ago, OpenAI’s heaviest internal user consumed about 100,000 tokens a month. Today, that figure is roughly the global per-capita average, and the top user consumes about 500 billion, he added. Costs could fall “in almost every way, except, you know, atoms are still atoms”, Mr Altman said. He called power “the very dominant factor” in how much AI the world can use. He said he hoped AI would deliver “a net gain for energy availability in the world”. Mr Altman also said OpenAI had solved one of the Millennium Prize problems, a set of unsolved mathematics problems. He said the work used 10,000 agents running an upcoming GPT model for about four days, collaborating with “no hierarchy”. The claim could not immediately be verified independently. He praised the UAE as “consistently the most forward-looking country in the world for AI adoption”, saying about 80 per cent of young people in the country were using ChatGPT .

title: Cameroon to receive Metal Shark patrol boat
body:
Louisiana, United States-based boatbuilder Metal Shark has been awarded a US Coast Guard Foreign Military Sales (FMS) contract to produce a patrol boat for Cameroon’s maritime forces.
The company on 12 October said the contract covers the supply of an 11.5 metre Metal Shark 38 Defiant patrol boat, transport trailer, spare-parts package, and operator training. The vessel will be constructed at Metal Shark’s production facility in Jeanerette, Louisiana.
Cameroon is a new market for Metal Shark, the company’s Senior Vice President of International Business Development, Henry Irizarry, said. He added that Metal Shark is proud to support partner nations in strengthening maritime security, operational readiness, and mission effectiveness.
The contract is worth $1.197 million according to US federal reporting publication GovTribe.
The welded aluminium 38 Defiant is described as a proven military and law-enforcement patrol platform designed to support coastal patrol, maritime interdiction, port security, search and rescue, and other security missions. “Initially proven in service with the US Navy and US Coast Guard, Metal Shark’s 38 Defiant platform is now operated by US partner nations across Africa, Asia, the Caribbean, Europe, Latin America and the Middle East,” the company said.
“The vessel combines high-speed performance and responsive manoeuvrability with Metal Shark’s signature Defiant-series pilothouse, which provides enhanced visibility and all-weather crew protection. The adaptable platform may be configured with multiple propulsion arrangements and mission-specific equipment to meet a broad range of mission profiles.”
Various powerplant options are available for the Defiant 38, including inboard diesels or multiple outboards, giving top speeds of up to 50 knots depending on engine configuration. The vessel may be equipped with an open bow or forward cuddy cabin. In addition, the pilothouse may be shortened for those who desire an even larger aft cockpit than the standard offering.
Metal Shark CEO Chris Allard said maritime security is taking on greater strategic importance worldwide. “Metal Shark is well positioned to meet that demand, and we remain focused on expanding our global reach, entering new markets, and delivering long-term value to the United States and its partner nations.”
“With over 70 US partner nation military forces now operating Metal Shark vessels, these awards further expand the company’s established role in supporting maritime forces worldwide,” Metal Shark added. It has delivered well over 2 000 vessels to date, including to Benin, Djibouti, Senegal, Kenya, Cabo Verde, and Morocco.
Cameroon’s navy is relatively well equipped in order to secure Cameroon’s oil installations and prevent maritime crime and is optimised for coastal and river patrol, especially in light of rising levels of piracy in the Gulf of Guinea. It has around 40 coastal, inshore and river patrol craft as well as several combat patrol vessels.

title: You Cannot Negotiate For TUC, Osifo Replies Ajearo As N70,000 Controversy Drags On
body: President of the Trade Union of Nigeria (TUC), Festus Osifo, on Monday, disagreed with the stance of Joe Ajaero, President of the Nigerian Labour Congress (NLC), over whose responsibility it is to negotiate salaries and allowances of Nigerian workers with the Federal Government. Osifo’s response comes as the labour unions bicker over the N70,000 transportation allowance recently approved for workers by President Bola Tinubu. The TUC President, while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Monday, described the N70,000 agreement by the NLC President as an aberration, saying that the TUC was not carried along in the negotiations. “Listening to Ajaero again today, I really pity the Labour movement and the quality of leaders that have been inflated on the NLC. “As I listened to Ajaero today, I was wondering if it is the same NLC that produced the likes of Adams Oshiomole, Hassan Sumonu, Ayuba Wabba and so on. “There is nowhere in ILO regulations that says a trade centre cannot negotiate for its members. It is not there! It is just that if you are going to the ILO, it is tripartite- the labour, government and the employers. And in describing that, it means that the list of the TUC members is joined together with that of the NLC and submitted to the Ministry of Labour, who forwards it to the ILO. “In that case, the two bodies must come together. We are not contesting the fact that NLC has more affiliates. “But what we are saying is that you have about 60 affiliates while we have about 40. You cannot! You cannot negotiate for a body that is represented, for a body that has a trade union. “You cannot negotiate for them on their behalf! It is not there anywhere! “Yes, if we go to negotiations- I sit down, you sit down, and we agree”. Osifo challenged Ajaero to produce the ILO regulation document that said either of the labour unions could negotiate on behalf of the other. “He should show me in the ILO Regulations where it says one party is going to negotiate without the other one being there or consulted. He should show me! He should show Nigerians! “ILO doctrine is that when you have more affiliates, and you are going for one of their events, it is not correct that the most represented will go and negotiate on behalf of the other one when the unions have their own umbrella. “Let Ajaero send a document to you that proves that! It cannot be found anywhere! He talked about the JNC (Joint Public Sector Negotiating Council ). I don’t truly think Ajaero has read the JNC constitution. I don’t truly think he knows what the JNC means. “Yes, you have a Masters in 1990. You cannot use a solution of yesterday to attack today’s problem. “And that is why in industrial relations, you need to keep updating, retooling and relearning. “First, the JNC means that when there are issues in the public sector, the JNC looks at it”. According to Osifo, the meeting where the N70,000 transport allowance was agreed upon was not the Council’s meeting and does not represent a general agreement by members. “But that meeting that took place was not the Council meeting. The Minister is not a member of the Council. Ajaero is not a member of the Council. The Council even has a quorum and the number of persons that must be seated to form a quorum. But at the end of the day, that meeting was not a JNC meeting. The members of JNC were not there! “Again, if you see the release that was sent out by those three bodies, you will discover that after the last minimum wage, we got about 33 per cent increment, and how does that work? Because from N30,000, we got N70,000. What you are supposed to do is that JNC will have to sit down and apply consequential adjustments. “You know what Ajaero used JNC to do? Ajaero sent JNC a questionnaire and asked them to apply N40,000 each to Nigerian workers. So they took N40,000, which is the difference between N30,00 and N70,000, and applied it across board. That is why the federal workers today are earning abysmally poor. “But I attacked him! I went to his office and told him that “Ajaero, this is wrong!” What you used JNC to do is fundamentally wrong!” The post You Cannot Negotiate For TUC, Osifo Replies Ajearo As N70,000 Controversy Drags On appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Defence oversight committee in favour of KZN soldier deployment, again concerned about late notification
body:
The latest mobilisation of soldiers – in KwaZulu-Natal – has the support of Parliament’s Joint Standing Committee on Defence (JSCD).
At the same time committee co-chairs Phiroane Phala and Mike Hala repeated its concern about what a Parliamentary Communication Services (PCS) statement has as “continued late submission of deployment notifications to Parliament”.
National Assembly (NA) Speaker Thoko Didiza was informed of the deployment by way of a Presidential letter signed by Cyril Ramaphosa dated 21 October authorising “employment” of 510 SA National Defence Force (SANDF) personnel to assist police in maintaining law and order in the province from 9 October to 30 November at an expected cost of R34 082 720.
However, a 30 October briefing by the SANDF to the JSCD stated the KwaZulu-Natal deployment will cost an estimated R18.5 million. Of this amount, R5 million is for the compensation of employees and R13.5 million for goods and services. “The expenditure for this deployment will be accommodated by means of reprioritisation of the 2026/2027 Depart of Defence budget allocation,” it said.
The 12-day delay between deployment and notification will see the JSCD correspond with Didiza as Parliament’s senior presiding officer to formally raise its concerns about recurring delays in informing Parliament about SANDF mobilisation as per standing Joint Operations Division instructions. These include over Operation Prosper, generally to support police in specific anti-crime efforts ranging from gangsterism, illegal mining and civil unrest, to external deployments. These include assisting eastern neighbour Mozambique in the wake of flood damage – “months after the mission concluded” according to National Council of Provinces MP Nicholas Gotsell – and wrapping up the South African commitment to MONUSCO, the United Nations (UN) mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and SAMIDRC (the Southern African Development Community Mission in Democratic Republic of Congo).
The JSCD qualifies its rebuke of the SANDF Commander-in-Chief by acknowledging the urgency of the KwaZulu-Natal deployment, in anticipation of potential anti-illegal immigrant marches. As per the statement, timeous notification of mobilisation, in and out of country, is essential if Parliament is to fulfil its Constitutional oversight and accountability responsibilities.
On the KwaZulu-Natal deployment, the JSCD statement notes wanton violence, destruction of property and threats to communities are inconsistent with the Constitution adding while the right to protest is constitutionally protected it must be exercised responsibly and with due regard for the rights of others.
Carl Niehaus, the Economic Freedom Fighter’s (EFF’s) representative on the Joint Standing Committee on Defence and the Portfolio Committee on Defence and Military Veterans, said the party supports the SANDF deployment to KwaZulu-Natal “with great reluctance, and only for the narrow purpose of protecting human life and preventing further violence against our people and against African nationals.”
“The security of communities cannot be left solely to a police service that is already overstretched. At the same time, the concerns that have repeatedly been raised about the efficiency of Operation Prosper and the quality of cooperation between the Department of Defence and the South African Police Service remain valid. Those concerns have not been resolved, and they apply with equal force to this employment,” he added.
According to Niehaus, the root cause of the crisis remains the prolonged failure of the government to manage migration properly. “That failure has created the space in which populist and reactionary forces can mobilise. It must be addressed at source. At the same time, the consequences of that failure cannot be allowed to fall on African nationals through violence, arson and intimidation.”
Niehaus cautioned that the deployment of the SANDF must not become the norm. “The Defence Force must not be turned into the default instrument of the state for managing marches, protests or political reactions. The right to assemble, to demonstrate and to protest is a fundamental constitutional right. It must not be eroded under the cover of maintaining law and order. Any use of the military in these circumstances must be confined to the narrowest possible parameters: actual violence, clear and imminent threats to life, and serious criminality that the South African Police Service cannot manage alone.”
The EFF representative also took up issue with the 12-day delay in informing the Speaker of the National Assembly of the deployment. “Once again, Parliament is being reduced to a rubber stamp. When notification arrives only after the deployment is well advanced, the ability of Members of Parliament to scrutinise the decision, to insist on clear rules of engagement, and to exercise meaningful oversight is systematically undermined. This pattern is becoming established. It must be rejected. Constitutional checks and balances cannot function when the executive presents Parliament with a fait accompli.”
Niehaus added that the EFF only supports the employment of the SANDF in KwaZulu-Natal under Operation Prosper “with the strongest reservations” and only because violence has occurred, human life is at risk, and fellow Africans must be protected.

title: Iranian Foreign Minister to Visit Turkmenistan, Seeking Closer Ties
body: Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi is leading a diplomatic and economic delegation on a visit to Turkmenistan this week, according to Iranian state media. Araghchi will travel to Ashgabat on Monday for talks with Turkmen officials on “areas of mutual interest,” reported the Islamic Republic News Agency, or IRNA. The report didn’t specify the areas, but Iran has been working to develop its relationships in Central Asia as it faces pressure because of conflict in the Middle East, Western sanctions, and disruption to its trade routes. On October 26, Araghchi and Turkmen counterpart Rashid Meredov spoke by phone about “continuing diplomatic consultations and political efforts to de-escalate tensions and establish lasting stability and security in the region,” Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said . Turkmenistan has a policy of permanent neutrality under which it commits to staying out of military alliances, promoting peaceful relations and not getting involved in other countries’ affairs. In July, it issued an unusually sharp statement after an attack on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea that the Iranian government blamed on Ukraine. The Turkmen government described the attack as unacceptable. The Caspian Sea is critical to Turkmenistan’s efforts to expand its role as a transit point on the Middle Corridor, a trade network linking China and Central Asia to Europe via rail and maritime links. The country’s main port is Turkmenbashi. Iran has a long border with Turkmenistan and is also a Caspian Sea littoral state, with its northern port of Amirabad. The sea is an alternative route for some of Iran’s regional trade, including with Russia to the north. Iran also offers Central Asia a southern route for goods to reach the Persian Gulf and beyond, though that route has been disrupted by blockades, restrictions and attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. In another area of collaboration, Iran imports electricity from Turkmenistan to offset shortages in northern Iranian provinces, and the two countries recently discussed expanding and extending the arrangement. They have also worked together on energy swap deals under which Iran would provide natural gas to other countries, including Azerbaijan and Iraq, and receive similar amounts of gas from Turkmenistan in return.

title: Storm Agneta Floods Rhodes, Sweeps Away 60 Cars and Damages Homes Across Greece
body: Storm Agneta has caused extensive flooding and damage across Greece, with Rhodes bearing the brunt of the severe weather after torrential overnight rainfall turned roads into raging torrents, swept away dozens of vehicles and flooded homes and businesses. The eastern Dodecanese island experienced particularly severe conditions in the early hours of Monday, November 2, with the village of Archangelos among the worst affected. An overflowing river sent large volumes of water through the area, inundating streets, damaging commercial properties and sweeping vehicles away in the powerful current. According to initial reports, at least 60 vehicles were swept away and damaged, while dozens of homes and businesses were flooded. Πλημμυρικά φαινόμενα από την ισχυρή καταιγίδα και στο νησί της #Ικαρίας . Βίντεο : Voula voulgari pic.twitter.com/nM4K3G3z6l — Forecast Weather Greece (@ForecastGreece) November 2, 2026 The neighbouring areas of Afantou and villages in southern Rhodes also experienced flooding, with heavy rainfall creating dangerous conditions across the road network. Second 112 emergency alert issued for Rhodes Authorities issued two emergency alerts through Greece’s 112 civil protection system as conditions deteriorated. The first message was sent at approximately 3.30 am, warning residents and visitors of dangerous rainfall and rising water levels, particularly around Archangelos. A second emergency warning followed at 10.52 am, urging people to restrict their movements to those absolutely necessary and follow instructions from authorities. Traffic was suspended at several locations, including Kolympia, Kalathos and Archangelos, as emergency services worked to address flooding and restore safe access. Firefighters, Civil Protection personnel, regional authorities and volunteer groups were mobilised to assist affected communities. Operations included removing vehicles swept away by floodwaters, clearing drainage systems, restoring water flow in streams obstructed by debris and carrying out interventions across the damaged road network. Although the worst rainfall had eased by Monday morning, authorities remained on heightened alert amid warnings that further storms could develop. Schools closed across four municipal districts The Municipality of Rhodes announced the closure of schools on Monday, November 2, across four municipal units: Archangelos, Afantou, Lindos and South Rhodes. The precautionary decision was taken to protect students and teachers and prevent unnecessary travel through areas affected by severe flooding. Firefighters respond across the Aegean and mainland Greece The Fire Service reported a significant number of emergency calls across several regions of Greece. On Samos, firefighters received 28 calls for assistance and carried out 10 water-pumping operations. Across the Dodecanese, crews received 18 calls. On Rhodes, they pumped water from three locations, cut down a tree and helped two people reach safety. On Kalymnos, firefighters carried out a water-pumping operation and removed a tree. In the central Greek port city of Volos, emergency crews received 12 calls, conducting seven water-pumping operations and two tree-cutting operations. Large boulder crashes into garage on Kalymnos The severe weather also created a dangerous situation on Kalymnos, where a massive boulder broke loose from a hillside in the Agios Vasilios area and crashed into a garage. The rock struck the structure, damaging it and a vehicle parked inside. Kalymnos Mayor Giannis Mastrokoukos told the Athens-Macedonian News Agency that the boulder stopped against the garage, potentially preventing a much more serious incident. A residential complex is located immediately below the structure. The mayor warned that the consequences could have been far worse had the garage not stopped the falling rock, given the homes situated further down the slope. Severe weather warning extended through Tuesday Greece’s National Meteorological Service (EMY) has updated its severe weather bulletin, warning of heavy rainfall and thunderstorms through Tuesday, November 3. The most affected areas are expected to include western and northern Greece, as well as the eastern Aegean islands and the Dodecanese. Local hailstorms are also possible. For Monday, heavy rain and thunderstorms are forecast across the Ionian islands from midday, followed by Epirus, western Central Greece and the western and southern Peloponnese from the afternoon. The Dodecanese is expected to experience intermittent severe weather until late Monday night. On Tuesday, storms are forecast to continue across the Ionian islands until midday and in Epirus, western Central Greece and the western and southern Peloponnese until the afternoon. Central and eastern Macedonia, Thrace, the northern and eastern Aegean islands and the Dodecanese are also expected to experience heavy rainfall and thunderstorms from the early morning until late afternoon. Authorities are urging residents and visitors to avoid flooded roads, stay away from overflowing streams and follow official Civil Protection instructions as Storm Agneta continues to affect Greece.
