title: End of the war? The US wants Russian gas back in Europe
body:
The United States wants to resume the supply of Russian gas to Europe through Ukraine. According to “The Wall Street Journal”, the proposal is part of discussions regarding the limitation of Russian and Ukrainian attacks on energy infrastructure. Washington hopes that an agreement could pave the way for an end to the war.
The US administration is considering restoring the transit of Russian gas through Ukraine. As reported by “The Wall Street Journal”, citing sources in the United States and Europe, the idea surfaced during talks regarding the possibility of reaching an agreement between Moscow and Kyiv.
The proposal was reportedly presented by American envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner during September talks in Moscow and Kyiv. It involves using existing pipelines through which Russian resources reached the European market for years.
Gas transit through Ukraine was suspended on 1 January 2025, following the expiry of the agreement between the parties. Kyiv refused to extend it, citing ongoing Russian aggression.
According to American assumptions, resuming gas supplies could provide an incentive for Moscow to limit attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. In exchange, Ukraine would refrain from strikes on Russian oil and gas sector facilities.
Washington is also considering a solution where the sale of Russian gas would take place through an American entity. The money obtained this way would be placed in a special account, limiting Russia’s ability to use it to finance war operations.
Ukraine could also earn from the resumption of transit by collecting fees for the transport of the resource through its territory.
However, it is not known whether Moscow would be ready to accept such conditions. Russia has previously rejected proposals regarding the limitation of attacks on energy infrastructure.
The American plan may face opposition from some European countries. Since the beginning of the full-scale Russian invasion, the European Union has been limiting the purchase of energy resources from Russia. The adopted solutions provide for a gradual end to Russian gas imports by the end of 2027.
According to “The Wall Street Journal”, some European governments oppose the American proposal. They fear a return to energy dependence on Moscow, which Russia previously used as an instrument of political pressure.
However, the Americans are said to be arguing that restoring part of the supply could lower gas prices in Europe, whilst simultaneously creating conditions for further peace negotiations.
The issue of possibly resuming gas transit through Nord Stream was also reportedly raised during the talks. Implementing such a scenario would, however, require resolving technical and legal issues, and above all, obtaining the consent of the countries involved.
These reports are significant because the United States has for years opposed increasing European dependence on Russian resources. Washington criticised, among other things, the construction of the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, pointing to threats to European energy security.
Currently, the US administration is said to be considering using gas supplies as one of the elements of negotiations regarding the end of the war.
For now, however, there is no information about an agreement being reached or about Russia and Ukraine’s consent to resume transit.
Reuters, which relayed the reports from “The Wall Street Journal”, noted that it was unable to independently confirm this information.

title: Turkey's Erdogan proposes South Korean partnership in nuclear power, AI, defense
body: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said South Korea could become a partner in developing Turkey's planned Sinop nuclear power station, according to an interview with Yonhap News Agency reported on Monday.Turkey has been studying the technical and economic terms of the Black Sea project with state-run Korea Electric Power Corp, Erdogan said.Ankara would weigh financing, electricity costs and benefits to the Turkish economy before choosing a partner, he added.Erdogan is due in Seoul on Monday for a three-day state visit, his first to South Korea since 2018.He will hold a summit with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday, Seoul's presidential office said.Defenses, semiconductors, AI, nuclear ties proposed between South Korea, TurkeyIn his interview with Yonhap, Erdogan also identified defense, semiconductors, artificial intelligence and robotics as potential areas for cooperation and called for more South Korean investment and joint production in Turkey.He said the countries were working towards a $15 billion bilateral trade target, while calling for efforts to address an imbalance in South Korea's favor.He invited South Korean companies to participate in Turkish transport and logistics projects linking Asia and Europe.

title: Dubai Airports celebrates the partnerships behind DXB’s success
body:
Dubai, UAE, Nov 2, 2026. Dubai Airports brought its airline and commercial partners together at Spirit of Excellence on October 29 to recognise their collective contribution to Dubai International’s (DXB) global connectivity and seamless guest experience.



Held at Atlantis The Royal, the gathering celebrated the shared effort behind DXB’s success. From airline and ground services to retail, dining, hospitality and transport, partners across the airport contribute to one connected guest journey, keeping Dubai connected to the world and extending the city’s welcome through its airport.

That partnership was particularly important through a challenging year. Faced with changing operating conditions and airspace restrictions, airlines adapted schedules and supported disrupted journeys, while commercial partners maintained services amid unpredictable footfall. Together, they helped keep Dubai connected while caring for its guests.

Eugene Barry, Chief Commercial Officer of Dubai Airports, said: “Confidence is contagious, and this year our partners and teams showed how much it matters. By maintaining high standards and offering the reassurance of familiar levels of service and hospitality across all our commercial touchpoints, our partners helped guests and colleagues navigate uncertainty and build a new platform for regrowth. We operate very different and diverse businesses, but together we all shape the experience and character of DXB. That shared responsibility gives our partnerships a purpose beyond the commercial relationship and makes every partner’s success part of our own.”

DXB has welcomed 31.5 million guests in the first half of 2026 and remains on track to exceed 70 million by year-end. The progress reflects the commitment of airline partners to rebuilding capacity and connectivity, supported by extensive coordination across the airport.



Robert Whitehouse, Vice President of Research at Dubai Airports, said: “Committing aircraft, crews and resources in a challenging global environment is a significant decision. Our airline partners backed those decisions with exceptional collaboration. Schedule coordination, normally undertaken once a season, had to be repeated as conditions changed. Their networks connect Dubai with individual markets and, together, support the hub’s wider reach. We are grateful for that commitment and will continue working closely with every airline to support the opportunities ahead.”

The evening also featured a fireside conversation between His Excellency Issam Kazim, CEO of the Dubai Corporation for Tourism and Commerce Marketing, and Paul Griffiths, CEO of Dubai Airports, on Dubai’s tourism and aviation outlook.

Dubai Airports continues to invest in terminal facilities and process improvements at DXB to improve guest flow and make journeys more intuitive. Making better use of existing capacity, these enhancements help deliver a more seamless guest experience and support partners in meeting changing expectations.



Each partner received a scale model of DXB’s iconic air traffic control tower, recognising their contribution to the airport’s shared success. The presentations brought together airline and ground service partners alongside businesses providing retail, dining, hospitality, transport and other commercial services.

The evening also looked ahead to Dubai’s busy winter season, with its calendar of international business, sporting and entertainment events attracting visitors from around the world. The focus was on a strong finish to 2026 and the opportunities of 2027, with airport and city partners working together to welcome guests and support Dubai’s continued success.

title: Most Finns reject normalising relations with Russia, poll shows
body:
President Alexander Stubb spoke by phone with Russian President Vladimir Putin last week.
Two in three Finns oppose the idea of normalising relations between Finland and Russia, according to a survey by Ilta-Sanomat .
In the poll, normalisation meant that diplomatic, economic and people-to-people ties between the two countries would be restored to their previous state at some point in the future.
About one in four supports starting the normalisation process.
There are no differences between age groups, with a majority in every age group opposed to starting normalisation.
The survey was carried out by Taloustutkimus, with more than 1,100 people responding via an online panel at the end of October. The margin of error is around three percentage points in either direction.
Finland's leadership has stressed that the phone call between Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre does not indicate the start of normalising relations with Moscow.
Finland closed its eastern border with Russia in late 2023, accusing Moscow of deliberately sending migrants across it, and it has remained shut since.

title: Show HN: I've updated my Linux System Call website and API
body:
Every Linux syscall table in one place, grouped by architecture: system calls for 27 architectures with their numbers, arguments and registers, from Linux 3.3 to 7.3.
Every architecture's table, with the full history of when each syscall appeared and when it was dropped, is also a plain JSON file at /<arch>/syscalls.json , for example /x64/syscalls.json .
Number in NR , arguments in ARG0 to ARG5 , then the instruction. The result comes back in RETURN .
Any kernel release, diffs between releases and more in the API docs .
Entries get added and, rarely, removed between releases. Each architecture page has a kernel selector, and its JSON download records when each entry first appeared ( since ) and when it was dropped ( removed_in ).
Removed entries stay visible: pick "all, with removed" in the kernel selector and each dropped syscall is marked with the release that dropped it.
Everything on this site is read from the kernel source itself. For each architecture, the generator walks the syscall table and the SYSCALL_DEFINE macros of every mainline release it scans, so these are the numbers the kernel actually dispatches on.
It also records each architecture's calling convention, the instruction that enters the kernel, so every syscall table shows exactly where the number and the arguments go.
A syscall whose since equals the first release scanned for its architecture was already there back then, and may be much older.
The short descriptions come from the Linux man pages project , and the io_uring ones from liburing . Whenever the data changes, the site is rebuilt from the syscall API .

title: The closer Russia to victory, the more aggressive the West in opposing it, says Shoigu
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. The West is stepping up its efforts to counter Russia, making them increasingly aggressive and sophisticated as Moscow moves closer to victory in the special military operation, Russian Security Council Secretary Sergey Shoigu said at the opening of the international week Peoples of Russia.
"The closer we get to victory and the successful conclusion of the special military operation, the more aggressive and sophisticated these attempts [by the West] become," Shoigu noted.
He stated that there was currently an "active effort to recruit and provide funding, and to bolster those prepared to support the destruction of Russian statehood from within."
At the same time, Shoigu stressed that Russia had "always stood united in repelling the aggressor."
"We have the means to counter this [Western aggression]," he said. "Above all, our unity - the unity of the peoples of Russia."
The international week is being held pursuant to a decree by President Vladimir Putin and coincides with National Unity Day, celebrated on November 4. The event is coordinated by the Office of the Russian Security Council.
The discussions will focus on such topics as the unity of Russia's peoples, historical memory and generational continuity, service to the Fatherland and responsibility for its future, and the importance of strong families.
Participants include representatives of government agencies, international organizations, the business, scientific and expert communities, cultural figures, and Russian public organizations.
The event is also attended by around 50 representatives from 35 countries, both from the near and far abroad, including countries designated as "unfriendly" toward Russia.
TASS is the event's strategic media partner.

title: What does the Million Mask March mean for the Philippines?
body: MANILA, Philippines – If you see a defaced Philippine government website this early in November, it could be a one-off event, but it also may be a single defacement of many, owing to a movement called the Million Mask March. The Million Mask March is a worldwide day of protest held on November 5 and is also colloquially known as “Operation Vendetta,” after the movie and British graphic novel V for Vendetta , wherein the main character of the story wears a Guy Fawkes mask. Originally set up by hacking collective Anonymous, the Million Mask March began in 2012 with the largest events occurring outside the Philippines, such as in London in the United Kingdom and Washington DC in the United States. The event is usually preceded by hacking activities or online defacements of websites to drum up interest and sentiment in conducting a Million Mask March in a given locality. These defacements and hacks decry a number of issues, such as political corruption, police violence and militarization. This was most strongly felt in the early iterations of the protest, especially in the Philippines’ 2013 Million Mask March, which saw more than 30 Philippine government websites crashed or defaced. A video from Anonymous on the affected sites back then apologized for the disruption but called on citizens to join the November 5 protest action. In response, police at the time also took steps to maintain public safety, but also invited protesters in for questioning. An impactful Million Mask March for 2026? Activity related to Million Mask March tends to fluctuate depending on the time frame of issues brought up. While the 2025 Million Mask March was apparently less pronounced and did not receive as much media coverage save for notices in online hacking communities, there’s no telling what might spur on a 2026 protest action. The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) could possibly be in for a long few days of work though, seeing as there is a new DICT secretary, former Social Security System chief Robert Joseph de Claro ,. There also seeming loss of trust in the institution owing to the actions — and resignation — of the previous DICT secretary, Henry Aguda, as regards the temporary banning of Discord and the threat to ban other services that may be responsible for the spread of nihilistic violent extremism . There’s also the preventive suspension of DICT eGov Undersecretary David Almirol over alleged conflicts of interest in the eGov app and the system’s development, which may bring an opportunity for bad actors or hacker-activists to take advantage of the situation. Must Read Conflict of interest? Audit questions DICT usec’s ties to former company Multisys Unfortunately, there’s no telling what could spark strong protest actions on November 5 in the Philippines, and it’s just as difficult to determine if an informal Million Mask March is coming this year. Perhaps it’s better to remember the fifth of November as a day when plans to bring injustices to the forefront of public consciousness comes to a head. Though in this country, that may as well be any given weekday. – Rappler.com

title: China envoy to visit Iran, Saudi Arabia and Oman
body:
TEHRAN, Nov. 02 (MNA) – China's Foreign Ministry has announced that Beijing will dispatch a special envoy to regional countries in an effort to ease ongoing tensions.
According to Reuters, China's Foreign Ministry said that the country's special envoy for Middle Eastern affairs, will visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month.
The visits aim to encourage the parties concerned to halt hostilities and return to the negotiating table, ease tensions, and prevent the expansion of the war across the Middle East, the Persian Gulf, the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa.
The ministry said the visits would also involve pursuing Chinese President Xi Jinping's initiatives to support regional peace and security.
Meanwhile, China's special envoy for African affairs will travel to Ethiopia, Djibouti and Egypt, while Beijing's special envoy for the Horn of Africa will visit Eritrea, the ministry added.

title: Access Bank appoints new deputy managing director, executive director
body:
Access Bank Plc has appointed Oluseyi Kumapayi as Deputy Managing Director, African Subsidiaries, and Olanrewaju Bamisebi as Executive Director, Information Technology and Digitalisation, as the lender moves to strengthen its operations, profitability and technology-driven services.
The appointments, which took effect on 27 and 28 October, respectively, followed the approval of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), according to a regulatory filing by Sunday Ekwochi, the Group Company Secretary.
Commenting on the appointments, the Group Chairman of Access Holdings, Aigboje Aig-Imoukhuede, said the decisions reflected the group’s strategic priority of translating its extensive banking presence across Africa and beyond into improved performance, operational efficiency and stronger shareholder returns.
“Access Holdings has built a substantial banking franchise across Africa and beyond. Our strategic priority is now to translate that scale into superior performance, greater efficiency, stronger returns on capital and sustainable value for shareholders,” Mr Aig-Imoukhuede said.
He said Mr Kumapayi’s elevation would strengthen the group’s efforts to improve the performance of its African subsidiaries, while Mr Bamisebi’s appointment would bring technology leadership closer to the bank’s operations, customers and commercial priorities.
The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Access Bank, Roosevelt Ogbonna, said the lender was focused on building a more productive, efficient and profitable institution through better utilisation of its capital, technology and established market presence.
He said the bank would prioritise improving returns across its African subsidiaries, simplifying technology platforms, strengthening operational reliability and accelerating innovation to improve customer experience at a lower cost.
Access Holdings said the appointments were part of its transition from a strategy focused on scale to one centred on value creation, profitability, capital efficiency and sustainable shareholder returns.
The group said its priority, having established a significant banking presence across Africa and selected international markets, was to maximise the value of its existing operations through improved subsidiary performance, disciplined capital allocation and technology-driven productivity.
It added that transferring executive responsibility for Information Technology and Digitalisation from the holding company to Access Bank was intended to integrate technology transformation more closely with banking operations, customer service, revenue generation and cost management.
The group said the move would accelerate digital transformation, simplify operating platforms, strengthen resilience and improve execution across its banking operations.
Mr Kumapayi was elevated from his previous position as Executive Director, African Subsidiaries, which he had held since November 2020.
He has over 25 years of banking experience spanning financial management, strategy, risk management, treasury and business development.
He joined Access Bank in 2002 and served as Group Chief Financial Officer between 2007 and 2020, where he contributed to strengthening the bank’s financial management and supporting its strategic development.
In his new role, he will retain responsibility for the bank’s African subsidiaries, with an expanded mandate to improve profitability, capital productivity, operational performance and cross-border business integration.
He will also support the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer in the broader leadership and strategic management of the bank.
Mr Kumapayi is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria. He holds an Executive MBA from IMD, Lausanne, and an Executive Master’s degree in Digital Transformation and Innovation Leadership from IE University, Madrid. He also holds degrees from the Universities of Lagos and Ibadan.
Meanwhile, Mr Bamisebi joined the board of Access Bank from Access Holdings, where he previously served as Executive Director, Information Technology and Digitalisation.
He has over 20 years of experience in technology transformation, digital banking, enterprise systems and operational management across the financial services industry and other sectors.
Before joining Access Holdings, he held senior positions at Equity Group Holdings Limited, including Group Director, Information Technology and Operations, and Managing Director of Finserve Africa.
He also served as Group Chief Information Officer at Diamond Bank, alongside other technology leadership positions at major Nigerian institutions.
In his new role, Mr Bamisebi will lead Access Bank’s technology and digitalisation strategy, focusing on improving operational efficiency, modernising technology platforms, strengthening cybersecurity and accelerating digital solutions to improve customer experience.
He holds a bachelor’s degree in Computing and Information Technology from the University of Derby and an MBA from Durham Business School. He is also an alumnus of the Cambridge Judge Business Senior Management Programme.

title: Ukrainian Drones Hit Major Oil Transport Hub in Samara Region
body:
Ukrainian drones struck one of Europe’s largest oil transport hubs in Russia’s Samara region, independent media reported Monday, as local authorities confirmed the overnight attack in the southern region without detailing any damage or casualties.
Samara region Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said early Monday that air defense systems were repelling an air barrage and urged residents not to post photos or videos online.
Samara’s Kurumoch International Airport temporarily suspended flights for two hours during the air raid alert.
The exiled news outlet Astra said it used eyewitness photos of a smoke cloud in Samara to identify at least one targeted facility as Transneft’s linear production and dispatch station. NASA satellite imagery also showed a large, black plume of smoke rising in the area where the site is located, directly southeast of the regional capital.
The Transneft station spans 216 hectares (534 acres) and has 71 storage tanks with a total capacity of 1.6 million cubic meters. It receives crude from Western Siberia, the republic of Tatarstan, the Orenburg region and Kazakhstan via four pipelines before routing it toward two refineries and the Druzhba export pipeline.
Monday’s attack marks the fifth drone strike on the Transneft production and dispatch station after reported strikes on Oct. 2, 7, 10 and 11.
It also came as Russia’s Emergency Situations Ministry said a major cyberattack targeted the app it uses to send people warnings about incoming air attacks. Ukraine reported a similar cyberattack on its air raid alert system earlier in the day, which it said sent out false messages about a radiation threat.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said it intercepted 212 Ukrainian drones across Russia and annexed Crimea between Sunday evening and Monday morning. Authorities in the Belgorod, Voronezh and Rostov regions reported minor damage and injuries.
In an interview with state TV channel Vesti on Sunday, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak, who oversees Russia’s energy sector, said Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries were adding to global fuel market imbalances and affecting prices.
That same day, Nizhny Novgorod region Governor Gleb Nikitin said a large-scale Ukrainian drone caused “significant damage” to an industrial facility. He did not identify the site that was hit. The region is home to the NORSI oil refinery, one of Russia’s largest.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also said Sunday that his armed forces had hit the Kamensky plant in Russia’s Rostov region, which he said was involved in the manufacture of Russian missiles.
Despite U.S. attempts last month to introduce an energy ceasefire in the war, which is now approaching its fifth anniversary, Russia and Ukraine have continued to target power grid infrastructure, as well as oil refineries and other facilities.
In an interview with Fox News on Sunday, Zelensky reiterated his position that Ukraine will halt its attacks on Russian refineries if Moscow also puts an end to its strikes on the Ukrainian electrical grid.

title: Azerbaijan gets just $65 of every $120 barrel of oil – where does rest go?
body: Azerbaijan’s oil revenues The price of Azerbaijani oil on the global market fluctuated between $120 and $130 a barrel in October, reaching $133 on 9 October. However, the state budget was drawn up on the basis of a forecast price of $65 a barrel. The government is now using the same benchmark price for the 2027 budget. Yet rising oil prices have not translated into the expected increase in either the State Oil Fund’s assets or state budget revenues. According to a report published by the State Oil Fund on 20 October, its assets have increased by just $462 million since the beginning of the year. Meanwhile, transfers from the fund to the state budget have fallen by 11.4% compared with the same period last year. JAMnews previously reported that the government plans to reduce transfers from the Oil Fund and increase income tax deductions from salaries in the 2027 budget. Now another question arises: If oil is selling for significantly more than the price assumed in the budget, where is the additional revenue going? Azerbaijan’s 2027 budget: how will fall in oil revenues be offset? State budget revenues from the oil and gas sector are forecast to decline, while tax revenues are expected to increase Why is the budget based on a price of $65 a barrel? Every year, when preparing the state budget, the government forecasts the average oil price for the coming year. It uses this estimate to calculate tax receipts and other revenues. In November 2025, Finance Minister Sahil Babayev told parliament that the government had set its 2026 oil price forecast at $65 a barrel based on average estimates from 22 organisations. At the time, Brent crude traded at $64–65 a barrel. However, the situation changed in early 2026. In its July report, the State Oil Fund noted that the conflict between the US and Iran had triggered “high volatility” in energy markets. According to figures that Samir Nasirov, head of the Central Bank’s Statistics Department, presented in September, Azerbaijani oil averaged $94.5 a barrel in the first half of the year. That was 33% higher than in the same period last year and approximately 45% above the price assumed in the budget. According to the Finance Ministry’s preliminary figures , the 2027 budget also assumes an oil price of $65 a barrel. However, in its medium-term expenditure framework for 2027–2030, the ministry describes the likelihood of oil prices falling below $65 next year as “low”. In other words, the budget relies on a price close to what the ministry itself considers one of the less favourable scenarios. Using a lower forecast price means that additional oil revenues go to the State Oil Fund rather than directly into the state budget. Economist Natig Jafarli made this point back in March, when oil prices began to rise. He said higher prices would affect “not the state budget directly”, but the consolidated budget, which also includes the State Oil Fund’s resources. According to Jafarli’s calculations, every $1 increase in the oil price brings the fund approximately $450,000 in additional revenue each day. Supporters of the government’s policy see this additional revenue as a reserve that could help finance security spending. In March, Vugar Bayramov, a member of the Milli Majlis Committee on Economic Policy, told OC Media that the additional revenue would allow the government to fund “priority areas such as national security”. Why are higher oil prices not bringing additional revenue into the state budget? The government determines how much money the State Oil Fund must transfer to the state budget each year before the financial year begins. It sets the amount out in the fund’s budget . According to the Finance Ministry, the fund transferred 9.628 billion manats (approximately $5.663 billion) to the state budget between January and September, exactly as planned. However, this was 1.23 billion manats (approximately $723 million) less than in the same period last year. Total state budget revenue from the oil and gas sector reached 12.93 billion manats (approximately $7.6 billion). This was 625.5 million manats (approximately $368 million), or 5.1%, above the forecast. Since the State Oil Fund made transfers as planned, tax payments from oil companies accounted for the additional revenue. According to the ministry, the Shah Deniz project paid 1.54 billion manats in taxes (approximately $906 million), SOCAR paid 1.3 billion manats (approximately $765 million), and the Azeri-Chirag-Gunashli project contributed 461 million manats (approximately $271.2 million). Overall, state budget revenues in the first nine months exceeded the forecast by 2.8%. In other words: In the first half of the year, oil prices were approximately 45% above the level assumed in the budget. Yet total state budget revenues exceeded the forecast by just 2.8% in the first nine months. $85bn despite falling oil revenues: how will Baku manage its growing foreign currency reserves? The growth came against the backdrop of a weakening oil and gas sector, falling exports and declining direct oil and gas revenues of SOFAZ. Если деньги остаются в фонде, почему его активы не растут? Согласно отчету Нефтяного фонда, значительная часть дополнительных доходов либо не поступила в фонд, либо была поглощена другими расходами и убытками. Нефтяной фонд, январь–сентябрь 2026 года (млн манатов): Indicator Amount Revenues from the sale of profitable oil and gas 7 343,9 Proceeds from the sale of the state’s stake in the Southern Gas Corridor 1 390,9 Other oil and gas revenues 5,8 Income from asset management 3 600,7 Total revenues 12 341,3 Transfers to the state budget -9 628,0 Expenditure on project implementation and management -53,2 Losses due to changes in gold prices and foreign exchange rates -1 874,0 Increase in the Fund’s assets 786.1 (approximately $462 million) Source: State Oil Fund. JAMnews calculated the figure in the final row using the fund’s published data on asset growth. The figures point to three conclusions. First, the fund’s revenue from oil and gas sales (7.34 billion manats) fell 2.3 billion manats short of the amount it transferred to the state budget (9.63 billion manats). Revenue from the fund’s overseas investments and proceeds from the sale of the state’s stake in the Southern Gas Corridor helped cover the gap. Second, changes in gold prices and exchange rates caused losses of 1.87 billion manats (approximately $1.01 billion). At the end of the first half of the year, losses stood at 3.69 billion manats (approximately $2.17 billion), but they narrowed in the third quarter. Gold has become one of the fund’s key assets in recent years. In its assessment of the fund’s 2026 budget, the Chamber of Accounts noted that rising gold prices had generated a significant share of the fund’s non-budget revenues in the first nine months of 2025. The same assessment warned that, as oil revenues and production volumes decline, the fund’s assets could “be rapidly depleted”. Third, despite higher oil prices, the fund’s oil revenues did not grow at a comparable rate. According to the fund’s report, receipts from the Azeri-Chirag-Gunashli field averaged 729 million manats (approximately $428.8 million) a month in the first half of the year, compared with 732 million manats (approximately $430.6 million) in the third quarter. JAMnews calculated these figures using data from the State Oil Fund. Oil production is declining According to preliminary figures from the Energy Ministry, Azerbaijan produced 19.9 million tonnes of oil, including gas condensate, between January and September. This was 3.9% less than in the same period last year. Exports show a similar trend. According to State Customs Committee data for January–August, the physical volume of crude oil exports fell by 7.8% compared with the same period last year, while their value increased by just 10.5%. In other words, although Azerbaijan sells each barrel of oil at a higher price, it exports less oil. Falling production partly offsets the additional revenue from higher prices. In September, economist Elchin Mammadov highlighted this contradiction in an interview with Sfera.az: “Although the average oil price has risen by around 30% this year compared with 2025, the latest published statistics point to a continued decline in the oil and gas sector.” He said the sector’s gross domestic product had fallen by 0.8%. In the assessment mentioned above, the Chamber of Accounts also forecast that oil production at the Azeri-Chirag-Gunashli fields would fall to 120.1 million barrels in 2026, down 3 million barrels from the previous year. Azerbaijan's $90bn reserves draw criticism from former opposition leader Politician Ilgar Mammadov has criticised Azerbaijan for accumulating $90bn in foreign currency reserves. What will change for citizens? According to the preliminary 2027 budget figures presented by the government, transfers from the State Oil Fund will fall by 935 million manats to 11.9 billion manats (approximately $550 million). The income tax rate on the portion of salaries up to 2,500 manats (approximately $1,470) in the private non-oil and gas sector will rise from 3% to 5%. It will increase further to 7% in 2028. Meanwhile, the government plans to cover 2.75 billion manats (approximately $1.617 billion) of the projected budget deficit of 3.17 billion manats (approximately $1.867 billion) through borrowing. News that the country’s foreign exchange reserves had exceeded $90 billion had already sparked public debate. Critics called on the government to use some of these funds to improve living standards. The government, meanwhile, sees reducing the budget’s dependence on oil revenues as a positive trend. Commenting on the preliminary 2027 budget figures, Vugar Bayramov welcomed the increase in the share of non-oil revenues to more than 60%, saying this would make the budget more resilient. Under this approach, the less the budget depends on oil revenues, the less vulnerable it becomes to falling oil prices. What happens next? Oil prices through the end of this year and into next year will depend largely on developments in the Middle East. However, the Finance Ministry’s forecast suggests that even if oil prices remain high, the State Oil Fund’s assets will not grow. According to the ministry’s medium-term expenditure framework, the fund’s assets are expected to stand at $73.9 billion by 2030. That is below their current level of $74 billion. An analysis by Meydan TV , based on the document, forecasts a 25.5% decline in oil and gas revenues to the budget between 2026 and 2030. Meanwhile, debt servicing costs are expected to rise to around 3 billion manats (approximately $1.765 billion). The government’s draft budget for 2027 once again assumes an oil price of $65 a barrel. It also provides for lower transfers from the State Oil Fund and higher income tax deductions from salaries. Social assistance is shrinking in Azerbaijan: Is poverty falling, or are low-income people losing support? According to the State Statistics Committee, the number of families receiving assistance fell by 1,400 from a year earlier, while the number of recipients fell by 4,000 Azerbaijan’s oil revenues

title: How Alaris Antennas Enable the Next Generation of Naval Intelligence
body:
As global naval forces look toward the adoption of Unmanned Surface Vessels (USVs), the technical focus is shifting toward a critical future necessity: radio frequency (RF) situational awareness. Without a human crew, next generation USVs must deliver intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to operate effectively in contested environments. This is where the adaptation of compact, wideband direction-finding (DF) antenna systems, such as those pioneered by Alaris Antennas, can provide a key enabling capability for autonomous maritime operations.
For a future unmanned vessel, RF awareness will shift from a supporting capability to an operational necessity, effectively supplementing human intuition. Whether operating independently or as part of a manned-unmanned team, a USV will need to interpret its surroundings in real-time without revealing its own presence. By integrating DF capabilities, these platforms could detect and locate communication or radar signals and identify potential threats, such as drone control links, all while maintaining a passive electronic profile. This “silent” sensing would allow a vessel to gather mission-critical intelligence without emitting signals that would tip off an adversary to its location, enabling passive intelligence collection without revealing platform location.
Integrating this level of sophistication into a maritime platform presents a unique engineering challenge for the coming years: the challenge of delivering high performance within strict size, weight and power constraints. Alaris Antennas is positioned to meet this challenge by leveraging its existing, mission-proven tactical technologies, including the DF-A0254, DF-A0257, DF-A0269, DF-A0303, DF-A0268 and DF-A0111. While these systems were originally designed for rigorous land-based tactical applications, their compact form factors and wideband performance provide a proven technological foundation that can be adapted for maritime applications. As these technologies are adapted for the sea, they will provide the dependable RF awareness that future defence users will require in environments where every centimetre and kilogram is a hard-won commodity.
However, the hardware of tomorrow must be as tough as the software is smart. The maritime environment presents significant operational challenges, defined by corrosive salt spray, and constant mechanical vibration and shock. Alaris is looking toward this future by building on its extensive operational heritage, including its established naval antenna capabilities and strong mechanical and environmental engineering expertise developed through years of designing rugged Electronic Warfare antennas for maritime platforms. As unmanned deployments are projected to grow longer and more autonomous, the design philosophy continues to evolve. By incorporating advanced corrosion-resistant coatings, and reinforced mechanical structures, Alaris is continuing to explore design approaches that support autonomous deployments with minimal maintenance.
As naval leaders define the future of force structures through the lens of unmanned systems, the balance of power will sit with those who possess the best situational awareness. Awareness is no longer just a functional requirement; it is a strategic vision. By evolving reliable, wideband DF solutions, Alaris Antennas is set to enable the next generation of unmanned vessels to sense, interpret, and respond to their environment with total confidence. In the high-stakes future of naval intelligence, the goal remains clear: to ensure that while the vessel may be unmanned, these systems provide the essential reconnaissance information needed to protect the mother ship and ensuring fleets retain situational awareness even when platforms operate without onboard personnel.

title: Injured in Izyum rises to 8, one killed
body:
The number of people who sought medical assistance following a Russian airstrike on Izyum has increased, including an 11-year-old boy, Head of the Kharkiv Regional Military Administration Oleh Synehubov reported.

"Currently, one person is confirmed dead... Preliminarily, 8 people were injured, including an 11-year-old boy," Synehubov wrote on his Telegram channel.

According to him, a guided aerial bomb (KAB) hit a five-story multi-apartment residential building, destroying floors one through three. Another KAB struck a four-story residential building.

At least 14 private houses, two shops, and six vehicles were also damaged in the city. Inspections of the area are ongoing.

As previously reported, as a result of the morning Russian airstrike on Izyum, one person was killed and at least three others were initially injured. The city is completely without electricity due to damage to high-voltage power lines.

title: No plans to destroy countries as colonial powers collapse — top Russian security official
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. Moscow has no plans to destroy any countries, as former colonial powers are collapsing on their own, Russian Security Council Secretary Sergey Shoigu said.
"I don’t quite get why we should do that. We have no plans to destroy any countries. Many of them - colonial powers - are collapsing on their own," he pointed out on the sidelines of the Peoples of Russia International Week.
"The reason is that those whom they once enslaved and turned into their colonies are awakening and rising as their self-consciousness and self-determination are reviving," Shoigu added.

title: ₦70k transport allowance: Relief for some, questions for all, By Posi Olatubosun
body:
Ultimately, a short-term allowance should be weighed against the more lasting alternatives available: a sustainable wage framework, targeted cash transfers for vulnerable households in the informal economy, and cheaper mass transport that lowers costs for every commuter. Relief for public servants is welcome, and labour has negotiated hard for it. A country where most workers have no employer to bargain on their behalf needs a wider safety net. The task is to turn a six-month concession into a lasting framework: fair wages, targeted support for the vulnerable and cheaper transport for all.
₦70,000 a month will ease the commute for civil servants. What about the trader, the okada rider and the farmer?
That is the question raised by the Federal Government’s agreement with organised labour to pay a monthly transport intervention of ₦70,000 to public service workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November. The same agreement provides for arrears of the peculiar allowance, backdated to 1 May, to be paid in three monthly installments, and for minimum wage negotiations to begin immediately. The deal followed weeks of pressure from the Nigeria Labour Congress over the pump prices of petrol, wages, tax relief and unpaid allowances. It may avert a strike and bring genuine relief to many households. But it also raises important questions about fairness, fiscal cost and what happens when the six months end.
The workers’ case is strong. Since the removal of petrol subsidy in May 2023, transport has become one of the heaviest burdens on household budgets. Earlier this year, civil servants in Abuja told the News Agency of Nigeria that commuting now consumes more than half of their salaries, with some daily fares more than doubling. Inflation has eased to 14.63 per cent, but food inflation remains close to 20 per cent, and the earlier surge in prices has not been reversed. Notably, the new allowance equals the ₦70,000 national minimum wage agreed in 2024.
For the lowest-paid public servants, it effectively doubles their monthly income for six months. That is significant relief. Precision matters, however. An allowance of this kind is not a wage increase, and it is not targeted at a need. It is a temporary, flat payment to a defined group of employees. Its value lies in speed and simplicity, but those same features shape its limitations. The test is whether it is the best use of scarce public resources to cushion hardship, and whether it is affordable for every tier of government that it covers.
The first concern is fairness. Public servants are an important constituency, but they are a small portion of Nigeria’s entire workforce. The majority of Nigerians earn their living in the informal economy as traders, artisans, commercial drivers, farmers and casual labourers. Many of them face the same transport costs with less job security and no employer to negotiate on their behalf. Critics, including opposition presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar, have already asked what the arrangement offers the millions of people without formal jobs. The question deserves a serious answer. Relief that reaches only those with a payslip risks widening the gap between the formal and informal economy.
The fourth concern is the cliff edge. The agreement does not state what happens after six months. Temporary payments have a way of becoming permanent expectations, especially in an election season. If the allowance ends abruptly in April 2027, just weeks after the general elections, workers will face a sharp fall in income. If it is extended, it becomes a recurrent commitment without a clear funding source.
The second concern is cost. The agreement has not been accompanied by a published estimate of its total cost. Simple arithmetic shows why one is needed. Every one million beneficiaries would cost ₦70 billion a month, or ₦420 billion over six months, before the peculiar allowance arrears are added. Nigeria is already spending heavily on debt service, which reached ₦5.28 trillion on domestic debt alone in the first half of 2026. The president has also asked the National Assembly to approve a new external borrowing plan of about $20.5 billion. In that context, citizens are entitled to know how the allowance will be funded, whether it is provided for in the budget, and what spending, if any, will be reduced to accommodate it.
The third concern pertains to the states. The agreement covers public service workers across all levels, which presumably includes the state and local governments. Their finances vary widely. Some states have already raised their minimum wages well above ₦70,000; others still struggle to pay salaries on time. Experience suggests caution. In 2023, when the Federal Government agreed to a ₦35,000 wage award for its workers, states were divided over whether they would follow. An allowance that some states pay and others cannot would create new grievances and possibly fresh industrial disputes.
The fourth concern is the cliff edge. The agreement does not state what happens after six months. Temporary payments have a way of becoming permanent expectations, especially in an election season. If the allowance ends abruptly in April 2027, just weeks after the general elections, workers will face a sharp fall in income. If it is extended, it becomes a recurrent commitment without a clear funding source. Either outcome needs to be planned for now, not improvised later.
The fifth concern is the wider economic effect. Putting additional cash into the hands of public servants will support spending in markets, shops and transport services, which is welcome for small businesses. But if the payments are financed by borrowing rather than savings or reallocated spending, they add to demand at a time when inflation, though easing, remains high, and pre-election spending is already expected to rise. The Central Bank cut its policy rate in September partly because price pressures were moderating. A sizeable fiscal injection without a clear funding source could complicate that progress and make further easing harder. That would ultimately hurt the same workers through higher prices and dearer credit.
…payment systems must be secure. Nigeria’s payroll has long been vulnerable to ghost workers and padded nominal rolls. Before the first installment is paid, federal and state authorities should verify beneficiaries through existing payroll and identity systems, so that the money reaches genuine workers, rather than leak through fraud. Independent audits after each payment cycle would strengthen confidence further.
None of this means the allowance is wrong. It means it should be seen as a bridge, not a destination. The more durable solutions lie elsewhere.
First, the minimum wage negotiations now beginning offer an opportunity to agree on a sustainable framework. Wages linked to productivity and reviewed regularly would protect workers more reliably than periodic emergency payments. Second, relief for the informal majority should come through targeted cash transfers. The National Social Register already provides a platform for this. Making it accurate, transparent and timely would allow government to support vulnerable households, regardless of where they work. This is the approach that the IMF has repeatedly recommended. Third, the root cause, the cost of moving people and goods, must be addressed directly. Expanding CNG-powered mass transit, improving urban rail and road networks, and encouraging competition in fuel supply would lower transport costs for everyone, not just salaried workers.
A cheaper commute benefits the trader and the farmer as much as the civil servant. Fourth, transparency should accompany every intervention. The government should publish the expected cost, the number of beneficiaries and the funding source, and report on disbursement. Public confidence depends on seeing that relief is honestly accounted for. Fifth, payment systems must be secure. Nigeria’s payroll has long been vulnerable to ghost workers and padded nominal rolls. Before the first installment is paid, federal and state authorities should verify beneficiaries through existing payroll and identity systems, so that the money reaches genuine workers, rather than leak through fraud. Independent audits after each payment cycle would strengthen confidence further. Every naira lost to an inflated payroll is a naira that could have supported a vulnerable household outside the public service.
Ultimately, a short-term allowance should be weighed against the more lasting alternatives available: a sustainable wage framework, targeted cash transfers for vulnerable households in the informal economy, and cheaper mass transport that lowers costs for every commuter. Relief for public servants is welcome, and labour has negotiated hard for it. A country where most workers have no employer to bargain on their behalf needs a wider safety net. The task is to turn a six-month concession into a lasting framework: fair wages, targeted support for the vulnerable and cheaper transport for all. That would be a relief worth celebrating.
Posi Olatubosun is a UK-based academic faculty member in accounting and finance.

title: NASS Roundup: Rising school fees, insecurity, poor telecom network, other stories from House of Reps
body:
The House on Tuesday urged the federal government to halt recent increases in tuition fees and other mandatory charges by public tertiary institutions, warning that the development could undermine the objectives of the Nigeria Education Loan Fund (NELFUND).
The call followed a motion moved by Ifeoluwa Ehindero (APC, Ondo), who said some public universities, polytechnics and colleges of education had increased their fees by more than 100 per cent.
He argued the increases could widen inequalities in access to education and make it harder for students from low-income families to benefit from the federal government’s student loan scheme.
The lawmakers urged the Federal Ministry of Education and the National Universities Commission to engage institutions’ management on suspending the increases and reviewing their tuition structures.
The House also mandated its Committees on University Education, Federal Polytechnics and Higher Technical Education, and Federal Colleges of Education to investigate the extent and justification for the increases.
The House Ad Hoc Committee on Telecommunications Service Quality rejected a request by the Association of Licensed Telecommunications Operators of Nigeria (ALTON) to allow its Chairman, Gbenga Adebayo, to represent telecommunications companies at its investigation into poor network services.
The committee, chaired by Olumide Osoba (APC, Ogun), insisted that the chief executives of MTN Nigeria, Airtel Nigeria, Globacom, Mafab Communications and other operators must appear individually to explain persistent complaints about dropped calls, poor internet connectivity, failed airtime and data transactions, and inadequate network coverage.
The committee gave the executives until 4 November to appear, warning that noncompliance could attract warrants of arrest.
The lawmakers argued that the operators held individual licences and should be directly accountable for service quality.
The investigation comes amid persistent subscriber complaints. Figures cited during the proceedings showed that the four major operators recorded a combined 413,587 consumer complaints in the first half of 2026.
Lawmakers seek security, humanitarian intervention after Taraba killings
Following the deadly bandit attack on Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State, the House on Thursday called for urgent security and humanitarian interventions for affected communities.
The lawmakers adopted a motion moved by Mohammed Audu (APC, Taraba), who said between 57 and 60 people reportedly died in the 23 October attack.
According to the lawmaker, the attackers opened fire on residents and traders at a community market, killing 10 people at the scene. In contrast, several others reportedly drowned in a river as they fled.
The House urged the federal government to strengthen intelligence-sharing among security agencies in Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi states and called on relevant humanitarian agencies to provide relief materials to affected families.
It also called for the completion of the abandoned Wase-Karim Lamido road project, which lawmakers said would improve access for security personnel responding to attacks.
The House referred the motion to the Committees on the North-East Development Commission, Works, and the National Emergency Management Agency for further legislative action.
The House Committee on Federal Polytechnics and Higher Technical Education gave the management of Kaduna Polytechnic 72 hours to submit financial records following concerns about declining internally generated revenue and the remittance of statutory deductions.
During an oversight visit to the institution on 28 October, the committee, chaired by Fuad Laguda (APC, Lagos), questioned why the polytechnic’s internally generated revenue fell from ₦1.478 billion in 2023 to ₦1.398 billion in 2024 and ₦1.332 billion in 2025 despite an increase in student enrolment.
The lawmakers also demanded documentary evidence showing that approximately ₦1.3 billion deducted as pension contributions had been remitted to the appropriate authorities.
They further sought explanations on the payment of death benefits to the families of more than 30 employees reportedly deceased between 2023 and 2025.
The Rector, Suleiman Umar, represented by the Deputy Rector (Academic), Aliyu Usman, denied any default in pension remittances and assured the committee that the requested documents would be submitted within the stipulated period.
The committee said it would review the documents before determining whether the institution had complied with its financial and statutory obligations.
The House also called on the federal government to establish a transparent regulatory framework for importing electric vehicles (EVs), compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles and other clean mobility equipment into Nigeria.
The resolution followed a motion moved by Ademorin Kuye (APC, Lagos) on 27 October.
Mr Kuye argued that although the government had introduced fiscal incentives, including import duty and tax reliefs, to encourage investment in cleaner transportation technologies, the policy required clear regulations to ensure local investment and consumer protection.
Under the proposed framework , companies seeking approval to import the vehicles would be required, where applicable, to establish certified maintenance centres, provide genuine spare parts and warranty support, and employ and train qualified Nigerian technical personnel.
They would also be expected to invest in electric vehicle charging infrastructure or CNG refuelling facilities and comply with relevant safety, environmental and technical standards.
The House urged the National Automotive Design and Development Council, the Bureau of Public Procurement, the Standards Organisation of Nigeria and the Nigeria Customs Service to develop objective criteria for approving importers.
It mandated the relevant House committees to monitor implementation and report back within four weeks for further legislative action.

title: Putin successfully counters Western efforts to isolate Russia — media
body:
NEW YORK, November 2. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin is successfully countering Western attempts to isolate Moscow internationally, The New York Times ’ Moscow bureau chief Paul Sonne wrote in an article published on the newspaper’s website.
"President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia engaged in a frenzy of diplomatic activity in the Russian capital this past week that underscored how, nearly five years into his war against Ukraine, he is thwarting Western attempts to isolate him and muscling his way back to center stage in global affairs," the article said.
Sonne described events such as Putin’s telephone conversation last week with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store as "rare." He also cited visits by African leaders to Moscow and engagement with the US administration as evidence of Russia’s active diplomacy.
"As Mr. Putin chips away at his ostracism in the West, relations between the United States and Ukraine have continued to deteriorate, underscoring Kiev’s vulnerability ahead of what is expected to be the worst winter of the war," Sonne added.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov previously said the West was promoting the idea of Russia’s supposed "international isolation," although the country’s diplomatic activity demonstrated that no such isolation existed. He noted that, despite all the talk of isolation, Russia continues to participate actively in international forums. By expanding its foreign ties, Russia "seeks to make the most of the opportunities opening up in this area to make its citizens’ lives safer and better in every respect," Lavrov said.

title: U.S. proposes resuming Russian gas sales to Europe through American intermediary, but European officials firmly reject idea, WSJ reports
body: The United States has proposed a plan to Vladimir Putin that would let Russia sell its natural gas to Europe through an American intermediary, bypassing European sanctions, sources told The Wall Street Journal. Donald Trump’s special envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, put forward the idea during trips to Moscow and Kyiv in September, the newspaper’s sources said. The White House wants Russia to funnel proceeds from gas sales into an escrow account in a third-country jurisdiction, preventing the Kremlin from using the money to finance the war. American negotiators believe Russia’s return to the European natural gas market would give Putin a powerful incentive to agree to an energy truce in Ukraine. Gas supplies would also provide Kyiv with income from transit fees, and the sales could open profitable opportunities for American investors. Trump’s negotiators tried to present the plan to European leaders as a way to lower energy prices ahead of winter, when Europe’s gas reserves fell to their lowest level for this time of year in several years, The Wall Street Journal reported. Europe’s official position is that the EU will not resume buying Russian gas. The Trump administration expects that resistance to prove “less rigid than meets the eye.” In private, however, European officials categorically reject the idea. One senior official from a Scandinavian country said resuming purchases of Russian gas would contradict everything Europeans stand for. Another senior official from a major European country compared the plan to former British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain’s sacrifice of Czechoslovakia in his dealings with Hitler. EU countries agreed in early 2026 to fully phase out Russian liquefied natural gas by January 1, 2027. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russian companies would soon redirect part of their LNG supplies from Europe to “friendly” countries. Senior Russian and American officials held talks in early October 2026 on bringing an American investor into the Nord Stream pipeline projects, Reuters reported. Russian presidential special representative Kirill Dmitriev and Jared Kushner took part in the discussions. A deal on American participation in the Nord Stream pipelines would let the United States profit from energy supplies to Europe after the war ends, Reuters noted . title: Entering Holy Kaaba with Tinubu a blessing beyond measure – Abdul Samad Rabiu
body: Billionaire industrialist and Chairman of BUA Group, Abdul Samad Rabiu, has described his entry into the Holy Kaaba alongside President Bola Tinubu as a rare spiritual privilege and an experience he would cherish for the rest of his life. Rabiu disclosed this in a Facebook post on Sunday night, sharing a photograph of himself with Tinubu He wrote, “Some moments in life are beyond words, moments that touch the soul and remain forever engraved in the heart. “Alhamdulillah, today I was profoundly humbled and blessed to be among those granted the extraordinary honour of entering the Holy Kaaba alongside His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR. “It was a once-in-a-lifetime blessing, an honour beyond measure, and a moment of divine grace that will remain etched in my heart for as long as I live.” Rabiu said his prayers at the sacred site extended beyond himself and his family to Nigeria, expressing hope for lasting peace, unity and prosperity in the country. He added, “In that most sacred of places, my thoughts and prayers were not only for myself and my family, but for our entire nation. “May Almighty Allah accept our prayers and bless our beloved nation with lasting peace, unity, and prosperity.” Rabiu was among the delegation that accompanied Tinubu to Makkah for Umrah, the lesser pilgrimage, on Friday, which included Oando Group Chief Executive Officer, Wale Tinubu, state governors and other senior government officials. Speaking at a dinner hosted for members of the delegation in Makkah on Saturday, Rabiu pledged the continued support of the business community for the administration and thanked the president for the rare spiritual opportunity. Tinubu had also told journalists after performing the Umrah that he felt fulfilled, describing the experience as spiritual. The post Entering Holy Kaaba with Tinubu a blessing beyond measure – Abdul Samad Rabiu appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Fuel crisis disrupts Khartoum transport, drives up agricultural production cost
body: The fuel and transport crisis in Sudan’s capital, Khartoum, has worsened in recent days amid acute supply shortages and a sharp rise in fuel prices. The situation has brought public transport to a near standstill, placing additional pressure on residents, drivers and farmers, as living costs and service-related challenges mount in several Sudanese cities. In the Al-Shuhada area of Omdurman, Mohammed Saif, a student, complained of overcrowding and difficulties finding public transport, saying large numbers of passengers had been left stranded while waiting for vehicles. “The authorities should deploy additional buses to ease the movement of residents,” he said. Meanwhile, Ali Al-Amin, a Khartoum resident, said drivers are being forced to spend an entire day queuing at petrol stations before returning to work the following day. “The situation has negatively affected our livelihoods and household incomes,” he lamented. The impact of the crisis has extended beyond the transport sector to agricultural activities. Mohammed Abdallah, a farmer, said the market price of a jerrycan of diesel, equivalent to four gallons, had risen to around 600,000 Sudanese pounds. “This sharp increase will drive up agricultural production costs,” he warned. “I appeal to the Ministry of Agriculture and relevant authorities to intervene and ease the burden on farmers.” In response to the transport crisis, Khartoum State Police have launched a mass transport initiative, deploying ten trucks belonging to the Operations Department to carry residents between different areas of the state. The initiative is intended to ease overcrowding and help stranded passengers reach their destinations. “The vehicles will be deployed along designated routes, and we will continue this operation until the fuel crisis is resolved,” the Khartoum State Police media department said in a statement. The developments come amid a wider crisis affecting fuel supplies, transport costs and essential services across Sudan. Cities including Omdurman, Khartoum and Bahri, as well as Kosti, Wad Madani, Sennar, Damazin, El Obeid, Kadugli, El Fasher and Nyala, are facing varying degrees of difficulty in accessing fuel and maintaining services and transport networks, against the backdrop of the ongoing war and deteriorating economic conditions. The crisis has raised concerns that its effects could further disrupt residents’ mobility, markets and agricultural activities, at a time when large sections of the population depend on public transport and fuel to meet their daily needs and sustain their livelihoods. The post Fuel crisis disrupts Khartoum transport, drives up agricultural production cost appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Russia needs to strengthen movie industry export potential — presidential advisor
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. The Russian movie industry needs to expand its export potential, as negative images of Russians are often portrayed in foreign films, Russian presidential advisor Elena Yampolskaya told TASS in an interview.
"In Russia, the industry receives such support measures as full state funding for the production and distribution of national films, including movies for children and youth, as well as family films. At the same time, it seems important to me to increase our export potential: foreign cinema often reproduces negative images of Russians, and the domestic industry must counteract this trend. It is important that a movie forum will be held as part of the Peoples of Russia International Week, which will become one of the key platforms for fostering intercultural dialogue," she said, calling cinema a tool of soft power. "It conveys national culture in an emotional and accessible way and shapes the image of the country. In recent years, a lot has been done to ensure the rapid development of the national movie industry and boost its competitiveness," the advisor said.
She emphasized that movies promoting Russian spiritual and moral values are also extremely important for the citizens of the country. "Of course, no one is going to do away with the study of languages or world culture. But after all, what a person loves from childhood is where their homeland is: films, music, holidays, images, heroes, and speech. We have a very rich heritage that we have the right to be proud of and that we are obliged to further develop for the sake of a decent future," Yampolskaya added.
