title: Al Habtoor Group board approves sale of all assets and investments in Lebanon
body: Dubai-based Al Habtoor Group said its board of directors had approved the sale of the company's assets and investments in Lebanon , after it ceased operations there. The company, which has hotels, commercial and residential properties in Lebanon, said in January that it was ceasing operations and would terminate its employees in the country due to "prolonged instability" and an investment dispute. The conglomerate, which made investments across hospitality, retail, leisure, real estate and banking-related activities in Lebanon, said at the time that it suffered losses exceeding $1.7 billion. "Following careful consideration, the board has determined that the complete divestment of the group’s Lebanese assets represents the most appropriate course of action, consistent with its commitment to responsible investment management, capital allocation, and the protection of its interests," Al Habtoor Group said on Monday. The company said it intends to undertake the divestment "through a structured and commercially driven process, with each asset evaluated on its individual merits and transactions pursued in accordance with appropriate market conditions and valuations". In February, Al Habtoor Group said it also appointed law firm White & Case to begin arbitration proceedings against Lebanon in the US. The case is based on the dispute resolution mechanisms provided under the UAE-Lebanon bilateral investment treaty, Al Habtoor Group said at the time. The group established its presence in Lebanon with the opening of its first hotel in 2001. It said it "has made substantial investments" since then and has remained committed to the country through successive periods of economic and political uncertainty. The board’s latest decision "reflects a considered shift" in its investment strategy and its plan to concentrate resources on markets "offering greater long-term stability, investment certainty, and sustainable growth opportunities", it said. Al Habtoor Group will announce further details regarding the divestment process, it added. Lebanon has been mired in an economic crisis since 2019, one of the worst in modern history, according to the World Bank. The lender expects Lebanon's economy to contract by 6.4 per cent in 2026. The country, which is heavily reliant on imports, is also struggling from the fallout of the Iran war, as it is more exposed to shocks such as the disruption to shipping and energy supplies. The International Monetary Fund said last month that it was advancing discussions with Lebanon as part of broader efforts to support vulnerable countries in the Middle East and North Africa.

title: Zelenskyy: I must tell Trump truth – USA must not help Russia, Putin
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy emphasized the need to speak frankly with U.S. leader Donald Trump about the real situation in Ukraine and stated that the United States must not help Russia, and the U.S. President must not help Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin.
In an interview with Fox News, when asked by a correspondent whether he fears that Trump might perceive his statements as an attempt to pressure the American president or U.S. society, Zelenskyy noted that he does not consider openness with partners to be a problem.
"I don't have any concerns when I share the truth between partners. And our countries are huge partners. American society is a huge supporter. And that's why I have to share with President the truth, the real situation: America can't help Russia. The President can't help Putin," Zelenskyy said.
The President also drew attention to the consequences of Russian missile and drone attacks on Ukraine. According to him, last night four separate regions came under strike, with energy infrastructure facilities becoming the main targets, leaving hundreds of thousands of people without electricity.
Zelenskyy noted that air raid alerts sounded throughout the night in Kyiv, and many people waited out the danger in the metro system.

title: GES cancels two-day mid-term break for basic schools in November
body: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has cancelled the two-day mid-term break scheduled for basic schools on November 5 and 6, 2026, as part of efforts to make up for instructional time lost during the recent industrial action. In a notice to the public, GES Management said all basic schools are expected to remain open and continue normal academic activities on both days. The cancellation means pupils and teachers will not observe the scheduled break and are expected to report to school as usual on Thursday, November 5, and Friday, November 6. The Service has urged teachers, students, parents and guardians to take note of the change and be guided accordingly. The notice was signed by Daniel Fenyi of the Ghana Education Service (GES).

title: Iran says "ball is in the U.S. court" on any deal to end the war
body:
Updated on: November 2, 2026 / 8:30 AM EST / CBS News
Iran's government-run broadcaster IRIB said Monday that 11 oil tankers had "caught fire" in the Strait of Hormuz in the previous nine days, disputing U.S. Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper's assertion last week that "all primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear."
In a post on X, IRIB said the 11 tankers had caught on fire since Oct. 25, the day on which it claimed Cooper made his recent fly-over of the strait.
The Iranian network offered no evidence, but claimed some of the vessels sank "to the depths of the sea."
Since the start of the war in February, Iran has targeted vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz in an effort to assert control over the narrow waterway, through which about a fifth of the world's crude oil supply typically passed prior to the conflict.
Cooper said last week in a Friday video statement that he saw no Iranian navy vessels in the strait during his flyover earlier in the week.
Later Friday, however, the U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center said there had been 30 attacks on commercial vessels in the month of October alone, a record high.
The U.S. military and President Trump have repeatedly declared Iran's navy destroyed and insisted that southern shipping lanes through the strait are available to merchant vessels, but ongoing Iranian threats and attacks have kept the risks and costs for shippers high, which has helped Tehran keep maintain pressure on global energy prices.
Iranian officials repeated warnings Monday of possible gas shortages for residents ahead of the winter, and they called on people to conserve the resource.
First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said he had to be honest about the stability of Iran's gas network in the colder months, as he asked the public to help conserve it.
Aref cited "imbalances accumulated over previous years and war-related damages," and warned that prices would increase for consumers who fail to conserve.
It is not the first time an Iranian official has warned about shortages. On October 25 , Iran's parliament speaker said natural gas consumption across Iran had to be reduced by 10%.
Iran's economy has been devastated by years of international sanctions, and the U.S. turn to economic warfare after the initial bombing campaigns of the ongoing conflict have strained finances for Tehran even further. The regime has not shown any willingness to bend on its demands to end the war, however, despite the economic pain for most Iranians.
Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson said Monday that the next move in the standoff with the United States is for President Trump to make.
"The ball is in the U.S. court, because our demands have been stated very clearly and transparently, and Iran's demands are reasonable and logical," Esmaeil Baqaei told journalists in Tehran.
Baqaei said ongoing negotiations, which have been brokered by Qatar, Pakistan and other mediators, were centered around the a seven-day proposal that Iran originally presented to the U.S. side in September, which calls for frozen Iranian assets to be released, the U.S. naval blockade to be lifted and an end to fighting on all fronts, in exchange for the phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and further negotiations on other topics.
President Trump rejected the initial proposal, but both sides have since exchanged revisions, and Mr. Trump has said repeatedly in recent weeks that he just needs to make a decision on whether to launch new attacks on Iran, or to make a deal to end the war.
Speaking Sunday to a radio network ahead of a campaign rally in Iowa, Mr. Trump said he would finish with the war soon, "one way or the other."
"Either they'll make a deal, or we'll just end it," he said, without offering any further context.
President Trump told reporters Sunday that he'd spoken with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday and had a "very good talk with him."
Mr. Trump gave no details but said the two had discussed the war in Iran.
According to sources cited by Axios , Netanyahu pushed for Mr. Trump to strike Iran but the president wants to let the negotiations play out.
The U.S. and Iran both engaged in indirect talks via mediators led by Qatar who are pushing to strike a deal between both sides before the conflict escalated.
Mr. Trump has repeatedly hinted he is considering resuming attacks on Iran after the midterm elections.
Qatari mediators are leading indirect talks aimed at reaching a deal between the U.S. and Iran, but the closed door negotiations have been punctuated by exchanges of threats between the leaders of both countries.
Iranian negotiators are in Qatar for talks on a proposal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz soon, according to Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who added the outcome depends on answers provided by the United States.
On Saturday, President Trump said the U.S. still had to "take care of" one or two more potential targets in Iran, citing a suspected nuclear complex at Pickaxe Mountain. On Sunday he reiterated the threat, saying he may have to give Tehran "the hammer" at some unspecified time.
Meanwhile, Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei warned on Saturday there would be no "geographical limitations" should the fighting with the U.S. resume, adding that there is a "vast theatre" to inflict damage.
Both sides have previously acknowledged that indirect talks are underway but consistently exchange threats.
The United Arab Emirates' presidential adviser said Sunday that his country hopes a diplomatic breakthrough in Qatar-led mediations is possible, but that they are also preparing for the possibility of escalation.
Speaking at a security forum in Bahrain, Anwar Gargash said Iran's attacks on Gulf countries such as the UAE made this a "watershed year" for the region.
"We don't really want to see another round of confrontation in the region," Gargash told the audience. But he added that his country and the region are braced for the "the worst," referring to the resumption of active hostilities.
The UAE was consistently targeted by Tehran in the opening weeks of the war in retribution for U.S. strikes on Iran, disrupting tourism and daily life, and effectively throwing the security landscape of the region into question.
A vessel was struck on Sunday by "an unknown projectile" in the Strait of Hormuz, a British maritime security agency said, after Qatari media reported an earlier attack on a gas tanker.
Britain's UKMTO maritime agency said "the master of a merchant vessel has relayed a mayday call... stating that another vessel has been struck by an unknown projectile" in the strait.
Earlier, Qatar's state news agency said a Qatari gas tanker had been attacked on Friday with "unidentified objects" while transiting Gulf waters. None of the crew members onboard the vessel were injured, and there was no environmental impact from the attack, the report said.
The attack struck a liquefied natural gas carrier, Al Mayeda, which belongs to the Qatar Gas Transport Company, Qatar News Agency said.
Since the Middle East war began in February, Iran has been targeting vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Gulf in an effort to assert control over shipping.
President Trump said he believes the U.S. will soon put the war with Iran away, "one way or the other."
The president was speaking to Right Side Broadcasting Network before a campaign rally in Iowa on Sunday.
"We've had such a victory, and we'll put it away very soon, one way or the other," Mr. Trump said. "Either they'll make a deal, or we'll just end it… The job we've done is amazing."
Earlier Sunday, Iran's top diplomat said he hopes there is "rationality" on the U.S. side as diplomatic efforts seek to avert a return to all-out war.

title: Hypersonica raises a hundred million for deep strike
body: Hypersonica, the British-German company developing hypersonic deep-strike systems for Europe, has raised €100 million in a Series B round co-led by Lightspeed and General Catalyst, money it will put into accelerating development, increasing its testing cadence and expanding operations across Europe, according to the company. Existing investors including Plural and 201 Ventures continued their participation in the round, which the company says is expected to support the creation of hundreds of highly skilled engineering and manufacturing jobs across the United Kingdom and Germany. Co-founders Dr Philipp Kerth, the chief executive, and Dr Marc Ewenz, the chief technology officer, said: “The debate about whether Europe needs hypersonic deep-strike capability is over. Governments have recognised the requirement and begun funding programmes. The challenge now is delivery. Europe needs credible hypersonic long-range capability, and more value for every pound and euro it spends. “We have shown that next-generation hypersonic systems can be developed in Europe faster and more affordably than conventional wisdom suggests. And we’re proud to be backed by investors who share our conviction that Europe should be able to develop and produce advanced strategic capabilities itself. “Series B marks our transition from demonstration to delivery. This funding will accelerate development, increase testing cadence, support European reindustrialisation and help ensure Europe has access to sovereign capability developed and produced in Europe.” Alexander Schmitt, a partner at Lightspeed, said: “Hypersonica is redefining how advanced defence capability gets built. The team pairs deep technical expertise with exceptional speed of execution, and the strength of our support reflects our confidence in both the technology and their ability to deliver.” Jeannette zu Fürstenberg, president and managing director at General Catalyst, said: “Strategic autonomy begins with the ability to build critical technologies at speed, at scale and at a fraction of the cost of traditional systems. That is exactly what Philipp, Marc, and the Hypersonica team are doing. They combine the ambition to tackle one of Europe’s most critical capability gaps with the engineering excellence to actually solve it. As Europe invests in its security and resilience, it will be companies like Hypersonica that play a defining role in translating ambition into real capability.” The company tested its HS-1 prototype in February, reaching speeds above Mach 6 over a range exceeding three hundred kilometres and becoming the first privately funded European defence company to achieve that. It says the development model behind the flight reduces costs by more than eighty per cent against conventional approaches, and that it has since expanded its engineering team, deepened engagement with governments and strengthened partnerships across the European defence industrial base. Government money has started moving in the same direction, and the Defence Investment Plan allocates an initial £770 million over four years to the United Kingdom-German Deep Precision Strike programme under the Trinity House Agreement, and a NATO-led multinational initiative announced in July envisages £37 billion of investment in deep precision strike over the next decade. Long-range conventional strike has been the most visible European capability gap since the war in Ukraine began. Britain and France hold Storm Shadow and SCALP, air-launched weapons with ranges in the low hundreds of kilometres, and the ground-launched systems that would reach further were removed from European arsenals by the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty. Filling the gap has so far meant buying American, which brings export control conditions with it. The company stresses that it develops, owns and controls its technology in Europe and that its systems are free of the International Traffic in Arms Regulations, the American export regime that gives Washington a say over where a weapon containing United States components can go and how it can be used. European governments have pushed harder on that point since 2022. Hypersonic weapons travel above Mach 5 and manoeuvre during flight, so they follow nothing like the predictable arc of a ballistic missile and are considerably harder for existing defences to engage. Russia and China have both fielded systems of this kind, and the European Long-range Strike Approach brings together France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Britain, the Netherlands and Sweden on a parallel effort. Hypersonica aims to deliver hypersonic deep-strike systems by 2029, and it raised €23.3 million in a Series A round led by Plural in February, announced alongside the HS-1 flight. The company operates from Munich and London. The post Hypersonica raises a hundred million for deep strike first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Loading on Russian Railways network down 1.4% in October — operator
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. Loading on the Russian Railwayus network in October amounted to 95.6 mln metric tons, down by 1.4% compared to the same period last year, the holding company said.
The rise in loading was provided by Kuybyshevskaya (+22.1%), Trans-Baikal (+13.9%), Oktyabrskaya (+5.6%), Far Eastern (+5.1%) and Gorkovskaya (+4.7%) railways, the Russian Railways said.
An increase is noted in shipment of metallurgical freight, including ferrous metals (+8.7%), non-ferrous ore (+9.8%), coke (+21.1%), and scrap metal (+22.5%). Railway shipments of cement (+9%) and chemicals (+9.4%) increased as well.
"The freight turnover continued growing in October (+2.5%) amid the negative overall dynamics of shipments associated with external factors, which reflects the ongoing reorientation of cargo flows and increasing transportation distance," Russian Railways said.
Loading in January - October 2026 totaled 920 mln metric tons and dropped by 0.8% year on year.

title: Russian forces attack homes, energy, logistics infrastructure in Zhytomyr region, three injured
body:
According to Ukrinform, Head of the Zhytomyr Regional Military Administration Vitalii Bunechko reported this on Facebook .
"The enemy continues to terrorize the Zhytomyr region. Over the past day and overnight, the Andrushivka, Berdychiv, Zhytomyr, Zviahel, Korosten, Ruzhyn and Cherniakhiv communities came under attack by strike drones," the official said.
According to him, Russian forces targeted energy and logistics infrastructure facilities, civilian administrative buildings and private homes. Efforts to deal with the aftermath of the Russian attacks are ongoing.
"Three people have been reported injured so far, including one child. They are receiving the necessary medical care," Bunechko added.

title: Tinubu: I Remain Committed To Building A Prosperous Nigeria
body: .Appreciates God for obliging him rare favour and privilege to lead Nigerians .Thanks King Salman for granting him access to Ka’abah Deji Elumoye in Abuja President Bola Tinubu on Monday reiterated his commitment to Project Nigeria and his determination to build a prosperous nation, invest in the future of young Nigerians, and pursue development in line with the will of Almighty Allah and the people’s aspirations. The President stated this while reflecting on his spiritual journey to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah, during which the Custodian of the Holy Mosques of Makkah and Madinah, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, granted him a rare privilege of leading Nigeria’s delegation to pray inside the Holy Ka’abah. At the Ka’abah, Tinubu offered prayers of gratitude to Almighty Allah for the privilege of serving as Nigeria’s President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces. Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal of Masjid al-Haram led the President into the Ka’abah. Tinubu thanked the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, for granting him and members of his Nigerian delegation the opportunity to enter the Holy Ka’abah in Makkah and offer prayers to Almighty Allah. The President described the honour as a historic and deeply cherished spiritual experience, reflecting the longstanding bonds of friendship, mutual respect and cooperation between Nigeria and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. His words: “I want to say a big thank you for the faith, for the recognition. I can’t believe the fencing of the Ka’abah is in Green-White-Green, which reminds us of the Nigerian identity. “I thank the Crown Prince and all the administrators of the holy land. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as the leader of the delegation and the country. “We are all facing challenges and hostility around us. We will overcome them with faith in God Almighty. I’m grateful forever. I thank the King and the royal Crown Prince. “It is an honour that I enjoyed, and it is gracious of them to have allowed me to enter inside the Ka’abah. This is history.” Tinubu said he asked Allah for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians, and expressed confidence that his prayers have been answered. According to him: “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that prayer has been granted. Before the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then, and He did. And I promised that I would come back to thank Him.” Reflecting on the message from the Holy Qur’an in Surah Aal-Imran, Verse 26, which affirms that Almighty Allah is the Owner of all sovereignty, granting power and authority to whom He wills and taking them away from whom He wills, the President said power is a trust that must be exercised responsibly, with humility and in the service of the people, recognising that no position of authority is permanent and that ultimate sovereignty belongs to Almighty Allah. “There is no other God but Almighty Allah. He is the giver and the taker. He owns power and authority. He says, ‘ If I give you, use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person. I am the only One who has that authority,” the President said, quoting the words of the Qur’an. Tinubu said faith in Allah had strengthened his conviction that his emergence as Nigeria’s leader was an extraordinary blessing that must be matched with dedicated service to the country. “I have faith in that, and I believe extremely well that He has done me and my country a great favour. Out of many millions of people, to be the President and Commander-in-Chief is a favour that only Almighty God can do to a human being,” he stated. The President emphasised that his commitment to Project Nigeria had become even stronger, assuring Nigerians of his resolve to pursue policies and programmes that would promote prosperity, national development and shared progress. “My commitment to Project Nigeria is higher. I am determined to usher in prosperity and fully develop the country, consistent with the wish of Allah and the support of the people. “It is important to put Allah first, then move on. Follow your conscience. Follow the right path that will lead Nigeria to that greatness,” Tinubu said. On the nation’s economic outlook, the President expressed optimism about the progress made under his watch, describing the economic foundation as solid and the country’s emergence from a difficult period as encouraging. “The foundation is solid, and the economy has come out of the dark tunnel. This is inspiring.” He maintained, however, that nation-building requires sustained investment in young Nigerians’ future, noting that today’s leaders’ decisions will determine how future generations remember them. “We need to build a future for our youth. If we don’t invest in their future, how do we want to be remembered as leaders 50 years from now? That’s the main thing. So this is a rare privilege to lead the country,” he added. Tinubu reiterated that his administration would remain focused on strengthening the country’s economic foundations, expanding opportunities for young people and creating the conditions necessary for Nigerians to realise their potential. The President thanked Almighty Allah for the opportunity to lead Nigeria and reaffirmed his determination to justify the confidence the Nigerian people have placed in him through purposeful leadership and an enduring commitment to national progress. Apparently seized by emotions, Minister of Justice Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), his Health and Social Welfare counterpart, Prof Ali Pate, Governors of Borno, Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Yobe and Kwara States as well as captains of industry, including Chairman of BUA, Abdulsamad Isiaka Rabiu and CEO of Oando, Wale Tinubu, expressed gratitude to Allah and the President for allowing them to enter and pray with him in the most holy mosque and sacred ground in Islam.

title: British patrol ship ‘opens fire’ near Falkland Islands
body: HMS Medway has put 120 rounds downrange from her 30mm automatic gun during training in the South Atlantic, carried out with staff from Flag Officer Sea Training embarked, according to the Royal Navy. The ship said: “120 rounds downrange. With @FOST embarked, we took the opportunity for further routine training and put our 30mm Automatic Small Calibre Gun through its paces again. Practice = Precision.” Flag Officer Sea Training sends its assessors to sea with warships to put crews through the full range of warfighting serials and certify that a ship is ready for operations, a process most vessels go through in home waters before deploying. The 30mm Automatic Small Calibre Gun is the main armament of the River class, a stabilised mounting firing a high explosive round out to around two and a half kilometres, and the weapon a patrol vessel would use against a small craft that failed to comply. Accuracy with it depends on gunners who shoot often. Keeping the weapons serviceable in that climate takes work of its own, of course. The ship’s weapon engineers have been maintaining the armament through the South Atlantic weather, and Medway said of them : “The Falklands wind doesn’t make maintenance any easier! Our Weapon Engineers work hard to keep our equipment ready when it matters, whatever the weather throws at them.” Medway carried out live machine gun firings at the edge of the Falkland Islands Conservation Zone during a four-day patrol at the end of July, British Forces South Atlantic Islands stated at the time. The patrol, designated Operation Southern Vigilance, ran from 26 to 29 July, and the ship’s company fired mounted machine guns and worked through a man overboard exercise alongside an RAF A400M Atlas transport aircraft, work the command describes as maintaining operational readiness. According to British Forces South Atlantic Islands, the deployment demonstrated Britain’s enduring commitment to the Falkland Islands by maintaining a visible presence and a capable force, helping to deter potential adversaries. Other training has continued alongside the gunnery, and the ship carries a Rigid Raider in addition to two Pacific 24 seaboats, allowing it to land personnel and equipment ashore, and it has been running routine exercises with 2nd Battalion, The Parachute Regiment. Seaboat coxswains have been practising approach and pacing drills with peer-to-peer coaching in the evenings. HMS Medway is a River class offshore patrol vessel commissioned in 2019, and she took over the South Atlantic Patrol Task from HMS Forth, which held the role for several years after replacing HMS Clyde. The class displaces around 2,000 tonnes and carries a 30mm gun, machine guns and a flight deck able to take a Merlin, with an endurance suited to long independent patrols in remote waters. The ship is the only Royal Navy vessel permanently assigned to the region. British Forces South Atlantic Islands also operates Typhoon fighters and A400M and Voyager aircraft from RAF Mount Pleasant on East Falkland, alongside an infantry company, Sky Sabre air defence and a radar station on Mount Byron. The post British patrol ship ‘opens fire’ near Falkland Islands first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Haas: Postgres 19 is late, and it's AI's fault
body:
In the end, I don't think that the delay in shipping PostgreSQL 19 is particularly concerning. It is not a long delay in the grand scheme of things, and it emerges directly from the project's concern for quality. The long-term picture is less clear and in some ways more troubling: given that we have forty years of bugs that humans were unable to find but LLMs are quite capable of discovering, how are we ever going to catch up, and how will PostgreSQL continue to innovate? Right now, I'm not sure. What I do know is that I, and many others, are working really hard to figure it out. LWN looked at the PostgreSQL 19 release and its challenges in September. to post comments This doesn't sound like a bad thing Posted Oct 30, 2026 18:43 UTC (Fri) by vadim (subscriber, #35271) [ Link ] (2 responses) I understand the appeal for adding more and more features, but in a database, stability is absolutely critical. If Postgres 19 comes out with less new fancy features but far higher quality, that's a huge "selling" point in my mind. And I don't know about Postgres' policies, but you're not limited to using AI just to find bugs, it can also be used to fix them, write tests, etc. That'd be of help with the catching up. This doesn't sound like a bad thing Posted Oct 31, 2026 0:24 UTC (Sat) by fraetor (subscriber, #161147) [ Link ] It also might not end up so bad in the end. As far as I understand, all of these large features that were reverted for PG19 were originally written before AI tools were considered nearly as effective as they are today. Perhaps new features that are only just starting development will have more bugs found as part of development and thus arrive more robust. This doesn't sound like a bad thing Posted Oct 31, 2026 2:16 UTC (Sat) by alp (subscriber, #136414) [ Link ] Some of the reverted ones at least are not fancy. Temporal DB support is a standard way of doing what is being done ad-hoc in application code N different ways. Property graph queries some could argue at the very least is fancy, GROUP BY ALL and online disabling DB-level data checksums really aren't. A few others are optimisations. The original blog post has the worst title ever Posted Oct 31, 2026 9:33 UTC (Sat) by iustin (subscriber, #102433) [ Link ] (6 responses) Both here, on the blog itself, and on Phoronix, this title is so bad I wonder the original author actually thought. In my personal opinion, the actual title should have been "Postgres 19 is late, and we're thankful to AI for all the bug fixes". The original blog post has the worst title ever Posted Oct 31, 2026 14:47 UTC (Sat) by rsidd (subscriber, #2582) [ Link ] (3 responses) Yes. One can complain about AI slop non-bug reports. But when there are real bugs, how is it AI's fault? The original blog post has the worst title ever Posted Oct 31, 2026 17:16 UTC (Sat) by cyperpunks (subscriber, #39406) [ Link ] (1 responses) > Yes. One can complain about AI slop non-bug reports. But when there are real bugs, how is it AI's fault? The fault is insuffient quality of software produced, as AI has raised the bar for quality ny a significant amount. The promise (it seems) is/was faster development of new features, however due to the side effect of much better QA done by AI, the development has slowed down instead. This is not unique to Postgres, it's not unique to Open Source software, it's everywhere. Countless projects and org are now very busy fixing yesterday problems with no time to create shiny new features. The original blog post has the worst title ever Posted Nov 2, 2026 4:11 UTC (Mon) by rsidd (subscriber, #2582) [ Link ] >due to the side effect of much better QA done by AI, the development has slowed down instead. This may not be a bad thing. There is a finite number of bugs in any given piece of software, even huge and ancient projects like Postgres or the Linux kernel. Maybe we will find all of them in a year or so, and also catch new bugs during development before release. Projects have to figure out the workflow, but the overall result may be a net positive. The original blog post has the worst title ever Posted Nov 2, 2026 3:47 UTC (Mon) by welinder (guest, #4699) [ Link ] > Yes. One can complain about AI slop non-bug reports. But when there are real bugs, how is it AI's fault? It's AI's fault if the reports are of poor quality, even if there is an underlying, real bug. "Poor quality" can cover a multitude of sins, including burying the relevant information in, quite plainly, too many f-ing words with no indication of which parts are important and which parts are not. That generates real work and chasing bogus leads is very exhausting. If only the report would say "In liboink v1.2.3, your allocation at foo.c:1234 is one byte to short. Sample program, stack trace, and suggested patch attached." Facts, not speculation. And a patch needs to (1) apply, (2) not contain old commented-out code, (3) not contain comments about the old code, (4) follow the coding style of the project it's intended for, (5) not try to fix or change anything unrelated. If I have to edit the patch, that patch isn't very helpful. Something like that); certainly Haas is not saying it’s a bad thing in the text. The original blog post has the worst title ever Posted Nov 1, 2026 10:05 UTC (Sun) by iustin (subscriber, #102433) [ Link ] I think I mostly agree? It sounded neutral to me, not positive. But I still claim the title as written was a bit disheartening to read. Anyway, looking forward to a better Postgres…

title: Next winter may be tougher for Kiev than the previous one — news agency
body:
MOSCOW, November 2. /TASS/. The upcoming winter may affect the Ukrainian capital more severely than the winter of 2025-2026 amid critical power shortages, RBC-Ukraine reported, citing sources.
In the event of further explosions, Kiev may face prolonged disruptions to subway services and critical electricity shortages, a source told the Ukrainian news agency. "If the situation gets really bad, the maximum the city can do within its own authority will be to ensure water, electricity and heat supplies to critical infrastructure and an operational sewage network," the news agency quoted him as saying.
Earlier, Ukraine’s DTEK grid operator reported emergency blackouts in and around Kiev.
Ukraine has been grappling with electricity supply problems amid large-scale damage to its energy infrastructure. An emergency was declared in the country’s grid system. Daily multi-hour power cuts are still being implemented across many regions.

title: Police Found 10-Year Old Wandering In Anambra, Seek Parents
body: The Anambra State Police Command has rescued a 10-year-old boy, identified as Chinecherem Onuwasoanya, who was found wandering in Okpoko, Ogbaru Local Government Area, after losing his way home. The boy, who said he is from Ebenebe community in Anambra State, was rescued by operatives of the Okpoko Police Division on the afternoon of Sunday, November 1, 2026. The Police Public Relations Officer, Tochukwu Ikenga, said in a statement that the boy had gone out to play but could not find his way back home or locate his family members. He said a concerned resident who found the child wandering took him to the Okpoko Police Division for assistance. The police said efforts had begun to contact the boy’s parents or guardians and reunite him with his family. The Commissioner of Police, Anambra State Command, Nnanna Oji Ama, commended the Good Samaritan for bringing the child to the police station and urged residents to remain alert and support efforts to protect children and other vulnerable persons. The police commissioner also advised parents and guardians to provide adequate supervision for their children and take precautions to ensure they can be identified and traced if separated from their families. The police appealed to the public, asking anyone with information that could help locate Chinecherem’s parents or guardians to contact the Okpoko Police Division or the Anambra State Police Command. The post Police Found 10-Year Old Wandering In Anambra, Seek Parents appeared first on Channels Television .

title: GMet warns of possible drop in Volta River inflows amid El Niño conditions
body: The Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) has warned that persistent El Niño conditions could reduce water inflows into the Volta River, potentially affecting hydroelectric power generation at the Akosombo Dam. El Niño, the warm phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), is a naturally occurring climate phenomenon that influences rainfall and temperature patterns across different parts of the world. Deputy Director of Research and Applied Meteorology at GMet, Francisca Martey, said below-normal rainfall expected across parts of West Africa could affect water resources shared by Ghana and neighbouring countries. She explained that the phenomenon was influencing rainfall patterns, resulting in prolonged dry spells and warmer conditions in parts of Ghana. She noted that the impact extended beyond Ghana, as neighbouring countries within the wider West African region were also expected to experience below-normal rainfall. “It means that those people in our other countries also get below-normal rainfall, which affects our water resources,” she said on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Monday, November 2, while discussing the phenomenon. The host raised concerns that reduced rainfall could lead to lower inflows into the Akosombo Dam and, consequently, affect electricity generation from hydroelectric sources. Mrs Martey agreed, highlighting the potential implications of the weather phenomenon for Ghana’s water and energy resources. Read Also: GMet warns of possible drop in Volta River inflows amid El Niño conditions The warning comes as Ghana prepares for a period of prolonged dry conditions, with GMet projecting above-normal temperatures and below-normal rainfall in the coming months. Mrs Martey said the agency had already forecast extended dry spells and reduced rainfall across much of the country during the September-October-November (SON) period. “We’re going to have long dry spells. We’re going to have below-normal rainfall,” she said. She added that the conditions were expected to persist into the December-January-February (DJF) period, when the Harmattan season would bring drier air and warmer temperatures. “We expect that December, January, and February will be warmer,” she stated. According to her, northern Ghana could experience more pronounced effects because of its vulnerability to rainfall deficits and its importance to the country’s food production. “Although the El Niño affects the whole country, its impact is higher on the northern areas,” she said. She warned that prolonged dry conditions could affect farmers, particularly those in communities that depend on stored rainwater for agricultural activities. “The little rainwater that they have kept or saved would also dry up,” she said. Mrs Martey urged farmers to adopt climate-smart agricultural practices, including mulching, to conserve soil moisture and minimise the effects of prolonged dry spells. She said GMet was engaging stakeholders in agriculture, health and water resources management, as well as the general public, to improve preparedness for the anticipated weather conditions. She also advised Ghanaians to stay hydrated and protect themselves against dusty conditions expected during the Harmattan season.

title: Who’s coddling Bato dela Rosa? Not us, says MNLF
body: If Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa is, indeed, hiding in Mindanao, the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) insists they’re not the ones sheltering him. In a statement, the MNLF denied it is the “powerful armed group” that had been “cuddling” (or shouldn’t that be coddling?) Dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court (ICC) over his alleged role in the bloody drug war of the Rodrigo Duterte administration. “The MNLF is not cuddling Senator Bato. There is no established formal relationship between Sen. Ronald ‘Bato’ dela Rosa and the MNLF,” the group said in its statement. Dela Rosa has been out of public view since May amid the ICC arrest warrant. The MNLF made the statement after Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said that he had received information that the legislator was being protected by an “armed” group in Mindanao. Remulla had also warned that attempting a forced arrest on the lawmaker could cost “10,000” lives, to explain why he would rather negotiate the senator’s surrender. The interior chief did not identify the alleged armed group. The MNLF, however, was quick to distance itself from the speculation, saying the personal ties between former president Rodrigo Duterte and MNLF founder Nur Misuari should not be construed as evidence that the group was hiding dela Rosa. “The claim that the MNLF may be protecting him is speculation, not a confirmed fact. Reports emphasize that the MNLF is fragmented and that it is uncertain whether the Misuari faction would-or could-shield him from arrest,” the group said. “So, the accurate answer is: dela Rosa appears to have personal and political connections to figures associated with the MNLF, especially through Duterte’s relationship with Nur Misuari, but there is no verified evidence that he is an MNLF member, ally in an operational sense, or currently being protected by the group,” it added. Partido Demokratiko Pilipino Lakas ng Bayan, Dela Rosa’s political party, has appealed to the Supreme Court for a swift resolution of Dela Rosa’s case. The senator’s camp also urged the High Court to reverse its earlier ruling and stop the use of an ICC warrant of arrest against him. But with the senator still nowhere to be found, could his arrest be drawing closer? The Philippine National Police has intensified its manhunt for its former chief after the one-week deadline for his voluntary surrender lapsed. Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson , who previously called for Dela Rosa’s safe arrest, has a reminder for authorities: Keep their operations under wraps. “When pursuing a high-profile target or handling a sensitive live case, secrecy discipline is key — unless disinformation is necessary to flush the quarry into the open,” Lacson, a former PNP chief, said in a social media post. Did Lacson have anyone in particular in mind when he gave the unsolicited advice? – Rappler.com

title: African players in Europe: Defender Hakimi’s historic hat-trick
body: Reigning African Footballer of the Year and Paris Saint-Germain defender Achraf Hakimi claimed a first career hat-trick at the weekend in a 5-1 Ligue 1 rout of bottom club Le Havre. Meanwhile, Nicolas Jackson continued to defy critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea by scoring his eighth goal in 12 appearances for Aston Villa, who drew 1-1 with Fulham. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: FRANCE ACHRAF HAKIMI (Paris Saint-Germain) Morocco captain Hakimi was involved in all five goals as defending European champions and Ligue 1 leaders PSG inflicted a seventh defeat in nine matches on Le Havre. Apart from his hat-trick, he set up goals for Mika Godts and Senny Mayulu. ENGLAND NICOLAS JACKSON (Aston Villa) In-form Jackson scored again, but it was not enough for Unai Emery’s men to defeat struggling Fulham. The Senegal international coolly slotted home from Johan Manzambi’s pass for a fifth Premier League goal in his last five games. TAIWO AWONIYI (Coventry City) Awoniyi netted his first league goal for Coventry in a 3-1 win over Sunderland that hauled the Sky Blues out of the relegation zone. The Nigerian made the most of his first start since September as he won possession himself before surging into the Sunderland box and firing into the bottom corner. SPAIN YAN DIOMANDE (Real Madrid) Ivory Coast teenager Diomande completed the scoring before half-time as Real Madrid triumphed 3-0 at Racing Santander in La Liga. The record signing by the 15-time European champions lashed home from the edge of the box after 37 minutes. ITALY M’BALA NZOLA (Cagliari) Angolan Nzola gave mid-table Cagliari the lead midway through the first half, but Serie A pacesetters Lazio hit back to win 2-1 in Rome. Nzola struck from the edge of the six-yard box to net in successive matches for the first time in 70 months. GERMANY SERHOU GUIRASSY (Borussia Dortmund) His second-half goal put Borussia on track for an impressive 2-2 Bundesliga draw at leaders Bayern Munich. After Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane missed a penalty, Dortmund went to the other end of the pitch and Guirassy equalised. It brought the goal tally of the Guinea striker in all competitions to eight this season. IBRAHIM MAZA (Bayer Leverkusen) Leverkusen were outplayed by Stuttgart in a 4-2 defeat, but Maza left the pitch with his head held high. After the Algeria midfielder showcased his stunning dribbling, he scored after 79 minutes with an unstoppable header. BILAL EL KHANNOUSS (Stuttgart) El Khannouss provided the creative spark as Stuttgart snapped a run of poor form to win at Leverkusen. The Moroccan scored with a superb low shot early in the second half and helped create Stuttgart’s fourth for Ermedin Demirovic. title: North Korea to continue to rapidly strengthen its nuclear capabilities — agency
body:
PYONGYANG, November 2. /TASS/. The DPRK has no plans to alter its course toward the accelerated buildup of its nuclear deterrent forces in response to the military activities of the United States and the Republic of Korea, Kim Jong Sik, first vice department director of the Central Committee of the Workers' Party of Korea (WPK), said, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported.
"We are confident in our capabilities and determined to respond to everything," he said, adding that "the national defense policy of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), which aims to bolster the country's nuclear war deterrent at an even faster pace, will not change in the slightest."
Kim Jong Sik condemned the US-South Korea joint exercises Iron Mace, which were conducted from September 29 to October 2. According to him, the maneuvers, during which the joint use of US nuclear forces and South Korean conventional weapons was practiced, were "the most hideous nuclear war rehearsal aimed at using nuclear weapons against the DPRK."
The North Korean official also highlighted the Hoguk and Freedom Flag exercises held in South Korea in October, as well as the Keen Sword exercise in Japan. He said that Washington and its allies are intensifying military activity in the region, including the deployment of intelligence units and aircraft sent from the United States.
According to Kim Jong Sik, North Korea is confident in its capabilities and ready to respond to any developments. Pyongyang will continue to build up its nuclear forces, which it views as a means of protecting national sovereignty and maintaining peace in the region, he said.

title: Russia’s Finance Ministry proposes automatically transferring pension savings into long-term savings program
body: Russia’s Finance Ministry has drafted a bill that would move the funded portion of pensions into the long-term savings program ( PDS ), the Russian business news outlet RBC reported. The transfer would happen automatically starting April 1, 2027. The government commission on legislative activity will review the bill as early as this week, and it is expected to go to the State Duma in early November 2026, according to RBC’s sources. The measure covers both the funded pensions of so-called “silent” citizens — people who never applied to transfer their pension savings to non-state pension funds or private management companies — and the funds held by clients of non-state pension funds (NPFs). In total, 6.6 trillion rubles in pension savings are expected to move into the long-term savings program: 2.98 trillion rubles belonging to “silent” citizens and managed by the state-owned management company VEB, and 3.6 trillion rubles held by 24 non-state pension funds. “The proposed measure equalizes the rights and opportunities to build long-term savings for both current clients of the Social Fund of Russia and clients of non-state pension funds,” the Finance Ministry said. This will give citizens more options for managing these funds, as well as create conditions for building additional capital. The Finance Ministry told RBC that an “authorized fund” with mandatory state participation would be created to manage the funds of “silent” citizens. According to the outlet’s sources, the new structure is expected to include NPF Blagosostoyaniye and NPF VTB Pension Fund. Russia has frozen contributions to the funded portion of citizens’ pensions since 2014. Before that, the funded portion was built from contributions equal to 6% of the earnings of citizens born in 1967 or later, which could stay with the Social Fund or be transferred to a non-state pension fund to boost returns. Another 16% of earnings went toward the insurance portion of the pension. After 2014, the portion of earnings that had previously funded pensions has gone toward the insurance portion to pay current retirees. The Russian business daily Kommersant notes that deputies in the State Duma discussed the proposal to automatically transfer the funded portion of pensions into the PDS back in June 2025. Anatoly Aksakov, head of the State Duma committee on the financial market, initiated that discussion, saying the move would help develop private long-term investment in Russia. title: Tinubu reaffirms commitment to Project Nigeria
body: President Bola Tinubu has reaffirmed his commitment to Project Nigeria, pledging to build a prosperous nation, invest in youths and pursue development guided by Almighty Allah and Nigerians’ aspirations. The president stated this on Monday while reflecting on his spiritual journey to Saudi Arabia for the lesser Hajj, during which he was granted the rare privilege of praying inside the Holy Ka’abah. King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, granted the President and members of his delegation access to the sacred structure in Makkah. At the Ka’abah, Tinubu offered prayers of gratitude to Almighty Allah for the privilege of serving as Nigeria’s president and commander-in-chief of the armed forces. Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal of Masjid al-Haram led the President into the Ka’abah. Tinubu thanked King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for granting him and members of his delegation the opportunity to enter the Holy Ka’abah and offer prayers. He described the honour as historic and a deeply cherished spiritual experience, reflecting the longstanding bonds of friendship, mutual respect and cooperation between Nigeria and Saudi Arabia. “I want to say a big thank you for the faith, for the recognition. I can’t believe the fencing of the Ka’abah is in green-white-green, which reminds us of the Nigerian identity. “I thank the Crown Prince and all the administrators of the Holy Land. I thank them for the hospitality and recognition given to me as the leader of the delegation and the country. “We are all facing challenges and hostility around us. We will overcome them with faith in God Almighty. I’m grateful forever. I thank the King and the royal Crown Prince. “It is an honour that I enjoyed, and it is gracious of them to have allowed me to enter inside the Ka’abah. This is history,” he said. The president said he prayed for wisdom and resilience to continue serving Nigerians, expressing confidence that Almighty Allah had granted his request. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that prayer has been granted. Before the 2023 election, I did the same thing. “I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then, and He did. And I promised that I would come back to thank Him,” the President said. Reflecting on Surah Aal-Imran, Verse 26 of the Holy Qur’an, the President said sovereignty belonged ultimately to Almighty Allah, who grants and withdraws power. He said the message underscored the need for leaders to exercise authority responsibly, with humility and in the service of the people. “There is no other God but Almighty Allah. He is the giver and the taker. He owns power and authority. “He says, ‘If I give you, use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person. I am the only one who has that authority.” Tinubu said his faith had strengthened his conviction that becoming Nigeria’s leader was an extraordinary blessing that must be matched with dedicated service. “I have faith in that, and I believe extremely well that He has done me and my country a great favour. ”Out of many millions of people, to be the President and Commander-in-Chief is a favour that only Almighty God can do to a human being,” he stated. The president said his commitment to Project Nigeria had become stronger, assuring Nigerians of his determination to pursue policies that would promote prosperity and shared progress. “My commitment to Project Nigeria is higher. I am determined to usher in prosperity and fully develop the country, consistent with the wish of Allah and the support of the people. “It is important to put Allah first, then move on. Follow your conscience. Follow the right path that will lead Nigeria to that greatness,” he said. On the economy, Tinubu expressed optimism about the progress recorded under his administration. “The foundation is solid, and the economy has come out of the dark tunnel. This is inspiring,” he said. He said nation-building required sustained investment in young Nigerians, stressing that present leadership decisions would shape how future generations remembered them. “We need to build a future for our youth. If we don’t invest in their future, how do we want to be remembered as leaders 50 years from now? That’s the main thing. So this is a rare privilege to lead the country,” the president added. Tinubu reiterated his administration’s commitment to strengthening the economy, expanding opportunities for young people and creating conditions for Nigerians to realise their potential. He thanked Almighty Allah for the opportunity to lead Nigeria, pledging to justify the confidence reposed in him through purposeful leadership and sustained commitment to national progress. (NAN) The post Tinubu reaffirms commitment to Project Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Xi Jinping warns against great-power conflict in the Gulf as China, Oman eye trade pact
body: The Middle East and Gulf region should not become a battleground for great-power rivalry, and China is willing to work with Arab nations to achieve lasting peace, Chinese President Xi Jinping told Oman's sultan on Monday.China has traditionally played a low-key diplomatic role in the Middle East, but has stepped up efforts to try to help end tensions amid the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has snarled the Strait of Hormuz and driven up global energy and shipping costs.Xi told Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said that the world is undergoing "profound changes unseen in a century.""The Middle East Gulf region should not become an arena for great-power rivalry and geopolitical conflict. Peace and stability in the region require joint nurturing and protection by all parties," Xi said, according to China's Foreign Ministry.China has consistently been committed to stopping the war, and hopes to contribute "wisdom and solutions to resolving the region's security dilemmas," he added.China is willing to strengthen communication and coordination with Arab countries, including the Gulf Cooperation Council states, to work together toward restoring peace and achieving lasting stability and security, Xi said.Last week, China's Foreign Ministry said the country will soon be dispatching its special envoys to the Middle East to promote engagement and de-escalation.First China tripHaitham arrived in Beijing on Sunday for a two-day visit, the first by an Omani head of state since the countries established ties in 1978.Haitham told Xi his government had deep appreciation for China's positions on key issues concerning the region, Omani state media reported."We believe that development and stability are inextricably linked," he said."The prosperity of nations requires an environment defined by security, peace, respect for state sovereignty, and adherence to international law - an environment where disputes are resolved through peaceful means."New avenues for trade, investment with Oman, ChinaHe also said Oman was open to entering into a preferential bilateral trade and investment agreement with China."We are confident that such an agreement would open new avenues for trade and investment, facilitate and enhance commercial and investment exchanges between our two nations," Haitham said.China is Oman's largest trade partner, with tourism and business links boosted by direct flights between Beijing and Muscat since November last year.Oman, which exports crude oil and energy products to China, has also been looking to further develop its renewable energy supply chains and digital commerce.The Omani leader, who was welcomed on the tarmac in Beijing by People's Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng, also emphasized cooperation between investment and financial institutions.

title: South Sudan elections unlikely as academics cite legal, administrative hurdles
body: Two experts at the University of Juba have cast doubt on South Sudan’s ability to hold general elections on 22 December, citing administrative shortcomings, legal uncertainties, insecurity, and the incomplete implementation of the country’s 2018 peace agreement. Prof. Abraham Kuol Nyuon, a political science professor, told Radio Tamazuj that the elections were unlikely to take place as scheduled, predicting a possible two- to three-month extension because of what he described as inadequate preparations by the National Elections Commission (NEC). Dr. Geri Raymondo, a law lecturer at the University of Juba and legal expert, said the challenges went beyond logistical preparations, arguing that unresolved constitutional questions, insecurity, and incomplete security sector reforms raised concerns about the country’s readiness to hold elections. Prof. Nyuon said the launch of civic education by the NEC had initially raised public expectations that the elections would take place. However, he questioned the effectiveness of the preparations, particularly outside the capital, Juba. He said posters promoting civic education could be seen in parts of the capital, but questioned how effectively voters were being reached in the states. “The chances are very high that December 22 is not feasible,” he said, adding that elections required extensive preparations and could not be treated as a one-day event. He also raised concerns about logistical arrangements and voter registration, saying the commission appeared not to be sufficiently prepared despite the approaching deadline. For his part, Dr. Raymondo equally questioned whether the necessary electoral processes had been completed, arguing that conducting elections required more than organising voting on a particular date. “Election is a process. It’s not voting,” he said, emphasising the need to comply with the Constitution and the National Elections Act. However, the two experts gave differing accounts of the status of voter registration. Raymondo said registration had taken place but questioned whether the wider electoral preparations, including voter education, were being adequately implemented on the ground. Nyuon said voter registration was still outstanding. The National Elections Commission’s position on the status of the process was not available in the interviews. Legal questions over election law Dr. Geri Raymondo, a law lecturer at the University of Juba and legal expert, speaking to Radio Tamazuj. (RT photo) Raymondo raised concerns about the 2026 amendments to the Election Act 2012, saying the changes had not been made publicly available despite the approaching election date. He questioned whether the electoral process could proceed with confidence while the public lacked access to the amended legislation. The legal expert also challenged the process through which constitutional amendments linked to the peace agreement were adopted, arguing that the required participation and approval of signatories had not been secured. Raymondo referred to Article 8.4 of the Revitalised Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan, which he said required approval by two-thirds of the relevant members of the national government and the agreement’s monitoring body. He argued that some signatories had not participated in the process, raising questions about compliance with the agreement and the constitutional framework. The claims could not be independently verified from the interviews, and the status of the amendments and the process through which they were adopted requires clarification from the relevant authorities. Raymondo warned that elections conducted in violation of the Constitution and the National Elections Act could be challenged. “If any elections [are] being conducted contrary to, in violation of the Constitution and the National Elections Act, the impact is that the election is null and void by nature,” he said. He added that a disputed electoral process could damage South Sudan’s international standing and undermine public confidence. Nyuon also discussed the amended election law, saying disagreements surrounding the amendments could contribute to continued uncertainty. He linked the changes to the use of constituencies established for the 2010 elections, arguing that the same constituencies were still being used. His account of the amendments’ legal status differs in emphasis from Raymondo’s concerns and requires clarification from the authorities responsible for the legislation. Unfinished peace agreement and security concerns Beyond the legal framework, Raymondo argued that the incomplete implementation of the 2018 peace agreement remained a major obstacle to credible elections. He pointed to the unification of armed forces as a key outstanding priority, saying the country needed a unified national army to improve security. He also cited the permanent constitution-making process, the return of internally displaced people and refugees, and the need for a population census and constituency-related arrangements as issues that should be addressed. Raymondo questioned whether elections could be conducted credibly while insecurity persisted and important provisions of the peace agreement remained unimplemented. He argued that the country should prioritise peace and national unity rather than focus solely on the election date. “For us, the people of South Sudan, we need peace. Election is not our first requirement,” he said. He called on political leaders to engage in dialogue and agree on a way forward if the elections could not be held as scheduled. Nyuon, meanwhile, focused on the preparedness of electoral institutions and political parties, saying the government needed to ensure that the commission had adequate funding and sufficient time to complete its work. He warned that further delays could erode public confidence in the government’s commitment to holding elections. Political participation under scrutiny The experts also raised concerns about the participation of political parties in the electoral process. Raymondo argued that preparations should involve all political parties rather than being dominated by one side. He said the NEC should communicate electoral procedures to all parties and ensure that political stakeholders had an opportunity to participate. He also raised concerns about reports that some aspiring candidates had faced restrictions on travelling outside Juba, arguing that restrictions on movement within the country could infringe constitutional freedoms. Nyuon said most political parties had not adequately prepared their candidates through internal primaries, while the ruling Sudan People’s Liberation Movement (SPLM) appeared to be more active. He warned that limited preparation by other parties could result in a contest dominated by the SPLM. “Election is not done by force,” Nyuon said, arguing that political parties needed to prepare if they intended to participate. The experts’ comments raise questions about whether the electoral process can accommodate meaningful political competition within the remaining time. However, the extent of preparations by individual parties and any alleged restrictions on candidates would require further verification. Experts propose different ways forward The experts differed in their emphasis on how the country should respond if the December elections cannot proceed. Nyuon predicted that a delay of two to three months was possible, arguing that the NEC should advise the president on a realistic timetable and the steps required to complete preparations. He urged the government to fund the institutions responsible for organising the elections so that any extension would not become prolonged. “My advice to the government is that since citizens’ hope is only in elections, and they want to elect a new government, it is good that the government should be able to fund the institutions that deal with election issues,” he said. Raymondo called for dialogue among the signatories to the peace agreement, saying they should agree on an arrangement to govern the country if elections could not be held on time. He suggested that the parties consider forming a temporary technical government for a specified period while addressing outstanding peace and security issues. Raymondo said ordinary citizens were more concerned about peace, insecurity, hunger and other pressing needs than political competition. “Election will come. Whether you like it or not, one day elections are going to be conducted. But before the election, we need peace,” he said. South Sudan’s general elections are scheduled for December 22, 2026. The assessments by the two experts point to questions over the legal framework, institutional preparedness and political conditions needed to conduct the polls. Neither expert’s prediction constitutes an official decision to postpone the elections. The National Elections Commission and the government would need to clarify the outstanding preparations, the status of the amended election law and whether the December timetable remains achievable. title: Hellenic Navy Liberates Mount Athos on November 2, 1912
body: The Hellenic Navy liberated Mount Athos on November 2, 1912, during the First Balkan War, marking a significant moment in the history of Greece and the Holy Mountain. The operation began when the Greek destroyer Thyella landed 40 marines at the port of Dafni. The force subsequently advanced to Karyes, establishing Greek control of the administrative centre of Mount Athos. The operation was reinforced by the arrival of the armoured cruiser Georgios Averof , accompanied by the destroyers Ierax and Panther , as well as an additional 200 marines. The naval deployment secured the liberation of the monastic peninsula, which holds enormous religious and historical significance for the Greek Orthodox world. November 2 remains an important date in the history of the Hellenic Navy and Greece’s liberation during the Balkan Wars, commemorating the role of the Greek fleet in extending the country’s control across the Aegean. title: Zelenskyy: Ukraine to keep striking Russian refineries until energy attacks stop
body:
Ukraine will continue launching strikes on Russian oil refineries unless the Russian Federation ceases its attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated in an interview with Fox News.

"We asked that we can't not respond after Russia's attack on our energy, after Russia is killing our people, if attacks on our electricity, gas refiners and everything.We said if you want us not to attack russia's refineries, they have not the attack our energy system," Zelenskyy said.

According to him, the Ukrainian side has repeatedly discussed the issue of strikes on Russian oil refineries with U.S. President Donald Trump and his team.

At the same time, Zelenskyy proposed an alternative—supplying Ukraine with Patriot missiles to protect its energy infrastructure. He noted that Ukraine is prepared to pay for them independently.
