title: ABU scientists win N1.2bn climate research grants
body: Scientists at the Institute for Agricultural Research (IAR), Ahmadu Bello University (ABU), Zaria, have secured four international research grants worth approximately N1.213 billion to advance climate-resilient agriculture in Nigeria. The grants, valued at $948,678.53, were awarded under the Action Research for Climate Adaptation in Agriculture (ARCAA) programme, a joint initiative of Research Triangle Institute (RTI) International and the Regional Universities Forum for Capacity Building in Agriculture (RUFORUM), with support from the Gates Foundation. The achievement makes IAR the only Nigerian institution to secure more than one grant under the highly competitive programme, accounting for four of the eight successful proposals from Nigeria. A statement by Dr Sharhabil Musa Yahaya, of the Agricultural Extension Unit of IAR, said the programme attracted 149 concept-note submissions, out of which only 14 were selected, representing a success rate of about 9.4 per cent. He said the four research projects will focus on developing alternative livestock feed from locally available materials, promoting solar-powered farmer-led irrigation, scaling up climate-resilient and drought-tolerant maize hybrids, and improving access to climate-resilient groundnut varieties through inclusive seed systems. According to him, the projects are expected to boost agricultural productivity, strengthen farmers’ capacity to withstand climate change and promote sustainable farming practices, particularly in Northern Nigeria. Commenting on the stride, Prof. Ado A. Yusuf, Executive Director of IAR, described the achievement as a testament to the dedication and research capacity of the institute’s scientists. He said the success demonstrated the quality of research ideas being developed at the institute and their relevance to the needs of farmers and the wider agricultural sector. Yusuf said the institute was committed to ensuring that research excellence translated into practical benefits for farmers, stronger agricultural systems and improved national food security. He congratulated the successful scientists and their research teams, assuring them of the institute’s continued support for innovation, collaboration and partnerships capable of addressing critical agricultural challenges. Similarly, the Vice-Chancellor of ABU, Prof. Adamu Ahmed, described the feat as an outstanding achievement that reflected the university’s growing reputation as a centre of research excellence in Africa. Ahmed said securing four of the 14 grants selected from 149 submissions, including half of Nigeria’s successful entries, demonstrated the quality of research capacity developed by the university.

title: Highly capitalised stocks push gain to N2 trn in October
body: …As investors reap N4.5trn WoW By Peter Egwuatu The Nigerian stock market strengthened Month-on-Month (MoM), in October 2026, as renewed buying interest in heavyweight stocks lifted the benchmark of the Nigerian Exchange, NGX Index above the 250,000-point psychological threshold. The rally added N2.01 trillion to market capitalisation, reflecting strong price appreciation in selected large-capitalised stocks across the Industrial Goods, Financial Services and Energy sectors. According to analysts, although the market’s upward movement suggests renewed investor confidence, the uneven distribution of gains points to a selective investment strategy. Investors appear to be concentrating on stocks with significant market influence while maintaining a cautious approach towards other equities. This divergence between index performance and market breadth remains an important consideration in assessing the sustainability of the current rally. Specifically, breakdown of trading in October showed that the NGX market capitalisation closed at N165.114 trillion from 163.104 trillion in September. Similarly, the NGX All Share Index, ASI surged by 1.2% to close at 254,299.49 points from 251,211.67 points in September. Meanwhile on Week-on-Week, WoW the market gained N4.595 trillion as market capitalisation rose from N160.519 trillion the previous week in October to close at N165.114 trillion last week while the NGX ASI rose by 2.9% from 247,222.27 points previous week to close at 254,299.49 points last week. On the global market, the oil prices continued to record performance as the retreat in prices last week reflected a reassessment of geopolitical risks as diplomatic efforts sought to revive peace negotiations. However, analysts noted that the outlook for oil remains sensitive to developments in the region, and renewed escalation could quickly alter market expectations. For Nigeria, movements in crude oil prices have implications for government revenue, foreign exchange supply and broader economic expectations. Higher oil prices can support public revenue and external balances, although their overall effect depends on production levels, domestic fuel costs and other economic conditions. Lower oil prices may ease some cost pressures but could also weaken revenue expectations if the decline is sustained. The effect on listed companies will vary according to their exposure to energy prices, foreign exchange movements, production costs and domestic demand. On market outlook, analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited stated: “Investors should therefore consider international oil movements alongside domestic economic indicators and company-specific developments rather than treating changes in crude prices as a uniform signal for the entire equities market. ‘‘More broadly, expectations regarding interest rates, inflation, corporate earnings and foreign exchange conditions may influence portfolio allocation decisions. ‘‘Where investors anticipate improved corporate profitability and more favourable financing conditions, equities may continue to attract demand. ‘‘Conversely, uncertainty over costs, earnings and valuations could encourage profit-taking in stocks that have recorded substantial price appreciation.” The post Highly capitalised stocks push gain to N2 trn in October appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Gunmen kill soldier, cart away weapons in Plateau
body: Gunmen, on Saturday night, attacked troops of Operation Enduring Peace, OPEP, at a checkpoint in Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State, killing a soldier and carting away two weapons. The incident occurred at about 8pm at the Sopp Checkpoint in Ungwan Boka community, Riyom LGA. Sources revealed that personnel of the operation were on duty when gunmen suddenly opened fire on them, killing the victim and taking away his rifle. The attackers, according to security sources, opened fire from different directions, leading to an exchange of gunfire before they fled into the surrounding bushes. The sources said, “The attack occurred while the troops were keeping vigil at the checkpoint. “The gunmen opened fire from different directions, forcing the troops to engage them in a gun battle.” Confirming the incident, spokesman of OPEP, Captain Chinonso Polycarp Oteh, described the attack as deliberate and unprovoked, saying troops have been deployed there to restore normalcy. Oteh said, “It was a deliberate and unprovoked attack on troops at Sopp Check Point, Ungwan Boka in Riyom Local Government Area. “Troops have restored normalcy in the area and are maintaining aggressive pursuit of the perpetrators in order to apprehend them and recover the carted-away weapons. “The situation remains under control, while troops continue to sustain heightened vigilance to prevent any further security breach and reassure residents of their safety. “The public is urged to remain calm, go about their lawful activities and volunteer credible information that could assist security agencies in their ongoing efforts, “ Captain Oteh added.

title: Dr Sultan Al Jaber urges energy security overhaul as nearly billion barrels drawn from oil markets
body: The disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has drained nearly one billion barrels from global oil inventories, exposing the need for a fundamental rethink of energy security, the Adipec conference in Abu Dhabi heard on Monday. “Simply put, the world has eroded its supply buffers,” said Dr Sultan Al Jaber, UAE Minister of Industry and Advanced Technology and managing director and group chief executive of Adnoc. “But, trust me, supply is only half the story. The other half is delivery." During the event's opening ceremony, Dr Al Jaber called for greater investment in supply infrastructure and artificial intelligence to help the energy industry withstand future shocks, warning that securing production was no longer enough to guarantee that supplies reach consumers. Referring to OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, who attended the ceremony, Dr Al Jaber said, “Sam, from the moment ChatGPT was born, the world has asked what energy can do for AI. And now, together, we will find out what AI can do for energy.” He spoke as Adnoc announced an agreement with OpenAI and G42 to become the world's first energy company to deploy OpenAI's Frontier platform, with plans to transform the Abu Dhabi energy company's field development, well management and commercial operations. The partnership, guided by Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, would make Adnoc's systems smarter, safer, more secure, more resilient and more productive, Dr Al Jaber said. The Iran war severely disrupted energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz and exposed weaknesses in global supply chains, he added. “For years, our industry optimised for just in time,” Dr Al Jaber said. “And to tell you the truth, we got very good at it. This year we got the bill for just in case.” Diesel stocks in some markets have fallen to their lowest seasonal levels in 35 years, while others face a 600 billion cubic feet gap in LNG supplies, he said. Shipping and logistics costs, which accounted for less than 5 per cent of the cost of a barrel before the disruption, now exceed 30 per cent. “Energy security is not only measured at the point of production. It is now also measured at the point of delivery,” Dr Al Jaber said. He outlined five priorities for strengthening energy security: accessible supply, routes to market, operational intelligence, investment confidence and people. He also called for intelligent energy systems capable of anticipating risks, improving performance and reducing costs. On investment, Dr Al Jaber said: “Capital follows confidence. Policy must create it … finance must accelerate it … and insurance must keep trade moving.” He said the UAE would continue to advocate dialogue, diplomacy and political solutions to support stability in energy markets and the global economy. “Talent stayed. Capital stayed. Investment kept coming … and the economy kept moving,” he said. “That is the UAE model, pressure-tested and proven by results.” Dr Al Jaber said Adnoc's preparedness had been developed years before the disruption. “We did not write our resilience playbook during this disruption. We wrote it years before,” he said. “Energy leadership is not measured by what you produce in good times. It is measured by what you deliver in hard times.” “Because when it counts the most. You can count on the UAE,” he added.

title: 9 dead as jet nosedives and erupts into fireball near busy roadway in South Florida
body:
Law enforcement respond to a plane crash in Palm Beach County, Fla., on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Mark Elias/AP hide caption
A business jet carrying nine people nose-dived into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes near a busy roadway. Everyone on board was killed, the nation's transportation secretary said.
Video recorded by people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the Bahamas-bound aircraft plunged from the sky before striking near the Palm Beach County roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining a crater as people milled about, expressing shock that it landed only feet from homes and inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy posted on X that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County at 12:50 p.m. and called it a "horrific tragedy." The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board's investigation, he said.
Law enforcement respond to a plane crash in Palm Beach County, Fla., on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Mark Elias/AP hide caption
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured or killed.
"It was a cataclysmic plane crash," DeSantis told reporters at the scene. "It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road."
Rain pounded the region on Sunday. A flood watch due to excessive rainfall was in effect through Monday afternoon, the National Weather Service said.
The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.
The plane was heading east at 35,000 feet (about 11 kilometers) when pilots reported turbulence, icing and precipitation and requested to climb another 2,000 feet (about 610 meters).
Moments later, the plane entered a steep dive, first 10,000 feet per minute, then 20,000 feet per minute and up to 30,000 feet per minute, speeding the plane beyond its design limits, according to air traffic control recordings and flight tracking data.
A pilot declared an emergency and issued distress calls. The plane banked sharply to the right before it smashed into the ground.
Minutes before the crash, the pilot reported ice accumulating on the jet and turbulence that was jolting it by as much as 700 feet (213 meters), according to air traffic control recordings captured by LiveATC.net.
"We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence," the pilot told controllers.
But the situation rapidly deteriorated. After encountering precipitation and requesting to climb, the pilot declared an emergency as the aircraft began losing altitude at an alarming rate.
"We're descending 8,000 – mayday, mayday - we're descending 10,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed.
"We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed, before delivering a devastating acknowledgment of what was about to happen. "We're going to crash into the ground."
Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, said the jet was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.
Steve Arroyo, an aviation safety expert, said icing and turbulence could have been factors in the crash and may have caused the plane to stall while it was cruising at 34,000 feet (10,363 meters).
There are many potential factors and the NTSB will consider all of them, including how the pilot responded to the icing and turbulence reported over the radio. But investigators won't rule anything out at this early stage, he said.
The NTSB said investigators were expected to arrive at the crash site on Sunday and Monday. A media briefing is scheduled for Monday in West Palm Beach.
Palm Beach County authorities were evacuating about 600 people from a nearby mobile home community while federal officials investigate the crash. The road will be closed until further notice, county officials said.
The crash occurred in Greenacres, Florida, according to Palm Beach County sheriff's officials. The city of 45,000 people is about 7 miles (11 kilometers) southwest of West Palm Beach.

title: Dangerous spices: How melted nylon additive keeps plantain chips crunchy
body: By Elizabeth Adegbesan For some years, plantain chip has been one of Nigeria’s ultimate snacks which is affordable, accessible, and portable. But as inflation hovers at historic highs, a sinister economic survival tactic has crept into the informal food sector. Economy&Lifestyle discovered that to cut costs and keep chips crispy for days, some street entrepreneurs are turning to a dangerous additive: melted cellophane bags. The cost of a crunch The mathematics of running a small-scale food business in Nigeria today is brutal. The price of vegetable oil, cooking gas, and raw plantains has tripled over the last two years. For vendors like Halima Mohammed, who operates a roadside frying station, the pressure to maintain profit margins without raising prices is suffocating. “If I increase the price of a small pack from N200 to N400, the students will walk away. “People don’t have money. So, vendors look for shortcuts to make the oil last longer and keep the chips from getting soggy in humidity.” The “shortcut” involves tossing polyethylene plastic bags directly into the scalding oil. As the plastic melts, it blends with the vegetable oil, creating a glazing agent. When the plantain slices are fried in this mixture, they form a glassy, ultra-crisp outer shell. Crucially for vendors, the plastic coating prevents the chips from absorbing moisture, extending their shelf life from two days to over two weeks. A lifestyle of hustle and denial In the underbelly of Nigeria’s entrepreneurial ecosystem, the practice is an open secret, driven by sheer desperation. The lifestyle of a micro-entrepreneur in Nigeria is defined by any-way-raw-iron—a slang term for survival by any means necessary. With no safety nets and a failing grid that forces reliance on expensive petrol generators, the boundary between ethical business and hazardous malpractice has blurred. Osaro Jimoh, a distributor who supplies packaged chips to traffic vendors on the , admitted that the market rewards the longest-lasting product. “The boys selling in traffic need chips that stay crunchy under the hot sun for days. “If the chips go soft, the motorists will throw them back at us. Nobody asks how the crunch is made; they just want the crunch. “I don’t know the preservative used to achieve such crunchiness.” For the millions of consumers who rely on these cheap snacks to get through grueling multi-hour commutes, the lifestyle implications are passive but deadly. Plastic-infused oil releases carcinogenic compounds, heavy metals, and microplastics into the food, posing severe long-term risks to liver and kidney health. The regulatory blind spot Agencies have repeatedly warned the public against consuming street foods prepared with plastic additives. However, enforcing regulations in a vast, informal economy is nearly impossible. Millions of fryers operate out of residential backyards, unbranded and untraceable. Public health advocate, Dr. Duro Ifagbemi, emphasized the gravity of the situation. “We are looking at a ticking time bomb of gastrointestinal complications and cancer cases,” he warned. “But you cannot solve a public health crisis without addressing the economic reality. “When people are starving, long-term health risks feel invisible compared to immediate poverty.” Surviving at all costs Though Mohammed denied using the plastic trick herself but acknowledges that the economic system pushes many over the edge. “Nigeria makes entrepreneurs out of necessity, not out of choice. “When the government makes it impossible to do business cleanly, people will find a way to survive in the dirt.” Until the macroeconomic pressures ease, the crisp snap of a roadside plantain chip will carry a cost far heavier than the few Naira exchanged on the asphalt. The post Dangerous spices: How melted nylon additive keeps plantain chips crunchy appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Professor Snyder and ‘Trump’s Big Lie’
body:
In his recent article reprinted in Kyiv Post “Trump’s Big Lie About Ukraine,” Professor Timothy Snyder has done a superb job exposing US President Donald Trump’s false narrative about Ukraine’s contributions to the US, Europe, and world peace.
According to Trump, the US has “done a lot” for Ukraine, but Ukraine has “done nothing” for the US. In other statements, Trump intimated that Ukraine has been a free-loader in receiving “billions” from the US but has given “nothing back”.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
So, here are some estimates of how much the US has saved and how much Russian military power Ukraine has destroyed in exchange for the “billions” it has received.
Let’s first agree on how many billions the US has actually provided “directly” to Ukraine. According to a recent New York Post article , direct aid to Ukraine during former US President Joe Biden’s administration totaled $130 billion. Although Congress approved $164 billion in Ukraine-related funding, that included associated US activities, indirect costs, and payments to third parties, not direct aid to Ukraine. A reasonable starting point for calculating US investment in Ukraine’s defense is $150 billion.
Trump’s comments indicate that he may have forgotten why Biden gave Ukraine $150 billion. He should review Russian President Vladimir Putin’s oft-repeated insistence on restoring Russian geopolitical influence and control over territory once governed from Moscow.
The 2022 US National Security Strategy (NSS) identifies Russia as an existential threat, and states that Russia’s invasion of Ukraine demonstrates its willingness to use military force to redraw borders and undermine European security. Had Putin defeated Ukraine, he would have greatly increased Russia’s military power and been emboldened to move against NATO and embroil US forces in NATO’s confrontation with Russian troops. It was only a matter of time.
However, Ukraine defied all expectations and, for almost five years, has held Putin’s forces in check and frustrated Putin’s ambition. NATO’s European members acknowledge they were entirely unprepared to face the threat. They have only begun developing their own military-industrial base and increasing their forces. But they will need at least five more years to become independent of the US.
As long as Europe and the US continue providing Ukraine what it needs to defend itself, Ukraine will hold Russia back. Putin will not open a “second” (NATO) front while facing a powerful, undefeated Ukraine to its south. But, if Ukraine is defeated, and Russia absorbs Ukraine’s human and material resources into its military, then only US deterrence stands between Russia and Europe.
The conservative American Enterprise Institute , in assuming that the US would honor its NATO commitment to deter Russia, estimated that the long-term cost to the US would likely be far higher than the cost of supporting Ukraine. Without Ukraine, Russian forces would be poised on the borders of a half dozen NATO countries, capable of immense mischief, and undeterred by either a solely European NATO or a Ukrainian “second front.”
The Institute estimates that “a world in which Russia prevails would be more dangerous and more expensive for America, requiring an estimated increase of $808 billion in US defense spending over five years.” A separate RAND perspective did not offer cost estimates, but concurred that a Russian victory would impose additional “colossal” costs on the US and its allies.
What would it then cost the US to participate with other NATO countries in stopping a much strengthened and emboldened Russia? No publicly available information can be found, but Ukraine’s experience can serve as a model, and artificial intelligence (AI) may have to do the heavy lifting.
AI was tasked with the following: “What would it cost the US if American Forces had to fight a conventional NATO-Russia war and absorb casualties and equipment losses on the scale of Ukraine?” We included assumptions such as three levels of US participation in the conflict, the types and costs of equipment, the current versus original value of equipment, potential casualty numbers, duration of hostilities, and, most importantly, comparison with America’s wars of this century.
The one factor that made the greatest difference but was most elusive was the probable casualty count and type because the US has the highest veteran life-care cost in the world, but no experience with new-generation warfare.
AI’s “reasonable and central” estimate of the costs the US would bear if Ukraine had been defeated and it participated 50% in the fighting to stop Putin’s move into Europe is $2-3 trillion. This may seem high to some and low to others, but it’s not unreasonable compared with the estimated cost of the Afghanistan war ($2.3 trillion), the Iraq war ($1-2 trillion), and even “peaceful” 5-year deterrence ($0.8 trillion). According to Brown University’s analysis of the 20 years of US Middle East wars, the total cost of those wars would be about $8 trillion.
One final factor we must not overlook is the military loss that Ukraine has inflicted on Russia. Notwithstanding Putin’s bravado in threatening one country or another with extinction, or declaring (as he has done recently) that he is “ready for war in Europe”, the simple reality is that Ukraine has inflicted such damage on Russia’s military capability that it is much weaker than it was before the war.
The Center for Strategic and International Security (CSIS) estimates that as of July, Putin’s military force has sustained 1,400,000 casualties, of which 450,000 have been killed. In addition, the CSIS estimates that Russia has lost one third to one half of its pre-invasion major combat equipment and has been forced to draw heavily from Cold War stockpiles to sustain the war.
It would take a long time to rebuild Russia’s conventional forces to a level that Putin, known to be a cautious man, would consider ready to launch a “war on Europe.” This should also be credited to Ukraine as a deterrent… and one that is still growing.
For those whose minds are open and eyes can see beyond their personal interests, it should be obvious that for every $1.00 that the US has provided Ukraine, Ukraine has “given back”, with its blood and suffering, and in addition to the invaluable boons and blessings listed by Professor Snyder, an estimated $20.00 saving of the costs the US is likely to incur if it were to honor its obligations to deter Russian attacks or in supporting our NATO allies in defeating those attacks.
As a side note, it bears remembering that Ukraine had “done a lot” for the US in destroying Russia’s ICBM force targeting hundreds of US cities, but the US had “done nothing” in return except default on its commitments. Had the US honored the terms of the Budapest Memorandum guaranteeing Ukraine’s sovereignty, Putin would not have invaded.
Ukraine would not need the “billions” that President Trump is bemoaning. And the five years of bloodshed and destruction need not have occurred. So, Mr. President, which came first... the chicken or the egg?
The views expressed in this opinion article are the author’s and not necessarily those of Kyiv Post.

title: Monitoring Of 62 Ebola Contacts To End By November 13 — NCDC
body: The 62 contacts identified following the confirmation of an imported Ebola case in the country are expected to complete monitoring by November 13, 2026, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has said. The agency disclosed this in its latest Ebola Disease Situation Report obtained by Channels Television on Monday. Nigeria confirmed its first case of Ebola disease in the current outbreak on October 20, 2026, after laboratory tests detected the Bundibugyo virus in a woman who had travelled to the country from Uganda. Although the NCDC did not provide a breakdown of the contacts according to their individual monitoring completion dates, it noted that the contacts were scheduled to complete follow-up at different times between October 31 and November 13. According to the report, “Sixty-Two (62) contacts” had been identified, adding that “Contacts are expected to complete follow-up by November. Expected completion dates range from 31 Oct to 13 Nov 2026.” The development indicates that November 13 is the latest projected date for completing the monitoring of all contacts currently identified in connection with the confirmed case, although surveillance and contact-tracing activities remain ongoing. It said contact tracing and monitoring were continuing, while additional contact tracers had been mapped and trained to strengthen surveillance. The agency also disclosed plans to “engage and assess additional contacts for possible evacuation to the quarantine facility” and “continue follow-up of contacts in quarantine.” It added that a high-level stakeholder meeting had been held with partner agencies to strengthen coordination, resource mobilisation and accountability in the response. Among its next steps, the NCDC listed the continuation of coordination across One Health sectors and partners, implementation of the Incident Action Plan and strengthened preparedness in states considered at high risk. On laboratory investigations, the agency disclosed that 18 samples had been tested since the outbreak was confirmed, with one positive result and 17 negative results. It stated that the positive sample was from the index case, while the 17 negative samples comprised 15 collected from contacts of the confirmed patient and two from suspected cases. The report said, “Laboratory confirmation reported on 20th October 2026,” adding that “Phylogenetic sequencing concluded by NCDC NRL & The African Centre of Excellence for Genomics of Infectious Diseases (ACEGID).” It said the scope and strategy for identifying contacts had been reviewed and expanded, while the case definitions for Ebola disease had also been reviewed to improve the identification and management of suspected infections. The report further listed plans to review guidelines on contact tracing, self-quarantine, self-care kits and the Ebola call protocol, as well as develop an Ebola disease dashboard on the Surveillance Outbreak Response Management and Analysis System, SORMAS, to improve contact management. On coordination, the NCDC said the National Incident Management System had been activated under the leadership of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate. It said the implementation of prioritised response activities had continued across thematic areas, while the Incident Action Plan had been finalised. It also disclosed that standard operating procedures and job aids had been validated for sample reception, molecular detection and genomic sequencing. The Agency said it would maintain uninterrupted Ebola testing and confirmation at the National Reference Laboratory, with plans to expand testing capacity to Lagos. It also listed the need to maintain diagnostic testing and laboratory records, share reports of genomic sequencing conducted on the confirmed case sample, and pre-position additional laboratory reagents and commodities across the national network of laboratories. The Agency also noted that an inspection and assessment of the isolation centre had been conducted and that the medical evacuation of the index case had been supervised, with measures taken to protect healthcare workers. Among its next steps, the NCDC said it would review and disseminate approved procedures and guidelines covering triage, isolation, supportive care, psychosocial support and discharge. It also planned to establish referral mechanisms for suspected cases, from the point of detection to designated treatment centres, while identifying and optimising treatment facilities in states with designated points of entry. On case management, the NCDC said it had further engaged the University of Abuja Teaching Hospital on its readiness to serve as an isolation and treatment centre. It disclosed that a needs assessment and optimisation of the hospital had been concluded, while the FCT team had been engaged on clinical care and psychosocial support for contacts in quarantine facilities. The agency added that it had secured a dedicated ambulance and placed it on standby for safe patient referral. On infection prevention and control, the report disclosed that needs assessments had been conducted across states and health facilities, while healthcare workers were being sensitised on appropriate infection prevention measures. It said engagement had also been held with the facility managing the index case on compliance with infection prevention and control guidelines, including standard and transmission-based precautions. The agency listed refresher training for environmental health officers and terminal cleaning at the residence of the index case as part of its response activities. It further planned to implement an infection prevention and control ring strategy across concentric perimeters to strengthen screening and isolation measures, as well as assess surge capacity for isolation at Karu General Hospital in the FCT. According to the World Health Organisation, the patient developed symptoms on October 7, four days after arriving in Nigeria, and sought medical attention at a private health facility in Abuja on October 11. The laboratory confirmation on October 20 made Nigeria the fifth country to detect the virus since the outbreak was declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo on May 15, 2026. The index patient was subsequently evacuated to Switzerland on October 26 for further medical care, alongside her husband, who was identified as a close contact. title: US trying to negotiate Russian gas supplies to Europe via Ukraine — WSJ
body:
NEW YORK, November 2. /TASS/. The United States is said to support the swift resumption of Russian gas supplies to Europe through Ukrainian pipelines, The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reports, citing US, European, and Ukrainian officials.
The proposal advanced by US envoy Steve Witkoff and Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner involves utilizing an American intermediary and an escrow account to bypass European sanctions, the newspaper said.
Washington also attempted to present this idea to European leaders as a method to reduce hydrocarbon prices amid record low European gas inventories ahead of winter.
The White House proposed storing the funds from the sale of Russian gas under this proposal in an escrow account under the jurisdiction of a third party, the news outlet noted.
Washington is also said to consider the resumption of the Nord Stream pipeline's operation as a potentially important component of a larger deal, which would not only lead to a resolution of the Ukrainian crisis but also settle Russia's long-standing disagreements with the European allies of the United States, WSJ added.
The White House and the US Department of State have not yet responded to the TASS request for comment.

title: Troops rescue 11 kidnapped victims in Kebbi operations
body: Troops of Operation FANSAN YAMMA have rescued 11 kidnapped victims in two separate operations in Danko-Wasagu Local Government Area of Kebbi. The Acting Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force, North West, Capt. Sinivie Tamuno, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday. Tamuno said the first operation occurred on Friday, following a distress call about terrorists blocking the Ribah-Dirindaji road. He said the terrorists were attempting to invade Ribah town when troops of Sector 2 responded to the distress call. According to him, troops discovered that the terrorists had fled with seven residents upon their arrival. He said the troops pursued the fleeing terrorists towards Rambo village, forcing them to release the captives under sustained pressure. “The rescued victims were Sa’adu Bala, 53; Nura Musa, 25; Dantami Yahyi, 57; Nasiru Muhammad, 21; Abdulakeem Abubakar, 23; Abdulahi Maikudi, 32; and Zaki Gambo, 56. “The victims, all indigenes of Ribah, had been reunited with their families,” he said. Tamuno said another operation occurred when troops conducting routine patrols in the Wasagu-Falfala area came under fire from terrorists. He said the terrorists had laid an ambush along the troops’ route before opening fire on the advancing security personnel. He added that the troops responded with superior firepower, forcing the attackers to flee in disarray. “During a follow-up search, the troops discovered four kidnapped victims abandoned by the fleeing terrorists. “The rescued victims were identified as Lawali Ali, 20; Samaila Shaibu, 14; Kasimu Shaibu, 20; and Aliyu Bala, 18,” he said. Tamuno said the rescued victims, who were residents of Wasagu village, had been handed over to the village head.(NAN)

title: Oman, China reaffirm strategic partnership, announce wider cooperation
body:
MUSCAT: Oman and China have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening their strategic partnership and expanding bilateral cooperation across economic, technological, energy, financial and security sectors, according to a joint statement issued on the occasion of His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik's state visit to the People's Republic of China. The joint statement emphasised the importance of elevating bilateral relations to broader and deeper levels, highlighting the role of high-level diplomacy in guiding cooperation between the two countries. Both sides acknowledged the depth of historical ties between Oman and China, which extend back more than 1,200 years, and expressed their determination to build on this longstanding relationship. The statement reaffirmed the commitment to the One-China principle, with Oman reiterating its support for United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758. China also praised Oman's role in promoting dialogue, resolving differences and supporting peace and stability in the region. On economic cooperation, both countries agreed to strengthen the alignment of China's Belt and Road Initiative with Oman Vision 2040, while expanding development partnerships and investment opportunities. The two sides agreed to deepen cooperation in the oil and gas sectors, renewable energy and energy storage, while exploring wider opportunities in artificial intelligence, advanced technologies, digital infrastructure and space. The joint statement also welcomed Oman's participation as a founding member of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation, reflecting the growing importance of emerging technologies in bilateral relations. In the financial sector, both countries highlighted cooperation through a local currency swap agreement and the development of digital payment systems and digital currencies. The statement further outlined plans to expand collaboration in culture, education, tourism, civil aviation and people-to-people exchanges, aimed at strengthening mutual understanding and connectivity. Oman and China also agreed to enhance military, security and judicial cooperation, including coordination to address common security challenges. At the regional level, both sides emphasised the importance of advancing negotiations towards the conclusion of a free trade agreement between China and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. The joint statement reflects the two countries' shared ambition to strengthen their longstanding partnership and establish new avenues of cooperation in strategic sectors that support their long-term development priorities.

title: East Front News #118: Putin is taking over Africa and Mig-29 jets for Ukraine
body:
East Front News is a weekly newsletter summarising the past week’s most important events concerning security and the situation in the Central and Eastern Europe region. It includes original opinions and comments, along with key news items significant from a Polish perspective. If you would like to receive this newsletter, please sign up by clicking HERE .
Russia is launching another major diplomatic and military push in Africa. More than 2,000 participants were expected at the Russia–Africa Summit in Moscow, with the Kremlin offering African partners air-defence systems, counter-drone technologies, military cooperation, nuclear energy and cybersecurity solutions.
Moscow increasingly combines arms exports with Russian military personnel, long-term security agreements and political support for African governments. The summit demonstrates that the war in Ukraine has not prevented Russia from expanding its influence on Europe’s southern flank.
Ukrainian MP Oleksiy Honcharenko claims that Volodymyr Zelenskyy rejected a 2023 peace proposal under which Russia would allegedly have withdrawn from most territories occupied after February 2022.
The problem is that the account contradicts Moscow’s own publicly stated position at the time. The analysis examines whether such an offer actually existed and challenges a narrative that could become an important element of Russian information warfare.
Russian authorities claim that 613 Ukrainian drones were heading towards the Moscow region during a massive overnight attack on 28–29 October. The operation lasted for more than ten hours.
The attack forced temporary restrictions at Domodedovo, Vnukovo and Zhukovsky airports and demonstrates Ukraine’s increasing ability to impose significant operational and psychological costs deep inside Russian territory.
Russia is not only fighting for Ukrainian territory but also attempting to permanently transform the population living under occupation. Russian passports, forced population transfers and the deportation of children are being used to make future reintegration with Ukraine increasingly difficult.
Access to healthcare, pensions, property rights and public services is increasingly linked to Russian citizenship. The demographic consequences — including deportations and the separation of Ukrainian children from their families — could remain visible for decades.
Poland will transfer another two MiG-29 fighters to Ukraine. One aircraft has already reached the end of its operational service life, while the second remains in active use.
The fighters will form part of a wider Polish military assistance package potentially worth around €50 million. Kyiv is also expected to receive additional air-defence equipment.
Germany’s permanent brigade in Lithuania will conduct electronic reconnaissance against Russian and Belarusian military activity. German troops will collect data on radars and other electromagnetic emissions from Kaliningrad and Belarus.
The Bundeswehr is also testing drone detection, jamming and signal-interception systems. The mission directly strengthens NATO’s situational awareness around the Baltic states and the Suwałki Gap.
Latvia has already recorded more than 12,000 attempted illegal border crossings from Belarus in 2026 — more than during the whole of 2025. Recent incidents suggest that migration pressure may increasingly be combined with sabotage against border infrastructure.
The key change is the possible use of migrants and criminal groups as cover for hybrid operations rather than relying exclusively on mass border pressure. Poland has meanwhile deployed Border Guard officers to assist Latvia.
NATO may be able to defeat Russia in a conventional conflict, but conventional superiority alone does not guarantee effective deterrence. Moscow is increasingly operating below the Article 5 threshold through sabotage, cyber operations and information warfare.
Harry Nedelcu argues that NATO therefore needs a theory of victory for hybrid warfare as well. A disorderly reduction of the US military role in Europe could create vulnerabilities before European allies are capable of replacing key American capabilities.
Ukraine has begun testing the Obria Nano satellite as a first step towards creating an independent satellite communications network controlled by Kyiv.
The objective is strategic: to reduce dependence on Starlink and Starshield after recent restrictions demonstrated that critical Ukrainian military communications can still be influenced by decisions made in the United States.
Poland is close to securing a European service centre for PAC-3 missiles used by Patriot air-defence systems. Warsaw has been competing with several countries, including Germany, for the investment.
Locating the facility in Poland would provide not only industrial benefits but also an important strategic capability on NATO’s eastern flank, where demand for air-defence missiles is rapidly increasing.
Germany plans to test Ukraine’s Bars cruise missile as Berlin looks for cheaper long-range strike capabilities to strengthen deterrence against Russia.
The development is significant because Ukraine is gradually moving from being exclusively a recipient of Western weapons towards becoming a potential supplier of combat-proven systems to major European NATO states.
Poland and the United Kingdom are deepening cooperation on next-generation air-defence missiles. The initiative comes as European states seek to expand their own production capacities after years of dependence on limited inventories.
For Warsaw, the programme could strengthen both national air defence and Poland’s position within the European missile industry.
Poland wants EU SAFE financing rules to accommodate defence equipment incorporating technologies or components originating outside the European Union, including systems from the United States, South Korea and Türkiye.
The issue is particularly important for Warsaw because several of Poland’s largest military modernisation programmes rely on non-EU suppliers. Restrictive rules could therefore complicate the use of European defence financing for existing Polish programmes.
Four naval vessels for Denmark are being built partly in Gdańsk. Three will be 60 metres long and one 72 metres, with the vessels designed for environmental protection, minelaying, patrol and surveillance missions.
The programme is worth around DKK 1.9 billion. Hulls and superstructures will be constructed in Poland before the ships are transferred to Denmark for final outfitting, with entry into service planned between 2028 and 2030.

title: Jet from Texas crashes near homes in Palm Beach, Florida, killing 9 on board
body: A business jet with nine people aboard nose-dived and crashed near homes in Palm Beach County, Florida, Sunday afternoon, killing everyone on board, officials said.No one on the ground was injured, Gov. Ron DeSantis told reporters at a news conference. Approximately 600 people were evacuated from the crash site near a mobile home park in Cresthaven, local officials said.The Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County just before 1 p.m., according to the Federal Aviation Administration. The agency said the aircraft had left Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was bound for the Bahamas. Details about what may have caused the crash had not yet been shared."It was like a missile coming down and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere. And to have those people on board, it's really a tragic way to see people pass away," DeSantis said.Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed on X that all nine people on board have died."Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost," Duffy wrote.Air traffic control audio captured the pilot's last communications with the ATC tower before the aircraft went down. The pilot can be heard saying they were descending 10,000 feet per minute, according to the audio on LiveATC.net. The pilot later declared an emergency, yelling, "We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute."The pilot is later heard telling the tower: "We're gonna crash ... We're out of time."The National Transportation Safety Board said Sunday it is launching a go-team to investigate the crash, with investigators expected to arrive later Sunday and Monday morning.Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, told the Associated Press that the jet was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight."This is definitely a tragedy," he said.Video from dashboard cameras in cars nearby captured the terrifying moment the aircraft plunged from the sky.The Palm Beach Sheriff's Office said all northbound and southbound lanes of Military Trail near Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North were closed until further notice.

title: Educator Who Changed Kazakh Schooling: Remembering Ybyrai Altynsarin
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – In 1864, a school with just 16 boys opened in Turgai, marking an important step toward expanding secular education across the Kazakh steppe. Its founder, Ybyrai Altynsarin, would become one of the most influential figures in Kazakh educational history, a legacy Kazakhstan honors on the 185th anniversary of his birth on Nov. 2. Ybray Altynsarin, a pioneering Kazakh educator, writer and ethnographer. Photo credit: ratel.kz Altynsarin’s efforts to expand access to schooling, develop educational materials in the Kazakh language and promote learning among girls transformed education across the Kazakh steppe. Born on Nov. 2, 1841, in what is now the Kostanai Region, Altynsarin lost his father at an early age and was raised by his grandfather, Balgozhy Zhanburchin. In 1850, he enrolled in a boarding school for Kazakh children under the Orenburg Border Commission, graduating seven years later. In 1860, he was appointed to establish a primary school for Kazakh children in a small town of Turgai. Despite limited funding and a resistance from local authorities, Altynssrin pursued the project, and the school finally opened on Jan. 8, 1864, with 16 boys enrolled. Altynsarin was committed not only to teaching but also to improving students’ moral and intellectual development. In a letter dated March 16, 1864, he described his enthusiasm for the work, writing that the boys had learned to read and write in Russian and Tatar within just three months. Building a modern education system In 1879, Altynsarin was appointed inspector of schools in the Turgai Region, a position he held until his death. From that position, he helped lay the foundations of a broader and more modern education system, opening four two-class Russian-Kazakh schools across the region and supporting the establishment of vocational, agricultural and girls’ schools, as well as schools for the children of Russian settlers. He placed particular emphasis on the quality of school facilities and the availability of books. Altynsarin planned to establish libraries for teachers and students at schools throughout the region, raising money for the initiative. “The purpose of these libraries is not only for students and teachers to use the books,” he wrote, “but also for graduates and literate people in general to have places in the steppe from which they can borrow useful books and guides for further self-education.” Altynsarin was committed not only to teaching but also to improving students’ moral and intellectual development. Photo credit: okmpu.kz Altynsarin was also a strong advocate for expanding educational opportunities for girls. With his support, a girls’ school opened in Irgiz, followed by similar institutions in Turgai, Kostanai and Aktobe in the years after his death. Recognizing the importance of teacher training, Altynsarin supported the establishment of a teachers’ school to prepare Kazakh educators. He also promoted libraries at schools, raising funds to provide books and learning materials for both students and teachers. He believed these libraries should serve not only pupils but also people who had completed their studies and wished to continue learning independently. These efforts reflected his broader vision: an education system supported by trained teachers, accessible learning materials and institutions that could serve the community. Contribution to Kazakh literature Beyond his work in education, Altynsarin helped shape the development of Kazakh written literature. He adapted the Cyrillic script for writing Kazakh and translated works by Russian authors, including Lev Tolstoy, Ivan Krylov and Konstantin Ushinsky, making their writings accessible to Kazakh readers. His own literary works included stories, fables, poems and adaptations of folklore. Among his best-known stories are “The Son of a Rich Man and the Son of a Poor Man,” “Mother and Son” and “The Clean Spring”. Through his writing, he promoted education, ethical conduct and the ideals of enlightenment. Altynsarin also documented Kazakh customs and traditions as an ethnographer. In 1868, he presented a study of courtship and wedding traditions in the Orenburg region to the local branch of the Imperial Russian Geographical Society. His research combined observations of everyday life with criticism of practices he considered outdated. A lasting legacy Altynsarin died at 47 on July 29, 1889, and was buried near his home on the banks of the Tobol River in what is now Kostanai. His influence extended far beyond the schools he established. Through his textbooks, literary works and efforts to expand access to education, including opportunities for girls, Altynsarin helped make learning more accessible to generations of Kazakh children. He id remembered as one of Kazakhstan’s foremost educators and enlightenment figures, whose belief in learning and the development of local expertise helped shape the country’s modern educational tradition. title: Is Darline Graham the canary in coal mine for midterm war backlash?
body:
This South Carolina contest is unexpectedly close in Tuesday's elections, drawing the president three times to shore up votes
Solid red South Carolina hasn’t elected a Democratic senator this century . But in the race between Republican. Darline Graham and her Democratic challenger, it’s now a draw.
The New York Times called the race a toss-up on Wednesday, with Graham, the sister of the late Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham, and Democrat Annie Andrews both receiving 48% in their latest poll. Fox News made the same call on Thursday.
Democratic Senate candidates in the state don’t tie Republicans. But against the backdrop of Donald Trump’s war and escalating energy and food prices, all bets appear to be off.
“It’s a f***ing train wreck,” said Rep. Nancy Mace, (R-S.C.) of the race on Wednesday. “It’s a mess.”
Former South Carolina Gov. Mark Sanford, after calling the political circumstances “absurd,” noted how President Donald Trump has campaigned three times in the state, twice in one week. It is unusual for Republicans, let alone a Republican president, to have to actively campaign here to firm up votes.
“I think it's crazy…It should be an absolute shoe-in.” he told CNN.
During one of his recent rallies, Trump called Andrews a "radical left lunatic.” Graham denounced her as “the most radical liberal candidate ever to run for office in the history of South Carolina.”
“She’s just plain old bat shit crazy,” Graham claimed.
“Is it bat shit to want cheaper gas and groceries?” Andrews shot back on X.
As elsewhere in the country, prices are rising in South Carolina because of the Iran war , which is threatening a number of Republicans in typically safe red states . The fact that Graham was sworn in mere days after her brother’s death in July has not sat well with many voters either, inviting charges of nepotism and questions about her competence.
But if prices weren’t going up and Trump and his agenda were still as popular in South Carolina as they were in 2024 or before that, it would be easier to imagine Graham getting a pass.
Voters know the president who once promised no new wars is now engulfed in an eight-month-long one in Iran , something they are reminded of every time they pump gas. The state is home to eight military bases and military families have been directly affected by the war.
"My opponent...had the opportunity to vote to end the war. But three times in a row, she voted to continue it,” said Andrews in the only debate between her and Graham last month.
“This reckless war in Iran has helped drive fuel prices to record highs,” Andrews said at a campaign stop in late September. “Darline Graham has voted multiple times to continue this war that is directly responsible for the six-dollar diesel.”
“We need to lower the damn diesel,” Andrews declared.
If voters are souring on war along with surging prices, Graham being the sister of one of the biggest war cheerleaders in modern political history is probably not a positive. Nor are perceptions that Graham was installed as a reliable pro-war, pro-Trump vote, just like her brother.
“They don't like the idea of a puppet,” Sanford said of Graham and voters. “Somebody who, you know, do as (they’re) told by the president just because he helped drag (her)...across the finish line” during the Republican primary.
When Graham clumsily said “national security is not my thing” to a question about the importance of Taiwan and the South China Sea during an August primary debate, Trump defended her gaffe: “She is going to do what the military wants, and really what the president wants.”
“She understands that national security is my thing,” Trump added.
That state Republicans like Mace and Sanford are griping publicly is indicative of broader frustration. Graham’s closest opponent in the GOP primary, Rep. Ralph Norman, has been urged to campaign for Graham but he still refuses . “My family is not going to vote for Darline Graham. They’re just not,” said Norman, who ran as a war skeptic . An anonymous House Republican called the competitive Senate race in South Carolina “embarrassing,” and said that Graham was “dragging Rs down the ticket,” according to NewsNation reporter Joe Khalil.
Graham’s war quandary is not dissimilar to at-risk Republicans in other states, like consummate hawk Mike Rogers in Michigan, who is now lamenting that “the war with Iran needs to end and end quickly.” Like other Democrats, Rogers’ opponent, Abdul El-Sayed, presents himself as an antiwar, and like other Democrats, a real “America First” candidate .
“A real America first approach, a real Iowa first approach, is let's take care of our citizens here and I would be fundamentally against the war,” said Democrat Josh Turek who is in a dead-heat race for Iowa’s senate seat against Trump-endorsed Republican Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa).
Neck-and-neck poll findings do not mean the race is lost for Darline Graham, but she has already lost the confidence of many in her party. Perhaps most voters will agree.
Because South Carolinians, like most Americans, like affordability. They also dislike wars that make affordability impossible, and especially those they were promised wouldn’t happen.

title: His Majesty meets Chinese Premier, discusses strategic cooperation
body:
MUSCAT: His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik held a meeting with Li Qiang, Premier of the State Council of the People's Republic of China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Monday, as part of His Majesty's state visit to China. The meeting discussed ways to strengthen strategic cooperation and expand economic, trade and investment partnerships between Oman and China. Both sides also exchanged views on several current regional and international issues of mutual interest.
MUSCAT: His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik held a meeting with Li Qiang, Premier of the State Council of the People's Republic of China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Monday, as part of His Majesty's state visit to China.
The meeting discussed ways to strengthen strategic cooperation and expand economic, trade and investment partnerships between Oman and China. Both sides also exchanged views on several current regional and international issues of mutual interest.
During the meeting, the Chinese Premier welcomed His Majesty the Sultan and the accompanying official delegation, highlighting the significance of the visit in reflecting the strength of Oman-China relations and the mutual commitment to advancing cooperation. He emphasised the importance of further expanding bilateral ties, particularly in the economic, investment and commercial sectors, to strengthen the strategic partnership and support the future aspirations of both countries. Earlier, His Majesty the Sultan and Chinese President Xi Jinping held an expanded session of official talks at the Great Hall of the People, reviewing existing areas of cooperation and exploring opportunities for further collaboration. The discussions focused on technology and innovation, artificial intelligence, energy, renewable energy, manufacturing, logistics, digital trade and food security, alongside strengthening integration between economic zones and ports. His Majesty's two-day state visit, which began on November 1, marks the first visit to China by an Omani head of state since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries in 1978.

title: Edward Asare inducted as Full Member of CIMG
body: Marketing Communications and Public Relations Professional, Edward Asare, has been inducted as a Full Member of the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG), marking another milestone in his professional career. Mr Asare announced his induction in a social media post, expressing gratitude to the leadership of the Institute for their guidance and encouragement throughout the process. He particularly acknowledged the Institute’s President, Michael Abbiw, and Vice President, Ama Amoah, for their support. He also expressed appreciation to Prof. Kobby Mensah of the University of Ghana Business School (UGBS), who taught him during his MBA in Marketing programme, for his contribution to his academic development. He further acknowledged Amin Ayarnah for helping him understand and navigate the membership process, as well as Chris Atadika, PhD, his course mate and former teaching assistant, for his role during his MBA studies. Mr Asare also congratulated fellow inductees Agatha Nketsia, Samantha Abdallah and Veronica Lariba, while expressing his commitment to learning from fellow members and contributing to the Institute’s work. With professional experience spanning media, banking, insurance and the public sector, his work focuses on digital communication, media relations, brand storytelling and stakeholder engagement. He is also a speaker, trainer and mentor with an interest in sharing practical insights on marketing, communication and digital media.

title: Provident Scheme to replace gratuity for expats in Oman from July 2027
body:
Muscat: The new Provident Fund Scheme for expatriate or non-Omani workforce will come into effect from July 19, 2027. The scheme requires employers to contribute 9% of each worker’s basic wage monthly, in accordance with the Social Protection Law. Provident Scheme From the date of implementation, the Scheme will replace the end-of-service gratuity for the period of service covered by the Scheme. Workers' savings and the returns accrued on them will be disbursed in accordance with the provisions of the Social Protection Law.
Muscat: The new Provident Fund Scheme for expatriate or non-Omani workforce will come into effect from July 19, 2027.
The scheme requires employers to contribute 9% of each worker’s basic wage monthly, in accordance with the Social Protection Law.
From the date of implementation, the Scheme will replace the end-of-service gratuity for the period of service covered by the Scheme.
Workers' savings and the returns accrued on them will be disbursed in accordance with the provisions of the Social Protection Law.
End-of-Service Gratuity for Previous Service Periods (Before July 19, 2027)
The gratuity for previous service periods may be settled through one of the following options:
1. Retained by the Employer: The Employer keeps the gratuity and pays it to the worker at the end of service. It is calculated using the worker's basic wage at that time, in accordance with the Labour Law
2. Paid Directly to the Worker: The gratuity is paid into the worker's bank account upon implementation of the scheme.
3. Deposited with the Social Protection Fund: The gratuity is deposited into the worker's account with the Social Protection Fund.

title: A400000 Winners
body:
This site is supported by donations to The OEIS Foundation .
We are pleased to announce the winning sequences in the OEIS 400k celebration. Well over 100 nominations were received, covering a great many topics collectively showing that the spirit of the OEIS is alive and well.
The selection committee consisted of Sean A. Irvine , Jonas Karlsson , Hugo Pfoertner , and Neil J. A. Sloane . Committee members abstained from providing evaluations on sequences they authored or were closely involved with. The selection committee would like to thank all the people who took time to nominate a sequence.
A400000 (previously A399633 ) Eric Fox The city-building sequence: a(n) = the height h of the shortest building which can see exactly h earlier buildings.
The height of a building in Eric Fox's City-Building sequence is determined by how many existing buildings it can see. This impressed all the judges as by far the most brilliant invention of 2026. There are already 25 other sequences that reference it.
A399995 (previously A394611 ) Joshua B. Weinstein a(1) = 0. For n > 1, a(n) is the number of ways to write a(n-1) as the sum of two earlier terms with distinct positions in the sequence. A simple definition leading to a frustratingly difficult unsolved problem.
A399996 (previously A400866 ) Dmitry Kamenetsky Number of free polyominoes with 2n cells that can be dissected into two congruent polyominoes. The best polyomino sequence of the year.
A399997 (previously A397960 ) Wujie Gu a(n) is the maximum number of distinct positive differences of an n-element subset of {0, 1, ..., n*(n-1)/2}. An instant classic extremal set-theory problem.
A399998 (previously A400887 ) Rok Cestnik a(n+1) = a(n-a(a(n))^2) + 1, a(0) = 0. A new twist on the classic Hofstadter recurrences.
A399999 (previously A400462 ) Ed Pegg Jr Number of ways to cut a 30-60-90 triangle into n 30-60-90 triangles. One of several triangle dissection problems, lovely pictures.
A400001 (previously A400663 ) Felix Huber a(n) is the number of congruence classes of nondegenerate triangles whose vertices are points of an n X n X n grid. One of several excellent Huber sequences relating to triangles.
A400002 (previously A400976 ) Aidan Markey Start with a set of two adjacent points in a hexagonal lattice. At each iteration, add to the set the lattice points which are adjacent to exactly two points already in the set, but only if those two points are adjacent to each other. The sequence gives the number of points in the set after n iterations. An unusual sequence of clusters.
A400003 (previously A399179 ) Michael S. Branicky and N. J. A. Sloane The sequence of binary decisions that defines the unique infinite path in the base-10 comma child graph. Previously MSB/NJAS had to use Koenig's Lemma and the Axiom of Choice to show that it was possible for the kangaroo to escape death. Chris Randall and Paul Roberts showed without using AI that there is a unique path with a simple recurrence.
A400004 (previously A401021 ) Scott B. Farrar Half the minimum surface area of a rectangular box with positive integer side lengths and volume at least n. A new problem with a classic feel.
A400005 (previously A395645 ) Rémy Sigrist Consider the square spiral with its cells numbered starting at 0. Three players, Red, Green and Blue, take turns and place knights at the smallest unoccupied cell not attacked by an existing knight of a different color. Sequence lists squares occupied by a Red knight. A representative of many astonishing sequences of knights on an infinite chessboard, a popular topic after a Numberphile video appeared.
These are a further ten nominated sequences which the committee found particularly attractive or interesting. These sequences have all received the keyword “nice” but retain their original A-numbers.
A394184 ( Charles L. Hohn ) Number of primitive tessellations of paths of length n in the square lattice, reduced for symmetry (with rotations, reflections, and translations not counted as distinct).
A396596 ( Hal M. Switkay ) Natural numbers k such that the sum of the x-th powers of the divisors of k achieves a record, for some x <= 0.
A397182 ( N. J. A. Sloane ) a(n) = maximum number of regions the plane can be divided into by drawing n constrained long-legged A's
A398965 ( Jens Ahlström ) Squares visited by a "Carpenter" (Dabbaba + Knight) moving on a spirally numbered board always to the lowest available unvisited square.
A399136 ( Stephen J. Pursey ) a(n) is the smallest number of cells in a polycube that has a cavity consisting of exactly n cells.
A399138 ( Aleksei Kudriashov ) a(n) = maximum number of points in an n X n X n grid with no three collinear.
A399946 ( Eliott Grillet ) Maximum terminal value in the Gilbreath reduction of graceful paths of order n.
A400615 ( Jakob Süskind ) Maximum number of edges in the Hasse diagram of a lattice with n elements.
A400939 ( Zlatko Damijanic ) The halving Recaman walk: a(1) = 1; for n > 1, a(n) = a(n-1)/2 if a(n-1) is even and a(n-1)/2 has not already appeared, otherwise a(n) = a(n-1) + n.
A401169 ( Scott Duke Kominers ) A quadratic form represents every Fibonacci number iff it represents these ten numbers.

title: Did you observe a 'fireball' in the skies of Oman on Sunday
body:
The Oman Society for Astronomy and Space (falakoman) said that it has been closely following the discussions surrounding the light phenomenon observed in the skies over the Sultanate of Oman on Sunday evening, around 7 pm.
The Oman Society for Astronomy and Space (falakoman) said that it has been closely following the discussions surrounding the light phenomenon observed in the skies over the Sultanate of Oman on Sunday evening, around 7 pm.
Initial observations suggest it may be a fireball—a highly luminous meteor resulting from a space object entering the atmosphere at high speed, causing it to glow and leave a bright light trail. The Falakoman clarified that the appearance of this phenomenon does not necessarily indicate a meteorite impact on Earth's surface, and it may be accompanied by a natural sonic boom produced by shockwaves as the object passes through the atmosphere. The Society said the importance of exercising caution in sharing information and avoiding interpretations not based on scientific evidence.

title: The Problem with C++ Safety: Modern C++ Is a Mindset, Not a Standard
body:
In the first part of this article, we have taken a look at two attempts to decide whether a given string is a palindrome. Both implementations were written in “Classic C++” and didn’t feel great: the code was difficult to read, hard to understand and consequently the defects were difficult to detect. Now it’s time to continue the story and to take a look at a better solution, the “Modern C++” solution.
So let’s take a look at a modern C++ solution.
Yes, it’s that simple: a single function call to the std::equal() algorithm. We compare the first half of the range represented by forward iterators with the second half of the range represented by reverse iterators.
“But Klaus, wait a second: this std::equal() algorithm is ages old! This has been part of C++98! This isn’t modern, is it?”
If this is what you are thinking, then I have some important information for you: modern C++ is not about new features or new C++ standards. It is about writing correct, fast and safe code by default. It is about a certain mindset. So to prove my point, ask yourself the question from before: are you certain that there are no safety or security related issues?
There are none, right? And it is so easy to verify: no if statements — in fact, no conditionals at all, no pointers or indices, no explicit loop. It’s just a single, simple function call. So this code is correct by inspection. It is correct by default. And it is simple. And fast.
There is even a newer, even more elegant solution:
This is the C++20 ranges-based solution. We are using the std::ranges::equal() function on the string and its reverse representation directly. We don’t even need iterators anymore. Admittedly, we are now comparing the entire range and not just the first and second half. However, performance aside, the simplicity, the elegance, and the correctness by default are amazing! This is what we refer to as “Modern C++”.
“OK, Klaus, I agree this is simpler and correct by default. But does this really mean that the loop-based solution is bad? After all, it works, doesn’t it?”
You are correct, it “works”, ignoring the UB for single-character strings. But it is more complicated, requires more effort to verify, takes more time to write, is more difficult to read and understand, requires considerably more testing and just isn’t correct by default. All of which means that, in the end, it is considerably more expensive, too. There simply isn’t a good enough reason to write it in this classic style anymore. This is exactly what I perceive as the real problem in our community.
Too many C++ developers have not embraced modern C++ yet and still use the dangerous and more error-prone constructs by default. Too many C++ developers don’t know about the modern ways of doing things or, for whatever reason, still prefer to write the more explicit code. Because of this, they work by default in the “unsafe mode” of C++.
To me this feels like an educational problem, a teaching issue. For too many decades people have written this classic C++ and “it was OK”. By now people feel too comfortable, feel too familiar with this style. This is the real problem.
Unfortunately, this problem is currently getting scaled up significantly: With the use of AI tools, people generate this kind of classic C++ automatically. And yes, I have got proof: I asked ChatGPT to generate an is_palindrome() function for me (see Figure 1). Guess what: it gave me almost exactly the function from the original LinkedIn post. And no: it didn’t even consider suggesting the use of an algorithm.
So why don’t these modern tools use the modern way? Well, despite the name, AI has nothing to do with intelligence. It is a statistics-based tool. If more people use the classic way, then statistically this is the “correct” solution. So it is not a big surprise that AI tools will rather write a for loop for you instead of using an algorithm.
I should be honest and state that this is not true for every AI tool on the market. Some are better than others, some actually suggest using an algorithm. However, this unfortunately doesn’t resolve the problem: AI tools may suggest outdated solutions, which are not best practice anymore.
Luckily many people in the community know better than the AI tool and know about the modern solutions. Let me use this opportunity for a shout-out to some people that quickly posted a good and modern solution to the original LinkedIn post. Many thanks to Alex Dathskovsky and Sergii Rybin for posting an algorithm-based solution. Honestly, we need more people like you that help to spread the information on how things should be done today. Thank you very much!
So what else can we do? I for one can do my part as a C++ trainer: I can tell people. I can teach people. I can show people. And this is what I want to do here in Rainer Grimm’s blog: in the coming months I want to talk about the modern way of doing things in C++. I want to demonstrate how we work today, in the hope that this makes a difference, in the hope of establishing the modern C++ mindset and of maybe (hopefully!) contributing to the general realization, even beyond the C++ community, that C++ can be incredibly safe, if we just use it as it is supposed to be used.
In the following months, I’ll write about bounds safety, type safety, lifetime safety, initialization safety, and — as a special add-on — about undefined behavior. And I will demonstrate that with very little effort, you can avoid all of these safety problems easily and by default.

title: Taiwan plans UAV acquisitions to boost maritime domain awareness
body:
Taiwan’s Republic of China Navy (ROCN) is seeking to significantly expand its unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) fleet to enhance its maritime domain awareness and targeting capabilities.
According to 2027 defence budget details released in late August this year, Taiwan has earmarked NT$52.78 billion (US$1.67 billion) to acquire two types of UAV.
The first is a vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) UAV being procured under Project Yuan Xiao (Distant Owl).
When the project was first reported as part of the NT$1.25 trillion (US$40 billion) special defence budget in late 2025, the UAV was specified to have a full-load endurance exceeding 13 hours, a guidance range of more than 130km, and an operating altitude above 15,000ft. Payload requirements included thermal and optical imaging, as well as laser-ranging capabilities.
It is understood the ROCN has set its sights on Shield AI’s V-BAT VTOL platform. A total of NT$36 billion (US$1.14 billion) is allocated for the programme between 2026 and 2029 to procure 280 Group 3 UAVs, 140 guidance and control systems and 82 transport vehicles.
The definition of a Group 3 UAV is one weighing between 25kg and 599kg, able to fly at altitudes between 3,500ft and 18,000ft, and with a top speed of less than 250kt.
The V-BAT has been combat-proven in Ukraine, where its autonomous systems enable it to operate in GPS-denied and communications-degraded environments.
According to reports, V-BATs could be deployed aboard ROCN surface combatants equipped with helidecks, providing them with an organic, persistent UAV capability to find, fix, track, target and engage adversary vessels.
V-BATs could also serve with the ROCN’s Haifeng brigades under its Littoral Combatant Command. These units operate both land-based mobile and fixed Hsiung Feng II and III anti-ship missile systems.
Shield AI and its local partner, the Aerospace Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC), announced on 13 October 2026 that they had delivered the first of twelve V-BATs ordered by Taiwan’s Coast Guard Administration for its shipborne UAV programme in July.
When asked by the media about the ROCN’s requirement, Shield AI declined to provide details, but it did confirm it would bid for the programme.
The second system mentioned in defence budget documents is the National Chung-Shan Institute of Science and Technology’s Rui Yuan II (Albatross II) medium-class UAV.
Plans call for the procurement of 32 aircraft, eight control stations and 48 transport vehicles between 2026 and 2029, at a cost of NT$16.78 billion (US$530 million).
The Rui Yuan II has an endurance of 16 hours, and a guidance and control range exceeding 300km. Its modular payload configuration can accommodate sonobuoy dispensers and various effectors, including the Jinfeng-1 reconnaissance and strike loitering munition. The UAV is also equipped with a ventral radome housing a maritime search radar.
The Rui Yuan II is expected to replace the Rui Yuan I platform, which was transferred from the ROC Army to the ROCN about a decade ago, and which is equipped with a limited electro-optical payload.
Among its priority targets in opening strikes, the People’s Liberation Army would likely include ROCN land-based maritime radar stations and command-and-control (C2) facilities, seeking to disrupt Taiwan’s maritime surveillance and coordination capabilities.
Cut off from C2 networks, defence analysts say ROCN surface combatants and Haifeng brigades may have to take the initiative by relying on organic UAV capabilities such as the V-BAT to independently complete the kill chain.
